quote: Using a qualitative interpretivist approach and thematic analysis of scholarly and institutional practice documents, this research proposes the GENESIS framework
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative thematic analysis of documents that proposes a conceptual assessment framework. It is not an empirical intervention study with a control group or a quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study under E6. Design and outcome criteria are clearly not met. E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that is supported by the abstract, since E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone.

quote: The study utilizes a cross-sectional survey methodology to collect data from EFL students enrolled in English language programs in Khaf city.
rationale: The study concerns English as a foreign language, which is non-STEM content (E2). It is also a cross-sectional survey measuring perceptions rather than a quantitative learning outcome, with no control group, so it would fail E3, E5 and E6 as well. Under the protocol's order, E2 is reported first.
rationale_note: Exclusion made at abstract stage on positive evidence of non-STEM content and survey design.

quote: A total of 784 student-chatbot interactions were categorized into ICAP modes in order to examine patterns in question types and their association with conversation length, student performance
rationale: The abstract describes an observational analysis of student-ChatGPT interactions in a biology exam review, correlating question types with conversation length and performance. There is no separate control group without generative AI and no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison design, so the comparison and design criteria are not met. Under the rule that exclusion requires positive evidence, E3 is applied because no non-generative-AI comparison group is evident. Biology is STEM-adjacent, but the design failure alone is sufficient for exclusion.

quote: This study examines data from 100 students and 100 teachers collected through structured questionnaires.
rationale: The abstract describes a questionnaire-based perception study of students and teachers with no control group and no learning outcome measured. Design is a survey, which is not an eligible design. Per the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing) is uncertain from the abstract, but the clearest positive failure is the absence of any comparison group, so E3 is applied. Abstract-stage evidence is positive for failure of comparison and outcome, so exclusion is justified.

quote: Using a qualitative interpretive design, nineteen purposively selected participants - CS students, ICT managers, and university lecturers were interviewed through semi-structured interviews
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. Per the exclusion-code order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly evidenced as a failure at abstract stage, and the first clearly applicable code is E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's quantitative sense, since the design is qualitative interpretive with no comparison or outcome measure). Exclusion is warranted on the positive evidence of a qualitative design with no control group.

quote: Employing a pre-experimental single-group pre-test/post-test design, the research assessed changes in cognitive outcomes and holistic competencies among 31 pre-Senior High School students in Ghana
rationale: The abstract explicitly describes a single-group pre-test/post-test design with no comparison group, which fails the comparison and design criteria (E3: no control group without generative AI). The rule for E3 applies: one group measured before and after.

quote: A qualitative interpretive design was used, based on semi-structured interviews with thirty Arab students
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study with thematic analysis, with no experimental or comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of an eligible comparative design. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is used as the first applicable code in the order of the protocol's design-related failures; E3 or E5 would also fit, but the qualitative design is the most direct failure. The STEM domain is not stated in the abstract.

quote: A rapid review of the literature was performed utilizing a librarian-generated search strategy
rationale: This is a rapid review of literature, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It also focuses on medical education (health professions), which fails the STEM domain criterion. Excluding on E6 as the first applicable code in order is reasonable, though the review's own exclusion of medicine would also apply. Only seven studies were quantitative, but the review itself is not an empirical study.

The abstract describes a development framework and tutorials for Colab/Gradio interactive modules with automated grading. It reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no learning outcome. The only mention of large language models is speculative ("chatbots will be able to guide students"), so there is no positive evidence of a learner-facing generative AI intervention tested against a control. Its design is a tool/tutorial contribution, not a comparative study. Excluded on E3 (no control group without generative AI), since the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group. Note that E1 could also apply, since generative AI is not clearly part of the learner activity. E3 was chosen as the first code that the abstract supports.

quote: Entrepreneurship education extends across interdisciplinary knowledge fields, incorporating subjects like finance and risk management
rationale: The content is entrepreneurship education (finance, risk management), which is not one of the protocol's STEM domains. The abstract also compares LLMs with a graph convolutional model on question answering, not a learner-facing control design with a non-generative-AI learning group, so the design is unclear. Exclusion under E2 (content not STEM) applies first in the code order.

quote: The application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in education is increasingly promising.
rationale: Abstract describes ChatGPT use by postgraduate Islamic Education Management students to write scientific articles, with a control group and test-based outcomes. However, the content is scientific article writing in Islamic education management, which is not a STEM domain (science, math, statistics, engineering, CS, programming, data science). Excluded under E2. Other criteria appear met at abstract level.

quote: This article tries using Large Language Models (LLMs) for creating warm starts. Results are compared against Gaussian Process Models and Tree of Parzen Estimators.
rationale: The LLM is used to generate warm-start configurations for an active learner in software configuration optimization. No learner interacts with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, so E1 applies. Population (no learners) and the learning-outcome framing are also not met, but E1 is the first applicable code. Abstract stage exclusion is justified by positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing.

quote: Using survey data from 48 students in a graduate programming course, we assessed how these learning styles and GenAI usage profiles impact students' confidence and frustration when learning to program.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey study of confidence and frustration (affective perceptions) with no quantitative learning outcome and no control group comparison. Outcomes are affective, which the protocol excludes, and the design is survey-based rather than an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Excluded at E5 as the first applicable code in order; E1/E2/E3/E4 are not clearly failed from the abstract alone, but E5 is positively evidenced.

criteria.outcome_note: no comparison or learning outcome described

quote: The developed approach provides a more interactive and personalized coding-learning environment and demonstrates the potential of combining LLM assistance with learner behaviour analysis.
rationale: The system uses a local LLM (Qwen2.5-Coder via Ollama) for questions, hints and evaluation in a programming context, so intervention and domain appear met. However, the abstract describes only system development and features (monitoring, logging, feedback) with no control group, no comparative design, and no reported learning outcome such as achievement or problem-solving scores. This is positive evidence that no quantitative learning outcome is reported, so exclude under E5. Note that the abstract gives no evidence of a comparison or empirical evaluation either; if the full text reports a controlled study with learning measures, it could be reconsidered at fulltext.

quote: In this study, we, three MTEs, utilized a self‐study methodology to first highlight how our domains of knowledge informed our prompt engineering techniques
rationale: The abstract describes a self-study of three mathematics teacher educators reflecting on prompt engineering with ChatGPT. It has no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is a qualitative self-study, which is not an empirical comparative design, so it fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. Exclusion uses E6 (not an empirical study) as the primary reason; the study is not an experiment.

criteria.comparison_note: no control group described in abstract

quote: In a Spring 2025 deployment in an Operating Systems course with approximately 100 students, CodeDive captured nearly 25,000 code snapshots and over 4000 execution events with a low overhead.
rationale: Abstract describes a platform for behavioral tracking and a single deployment with no comparison group, no learning-outcome measure, and no indication of a generative AI tool learners interact with (LLMs are discussed only as an integrity concern). Positive evidence of a failed criterion exists: no control group and no quantitative learning outcome reported. Excluded at the first applicable code in order that the abstract supports; E1 would be the earliest code, but the abstract does not establish that the intervention is learner-facing generative AI, so E3 is the clearest failing criterion. Possibly E1 on fulltext review. Note: under the protocol's code order, E1 precedes E3; the abstract gives no positive evidence of a learner-facing generative tool, so this is a provisional exclusion.

quote: This cross-sectional survey study recruited 386 medical students from three public universities in Saudi Arabia.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey measuring perceptions of ChatGPT's effectiveness, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of failure exists on design (survey, no comparison) and outcome (perceptions only). Medical education also raises a domain concern (health professions). The first applicable code in protocol order is E3 for no control group, but the abstract's clearest failure is the perception-only outcome; E5 is reported as the decision code applied here.

quote: Among the groups, we found significant differences in performance on conceptual assessments of the laboratory content
rationale: At abstract stage, the study compares students using AI-generated simulations against physical equipment and prebuilt simulator groups, with a conceptual assessment outcome in physics (STEM) for a second-semester college physics course (higher education). Design is not explicitly stated as randomized or quasi-experimental, so design is unclear, but the abstract does not give positive evidence of failure. Effect size (eta squared) is reported, and the publication is a journal article in PRPER. Include for full-text check of design and effect-size data.

quote: Data collection involved questionnaires on prior experience with the content, self-assessed AI competencies, and user perception of the chatbot.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study reports a single-group test of a GPT-4o chatbot with 25 preservice mathematics teachers, with no mention of a control group. Outcomes are questionnaire-based perceptions and self-assessed competencies, not a quantitative learning measure. Perception-only outcomes fail the outcome criterion (E5). Design also appears to be a single-group feasibility/perception study, which would be E3 if the control-group question were settled; E5 is the first code that clearly applies on the abstract evidence. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence.
criteria_note: Design not_met: no control group described.

quote: Through a literature review approach, this paper analyzes the opportunities and challenges, and proposes pedagogical directions
rationale: The record is a literature review, not an empirical study with a control group and quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). No experimental design or comparison group is described, so it would also fail the design and comparison criteria.

quote: Large language models (LLMs) offer scalable alternatives, but their validity for evaluating multimodal student work is uncertain.
rationale: The LLM (Gemini 2.5 Pro) is used to score student video presentations, not as a learning tool the learners interact with. This is AI used for grading, which the protocol excludes, so E1 applies. There is also no control group of learners without generative AI; the comparison is LLM scoring against expert scoring. Population and domain are not clear from the abstract but are not needed given the first applicable code.

criteria.rationale_note: ChatGPT is used only for grading; learners do not interact with it

quote: This study investigates ChatGPT as an automated grading tool for programming assignments in higher education.
rationale: The generative AI (ChatGPT) is used as an automated grader of assignments, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. Per protocol, AI used only for grading is excluded, and the study compares AI grading against faculty grading rather than a learner control group. The outcome is grading agreement and student perceptions, not a learning outcome. Exclusion code E1 applies first, since the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

quote: Each portfolio was scored by GPT-5, using the same detailed rubric integrated into a structured prompt designed with a prompt engineering framework.
rationale: GPT-5 is used only to score lecturers' student portfolios (automated grading). No learner interacts with the generative AI tool, so the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI (E1). The study also has no control group without generative AI and is a reliability/agreement study rather than a learning-outcome design, and the domain is medical professionalism, which is not STEM. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

criteria.domain_note: Radiology is a health professions field, which the protocol excludes

quote: This white paper explores the impact of LLMs on radiology education, highlighting their potential to enrich curriculum development, teaching and learning, and learner assessment.
rationale: The record is a white paper / task force position paper, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It also has no control-group comparison or quantitative learning outcome, and its radiology focus is a health professions domain. Exclusion code E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol order that the abstract supports.

quote: A questionnaire was distributed to 153 respondents and descriptive statistics was used to analyse the data.
rationale: The study is a descriptive questionnaire survey of perceptions of generative AI among pre-university students. It has no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; it reports only perceptions. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). Criteria note: the design is a survey, which also fails the design criterion, and there is no comparison group (E3 would also apply, but E5 is the first applicable code in the order of the protocol's list is not strictly first; see note: E1 cannot be assessed from the abstract, E2 unclear, E3 applies since there is no control group without generative AI, and E3 precedes E5 in the code order).

criteria.criteria_note: Participants are in-service teachers; no learner interaction or control group; qualitative design

quote: the participant group consisted of six middle school mathematics teachers working at Science and Art Centers in Turkey
rationale: The study is a basic qualitative design examining in-service mathematics teachers' opinions on AI-generated education programs (DIEP). It has no learner-facing AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Participants are in-service teachers, which the protocol excludes. The design is qualitative, so the record fails the empirical-study requirement; E6 is the most applicable code. Although the intervention criterion is not clearly positive for exclusion, the record fails several criteria on positive evidence, so exclusion is justified at the abstract stage.

quote: Results indicated high satisfaction (mean 4.65/5) and strong recognition of Ask ME's ability to provide timely, contextually relevant answers
rationale: Abstract describes a mixed-methods pilot with a single cohort of 120 first-year programming students evaluated through satisfaction ratings, usage logs, and a survey. No control group is mentioned and the only outcomes are satisfaction, perceptions, and usage, which the protocol excludes. Although the intervention (LLM assistant over Canvas) and population (university students, C# programming) appear to fit, the outcome criterion fails on positive evidence. Exclusion code E5 applied (no quantitative learning outcome). Abstract-stage exclusion is supported by the description of satisfaction-only outcomes.

quote: This article presents a systematic literature review with a PRISMA-informed narrative synthesis on the ethical use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI)
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review with narrative synthesis, not an empirical study. It has no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that fits; E1 and E4 are also unclear from the abstract but the review-type design alone is sufficient.

quote: Six groups of three to five students used an online messaging tool with a GPT‐4.0 enabled chatbot for a CPS activity.
rationale: Abstract describes a single set of six groups using a GPT-4 chatbot for a CPS activity, with network analysis of interactions. No control group without generative AI is mentioned, and the design appears observational. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is present, so exclude under E3. Domain, population, and outcome are not stated in the abstract and are not the basis for exclusion.

The study concerns EFL English pragmatics (metapragmatic awareness in English expressions), which is language learning and not STEM content, so E2 applies. The abstract also describes a qualitative-style design (discussion transcripts, interaction logs, reflection journals) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so E3 and E5 would likely apply as well, but E2 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: The current practitioner‐focused study presents two use cases exploring how GenAI tools... can support qualitative data analysis in leadership contexts.
rationale: The study concerns qualitative data analysis in leadership research and education, which is not STEM content (E2). It is also a practitioner-focused use-case report with no control group or quantitative learning outcome described in the abstract. E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order, so it is reported. Abstract gives positive evidence the domain fails.

quote: Using a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design, quantitative data were collected from 451 students across Grades 7 to 12 through online surveys
rationale: The study is a survey and focus-group mixed-methods study of AI tool use and academic integrity perceptions. It has no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparative study meeting the design criteria, so it is excluded. Using E6 (not an empirical study) is the closest code given the survey/qualitative design, though the study is empirical; the failing criteria are design (no comparison), outcome (perceptions only), and domain is not STEM. Under the protocol's ordering, E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract, and E3 (no control group) would be the earliest clear failing code. Recording E3 as the first applicable code given no comparison group is the more accurate choice.

quote: this study aims to demystify the potential generative AI by evaluating the performance of ChatGPT in addressing operations management problems and questions
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT's performance on operations management questions classified by Bloom's taxonomy. It appears to be an evaluation of model output rather than an empirical learner study with a control group. There is no described comparison group without generative AI and no learner outcome. This is not an empirical learning study, so E6 applies. Note that E3 (no control group) would also plausibly fit. Operations management is also arguably not in the protocol's STEM list. Exclusion is based on positive evidence from the abstract that the design lacks a comparison group and learners.

quote: The research was developed under a quantitative approach, with an explanatory level and pre-experimental design.
rationale: The abstract describes a pre-experimental design with a single group of 38 students measured before and after an eight-week Khanmigo intervention, with no separate control group without generative AI. Per the protocol, single-group pre-post designs are excluded (E3). Intervention (Khanmigo, an LLM-based tutor), secondary-school population, mathematics domain, and quantitative outcome appear to be met.

quote: This research is a qualitative descriptive method.
rationale: Exclusion is based on the abstract's own evidence. The study concerns ChatGPT for English writing skill, which is non-STEM (language learning), so E2 applies first in code order. It is also a qualitative descriptive study with perception-only data and no control group (E3/E5 would also apply), but the first applicable code in order is E2. Note: code order lists E1 before E2; E1 is not triggered because ChatGPT is learner-facing generative AI.

quote: Data were collected through surveys from students (n=31) who took a Clinical Reasoning module at a medical school.
rationale: Abstract describes a medical clinical reasoning module (health professions education, which the protocol excludes from the STEM domain) using a survey-based mixed-methods design with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Generative AI appears only as a context for assessment integrity, not as a learner-facing intervention. E2 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly positive from the abstract; the design also lacks a control group (E3) and quantitative outcome (E5), but the domain exclusion is the first failing criterion encountered in the sequence given the record.

quote: This study investigates the influence of perceived usefulness, ease of use, credibility, and social influence on marketing students' attitudes toward using ChatGPT for learning
rationale: The study is a survey (nineteen-item questionnaire) of attitudes among marketing students. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the outcome is attitudes, which are affective and excluded. Marketing is also not a STEM domain. E5 is the first applicable code in the order given, with E2 and E3 also likely to apply. Exclusion is positive evidence from the abstract, so the decision is clear.

criteria.outcome_note: Outcomes are Likert-scale surveys of familiarity, satisfaction, and perceived utility

quote: two Likert-scale surveys were administered to 24 prospective Physics teachers in Ecuador, both before and after an intervention workshop
rationale: Single-group pre-post survey design with no control group (E3 would also apply), but the first applicable code in order is E5: the outcomes are perceptions, satisfaction, familiarity, and self-reported utility rather than a quantitative learning measure. Abstract gives positive evidence that the outcome criterion fails. Also, the design is a single-group pre-post, so no comparison group is evident.
rationale_note: Exclusion code order: E1 (intervention is ChatGPT, learner-facing in workshop, met), E2 (physics, STEM, met), E3 (no control group, would apply), E4 (pre-service teachers, higher education, met), E5 (no learning outcome, applies first among those checked). Per protocol, report first applicable code in order: E3 precedes E5 in the list. Correction below.

quote: This review provides a stakeholder-purpose mapping of AI chatbot applications and evaluations in health care.
rationale: The record is a scoping review (secondary synthesis), not an empirical study with a control group. It also focuses on health purposes, which falls under the health professions domain exclusion. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in order that fits the review design; the health-domain issue would also apply.
rationale_note: Scoping review of health-focused chatbot studies; no STEM learning intervention or comparison group evaluated.

quote: The results showed that ChatGPT had a positive effect on college students' mathematical creativity
rationale: At abstract stage, the record shows a quasi-experiment with an experimental group using ChatGPT on a mathematical creativity task versus a control group that did not, with college students and a quantitative creativity outcome, published 2026 in a journal. No positive evidence of failure on any criterion. Effect-size statistics and full-text language cannot be judged from the abstract, so the record advances to full text.

quote: The experimental group engaged in AI-assisted learning using ChatGPT, while the control group received conventional instruction.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study appears to be a pretest-posttest control-group experiment with secondary students using ChatGPT (generative AI) versus conventional instruction in mathematics, published 2026. Outcome (accuracy, mathematical thinking) appears quantitative and no positive evidence of failure is present. Effect-size data, publication type (journal article per venue name), and full-text language cannot be verified from the abstract, so the record advances to full-text screening rather than being excluded.

quote: The approach used in this study is qualitative with a descriptive method
rationale: Content is Pancasila Education (civics/national ideology), which is not STEM, so E2 applies first in the code order. The study is also qualitative and descriptive with no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported, so E3 and E5 would apply as well. Under the rule that the first applicable code is reported, E2 is given.

Abstract describes a ChatGPT-based knowledge distillation method for programming Q&A with reported loss reductions and answer accuracy. It is a model-engineering paper; the abstract does not show a learner-facing interaction, a control group without generative AI, or a student learning outcome. No positive evidence of a failed criterion is present, so the record is advanced to full text to check whether learners used the tool and whether a comparison group with learning measures exists. Publication venue (Advanced Electromagnetics) is also unusual and should be checked for publication type and eligibility at full text.

quote: This presentation introduces the Prompt to Practice Extended Reality Learning Design Framework, a pedagogy led model for using generative artificial intelligence and vibe coding to design immersive simulation scenarios.
rationale: The record is a conference-style presentation introducing a conceptual design framework. It describes educators using generative AI to design scenarios, not learners interacting with generative AI, and reports no comparison group or quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Although E1 (intervention not learner-facing) could also apply, E6 is the clearest failure supported by the abstract.

quote: Data were collected through post-activity surveys and open-ended questions and then manually analyzed to generate themes.
rationale: Descriptive qualitative study of participant perceptions with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Design is qualitative, not an experiment or quasi-experiment, and the domain is health professions education (assessment design), which is outside STEM. Exclusion code E5 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that clearly fails on the abstract's evidence; E6 (not an empirical study) would also be defensible since the study is empirical but qualitative. Because the abstract shows only perceptions and no comparison, the record is excluded at abstract stage.

quote: Using Zhaopin.com as the data source and employing a key attribute extraction method based on ChatGLM3 along with prompting engineering techniques
rationale: The study uses an LLM (ChatGLM3) to extract attributes from job postings for analysis; learners do not interact with the generative AI tool, so it is not learner-facing (E1 would apply first by strict order). No control group, no learning outcome, and the design is a descriptive text analysis. Per the ordering rule, E1 is the first code that applies, since the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

quote: Anatomy in the Age of AI: A Mixed-Methods Study of Student Engagement and Usability of a Course-Specific Chatbot
rationale: Title indicates a course-specific chatbot in anatomy, which is a health professions/medical education subject. Protocol excludes health professions education, so the content is not STEM as defined. The title also points to a mixed-methods study focused on engagement and usability, suggesting perception outcomes rather than a quantitative learning measure, but this is not needed for the decision. No abstract was available. Exclusion is on the first applicable code, E2.

Abstract describes computer science higher education students using generative AI tools (ChatGPT, Copilot) and an NLP/ML analysis of student engagement and predicted outcomes. It does not indicate a separate control group without generative AI, an experimental or quasi-experimental design, or a quantitative learning outcome with effect-size data. Positive evidence of failure is not clear from the abstract, so the record advances to full text to check design, comparison, and outcomes.

criteria.outcome_note: algorithmic thinking and self-efficacy; self-efficacy is affective and should not be extracted, but algorithmic thinking is a learning outcome

quote: The results indicate that AI assistants, equipped with functions such as timely feedback, personalized support, emotional companionship, and cognitive scaffolding, exert a significantly positive effect on students’ algorithmic thinking and self-efficacy.
rationale: At the abstract stage, the intervention is an LLM-driven AI programming assistant used by university students in a programming/algorithm course, and algorithmic thinking is a quantitative-sounding learning outcome. The abstract does not state whether a control group without generative AI existed or the study design (randomized or quasi-experimental), so E3 and design cannot be confirmed as failing. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record advances to full text to check the comparison group, design, and effect size data.

quote: Adopting a mixed-methods design with a one-group pretest-posttest experimental approach, the study analyzed data from 34 Grade 8 students
rationale: The study uses a one-group pretest-posttest design with no separate control group that does not use generative AI. Comparisons are among instructional strategies (PBL, Think-Pair-Share, Jigsaw) all with AI, and pre-post within one group is explicitly E3. Abstract gives positive evidence of failure on the comparison criterion.

quote: This small-scale exploratory survey study examines familiarity with, frequency and purposes of use of, attitudes toward, verification practices, and language choices in GenAI among 30 second-year undergraduate students
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive survey study of 30 students with no control group and no experimental comparison, so the comparison and design criteria fail. No quantitative learning outcome is reported; the measures are usage, perceptions, and language choices. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that is clearly supported, but the more precise fit is the design failure (survey, no comparison). Strictly, code E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) and E6 (not an empirical study? no, it is empirical) are also relevant; under the order given, E3 is reported as the first clear failure of the comparison criterion.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on clear positive evidence of a survey design without a comparison group.

quote: Findings reveal that LLMs enhanced conceptual understanding, clarified methodologies, and assisted with command syntax, while CAS ensured computational accuracy and result validation.
rationale:
Abstract describes an LLM plus CAS mathematics lab for civil engineering students (STEM, higher education, learner-facing generative AI). However, it describes a case study with quantitative and qualitative methods and does not state a control group or comparison condition. Familiarity with AI tools and perceived usefulness suggest perception outcomes; it is unclear whether a quantitative learning outcome with a comparison group exists. Not excluded at abstract stage; full text needed to check design, comparison, and learning outcome.</rationale>

quote: This study, conducted with 112 Saudi engineering EFL learners, used an eight-week quasi-experimental design to examine the impact of AI-mediated speaking practice on anxiety and performance.
rationale: The study concerns English as a foreign language speaking practice, which is language learning and not STEM content, even though the learners are engineering students. The domain criterion fails on positive evidence, so the record is excluded under E2. The AI tool is described only as AI-mediated speaking tools, without confirming it is generative, but the domain failure alone is sufficient.

quote: a quasi-experiment was conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method in a 10th grade computer programming course in a high school
rationale: Generative AI (dialogue-based, prompt-designed agents) is used by students in a high school programming course. The control group uses traditional computer-supported collaborative programming, a non-generative comparison. The design is a quasi-experiment. Outcomes include computational thinking and learning achievement, which are quantitative. Programming is STEM, and high school students meet the population criterion. Journal article, 2025. No criterion appears to fail at abstract stage; the SMD computability is unverified but not evidence of exclusion.

quote: We fine-tuned VisualGLM-6B on 2,380 annotated images from 30 classroom videos, covering five interaction types
rationale: The multimodal LLM is used to classify teacher-student interactions in classroom videos (an observation/analysis tool), not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. There is no control group and no learning outcome; the reported accuracy is model classification performance. Excluded under E1 as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. Decision is clear from the abstract alone, so the abstract-stage rule of excluding only on positive evidence is satisfied by the absence of any learner interaction and of a comparison group.

quote: This research study explored the perspectives of 20 educational technologists from four Saudi Arabian universities
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of educational technologists (not students), using thematic analysis. It has no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical quantitative study meeting the protocol, so it fails on design and outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is used as the primary code, reflecting a qualitative perspectives study; the population is also not students, though E4 would be a secondary issue. Per the protocol's first-applicable ordering, E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract, so E6 is the first clearly applicable code given the qualitative design.

criteria.criteria_note: No control group described; outcomes are reflections, thematic analysis and self-assessment survey

quote: Reflection journals and final lesson plans were analyzed thematically, while 20 participants completed a self-assessment survey on lesson design competency.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group study of pre-service mathematics teachers with qualitative reflection analysis and a self-assessment survey. There is no comparison group without generative AI, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. Exclusion is on E3 as the first applicable code in the ordering that fits the design (no control group); E5 would also apply since outcomes are perceptions. Positive evidence of missing comparison group is present in the abstract.

quote: A quantitative pre-experimental design was employed involving 33 students.
