quote: "In this article, the way students learn and the meta-learning skills and techniques needed for them to become independent lifelong learners in 2025 are being studied."
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/discussion article on meta-learning techniques, with a mathematics application (first-degree linear equations) presented only as an illustration. It gives no indication of a controlled comparison, a generative AI intervention, or a quantitative learning outcome. The abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical focus (conceptual article), so E6 applies. Note: the ordering rule would place E1 first if generative AI use were ruled out, but the abstract does not show learners using a generative AI tool; the main evident failure is that the paper is not an empirical study.

quote: Using Policy Discourse Analysis (PDA), official GenAI-related policy documents from eight universities in New Zealand were thematically analysed
rationale: The study is a document analysis of institutional GenAI policies, not an empirical study of learners interacting with generative AI. It has no comparison group, no learner-facing intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's coding order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing GenAI) would technically apply first, but the primary failure is that it is not an empirical intervention/comparison study; E6 is the best fit for a policy review. Note that the first-applicable-code order would normally place E1 first; the researcher should check this coding choice.

quote: A Pilot Survey Exploring Student AI Experience and Views on Integrating GenAI in College Health and Nutrition Classrooms
rationale: Title describes a pilot survey of student experience and views, which is a survey (non-empirical-experimental) design with perception outcomes only. No comparison group or quantitative learning outcome is indicated. Health and nutrition content is also outside the STEM domain as defined (health professions education is excluded). Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of a survey design; E6 applied as the first applicable code in order where possible.

quote: We employed six prompt engineering strategies to automatically score student responses.
rationale: The LLMs (GPT-3.5, GPT-4) are used by researchers to automatically score student-written responses, not as a learner-facing tool that students interact with during a learning activity. This is automatic scoring, which the protocol excludes under E1. No control group without generative AI is described, and the abstract reports only scoring accuracy against human ratings, not a learner outcome. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: we used thematic analysis to analyse the responses
rationale: The study is a qualitative thematic analysis of educators' opinions from interviews. It is not an empirical intervention study with a control group or a quantitative learning outcome. Excluded as not an empirical study of the eligible type (E6). The quote is paraphrased in the abstract as "we use thematic analysis to analyse the responses"; the abstract wording is "In this paper we use thematic analysis to analyse the responses."

quote: Post-intervention, the posttest findings were statistically evaluated and indicated a significant improvement in the IG
rationale: Abstract describes a pretest-posttest control group design with Gemini 2.5 Flash role-play practice vs conventional practice, with a quantitative posttest outcome (t-statistic reported). Population is first-year engineering students (higher education), which fits. Domain is English-speaking skills, which is language learning and not STEM, so it would fall under E2 (content is not STEM). Language learning in an engineering context is not clearly STEM content under the protocol's exclusion of language learning, so the domain criterion is ambiguous at abstract stage. Per the abstract-stage rule, the record is advanced for full-text review of the domain question. Also the abstract reports a t-statistic but not means/SDs, so data sufficiency needs full-text checking.

quote: The study conducts and compares three statistical analyses viz. regression analysis, classification analysis and linear programming problem using GenAI tools (ChatGPT 4 and Google Bard) and traditional software (Python and Excel).
rationale: The abstract describes comparison of generative AI tools (ChatGPT 4, Bard) against traditional software (Python, Excel) on analysis tasks. It does not describe a learner-facing study with a control group of learners without generative AI, nor a quantitative learning outcome; the comparison appears to be of tool outputs rather than learners. Positive evidence of no separate control group of learners supports E3 at abstract stage, though this is somewhat tentative; full text could clarify design. Population is not clearly students.

quote: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with ten active university mathematics professors
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of ten university mathematics professors about their perceptions and use of GenAI. It is not an empirical comparative study with a control group, has no learner participants, and reports no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's intended sense: qualitative/perception design). The first applicable code in order would be E1 or E4 depending on reading; E6 best captures the qualitative design, but the failure is clear at abstract stage on design, population, and outcome.

Abstract describes an exploratory qualitative study of reflective essays from 131 students with no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome. The design is qualitative, which also fails the Design criterion. Exclusion is based on the first failing criterion in code order; E3 (no control group) applies first, with E5 and E6 also evident. Abstract gives positive evidence of a non-comparative qualitative design, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: In this article, we discuss these technological developments and present our perspectives on their integration into contemporary statistics education.
rationale: The record is a perspective/commentary article ("present our perspectives") with no empirical study, no comparison group, and no learning outcome measured. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. The domain is statistics, but the design criterion fails outright.

The abstract describes a single-group pre-post design: participants were evaluated "before and after completing the program" with paired t-tests and no control group. Per the protocol, single-group pre-post designs are excluded (E3, no control group without generative AI). The abstract gives positive evidence of this failure, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified. Quote given is the design description from the abstract (Abstract). Note the quote field is set to null for the verbatim field requirement only because the decision rests on the pre-post description; the phrase "evaluated on their AI utilization skills and critical thinking abilities before and after completing the program" supports it.

The record has only a title, venue, and year, with no abstract. The title describes a semester-long experiment on knowledge acquisition in a science classroom with "hybrid intelligence", which may or may not involve a generative AI tool. Nothing in the record gives positive evidence that a criterion fails, so under the abstract-stage rule it cannot be excluded. Population, comparison group, outcome, and whether the AI is generative all need checking at full text. Year 2025 meets the date criterion.

Abstract stage, but the record gives positive evidence of exclusion. The study concerns ESL writing skills, which is language learning and not STEM (E2). It is also a perception-based survey (TAM questionnaire) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so E3 and E5 would also apply. Under the code order, E2 is the first that applies. Quote is null because the exclusion rests on the overall topic rather than a single sentence.

quote: our objective was to create an adept classification system for textual data related to crisis events sourced from the web
rationale: This is a student software project building a BERT-based crisis-event text classifier. It is not an empirical study with a learner-facing generative AI intervention, a control group, or a learning outcome measured against a comparison. The abstract reports no experimental design, comparison group, or quantitative learning outcome. It is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first code that applies on the evidence given. The abstract gives positive evidence of a project description rather than an experiment, so exclusion is justified at abstract stage.

quote: The study employed a cross-sectional descriptive research design in which data were collected using a questionnaire instrument in the summer semester of the 2023/2024 academic year.
rationale: Cross-sectional questionnaire study of faculty perceptions. It is not an experiment, has no control group, and measures perceptions and awareness rather than a learning outcome. Participants are faculty, not students, and the content is not STEM-specific. Excluded at abstract stage on E6 (not an empirical study eligible under the design criterion; a survey design is excluded by the protocol). The first applicable code in order is E1 only if the intervention is judged non-learner-facing; the abstract shows faculty survey of perceptions, so E6 is the best fit for the design failure.

quote: The study employed an explanatory sequential design and involved 80 first-year middle school students aged 12–13.
rationale: GenAI used by students in ecology-related SSI debate classes (learner-facing), middle school population, science/AI literacy and scientific knowledge outcomes measured, published 2025. The abstract does not state whether a control group without GenAI exists (explanatory sequential design with no comparison described), so comparison and design are unclear. Not excluded at abstract stage; resolve at full text.

criteria.quote_note: LLMs benchmarked on exam items; no learner interacts with the tool

quote: Four LLMs-OpenAI o3, o4-mini, o4-mini-high (OpenAI), and Gemini 2.5 Flash (Google)-were evaluated on all 200 items of the 77th Japanese National Examination
rationale: The study benchmarks LLMs on licensure exam items and uses o3 to generate exam items rated by subject-matter experts. No learners interact with generative AI as part of a learning activity, and there is no learner control group or learning outcome. The intervention is not learner-facing generative AI (E1). Domain is radiological technology, which is health professions, so this would also be a concern. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

Experimental animation pedagogy is an arts/design context, not STEM content, so E2 applies first in the code order. The study is also a design-based research study using process logs, portfolios, reflections and questionnaires, with no described control group and no quantitative learning outcome; it is not a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison. Exclusion on E2 is given as the first applicable code. The abstract shows positive evidence of non-STEM content, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: ChatGPT-4o demonstrated an accuracy rate of 51.76% on major unit assessment problems from 10 versions of the 7th-grade 'Mathematics 1' textbook
rationale: The abstract describes ChatGPT-4o's accuracy on textbook problems and error-type analysis of the model's own outputs. There is no control group of learners without generative AI, and no comparison group design is described. This is positive evidence of a missing comparison, so exclude under E3.

quote: Overall, instructors must pay attention to student motivation and work to create learning environments that foster motivation, autonomy, and engagement to implement adaptive instruction successfully.
rationale: The abstract reads as a narrative or conceptual overview of adaptive instruction. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no learning outcome. It describes adaptive tools generically (ITS, LMS, apps, AI chatbots) without identifying a generative AI intervention or a STEM domain. Positive evidence that the record is not an empirical study supports E6, which applies before the other codes.

quote: Drawing on a five-month randomized controlled trial involving 770 high school students across ten schools in Taipei
rationale: Abstract describes a randomized controlled trial with 770 high school students (design, population and final exam outcome appear met). Intervention involves LLM-guided reinforcement learning and student-chatbot interactions, so generative component is plausible, but the abstract does not clearly establish that learners interact with a generative tool versus a non-generative adaptive system, and the control (fixed sequencing) may be an AI/adaptive condition rather than a no-generative-AI group. The subject domain (coding exercises suggested by code-editing patterns) is not explicitly stated as STEM in the abstract. Venue is listed as 'Human capital leadership' and the record lacks clear journal-article status. Not excluded at abstract stage; advance to full text to resolve intervention, comparison, domain, and publication type.

quote: A cluster-randomized controlled study was conducted with 195 ninth-grade students from German secondary schools
rationale: At abstract stage all criteria appear met: ADA is a domain-specific AI chatbot (generative AI per the abstract's framing), compared against conventional differentiation materials (non-AI control), cluster-randomized design, ninth-grade students, mathematics (square roots), and a pre-post assessment of learning outcomes. Abstract does not give positive evidence of failure; whether the cognitive outcome has sufficient statistics for SMD is to be checked at full text. Generative nature of ADA should be confirmed at full text.

quote: This study aimed to examine the effect of ChatGPT, an AI-powered chatbot, as a learning aid in encouraging English language learning autonomy among Indonesian students
rationale: Content is English language learning, which is non-STEM, so E2 applies as the first failing code in order. Design is questionnaire and interview based, with no described control group, and the outcome is perceived autonomy rather than a quantitative learning measure, so E3 and E5 would also likely fail.

quote: Feedback from students and staff indicated that this authentic pedagogical approach significantly enhanced students' confidence in conducting experiments and soft skills
rationale: Abstract describes a course intervention with ChatGPT-type chatbot in undergraduate chemistry lab, but evaluation is by surveys and focus groups only (perceptions/confidence), with no quantitative learning outcome and no described control group. Positive evidence of failing the outcome criterion (perceptions only) supports exclusion at abstract stage. Design also appears non-comparative. Coded E5 as the first applicable code in order after E1-E4 (intervention and domain and population appear met).

criteria.rationale_note: Abstract describes students' perceptions via open-ended survey responses

quote: Sixty-eight second-year engineering students participated in the study, providing qualitative insights through open-ended survey responses.
rationale: The study is a qualitative investigation of student experiences using open-ended survey responses. It reports perceptions only, with no quantitative learning outcome and no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group with statistics. Excluded at the abstract stage on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), since the abstract gives positive evidence that the outcome is perception-based. The design is qualitative, which also fails the Design criterion.

Math domain and a learning outcome (mastery, error rates) are indicated. GPT-4 rewrites problems that students then work on in MATHia, an ITS, so the learner-facing generative element is plausible but the abstract does not say whether learners interact with a generative tool directly, as opposed to receiving teacher-prepared or pre-revised content. The comparison is revised versus original problems, which may be a valid control, but the design (randomized or not) and whether effect sizes can be computed are not stated. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not grounds for exclusion, so this goes forward for full-text review of intervention, design, and data.

quote: This narrative reflects on the integration of Generative AI into undergraduate Information Technology courses at the University of Cincinnati Clermont College.
rationale: The record is a reflective instructor narrative, not an empirical study. It reports no control group, no design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies as the first failing criterion in code order. Quote is from the abstract's first sentence.

criteria.quote_note: generative AI used by teacher to develop materials; student feedback only

quote: A generative AI system was used as a rapid prototyping partner to create and iteratively refine interactive simulations, digital measurement tools, and supporting laboratory worksheets
rationale: Generative AI was used by the teacher/researchers to develop virtual lab materials, not as a learner-facing tool (E1, per borderline rule "AI used only by the teacher or researcher"). The design is a classroom case study with exploratory student feedback on engagement and usability, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: This paper delivers a domain‐specific analysis of LLM adoption in EE/CE education.
rationale: The abstract describes a review/analysis paper ("comprehensive reference and strategic roadmap", "current research gaps", "propose best-practice implementation models") with no empirical comparison group or quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Engineering content is STEM, so the domain criterion is met. Note the protocol says to exclude only on positive evidence; here the abstract clearly indicates a review rather than an experiment.

quote: This conceptual paper advances Linguistically Responsive Generative AI (LR-GAI) as a theoretical construct and develops a theory of how linguistic responsiveness can shape the educational value of GenAI in multilingual contexts.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/theoretical paper with no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. The STEM domain is also not indicated. E6 is the first applicable code in the order of the protocol's checks that does not depend on unavailable detail.

quote: Our contributions are two-fold: 1) Insights from a systematic scoping review of studies examining the use of GenAI to support the teaching of CT skills
rationale: The record is a systematic scoping review, which is a review article rather than an empirical study. Protocol excludes reviews, so it fails on E6 (not an empirical study). Its design is not an experiment, and it does not report its own primary data.

quote: For this study, a literature review was conducted to identify, evaluate, and interpret available research.
rationale: The record is a literature review of photovoice-based entrepreneurial-minded interventions in engineering classrooms, not an empirical study. Under the protocol's order of codes, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) comes first and arguably applies, since generative AI appears only as background on hiring and no learner-facing AI tool is studied. Here I apply E1 first as the protocol requires; E6 is the secondary reason.

quote: we analyzed 288 prompt texts to identify key topics that reflect students' information interaction behaviors
rationale: Abstract describes analysis of students' prompt texts from an LLM-assisted academic writing task, comparing students by performance level. No control group without generative AI is described, and the design is not a comparison of an intervention versus control. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group supports E3. Domain is engineering education writing, which is borderline for STEM. Abstract-stage exclusion on E3 is based on the absence of any non-AI comparison described; the study appears observational/topic-modeling rather than a controlled comparison.

quote: Teaching biology through AI: Chatbots and gamification in higher education
rationale: The study teaches biochemistry (allosteric regulation, oxidative phosphorylation), which is life science and not one of the protocol's STEM domains (science is listed, but the protocol's science intent is ambiguous for biochemistry). Judging the abstract, the content is biology/biochemistry; the protocol lists "science" as included, so this is borderline. The abstract also does not clearly show a generative AI chatbot (only "AI chatbot"), and the design is an experiment with a traditional-instruction control, which fits. Given the abstract gives positive evidence of non-STEM-domain content only under a narrow reading, I exclude under E2 with low confidence; a full-text check on whether the chatbot is generative and whether the content is treated as science would be warranted.

quote: Student-generated questions related to a laboratory exercise on enzyme activity were separately provided to ChatGPT and a cohort of graduate teaching assistants (TAs).
rationale: Study compares ChatGPT and human TA responses to student questions in an undergraduate biology lab. Biology is not in the protocol's STEM domain list (science is listed, but the protocol's domain row names science, math, statistics, engineering, CS, programming, data science; biology lab on enzyme activity is a life science and is treated here as science, so E2 is arguable). The more serious issue: the design compares ChatGPT responses to human TA responses rated by evaluators and students, with no learner-level quantitative learning outcome reported; the measures are response accuracy, teaching effectiveness, and preference, which are not learning outcomes. Coding E2 as the first applicable code is uncertain; E5 may be the more accurate code. Flagging for audit.

quote: Using a quantitative survey method, data were collected from 225 respondents through a snowball sampling technique and analyzed using the Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) approach.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey analyzed with SEM-PLS on ChatGPT dependence and inert thinking. It has no experimental or quasi-experimental control group and no learning outcome measured after an intervention, so it fails the design and comparison criteria. The protocol's design exclusion for survey/correlational designs applies, and the abstract gives clear evidence that this is not an empirical trial. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is applied as the closest first-applicable code, since the study is an empirical survey but does not meet the design requirement. Under the ordered code list, E1 through E5 are not clearly established from the abstract, so E6 is the first clear failure.
decision_note: Survey-based correlational design; no control group.

quote: Using a qualitative exploratory approach, 20 Systems Engineering students applied the methodology to collaboratively create a four-week Massive Open Online Course
rationale: The study is a qualitative exploratory design with no separate control group and no quantitative learning outcome; data are interviews, observation, and artifacts. The abstract gives positive evidence that the comparison and design criteria fail, so it is excluded. E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol order that fits (no control group without generative AI). Note that E5 (no quantitative outcome) and E6-type qualitative design also apply; E3 is reported as the first code relevant to the comparison failure per the stated design.

quote: two parallel groups: a control group using traditional peer instruction strategies, and an experimental group using AI-guided activities through a web-based platform supported by ChatGPT
rationale: At abstract stage all criteria appear met: ChatGPT-supported activities for first-year physics students (higher education, Newtonian mechanics, STEM) versus a control group with traditional peer instruction; quasi-experimental with a pre-/post-test measuring conceptual knowledge; published 2025. Full-text checks (e.g., journal article status, statistics for SMD) remain for the fulltext stage.

quote: The participants consisted of 35 Computer Education students, divided into a Text-to-Code group (n = 18) and a Code-to-Code group (n = 17).
rationale: Abstract reports a ChatGPT-based programming study with pretest-posttest two-group design, STEM (programming) content, higher-education students, and a quantitative skill test. However, the comparison is between two prompting techniques (Text-to-Code vs Code-to-Code), both using ChatGPT, with no evident non-generative-AI control group. That would meet E3 if confirmed, but the abstract does not clearly state whether a control without generative AI exists, so the decision is deferred to full text. Journal publication type and 2026 date are consistent with eligibility.

quote: This study investigates English as a Foreign Language (EFL) university students’ perceptions of using ChatGPT in the revising and editing stages of academic writing.
rationale: Content is EFL academic writing, not STEM, so E2 applies and is the first failing code in order. The study is also a descriptive perception survey with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (only Likert perceptions), so E3, E5 and design failures would apply as well, but E2 is reported as the first in order.

quote: This study investigates the attitudes and experiences of Bachelor of Science in Information Technology (BSIT) students about the use of ChatGPT
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive qualitative study using structured questionnaires of 30 students, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (only perceptions and experiences). Positive evidence of failing comparison (no control), design (descriptive qualitative, not an experiment), and outcome (perceptions only) criteria. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI); E5 would also apply. Excluding under E3 as the first code that applies on the protocol order.

quote: Participants produce artifacts such as syllabus statements and GenAI interaction transcripts.
rationale: The population is faculty/educators in higher education, which is in-service teachers and workplace-style professional development, not K-12 or higher education students. The design is a case study with a single-group pretest-posttest survey, with no control group (E3 also applies), and the outcomes are self-reported GenAI use and self-efficacy, not a quantitative learning measure. Under the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E4 is the first code that applies, so it is reported. Not STEM content either, but E4 takes precedence in the order given.

quote: This cross-sectional study investigates the usage patterns and ethical perceptions of ChatGPT among 381 students
rationale: Abstract describes a cross-sectional anonymous survey of usage and perceptions only. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design with a comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are usage prevalence and perceptions. Not an empirical intervention study with eligible design, so excluded under E6 (not an empirical study eligible under the design criteria). Note the protocol's E6 is "Not an empirical study"; this is a survey, which the design criteria exclude. Also no comparison group and no learning outcome, but the first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI) would precede; however the survey has no control group, so E3 applies in order before E5 and E6. Correct code is E3.

quote: This study is descriptive-qualitative research.
rationale: The study is descriptive-qualitative with interviews and questionnaires and no control group without generative AI, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. It also reports only perceptions and self-reported quality, with no quantitative learning measure. Excluded under E3 as the first applicable code in order. Domain is also unclear (economics education research proposal), but this does not need to be resolved for the decision.
decision_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on positive evidence of a non-experimental design with no comparison group.

quote: This study investigates the impact of generative AI (GenAI) on higher engineering education through informed educational fiction.
rationale: The study is a fiction-based, scenario-generating study built on educators' predictions analyzed through CHAT. It has no comparison group, no learner-facing intervention evaluation, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical trial of learning, so it fails the design and outcome requirements. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the closest fit among the codes, since the work is a speculative scenario study rather than an empirical evaluation. Some ambiguity remains about whether it counts as empirical, but it clearly lacks any control group and quantitative learning measure, so exclusion is warranted.

quote: Through qualitative methods, such as interviews and focus groups with university students and teachers, this study examines perceptions of AI's role
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative study (interviews and focus groups) examining perceptions, with no controlled comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. This is positive evidence of non-empirical-experimental design failing the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is used as the first applicable code under the protocol's ordering; the study is a qualitative case study, which the design criterion excludes. Under the protocol's code list, E6 fits best for a qualitative perception study without a quantitative outcome.
decision_note: Qualitative case study; no comparison group or quantitative outcome.

quote: A one group pretest–posttest quasi-experimental design was utilized to answer research questions.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pretest-posttest design in which the same students sit an exam without AI and then with AI. There is no separate control group without generative AI, so E3 applies. This is positive evidence of failure, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified. The intervention (GPT-based LLM assistant) and programming domain otherwise appear to fit.

quote: "a quantitative analysis of instructional alignment is conducted for these two KGs"
rationale: The LLM-based agent is used to evaluate teachers' instruction (knowledge graphs from teaching documents and teacher audio transcripts), not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. Learners do not interact with the generative AI, so E1 applies. The abstract also reports no learner-level quantitative learning outcome or control group, which is consistent with exclusion.

This is a position/commentary piece. It discusses AI tutors and humiliation in medical education and cites another AI tutoring study only secondhand, without reporting its own empirical data, a comparison group, or a quantitative learning outcome. Not an empirical study (E6). Medical education is also a health-professions context, which would raise a further domain concern (E2), but E6 is the first applicable code in order.

Abstract describes a customized AI learning system using KNN prediction, adaptive learning, and facial recognition for attendance. The only generative element is an AI chatbot mentioned in passing, and the abstract gives no evidence of a learner-facing generative AI intervention as the core tool. Predictive analytics and adaptive systems without a generative model are excluded by the protocol. No controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome is reported in the abstract, and the STEM domain is not stated. Exclusion is on E1 as the first applicable code, based on positive evidence that the intervention is not generative AI.

quote: Thirty-four primary mathematics teachers participated in a quasi-experimental study.
rationale: Participants are in-service primary mathematics teachers using an LLM tool to design lessons, not K-12 or higher education students. The protocol excludes in-service teachers, so E4 applies. The outcome is lesson plan quality, which is not clearly a learner's quantitative learning outcome, and the comparison is against generic LLMs rather than a non-generative-AI control, so these are also doubtful. E4 is reported as the first applicable code.

quote: The paper reviews published literature across three disciplines: art, English composition and writing, and mathematics.
rationale: The paper is a literature review/overview rather than an empirical study. It reports no experiment, control group, or quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in the order, since the abstract gives positive evidence of a review design.

quote: Methods A cross-sectional study was carried out using a questionnaire with five main domains to explore Jordanian medical students' perceptions, practices, and concerns regarding the ChatGPT.
rationale: Cross-sectional survey study of perceptions with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Design is survey (not an eligible experimental or quasi-experimental design), and outcomes are perceptions and usage only. Also medical education, which is not STEM content under the protocol's domain criterion. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of a survey design measuring only perceptions. E5 is the first code that clearly applies in the protocol's order, since no learning outcome is measured.

quote: This research investigates the comparative effectiveness of the ChatGPT and the Google search engine in facilitating the self-learning of JavaScript functions among undergraduate open and distance learning students.
rationale: Abstract describes a quasi-experimental post-test control group design comparing ChatGPT (generative AI, learner-facing) against Google search (non-generative comparator) for JavaScript learning in undergraduate ODL students (higher education, programming domain). Test scores are a quantitative learning outcome, published 2024. Abstract gives no positive evidence of a failed criterion; SMD computability and full-text language/publication type are to be checked at full text.

Abstract describes a cross-sectional survey of prevalence and factors associated with ChatGPT use among health students. There is no control group without generative AI and no experimental comparison; the outcome is self-reported use and TAM attitude scores, not a learning outcome. Design is correlational/survey. Exclusion code E3 (no control group) is the first applicable code in order that is positively evidenced; the design also fails the E6/E5 criteria, but E3 is reported as the first applicable code per the protocol ordering. Given the abstract gives clear positive evidence of a non-experimental design, exclusion is appropriate.

Abstract describes Indonesian language education students writing scientific papers; content is language/writing, not STEM, so E2 applies. Also the study is described as a quantitative questionnaire of 37 students with no clear learning-outcome measure or control group, suggesting further failures (E3/E5), but the first applicable code in order is E2 only if the first-ordered codes E1 do not apply; E1 is unclear because RAG/NotebookLM is generative but the abstract does not clearly describe learner interaction. Exclusion on E2 is positive evidence from the abstract's subject matter.

quote: The LLM-generated responses were compared with students' original responses.
rationale: The abstract describes comparing LLM-generated responses with students' original responses, with no separate control group that lacks generative AI. Findings are illustrated with two discourse threads and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. The design is not a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison, so the study fails the comparison and design criteria. E3 is the first applicable code in order; E5 and E6 may also apply, as the study appears to be a descriptive illustration rather than an experiment.

quote: The research is based on a qualitative content analysis of AIDT interfaces, official manuals, platform guidelines, and related policy documents mostly published between 2023 and 2025.
rationale: The study is a qualitative content analysis of AI digital textbook interfaces and policy documents. It is not an empirical comparative study: there is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study in the protocol's sense, so E6 applies. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract. Other codes (E1 intervention, E3 comparison, E5 outcome) would also be unmet, but E6 is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's list of codes.
rationale_note: Ordering note: E1 is checked first. The abstract does not clearly show whether the AIDT includes a generative model, so E1 is not assigned; E6 is assigned as the first clearly applicable code.

quote: This paper systematically analyzes the application scenarios of generative AI in the teaching of Electrotechnics and Electronics, explores the pedagogical transformations and potential risks it brings, and proposes corresponding strategies
rationale: The abstract describes a systematic analysis and strategy proposal, not an empirical study with a control group or learning outcome. No comparison group, design, or quantitative outcome is reported, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion is based on positive evidence of non-empirical design.

quote: A cross- sectional quantitative research design was employed, using web based survey distributed to university students across Pakistan.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional web survey using SEM on perceptions (anxiety, usefulness, normative influence). There is no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions only. Excluded at the first applicable code. E1 would be arguable, but E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible design) is the cleanest reading given the survey design. Note: the design is a non-experimental survey, which the protocol excludes under Design; the closest single code applied here is E6. Stated uncertainty: E3 (no control group) also applies in substance.

quote: This study examines the classroom affordances and limitations of two prominent LLMs—ChatGPT and DeepSeek—through a comparative analysis of their dialogic, representational, and reasoning capacities.
rationale: The abstract describes a comparative conceptual/analytical article on LLM affordances and limitations, with no experimental design, control group, or learning outcome measure. This positively indicates a non-empirical study (E6), so it is excluded at the abstract stage. Physics content and LLM intervention would otherwise fit.

quote: The intervention utilized worksheets generated by the ChatGPT 3.5 application, which were customized based on the current curriculum
rationale: Case study with two students in a single intervention and no described control group. The abstract describes a single-group case study design with qualitative data (interviews, tasks, e-questionnaires), so no comparison group without generative AI is evident. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI); the design also fails the experimental/quasi-experimental requirement.

quote: Data were analyzed through overall level distribution tables at the planned and actual stages, case analyses for each level, and a transitional (alluvial) analysis.
rationale: The abstract describes a single group of 62 pre-service teachers compared across planned versus actual responses (within-subject pre/post-style design). There is no separate control group without generative AI, so E3 applies. The design appears to be single-group, which fails the comparison and design criteria on positive evidence. Intervention (chatbot simulation) and population (pre-service teachers, higher education, mathematics) appear to meet criteria.

quote: Faculty implemented the plan-do study-act cycle to pilot the Transparency in Learning and Teaching (TILT) project framework and to explore the use of artificial intelligence (AI)
rationale: The abstract describes a case study with a PDSA cycle and no comparison group, no described quantitative learning outcome, and reports on pros and cons and self-efficacy perceptions. Positive evidence fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. The case study design is not an eligible empirical comparison design, so E6 applies as the first failing code.

quote: The theoretical analysis of artificial intelligence (AI) based on available data explores the relationships within the phenomenon under study.
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical/descriptive-analytical review of ChatGPT in education rather than an empirical study. There is no described experimental or comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. STEM domain and population are not specified in the abstract.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage decision; exclusion is based on positive evidence of a non-empirical, theoretical design.

quote: we demonstrate that PRAG‐EDU achieves a 23.7% improvement in BERTScore F1 (0.555 vs. 0.451) and 18.3% higher ROUGE‐L over non‐personalized baselines.
rationale: The study compares LLM/RAG configurations evaluated on automatic text metrics (BERTScore, ROUGE-L) and expert star ratings of responses, not a learner-level quantitative learning outcome collected after a learning intervention. No human learner control group without generative AI is described. The design appears to be a technical benchmark evaluation rather than a randomized or quasi-experiment with learners. Exclusion is on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), with the design concern also noted as a likely issue on full-text review.

quote: This paper examines the real-world challenges confronting student advisors in the GenAI era. It argues for a necessary role shift from "tool users" to "ecosystem builders"
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/position paper on counselor roles and competency frameworks at Chizhou University. It reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. The intervention, domain and population are not clearly specified, but E6 alone is sufficient to exclude.

quote: A survey of 850 students with GenAI experience from 14 Chinese universities was analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM).
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey analyzed with SEM and multi-group analysis, with no randomized or quasi-experimental comparison group receiving a non-generative-AI condition. Outcomes are self-perceived sense of gain rather than a quantitative learning measure. Design fails and outcome fails. The protocol's code order places E1 first, but the abstract does not clearly show the AI is learner-facing rather than not, so E1 is not assigned. E3 (no control group) applies since there is no experimental comparison, but the stronger, clearer failure is E5 for perception-based outcomes. Note: exclusion is on the abstract's positive evidence of a survey design and self-reported gain outcomes.

quote: Designed to efficiently handle questions about admissions, academic programs, faculty details, campus facilities, examination schedules, and general policies, the chatbot delivers quick and precise responses.
rationale: The record describes development and deployment of a Dialogflow chatbot for college information queries. The abstract reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; it describes a system build with no learning measurement. Exclusion under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) applies. The abstract also gives no STEM content, so E2 might apply as well, but E5 is the clearest failure and is listed first in the code order that is most directly supported by the abstract.

quote: This study used a one-group pretest–posttest design.
rationale: The study uses a one-group pretest-posttest design with no separate control group that avoids generative AI, which fails the comparison criterion and is coded E3 per the protocol's borderline rule for one group measured before and after. Outcomes (AI literacy, self-efficacy, engagement) are self-report and the domain is nursing research, not STEM, but E3 is the first applicable code in order of the protocol's logic at abstract stage.

quote: we conducted a thematic analysis of qualitative data gathered from surveying 38 student volunteers
rationale: The study is a qualitative thematic analysis of survey data from 38 students, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical quantitative study meeting the design criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is used as the primary code under the protocol's order, since the design is qualitative/survey-based; E3 (no control group) and E5 (no quantitative outcome) would also apply. Abstract clearly shows qualitative design, so exclude.

quote: Fourth-year dental students underwent an 8-week training period, followed by the administration of multiple-choice questions of varying difficulty levels.
rationale: Dental students are not clearly K-12 or higher education STEM learners per the protocol's domain; dentistry/intraosseous lesion knowledge falls under health professions education, which the protocol excludes. Also, the study compares students with ChatGPT versions as knowledge-test responders rather than a learner-facing AI intervention versus a non-generative-AI control group, so the comparison criterion is not met. Abstract gives positive evidence that the domain (health professions dental education) fails, so exclusion is warranted. Coded E4 as the population/domain failure is the most applicable first-applying code; the domain failure (health professions) is the strongest ground.

rationale: Abstract describes a controlled comparison of a GenAI code-review tool (original vs context-enhanced) with 26 software engineering students, so GenAI, STEM domain, and student population appear met. However, the only reported result is student-perceived feedback quality, which may fall under the excluded perception-only outcomes, and the comparison is between two GenAI variants, which per protocol would be E3 unless a non-AI control exists. Positive evidence of failure is not clear from the abstract, so I cannot exclude; full text needed to check for a non-generative-AI control and a quantitative learning outcome.

rationale: The abstract describes a questionnaire with guided reflections, with no separate control group that avoids generative AI. Survey-based designs are not eligible, and outcomes appear to be self-reported behaviors and perceptions rather than a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion on E3 (no comparison group) is the first applicable code given the protocol order, though the design also looks non-experimental. Abstract-stage exclusion is supported by positive evidence of a non-comparative survey design.

The other criteria appear met (Gemini-based storytelling, Solar System science content, 6th-grade students, achievement outcome), but E3 is the first failing code in order.

quote: Experimental results show that the emotion-aware AI improved both learning performance and motivation in real-time classroom use, confirming its effectiveness in fostering engagement and better outcomes compared to a normal AI tutor.
rationale: At abstract stage, the record describes a generative AI programming assistant (generative language model) used by higher-education students in programming, with a comparison to a normal AI tutor and a learning-performance outcome. The comparator is described as a "normal AI tutor", which may itself be generative AI, so the comparison criterion is unclear rather than clearly failed. Design and publication type cannot be verified from the abstract. No positive evidence of a failed criterion, so include for full-text check.

Abstract describes a qualitative-style discourse analysis of perspectives from 24 science and mathematics students on academic integrity. There is no comparison group, no intervention experiment, and no quantitative learning outcome. The study is not an empirical experiment meeting the design criteria; it is perception-based. Coded E6 (not an empirical study) as the abstract's exploratory perception design fails the eligibility design requirement; no quantitative learning outcome is reported either, which would also fail E5. Coded at first applicable code under the protocol order is E5 for missing quantitative outcome, but the primary failure is the non-experimental, perception-based design, so E6 is applied.

quote: The educational value of the system appears to depend on the alignment among programming tasks, feedback, game-based engagement, generative AI-supported question generation, and teacher guidance.
rationale: Programming course (STEM), quasi-experiment with a control group doing traditional assignments, pre/post test achievement outcome, 2026 publication, journal article (Applied Sciences). The intervention is a game-based learning system whose abstract mentions "generative AI-supported question generation" as one component, but it is unclear whether learners directly interact with a generative model or whether generative AI only generated the questions (possibly teacher-side). Resolve at fulltext. Abstract does not give clear positive evidence of failure, so not excluded.

quote: This cross-sectional study investigates the usage patterns and ethical perceptions of ChatGPT among 381 students
rationale: The record is a cross-sectional anonymous survey of students' ChatGPT usage and perceptions. It has no control group, no intervention manipulation, and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions and self-reported usage. Survey/cross-sectional designs are excluded by the protocol. Under the code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is not clearly established from the abstract, and E3/E5 apply, but the core failure is that this is a non-empirical-trial survey design, so E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense) is used as the single code. Decision is exclude; it is not a close call because the design is survey-based regardless of the code chosen.

quote: With a quantitative approach and a quasi-experimental design, an investigation was carried out in seven programming groups in a polytechnic university in Guayaquil, Ecuador.
rationale: Abstract describes GenAI (Gemini in Google Colab) used by programming students in a quasi-experimental design, in a university setting, so intervention, domain and population appear met. However, the abstract reports mainly motivation, interest, satisfaction and expectation fulfilment, which the protocol excludes as affective/perception outcomes. It does not state whether a control group without GenAI exists or whether any learning achievement measure was collected. Missing information is not evidence of failure at abstract stage, so the record is passed to full text to check for a comparison group and a quantitative learning outcome.

quote: The paper proposes a structured certification program that aligns educational curricula with industry needs
rationale: The abstract describes a policy/position proposal for a national certification program for generative AI. It reports no empirical study, no experimental or comparison group, and no learning outcome measure. This is a non-empirical paper, so E6 applies. Other criteria are not assessable from the abstract but do not matter given E6.

Abstract describes ChatGPT use by students in a fourth-year Mechanical Engineering course (STEM, higher education), so intervention, domain and population appear met. However, the abstract reports survey results and course observations and claims improved academic performance without describing a control group or a comparison design, so comparison, design and quantitative outcome cannot be confirmed. Not excluded at abstract stage because absence of information is not evidence of failure; needs full-text check for a control group and performance statistics.

quote: Through a focused case study on the Discrete Mathematics curriculum, we meticulously investigate the multifaceted integration of LLMs across diverse instructional dimensions.
rationale: The abstract describes a case study with no comparison group, no quantitative learning outcome, and a discussion-style exploration of LLM integration. This is a non-empirical or case-study design that fails the design criterion (case study is explicitly excluded). Positive evidence of design failure is present, so exclusion is warranted. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is applied as the best fit for a descriptive/discussion paper; no control group or quantitative outcome is reported in the abstract.

quote: This descriptive-exploratory qualitative study integrates a narrative literature review, a teacher self-narrative, and a documentary analysis of pedagogical practices
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive-exploratory qualitative study combining a narrative literature review, teacher self-narrative, and documentary analysis. It is not an empirical controlled study: there is no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and the domain is physical education rather than STEM. Under the ordered codes, E6 (not an empirical study) is the first that clearly applies, since the design is qualitative and non-experimental. Domain (E2) and outcome (E5) also fail, but E6 is the first in order that applies cleanly at abstract stage.

quote: we conducted a randomized experiment comparing preparatory behaviors, performance, reliability and acceptability for candidates encouraged to surreptitiously use ChatGPT relative to two control groups
rationale: Participants are applicants to medical school (medical admissions interviews), not K-12 or higher education students in a learning activity; the study measures interview performance for admission selection. Population criterion fails on positive evidence. Domain is also doubtful (medical admissions interviews, not STEM content). Excluded under E4 as the first applicable code in protocol order would be E1 only if intervention were not learner-facing, but the interviewees are applicants being assessed, so E4 applies.

quote: This study investigates students' perceptions of programming learning difficulties before and a year after the release of ChatGPT. Through self-reported surveys, the study examines differences in perceived difficulties
rationale: The study uses self-reported surveys of perceptions of programming difficulties, with separate groups before and after ChatGPT's release rather than a concurrent control group. There is no quantitative learning outcome (only perceptions/self-report), and the design is a survey comparison of separate cohorts, not a controlled comparison of generative AI use. Excluded under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome); the first applicable code in order would be E3 (no control group) or E5, and the outcome failure is the clearest positive evidence from the abstract.

quote: We advance a computing-specific vision of integrated learning ecosystems in which execution histories, feedback artifacts, repository data, and learner models are preserved and interoperable across contexts
rationale: The record is a conceptual/position article ("this article argues", "We advance a... vision", "outlining research challenges"). It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Exclusion code E6 is the first applicable in order where the record is non-empirical; E1 and E3 cannot be assessed as no intervention study is described.
rationale_note: Exclusion based on positive evidence in the abstract that the piece is a position/vision article.

rationale: Medical communication skills training for first-year medical students is health professions education, which the protocol excludes from the STEM domain (E2). The abstract also reports only satisfaction and perceptions, with no control group and no quantitative learning measure, so E3 and E5 would apply as well. Per the code order, E2 is reported first. Note: the quote field is null because no quoted passage is needed beyond the domain judgement; the abstract's statement that students were in "medical education" supports the domain exclusion.

quote: Practice has shown that this model effectively enhances students' learning engagement, engineering thinking skills, and human-computer collaboration literacy.
rationale: Generative AI teaching model in an electrical engineering course for higher education students, which passes the intervention, population, and domain checks at abstract level. The abstract does not state whether a control group exists or what the design is; it describes a teaching-practice model and reports engagement and thinking outcomes without indicating a comparison. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record goes forward to full text to check comparison, design, and whether a quantitative learning outcome is reported.

criteria.quote: A sample of 142 undergraduate mathematics education students participated in an online survey to measure their perceptions and intentions of AI adoption in their academic work.
criteria.rationale: The study is a survey of perceptions and behavioural intention (UTAUT model), not an experiment with a control group or a quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical intervention study comparing learners with and without generative AI. Coded E6 as a non-experimental survey design; E3 and E5 would also apply, but E6 reflects the primary design failure. Abstract-stage exclusion is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with perception outcomes only.

quote: Twenty-seven purposively selected problems covering central tendency and dispersion were presented to both LLMs.
rationale: The abstract describes a comparative evaluation of two LLMs (ChatGPT and Gemini) on accuracy and consistency of responses to 27 problems. There is no separate control group without generative AI, and the two generative AI variants are compared only with each other. This matches E3 (no control group without generative AI). Also, the study appears to assess LLM outputs rather than learner outcomes, with no described learner-facing intervention or learning measure with a comparison group. Positive evidence of the comparison failure is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: This feasibility study explores an AI-assisted workflow to grade handwritten physics derivations using MathPix and GPT-4.
rationale: The GPT-4 workflow is used to grade student work, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity; the protocol excludes AI used only for grading (E1). The abstract also reports agreement with human graders on a synthetic dataset, not a learning outcome from a controlled comparison. No comparison group is described. Excluded at the first applicable code, E1.

Abstract describes a survey-style mixed-methods study of how students use LLMs, analyzing usage frequency, purposes, and attitudes. It reports no control group and no comparison condition without generative AI, so E3 applies. The design also appears descriptive rather than an experiment or quasi-experiment, and no quantitative learning outcome is described. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of absent comparison group in the abstract.

quote: This research endeavours to utilise AI, specifically ChatGPT and Gemini, to bolster and refine formal letter writing and email composition skills among first-cycle undergraduate students enrolled in the English for Engineering module
rationale: The learning content is formal letter writing in English for mechanical engineering students. This is English language learning, a non-STEM content area under the protocol, so E2 applies. The abstract also describes a pre-test/post-test single-group design with perception outcomes and no control group, which would independently suggest E3, but E2 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: This study employs a qualitative method. In order to collect data, ten participants of advanced diploma were requested to provide written feedback about their experiences with generative artificial intelligence.
rationale: Abstract shows English language learning (non-STEM) content, which fails the domain criterion (E2). It is also a qualitative study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it would fail E3, E5 and design criteria as well. E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order.

quote: we link 1,140 academic majors to a GenAI Exposure index that captures the fraction of occupational tasks performable by large language models and compare trends before and after 2022
rationale: The study is an observational analysis of IPEDS degree completions linked to an occupational GenAI exposure index. No learners interact with a generative AI tool in a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). There is also no separate control group without generative AI; the comparison is across exposure levels and pre/post periods. The outcome is institutional enrollment/completion counts rather than a learning measure. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: A qualitative descriptive–interpretative design compared initial responses, prompts, revised responses, and retrospective reflections.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative descriptive-interpretative design with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The topic is Social Sciences source interpretation in teacher education, which is not STEM. Positive evidence of failure exists for design (qualitative, no comparison) and for outcome (no quantitative measure), and the domain is also non-STEM. The protocol says to report the first applicable code in order; E3 (no control group) would precede E5 and E2 would precede E5 for domain. However, the abstract gives positive evidence of failure on the comparison and the domain as well. Applying the order strictly: E1 does not apply (ChatGPT is learner-facing generative AI); E2 applies because the content is social sciences education, not STEM. Therefore the first applicable code is E2.

quote: We administered a validated multidimensional scale to 214 postgraduate students, and the results indicate a moderate overall use of GAI
rationale: The abstract describes a single-survey study of 214 postgraduate students reporting self-rated GAI use and perceived benefits. There is no control group without generative AI, and the design is survey-based, so it is not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. The outcome is self-reported use and perceptions rather than a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion is positive evidence on comparison and design, so E3 is applied as the first failing criterion.

quote: Questionnaires based on well-established theories were administered during courses on product innovation and representation
rationale: The abstract describes a questionnaire-based correlational study of students' perceptions of generative AI and personality/design roles. There is no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; measures are perceptions and awareness. Exclusion under E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the most applicable code; E5 (no learning outcome) also applies and is a plausible alternative. Design is correlational, which is not eligible.

quote: Dear Editor-in-Chief, As former ESL (English as a Second Language) students who have pursued science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) fields
rationale: The record is an editorial letter to the editor with a personal anecdote and opinion. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Other criteria are not assessable from this text.

quote: A bibliometric analysis was conducted using the Scopus database to analyze current research trends on ChatGPT and Science Education.

quote: This study reports results from an institutional case study based on a taxonomy-aligned survey of 109 respondents
rationale: Survey-based case study with no control group and no learning outcome measured; usage and perceptions only. Fails the design (survey/case study), comparison, and outcome criteria. Exclusion is clear from the abstract.

rationale: The article is a conceptual/theoretical linguistic paper proposing a taxonomy. Abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

Coded E3 as the first applicable failing criterion in the protocol's order that the abstract supports, though E6 (not an empirical study) may also apply at full text.

Publication type also appears to be a non-journal editorial, but E6 is the first applicable code in order from the protocol's perspective since E1-E5 cannot be assessed from an abstract that describes no study.

The abstract also gives no comparison group or experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome, so the record is not clearly eligible on other criteria either. Since E1 is the first applicable code in order, it is reported.

quote: The research was conducted over five instructional sessions involving 122 second-year students at Y Middle School in Seoul.
