rationale: The record is a practical guide/pedagogical framework paper, not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, control group, or learning outcome data. Sport management is also not clearly STEM. Excluded under E6 as not an empirical study; the first applicable code in order is E1 only if intervention is judged non-learner-facing, which is unclear, so E6 is the best fit.

quote: Sentiment/thematic analysis using a generative AI-driven large language model revealed learners held positive perceptions of SI
rationale: The generative AI (LLM) is used by researchers for sentiment/thematic analysis of learner responses, not as a learner-facing tool in the learning activity. The SI sessions are peer-led, not generative AI. Per the E1 code, the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. Additionally, the outcomes are largely perceptions and preferences, and the grade comparison is across dosage strata rather than a generative AI control comparison, so E3 and E5 would also be plausible. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Drawing on current adoption statistics, educator testimonials, and technical analyses, this paper demonstrates that these tools have moved beyond experimental novelty
rationale: The abstract describes a discursive/analytical review drawing on adoption statistics, testimonials, and technical analyses, with no comparison group or experimental design. This is positive evidence that the record is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. STEM content is also not evident. No quantitative learning outcome is reported in the abstract.

quote: The study adopts a mixed-method research design using questionnaire responses, classroom interaction data, learning management system records, and performance evaluation results
rationale: Abstract describes a GenAI-enabled engineering classroom with students and reports performance gains "compared with traditional classroom practices," which suggests a comparison group, but the design is described as mixed-method and does not clearly state a randomized or quasi-experimental control group. Venue is unclear (a journal name without clear peer-review indication) and the record's DOI is a Zenodo repository link, so publication type is also uncertain. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is passed to full text for checking the comparison, design, and publication type.

quote: we pilot if artificial intelligence (AI) large language models (LLMs) can be utilised to create a large-scale overview of master's theses' characteristics efficiently
rationale: The LLM is used by researchers to categorise thesis texts, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. No control group or learning outcome is described; the study is a text-coding pilot. Excluded under E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI). Also no comparison group without generative AI and no quantitative learning outcome appear in the abstract.

quote: The study was conducted based on a quantitative approach and a questionnaire was administered to undergraduate students. The data obtained were processed using descriptive statistics and correlation analysis methods.
rationale: The abstract describes a questionnaire survey with correlation analysis of self-reported AI tool use. There is no separate control group and no experimental comparison, so the design is survey/correlational rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison design. Positive evidence of failure exists for comparison and design, so the record is excluded at abstract stage. E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order (intervention and domain are not clearly positive evidence of failure, but the absence of a control group is).

quote: We focused on a specific course on scientific research in engineering, in which we measured the competencies, expressed in terms of the indicators, mastery, comprehension and synthesis capacity, in students who decided to use or not ChatGPT
rationale: At abstract stage, the study appears to compare students who used ChatGPT with those who did not, in an engineering research course, with competency measures. Design, comparison structure, and effect-size data cannot be confirmed from the abstract, and no positive evidence of a failed criterion is present. Advance to full text. Note the abstract mentions students who chose to use ChatGPT, which may be self-selected groups; this needs checking at full text.
rationale_criteria_note: Design and comparison unclear; no exclusion evidence in abstract.

quote: Responders not aware of ChatGPT or never used it for academic purposes did not continue with the survey, by design.
rationale: This is a cross-sectional anonymous survey of pharmacy students about ChatGPT use. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; it reports only usage and perceptions. Design is survey (not an eligible design) and no comparison group exists. Coded E3 as the first failing criterion in order from E1 (intervention is not clearly learner-facing learning activity, but the abstract does not establish a clear E1 failure). Pharmacy is also not clearly STEM. Excluded on positive evidence of no comparison group and survey design.

quote: The study utilized the 2021 AAMC SJT practice exam, querying the LLMs to rate the effectiveness of various behavioral responses to each scenario.
rationale: The study evaluates LLMs answering a medical school situational judgment test; no learners interact with the LLM, there is no human control group, and the content is social judgment for medical school admission rather than STEM. Exclusion under E1 would be the first applicable code by order, since the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI (LLMs are tested directly as respondents). Per the code order, E1 applies first. Note the record is excluded on the first applicable code, which is E1, not E4.

quote: we introduced an elective course titled “Generative AI and Cybersecurity” for MS and upper-division BS students
rationale: The abstract describes a course description with no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome; it reads as a descriptive course report. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) applies as the first failing criterion checked in order that is clearly evidenced. Cybersecurity is arguably STEM-adjacent (computer science), but this is not decided since the design already fails. Intervention and population appear met.

quote: Three methods were tested: machine learning, deep learning, and few-shot prompting with large language models.
rationale: The study is an automated classification of peer code review feedback text. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; LLMs are used only as classifiers on feedback data. No learner-facing generative AI intervention and no control group comparing learning outcomes is described. No quantitative learning outcome is measured (classification F1 is a tool performance metric). Code E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Survey results show that most students rate chatbots and virtual assistants as moderately to highly effective, increasing learning motivation and providing ease of access.
rationale: The abstract describes AI chatbots/virtual assistants for solving math problems, which plausibly involves generative AI, and the domain is mathematics. However, the reported evidence is survey-based student ratings, and the abstract does not mention a control group, a experimental design, or a quantitative learning outcome. The abstract also claims enhanced learning outcomes, but without any described comparison. Missing information is not evidence of failure at the abstract stage, so this is unsure and should be checked at full text for a control group, a quantitative outcome, and whether the chatbot is generative.

Abstract is absent from the index, so there is no positive evidence that any criterion fails. The title indicates a programming (STEM) topic, a 2026 publication date, and a chatbot intervention in a flipped classroom. Whether the chatbot is generative, whether a control group exists, the design, the population, and the outcome cannot be determined from the title alone. Advance to full text for assessment.

quote: The results show that large-scale language model technology has unique advantages in explaining chemical knowledge, experimental demonstration, and online course creation
rationale: The abstract describes a scientometric CiteSpace co-occurrence analysis of keywords, not an empirical learner-facing experiment. There is no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no learner intervention described. The design is not an empirical study of the eligible type, so exclude under E6. The quote is the closest verbatim support for the review-style findings.

quote: Experimental evaluation on real‑world cellular traffic data shows up to 15% reduction in root-mean-square error (RMSE)
rationale: The study forecasts 5G/6G network traffic with an LLM-based hybrid model. It involves no learners or learning activity, so it is not about STEM education. Under the protocol's exclusion code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) would apply first, since the LLM is used as a forecasting component rather than a learner-facing tool. Still, the record is clearly outside the review's scope. I am reporting E2 as the primary code, because the content is network engineering prediction, not STEM learning content, and no learner is involved. Note that by strict code order E1 precedes E2; the auditor should consider switching to E1 if that is the preferred reading.

quote: Initial usability feedback gathered from 24 participants indicated manageable workload, although perceived system performance was rated lower due to sensor calibration issues during the prototype testing phase.
rationale: The abstract describes a prototype kiosk (HealthBot, with an LLM component) evaluated only through usability and perceived-workload feedback from 24 participants. There is no control group, no comparative design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Usability/perception outcomes do not qualify. Exclusion on E5 is applied, although the abstract also gives no evidence of a control-group design (E3), so the choice of E5 as the first applicable code is a judgment call. Per the protocol's ordering rule, E1 does not apply because the LLM is learner-facing in the sense that it generates advice for users, but the abstract is unclear on this, so E5 is the chosen code.

quote: Generative AI-assisted learning of the Living Qur’an and Hadith had a positive and significant effect on students’ HOTS
rationale: Content is Living Qur'an and Hadith, Islamic studies, which is not science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, or data science. Fails the STEM domain criterion (E2). Other criteria appear met at abstract stage: generative AI learner-facing, quasi-experimental control group, HOTS essay test outcome, higher education students, 2026 publication. Domain exclusion is positive evidence from the abstract, so exclude.

quote: The methods used were questionnaires for and FGD with 40 ESP Material Development class students.
rationale: Abstract describes a questionnaire and focus group study of perceptions with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Design is survey/qualitative, so it is not an empirical experimental study meeting the protocol. Exclusion E6 (not an empirical study eligible under the design criteria) applies at abstract stage; the more precise reason is that it is a survey/perception study. Domain (ESP materials, English language) also appears non-STEM. Coded E6 as the first applicable code given the design; no comparison or learning outcome is reported.

quote: These initial observations show that LLMs can encourage self-guided research, offer on-demand feedback, and strengthen cohort identity
rationale: The abstract describes an exploratory use-case report of LLM integration in a first-year computer science cohort. It gives no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome; findings are described as exploratory observations. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is present, so exclude under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Under the protocol's ordering, E3 is the first applicable code given the design lacks a comparison. Note that the design is also not an experiment, which supports the exclusion.

criteria.criteria_note: descriptive survey of teachers

quote: A descriptive survey design was adopted.
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of in-service secondary Biology teachers on perception, adoption and utilization of generative AI tools. It is not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a control group, it has no learner-facing AI intervention, and its outcomes are perceptions and self-reported use rather than learning outcomes. Exclusion at E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of an eligible design) is the first applicable code in the order given; E1 (teacher-only use) and E3 (no control) would also apply. Under the abstract-stage rule, the positive evidence of a survey design supports exclusion.

criteria.outcome_note: post-test scores and learning gain reported
criteria.intervention_note: comparison group uses MATLAB built-in copilot, which is itself generative AI; the treatment is an AI-assisted feedback system, likely LLM-based but not stated

quote: We compared this with MATLAB’s built-in copilot. In a class study with 60 students, both groups did the same lessons and tasks; only the feedback differed.
rationale: MATLAB programming is STEM, students are higher education (core engineering courses), and a post-test outcome is reported. Two concerns remain at abstract stage. First, the control arm uses MATLAB's built-in copilot, which is itself a generative AI tool, so the comparison may be two generative AI variants (E3) rather than a no-generative-AI control; this cannot be resolved from the abstract. Second, the treatment is described as an AI-assisted system without stating whether it is generative. Neither point is positive evidence of failure at abstract stage, so the record is passed to full text. Design (randomization or quasi-experimental comparison) is also not described in the abstract.

quote: This study asks what Vietnamese AI policy actually requires of higher education institutions, and whether those requirements reach the classroom
rationale: The study is a policy document analysis of 31 Vietnamese AI policy instruments. It involves no learner interaction with generative AI, no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no STEM content focus. It is not an empirical intervention study. Coded E6 as the first applicable code is E1 (intervention not learner-facing), but the core failure is that it is not an empirical study; the abstract gives no learner-facing intervention at all, so E1 would also apply. Following the order of codes, E1 is the first that applies, so the code should be E1 rather than E6. The record is excluded either way.

quote: This study addresses the gap between the theoretical framework of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) literacy and its practical development
rationale: The abstract describes a 16-week qualitative study of 16 humanities students with structured dialogues, questionnaires, reflections and interviews. There is no control group and no quantitative learning comparison, so the design fails the comparison and design criteria. It is a single-group qualitative study. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol order that the abstract clearly supports; E5 (no quantitative outcome) and E6 (not an empirical study) are also plausible, but the design flaw is the primary reason. Abstract-stage exclusion is justified because positive evidence of failed comparison/design is present.

criteria.population_note: medical students; domain is medical education, not STEM

quote: A cross-sectional questionnaire-based study was conducted among 297 undergraduate MBBS students at AIIMS, Rishikesh.
rationale: The design is a cross-sectional survey with no control group, which fails the comparison and design criteria. It also reports only usage and perceptions, with no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's code order, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first code that applies. Domain (medical education) is also outside STEM, but the abstract is clear enough on the comparison failure that E3 is the assigned code.
rationale_note: Abstract stage; exclusion is based on positive evidence of a non-comparative survey design.

quote: This paper introduces an experiential learning innovation that empowers sales students to utilize GenAI effectively within the sales process
rationale: The course is professional selling, a marketing/sales topic, which is not STEM content (E2). The abstract also describes an innovation paper with participant feedback only, with no control group or quantitative learning outcome, so it would fail E3 and E5 as well. E2 is the first applicable code in the protocol order.

criteria.criteria_note: Qualitative design with semi-structured interviews and policy document analysis; no control group or quantitative learning outcome; participants are school leaders and teachers rather than students.

quote: Using a descriptive-exploratory qualitative design, the study conducted semi-structured interviews with school leaders, including principals and district supervisors
rationale: The abstract gives positive evidence that the study is a qualitative, non-empirical-experimental design (interviews and policy analysis) with no control group, no quantitative learner outcome, and participants who are school leaders rather than students. It fails the design, comparison, outcome, and population criteria. Under the protocol's exclusion code order, E1 (intervention) is unclear here, and E2 (content) is not clearly applicable, so E6 is the first clearly applicable code for a non-empirical (qualitative) study. Note: the population is also not students, which would be E4; but the design failure (E6) is the more fundamental, clearly evidenced reason.

quote: We evaluated four state-of-the-art multimodal LLMs (ChatGPT-5.1, Gemini-2.5, Grok-4, Claude Sonnet-4.5) on 208 image-based examination questions
rationale: The study compares only generative AI models against each other on exam questions; there is no control group without generative AI. Models are evaluated directly rather than learners interacting with them in a learning activity, and the design is a model benchmark rather than a learner comparison. Per the protocol, studies comparing only generative AI variants are excluded under E3. Domain (anatomy/pathology/radiology, partly medical) also raises a possible health-professions concern, but the first applicable code in order is E3 for the comparison failure.

quote: The findings reveal a hesitance among educators... Conversely, many adult learners demonstrate enthusiasm for learning about its potential benefits despite having limited understanding.
rationale: The study uses surveys and focus groups on knowledge and attitudes about generative AI among EAL learners, educators and leaders. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design with a control group and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions and attitudes only. Also the content is language learning, not STEM, which would be E2, but the first applicable code in order is E5 for no quantitative learning outcome... Note: E2 precedes E5 in order, and the study is non-STEM (EAL/digital literacy); applying the protocol order, the correct code is E2.

quote: Data were collected through a validated questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and multiple regression.
rationale: Abstract describes a single-group experimental design with students interacting with ChatGPT, measured only by a perception questionnaire of five dimensions (ratings of usefulness). No control group is mentioned and no quantitative learning outcome (achievement, knowledge, problem solving) is reported; outcomes are perceived ratings. Exclusion E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). Comparison group absence (E3) is also suggested, but E5 is the first code that clearly applies on the abstract's evidence per the perception-only outcome. Not STEM content is also unclear. Excluded on positive evidence that outcomes are perceptions only.

quote: Searches of Google Scholar, Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, and ScienceDirect covering 2022 to 2026 produced a two-tier evidence base
rationale: The record is a narrative synthesis/review that draws on surveys, a secondary-school field experiment, and a preprint, rather than reporting an empirical primary study with a control group and SMD-computable data. It is not an empirical study of its own, so E6 applies. Although the abstract mentions experimental syntheses, the paper itself is a review, which the protocol does not admit as an empirical study. The abstract gives positive evidence of a review design.

quote: Student Registration Chatbot: A Large Language Model Approach - A Case Study of Adekunle Ajasin University
rationale: The chatbot is a GPT-3.5-based generative tool used by students, but it supports administrative student registration (login, password reset, fee status, results, course registration errors), not STEM learning content. The domain criterion fails, so E2 applies (first failing code in order that is clearly evidenced; E1 does not apply since the tool is learner-facing and generative). The abstract also reports only waiting time and cost metrics compared against an existing model, not a learning outcome, so E5 would also be relevant, but E2 is the first applicable code.

quote: Participants in the AI Tutor group demonstrated significantly greater cognitive rehabilitation gains, particularly in working memory, processing speed, and maths performance compared to both the Traditional Tutoring and Control groups (p < 0.001).
rationale: Abstract does not indicate that the AI tutor is generative (no LLM or generative model mentioned); it describes an AI-driven virtual tutor, and the study's focus is cognitive rehabilitation in pediatric cancer survivors rather than STEM learning. Under the abstract-stage rule, a bare "AI" tutor is unsure, not a positive failure, and the cognitive rehabilitation focus is not clearly STEM content. However, the intervention is a rehabilitation-oriented AI tutor with no evidence of learner-facing generative AI, so this is a judgment call. Recording as exclude on E1 because there is no positive indication of a generative model; the reviewer should check at full text if the record is considered for advancement.
decision_note: Per rule 2, abstract-stage exclusion requires positive evidence. The abstract shows no generative model, so this should be unsure rather than exclude.

quote: we conducted scenario-based training with three in-service mathematics teachers using ChatGPT
rationale: Participants are three in-service mathematics teachers, which the protocol excludes (in-service teachers are not K-12 or higher education students). The study is a small qualitative interview-based study of teacher noticing with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E4 is the first applicable code in protocol order that is clearly evidenced; E3 and E5 also apply on the abstract, but population failure is the first in the order. Abstract shows positive evidence, so exclusion is appropriate.

quote: Generative AI-assisted programming on the computational thinking of high school students
rationale: Abstract describes a generative AI-assisted programming intervention with high-school students, a computational thinking outcome (quantitative, p-values reported), and an "experimental group," implying a comparison group. The abstract does not state the control condition or whether assignment was randomized or quasi-experimental, and does not give SMD data; these are not positive evidence of failure, so the record advances to full text. Journal article in Frontiers in Psychology, 2026, meets date criterion.

quote: Using an explanatory case study with a mixed-methods approach, the study examines the simulation’s usability, design challenges, and instructional utility
rationale: The abstract describes an explanatory case study using usability surveys and reflective journals, with no control or comparison group. Case study designs and perception-based data do not meet the comparison, design, or quantitative outcome criteria. The exclusion code is E3 because there is no control group without generative AI. Domain is also unclear: the abstract refers to teaching competencies rather than STEM content.

quote: "A descriptive, cross-sectional, non- experimental study was conducted with a purposive sample of 124 first-year Human Anatomy students"
rationale: The study is a descriptive, cross-sectional, non-experimental survey of satisfaction with ChatGPT use. It has no control group without generative AI, so it fails the comparison and design criteria (E3). It also reports only satisfaction and perceptions, with no quantitative learning outcome (would be E5). E3 is the first applicable code in order. Human Anatomy is arguably health/medical content, which may raise a domain question, but the design failure is decisive.

quote: Results from the surveys and interviews indicated that students used ChatGPT to explain and summarize information, answer questions, provide feedback, create texts, and write code.
rationale: Abstract describes a survey and interview study of acceptance and self-efficacy (perceptions), with no experimental or control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Design and comparison criteria are not met on positive evidence; the outcome is self-reported self-efficacy and acceptance, not learning performance. Domain is unclear (general undergraduate use, not clearly STEM). Excluded at abstract stage on E5 as the most direct failure, though E3 (no control group) would also apply.
rationale_note: Note: first applicable code in order is E1 check (intervention is generative, learner-facing, so not E1); E2 unclear; E3 applies since survey design has no control group. Per protocol order, E2 is unclear, so E3 is the first clearly failing code.

criteria.quote: A descriptive survey research design was adopted, with a population comprising STEM students across different academic levels.
criteria.rationale: Survey-based descriptive design with no control group and no learning outcome; only awareness, usage, and perceptions are reported. Per protocol order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is not clearly established from the abstract, so the first clear failure is E3 (no control group without generative AI).

quote: A descriptive survey research design was adopted, with a population comprising STEM students across different academic levels.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive survey with no comparison group and reports only awareness, usage and perceptions rather than a quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of a failed criterion exists (no control group; survey design), so exclusion at abstract stage is justified. Code E3 is used as the first failing criterion that is clearly evidenced; the survey design would also fail E5 and E6, but the protocol's ordering places E3 first among those clearly evidenced.

quote: A quantitative method was employed with a sample of 29 students from various semesters. The research instrument utilized was a questionnaire using the Likert Scale
rationale: The abstract describes a single-sample descriptive questionnaire study of students' perceptions of ChatGPT use, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (only Likert perception scores). Positive evidence of missing comparison group and missing learning outcome exists, so exclusion is warranted. E3 is the first applicable code in protocol order, since no control group without generative AI is reported; E5 would also apply. Reporting E3 as the first failing code per the ordering rule.

quote: A large-scale analysis was conducted across 56 CLOs to assess internal consistency, followed by expert validation from two academic reviewers who evaluated a sample of AI-generated feedback for accuracy, usefulness, and cognitive alignment.
rationale: The ChatGPT tool is used by faculty and curriculum designers to evaluate course alignment, not by learners in a learning activity (this would be E1 at fulltext). The abstract reports no comparison group, no learner population, and no quantitative learning outcome; the evaluation is of AI-generated feedback quality and internal consistency. Positive evidence shows the AI is used by teachers/designers, and there is no control group or learner outcome, so the record is excluded. Using E5 as the first applicable code at abstract stage given the absence of any learner outcome; E1 could also apply since the tool is used by faculty, not learners. Stated for audit: the first code in protocol order that is clearly supported is E1, since the AI is used only by faculty to evaluate course design.

quote: We conducted a cross-sectional online survey.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of perceptions and familiarity with AI chatbots, with no learning intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Survey design is explicitly excluded by the protocol's design criterion. Under the code order, the first applicable code is E1 only if the intervention is absent; here there is no learner-facing intervention evaluated, but the clearest failure is that it is not an empirical intervention study (survey design, E6). Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract.

quote: This study analyzed the perceptions and usage patterns of generative AI ChatGPT among 181 first-year non-major students
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group survey of perceptions and usage with no control group, so there is no comparison group without generative AI. Outcomes are satisfaction and perceptions rather than a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in protocol order for the missing control group. The study is also a survey design, which the protocol excludes, but E3 is reported as the first failing code.

quote: the use of ChatGPT as a writing support tool in English
rationale: The study concerns ChatGPT for English writing support, which is language learning and not STEM content. This is positive evidence that the domain criterion fails, so the record is excluded under E2. The abstract also describes perception-focused aims with pre- and post-tests and no clear control group, but the domain failure alone is sufficient. Exclusion code E2 is the first applicable code in the protocol order.

quote: aimed at enhancing literacy among young children and lower-grade elementary and middle school students
rationale: The study targets literacy (language learning), which is non-STEM content, so E2 applies. Generative AI (GPT) is used in a learner-facing app, but the abstract describes app development with no comparison group, no design description, and no quantitative learning outcome. E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order that the abstract positively supports.

criteria.outcome_note: Outcome is self-reported productivity via Likert survey, not a learning measure

quote: This study aims to analyze the effect of ChatGPT usage on the productivity of students in the Information Technology Study Program at Politeknik Negeri Tanah Laut. A quantitative research approach with a survey method was employed.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey-based correlational design (Likert questionnaire, simple linear regression) with no separate control group that avoids generative AI. Per the protocol, correlational and survey designs are excluded and there is no comparison group, so E3 applies as the first failing criterion in code order. The outcome is self-reported productivity, not a quantitative learning measure, which would be a secondary failure (E5). Domain is not clearly STEM, but this is not needed to decide.

This is a survey-based SEM study of attitudes and behavioral intentions toward ChatGPT use. It has no learner-facing intervention with a control group, no quantitative learning outcome (only perceptions and intentions, which the protocol excludes), and it is a cross-sectional survey design rather than an experiment or quasi-experiment. Domain is also not clearly STEM. Exclusion is on the outcome criterion, since the abstract gives positive evidence that only perceptions/intentions were measured. The design and comparison failures would also apply; the first applicable code in order is E1 only if intervention is judged not learner-facing, which the abstract does not clearly show, so E5 is the first code with positive evidence.

quote: This perspective article presents a theoretically grounded argument, drawing on established physics education research (PER)
rationale: The record is a perspective article presenting a theoretical argument, not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, control group, or quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Note that the protocol's first-applicable-code order would place E1 first if intervention were judged absent; the abstract does not give clear positive evidence of a learner-facing tool, but E6 applies on the design alone.

quote: Results show that AM supported by ChatGPT significantly enhances students' argumentative writing skills, particularly in clarity and argument structure in depth.
rationale: ChatGPT is used by learners within an argument-mapping activity, and the outcome is a quantitative pre/post test of argumentative writing. Population (Nursing and PGSD students) is higher education. However, the domain appears to be argumentative writing rather than STEM content, which is unclear from the abstract. The abstract does not state whether a control group without ChatGPT exists, so the comparison and design are unclear (it mentions a pre-post design, which could be single-group, E3). Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is passed to full text for checking the comparison group, design, and STEM domain.

quote: This paper explores the transformative potential of Gen-AI in modern physics classrooms by examining its role in improving teaching strategies
rationale: The abstract describes a narrative/discussion paper that draws on current studies and presents a "comprehensive view" with recommendations. It reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study. Exclusion under E6 is supported on positive evidence that the paper is a review-style essay, not an empirical study.

quote: We find that only the ChatGPT condition produces statistically significant learning gains compared to a no-help control
rationale: Abstract reports a randomized three-condition experiment (N=274) with ChatGPT-generated hints for learners, a no-help control, and learning gains on math problems (algebra, statistics). Population is not explicitly stated as students in the abstract, but nothing indicates exclusion; publication-type and data sufficiency cannot be checked from the abstract. Advance to full text to confirm learner population and SMD data.

criteria.domain_note: biology is not in the protocol's STEM list; see rationale

quote: Pre- and post-surveys (N=225) indicated strong student satisfaction; 72% would reuse Schema Study in future biology courses.
rationale: Abstract reports a single-group pre/post survey design with satisfaction, self-efficacy and usage outcomes, with no control group without generative AI (E3). No quantitative learning outcome is reported; independent performance is explicitly evaluated outside the app and not reported here. Introductory undergraduate biology is also arguably outside the protocol's STEM list (science is listed, so this is likely in scope). E3 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly evidenced. Note that E5 could also apply; E3 is reported as the first clear failure given the design description.

criteria.quote_note: n/a

quote: Drawing on Bloom's Taxonomy, a trend analysis of academic performances and focus group discussions, it proposes a transformed approach to assessment design
rationale: The study redesigns assessment questions so that ChatGPT-3.5 struggles to solve them. ChatGPT is used to test questions, not as a learner-facing tool within a learning activity. The abstract describes a trend analysis across years (2020-2024) with no control group using generative AI, so the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI (E1). Comparison and design are also unclear, but E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: we propose to analyze the outputs of Student Evaluations of Teaching (SETs) by using techniques relating to Generative AI (GenAI) and more precisely the multidimensional data analysis
rationale: GenAI is applied to analyze student evaluation survey outputs for program improvement and guidance, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. No control group, learning outcome, or experimental design is described. Excluded under E1 as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. Other criteria are not clearly addressed in the abstract.

quote: A correlational quantitative method was employed using the data collected through an online questionnaire distributed randomly to 293 science and engineering students
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational survey design analyzed with SEM, with no separate control group that avoids generative AI. Positive evidence of a failed comparison and design criterion supports exclusion. Under E3 (no control group without generative AI) and the design requirement, the study does not qualify. Also, the outcome is self-reported constructs with "student performance" unclear. Coding E3 as the first applicable code in protocol order given the absence of any comparison group.

quote: This study comparatively analyses the institutional guidelines of ten global elite universities

E6 (not an empirical study) is the most accurate single code for a documentary analysis, and it is stated plainly in the abstract ("qualitative, descriptive-analytical approach, grounded in documentary analysis").

quote: Benefits and risks of ChatGPT in future education

quote: This paper reflects on our strategy development process via Kolb’s experiential learning reflective framework

Stakeholder feedback is mentioned but no measured learning outcome is reported.
rationale_note: Exclusion based on positive abstract evidence of a non-empirical reflective design.

quote: Sixty preservice teachers were randomly assigned to either the BERT or Llama3 group, both participating in a workshop on the academically productive talk (APT) framework.

Also, the two arms both use generative-model tools (fine-tuned BERT is not clearly generative; Llama3 is), so there may be no non-generative-AI control group (E3 risk). The population and domain failures are positive evidence from the abstract, so exclude with E4 as the first applicable code in order is arguably E2 (content not STEM). Given the protocol's ordering, E2 comes before E4; on reflection the content (teacher dialogue pedagogy, not a STEM subject) fails the domain criterion first.

quote: We conducted multiple experiments with computer engineering students (experiment group: n =41 to 56), who were asked to use ChatGPT to answer previous test questions before learning about the related topics.

E1 would also apply, but E3 is the first code evaluated in the protocol's order that is clearly supported... quote: The research focuses on describing interaction patterns and the emerging learning needs. Conducted within a qualitative approach using an exploratory case study design
rationale: Qualitative exploratory case study of eight 10th-grade students interacting with ChatGPT on functions. No control group and no quantitative learning outcome; findings are descriptive prompt and response categories. Fails comparison and design criteria. Under the rule that the first applicable code is reported, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first failing code, with E5 and E6 also applicable. The record is excluded on the abstract alone.

quote: A comparative analysis of student outcomes in AI‐supported individual study versus traditional teaching methods.
rationale: Abstract describes a Vietnamese high school mathematics study with GenAI tools and a comparison against traditional teaching, which fits domain and population. However, the abstract does not state the design (randomized or quasi-experimental with a comparison group), whether the AI tool is generative in use, or whether a quantitative learning outcome was measured. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record advances to full text.

quote: Pre‐ and posttest surveys indicated significant (p < 0.001) increases in self‐efficacy for writing microcontroller programs
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group design: all students (n = 22) use ChatGPT and are measured by pre- and posttest surveys. There is no separate control group without generative AI, so the protocol's comparison criterion fails (E3). Outcomes are mainly self-efficacy and attitudes, which are affective and not eligible. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of a single-group design.

Abstract describes ChatGPT use in programming education with engineering undergraduates (STEM, higher education), so intervention, population, and domain appear met. Study 1 is a questionnaire/correlational design and is not eligible. Study 2 is a counterbalanced repeated-measures design with nine students using ChatGPT with and without, which is a within-subject comparison rather than a separate control group; whether it qualifies as a comparison group and whether it reports SMD-computable quantitative statistics (task time, efficiency, project assessment) are unclear from the abstract. Returning unsure to check the full text for the comparison, design, and data.

quote: Each problem's statement and reference solution are provided to GPT‐4 to produce a test suite that can be used by an autograder.
rationale: The LLM is used by the instructor/researchers to generate autograder test suites, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. Students only submit solutions to an autograder. This is E1 (AI used only by the teacher to prepare materials). No control group or learning outcome is reported in the abstract either, but E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: This qualitative descriptive study explored secondary students’ experiences of chemistry learning and AI-assisted academic support
rationale: The study is a qualitative descriptive design analyzing student excerpts thematically. It has no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical quantitative study meeting the design requirements. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is used as the first applicable code for a qualitative design; strictly, it is an empirical qualitative study, so E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) and E3 (no control group) also apply. The first code in order that clearly applies is E3 for the missing control group, but E3 precedes E5 in the list, and the protocol's design exclusion (qualitative designs) is closest to E6. Given the protocol's ordering, E3 is the first failing criterion for a study without any comparison group.

Excluding at abstract stage is justified because the abstract positively shows no comparison design or outcome data.

quote: This paper proposes a structured, three-layered framework for mitigating hallucinations in LLM-based educational tools

quote: Through surveys of 40 CS/SE students and 29 faculty members, complemented by in-depth interviews with 10 faculty

Coded E6 (not an empirical study eligible under the design criteria; survey/qualitative design), with E3 and E5 also failing.

Whether the control group lacked generative AI, whether the design is randomized or quasi-experimental, and whether statistics suffice for an SMD are unclear from the abstract and should be checked at full text. Other criteria are not assessable from the abstract, but E6 alone is sufficient for exclusion.

rationale_note: Abstract stage: not excluded because absence of control/outcome info is not positive evidence of failure.

quote: هدفت الدراسة إلى تصميم بيئة تعليمية قائمة على نموذج ذكاء اصطناعي توليدي والكشف عن فاعليتها في تنمية مهارات حل المشكلات البرمجية لدى طالبات قسم علوم الحاسب بالمرحلة الجامعية

E3 is the first applicable code in order that fits the lack of a comparison group; the design appears qualitative, which would also support E5/E6.

quote: We report an exploratory single case of a two-week orientation offered to non-traditional students entering online bachelor's degree programs.

Exclusion is on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), which is the first code that clearly applies in the protocol order given the abstract. Note that E3 (no control group) would also apply; under the rule of first applicable code in order, E3 precedes E5 in the list, so the code should be E3 instead. Corrected: E3 is the first applicable code because the absence of a comparison group is the earliest failing criterion.

rationale: The abstract describes evaluating ChatGPT's accuracy on a problem dataset. There is no learner-facing activity and no separate control group that does not use generative AI; the model is assessed alone, so the design is not a comparative experiment. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Note: the abstract-stage rule would normally favor advancing, but the absence of any comparison group is positive evidence that the comparison criterion fails.

quote: This article proposes the AI-Supported Heutagogical Development (AI-SHD) model, a novel theoretical framework
rationale: The abstract describes a proposed theoretical/conceptual framework (AI-SHD model) with no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. The study is not an empirical study, and its population is in-service primary school teachers, which is outside the eligible population. E6 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported; E4 (in-service teachers) also appears applicable but the primary failure is that it is not empirical.

quote: This study employed a qualitative research design.
rationale: The abstract states a qualitative design using interviews, focus groups and classroom observations. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The design is not an eligible experimental or quasi-experimental design, so the record fails the design, comparison and outcome criteria. The first applicable code in protocol order is E1 only if the intervention is not learner-facing, which is unclear here; E3 (no control group) is also a fair reading. Under the protocol's order, the strongest code for a non-empirical-comparison qualitative study is E6 (not an empirical study is arguably wrong since it is empirical). Rule 2 applies at abstract stage: the abstract gives positive evidence of a qualitative design with no comparison group, so exclusion is justified. Coded E3 because the defining failure is the absence of any control group, with the qualitative design also failing Design.

quote: No statistically significant differences in achievement threshold attainment were found between groups using and not using AI technologies (χ2=0,442; p>0,05).
rationale: At abstract stage, the study appears to involve LLM-based AI tools (large language models) with schoolchildren and university students and a comparison group not using AI, with a learning outcome (achievement threshold attainment). Design is described as a pedagogical experiment with a comparison of groups, but the abstract also relies on questionnaires and interviews, so the design and whether the outcome is a true learning measure cannot be confirmed. STEM domain is not stated in the abstract. No positive evidence of an exclusion criterion is present, so the record is advanced for full-text review.

quote: The study aimed to explore how a university instructor used the ChatGPT flipped model to impact university students' perceptions of the instructor's TPACK and students' self-regulated learning (SRL) ability in a general education course.
rationale: Generative AI (ChatGPT) use by university students is indicated, and the population is higher education. However, the abstract does not state whether a separate non-generative-AI control group exists (it reports pre-post tests, which could be single-group), and the domain is unclear: the course is a general education course, and the TPACK and SRL outcomes are not clearly STEM. The outcome is mentioned as SRL significant differences, but whether it is a quantitative learning measure or perception-based is unclear. Advance to full text to check comparison design, STEM content, and outcome measures.

quote: A qualitative exploratory design was employed involving 21 undergraduate students
rationale: The study is a qualitative exploratory thematic study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the abstract states it "did not quantitatively measure learning outcomes." Under the code order, E1 does not clearly apply (LLM use by learners is present), E2 is unclear given mixed programs, and E3 and E5 would also apply, but the design is non-empirical in the protocol's sense of excluding qualitative designs, so E6 is the best fit for the qualitative design. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence.
exclusion_code_note: E6 chosen; qualitative design is excluded under Design, and it is an empirical study, so E6 is arguably a misfit. Auditor may prefer E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), which the abstract states explicitly.

rationale: The record is a reflective/opinion essay on teaching and assessment in social science education in the age of AI. Outcomes are innovative outputs (likely a quantitative project scale) and passion for AI, which is affective and excluded per protocol; whether a quantitative learning outcome exists beyond the innovative-output scale needs full text. Abstract stage gives no positive evidence of failure, so unsure rather than exclude.
