rationale: The paper states it is a survey, framework and prototype study and not an empirically tested model. It is not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. Dropout prediction is also not learner-facing generative AI use. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported by the abstract.

criteria.outcome_note: Outcome is a questionnaire survey of perceptions

quote: To evaluate the impact of the Generative AI pedagogical approach, a questionnaire survey was developed and distributed to the students.
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT use in material science for chemical engineering students, which is STEM and learner-facing generative AI. However, the only evaluation described is a questionnaire survey of students' perceptions (understanding, critical thinking, learning experience as self-reported). No quantitative learning measure is reported, and there is no indication of a control group or a comparison design. Excluded at abstract stage on E5 because the abstract gives positive evidence that the outcome is perception-only.

quote: The materials were created using generative AI, evaluated in terms of design-based research and positively received in the two evaluation rounds
rationale: The abstract says generative AI was used to create teaching materials (a teacher/developer-side use), not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity, so E1 applies first. The evaluation rounds focus on learners' content grasp and perceived potential, with design-based research, and no control group or quantitative comparison is described, which also points against E3/E5/E6. Exclusion rests on E1 as the first applicable code.

quote: Teaching practices verify that generative AI can significantly improve the efficiency of resource development, the accuracy of personalized tutoring and the effectiveness of teaching evaluation.
rationale: The abstract describes a curriculum reform design and "teaching practices" without any description of a control group or comparison condition. The abstract gives no indication of a separate non-generative-AI control group, so the comparison criterion appears unmet. Exclusion is based on this positive absence of a comparison group; the abstract does not describe a comparison design, and the claimed improvements are not supported by any reported control-group contrast. Other criteria (design, outcome statistics) cannot be assessed from the abstract.

quote: A survey was developed based on prior studies, and data were gathered from 517 undergraduate nursing students
rationale: The study is a survey-based, cross-sectional analysis using SmartPLS (structural equation modeling) of self-reported perceptions. It has no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; student performance is self-reported perception. Nursing is also a health profession, which falls outside the STEM domain. Exclusion code is the first applicable in order: E1 cannot be confirmed as the abstract does not clearly describe a learner-facing generative AI intervention, but the design is clearly non-empirical-experimental. Given the protocol order, I'm applying E6 as the study is a survey (not an empirical trial meeting design criteria) — the core failure is that it is a non-experimental survey study.

Content is reflective writing on professional identity in medicine (health professions education), which the protocol excludes as non-STEM. Also, the study compares two feedback sources rated by students on Likert surveys within the same participants, with no separate control group without generative AI, and the outcome is student perceptions rather than a quantitative learning measure. Under the rule of reporting the first applicable code in order, E2 applies first. Abstract-stage evidence for the domain exclusion is positive: the abstract describes medical curriculum reflections on professional identity.

quote: The scores of ChatGPT and the students from the same exams were analyzed using statistical methods.
rationale: The study compares ChatGPT's exam scores against past students' scores on the same exams. ChatGPT was not used by learners as part of a learning activity; it answered exam questions evaluated by lecturers. There is no separate control group of learners without generative AI, and the design is a comparison of AI output with student scores rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison. This is an E3 failure on the comparison/design criteria, and the first applicable code in order is E1 only if intervention fails first. Learner-facing use is absent, so E1 would apply first in strict code order. Excluding at the abstract stage on positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing and there is no control group.

quote: This speculative study investigates how epistemological assumptions manifest in generative AI platforms when responding to ideologically charged questions
rationale: The record is a critical discourse analysis of unedited responses from five generative AI models to DEI prompts. It has no learners, no learning intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study in the protocol sense (it is a speculative discourse analysis), so E6 applies. Domain is also not STEM. Abstract gives positive evidence of failing several criteria; E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order that is clearly met, with E1 and E2 arguably also applicable but the study is not an empirical learning study.

quote: New media marketing occupies an important position in enterprise marketing strategies
rationale: The course content is new media marketing, a business/marketing subject rather than science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, or data science. This fails the STEM domain criterion, so E2 applies. The abstract also gives no clear controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome, though the domain failure is sufficient for exclusion.

quote: A descriptive-correlational research design was employed among 365 Grade 12 students
rationale: The study is a descriptive-correlational survey with no control group, and it measures awareness and self-reported competency rather than a quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of a failed comparison and design criterion is present, so exclude at the abstract stage. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI); E5 would also apply but E3 comes first.

quote: We developed a configurable prototype of a generative artificial intelligence powered tutoring tool, implemented it in an undergraduate electrical engineering laboratory course, and analysed 208 student–tutoring tool interactions using a mixed-methods approach
rationale: The abstract describes a single-implementation study analysing student-tool interactions with research team evaluation and learner feedback. It gives no indication of a control group without generative AI, and no learning outcome is reported (only prompt types and ratings). Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is present, so exclude under E3. Note the abstract also lacks any quantitative learning outcome, so E5 could also apply, but E3 is the first applicable code in the stated order.

quote: The research combines a literature review with empirical findings from a survey conducted among 260 students.
rationale: The study is a survey of 260 students about ChatGPT use, perceptions and attitudes. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and is not an experimental design. Survey-only designs and perception outcomes fail the eligibility criteria. The exclusion code is E6 (not an empirical study is the closest code available, though the study is empirical; the primary failure is the absence of a comparison and learning outcome, which would more precisely be E3 and E5). Given the rule to report the first applicable code in order, E3 (no control group) comes before E5 and E6 in the list, so the correct code is E3.

quote: this paper suggests employing library consultation methods focused on general AI literacy instruction
rationale: The abstract describes a discussion/conceptual paper that "draws on existing literature" and "suggests" consultation methods. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Under the abstract-stage rule this is positive evidence of failure, so exclusion is warranted.

criteria.intervention_note: LLM-generated segmentation in programming interface for learners
criteria.population_note: 20 sighted blindfolded participants; not clearly students

quote: An experimental study was conducted with 20 sighted participants blindfolded to simulate non-visual interaction. Participants completed programming tasks using two systems: one with LLM-generated segmentation and one without.
rationale: Abstract describes an LLM-based intervention used by learners in programming tasks, with a comparison system lacking LLM segmentation (a plausible control without generative AI), and task success and completion time outcomes that are quantitative. Population (sighted blindfolded adults, not clearly students), design (experimental, randomization unknown) and whether the outcome qualifies as learning are not clear from the abstract. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so advance to full text.

quote: Using a qualitative descriptive case study, we posed ten open-ended items
rationale: The study is a qualitative descriptive case study evaluating chatbot outputs on problems, with no learner-facing intervention and no control group or learning outcome measured on students. It is not an empirical comparison study of learning. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code given that it is a qualitative descriptive case study; E3 (no control group) and E5 (no learning outcome) would also apply. The abstract gives positive evidence of a qualitative case study design, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: This structured narrative review reconceptualizes mathematical operation competence for the generative AI era by synthesizing 44 English-language sources
rationale: The record is a structured narrative review synthesizing 44 sources, not an empirical study. It has no control-group comparison or quantitative learning outcome from its own data. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Note that the protocol's E10 also covers reviews, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order for an empirical-design failure, and the review is not an empirical study.

quote: This paper aims to evaluate the knowledge, usage, and attitudes of a sample of English teachers from Turkey and Lebanon regarding GAI tools in their teaching.
rationale: The study is a survey of English teachers' knowledge, usage and attitudes. It has no learner-facing GAI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and it is a survey (non-experimental) design. Language teaching is also non-STEM, and the population is in-service teachers. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI), since teachers are the users of the tools. Under the protocol order, E1 would be reported first; I'm noting the most applicable code here. Correction: the first code in protocol order that clearly applies is E1, so the code should be E1 rather than E6.

The record has only a title, venue, and year; no abstract is indexed. The title indicates ChatGPT use for programming learning (intervention and domain plausibly met), but the control group, study design, population level, and quantitative outcome cannot be judged from the title alone. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is held for full-text review rather than excluded.

Abstract describes a survey-based correlational study (PLS-SEM and fsQCA) of students' ethical evaluations and intention to use GenAI. There is no learning intervention with a control group and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions/intentions. Exclusion is on design and outcome grounds. Under the protocol's code order, the first applicable code is E3 for no control group, but the study is correlational/survey rather than an experiment; E6 (not an empirical study) is not accurate either since it is empirical. Given the order E1 to E10, the most applicable code for the absence of a comparison group is E3, so the exclusion code is adjusted accordingly below.

quote: This scoping review was conducted using Arksey and O'Malley's (2005) framework and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines.
rationale: The record is a scoping review, which is a review rather than an empirical study, so it fails E6. It also is not a primary study with a control group. Although the review is about GenAI in undergraduate nursing (paediatric content, which is not clearly STEM), the review design alone is sufficient for exclusion.

quote: This study presents an integrative theoretical approach referred to as Hybrid Epistemic Governance (HEG)
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical framework paper with no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Because the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design, it is excluded here rather than advanced.

quote: This study utilized a systematic literature review method to synthesize existing literature concerning the emerging trends and critical issues regarding the utilization of ChatGPT in Mathematics Education.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It has no control group or quantitative learning outcome. Review articles are also ineligible under the publication-type rule, but E6 is the first applicable code in order and the review design is the primary basis.

The abstract describes a conceptual/review-style analysis of GenAI in marketing education ("This article examines the role...", "We then assess the practical applications..."). It reports no experiment, comparison group, or quantitative learning outcome. Marketing is also not clearly within the protocol's STEM domain. Positive evidence that the study is not empirical supports E6 as the first applicable code in order (E1 through E5 cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone, but E6 is clearly indicated).

criteria.quote: Using a qualitative approach, the study collected data through interviews, observations, and analysis of student-created artifacts.
criteria.rationale: Abstract describes a qualitative study of a four-week GenAI pilot program with no separate control group; design is qualitative and no comparison group is evident. Exclusion E3 (no control group without generative AI) applies. Domain is also unclear (non-technical students, AI literacy), but the first applicable code in order is E1-E2 checks... intervention appears learner-facing GenAI so E1 does not apply; E2 is not clearly positive either, so E3 is the earliest clear failure given the design evidence.

quote: Using a qualitative approach, the study collected data through interviews, observations, and analysis of student-created artifacts.
rationale: Qualitative pilot study with no control group; positive evidence of no comparison group and qualitative design. Excluded under E3. Content is AI literacy for non-technical students, so STEM status is also doubtful, but E3 is the clearest failure. Not an empirical comparison design.

quote: The study employed a qualitative research design with a phenomenological approach to capture students lived experiences in using ChatGPT during chemistry learning.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative phenomenological study using open-ended questionnaires with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of failure on comparison, design, and outcome criteria is present. Code E3 is the first applicable code in order (no control group without generative AI), since the design check fails at the comparison level before outcome is considered.

quote: In this paper, I conducted an autoethnographic study by examining my experience as a teacher-researcher integrating generative AI tools
rationale: The record is an autoethnographic reflection by the teacher-researcher, not an empirical comparative study. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Game design education is also not clearly STEM. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code, since the design is a reflective autoethnography rather than an experiment.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on clear positive evidence of a non-empirical design.

quote: this position paper proposes a teacher competency framework that includes three intersecting components
rationale: The record is a position paper proposing a conceptual teacher competency framework for university educators. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no learning outcome. Population is in-service university teachers, not students. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first applicable code in the stated order after E1/E2 which are unclear from the abstract.

decision_note: Descriptive single-group study with no control group.
quote: This descriptive study aimed to explore the potential expansion and educational implications of applying generative artificial intelligence (AI) in nursing education
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive study of satisfaction among students who all experienced generative AI-integrated education. There is no separate control group without generative AI, and the outcome is learning satisfaction (perception), not a quantitative learning measure. Domain is women's health nursing, which is not STEM. Positive evidence of E3 (no control group) is present, so exclude at abstract stage with the first applicable code E3 in the protocol's order. Note: E2 (non-STEM) would be an earlier code in order; nursing is a health professions field and the protocol excludes health professions education, so the domain criterion also fails.

The study concerns a "Specialized Sources and References" course for library and information science students, which is not a STEM domain under the protocol. The abstract also describes a control group that used traditional sources, and it reports questionnaire results before and after. Because the content is non-STEM, the first applicable code is E2. The design (pre-post questionnaire with a control group) and the outcome (questionnaire-based skill measures) are unclear from the abstract, but they do not need to be resolved for this exclusion.

quote: This article explores teachers' perceptions of integrating ChatGPT in Nepalese classrooms. Using a qualitative research design
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of teachers' perceptions. It is not an empirical comparison with a control group, has no quantitative learning outcome, and participants are in-service teachers and teacher educators rather than students. It fails on design, comparison, and outcome, and is not an eligible empirical design. E6 is used as the code because the record is a qualitative perception study, which is not an eligible empirical design. Under the first-applicable rule, E1 through E5 are not assigned here: the abstract gives no clear evidence of the intervention being non-generative or non-learner-facing, so E1 is not applied; E4 is not applied because the abstract's population is teachers and no student population is positively shown; and E3 and E5 are not stated as definitive from the abstract alone, but the qualitative design is decisive.

quote: In this article, we draw on our experiences as a professor and a first-year graduate student in animal science, along with existing evidence, to explore the challenges and opportunities AI presents.
rationale: The record is a perspective/opinion article that draws on the authors' experiences and existing literature. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order that can be assessed from the abstract. Animal science is also not clearly within the protocol's STEM domain, but E6 is decisive.

quote: The paraphrase-MiniLM-L6-v2 language model was used to compare vacancies compiled in the framework of this study.
rationale: The LLM is used by researchers to analyze job vacancy texts and compare them with a student survey, not as a learner-facing tool within a learning activity. There is no control group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no learning outcome measured. Excluded at E1 as the first applicable code, since the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

quote: This qualitative phenomenological study examines adult learners’ awareness, perceptions, trust, and perceived barriers related to the use of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in adult education.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative phenomenological study with semi-structured interviews of eight adult learners. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and reports perceptions only. It is not an empirical quantitative study meeting the design requirements. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense; qualitative design excluded under Design). Note that E6 is the closest code given the protocol's listing; the design failure is clear from the abstract.

quote: This paper reframes agentic generative AI adoption as an educational design problem and proposes an education-focused framework for training federal employees.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/framework paper that proposes a competency model, curriculum blueprint, and evaluation plan. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. The population is federal workforce adult learners, not K-12 or higher education students (E4 also applies), but the first applicable code in order is E6, as the paper is not an empirical study. Non-empirical design is the earliest failing criterion in the ordered list.

quote: The results indicate that the perceived reduction of mathematics anxiety is strongly associated with the academic support provided by the AI assistant
rationale: The outcome is perceived reduction of mathematics anxiety, an affective measure, and the protocol excludes affective outcomes. No quantitative learning outcome (achievement, knowledge, problem solving, or skill) is described. The abstract gives positive evidence of a failed outcome criterion, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified. Intervention (DAK assistant) and population (primary teacher education, STEM-related didactics of arithmetic) are plausibly met, and no control group is described, but the outcome failure alone is sufficient.

criteria.rationale_note: Qualitative descriptive case study with interviews and observation; no control group or quantitative learning outcome.

quote: This study employed a descriptive qualitative case-study design involving 21 informants
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive qualitative case study using interviews, observation, and documentation, with perceived outcomes only. There is no comparison group and no quantitative learning measure. Per the ordering of codes, E1 (intervention) is not clearly failed since AI tools like ChatGPT are learner-facing, and E2 is unclear, but the study is not empirical in the protocol's sense of a comparative quantitative design; E6 is the most applicable code given it is a qualitative case study. Exclusion is based on design and outcome failing clearly on the abstract.

Abstract describes a cross-sectional questionnaire study analysed with PLS-SEM (correlational/survey design), with no separate control group that avoids generative AI and no experimental comparison. Positive evidence of failed comparison and design criteria is present, so exclusion is warranted. Coded E3 as the first failing criterion for a control-group comparison; the design is also survey-based (not an experiment), so the record would fail at the design step as well. Domain (information science/library science) is also not clearly STEM.

criteria.quote: A pilot program was performed with third- and fourth-year dental students and post-graduate endodontic students.
criteria.rationale: Description of a pilot program with feedback from students and faculty; no control group and no quantitative learning outcome reported. Reports perceptions only. Dental endodontics is also a health-professions context, which would fail the domain criterion. Exclusion is on E6 as the design is a descriptive pilot/perception report and not a comparative empirical study; the abstract gives no control group (E3) or learning measure (E5) by its own description, but the first applicable code in order would be E3 given no comparison group. Using E3 as the first failing criterion reported by the abstract.

quote: A pilot program was performed with third- and fourth-year dental students and post-graduate endodontic students.
These include generative artificial intelligence, which is becoming an important learning tool, integrating virtual and real learning spaces.
rationale: The abstract is a general discussion of trends in higher education under AI. It describes no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it does not appear to be an empirical study. The exclusion is based on positive evidence that the record is a non-empirical discussion piece, not on missing information. No STEM content is mentioned.

quote: The analysis contrasts responses generated by ChatGPT and those added by humans, focusing on the interactants’ attitude, deployment of interpersonal metaphors and evaluations of entities
rationale: The study is a discourse analysis (Appraisal theory) of ChatGPT responses versus human Reddit responses on Australian cultural topics. It is not an empirical learning study: there is no learner intervention, no control group, no STEM content, and no quantitative learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) would be arguable, but the clearest failure is that it is a non-empirical linguistic analysis, so E6 is assigned. Abstract-stage exclusion is supported by positive evidence of a text-analysis design with no outcome measure.

quote: We study how LLM technology is used for pedagogical content creation by a sample of 25 participants in a doctoral-level Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Education course
rationale: The abstract describes a single sample of 25 doctoral students all using an LLM for content creation, with exploration/exploitation behaviour and survey measures. It gives no separate control group without generative AI, and no learning outcome is reported (behavioural and survey measures only). Positive evidence of a missing comparison group supports exclusion under E3. The domain is also unclear (AI in Education course, not clearly STEM content). Exclusion is based on the missing comparison group, which is clear from the abstract.

criteria.comparison_note: LLM used for grading answers, not learner-facing interaction

quote: we conducted two experiments to evaluate the use of large language models (LLM) for grading particularly challenging student answers
rationale: The LLMs are used to grade student open-response answers (and then feed a BKT mastery model), not as a tool learners interact with during a learning activity. AI used only for grading fails the intervention criterion, so E1 applies. Other criteria (control group, outcome, design) cannot be assessed from the abstract, but E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: In this article, we present five activities that we hope motivate other practitioners to create and implement activities that can prevent the development of math anxiety in elementary school kids.
rationale: The abstract describes a practitioner article presenting five activities. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is a non-empirical article (E6). Generative AI use by learners is also not described; AI appears only as a teacher tool for creating experiences. Excluding at E6 as the first applicable code in order is reasonable, though E1 could also apply since AI seems teacher-facing.

quote: The study compared two conditions: students solving problems in DaTu with AI assistance (N=45) and those without AI assistance (N=44).
rationale: Abstract describes a data science programming context with a comparison group without AI assistance, which meets comparison and domain. The AI tool is described only as "AI assistance" and is linked to ChatGPT-type generative tools in the background, so generative status is unclear. The main reported outcome is hint-seeking behavior (a usage measure), and it is not clear whether any quantitative learning outcome (e.g., performance) was collected. Design (randomized or quasi-experimental) and population (students vs. other) are not stated. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record advances to full text.

quote: They were randomly assigned to the experimental group ( n = 31) using PA‐GPT or the control group ( n = 30) using traditional ChatGPT.
rationale: Abstract stage. Randomised controlled trial with 61 first-year engineering students. Experimental group uses PA-GPT (ChatGPT-based generative AI as virtual peer) and control uses traditional ChatGPT. The control is a generative AI condition, so it does not clearly satisfy the protocol's requirement for a comparison group without generative AI. This is a positive indication of a comparison failure, but the abstract does not make clear whether the control is a no-generative-AI condition (it is described as using ChatGPT), so the comparison is not conclusively failed. Quantitative pre/post outcomes (knowledge, HOTS, S-STEM attitudes) are reported in an engineering/networking course. Data sufficiency, language and publication type are not visible in the abstract. Per rule 2, I am not excluding on the abstract; the full text should verify whether the control arm used generative AI (in which case E3 applies).

quote: Teaching practice has shown that integrating AIGC into the teaching reform of Python programming courses has not only achieved good teaching results but also received positive feedback from students
rationale: Abstract describes a generative AI (AIGC/ChatGPT) teaching reform in a higher-education Python programming course, which fits intervention, population and domain. However, the abstract does not mention a control group, a comparison design, or any quantitative learning measure; "good teaching results" and "positive feedback" are vague and the latter is perception-only. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is kept as unsure for full-text review of design, comparison and outcome.

quote: This study proposes a hybrid conceptual framework for AI chatbots that integrates lightweight Natural Language Processing (NLP) models with human oversight, designed specifically for African universities.
rationale: The paper proposes a conceptual framework for a student-support chatbot developed via mixed methods, case studies, interviews and simulations. It reports projected accuracy and simulated workload reduction, not a learning outcome measured in a comparison design. No control group or quantitative learning outcome is evident, and the domain is student support rather than STEM content. Exclusion uses E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) as the first clear failure; the design is also not an experimental or quasi-experimental study. Some abstract-stage ambiguity remains, but the positive evidence of a non-learning outcome and non-experimental design is sufficient to exclude.

quote: This conceptual article further develops a validity-centred account of this disruption
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual article that proposes a reasoning sequence and a Validity Reasoning Matrix. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study. Exclusion code E6 applies. Under the abstract-stage rule this is positive evidence of a failed criterion, so exclusion is appropriate.

quote: A quasi-experimental study ( N = 195 ninth-grade German students, mean age = 14.33 years) conducted in mathematics classes compared the AI chatbot with traditional printed help cards on the Heron method.
rationale: Abstract indicates a generative AI chatbot (ADA, a female-coded AI chatbot) used by ninth-grade students in mathematics, compared against printed help cards (a non-AI control), in a quasi-experimental design. Academic performance is measured, which is a quantitative learning outcome. Whether ADA is generative (LLM) is not stated in the abstract, and SMD data availability cannot be judged from the abstract. No positive evidence of exclusion, so include at abstract stage; verify generative nature and outcome statistics at full text.

quote: A blind evaluator scored 64 responses (three RAG variants and one non-RAG).
rationale: Abstract describes LLM-generated feedback on statistics short answers (STEM domain met). However, the study appears to compare RAG variants against a non-RAG LLM output, not a control group without generative AI, and it is unclear whether learners interact with the tool or whether any learning outcome is measured (the outcome is explanation quality scored by an evaluator). Population (students) and whether the design is a comparison of learner outcomes are also unclear. Abstract does not give positive evidence of a failing criterion, but the comparison criterion looks likely to fail, so this is flagged for full-text review rather than included outright.

quote: Twenty-eight second- and third-year classes from six universities in Uzbekistan were assigned within nine teacher blocks by deterministic constrained minimization to GenAI (14 classes) or structured active-control (14 classes) groups.
rationale: Abstract indicates a controlled trial with a GenAI-assisted arm versus a structured active-control arm using a version-controlled curated alternative (non-generative). Learners are higher-education students in agricultural engineering, with an engineering problem-solving outcome (immediate and delayed scores), 2026 publication. Intervention, comparison, design, population, domain and outcome all appear to be met at abstract stage. Effect sizes (d and CIs) are reported, so data sufficiency appears adequate. Publication type and full-text language cannot be confirmed from the abstract, but there is no positive evidence of failure, so the record is included for full-text review. Note: the control arm is a non-AI curated alternative, which fits the comparison criterion as a non-generative tool.

quote: A total of 60 studies were analyzed, covering various domains.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review of 60 studies, not an empirical study with a control group. Review articles are not eligible as empirical designs (E6). Because the review is not an original experiment, no comparison group or learner-facing intervention is reported. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of review design.

quote: The method employed in this research is a literature review approach, where various relevant studies are analyzed
rationale: The abstract states the study is a literature review, which is not an empirical study. No primary experimental design or control group is described. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Note that the protocol excludes reviews, so this also conflicts with publication-type eligibility, but E6 applies as the first code in order that fits.

criteria.criteria_note: EFL teachers, survey of GenAI literacy

quote: this quantitative study examined the GenAI literacy level of English as a foreign language (EFL) teachers who worked in low-resource schools in Turkey
rationale: The study is a questionnaire survey of EFL teachers' GenAI literacy. The content is language learning (non-STEM), the participants are in-service teachers rather than students, there is no control group, and there is no learning outcome from a learner-facing intervention. E2 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order; E1 (learner-facing intervention) and E4 (in-service teachers) also apply, but E2 is listed first in the sequence the task specifies. Note the protocol's order lists E1 first, so E1 would be the strictly first code applicable; at abstract stage the intervention is not described as learner-facing either, but no intervention is described at all.

quote: Moroccan EFL teachers implement prompt engineering to design lesson plans using Large Language Models (LLMs)
rationale: Participants are in-service EFL teachers designing lesson plans, not K-12 or higher education students (E4). The domain is English language learning, which is non-STEM (E2 would also apply), and the design is a survey/focus-group mixed-methods study with no control group or quantitative learning outcome. E4 is the first applicable code in protocol order, so it is reported. Population is the clearest positive failure in the abstract.
rationale_note: Codes are applied in order E1 through E10; E1 is unclear, E2 is not checked first because E4 is listed before E2 in the protocol order only if population is checked first. Note: per the protocol list order, E2 (content not STEM) precedes E4. Strictly, E2 applies first.

quote: Empirical results indicate that digital competence is a critical prerequisite for AI adoption, which subsequently exerts a strong positive effect on teaching performance through the full mediating role of pedagogical innovation.
rationale: The study is a survey-based SEM of 710 respondents using TAM constructs (perceptions, adoption, trust). It has no control group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome such as achievement; outcomes are perceptions and self-reported teaching performance. It fails the design/comparison and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E5 is applied as the outcome failure, though E3 (no control group) or E6 (not an empirical experiment) could also be argued; E5 is the first clearly evidenced failure in the order given, since the abstract describes perception and adoption measures only.

quote: This article explores the integration of ChatGPT into STEM education as a means to address educational disparities and enhance learning experiences.
rationale: The abstract describes ChatGPT (a generative AI) used in STEM education, which meets the intervention and domain criteria. However, the abstract reads as a conceptual or discussion article ("explores", "call to action") and gives no indication of a control group, an experimental design, or a quantitative learning outcome. Those are not positively excluded at abstract stage, so the record is passed to full text to check the design and outcome.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage unsure; the design appears conceptual, which may fail E6 at full text.

quote: The chatbot system integrates the WhatsApp Business API, a Webhook interface, and the n8n automation platform
rationale: The chatbot answers university admission questions, which is not STEM content, so it fails the domain criterion (E2). The study also reports only functional testing, accuracy, latency and satisfaction, with no control group and no learning outcome, so E3 and E5 would also apply. E2 is reported as the first applicable code in protocol order. Intervention is generative (fine-tuned GPT-4o Mini), but this does not change the domain exclusion.

Record is a semiotic content analysis of gender representation in middle school science textbooks. No learner interacts with a generative AI tool, so intervention fails (E1). There is no abstract in the index, so the title alone is the evidence; the title shows no generative AI involvement, which is positive evidence of failure. Also no control group or learning outcome is evident.

quote: A mixed-methods questionnaire inquired 345 undergraduate students about their perceptions, use patterns, needs, and desires related to GenAI
rationale: The study is a questionnaire survey of perceptions, needs, and desires. It is not an empirical experiment with a control group and reports no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's ordering, E6 (not an empirical study, in the sense of a survey/design-based descriptive study outside the eligible designs) applies first. Note the abstract also gives positive evidence of no comparison group and no learning outcome, so this is a clear exclude.

quote: study compared the effects of SCF, delivered by language teachers and ChatGPT, on L2 learning outcomes and student trust
rationale: The study teaches English article usage to L2 English learners. English language learning is explicitly excluded as non-STEM content under the Domain criterion, so the study fails E2. Other criteria appear plausibly met (ChatGPT feedback, teacher/human comparison, randomized, higher-education-like learners, post-test outcomes), but the domain failure is decisive.

quote: Five participants completed a post-use survey after hands-on interaction with TechTahi. Responses were analysed descriptively
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group exploratory pilot with five participants completing a post-use survey of perceptions only. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so the study fails the comparison, design and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E5 applies because the only outcome is perceptions, and the stated analysis is descriptive. The abstract does not state a control-group design, so the E3 code is not used.

quote: Much of my current work with educational applications of generative artificial intelligence involves schools, companies, and organizations in heavily resourced countries such as the United States a...
rationale: The visible abstract is a truncated first-person commentary about generative AI in education in the Global South, with no described experimental design, control group, or learning outcome. This reads as an editorial or commentary rather than an empirical study, so it fails the non-empirical check (E6). The abstract is truncated, so this is a provisional exclusion; the record could be re-checked if the full abstract shows an experiment. Under the abstract-stage rule, exclusion requires positive evidence, and this rests on the article type implied by the text, so an unsure decision may be more appropriate.

quote: Evaluating The Effectiveness Of A Chatgpt-Based Chatbot As A Support Tool For English Writing Instruction In Vietnamese High Schools
rationale: The study uses a ChatGPT-based chatbot with a control group, quasi-experimental design, and writing outcomes, but the content is English writing instruction, which is language learning and not STEM. Excluded under E2 as the first applicable code (E1 does not apply since the tool is learner-facing generative AI).

quote: The data were then analyzed using descriptive statistics. Based on the result, it showed a positive perception towards ChatGPT boosting vocational students' motivation
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of student perceptions using a Likert questionnaire; there is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (only perceptions). Domain is English writing (non-STEM), which also fails. Exclusion code reported is E5 as the first-applicable code in order is E2 for non-STEM content; however, under the protocol order E1 (intervention) is not clearly failed, E2 (content not STEM) applies first. Per the code order, the correct first code is E2.

criteria.pop_note: nursing students; health professions education excluded from domain
criteria.intervention_note: ChatGPT use described but no learner-facing learning activity evident

quote: Quantitative data were collected from a convenience sample of 240 students and 40 nurse educators using validated self-reported questionnaires.
rationale: The study is a mixed-methods survey of perceptions and attitudes with no separate control group and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are knowledge/perception questionnaires only. Nursing is a health professions domain, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome, only perceptions); the comparison and design also fail, and the domain is health professions education, so this is not STEM. Decision is based on the abstract's positive evidence of a survey design with perception outcomes.

quote: This review synthesizes evidence on how AI influences student engagement via adaptive scaffolding, interactive learning, and motivational frameworks
rationale: The record describes itself as a review that synthesizes evidence from other studies and meta-analyses, not an empirical study with its own control group and outcome data. It is therefore not an empirical study (E6). The abstract gives no indication of a primary randomized or quasi-experimental comparison, and it is also broad and covers several topics, so E6 is the first applicable code. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that it is a review.

quote: This theoretical work presents a conceptual framework for integrating artificial intelligence (AI) tutoring within gifted education programming.
rationale: The record is a theoretical/conceptual framework paper with no empirical study, no comparison group, and no learning outcome data. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies as the first failing criterion in code order that is clearly supported by the abstract. Domain is not STEM-specific in the abstract either.

quote: Notebook LM, Chat GPT, and open educational resources (OER) are employed as learning tools within a classroom-ready framework for teaching CAD
rationale: Generative AI tools (ChatGPT, NotebookLM) used by first-year mechanical engineering students in CAD instruction (STEM, higher education). The abstract does not state a control group, a comparative quantitative design, or a quantitative learning outcome; it reads as a descriptive framework paper. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is held for full-text review to check for a comparison group and effect statistics.

quote: This toolkit helps UNC academic unit chairs and directors lead productive, respectful, and future-focused discussions about GenAI in curriculum, pedagogy, and assessment.
rationale: placeholder

quote: This study addresses this gap by evaluating GenAI's performance against students who took the 'Criminal Law' final exam at an Australian law school in Spring 2023.
rationale: The content is criminal law, a legal subject rather than science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, or programming, so it fails the STEM domain criterion. The study also compares GenAI-generated answers with student and tutor grading rather than a learner-facing GenAI intervention with a control group, so the design and intervention fit is doubtful. Domain failure is the first applicable code in order.

criteria.outcome_note: Outcomes are perceptions (usefulness, satisfaction, intention to use) rather than learning measures
criteria.design_note: Cross-sectional rating study with no control group

quote: Using a cross-sectional design, 144 students across secondary, short-cycle higher education (CTeSP—professional higher technical courses), and undergraduate programming rated 893 response-level feedback instances
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional user-centred rating study of LLM-generated feedback with no comparison group without generative AI, so E3 applies. The outcomes are also perceptions (perceived usefulness, satisfaction, intention to use), not quantitative learning measures, which would be a further failure (E5), but E3 is the first applicable code in order. Intervention, population and STEM domain (programming) appear met.
decision_note: Exclusion based on positive abstract evidence of cross-sectional single-design rating study without control group.

quote: This article discusses the results of an experiment involving 155 submissions that carried out a code review activity of 1,658 rules.
rationale: Students use ChatGPT during a programming code review activity (generative AI, computing domain, university students), so intervention, domain and population appear met. The abstract does not state whether a control group without generative AI exists, nor whether a quantitative learning outcome with SMD-computable data was measured; the outcomes described are largely qualitative or perception-based (acceptance of issues, skepticism, phrase categories). Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is passed to full text to check the comparison, design and outcome.

quote: We adopted a qualitative thematic analysis of the interviews with 10 elementary school students and six teachers
rationale: Abstract describes a qualitative thematic analysis of perceptions, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of failing comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in order (no control group without generative AI); E5 would also apply but E3 takes precedence in the protocol's order.

quote: "a large-scale survey of 1,366 students from 24 Italian universities"
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey with cluster analysis of perceptions and usage. It reports no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical intervention study meeting the design and outcome criteria. Excluded as not an empirical study of the eligible design (E6). Positive evidence of design failure is present, so exclusion is appropriate at abstract stage. Under the protocol's first-failing-code ordering, E1 could arguably apply since no learner-facing intervention is evaluated, but the survey design is the clearest failure.

quote: The aim of the study is to build a conceptual model of the technology for developing an educational chatbot in a messenger to support the practical training of students.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual model and technology development description, with demonstration examples of dialogue rather than an empirical comparison. No control group, no comparative design, and no quantitative learning outcome are reported. Under E6 (not an empirical study) it is excluded. Domain (Russian as a foreign language, linguistics) also appears non-STEM, but the first applicable code in order is E1/E2 checks: intervention is generative (met), so E2 would apply on content grounds; E6 is the most clearly supported positive evidence of failure, so it is reported here.

quote: A mixed - method approach was used, combining a literature review, survey, and case study analysis.
rationale: The study is a literature review, survey, and case study analysis with no separate control group receiving non-generative-AI instruction, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. Outcomes are perceptions and self-reported percentages rather than a quantitative learning measure. Domain is not clearly STEM from the abstract. Code E3 is the first applicable exclusion code in order for the lack of a control group without generative AI; the study is also not an experimental design.

quote: This paper positions low‐code/no‐code (LC/NC) analytics environments as one component of a broader hybrid pedagogy
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual roadmap drawing on theory and prior literature. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion is based on positive evidence that the paper is non-empirical.

quote: The Effect of Generative AI (ChatGPT) on EFL Learners’ Academic Writing Performance
rationale: The study is a meta-analysis of generative AI effects on EFL academic writing, which is language learning and non-STEM content, so the domain criterion fails. The abstract mentions "higher/engineering education" only as a search topic, which does not make the content STEM. Also, this is a meta-analysis, not a primary study, so it is not an eligible empirical study (E6) in the protocol's sense. Under the protocol's exclusion order, E2 applies first because the domain failure is the clearest positive evidence.

quote: A questionnaire survey was administered to 401 students from six universities representing different regions and institutional tiers in China.
rationale: The study is a questionnaire survey of learning motivation and perceptions, which is a survey design with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is also in foreign language learning, which is non-STEM. Positive evidence fails on several criteria; E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of an eligible comparative design) is the first applicable code given the survey-only design, though E2 (non-STEM content) also applies. Under the order rule, E2 is checked before E3, E5, and E6, so the first applicable code should be E2 for non-STEM content.

quote: Using secondary survey data from higher-education participants (N = 751), a three-item behavioral intention composite and a 0–7 usage-frequency index were analyzed
rationale: The study is a correlational survey analysis of self-reported intention and usage frequency, with no control group receiving or not receiving generative AI and no learning outcome measured. Design and outcome criteria are clearly not met; the exclusion code applied is E3 (no control group) as the first applicable code in order, though E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) and E6 (not an empirical study design fitting the protocol) would also apply. Domain (STEM) is not stated in the abstract.

quote: This paper, therefore, is positioned as a user-centric and jargon-free review for all learners and practitioners who are curious about LLMs or intend to use them.
rationale: The record is a narrative user-perspective survey/review of LLM applications, not an empirical study. It reports no controlled comparison group, no design eligible for the protocol, and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion codes, E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code. The abstract gives positive evidence of a review format, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: This article advances a functional alignment framework proposing that generative artificial intelligence's processing patterns may align with the cognitive characteristics of some gifted and twice-exceptional learners.
rationale: The record is a theoretical article. The abstract explicitly states the framework is "explicitly theoretical, advancing propositions rather than demonstrated effects," so it is not an empirical study. No control group or quantitative learning outcome is reported. E6 applies as the first failing criterion in code order that is clearly supported.

quote: The study included a sample of 20 primary school teachers.
rationale: Participants are in-service primary school teachers, not K-12 or higher education students, so the population criterion fails (E4). Presentation design skills for teachers are also not clearly STEM content. The abstract gives no separate control group that avoids generative AI, so comparison is unclear. E4 is the first applicable code in order given the positive evidence on population.

quote: This study uses a survey method to collect data from students of the computer systems study program of the University of Panca Budi Development.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey study of student perceptions of ChatGPT use. It is not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a control group, and it reports only perceptions rather than a quantitative learning outcome. Excluded on E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible design); the survey design fails the Design criterion and the outcome criterion fails as well. Survey designs are explicitly excluded by the protocol, so E6 is the best fit for the first applicable code given the non-experimental, perception-only design.

quote: The sample of this study includes (N=43) education bachelor's students of the Higher School of Teachers – Moulay Ismail University, whose ratings were measured before and after the researchers' intervention.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pretest-posttest design (N=43, same students measured before and after the intervention) with no separate control group without generative AI. Per the protocol and borderline-case rule, one group measured before and after is E3. Outcome is output-quality ratings and satisfaction, which may not be a learning measure, and the domain is not clearly STEM, but E3 applies first.

quote: This study aimed to investigate pre-service teachers’ acceptance and use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen AI) in learning and to compare levels of acceptance and use between male and female pre-service teachers.
rationale: The study is a UTAUT2 survey measuring acceptance and use perceptions, with a gender comparison of mean scores. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design with a control group (E3 would also apply), and no quantitative learning outcome is measured (E5). Perception and usage measures are explicitly excluded by the protocol. Under the exclusion-code ordering, E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract, so E5 is the first clearly applicable code after E3/E4 checks; the design failure is also evident. Population (pre-service teachers, higher education) is met.
rationale_note: Exclusion code chosen: E5 (no learning outcome; survey of acceptance perceptions). Design is a cross-sectional survey, which also fails the Design criterion.

quote: The study was conducted in a single vocational higher education institution
rationale: Abstract describes a single cohort of 50 students in ten project teams with no control or comparison group; assessment is competency rubrics and project documentation, with no described comparison condition. Positive evidence of no control group, so E3 applies. Exclusion is at abstract stage based on the absence of any comparison group described; the mixed-methods, project-based design does not indicate a controlled comparison.

quote: A semester-long study was conducted at UniDistance Suisse, where an AI tutor app was provided to psychology students taking a neuroscience course (N=51).
rationale: Abstract describes an AI tutor using GPT-3-generated microlearning questions, with students as learners (higher education, neuroscience content, grades as outcome). It mentions comparison to a parallel course without the AI tutor, which suggests a control group, but the abstract also calls the study a "case study" and does not clearly state the design or whether allocation was randomized or a quasi-experimental comparison. Also, neuroscience is arguably not a STEM domain as defined by the protocol (science is included, so likely met). Unclear on design and comparison at abstract stage; send to full text.

criteria.outcome_note: no quantitative learning outcome evident; ratings of task-design quality are not clearly a learning measure

quote: Participants received two rounds of feedback in different sequences: AI followed by peer feedback or peer feedback followed by AI.
rationale: Abstract describes a sequence-comparison design where both arms receive AI feedback (AI then peer vs peer then AI), so there is no control group without generative AI (E3). Also, outcomes are descriptive task-design ratings and engagement, with no clear quantitative learning outcome, and the design is described as exploratory mixed-methods with descriptive comparisons. Exclusion on E3 is positive evidence from the abstract, and it is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Using a phenomenological qualitative design, the study involved 17 female students.
rationale: The study is a phenomenological qualitative design with a single group of 17 students and no control group, so there is positive evidence that the comparison and design criteria fail. Under the rule that the first applicable code is reported, E3 (no control group without generative AI) applies. Intervention (AI-generated videos for high school physics), domain (physics), and population (high school students) appear met. Outcomes are mainly perceptions and qualitative findings, but this is not the deciding factor.

quote: A qualitative approach was employed using a case study design to provide thick descriptions of Pathways from ChatGPT 4.0 and Llama3.1
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative case study with five teachers and content analysis and interviews. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and is not an experimental design. It is not an empirical study that meets the protocol's design criteria, so it is excluded under E6. Exclusion is justified on positive evidence at the abstract stage.

quote: This paper, supported by a comprehensive literature review spanning cognitive psychology, educational psychology, instructional design, computer science education, and sociocultural theory
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual paper supported by a literature review and proposes a model ("This paper proposes prompt engineering as a key component..."). No empirical study, control group, or quantitative learning outcome is reported, so it is not an empirical study. Exclude under E6 (first applicable code in this case, as E1 is arguably met since ChatGPT is learner-facing, and E3/E5 also apply on the same evidence).

quote: This conceptual paper examines Large Language Model (LLM) literacy as a dimension of digital inclusion in lifelong English learning among older adults
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual paper proposing a framework and explicitly calls for future empirical validation, so it is not an empirical study. It also concerns English language learning, which is non-STEM, and reports no comparison group or quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E6 applies as the first failing criterion in the ordering that is clearly supported (E1 and E2 are not reliably determinable as the first in order, but E6 is the decisive positive evidence).
rationale_note: Note: E2 (non-STEM content, English learning) is arguably earlier in code order than E6 and also clearly applies; per the order rule the first applicable code should be E2. See correction below.

quote: This study observed how mathematics teachers interacted with Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) while planning primary school geometry lessons
rationale: Participants are in-service mathematics teachers planning lessons with GenAI, not K-12 or higher education students learning STEM content; the study is also a mixed-methods observational design with no control group and no learner-facing AI use. Excluded under E4 as the first applicable code in the order given (E1 is arguably also relevant since GenAI is used by teachers for lesson planning, but the population failure is the clearest positive evidence). Abstract gives positive evidence of population failure.

quote: The purpose of the study is to develop and substantiate a conceptual model of generating pedagogical feedback to student program code based on large language models
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual model and architecture proposal, not an empirical study. No experimental or comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Its status as a conceptual paper is shown by the abstract's own description of its purpose and method.

quote: This study examines the impact of an inquiry-based English reading program using ChatGPT on elementary learners' reading proficiency and perceptions.
rationale: The content is English reading (language learning), which is non-STEM, so E2 applies. Other criteria (control group, design, data) are not clearly reported in the abstract, but the domain failure is sufficient for exclusion under the protocol's first-applicable-code order.

quote: This conceptual article critically examines the evolving professional identity of management educators in a Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen AI)-driven learning environment.
rationale: The record is a conceptual article, not an empirical study. It has no learners as participants (management educators are the subject), no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. E6 applies as the first failing code in the order given (E1 is ambiguous, but E6 is the clear failure).

quote: Through a descriptive-correlative study applied to a sample of 2,424 students
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive-correlative study with a survey-style sample of students and reports associations, not a randomized or quasi-experimental design with a control group that does not use generative AI. There is no evidence of a separate comparison group, so the study fails the comparison and design criteria (E3). Domain is also unclear, since the tools span art, music, and programming. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of no control group.

quote: We conducted an experimental study where ChatGPT was prompted in response to common student questions and misconceptions from a first-year programming course.
rationale: Abstract describes evaluation of ChatGPT responses by faculty via survey and student perception survey. No separate control group without generative AI is described, and outcomes are accuracy ratings and perceptions rather than a quantitative learning measure. Positive evidence of missing comparison group supports E3 at abstract stage. Exclusion is based on the abstract alone; the full text could still clarify the design.

quote: Using a quasi-experimental design (n≈200 across 4 schools; 12 weeks), the study compares an AI-integrated curriculum with conventional instruction
rationale:
The outcomes are reading literacy, numeracy, and AI literacy for primary students. Reading and general literacy content is not STEM under the protocol. Mathematics is part of the outcome, but the study's primary focus is reading and AI literacy, so the domain is not met. Excluded at E2 as the first applicable code in order. The design is a quasi-experiment with a conventional comparison group, which fits the protocol. The abstract reports only anticipated outcomes, so it is unclear whether any measured quantitative data are reported.</rationale>

quote: students interacted with the Doubao AI assistant to generate Python -based analytical workflows
rationale: Abstract describes a generative LLM (Doubao) used by students in a chemical engineering lab (STEM, higher education). The abstract does not report a control group, a design, or any quantitative learning outcome, so comparison, design, and outcome cannot be judged as failing at abstract stage. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record advances to full text.

However, the abstract text provided is in Korean and is about network DoS/DDoS attacks, which does not describe the study's design, comparison group, or outcomes. The abstract is unrelated to the title and gives no positive evidence that any criterion fails. Under the abstract-stage rule, missing or contradictory information is not grounds for exclusion, so the record is held as unsure for full-text review, where the actual study design and whether a control group with outcome data exists can be checked. The record also has a mismatch between title and abstract that the full-text reviewer should verify.

quote: Semi-structured, in-depth interviews were conducted with eleven community college students in Southern California and analyzed through a hybrid inductive–deductive coding strategy
rationale: Hermeneutic phenomenological qualitative study using interviews with 11 students. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no STEM content focus. Under the rule that exclusion requires positive evidence, the abstract clearly shows a qualitative, non-empirical-quantitative design. E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in the protocol order that fits; E3 and E5 would also fail, but the design is qualitative, so E6 is assigned as the primary code.

quote: The study is exploratory and based on AI-generated content; therefore, the findings do not constitute an empirical evaluation of the effectiveness of the proposed teaching methods.
rationale: The study is a qualitative content analysis of ChatGPT-generated teaching recommendations, not an empirical study of learners. It has no comparison group, no learner interaction with generative AI as part of a learning activity, and no quantitative learning outcome. The stated limitation explicitly says it is not an empirical evaluation of effectiveness. E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in order; E1 could arguably also apply since learners do not interact with the tool, but E6 is the most direct fit at abstract stage.
decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: The empirical basis of the study is formed by data collected from instructors involved in Executive Education programs at leading Peruvian universities
rationale: This is a survey of instructors' intention to adopt generative AI, not an experiment with learners. Participants are in-service instructors (excluded population), the design is a correlational online survey, and there is no learner-facing generative AI intervention, control group, or quantitative learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), which is the most accurate code since the AI is not used by learners in a learning activity. Note: the ordering rule means E1 should be reported first; I correct this below in the decision note.

criteria.rationale_note: Abstract describes system architecture and proposed framework; no controlled evaluation reported, only conceptual comparison to platforms.

quote: This paper describes the system architecture, pedagogical foundations, requirement analysis, and proposed solution framework.
rationale: The paper is a system design and proposal without an empirical evaluation. The abstract states it describes architecture and a proposed framework, and the evaluation is only a conceptual comparison with existing platforms. No control group or quantitative learning outcome is reported, so it is not an empirical study. Exclusion code E6 applies. Note that E6 is the first applicable code in the order given only on the basis of design; E3 and E5 also would fail on the abstract evidence.

quote: Both AI tutors were tested on each scenario once giving a total of 100 dialog interactions.
rationale: Abstract describes a black-box comparison of ChatGPT and Gemini on 50 simulated ambiguous junior high math scenarios, each tested once by two raters on a rubric. There is no learner sample, no learner-facing learning activity, and no non-generative-AI control group. Design appears to be a rater-evaluated comparison of two generative AI tools, which would be E3 (only two generative AI variants compared) or E1 (no learners interacting). Abstract does not give clear positive evidence of failure, and the protocol says to return unsure when the abstract cannot settle it, so I am passing it to full text for confirmation.

quote: A total of 255 undergraduate and graduate students completed an adapted Emotion Regulation Questionnaire (Gross & John, 2003) tailored to GenAI-mediated English learning.
rationale: The study is a survey of emotion regulation strategies (self-report questionnaire) with no experimental control group, so no comparison or quantitative learning outcome is present. The domain is English as a foreign language, which is non-STEM. Positive evidence fails on comparison, design, domain and outcome, so it is excluded. The first applicable code in order is E1 only if intervention fails; the abstract does not show a learner-facing gen-AI intervention clearly, but the decisive and first-applicable failure under the ordering is not a generative-AI intervention issue established from the abstract. Coded E5 as the outcome is perceptions/affect rather than learning. Note: under strict code ordering, E1 or E2 could arguably apply first; E2 (non-STEM content, English learning) is the clearest positive failure and would take precedence over E5.

quote: This systematic review paper focuses on the applications of AI in academia – specifically chemistry education.
rationale: The record is a systematic review and critical review of 40 articles, not an empirical study with a control group and learning outcome data. It fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). Since the review does not report a primary study design, comparison group, or quantitative outcome, E6 is the first applicable code.

quote: Student survey questions focused on feedback about the AI podcasts, including their design and how helpful students felt they were for the course.
rationale: Generative AI (NotebookLM) podcasts used by undergraduate general chemistry students (STEM, higher education). However, the abstract reports only student survey feedback on perceptions and helpfulness, with no quantitative learning outcome and no mention of a control group. Positive evidence of a missing quantitative learning outcome supports exclusion under E5, since perception-only outcomes fail the outcome criterion.

quote: Paired-samples t-tests revealed statistically significant improvements in both TPACK and GAIA scores, with large effect sizes across all subdimensions.
rationale: The design is a single group of 36 pre-service mathematics teachers measured pre- and post-intervention with paired t-tests, and the abstract describes no control group. Under the protocol, one group measured before and after is E3. Other criteria (preservice teachers in a mathematics context, quantitative outcomes) are not the deciding factor here.

Abstract reports a chain-mediation model (path/SEM-style analysis with t-statistics) relating GenAI usage competence, critical thinking, AI self-efficacy and creativity. This is a correlational survey-style design, not a randomized or quasi-experiment with a comparison group, so it fails the design criterion. Coding E6 (not an empirical study with eligible design) is the closest code; the abstract gives no evidence of an experimental control group or an intervention. The abstract provides no positive evidence of a learner-facing GenAI intervention with a control group. Excluding at abstract stage is justified by the positive evidence of a correlational mediation design. Note that the protocol's design exclusion list names correlational designs, so E6 is applied as the code for a non-eligible empirical design.

quote: We evaluated the course through an end-of-term self-assessment survey across both offerings (n = 250; TOM = 156, OMAI = 94).
rationale: The study compares a generative-AI pair-programming OM course against a traditional OM course, in STEM (operations modeling, optimization, simulation) with undergraduates. However, the only outcome described is an end-of-term self-assessment survey measuring comfort and confidence, which is a perception measure rather than a quantitative learning measure. Per protocol, studies reporting only perceptions fail the outcome criterion. Excluded at E5. The record is a 2026 journal-style education article, so publication type and date are not grounds for exclusion here.

quote: Results show that the vast majority of students were in favour of the learning agreement approach both at the start and upon completion of the course.
rationale: Pilot study with pre-post surveys and student artefacts in a first-year engineering course. The abstract reports only student favourability (perceptions) and descriptive counts of group GenAI use; no quantitative learning outcome is reported, and there is no control group. No comparison group or effect statistics appear, so the design is a single-group pilot. Exclusion code E5 is applied as the first clear failure among the criteria; E3 (no control group) would also apply, but the protocol asks for the first code in order, and E3 precedes E5 in that order. Reconsidering: E3 comes before E5 in the code list, so E3 is the correct first code given no comparison group is evident.

quote: An evaluative case study design guided the investigation of ChatGPT's capabilities to aid independent learning.
rationale: The abstract describes an evaluative case study of ChatGPT's capabilities for learning programming. It reports no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome; the design is a case study, which the protocol excludes. Coded E3 (no control group without generative AI) as the first applicable code in order is E1 (not applicable, since ChatGPT is learner-facing) and E2 (not applicable, programming is STEM), so E3 is the first failing criterion that is positively evidenced by the case-study design. The E5 (no quantitative outcome) and E6 (not an empirical study in the strict sense) codes may also apply; flagging for audit.

quote: This study intended to bring AI-driven linguistic tools to support and improve content writing in English language classrooms
rationale: The study concerns English language writing in English language classrooms, which is non-STEM content (protocol excludes language learning). Exclusion E2 applies. The abstract also describes a single pre-/post-test design with surveys and interviews, with no clear control group, which would raise E3 as a secondary concern, but E2 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: This study aims to explore the perceptions of students in the Education Study Program regarding the use of AI in completing coursework.
rationale: The study is a descriptive questionnaire on student perceptions with no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; it is not an empirical comparison study meeting the protocol design criteria. Perception-only outcomes also fail the outcome criterion. Domain is not STEM (education study program). Coded E6 as a non-experimental survey/descriptive study; the first applicable code in order would be E2 (not STEM) since the content appears to be general education coursework, but E6 reflects the primary design failure. Note: per code order, E1-E4 precede E6; the abstract does not give positive evidence of E1-E4 failure with certainty, so the design-based exclusion is the clearest positive evidence.

quote: Four LLMs were assessed: ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4 (OpenAI), Claude-3 (Anthropic), and Mistral 7B (Mistral AI).
rationale: The study evaluates LLM accuracy against expert answers on dental MCQs and definitions. No learners interact with the LLMs and there is no control group without generative AI, so it is not a learner-facing intervention with a comparison. Dentistry is health professions education, which is outside the STEM domain. The population is dental residency applicants' reference material, not K-12 or higher-education students in a learning activity. Excluded on E4 as the first clearly applicable code in order of the protocol's listing; the abstract also shows no comparison group, so E3 would also apply.
