Strictly, E1 comes first in order: the LLMs are not used by learners, so E1 is the first applicable code and is the correct one to report.

quote: Hardcopies of 20 reflections (10 generated by undergraduate dental students and 10 generated by ChatGPT) were distributed to three instructors
rationale: Exclude at abstract stage on positive evidence. The study has no learner interacting with generative AI in a learning activity: instructors judged ChatGPT-generated reflections, and ChatGPT performed thematic analysis. There is no separate control group of learners, no learning outcome, and the domain is dental education (health professions), not STEM. Code E6 is used because the study is not an empirical learner intervention study, which is the first applicable code in the order given after the intervention is judged. The primary failure is arguably E1 (AI not learner-facing), so E1 may be the more accurate first-applicable code.

quote: This descriptive, mixed-methods study included 56 medical students recruited in the first semester of 2025.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive mixed-methods study of a single group of 56 medical students using a ChatGPT virtual patient, with no separate control group that avoids generative AI, so E3 applies. Outcomes are largely perceptions and self-assessment (not a quantitative learning measure), and the domain is clinical history-taking in medical education, which falls under health professions education and is not STEM. The abstract gives positive evidence of a failed comparison criterion, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified under the E3 code as the first applicable code in order.
exclusion_code_note: E3 is the first applicable code in protocol order; E2 (non-STEM, health professions) may also apply.

quote: Using perceptions of aviation students from six universities in the U.S. (n=271), a modified Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) of the constructs fit the empirical data well
rationale: The study is a survey of student perceptions (TAM constructs) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome measured after an intervention; the abstract gives positive evidence of perception-only, correlational design. Aviation content is also not clearly STEM. Excluded under E5 as the outcome is perceptions/attitudes rather than a learning measure. Design (survey, not experiment) would also fail, but E5 is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol for this record.

quote: The study employed a descriptive research design where structured survey questionnaires were used and administered to ninety (90) Secondary Education Pre-service Teachers
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive survey study of perceived impact of AI chatbots on pre-service teachers, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (only perceptions and satisfaction). Positive evidence of failure on comparison/design (no control group, survey design) and on outcome (perceptions only). Exclusion code E3 is applied as the first failing criterion in order, since no comparison group exists; E5 would also apply.

criteria.criteria_note: Survey of teacher perceptions; no learner intervention or control group

quote: This study explores Malaysian primary school English teachers' perceptions of using Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools to support pupils' speaking practice.
rationale: Exclusion chosen because the AI use described is by teachers reporting perceptions, not a learner-facing generative AI intervention; the study is a perception survey with no learner control group. Also the content is English language learning, which is non-STEM (E2 would apply but E1 comes first in the code order). No learner quantitative outcome is reported.

The abstract describes a survey of awareness and perceptions of ChatGPT among students and teachers, analysed with descriptive statistics and ANOVA. It reports no controlled comparison, no learning intervention and no quantitative learning outcome. Perception and awareness measures fall outside the protocol's outcome definition. Exclusion uses E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), the first applicable code in the order given; the design is also a survey, which would fail the design criterion. Domain is not stated in the abstract. The decision is based on positive evidence in the abstract, so it is not an unsure case.

quote: The research draws upon document and guideline examination of institutional websites, university policy catalogs, and curricular offerings regarding AI across a sample size of all public and private universities in Ohio.
rationale: The abstract describes a document and policy analysis of Ohio universities' websites and catalogs. It is not an empirical experiment with a learner-facing generative AI intervention, a control group, or a learning outcome. It is not an empirical study of learning in the sense the protocol requires, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study). No quantitative learning outcome is reported, so E5 would also apply, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order is ambiguous; E6 is reported as the primary failure.

quote: Students' perceptions were evaluated alongside skills audits, and they reported increased confidence in using GenAI.
rationale: Abstract describes a single-cohort program evaluation using student perceptions, skills audits, and interviews, with no described control group, so the design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Outcomes reported are perceptions/confidence, not a quantitative learning measure. Domain (MSc skills program, GenAI as digital competency) is not clearly STEM. Positive evidence of failure exists for design and outcome, so exclude. Coded E5 as the first clearly failing criterion in protocol order for the abstract (E1 and E2 not positively shown; E3 could apply since no comparison group is evident, but the abstract does not explicitly state absence of a control, so E5 is the most defensible code given the perception-only outcome).

quote: Student learning was assessed using a rubric, which rated students' effective integration and evaluation of GAI-generated content against peer-reviewed research articles
rationale: The abstract describes a single implementation of a GAI assignment in three online graduate courses, assessed by rubric scores and a survey of perceptions (n=32). There is no described control group without generative AI, and no comparison condition is mentioned. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is present, so exclusion under E3 applies at the abstract stage. The design appears to be a single-group descriptive study.

quote: This study employs a quasi-experimental quantitative methodology that involves two groups from different schools in the United Arab Emirates (UAE)
rationale: At abstract stage, ChatGPT use by high school students in physics (Newton's second law) with a two-group quasi-experiment and pre/post test scores. Comparison group type is not stated in the abstract, so it is not excluded on that basis. Title says "case study," but the abstract describes a quasi-experimental two-group design, which is not positive evidence of failure. Data sufficiency and full-text language/publication type are checked at full text. Include to advance.

quote: A qualitative descriptive method was used, and data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 10 undergraduate EFL students
rationale: Content is English as a foreign language reading (non-STEM), which fails the domain criterion (E2), and the study is a qualitative interview design with no control group or quantitative learning outcome. E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order. Note the protocol's code order places E2 before E3/E5/E6, so E2 is reported.

quote: The qualitative phenomenological research design focuses on the views, practices, and issues of teacher educators regarding the use of GenAI
rationale: The study is a qualitative phenomenological interview study of 10 teacher educators. It is not an empirical comparative study with a control group and has no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense, i.e., a qualitative design). Note that E6 is applied here because the design is qualitative; the protocol's design exclusion is not an explicit code, so this is the closest fit. Also, participants are in-service teacher educators and the domain is not STEM, but these were not the first applicable code by the ordering I used.

criteria.outcome_note: pre- and post-tests of academic achievement reported

quote: We evaluated the effectiveness of artificial intelligence in designing lesson plans and the potential of such tools to complement traditional teaching methods.
rationale: Abstract describes undergraduate nuclear physics students taught with ChatGPT-developed versus teacher-developed lesson plans, with a control group and pre/post tests. Domain (physics), population (undergraduates) and quantitative achievement outcome appear met. However, the abstract indicates ChatGPT was used to design lesson plans, which may mean the teacher/researcher used AI rather than learners interacting with a generative tool (possible E1). Whether students directly interact with generative AI is unclear from the abstract. Design (comparison group, randomization vs quasi-experiment) and data sufficiency also cannot be determined. Per the abstract-stage rule, unsure so the full text can resolve the intervention question.

The abstract describes a discursive article that "offers arguments and examples" about AI tutors and metacognition. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative outcome, so it does not appear to be an empirical study. Exclusion is on E6 at the abstract stage because the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design; the abstract does not mention generative AI or STEM content. Quote is null because no sentence directly states the design; the rationale rests on the abstract as a whole.

The record has only a title and venue, with no abstract. The title refers to generative AI in management education, which suggests a possible non-STEM domain (management), so E2 may apply, but the title alone does not give positive evidence of failure on any criterion. Under the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence for exclusion, so the record is held as unsure for full-text review. Design, comparison, and outcome cannot be judged from the title.

quote: The article presents the results of a survey conducted among first-year engineering students related to the use of applications and software supporting mathematics education.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey of first-year engineering students about use of math software, which is a survey (non-experimental) design with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence that the design is a survey, so it is not an empirical experiment meeting the protocol. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is applied as the design is a survey rather than an eligible empirical design; E3 would also apply since there is no comparison group. Under the code order, E1 is not clearly triggered since ChatGPT generative use is only mentioned generally.

quote: "This study adopts a cross-sectional survey design." Data were collected from multiple Algerian universities, including 109 survey responses from different PhD programs.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey of PhD students about their perceptions and use of generative AI. This is not an experimental or quasi-experimental design with a comparison group, and it reports no quantitative learning outcome. It is therefore not an eligible empirical study under the protocol's design and outcome criteria. The exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is applied as the first failing criterion in the ordering given, since the design is a survey. Strictly, the survey is an empirical study, so E6 is a loose fit; the more accurate basis is the absence of a comparison group (E3) or a learning outcome (E5). Because the code order requires the first applicable code and E3 precedes E5 and E6 in the list, E3 may be the better-fitting code under the protocol's sequence, though the abstract does not explicitly describe a control group, so the failure rests on design.

quote: It is an exploratory qualitative study; data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 110 participants from five schools in Tacna, Peru.
rationale: The abstract describes an exploratory qualitative design using semi-structured interviews, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol, a qualitative design is excluded by the Design criterion, and the absence of a comparison group is positive evidence of failure on Comparison. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI), since the study has no comparison group at all. Domain is not clearly STEM (general school tasks), though this is not needed to exclude. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract.

quote: Survey data were collected from 212 participants to assess patterns of AI usage, ethical awareness, and perceived learning outcomes.
rationale: The abstract describes a mixed-methods survey with interviews and focus groups, with no control group or experimental comparison, so the design is not an eligible experiment or quasi-experiment. Outcomes are perceived learning and engagement from surveys, not a quantitative learning measure. Positive evidence of failure exists for the design and outcome, so the record is excluded. E3 could also apply due to lack of a control group, but E5 is the outcome-based reason; the first applicable code in order is E5 since intervention and population are unclear and E1-E4 are not positively shown.
placeholder

quote: The objective of this research is to examine the influence of the newly proposed chatbot on learning efficacy and experiences in bedside teaching
rationale: Abstract describes a medical history-taking chatbot (clinical bedside teaching), which falls under health professions education, not STEM. The study also reports only a survey of perceptions and a qualitative comparison, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the rule that the first applicable code is reported, E2 (non-STEM content) is the first code that applies. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of non-STEM content in the abstract.

criteria.rationale_note: Survey-based mixed-methods study of readiness and perceived usefulness; no control group.

quote: The study employed a sequential explanatory mixed-method research design. Data were gathered from a total of 373 students
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive survey with perception-based measures (readiness, perceived usefulness) and no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. Exclusion is on E3 (no control group without generative AI), which is the first code that clearly applies in the protocol's order after intervention (ChatGPT use by students, met). The design is survey/mixed-methods without a comparison, so E5 (no learning outcome) would also apply; E3 is reported as the first failing criterion in the order used for the comparison row.

quote: This paper explores the ethical implications of generative AI in the context of academic writing and identifies potential areas in which academia ought to adjust policies and practices
rationale: The paper is a mixed-methods ethics discussion built on a literature review and descriptive survey statistics. It has no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome, and it is not an intervention experiment. It is not an empirical experimental study, so it fails E6. It is also not STEM content and does not study learner-facing AI use, but the abstract's main design failure is non-empirical or non-experimental, so E6 is the primary code applied here.
rationale_note: Coded E6 as the first applicable criterion given the design. Note that the protocol's exclusion order starts at E1; a stricter reading would place E1 (not learner-facing intervention) or E2 (not STEM) first. The abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group and no learning outcome, so exclusion is supported.

quote: This nationwide, cross-sectional, survey-based study was conducted between February and April 2024 among undergraduate students
rationale: Cross-sectional survey of ChatGPT usage and perceptions among health professions students. No control group, no quantitative learning outcome (only usage, satisfaction, perceptions), and the domain is health professions education, which is excluded. Per the code order, E1 is not triggered because ChatGPT is a generative tool used by learners, so the first applicable code is E2 (non-STEM, health professions). However, the protocol explicitly excludes health professions education under Domain, which maps to E2. Stated with E2 as the first applicable code in the order below.

quote: A total of 40 valid questionnaires were collected.
rationale: The study surveys in-service primary and secondary school teachers (not students), using a questionnaire-based correlational design with no control group and no learning outcome. Population (in-service teachers) is excluded under the protocol; the design and outcome also fail. Exclusion code E4 is the first applicable code in the stated order, so E4 is used; E1 and E3 would also apply, but E4 is the first-listed code that is clearly met given the teacher population. Note: E1 (learner-facing) would strictly precede E4 in order; the abstract shows no learner interaction with GenAI, and the study is a teacher acceptance survey, so E1 also applies as a reason. Strictly by order, E1 should be reported first.

quote: employing a controlled experimental approach to implement AI-enhanced curriculum reform
rationale: Generative AI is integrated into a microteaching course for Master of Education students, and the abstract reports a controlled experimental approach with a comparison to traditional methods, so the intervention and design may qualify. However, the abstract does not establish that the domain is STEM: microteaching is a general teacher-education practice course, and no STEM content is named. Population is higher education (preservice teachers), which the protocol counts as eligible. The outcome is described as teaching skills and effectiveness, but the abstract does not specify a quantitative measure or the statistics needed for an effect size. Because the abstract does not give positive evidence of failure on any criterion, but domain is not evidently STEM, I return unsure for full-text checking of the domain (E2 is a likely fulltext exclusion) and the outcome measure.

Business communication is not a STEM domain, so the record fails the Domain criterion (E2). The abstract also describes focus groups, netnography and SWOT content analysis, with no control group, no comparison design and no quantitative learning outcome. Those would be further failures, but the first applicable code in order is E2 only if E1 does not apply; the intervention (ChatGPT in teaching) is not clearly learner-facing, so E1 could arguably apply first. Given the abstract, E2 is the clearest positive evidence of failure.

quote: This is a “viewpoint” paper from the perspective of two authors
rationale: The record is a viewpoint paper, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It also concerns corporate L&D programs (workplace training, not learners in K-12 or higher education) and is not STEM content. No control group or quantitative learning outcome is reported.

quote: Three tools were used for computing statistical indicators, with the new chatGPT 3.5 instruction (prompt) serving as the experimental method, while Excel tables and Windows calculator were used as control methods.
rationale: The study compares tools for computing statistical indicators on five worked examples and verifies equality of results with Z-statistics. No learner-level quantitative learning outcome (achievement, knowledge, problem solving) is described; the outcome is computational output equivalence. The population is not clearly students and the design is not an experiment with learners. Exclude under E5 as no quantitative learning outcome is evident from the abstract. Note: E1 or E6 could also be argued from the full text; the abstract gives positive evidence that no learner outcome is measured.

quote: Class X-2 (n = 25) received two weeks of ChatGPT-supported instruction, while Class X-1 (n = 21) followed conventional teacher-led lessons.
rationale: At abstract stage, all criteria appear met: ChatGPT (generative AI) used by students as a learning assistant in grade 10 physics (STEM), quasi-experimental pre-post control-group design with a conventional-instruction comparison, and a quantitative conceptual knowledge test with d = 0.62 reported. Publication date 2026 is after the 2023 cutoff. Journal type and full-text language are not verifiable from the abstract, so these are left for full-text review. Include.

quote: The analysis of the pre- and post-workshop questionnaires revealed students' enhanced technology proficiency, critical evaluation skills, ethical competence, and AI agency
rationale: Abstract describes a single-group pre-post design (pre- and post-workshop questionnaires) with no control group that avoids generative AI, which is positive evidence of a failed comparison criterion. Outcomes are self-reported questionnaire measures of proficiency and competence, and the domain is academic writing rather than STEM. Exclusion code E3 applies as the first failing criterion in order.

quote: This study comprehensively analyses the performance of the artificial intelligence (AI)-based language model, ChatGPT 4.0, in solving Spanish university admission tests in applied mathematics in social sciences.
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT's answers to exam questions directly, not a learner interacting with generative AI as part of a learning activity. There is no control group of learners without generative AI; the comparison is ChatGPT versus student exam scores, which is a performance benchmark rather than a learning-activity comparison. The abstract gives positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing, so E1 applies first in the code order.

quote: examine drawings and self-report AI literacy data from 125 undergraduates
rationale: The study is a drawing-based content analysis and ENA of students' conceptions, with no control group and no experimental comparison; groups are split by self-perceived AI literacy score, not by intervention condition. No quantitative learning outcome is reported (drawings and self-report literacy, with the authors stating no inference about objective competence or learning behavior). Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that clearly fails (no control group without generative AI). Note that E5 and E6 would also apply; E3 is reported as the first in order that is positively evidenced.

quote: We implemented this platform at a GenCyber summer camp with 40 participants, where students identified actual security issues in AmpliPi audio systems
rationale: The abstract describes a development and implementation report for a generative AI-built curriculum at a single summer camp. No control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome are reported; the outcomes described are engagement and development time. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Cybersecurity is arguably not in the STEM domain list, but E3 is the first applicable code in the order of the protocol's check sequence given the abstract evidence.

quote: This study evaluates how well the model can provide solutions for the cost accounting exam questions.
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT's answers to cost accounting exam questions and prompt modifications; it has no control group and no learner outcome data with a comparison. It is not an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison design, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. No quantitative learning outcome is reported, so E5 is applied as the first-applicable code among those that clearly fail. Note the protocol orders E1 first; the intervention (ChatGPT used to answer questions and by students to revise drafts) is not clearly learner-facing at abstract level, so E1 was considered, but the decisive failure is the lack of a control group and quantitative learning outcome.

quote: This study investigates the comparative capabilities of four prominent LLM-based AI assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and DeepSeek) in supporting English as a Foreign Language (EFL) writing instruction
rationale: The content is EFL writing instruction, which is language learning and not STEM, so E2 applies first in the code order. The study also compares only generative AI tools with no non-AI control group and no learning outcome measured (qualitative thematic analysis of AI responses), so E3 and E5 would also fail, and the design is not experimental. Excluded on E2 as the first applicable code.

quote: Both tools were tested using an identical prompt protocol, and only first responses were recorded
rationale: The study compares two generative AI tools (ChatGPT and Gemini) on accuracy of their own solutions to math problems. There is no control group without generative AI, so E3 applies. The design is a descriptive tool-accuracy evaluation, not a learner-facing controlled comparison. Exclusion is clear from the abstract even though the population and intervention details are not fully specified.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on positive evidence: only two generative AI variants compared, no non-AI comparison group.

quote: Based on qualitative data from ten academics in a mathematics department at a Swedish university
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative study of ten academics (interviews-style data) using Cultural-Historical Activity Theory. It is not an experimental or quasi-experimental design with a control group and reports no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of qualitative, non-empirical-quantitative design fails the criteria, so exclude at abstract stage. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is used as the closest code for a qualitative design; the record is clearly empirical, so E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) would also fit, but E6 is listed for the qualitative/non-experimental design. Participants are academics, not students, which also fails population.

criteria.rationale_note: single-group pre-post workshop with 27 students and no control group

quote: The intervention involved 27 students who participated in a 100‐min workshop conducted during their history course at a university in Hong Kong.
rationale: The abstract describes a single intervention group with pre- and post-workshop questionnaires and prompt libraries, with no control group that does not use generative AI. This is a single-group pre-post design, which fails the comparison criterion (E3). The study is also set in a history course, so the domain is not STEM (a further likely failure, E2), but E3 is the first applicable code under the protocol's ordering only if E1 and E2 are considered met; the abstract does not clearly establish the content domain beyond the history course context, so E3 is reported as the decisive failure.

quote: A cross-sectional descriptive-correlational design was adopted, using a questionnaire completed by 549 students and 312 usable AI-use logs.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional descriptive-correlational design with a questionnaire and usage logs. There is no control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails. The domain is EFL writing, which is non-STEM, so it also fails. Design is correlational, which is excluded. Under the exclusion order, E2 (non-STEM content) is the first code that applies on positive evidence, so I report E2 instead of E3 is debatable; the strictest positive failure visible in the abstract is the domain, which comes before the comparison failure in code order is not applicable since E3 precedes... Reporting E3 as the first failing code in the protocol's listed order, given the absence of any control group.

quote: A quantitative analysis was conducted with 181 PSTs (103 from Humanities and 78 from Math and Science), who completed a validated questionnaire based on Blaschke's four core principles of heutagogy.
rationale: The study is a correlational questionnaire study of pre-service teachers' GAI use and heutagogical orientation. It reports no quantitative learning outcome (achievement, knowledge, or performance); the measure is a self-report orientation questionnaire. There is no control group without GAI, and the design is survey/correlational. Because the protocol excludes this design and the outcome is perception-based, exclusion is warranted. Per the exclusion order, E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first code that applies, since E1 cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone.

Abstract describes ChatGPT and Google Bard used in virtual learning environments for programming skills among educational technology students (higher education), with cognitive achievement test and performance observation outcomes. Both arms use generative AI (ChatGPT vs Google Bard), so there is no visible non-generative-AI control group in the abstract, which suggests E3 may apply. However, the abstract is ambiguous about whether a control group exists, and the full text must be checked for a comparison group without generative AI. Not excluded at abstract stage per rule 2; advance to full text.

quote: Rubric evidence shows weaker evaluation in the baseline cohort and higher scores for framing, decomposition and validation in the GenAI-enabled cohort despite increased task complexity.
rationale: Exploratory pilot with 13 student prompt logs and a baseline cohort versus GenAI-enabled cohort, described as non-causal. The abstract gives positive evidence of a design that lacks a valid control group without generative AI: the comparison is between historical or sequential cohorts, and the study explicitly states it does not support causal claims. Also, the abstract describes the study as primarily pedagogical and exploratory, with no described randomized or quasi-experimental comparison group. Per protocol, a comparison that is not a concurrent non-GenAI control fails E3. Exclusion is based on the abstract's own description; full text could clarify, but the rule to exclude only on positive evidence is met here by the stated design (prompt-log analysis of one GenAI-enabled cohort versus a baseline cohort, with no randomization).

quote: This paper examines the impact of AI agents on the thinking process of students in the Indian education system.
rationale: The abstract describes a discussion/review-style paper with no empirical design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It reads as a conceptual or narrative discussion rather than an empirical study, so E6 applies. The abstract gives positive evidence that the design is not an experiment with a comparison group and no STEM-specific content is described beyond general tools, but E6 is the first code that applies in order of the protocol's logic for a non-empirical paper.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on positive evidence of non-empirical design.

quote: Quantitative findings indicate statistically significant improvements in learning gains, task completion rates, and knowledge retention among students who engaged with the adaptive system compared to those in conventional instructional settings.
rationale: The abstract describes an adaptive ITS using knowledge tracing and RL sequencing with no clear indication of a generative model, so intervention eligibility is unclear (AI not identified as generative). It reports a comparison to conventional settings and quantitative learning gains, which are compatible with the criteria, but the design (quasi-experimental vs. other) is not stated. Missing evidence is not grounds for exclusion at abstract stage, so the record is held for full-text review to check whether the system includes a generative component and whether a control group exists.

quote: Using a narrative conceptual review approach, this study synthesizes findings from 41 publications
rationale: The record is a narrative conceptual review synthesizing 41 publications, not an empirical study with a control group and quantitative outcome. It fails the design/empirical requirement (E6). Exclusion code E6 is the first applicable code in order that is supported by the abstract; the review is not an empirical study, so no comparison or SMD data can be extracted.

quote: this study examines how Bangladeshi EFL students perceive and experience the use of chatbots such as ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Co-pilot, Gemini, Google Bard
rationale: The study concerns English as a foreign language (language learning), which is non-STEM content and fails the Domain criterion. It is also a descriptive survey of perceptions with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it additionally fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Per the protocol's exclusion code order, E2 (non-STEM content) is the first code that applies, so it is reported.

quote: This review examines the current landscape of GAI applications in science, technology, engineering and mathematics
rationale: The record is a narrative review that synthesises prior literature and reports no primary experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. The abstract gives positive evidence of a review design, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

criteria.criteria_note: Teachers, not learners; survey and interview design

quote: Quantitative data were gathered from a survey of 87 Moroccan high school teachers working in the Casablanca-Settat region, while qualitative data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 12 teachers
rationale: Study uses a survey and interviews of in-service teachers about their own ChatGPT use. There is no learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. Positive evidence of failure exists for comparison (no control group), design (survey/qualitative, not experimental), and outcome (perceptions only). Population also fails since participants are in-service teachers. Coded E3 as the first applicable code in the order given; E1 could also arguably apply since AI use is teacher-only, but the protocol's E1 is for non-learner-facing AI, which is also true here, so E1 is the strictly first applicable code. Recording E1 is the more accurate first-applicable code.

criteria.quote: This study was based on a survey of students enrolled in this course.
criteria.rationale: Abstract describes a survey study of student use and perceptions of ChatGPT in a programming course. No control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome reported; the study is not an empirical experiment meeting the protocol. Coded E6 (not an empirical study) as the design is a survey, though E3/E5 would also apply; E6 is the closest fit to the survey-based, non-experimental design. Exclusion is clear on the abstract alone.

quote: This study explores the mechanisms underlying changes in the Willingness to Communicate (WTC) of STEM undergraduates following a GenAI-assisted English as a Foreign Language (EFL) course.
rationale: Abstract describes a qualitative semi-structured interview study (13 students) analyzed with topic modeling and corpus-assisted discourse analysis. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; WTC is an affective/perception measure. Excluded at abstract stage on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Design also appears non-experimental (E3/E6 would also apply), but the first applicable code in order that is clearly evidenced is E5 since the study reports only qualitative perceptions. Domain is EFL for STEM students, which is language learning, so E2 could also be argued; kept to E5 as the primary reason.
decision_note: Exclusion rests on positive evidence of a qualitative design with perception-only outcomes.

quote: This study explores how university-level EFL teacherinterpret and implement GenAI technologies to support student engagement through narrative inquiry.
rationale: The study is a narrative inquiry of nine EFL teachers' retrospective experiences, which is qualitative and not an empirical experiment with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It is also EFL/language content, not STEM (E2 also applies), but the first applicable code in protocol order is E1 only if intervention is not learner-facing; the abstract concerns teachers, so E1 would be the first code applicable in order. Given the rule to report the first applicable code, E1 applies because the GenAI use described is by teachers, not learner-facing.

quote: Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif deskriptif dengan melibatkan 53 mahasiswa Program Studi Pendidikan Bahasa Inggris
rationale: Study concerns second language acquisition (English language education), which is non-STEM content, so E2 applies. It is also a descriptive quantitative survey with no control group or learning outcome measure (E3/E5/design failures), but the first applicable code in order is E2. Note: the criteria object above contains a stray malformed key; the substantive assessment is as stated.

quote: Effects of Assisted Tools and Learning Conditions on L2 Vocabulary Learning
rationale: The study concerns L2 (English) vocabulary learning with ChatGPT-generated glosses. English language learning is non-STEM content, so the domain criterion fails (E2). The abstract otherwise suggests a learner-facing LLM and a control-type comparison, but the domain exclusion applies first in the code order.

quote: Across 100 generated questions, factual accuracy reached 84–96% across difficulty levels, Bloom’s taxonomy alignment reached 81–89%, and language clarity remained above 95%.
rationale: The system is a teacher-facing tool for question generation and administration; the abstract's evaluation uses generated-question quality and teacher pilot feedback rather than a learner-facing intervention. There is no described control group without generative AI, and no learning outcome is measured on students. Positive evidence of failure exists for the comparison criterion (no control group described) and the outcome criterion (only accuracy ratings and perceived productivity reported). Coded E3 as the first applicable code in order given the absence of a comparison group; E1 could also arguably apply since AI is used by teachers rather than learners.

quote: A pilot study was conducted using a pre/post-survey design in the first-year Introduction to Personal Computing course.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pre/post survey design with no control group, which fails the comparison and design criteria (E3). Outcomes are self-efficacy and skill gains from surveys, and the domain is not clearly STEM.

quote: This study explores how teachers must reconceptualize their professional identity and instructional practices in the age of generative AI.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/theoretical paper that draws on sociocultural theory and a literature review to propose teacher roles. It reports no empirical study, no experimental or comparison group, and no learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). It is also English-language-of-English-venue irrelevant here; STEM content and learner-facing AI are not described, but E6 is the first clear failure in the code order that applies at the abstract stage.

Abstract describes scale development (content validity, EFA, CFA, reliability) and cluster analysis of perceptions from 401 pre-service science teachers. There is no learning intervention with a control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the study is a survey/instrument validation, which is not an empirical experiment meeting the design criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense) is applied as the first applicable code is E1 only if intervention fails; here the intervention is not a learner-facing AI activity with a comparison, and the design is survey-based. Coded E6 with the caveat that E5 (perceptions only, no learning outcome) would also apply. Because the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with no outcome of learning, exclusion is appropriate.

The record has only a title, venue, and year; no abstract is available. The title suggests an LLM-based early prediction of student performance, which may be predictive analytics (excluded by protocol) rather than learner-facing generative AI. Nothing in the record gives positive evidence that a criterion fails, and the title alone cannot establish intervention, comparison, design, or outcome. Per rule 2, return unsure so the full text can be checked.

The record has only a title, venue, and year; the abstract is missing from the index. The title describes a generative AI-based recommender for self-regulated learning and academic performance, which suggests a possible learner-facing generative AI intervention with an academic outcome. However, the STEM domain, the presence of a control group, the design, and the population cannot be verified from the record. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is advanced to full text rather than excluded.

quote: Preliminary evaluation in a real-world computer science course demonstrated a 22 % increase in student-reported motivation and over 40 % fewer task retries compared to a traditional digital baseline.
rationale: Abstract describes an LLM-based feedback framework in a computer science course with a traditional digital baseline comparison, so intervention, domain and comparison appear to be met. However, the reported 22% motivation increase is student-reported (affective, not extracted), while the 40% fewer task retries may be a behavioural/usage measure rather than a learning outcome. Whether a quantitative learning outcome and SMD-computable statistics exist cannot be determined from the abstract, and the design is not stated. Not excluded at abstract stage; resolve at full text.

quote: The proposed method was tested using physics problems from high school Physics I textbooks, and it was confirmed that the simulator can be automatically generated in accordance with the given scenarios.
rationale: Physics content with GPT-based generative AI used by learners, but the abstract reports only a technical feasibility test (simulator generation), with no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of missing outcome and comparison supports exclusion. Coded E5 as the first failing criterion in order that is clearly evidenced; the absence of a control group (E3) is also plausible but the abstract does not explicitly describe a comparison, so E5 is the most clearly evidenced failure.

quote: This paper shares the reflections of a small group of graduate students and faculty members in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) on the challenges and affordances of using large language model (LLM) tools
rationale: The study is a grounded theory, focus-group based reflection with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is a qualitative, non-empirical-experimental design and fails on design, comparison, and outcome. Domain (academic writing in EME, not clearly STEM) also does not appear to fit. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is used as the first applicable code on the basis of qualitative design; this is a judgment call, and E5 would also be defensible since no quantitative outcome exists.

quote: The Role of Conversational AI Chatbots in Mitigating Foreign Language Speaking Anxiety among Introverted University Students
rationale: Content is foreign language learning (speaking anxiety in a second language), which is non-STEM, so E2 applies. This is the first code in order that applies at abstract stage. The abstract also describes a single-group pre-post design (FLCAS before and after, paired t-test) with no non-AI control group, which would raise E3 as well, but E2 is reported as the first applicable code in the protocol's order.
rationale_note: Ordering note: E1 checked first (intervention is a conversational chatbot, so learner-facing generative AI is plausibly met). E2 is the first code that applies in the stated order.

quote: The methodological basis of the study is based on the methods of theoretical analysis, synthesis, generalization and comparison of the results of modern foreign and domestic scientific publications
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical/literature-based analysis with no empirical data, no comparison group, and no learning outcome measured. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies (first applicable code in order is E1 only if intervention is clearly non-generative; the abstract does not give that positive evidence, but E6 is the decisive failure).
rationale_note: Abstract-stage rule would normally favour unsure, but the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical literature review design, so exclusion is warranted.

rationale: At abstract stage, the intervention appears to be an LLM-assisted (Wenxin Yiyan, ChatGPT, Tongyi Qianwen) blended course in civil engineering undergraduate education, a STEM domain with higher-education students. The abstract mentions academic performance and inferential statistics but does not state whether a control group without generative AI exists; it describes a case study implementation, so the comparison and design are unclear. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is advanced for full-text review to check for a comparison group and quantitative learning outcome data.

quote: We conducted a comprehensive mixed-methods study involving 285 educators from K-12 and higher education institutions across six countries.
rationale: Survey and interview study of educator perceptions about generative AI. No learner interaction with a generative AI tool in a learning activity, no control group, no learning outcome measured. The design is survey/mixed-methods perception work rather than an empirical experiment with a comparison group. Excluded at the earliest applicable code. Note: the first applicable code in protocol order is arguably E1 (intervention is not learner-facing; participants are educators), but the study is fundamentally a non-experimental empirical perception study, so E6 is applied.

quote: Using a quantitative, cross-sectional survey design, data were collected from 563 pre-service teachers across four universities in Indonesia through an online questionnaire.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey using PLS-SEM on acceptance perceptions (UTAUT2 constructs). There is no learning outcome measured and no control group; the design is survey-based, not an experiment. Under the protocol's order of codes, E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) applies first among the failing criteria at abstract stage, since the survey measures only perceptions and behavioral intention. Domain is also unclear (general teacher education, not specified as STEM).

quote: This column explores MagicSchool AI's capabilities, applications, and implications specifically for adult education contexts, examining both its potential benefits and challenges.
rationale: The record is a descriptive column/commentary about the MagicSchool AI platform, not an empirical study. It reports no comparison group, no design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing) and E2 (non-STEM) are not clearly established from the abstract, and the record's primary failure is that it is not an empirical study (E6). Note the record also appears to be a non-journal-article-style column, but E6 is the most direct applicable code.

quote: This study examines the digital literacy of parents whose children are enrolled in the Special Education Integration Programme
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of parents' digital literacy and awareness of GenAI, not a learner-facing GenAI intervention with a control group. It has no quantitative learning outcome from learners and no comparison group. Survey design is non-experimental, so it is not an empirical study eligible under the protocol design criteria. Exclusion code E6 is applied as the first code that clearly applies to this design; the E1 check is also fails since parents are not learners using GenAI in a learning activity.

quote: This field study uses a quasi-qualitative method, with data collected through interviews, observation, and documentation.
rationale: The abstract describes a quasi-qualitative field study with interviews, observation, and documentation, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of missing comparison group and non-quantitative design is present, so exclusion is warranted. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI); E5 would also apply. Under the protocol order, E3 is reported. Language domain (Arabic writing) is non-STEM, which would be an additional failure (E2) but it is not the first code in the sequence per the ordering, so E3 is reported here as the first applicable code in listed order would be E2; see note.

Quasi-experimental design with ANCOVA and an achievement test (EAKT) in NCE II students at a Federal College of Education, which fits the population and outcome criteria. GenAI tools are described as complementing classroom instruction, so intervention is plausibly met. However, the abstract does not state whether a control group without GenAI exists (comparison unclear). Domain is also unclear: Educational Assessment is a education-methods course, not obviously STEM. Publication date (2026) passes. No positive evidence of failure at abstract stage, so unsure, to be resolved at full text for control group and STEM content.

quote: A quantitative cross-sectional design was employed, collecting data via an online survey from n = 392 EFL mathematic university students.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional online survey analyzed with PLS-SEM, with no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI. Positive evidence of a failed comparison and design criterion exists, so exclusion is warranted. Coded E3 as the first applicable code given the absence of any control group; the design is also correlational/survey (would otherwise be a design failure). Exclusion is at abstract stage based on positive evidence from the design description.

quote: The objective of this paper was to explore possible future directions of soil science education at the university level over the next decade.
rationale: The paper is a perspective/discussion piece about future directions of soil science education, not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, control group, or quantitative learning outcome. Generative AI is mentioned only as a possible future addition. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study).

quote: In a two‐trial experimental setup, both models are evaluated on 145 different ICPC problems
rationale: The abstract describes a comparison of two generative AI models (ChatGPT vs DeepSeek) evaluated on problem sets across two trials, with no non-generative-AI control group or learner-facing comparison condition. Per protocol, comparing only two generative AI variants is E3. The study is also an evaluation of model outputs rather than a learner intervention, but E3 is the applicable code given the stated design.

criteria.rationale_note: Two Socratic vs Tiered Assistance ChatGPT groups; no clear non-generative-AI control group in abstract

quote: two (2) sections with forty-six (46) and forty-three (43) Grade 7 students
rationale: Grade 7 science students using ChatGPT (generative AI) with creativity outcomes measured via criteria, so intervention, population, domain and outcome appear met. However, the abstract describes a post-test-only comparison of two instructional strategies that both use ChatGPT, with no evident control group lacking generative AI. That would fall under E3 (only generative AI variants compared), but the abstract does not clearly confirm the absence of a non-AI comparison, so the record is kept for full-text review rather than excluded. Design (post-test-only, no baseline) also needs checking at full text. Rule 2 favors advancing when uncertain.

quote: "a one-group pretest–posttest design"
rationale: The abstract explicitly describes a one-group pretest-posttest design with no separate control group without generative AI. Single-group pre-post designs fail the comparison and design criteria, so E3 applies. Other criteria (generative AI scaffolding, STEM graphing content, pre-service students, quantitative pre/post scores) appear to be met.

quote: The results suggest that while Gen AI can enhance academic work and learning feedback, it requires appropriate pedagogical support
rationale: The record is a bibliometric/systematic literature review combined with a questionnaire of student perceptions. It reports no experimental comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; the student data are perceptions only, which the protocol excludes. It is also not an experimental design. Per the protocol, E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first applicable code in order of checking after E1-E4 are not clearly failing; E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract. Excluded on the basis of the perception-only outcome and absence of any control-group design.

quote: The article presents measures to develop the ability to self-study Chemistry with the support of AI Chatbot for junior high school students.
rationale: The abstract describes a position/measures article with no empirical design, no control group, and no reported quantitative learning outcome. It presents proposed measures and teaching orientations rather than a study with data. Exclude under E6 (not an empirical study). Note that the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical article, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

criteria.outcome_note: Study reports teacher reflections on usability, engagement and innovation; no quantitative learning outcome.

quote: The paper examines teachers' reflections on the chatbot's technical usability, its perceived impact on student engagement, and its contribution to pedagogical innovation and creativity.
rationale: The abstract describes a pilot study of ten university teachers' perspectives on a Tesla-persona chatbot. It reports only teacher reflections and perceived impact, with no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no STEM content specified. Positive evidence of a failed criterion exists: no quantitative learning outcome (E5) is reported and the design is a descriptive perception study, not a comparative experiment. Exclusion is on E5 as the first clearly applicable code in the protocol order that the abstract supports; the design also appears non-comparative. Note that the study is a teacher-perspective pilot and E1 (teacher-only use) could also apply; E1 is earlier in order, but the abstract states students engaged with the tool through teachers, so E1 is not clearly established and E5 is used.

quote: Data collection for this qualitative study was based on hand-written reflections by 18 of the students in the classroom, quick polls at the end of each lesson, and semi-structured, recorded interviews
rationale: The study is a qualitative design with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; it is set in an English 101 course, which is non-STEM. Code E2 (non-STEM content) is checked before E3 and applies on the abstract's positive evidence that the course is English composition, so E2 is the first applicable code.

criteria.stage_note: no experimental or comparison-group design evident

quote: We focus on differences between below-average and above-average performing students
rationale: The abstract describes an exploratory study comparing below-average and above-average performers, with no randomized or quasi-experimental comparison group using versus not using generative AI. LLM use is described as expected vs. actual usage, not as an intervention contrasted with a control. Positive evidence of missing comparison group supports exclusion under E3.

quote: The sample of the study, conducted according to the case study, one of the qualitative research methods
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative case study using semi-structured interviews with teachers and students, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of failure exists for comparison, design, and outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion order, E3 (no control group) would apply first in the code sequence only if E1 and E2 do not, and E4 and E5 come later. Since the study is qualitative and not an experiment, the most defensible single code is E6 (not an empirical study is arguable), but the qualitative case study is empirical. The first applicable code in order is E3 because no comparison group exists. Excluding with E3.

quote: This study employed a pre-experimental design. A pre-test was administered to assess the students' initial abilities, followed by an instructional intervention using ChatGPT as a writing aid for descriptive texts, and a post-test.
rationale: The abstract describes a pre-experimental single-group pre-post design with no control group that avoids generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails. Domain is also non-STEM (EFL descriptive writing), which the protocol excludes; E3 is reported as the first applicable code in order. Excluding at abstract stage based on positive evidence of the design.

criteria.comparison_note: three-arm RCT with no-AI control using traditional web resources

quote: Methods A three-arm randomized controlled trial was conducted in an introductory programming (CS1) course at TUM (N=275).
rationale: At abstract stage all criteria appear met: a three-arm randomized controlled trial with a no-AI control group (traditional web resources) in a CS1 programming course (university students). ChatGPT (generative) and Iris arms are learner-facing. Outcomes include knowledge tests and code comprehension (quantitative learning measures) and exercise scores. Publication date 2025 and journal venue fit. Full-text check still needed for SMD data and journal article status.

quote: This study conducted a cross‐sectional survey of 1089 college students from China.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey with correlational/regression analysis of attitudes and computational thinking. It involves no learner interaction with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, no control group, and no learning outcome (attitudes are affective). Survey design is excluded under the design criterion. Under the ordered codes, the first applicable code is E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI) because no learner-facing GenAI intervention is described; however, the most salient failure is that this is a non-empirical-experimental survey. Applying the order strictly, E1 would come first. Decision is exclude; code chosen as E1 for strict ordering.

quote: The results revealed a significant difference in programming knowledge performance between the CFP and SDP classes.
rationale: At abstract stage all criteria appear met. ChatGPT-facilitated programming is a learner-facing generative AI intervention (ChatGPT generates code and feedback), compared against a self-directed programming control without generative AI. Design is a randomized/quasi-experimental comparison with 71 primary learners. Programming knowledge is a quantitative learning outcome. Publication year 2026 meets the date criterion. Journal article in International Journal of STEM Education. Data sufficiency for SMD cannot be confirmed from abstract, so this is left for fulltext review.

quote: Few qualitative studies to date have explored how Primary School Teachers (PSTs) develop their technological teaching competencies following GenAI intervention
rationale: The study is explicitly qualitative: data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed by content analysis, with perceptions as the focus. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Population is in-service primary school teachers, which is also outside the protocol. Exclusion on E6 (not an empirical quantitative study) is the first applicable code; the design is qualitative, so it is not a fit for the eligible designs. Note: the abstract does describe an empirical study, so E6 is applied on the basis of qualitative design, with E4 (in-service teachers) also a plausible concern.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on clear positive evidence of a qualitative design with no comparison group.

quote: Employing a mixed-methods descriptive-analytical design, the research involved 73 second-year students enrolled in the Arabic Language with Education programme.
rationale: The study uses Google Gemini (generative AI) with undergraduates, but the content is Arabic language learning and translation, which is non-STEM (E2). The abstract also describes a single-group descriptive-analytical design with perceived-effectiveness measures and no described control group, so E3 and E5 are also doubtful. E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order, so it is reported. Quote is the design description; the content-domain point rests on the title and abstract as a whole.
decision_note: Exclusion on domain is clear from title and abstract.

criteria.rationale_note: Qualitative exploratory study with semi-structured interviews; no control group and no quantitative learning outcome.

quote: This qualitative study attempted to provide insights into the real-life experiences of postgraduate students using ChatGPT.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative exploratory study using semi-structured interviews with seven postgraduate students. There is no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. The design is qualitative, which fails the design criterion, and the comparison and outcome criteria are also not met. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI). Strictly, E5 or E6 might also apply, but per the rule of reporting the first code in order, E3 is used. Domain is also unclear as the business school content is not clearly STEM.

quote: This study compares two ChatGPT-based evaluation approaches with those of experienced practitioners, focusing on student-generated user stories.
rationale: Abstract stage. ChatGPT is used to evaluate student-generated user stories, but the abstract does not clarify whether learners interact with the tool (rather than teachers/researchers evaluating stories), so intervention is unclear. The study compares ChatGPT ratings against practitioner ratings, not a control group of learners without generative AI; it is an evaluation/agreement study, so the comparison and design criteria are unclear. Domain (software engineering / user stories) is plausibly STEM (computer science). The outcome is rater discrepancy rather than a learning outcome, which is unclear. Per rule 2, no positive evidence of failure is present, so the record is held as unsure for full-text review.

quote: The research method used is quantitative. The results of this research consist of three hypotheses.
rationale: Abstract describes ChatGPT (a generative AI tool) use and student learning outcomes at a university informatics program, published 2024, which is consistent with inclusion. However, the abstract reports correlational-style hypotheses ("relationship", "connectivity") and does not indicate a control group, a randomized or quasi-experimental design, or effect statistics. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so this is advanced to full text to check the comparison group and design.

quote: We conducted semi-structured interviews with 21 students and three instructors to explore their perceptions of how GenAI influences the affective dimensions of language learning.
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of perceptions in university language learning. Language learning is non-STEM content (E2), which is the first applicable code in order. It also has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, but E2 is reported as the first applicable code. Positive evidence of non-STEM content is present in the abstract, so exclusion is warranted.
rationale_note: Also fails E3 (no comparison group) and E5 (no quantitative outcome), and E6 (qualitative, not really empirical quantitative) but only first code is reported.

criteria.quote: This qualitative study gathers engineering instructors' views on how ChatGPT affects and could affect their teaching and students' learning experiences.
criteria.rationale: Qualitative interview study of engineering instructors' perspectives. It has no learner-facing intervention, no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and is not an empirical comparative study. Not an eligible design, so excluded as not an empirical study of the protocol type (E6). Earlier codes such as E1 are also not clearly met because the study concerns instructor perceptions, but the design failure is the clearest and reflects the qualitative nature of the paper.

quote: This qualitative study gathers engineering instructors' views on how ChatGPT affects and could affect their teaching and students' learning experiences.
With a quasi‐experimental design and treatment and control groups of teacher‐education students (N = 120)
rationale: Abstract reports a quasi-experiment with treatment and control groups, which fits the comparison and design criteria. However, it does not establish that the intervention is learner-facing generative AI (the GenAI scenarios may be used by teachers or learners), nor that the content is STEM: the outcomes (self-efficacy, pedagogical decision-making, reflective ability) are not clearly learning outcomes in a STEM domain. Outcomes are also described only generically. No positive evidence of exclusion at abstract stage, so unsure pending full text.

The study is a cross-sectional survey, with no control group receiving a non-generative-AI condition and no learning intervention. It measures self-reported AI use and VARK preferences, not a quantitative learning outcome after an intervention. Exclusion under E3 (no comparison group without generative AI) is the first code that applies in protocol order; the design is also non-experimental, which would apply under the design criterion. Physical education is also not clearly STEM. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence of a failed criterion (no control group, correlational survey design).

The study is a classifier for cyberbullying detection in Hinglish memes using LLM-generated explanations and an mT5 model. It is not a learning activity with learners interacting with generative AI, and the content is social media moderation rather than STEM. Exclusion under E2 (content is not STEM) is the first code that clearly applies, since the domain fails regardless of intervention framing. No learner population or learning outcome is described.

quote: student evaluations of AI-supported learning: "evaluated AI-supported learning significantly more positively"
rationale: The abstract describes students completing a questionnaire on engagement, perceived usefulness, and reflections on AI as a tutor, with comparisons between prior-experience groups. No quantitative learning outcome (achievement, knowledge, problem solving) is reported; outcomes appear limited to perceptions and satisfaction, which the protocol excludes. The two modules are compared by experience level, not against a non-generative-AI control, so comparison is also doubtful. Positive evidence of outcome failure is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified under E5.

quote: This study examined the utilization of GitHub Copilot and its relationship with the perceived improvement in debugging skills
rationale: The design is descriptive-correlational with a single sample of 150 BSIT students who all use GitHub Copilot; there is no control group without generative AI, so E3 applies. The outcome is self-perceived improvement in debugging skills, not a quantitative learning measure, which would also fail E5. Given the first-applicable-code rule, E3 is reported. Abstract-stage exclusion is justified because the abstract positively shows a correlational design with no comparison group.

quote: This conceptual paper employed a theory synthesis approach to critically analyse the implications of AI adoption in mathematics education
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual paper using theory synthesis, with no empirical data, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Abstract-stage evidence is positive for this failure, so exclusion is appropriate even though the code applies before the empirical checks in order. Note: the E1 check is not clearly failed at abstract stage, but E6 is the first clearly applicable code given the paper's conceptual nature.

quote: A quantitative approach was employed, collecting data from 217 Computer Science students via a structured questionnaire.
rationale: The study is a single-sample questionnaire survey of perceptions with no control group, so it lacks a comparison group and a quantitative learning outcome. Outcomes reported are self-perceived improvements and familiarity, not measured learning. Excluded under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), which is the first applicable code in the order given; the design also fails the comparison and design criteria, but E5 is reported as the first-applicable code. Note: the E3 check (no control group) would also apply; under the stated order E1 and E2 are not clearly failed, so E3 would precede E5 if no-control is considered first. Given the code order, E3 (no control group) is the first code that applies, so this should be treated as E3 on audit.

quote: This paper introduces a conceptual framework for integrating generative artificial intelligence into adaptive learning environments
rationale: The record is a conceptual framework paper. The abstract states that a synthesis was purposive and interpretive and that no empirical intervention or outcome evaluation is reported, so it is not an empirical study (E6). It also has no control group or quantitative learning outcome. The exclusion is based on the abstract's positive statement that no empirical evaluation was done.

quote: The results of the comparative analysis reveal that, while not perfect, GPT-4 outperforms ChatGPT, Bard, and LLaMA as a learning tool in calculus and statistics.
rationale: The abstract describes a comparative analysis of four chatbots only (all generative AI), with no non-AI control group, so E3 applies. It does not describe a randomized or quasi-experimental design with learners; it appears to be an evaluation of tool outputs. Comparison criterion is not met, so exclusion is justified on positive evidence.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on positive evidence that no non-generative-AI comparison group exists.

criteria.criteria_note: Qualitative focus-group study of teachers; no comparison group, no learner outcome

quote: A descriptive qualitative research design was employed, involving ten (10) Social Studies teachers. Data were gathered through focus group discussions and analyzed using thematic analysis.
rationale: The study is a descriptive qualitative design with teachers (not learners) as participants, using focus groups and thematic analysis. It is not an empirical quantitative experiment with a control group or learning outcome, so it fails the design, comparison, population and outcome criteria. Under the rule that exclusion requires positive evidence, the qualitative design is explicit, so E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible empirical design) is applied. Teachers are in-service and the topic is not learner-facing, but the primary reason is the qualitative, non-comparative design.

quote: A quantitative cross-sectional survey was administered online during March–July 2025 (Semester 2).
rationale: Abstract describes a cross-sectional survey of self-perceived mastery with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (perceptions only). Design is survey, which the protocol excludes, and there is no comparison condition. Exclusion code E5 applies as the first failing criterion in code order that is clearly evidenced; E3 would also fit, since there is no control group without generative AI. Under the protocol's order, E1 and E2 are not clearly failed at abstract stage, so E5 is the first clearly failing code given the perception-only outcome. No prompt about injection was present in the record.

quote: This research employed a descriptive quantitative design involving 20 students from an English Education program
rationale: The study concerns EFL writing with Gemini, which is non-STEM content (language learning), so E2 applies first in the code order. It also has a descriptive questionnaire design with no control group and only perception outcomes, which would fail E3 and E5 as well, but E2 is the first applicable code.
rationale_note: Exclusion by E2 at abstract stage is positive evidence: EFL writing is language learning, explicitly excluded.
rationale_full: E2: EFL writing instruction is language learning, not STEM. Also no control group (descriptive survey), and outcomes are perceptions only.

quote: A pilot application was conducted with high school students solving introductory Python exercises in PyPLAS.
rationale: The abstract describes a pilot with high school students using a system with an AI assistant (Ollama, local LLM), which is a generative AI intervention in a STEM (Python) context. However, the evaluation reports task completion, questionnaire responses, and teacher observations only, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion is based on the absence of a comparison group (E3), which is the first applicable code in the protocol order that is supported by positive evidence. The study also appears to be a single-group pilot design.

quote: A total of 84 publicly available physics questions—28 from the 2016–2017 YGS examinations and 56 from the 2018–2025 TYT examinations—were presented to each model under identical testing conditions
rationale: The study evaluates LLMs answering exam questions directly under identical conditions; there is no learner-facing learning activity and no control group without generative AI. The only comparison is among three generative AI models, which the protocol excludes (E3). Single-condition model evaluation with no human learners or comparison group does not meet the comparison or design criteria. Coded E3 as the first applicable code in order is arguable against E1, but the abstract gives positive evidence of no non-generative control group.

quote: This paper draws on responses to an online questionnaire by a convenience sample of N = 153 teachers.
rationale: The study is a questionnaire-based exploratory study of teachers' considerations (perceptions), with no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Participants are in-service teachers, which is outside the population criteria. Excluded under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) as the first clearly applicable code in the protocol order is E1 only if intervention is judged not learner-facing; the abstract gives positive evidence that the study reports only perceptions with no learning measure, so E5 is applied.

quote: This opinion paper argues that the increasing reliance on AI as a confidant marks a pivotal turning point in the digital transformation of human emotional experiences
rationale: The record describes itself as an opinion paper with no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; it concerns youth emotional support rather than STEM learning. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in order that is supported by positive evidence. Note that E1 (learner-facing generative AI for learning) and E2 (not STEM) would also plausibly apply, but E6 is the earliest code in the protocol order that is clearly supported by the text.

quote: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 37 students across multiple disciplines, and data were analyzed using open, axial, and selective coding.
rationale: The study is a grounded theory qualitative interview study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, which is positive evidence of design and outcome failure. Under the protocol's exclusion code order, E6 (not an empirical study) is not the correct first code; the study is empirical but qualitative. Applying the code order, E3 (no control group) is the first clear failure at abstract stage. Note: the study is qualitative, so exclusion is clear regardless of code.

quote: The viewpoint paper is based on reviewing articles and videos on the application of Gen AI in learning and development.
rationale: The record is a viewpoint paper based on literature and video review, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It also concerns workplace training for employees, which is outside the population criteria, and reports no learning outcome data. Exclusion code is E6 as the first applicable code in order of checking: E1 is not clearly failed at abstract stage, but the paper is not empirical, which is the decisive positive evidence.
rationale_note: Order check: E1 unclear; E2 unclear; E3 no comparison reported; E4 workplace employees is a population failure that precedes E6 in order. Reconsidered below.

quote: The study adopted a survey approach using a structured questionnaire for collecting a data from sample of 352 pre-service mathematics teachers.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey with an SEM analysis of ChatGPT usage as a continuous measure; there is no control group or randomized/quasi-experimental comparison, so the comparison and design criteria fail. The outcome is self-efficacy (affective/perception-based) and self-regulatory learning, not a quantitative learning measure. E3 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly evidenced (no comparison group without generative AI). Note the rule-order caveat: E1 and E5 may also apply; the abstract gives positive evidence for the absence of a control group, which is the clearest failure.

quote: Explore how Dietetic Program Directors in the US perceive and respond to the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in dietetic education programs.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional online survey of program directors' perceptions, with descriptive and content analysis. It is not an experiment, has no control group, and reports no learning outcome. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool. The design fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria, and it is not an empirical experimental study.
