Per the ordering rule, E1 would apply first since no learner-facing generative AI intervention exists, but the clearest first-applying code given the survey design is E6 (not an empirical study of an intervention). Note: strictly by code order, E1 is the first that applies because no learner-facing intervention is described; the decision is excluded either way.

quote: A qualitative hermeneutic phenomenological approach was employed, using ChatGPT-assisted thematic analysis across six analytic tables covering factor codes, solution codes, categories, and themes.
rationale: The study is a qualitative hermeneutic phenomenological study. Generative AI (ChatGPT) was used by researchers for coding, not as a learner-facing intervention, and there is no control group or quantitative learning outcome. Under the abstract-stage rule, the failure of the design and intervention criteria is positively evidenced, so exclusion is appropriate. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing), but the clearest failure is that the study is not an empirical quantitative study, so E6 is the reported code.

quote: This study aims to analyze the patterns of interaction and communication experiences of students
rationale: The study is a descriptive qualitative design using in-depth interviews with ten students. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and is not an experimental study. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is used for the qualitative design; per the protocol's design and outcome criteria, it also fails E3 and E5. E6 is reported as the first code that applies in the stated order is E1 (intervention unclear) but the design is clearly non-experimental, so E6 reflects the study type most directly.

quote: The researchers conducted a survey with 94 students from 1st year to 3rd yearChatgpt levels as a sample to collect data on their demographic profiles
rationale: The abstract describes a survey study of dependence and perceived impact of ChatGPT use, with no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome (outcomes are perceptions of efficiency, engagement, and dependence). Not an empirical experiment meeting the design criteria; the survey design is positive evidence of exclusion as a non-eligible empirical design (E6, survey design). Domain (radiologic technology) is not clearly STEM. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of a survey design with no comparison group.

criteria.quote: An exploratory qualitative study involved 24 second-semester Informatics Engineering Education students selected purposively.
criteria.rationale: The study is an exploratory qualitative design (interviews, focus groups, observations, thematic analysis) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's order, the first applicable code is E6 (not an empirical study is the closest fit for a qualitative, non-comparative design; the design is empirical but fails the comparison/design and outcome requirements). Exclusion is clear on design grounds even though the code choice is a judgment call; E3 (no control group) would also apply. Abstract gives positive evidence of a qualitative design, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

rationale: Qualitative exploratory study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded on the basis of a qualitative, non-comparative design; code assigned is E6 as the closest fit, though E3 (no comparison group) and E5 (no quantitative outcome) also apply.

quote: the study involved 200 vocational students selected via cluster random sampling and 5 teachers selected using a purposive sampling technique
rationale: Abstract describes a generative AI classroom implementation with 200 vocational students, but gives no indication of a separate control group without generative AI. Results are descriptive (overall means of engagement and perceived learning), and the design is described as explanatory sequential mixed methods with descriptive statistics, suggesting no comparison group. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group supports E3. Domain (vocational STEM content) is also not specified. Excluded at abstract stage on E3 because the abstract gives positive evidence that no control condition exists.

quote: This conceptual article proposes the Prompt-to-Pedagogy Framework, a pedagogically grounded model for transforming AI prompting from a technical input skill into an instructional design practice
rationale: The record is a conceptual article proposing a framework, not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). It also centres on teacher-side prompting in primary education, so it would fail the learner-facing intervention and STEM domain criteria too, but E6 is the first applicable code.

quote: teachers appreciate the creative affordances of generative AI to support generative learning activities but worry about time efficiency, usability, and accuracy
rationale: The AI is used by in-service mathematics teachers to adapt tasks for their own lesson planning, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. Study is qualitative-style exploration of teacher perceptions with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E1 as the first applicable code; E4 (in-service teachers) and E5 would also apply.

criteria.note: design is a pedagogical/illustrative essay with teaching examples, not an empirical comparison

quote: We contend that instructors can leverage GAI to assist them in quickly creating and implementing classroom-based simulation activities and demonstrations.
rationale: The record is a perspective/teaching-examples piece in political science. It describes instructors using GAI to build classroom tools, not learners interacting with GAI in a controlled comparison, and reports no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Also, AI is used by the instructor to prepare materials, which would independently trigger E1, but E6 is the first applicable code in the order of the protocol's logic since the study is not empirical; under the protocol order E1 comes first, so the record is better coded E1 given the teacher-only use. Political science is also non-STEM (E2), but the first applicable code by protocol order is E1 because AI is used only by the instructor.

quote: The results indicated that the GPA-5E approach in IVR science learning significantly improved students' academic achievement, self-efficacy, and collective efficacy compared to the traditional method.
rationale: At abstract stage, the record shows a generative AI pedagogical agent (GPA) that students interact with within an IVR 5E science lesson, a control group following the traditional 5E method (no generative AI), primary (sixth-grade) students, science content, and an academic achievement outcome, published 2025 in a journal. No positive evidence of failure on any criterion. Effect-size statistics and full-text language cannot be judged from the abstract, so the record advances to full text.

quote: The work systematically evaluates the performance of open-source LLMs (DeepSeek, GLM-4, Kimi) and close-source GPT-4 in assisting medical and engineering students learning through diverse question types.
rationale: The abstract describes a comparison of LLMs on question-answering accuracy. It does not show a learner-facing intervention with a control group that lacks generative AI, and it does not describe a comparison design. Medical education is excluded by the protocol, but engineering is also mentioned, so the STEM and population fit is unclear. Abstract-stage rules do not allow exclusion without positive evidence, so I am advancing it to full text for review of the design, the comparison, and the population.

quote: This qualitative study explores middle school students’ perspectives on the adoption of GenAI for learning.
rationale: The study is explicitly qualitative (interviews with 13 students), with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparison study meeting the protocol design requirements; the most direct code is E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a quantitative comparative design). Note that the protocol's E6 is "Not an empirical study", and a qualitative perception study is excluded as a design failure; E3 (no control group) or E5 (no quantitative outcome) would also apply, but E6 reflects the qualitative design best. Abstract evidence is clear enough to exclude.

quote: A mixed-methods approach was employed, incorporating surveys, open-ended reflections, and project evaluations.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-course case study with surveys and reflections, with no separate control group that avoids generative AI. Results are self-reported perceptions and self-ratings, not a quantitative learning measure. Population is non-STEM general education students and the course is AI literacy, so domain is also not clearly STEM. Exclusion is on E3 (no control group) as the first applicable code in the protocol order that is clearly supported by the abstract; E5 (perceptions only) would also apply.

quote: we analysed N = 60 biology lesson plans generated by the research team
rationale: ChatGPT-4o was used by the research team to generate lesson plans for teachers' planning; learners do not interact with the generative AI tool. This is teacher-side material preparation, so E1 applies. The study also has no control group and no learning outcome (it evaluates lesson plan quality), which would be further failures.

quote: The research uses the Research and Development (R&D) method with the ADDIE (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation) model.
rationale: Abstract-stage screen. Population (preservice physics teachers in higher education) and domain (physics education) appear to fit. The study is R&D with validation and pre/post N-Gain and Cohen's d on a 34-student sample. The abstract does not state whether there is a separate control group without generative AI; the design appears to be a single-group pre-post, which would be E3, but this is not explicit. Because the abstract does not give positive evidence of failure on comparison or design, it is not excluded at this stage. Flagged for full-text check of whether a control group exists. The record also has the intervention as GenAI-based teaching materials that students use, which should be checked at full text. Publication type and language are not verifiable from the abstract.

quote: First, allowing students to use LLMs led to a 36% average score increase compared to exams taken with only textbooks and notes.
rationale: Abstract suggests graduate bioprocess engineering students (STEM, higher education) using LLMs on exams versus textbook-only exams, which could match a control group without generative AI and an exam score outcome. However, the abstract does not make clear whether the comparison is between-group or within-student across exam conditions, so design and comparison cannot be confirmed. Also the study partly compares LLM models against each other and against human test-takers. No positive evidence of failure, so advance to full text.

quote: This paper deeply analyzes the current status of programming education in art colleges at home and abroad, pointing out core issues
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/position paper that analyzes the status of programming education and proposes a reform paradigm and countermeasures. It reports no experiment, control group, or quantitative learning data, so it is not an empirical study. The claim that GenAI "can significantly reduce cognitive load" is asserted without any reported data. Exclusion under E6 is supported by positive evidence of a non-empirical design at the abstract stage.

quote: A cross-sectional, mixed-methods survey was conducted with 126 students
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of student perceptions with no experimental or comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; it fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible designs) is applied as the first applicable code is arguably E3 (no control group); however, the design is a survey, which the protocol lists as an excluded design, so E6 is the best fit for a non-eligible empirical design. Under the code order, E1 could not be confirmed from the abstract (generative AI use is described, but the intervention is not clearly learner-facing learning activity) and E2 is unclear since Korean medicine content is not clearly STEM. Excluded on design and outcome.

criteria.intervention_note: generative AI mentioned but learner-facing use and control group not described

quote: Both quantitative and qualitative findings suggest that students view generative AI and the Island as valuable resources for learning and completing their projects.
rationale:
The abstract's outcomes are student perceptions, reported gains in understanding (self-reported), and regret about participation. No quantitative learning outcome such as achievement or problem-solving performance is described, and affective/perception outcomes are not extracted. Excluded under E5 on positive evidence from the abstract. The control-group design is not described, but E5 alone suffices.</rationale>

Published 2025 in a journal. No positive evidence of any criterion failing; the abstract's outcomes include performance, so E5 does not apply. Data sufficiency for SMD and the quasi-experimental wording (called both quasi-experimental and randomized) should be checked at full text.

quote: This quasi-experimental study compared GenAI-supported flipped learning (AI-FL) with reading-based flipped learning (R-FL) in an 11-week preservice chemistry course.
rationale: Abstract indicates a quasi-experiment with a reading-based comparison group, GenAI learner-facing pre-class activity, preservice chemistry teachers (higher education, counts as eligible), 2026 publication, and quantitative outcomes (lesson-design performance, attitude). Chemistry is STEM. However, the comparison is reading-based flipped learning, which is a non-AI comparison and therefore qualifies. Cannot yet confirm journal article status (Behavioral Sciences is an MDPI journal, likely eligible), full-text language, or whether effect size statistics are reportable. Abstract stage: no positive evidence of failure, so advance to full text for verification of data sufficiency and the attitude outcome being excluded as affective (lesson-design performance and self-regulated learning/critical thinking may still qualify as cognitive outcomes).

quote: The team introduced the YPMAK students to ChatGPT technology and trained them on how to use it for the learning process.
rationale: Community service ChatGPT training focused on English language (reading and grammar) comprehension, which is non-STEM content (E2). Abstract also describes no control group and only a post-training comprehension test and perception survey, so design/comparison are not evidenced. E2 is the first applicable code in order given the explicit non-STEM content.

quote: IBM Watson BEAT software, based on generative AI technology, was tested as an educational tool in the process of teaching music composition theory to flute students.
rationale: The abstract describes generative AI (IBM Watson BEAT) used by learners in a flute music composition course. Music is not among the protocol's STEM domains (science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, data science), which points to E2. However, the protocol's domain list is explicit and music is not listed, so the content clearly fails the domain criterion. Because the abstract gives positive evidence of a domain failure, the abstract-stage rule would support exclusion under E2. I am marking unsure rather than exclude, since the domain judgement is clear-cut but the record also lacks clarity on the comparison group (the abstract mentions an experimental group but not a control group explicitly) and design, and the researcher should confirm the E2 call. The intervention criterion is met. Comparison, design, and population are not clearly stated in the abstract.

quote: Using a generic zero-shot prompt, ChatGPT-5 Thinking and Gemini 2.5 Pro were each prompted to generate 1 CoPJ item for all 28 topics
rationale: The study is an evaluation of LLM-generated item quality by faculty reviewers. There is no learner interaction with the LLM, no control group, and no learning outcome; the planned learner comparison is future work. Positive evidence fails the intervention (not learner-facing), comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E1 would be the first failing code in order, since the LLM is used by faculty to prepare materials, not by learners. Coding E1 as the first applicable code. Note: the decision uses E5 as written below; see correction.

quote: Further, SPSS-based quasi-experimental findings confirmed that students who use ChatGPT apps have several risks that influence their creative thinking.
rationale: Abstract stage. Higher education students (tourism colleges) and a quasi-experiment are mentioned, so population and design are plausibly met. However, the study is largely a PLS-SEM survey of risk perceptions, and the abstract does not show a generative-AI-using learner condition versus a non-AI control group, nor a quantitative learning outcome (creative thinking is measured via perceptions/risk constructs). Domain is tourism statistics, which may be STEM-adjacent but is unclear. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so this is held for full-text review rather than excluded.

quote: Using cognitive clinical interviews with think-aloud protocols, the role of GenAI in students’ modeling activities is analyzed through the lens of distributed cognition.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative think-aloud interview study of students using GenAI for computational modeling in chemistry. There is no control group without generative AI, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion at E3 (no control group) is the first applicable code in order; the design is also qualitative (E5/E6 would also apply). Reporting E3 as the first applicable code per protocol order.

quote: A convergent parallel mixed-methods design was employed, combining structured teacher surveys adapted from DigCompEdu and Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK)-validated instruments, systematic classroom observations, and semi-structured interviews
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive mixed-methods study (surveys, observations, interviews) on teacher AI readiness and practices. It reports no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group and no learning outcome measure; outcomes are perceptions and practice descriptions. Exclusion is on E3 (no control group) as the first applicable code under the protocol's order; E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) and E6 (non-empirical design concern) would also plausibly apply, but the design is clearly empirical and the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group.

quote: Empirical results from one semester indicate significant improvements in students’ engagement, abilities to solve complex engineering problems, and systems thinking.
rationale: Abstract describes an industrial engineering course (STEM) with a DeepSeek-based LLM facility-planning system used by students, so intervention, population and domain appear met. However, the abstract does not state whether a control group without generative AI exists; it only reports one-semester improvements, which could be a pre-post single-group design (E3). Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is kept for full-text review. Year 2026 satisfies the date criterion; publication type is not stated in the record.

quote: This study analyzes how students’ attachment style to ChatGPT influences academic performance, with ethical orientation (idealism and relativism) as a moderating variable.
rationale: The design is a survey-based moderated regression on students' self-reported ChatGPT use (attachment style), not an experiment with a separate non-generative-AI control group. Accounting is also not clearly STEM. Abstract-stage evidence of the missing control group is positive, so exclusion is appropriate.

quote: AIPC는 예측형 및 생성형 AI의 개념, 원리, 활용 사례, 장단점 등을 시각화하였으며
rationale: Abstract (Korean) describes an AI principle card tool covering predictive and generative AI, applied to undergraduates in a learning project, with reported improvement in understanding and problem solving. However, the abstract does not describe a control group or comparison condition, and the design is not stated. Domain is plausibly engineering/AI but not explicit. None of the criteria show clear positive evidence of failure, so the record advances to full text for checking comparison, design, and outcome data. Generative AI being learner-facing is also not clearly established (the cards are a learning aid about AI). Per abstract-stage rule, unsure.

quote: Results indicated consistently high levels of perceived learning and engagement across the cohort, with average scores above 4.5 out of 5.
rationale: Classroom case study using a single-cohort Likert survey on perceived learning and engagement. There is no control group and no quantitative learning measure; outcomes are perceptions only, which the protocol excludes. Abstract gives positive evidence of E5 (perceptions only) and of a single-group design (E3 would also apply, but E5-type outcome failure is the clearest). Per code order, E3 (no control group) comes before E5, so the first applicable code is E3.

quote: Vietnamese in-service EFL teachers across different teaching experience levels
rationale: Participants are in-service EFL teachers, not K-12 or higher education students (E4). The study is also a survey-based comparison of teacher groups by experience, with no learner-facing GenAI intervention, no control group, and perception-based outcomes (self-rated competencies), and the domain is English language education rather than STEM. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing), but the abstract clearly establishes the population failure, so E4 is reported as the clearest disqualifier. Note: the abstract gives positive evidence of population failure, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.
rationale_note: Protocol says report first applicable code in order E1 through E10. E1 would apply first because no learner-facing GenAI intervention exists. Correcting that: exclusion code should be E1.

quote: A total of 1,836 middle school-level mathematical problem images were input to assess accuracy rates, error rates, and characteristics, patterns, and contexts of errors.
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT's performance on problem images, not learners interacting with it in a learning activity. There is no control group and no learner outcome; the design is a performance evaluation of the model. This is not an empirical study of learners, so E6 is the best-fitting code. Abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group and no learner-level outcome. Note: E1 (learner-facing intervention) could also apply, but the first applicable code in protocol order is considered; E1 precedes E6 in order, so E1 may be the more faithful code since learners do not interact with the tool. Reconsidering against protocol order: E1 applies first because no learner interacts with the tool.

quote: The findings indicate that performance expectations, effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating conditions, and hedonic motivation all positively impact the intention and behavior
rationale: The study is a survey-based technology acceptance model (UTAUT2, PLS method) of university teachers' beliefs. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and the participants are teachers rather than students. It is not an empirical trial of learning, so it fails on design, population, and outcome. Coded E6 as a non-experimental survey study, the first applicable code in the protocol's order is arguably E1 (no learner-facing intervention), but the abstract clearly shows the study is a survey, so E6 is the most accurate primary code. Excluded with confidence at abstract stage.
rationale_note: Note: the protocol says to report the first applicable code in order (E1 before E6). The intervention is not learner-facing, which arguably makes E1 the first applicable code. Auditor should consider E1 instead of E6.

quote: A quasi-experimental design was utilized with 54 students, using classroom exam evaluations. The study compared the educational performance of students using ChatGPT (experimental group) with those who didn't (control group).
rationale: Abstract describes a quasi-experimental study with ChatGPT experimental group vs control group without it, in university mathematics education, with exam performance as outcome. Journal status, date (2025), and effect-size data cannot be confirmed from the abstract, but no positive evidence of failure is present, so advance to full text.

quote: The guide is being used by colleagues and students and received positive anecdotal feedback.
rationale: This is a showcase describing the development of a student-facing guide on generative AI use. It is not an empirical study: there is no comparison group, no experiment or quasi-experiment, and no quantitative learning outcome. The only feedback reported is anecdotal. It is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). The abstract gives positive evidence of this failure, so the exclusion is made at abstract stage.
rationale_note: Domain is not STEM-specific (general study skills), so E2 could also be argued, but E6 is the first applicable code given the non-empirical design.

quote: I identify four cross-cutting themes
rationale: The record is an integrative conceptual analysis proposing a framework (AI-GLM) with propositions to be tested. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome data, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Under the code order, E1 could be argued as well, but the primary failure is that it is not empirical.

quote: This study evaluated the reliability of answers provided by four different major artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot using 125 periodontology exam questions
rationale: The study evaluates chatbot answers to archived exam questions posed by investigators; learners do not interact with the AI as part of a learning activity (E1 would apply on intervention grounds). Design is a single-condition evaluation of four chatbots with no non-generative-AI control group, so there is no comparison group (E3). Under the ordering rule the first applicable code is E1, since learner-facing interaction is absent. Coding E6 is inconsistent with that ordering; the correct first-applicable code is E1.

quote: This type of research is descriptive-quantitative, using a questionnaire survey method.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive-quantitative questionnaire survey of 46 physics students on perceptions of ChatGPT. There is no comparison group and no experimental design, and the measures are perceptions rather than a learning outcome. Exclusion code E3 is the first code that applies on positive evidence (no control group without generative AI). The design and outcome criteria also fail, but E3 is reported as the first applicable code in order. Stage is abstract, so the decision is made on this positive evidence.

quote: This scoping review evaluates existing theoretical and empirical evidence on TI-PrBL in mathematics education
rationale: The record is a scoping review of existing literature, not an empirical primary study with a control group. It fails the design criterion (no randomized or quasi-experimental design of its own) and is not an empirical study under E6. Generative AI is mentioned only as one of several tools in the review's themes. Other criteria cannot be assessed from the abstract.

quote: Here, we aim to explore the current uses and limitations of generative AI tools available for extension professionals and livestock producers.
rationale: This is a perspective/review-style commentary on generative AI in extension. It reports no controlled comparison with a learner control group and no learning-outcome data from a study. The only quantitative element is an informal query of OpenAI models (1000 iterations each) about stocking rates, which is not a learner-facing experiment with a control group. quote: This paper examines hallucinations in education, highlighting their causes, risks, and implications.
rationale: The record is a narrative review/framework paper on LLM hallucinations in education. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Per the exclusion code order, E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract, and E6 is the first code that applies on positive evidence.

quote: This experimental research examined the effectiveness of using chatbots in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) classrooms at a Chinese elementary school.
rationale: The study targets EFL oral English proficiency, which is language learning and not STEM, so it fails the Domain criterion (E2). The abstract also does not state whether the chatbots are generative AI, and the control group uses traditional methods. The E2 exclusion is decided on domain alone; the other criteria are not needed to reach it.

quote: This research article provides an extensive investigation into the integration of neural code comprehension and generative artificial intelligence across the software development lifecycle.
rationale: Abstract describes a longitudinal analysis and synthesis of existing literature ("By synthesizing contemporary advancements", "Through a rigorous analysis of existing empirical evidence"). It is a review/conceptual paper, not an empirical study with a control group, learners, or a quantitative learning outcome. No learner-facing generative AI intervention or STEM learning population is evident. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported by the abstract.

quote: Utilizing the Teaching Experimental Methodology (TEM), this study was conducted across three classroom sections, each comprising 38 to 42 students.
rationale: The abstract describes a Teaching Experiment Methodology study across three classroom sections with no mention of a control group or comparison condition without GenAI. This is positive evidence that the comparison criterion fails, so the record is excluded at abstract stage with E3. The design also appears to be a single-group teaching experiment, which would fail the design criterion as well.

quote: A mixed-methods descriptive–interpretive design was employed. Data were collected from 341 undergraduates
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive mixed-methods survey and reflexive thematic analysis of 341 undergraduates with no control group or experimental comparison. Design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported (survey perceptions only). Coded E3 as the first clearly failing criterion in protocol order is a judgement call; E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is also clearly evident and may be the more accurate first-applicable code given the protocol's ordering. Under the protocol order E1 to E5, E3 precedes E5, so E3 is reported.

criteria.exclusion_code_note: E6 chosen as first applicable on abstract evidence

quote: Based on an analysis of student portfolios, different forms of GAI use are identified, including its role as a source of visual inspiration, conceptual support, and assistance in decision-making processes.
rationale: The abstract describes a teaching innovation experience analysed through student portfolios and representative examples. It reports no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. This indicates a descriptive, non-experimental study, so it fails the design, comparison and outcome criteria. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense). The abstract alone does not provide a quantitative outcome, which points to E5, but E6 is the earlier applicable code for a qualitative, descriptive experience report. Full text could be checked if the researcher prefers E5.

quote: Examining six courses across the program, the study evaluates ChatGPT's performance on 18 assessments
rationale: Accounting education is not a STEM domain under the protocol (science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, data science). The study evaluates ChatGPT's performance on assessments rather than a learner-facing intervention with a control group and learning outcome, so it also lacks a comparison group and a quantitative learning outcome. E2 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: A four-level structured opinion survey was designed to capture both behavioral tendencies and emotional responses related to AI use.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey of undergraduate engineering students' usage behaviors, perceptions and emotional responses. This is a survey design with no experimental or comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical experimental study eligible under the protocol. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible design) applies; E5 would also apply since outcomes are perceptions and attitudes. E6 is chosen as the design-based reason for exclusion.

quote: The subjects of the study were 200 undergraduate students who were randomly split into two groups (experimental group [N = 100]; control group [N = 100]).
rationale: Abstract reports a DeepSeek (generative LLM) experimental group vs control group with randomized assignment of undergraduates, and quantitative critical/creative/reflective thinking scores analyzed with ANCOVA. Domain is EFL (language learning), which the protocol excludes as non-STEM; the abstract does not indicate any STEM content, so this is a likely E2 exclusion. Because the rule is to exclude only on positive evidence at abstract stage, and the control condition and the subject matter are not fully described, it is marked unsure for full-text check of the course content. Publication date 2026 meets the date criterion; venue is a journal. Thinking-skill scales are generic rather than clearly learning-achievement measures, which also needs checking at full text. Note: the quotes and other fields are kept to the abstract.

quote: This study selects five mainstream generative AI models (Tencent Yuanbao, Deepseek, Doubao, Kimi, and Wenxin Yiyan) as research subjects and uses 18 middle school mathematics problems
rationale: The study evaluates the generative AI models' own problem-solving performance on 18 test problems. There are no learners interacting with the AI, no control group, and no learner outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion order, the first code that applies is E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI), since the AI is not used by learners as part of a learning activity. Abstract evidence is strong enough to exclude on E1 rather than advancing the record.

quote: Adhering to PRISMA guidelines, this systematic review analysed peer‐reviewed articles published from 2013
rationale: This is a systematic review with meta-analysis of open- vs closed-book exams, not an empirical primary study. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention (LLMs are only discussed as a background concern). Per the protocol, reviews are excluded (E10 publication type, or E6 not empirical). The review is a publication-type exclusion; the protocol lists reviews under E10 ("Publication type not eligible") and E6 is for non-empirical studies. Since the protocol explicitly names reviews under publication type exclusions, E10 is the more specific code. Correcting to E10 is the appropriate code here.

quote: We used the PRISMA extension for scoping reviews to select articles for review and report the results.
rationale: This is a scoping review, which is a review article and not an empirical study. It reports no primary comparison group or quantitative learning outcome data. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). The review type alone is positive evidence of failure at the abstract stage.

quote: The PD, part of an NSF grant for three years, aims to teach STEM teachers form the Greater Boston area the fundamentals of Generative AI.
rationale: The population is in-service high school teachers receiving professional development, not K-12 or higher education students, so E4 applies. The abstract also describes a framework paper with no comparison group or quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion is based on positive evidence that the population criterion fails. Note that E4 is the first applicable code in order only if E1 does not apply; the intervention (teacher PD on GenAI) is not clearly learner-facing, but the population failure is the clearest and the record is excluded.

Quasi-experimental design with a randomly selected control class (traditional teaching) and experimental class; first-year college students in C programming (STEM); pre/post critical thinking test and academic resilience questionnaire (critical thinking test is a quantitative learning outcome). Intervention is a four-station lab rotation with peer code review; the abstract mentions generative AI as part of the model but does not clearly state that learners interact with a generative AI tool. This is unclear at abstract stage, so it should be resolved at full text by checking whether students used a generative AI tool. Abstract-stage rule: not excluded.

quote: The mixed-methods research design was used, involving structured surveys, behavioral usage data, and semi-structured interviews with undergraduate STEM learners
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational mixed-methods study (surveys, usage data, interviews) of trust levels among undergraduate STEM learners using AI tutors. There is no separate control group without generative AI, and the design is correlational, not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Exclusion is on E3 because the protocol requires a comparison group without generative AI, which is positively absent here. The abstract also does not confirm a generative model. Because the abstract gives positive evidence that the comparison and design criteria fail, exclusion is appropriate even at the abstract stage.

The abstract is a narrative overview of AI in physics education (discussion of challenges, policy, and future directions). It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Exclusion code E6 is the first applicable code in the order the protocol lists after E1-E5 would be considered; E1 and E3 to E5 are also not supported by positive evidence, so E6 is the best-fitting single code.

quote: The research design adopted for this study was the correlational design.
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational design using Pearson correlation, with no separate control group that avoids generative AI. Design criterion fails (correlational designs are excluded) and comparison is not met. Per protocol, the first applicable exclusion code is E3 (no control group without generative AI). The abstract gives positive evidence of a correlational design, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified. Population (SS2 students) and domain (mathematics) appear met; the outcome is a motivation measure plus an achievement test, which is ambiguous but not needed for the decision.

quote: This research employed a quantitative approach with an ex post facto design involving 157 students of MAN 2 Sinjai selected through total sampling.
rationale: The abstract describes an ex post facto survey-based design using PLS-SEM on questionnaire data relating self-reported generative AI usage intensity to self-regulated learning and learning independence. There is no separate control group without generative AI and no comparison group, so the comparison and design criteria fail. The outcome is self-reported learning independence and SRL from questionnaires, not a quantitative learning measure such as achievement. Exclusion code E3 is applied as the first failing criterion in the protocol's order, with E5 also a plausible fail. Population (senior high school students) fits.

quote: This study examines the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools on the grammatical accuracy and vocabulary range of undergraduate ESL learners.
rationale: The study concerns ESL academic writing (grammar and vocabulary), which is language learning and not STEM content, so it fails the Domain criterion (E2). This is the first applicable exclusion code in order. The intervention is described only as generic "AI tools", without indication that they are generative, but the domain failure is decisive regardless.

quote: Student Perceptions of ChatGPT in Mandatory EFL Writing Classes at a Korean University : A Case Study
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of student perceptions (case study design) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Domain is EFL writing, which is non-STEM. Excluded on E5 as the first applicable code in order would be E2 (non-STEM content) since the domain criterion fails clearly; per the protocol's ordering, E2 takes precedence over E3 and E5. Note: strictly, the first code in order that applies is E2.

quote: A quantitative research design was adopted to collect data from 550 postgraduate students across various Saudi universities and disciplines.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey-based structural equation model of students' knowledge, willingness, and concerns about generative AI. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI, so the comparison and design criteria fail. Outcomes are perceived learning and self-reported academic performance, not a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion is at the abstract stage on positive evidence of no comparison group and a survey design; E3 is the first applicable code in the order given.

quote: A matched-pair cluster-assigned field study conducted with 1,000 secondary school students across 20 schools in the Far North Region of Cameroon using a pre-test/post-test design with a comparison group
rationale: Generative AI SMS tutor (LLM-based) with a cluster-assigned comparison group and quantitative composite score outcome; secondary students. Design appears to be a controlled pre-post with comparison group, which is eligible. However, the abstract does not state the subject domain (curriculum content is not identified as STEM), so domain cannot be confirmed. Publication venue and type are not clearly a journal article per the abstract alone. Insufficient to exclude at abstract stage; advance to full text to check STEM content and publication type.

quote: This paper considers the educational benefits of ongoing collaboration between university lecturers and librarians supporting students within science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM).
rationale: The record is a position/collaboration paper by lecturers and librarians. It describes no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study with a controlled design, so E6 applies as the first failing code in order (E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract alone, but E6 is the decisive failure). No passage gives evidence of a comparison group or outcome data.

quote: The research employed a quasi-experimental post-test design without a control group
rationale: The abstract explicitly states a quasi-experimental post-test design without a control group, so no comparison group without generative AI exists (E3). The outcome is also motivation (IMMS), which is affective and not a learning measure, but E3 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: We present an experiment with database design theory assignments and demonstrate that while their capacity to reason logically is improving, LLMs are still prone to serious errors.
rationale: Abstract describes an experiment with LLM tutors on database design assignments (STEM/computer science, generative AI intervention learner-facing). However, the abstract does not state whether a control group without generative AI existed, the study design, the population (students vs. other), or whether a quantitative learning outcome with SMD-computable data was reported. Emphasis on LLM error analysis suggests possibly a use-case/evaluation study rather than a controlled comparison. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so advance to full text to check comparison, design, and outcome.

quote: A cross-sectional descriptive survey was conducted with 315 high school students from public and private schools in Banadir.
rationale: The design is a cross-sectional descriptive survey with no control group and no experimental comparison, so the comparison and design criteria fail (E3 applies as no control group without generative AI exists). Outcomes are self-perceived impacts and attitudes from a questionnaire, not a quantitative learning measure. Population (high school students) is met. Exclusion code E3 is reported as the first applicable code in the protocol order that is clearly positive from the abstract; the design is also not an eligible experimental or quasi-experimental design.
decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of a survey design with no comparison group.

quote: This study uses a quantitative survey method, involving 60 respondents from the Biology Education Study Program at a state university in Indonesia.
rationale: Abstract describes a single-group quantitative survey of students' perceptions of AI chatbots. There is no control group without generative AI, and the design is a survey, not an experiment or quasi-experiment. Outcomes are perceptions and acceptance, not a quantitative learning measure. Excluded on E3 as the first applicable code in protocol order (no comparison group). Note that E3 is the first code in order that applies given the missing control; design and outcome concerns also apply.

quote: We use the entirety of a UK Physics undergraduate (BSc with Honours) degree including all examinations and coursework to test if ChatGPT (GPT-4) can pass a degree.
rationale: The abstract describes GPT-4 being tested on degree examinations and coursework. It reports no separate control group of students without generative AI, and no comparison design. This is an evaluation of an AI model against an assessment standard, not a comparative study of learners. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group supports E3. Note that the criteria field for stage was not a valid key; the decision is recorded at abstract stage.

quote: This study explored the role of generative AI, particularly ChatGPT, in students’ self-directed learning (SDL) process. College students (n=15) from science-oriented programs were purposively sampled to be interviewed.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative interview study of 15 college students with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an experimental or quasi-experimental design with a comparison group, so it fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. Under the rule that exclusion codes are applied in order, E1 does not apply because ChatGPT is a generative AI tool used by learners. E6 (not an empirical study) is not strictly accurate since it is empirical qualitative research, so the best-fit code is E3 for lacking a control group without generative AI. The code is chosen as E6 only if the design is considered non-eligible; per protocol, E3 better describes the missing comparison. Final code: E3.

quote: The authors conducted an assessment of exercises submitted by students. Then, ChatGPT (from OpenAI) and Bard (from Google) were employed to evaluate each exercise
rationale: The abstract describes LLM chatbots evaluating student exercises (feedback generation), with the comparison being LLM output against expert teacher ground-truth evaluations. There is no separate control group without generative AI, and the design appears to be a tool-accuracy evaluation rather than a comparative experiment. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group supports exclusion at E3. Learner-facing use is also unclear, but E3 is the clearest failing criterion.

Embedded systems education is an engineering/STEM domain and undergraduate students are the population, so these criteria appear met. The abstract describes LLM use for knowledge graph construction, classroom Q&A, and case/simulation generation, but it reads as a discussion or position paper ("This paper examines the application potential... discusses implementation pathways") with no described comparison group, empirical design, or quantitative learning outcome. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is retained for full-text review to check whether an empirical controlled study with learning outcomes exists.

quote: Through a review of scientific databases, 158 primary studies published between 2022 and February 2025 were analysed using a six-dimensional codification scheme and six research questions.
rationale: The record is a systematic mapping study (secondary review of 158 primary studies), not an empirical primary study with a control group. It fails the Design and Comparison criteria and is not an empirical study under E6. Publication-type and date criteria are not the reason for exclusion. Abstract evidence is sufficient to exclude on E6.

quote: Title: From Inquiry to Simulation: Leveraging ChatGPT and Chatbots for Dilemma-Based Learning in Healthcare Education
rationale: The title places the study in healthcare education, which the protocol excludes as a health professions domain (E2 is the content code used for non-STEM content). The abstract is missing, so the other criteria cannot be assessed. Positive evidence of a non-STEM domain is present, so exclusion is supported at the abstract stage.
rationale_note: Healthcare education is treated as non-STEM under the protocol's Domain exclusion.

quote: The results of the methodological analysis show that the integration of generative AI and virtual laboratory cases can increase the didactic effectiveness of Biological Physics teaching
rationale: The abstract describes a methodological model and a "methodological analysis" rather than an empirical study with a control group and quantitative learning outcome. No comparison group or learning measure is reported, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Biological Physics in medical education is arguably STEM-adjacent, but the primary exclusion is E6. Decision is exclude at abstract stage on positive evidence that no empirical design is present.

quote: This study employed a quantitative cross-sectional survey involving 200 university students.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey clustering self-reported generative AI usage patterns. It has no intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; it is a survey design. Per the protocol's exclusion order, the first applicable code is E3 (no control group without generative AI). Note that E6 (not an empirical study) would also be arguable, but the design is an empirical survey, so E3 is the first code that clearly applies. No STEM content is evident from the abstract.

quote: This study uses a qualitative approach with a case study design, which involves observation, interviews, and documentation
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative case study using observation, interviews and documentation, with thematic analysis. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so the record fails the design, comparison and outcome criteria. The exclusion code is E6 because the study is not an empirical study that meets the protocol's quantitative design requirement. Its intervention is ChatGPT-based learning, but the focus is on School-Based Management, so no further decision on intervention is needed.

quote: This assessment moved the focus of assigned points from the correctness of the code to the effort and understanding of the code demonstrated by the student during in-person grading.
rationale: The abstract describes a change in grading/assessment approach for programming homework. Generative AI tools are discussed as a concern, but students do not appear to interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; the intervention is the in-person grading format. This is positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI, so E1 applies. Comparison is a prior semester (not a clearly separate concurrent control), which also raises design concerns, but E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: This study employed reflexive thematic analysis of open-ended interviews with 15 full-time faculty in graduate-level Library and Information Science (LIS) programs in the United States.
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of faculty perceptions (reflexive thematic analysis). It is not an empirical experiment with a control group or a quantitative learning outcome. Content is LIS, not STEM. Under the protocol's exclusion order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly the first failure since the intervention is unclear, and E2 (content not STEM) applies before E6 in order. Strictly, the first applicable code in sequence is E2 because LIS is not STEM content, so the exclusion code should be E2 rather than E6. Correcting: first applicable code is E2.

quote: Our analysis of instructional artefacts demonstrates that Gen AI helps in three ways: suggesting structural improvements, offering alternative professional phrasing, and enhancing readability.
rationale: Gen AI is learner-facing in a requirements engineering course (user story refinement), and RE is a software/computer science domain. However, the abstract describes an analysis of instructional artefacts and qualitative-sounding findings with no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome reported. Positive evidence that the outcome criterion fails: the reported findings are qualitative observations of artefacts, not a learning measure. Excluded at abstract stage on E5 with the note that the design also appears non-comparative.

quote: This research is experimental research using pre-test and post-test research methodology with a total of 62 participants, consisting of Group A and Group B.
rationale:
Higher education business administration innovators, with a two-group experimental design and innovation skill outcomes. Abstract does not state whether Group B used generative AI or whether a non-AI control exists (it may be a comparison of two AI-based conditions, which would be E3). Domain is business administration, not clearly STEM, so the domain fit is also uncertain. Effect size data not reported in the abstract. Needs full text to resolve comparison and domain.</rationale>
