quote: Using a two-step, mixed-methods approach, we examined the perceptions of ten online and distance learning students from diverse disciplines regarding the design of a hypothetical AI Digital Assistant (AIDA).
rationale: The study is a perception-based mixed-methods interview study of ten students about a hypothetical AI assistant. It has no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical intervention study meeting the protocol, so it fails on design, comparison and outcome. E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol sense) is the best fit for a qualitative perception study; the exclusion is clear from the abstract even though the code choice is a judgment call.

quote: The results indicate that the AI-supported PBL model significantly improved students’ academic performance, programming competence, and self-directed learning compared with conventional instruction.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study describes an LLM-based AI teaching assistant used by undergraduates in a Python data structures course, a controlled experiment with a conventional-instruction comparison, and academic performance/programming competence outcomes. Design (controlled vs. quasi-experimental), effect-size data, and publication type are not stated; missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record advances to full text.

quote: The students rated the overall scientific accuracy of the responses significantly differently
rationale: Students evaluated ChatGPT responses (perceived linguistic quality and scientific accuracy). The outcome is student perception rather than a quantitative measure of learning, so the protocol's outcome criterion is not met (E5). No control group without generative AI is described; all conditions are labelled ChatGPT or a sample solution, and the study does not appear to measure learning. Exclusion at abstract stage is based on positive evidence that the outcome is perception-only.

quote: The research employed a quantitative survey design, utilizing validated scales to measure familiarity, usage experience, and perceived learning impact.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey with no control group and no learning outcome measured by a quantitative test; perceptions and self-reported impact only. Survey design and perception-only outcomes fail the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. Per the exclusion code order, E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract, so the first clearly applicable code is E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a comparative/quantitative learning design is not met; the study is a survey). Given the protocol's strictness on design, E6 is used as the best-fitting code; the record is clearly outside the eligible design, so exclusion is supported despite the code being a judgment call.

quote: GenAI models were evaluated in a controlled, non-interactive environment using standardized prompts.
rationale: The generative AI models were benchmarked on MCQs in a non-interactive environment; learners do not interact with the tool as part of a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). The human comparison is a historical cohort of MSc students answering the same questions, not a control group of learners using a non-genAI condition, and the design is a benchmarking study rather than an experiment. E1 is the first applicable code in protocol order.

criteria.stage_note: descriptive-correlational survey design with no control group

quote: The study employed a descriptive-correlational research design involving 246 junior high school students
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive-correlational survey of 246 junior high students with no control or comparison group, so the study fails the comparison requirement. Its design is also a survey, which the protocol excludes. Per the protocol's code order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly failed at abstract stage, but the comparison failure is positive evidence, so the record is excluded as E3 (no control group without generative AI). Outcome is also questionable (self-reported attitudes, perceptions, and a grade-based academic performance measure), but the first applicable code is E3.

Cross-sectional online survey with descriptive statistics only; no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome (outcomes are AI use, usefulness, confidence, concerns). Not an empirical trial meeting the design criterion; coded E6 as a non-experimental survey study (first applicable code in order would be E1 only if intervention were clearly not learner-facing GenAI, which is unclear here, so E6 is the most direct failure). Medical education is also a health-professions context, which further argues against eligibility.

quote: This research is qualitative by applying case study design.
rationale: Qualitative case study of five English-program students' perceptions of ChatGPT for English language learning. Content is non-STEM (English language learning), so E2 applies. Also no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and qualitative design, so it would fail other criteria too.

quote: An open‐source, local LLM was used to score each comment according to four rubric criteria.
rationale: The LLM is used by researchers to score peer feedback comments, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity, so E1 applies (first applicable code). The study also has no control group and no learning outcome measure (reports IRR and feedback quality descriptives), which would fail E3 and E5 as well. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing.

quote: The aim of this study was to comparatively analyze the perceptions of students from public and private Latin American universities regarding GenAI
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey comparing perceptions (usefulness, trust, creativity, emotions) of students at public versus private universities. It has no learning outcome measured after an intervention, and there is no GenAI learning activity or control group without GenAI. Perception-only outcomes fail the quantitative learning outcome criterion, so E5 applies. Under the rule that a study is excluded only on positive evidence, this exclusion rests on the abstract's description of a cross-sectional perception survey. Design (survey) also fails, but E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order, so it is reported.

quote: Comparing the lexical complexity, syntactic complexity, accuracy, and fluency of the four groups
rationale: The study concerns second language (L2) writing, which is language learning and not STEM content. This is positive evidence that the domain criterion fails, so the record is excluded under E2. Other criteria appear met or unclear (2x2 quasi-experiment with a control group; GenAI used by learners; writing outcomes), but E2 is the first applicable code in order.
decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage on E2.

quote: Our study focuses on the estimation of the performance of GPT-4 and Claude 3.5 Sonnet in laboratory-related image recognition tasks
rationale: The study evaluates model accuracy on image recognition of lab devices. It involves no learners, no control group, and no learning outcome in students; it is a model performance evaluation. Positive evidence of failure on comparison/design and outcome criteria (E5 applies as no quantitative learning outcome; the study measures model accuracy, not learning). Under the rule of first applicable code, E1 (learner-facing intervention) is not clearly established either, but E5 is the most evident failure. No learners participate per the abstract.

quote: Compared with conventional teacher feedback, the model fosters autonomy, reflection, and frequent revisions
rationale: The study is set in a college English writing course (L2 writing), which is language learning and non-STEM content, so the domain criterion fails (E2). The abstract also gives no clear quantitative learning outcome or statistics for a comparison, but E2 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: The survey results based on a student sample in Taiwan show that internship experience is more significant than ethics instruction on swaying ethical perceptions and behavioral inclinations of adopting AI applications.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey study of communication students. Surveys are excluded by the design criterion, and the outcomes are ethical perceptions and behavioral inclinations (perceptions/attitudes), not a quantitative learning measure. Content is communication ethics rather than STEM. Because the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design (not an experiment), the record is excluded as not an empirical study eligible under the protocol's design rules; the first applicable code in order would be E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) or E2 (not STEM), but the abstract does not clearly establish these, and the clearest failing criterion is the survey design with perception-only outcomes. Coding follows the protocol order for the strongest positive evidence.

quote: This mixed-methods study combined a one-group pretest-posttest design with qualitative content analysis.
rationale: The abstract describes a one-group pretest-posttest design with no control group, which is positive evidence of failure on the comparison criterion (E3). The content is nursing care and clinical communication, which is health professions education and so also outside the STEM domain, but the protocol's ordering places E3 first among applicable codes for this record's stage decision. Exclusion is clear from the abstract alone.

quote: A 9‐week course was implemented for 40 Chinese undergraduates, who completed 5 rounds of collaboration with a GenAI chatbot named ERNIE Bot.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group process study of undergraduates collaborating with a GenAI chatbot (ERNIE Bot). There is no control group without generative AI, and the analysis is of conversation codes and epistemic network analysis rather than a learning outcome compared across groups. Positive evidence of no comparison group supports E3. The outcome also appears not to be a quantitative learning measure (E5 is a possible alternative), but E3 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: The study designed a questionnaire, carried out a questionnaire survey, and statistical analysis.
rationale: The abstract describes a questionnaire survey on acceptance and attitudes (technology acceptance model) with no experimental or comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. This is a survey design, so it is not an empirical experiment meeting the design criterion. The exclusion code is E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible design); the survey is not a learning-outcome study. Positive evidence of failure is present for design and outcome, so exclude at abstract stage.

quote: This study used a descriptive survey design as the research was interested in both the idea and attitudes of respondents
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey on perceptions of ease of use and usefulness of ChatGPT among law students. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and law is not STEM. Survey design is not an empirical experimental design eligible here, so it is excluded as not an empirical study under E6 (the first applicable code in order would be E2 for non-STEM content, but the design and outcome failures are decisive; E2 is the first code in sequence that applies on the domain). Per protocol order, E2 applies first because content is law, not STEM.

quote: Data were collected using a structured questionnaire adapted from previously validated instruments and analyzed through descriptive statistics and independent-samples t-tests.
rationale: Study is a perception survey on ChatGPT for English vocabulary learning. Content is English as a foreign language, which is non-STEM (E2). It also has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome (perceptions only), and a survey design, so it would fail E3, E5, and E6 as well. Per the code order, E2 is reported first. The E2 failure is clear from the abstract, so the exclusion is justified at this stage.

quote: This publication takes a closer look at three technologies: virtual reality (VR) applications, the use of smartphones as measuring devices, and the use of numerical algorithms and the Julia programming language in the age of GenAI-Tools.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/position publication about course design in engineering mechanics. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is not clearly established from the abstract, so the first applicable code is E6, not an empirical study. Exclusion is based on positive evidence that the record is not an empirical study.

quote: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 512 pharmacy students at King Khalid University. A structured questionnaire assessed demographics, knowledge, attitudes, and practices.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional questionnaire survey of attitudes and practices with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Survey designs and perception-only outcomes fail the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E5 is given because the outcomes are perceptions and self-reported attitudes rather than a measured learning outcome; the design also fails E3 (no control group) and the study is not an experiment.

quote: A quantitative analysis was conducted to assess the relationship between prompt techniques and response quality.
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational/regression analysis of students' prompt techniques and ChatGPT response quality. There is no described control group that does not use generative AI, so the comparison criterion appears not met. Positive evidence of no comparison group is present in the abstract (single exploratory analysis of prompts), so exclusion at abstract stage is justified with code E3. Design also appears correlational, which would be a further failure.

quote: Assessing ChatGPT's Performance Compared to Dental Students in an Undergraduate Pediatric Dentistry Exam: Comparative Cross-Sectional Study
rationale: Content is pediatric dentistry, a health professions field, not science, mathematics, engineering, computer science, or data science. Also, the study is a comparative cross-sectional design in which ChatGPT answered the same exam questions as students; students did not interact with the AI as a learning activity, and there is no clear learner-facing control group without generative AI. Excluded on the first applicable code in order, E2 (non-STEM content). Under the protocol order, E1 is checked first; the abstract does not clearly show learner-facing use, so E2 is the code applied here.

quote: This type of research is field research using a qualitative approach. Researchers conducted in-depth interviews as a data collection technique.
rationale: The study is a qualitative field study based on in-depth interviews, with no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and Arabic language content (non-STEM). Under the protocol's order, E1 does not apply (students do use ChatGPT, a generative tool). E2 (Arabic language is non-STEM) is the first code that applies in order of the protocol codes, so the correct first applicable code is E2 rather than E6. Excluding with E2 as the first applicable code.

criteria.quote: Quantitative results show that nearly all students use AI in some form—with ChatGPT being the most common— and usage remains consistent across genders.
criteria.rationale: Abstract describes a survey-style perception and usage study of secondary students with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Reports only usage and perceptions, which the protocol excludes. Under the code order, E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). Design also appears non-experimental, but E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order from E1-E4 being unclear or met.

quote: Quantitative results show that nearly all students use AI in some form—with ChatGPT being the most common— and usage remains consistent across genders.
A descriptive survey design was employed involving a population of 287 Biology teachers
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of in-service secondary Biology teachers on awareness, perception, and utilization of GenAI. It has no learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. Survey designs are not empirical experiments eligible under the protocol, and the population is in-service teachers, which is excluded. Under the code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing) is the first applicable code, but E6 (not an empirical study/ineligible design) is the most accurate primary reason for a survey. Note: the code ordering would place E1 first; the decision applies E6 as the design-based failure.

quote: Psychological and Behavioural Impacts of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Independent Learning among University Students: A Prisma-Guided Structured Literature Review
rationale: The record is titled and described as a PRISMA-guided structured literature review, which is a review rather than an empirical study. It therefore fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). The abstract gives no experimental design, comparison group, or quantitative learning outcome. Fails on design as well, since a review has no eligible design. Coded E6 as the first applicable code after the intervention and domain checks, which remain unclear from the abstract.

Abstract describes a classroom action research study with a single cohort of 40 senior secondary students (physical computing with micro:bit). It reports survey percentages and thematic analysis, with no separate control group that avoids generative AI. Single-group design with no comparison means E3 applies. Intervention is physical computing; the abstract does not describe learners using a generative AI tool as part of the activity, so E1 could also be argued, but the comparison failure is the clearest positive evidence. Outcomes are largely perceptions. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of no control group.

The abstract describes a method for LLM-based thematic transformation of datasets for case-based data science learning. It reports no experimental comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; the claims about engagement and pedagogical advantages are not learning measures, and the paper appears to be a methods/design paper. Excluded at E5 as no quantitative learning outcome is evident. Note that the design and comparison are also not described, so this is a judgment on the abstract alone.

criteria.stage_note: abstract-stage review; data and publication type not verifiable from abstract

quote: the 30-student strong control group had traditional flipped instruction. Cognitive test data, psychomotor tests, and self-reported learning questionnaires measured data.
rationale: Abstract describes an AI chatbot-supported flipped learning group for vocational high school computer programming students, compared against a traditional flipped instruction control group, in a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest design with cognitive (procedural knowledge, coding and debugging) outcomes and reported effect sizes. No abstract-level evidence of failure on any criterion. Chatbot is presumed generative given it is an AI chatbot, but this is not explicitly stated; full text should confirm the generative nature and that the control group does not use generative AI. Journal status and full-text data sufficiency are not verifiable from the abstract, but the venue appears to be a journal.

quote: The Impact of Kahoot and ChatGPT Educational Technologies on Nursing Students' Sexual Health Knowledge and Attitudes
rationale: Title indicates the content is sexual health education for nursing students, which is health professions education and not STEM under the protocol. No abstract is available. Exclude on E2 (content not STEM). Note that the title also mentions attitudes, which would be affective and not extracted. The record is excluded at the abstract stage on positive evidence from the title alone.

quote: "employed. The respondents were 76BSEd Math students" and "a quantitative descriptive-correlational research design was employed"
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive-correlational survey design with no control group receiving a non-generative-AI condition; ChatGPT use is measured by questionnaire rather than assigned as an intervention. Positive evidence of a failed comparison and design criterion is present, so exclude under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Note the design is also not experimental or quasi-experimental, which would be a further failure of the design criterion.

quote: This study explored how AI scaffolding helped support English oral communication among Thai and Chinese EFL university students
rationale: The study concerns English as a foreign language oral performance, which is language learning and non-STEM content, so E2 applies. The abstract also describes a single comparative case study of ten students with no control group that does not use generative AI, which would independently fail E3 and the design criteria. Under the rule that the first applicable code is reported, E2 is given. Quote is from the abstract, though the exact supporting wording for E2 is the EFL focus, which is quoted above.

quote: This study investigates the experiences of Dhaka University students using ChatGPT (free version) for science education theses, identifying differences between users and non-users. Utilizing semi-structured questionnaires and a case study methodology
rationale: Abstract describes a case study using semi-structured questionnaires and thematic analysis of experiences, which is a qualitative design, not an experiment with a quantitative learning outcome. No quantitative learning measure is reported. Exclusion at abstract stage is justified by positive evidence of a qualitative case study design (E6 not an empirical quantitative study; the code E6 is used as the closest fit for non-experimental/qualitative design). Design and outcome criteria fail on the abstract's own description.

quote: "an exploratory and correlational study conducted with 37 computer science students who used ChatGPT as a support tool"
rationale: The abstract describes an exploratory correlational study of 37 students who all used ChatGPT, with no separate control group that did not use generative AI. Correlational designs are excluded by the design criterion, and there is no comparison group, so E3 applies as the first failing code. Grades are mentioned, so the outcome is at least plausibly quantitative, but the comparison and design failures are sufficient.

criteria.outcome_note: formative achievement mentioned in title only

quote: Implementing a POE–Socratic ChatGPT routine in Jordanian Tawjihi physics (Grades 11–12): student reactions, group process, and formative achievement
rationale: Abstract is not indexed; only the title is available. The title indicates a ChatGPT (generative AI) routine with Grades 11-12 physics students (STEM, school population), and a formative achievement outcome. Nothing in the title shows a failed criterion, but the control group, study design, and whether achievement data support an SMD cannot be judged from the title. Per the abstract-stage rule, advance to full text for these checks.

The record is titled as a study on ChatGPT overreliance and writing skill, but the abstract describes a descriptive survey of teachers' and school heads' perceptions of science teaching strategies (lecture, lab, demonstration, inquiry, cooperative learning). It contains no generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learner quantitative outcome. The abstract is inconsistent with its title, but the abstract gives positive evidence that the study is a perception survey without an intervention, so it is excluded under E1 as not learner-facing generative AI, with E6 (not an empirical intervention study) being the more fitting code. Note the first applicable code in order is E1 because no learner-facing generative AI is described; the abstract contains no such intervention.

quote: A cross-sectional descriptive study was carried out across various NGOs in India
rationale: Abstract describes a cross-sectional descriptive survey of access and usage perceptions, with descriptive statistics only and no control group receiving a non-generative-AI condition. No quantitative learning outcome is reported (usage and perceptions only). Excluded on design/comparison (E3) as the first applicable code per protocol ordering; the study also lacks a learning outcome (E5), which would apply at a later code if E3 were not triggered. Positive evidence of no control group and non-experimental design is present in the abstract.

quote: Studi ini bertujuan untuk menyelidiki persepsi mahasiswa Pendidikan Bahasa Jerman terhadap penggunaan ChatGPT sebagai media pembelajaran.
rationale: Study is a descriptive survey of German language education students' perceptions of ChatGPT. German language learning is non-STEM (E2). Also no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, but the first applicable code in order is E1 check: intervention is generative AI used by learners, so E1 does not apply; E2 is the first failing criterion in order. Outcome is perception-only (E5 also applies but E2 comes first in the listed order only if E1 passes, which it does).

criteria.stage_note: descriptive correlational design, no control group

quote: A descriptive correlational design was employed.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive correlational survey design of 303 students with no comparison group receiving or not receiving generative AI, and no learning outcome measured as an intervention effect. Positive evidence that the comparison criterion fails, so excluded under E3. Note the design also fails the protocol's Design criterion (correlational designs excluded), but E3 is the first applicable code given the no-control-group evidence; the protocol order lists E3 before the design issue is not a code, so E3 is reported as the closest code.

quote: This study examined the authors' experiences with teaching technical material in English to international students using mixed-language classrooms.
rationale: The abstract describes English Medium Instruction with a Language Responsive Delivery Model, an action research study of instructor practice. Generative AI appears only as a future trend ("integrating generative AI, large language models..."), not as a learner-facing tool used in the study. No control group is described, and the design is action research with classroom observation rather than a randomized or comparison-group design. Exclusion E1 applies because the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. Codes are applied in order and E1 is the first that applies on the abstract.

quote: Leveraging the GPT-3.5 Large Language Model (LLM) and a NAO social robot, the research investigates the feasibility and effectiveness
rationale: At abstract stage: the robot uses GPT-3.5 (generative LLM) with learners interacting with it, primary school maths (STEM), and a cognitive outcome is mentioned. However, the abstract does not state whether there is a control group without generative AI; it reports a "significant improvement" with no mention of a comparison. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is advanced to full text to check the design and comparison, and the effect-size data.

criteria.rationale: Abstract describes teachers' experiences and readability evaluation of AI-generated problems, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome for students. Exclusion at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is based on positive evidence in the abstract that the reported measures are perceptions and readability, not student learning. Design also appears non-experimental (qualitative/descriptive), but the first applicable code in order is E5 given the protocol's ordering, which places E3 before E5; the abstract gives no evidence of a comparison group, so E3 is not positively evidenced. Note: strictly, E3 would be the first code in order only if a no-AI comparison were evidenced, which it is not.

quote: evaluates the readability of AI-generated problems
rationale: The abstract describes teachers' experiences with the MagicSchool tool and a readability evaluation of AI-generated problems. It reports no control group and no student learning outcome measured quantitatively. Positive evidence of a failing criterion is present (no quantitative learning outcome; the design appears descriptive), so exclude under E5. Note that E6 (not an empirical study) could also be argued; the abstract reads as a descriptive exploration, but E5 is the clearest positive failure visible in the abstract.

quote: The findings showed that the success rates of GPT-4o and GPT-4 were close to each other, with a slightly higher success rate of GPT-4o.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study compares the performance of several AI chatbots solving textbook problems (ChatGPT versions, MathGPT, Gemini) and reports perceptions from students and teachers. No control group without generative AI is described; the comparisons are between generative AI tools themselves and the study evaluates chatbot outputs rather than learners' learning outcomes. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is present, so exclude under E3. Quantitative learning outcome is also doubtful (success rates of AI solutions, not learner achievement).
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on E3 based on the absence of any non-generative-AI comparison group.

quote: The article analyzes the theoretical foundations and practical opportunities of using artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in primary school mathematics education.
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical/analytical article that reviews international experience and discusses opportunities and challenges. It does not report an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome data. It is not an empirical study, so it fails E6. Although the abstract mentions determining impact on pupils' learning outcomes, this is framed as a review of others' experience rather than an original experiment, and no comparison group or effect data are described.

criteria.stage_note: observational screen-recording and sequential analysis; no control group without generative AI described

quote: Screen recordings of 363 second-year students completing an individual Python 3.12 data-visualisation assignment were coded into 3985 activity episodes and analysed using descriptive statistics, lag-1 sequential analysis, and cognitive network analysis
rationale: The study is observational: it codes screen recordings of students using ChatGPT in a programming assignment and analyses behavioural sequences. No control group without generative AI is described, and the comparison of high- and low-achieving students is a comparison of observed behaviour distributions, not an intervention contrast. Fails the comparison and design criteria, so it is excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Design is non-experimental, so E6 could also be argued, but E3 is the first applicable code in the stated order of the protocol's comparison requirement.

quote: Students' satisfaction, virtual patient's accuracy, its realism, and quality were evaluated with a quantitative survey.
rationale: The study is a survey measuring satisfaction, perceived realism, and accuracy of a GPT-4 anamnesis role-play bot. No learning outcome is measured and there is no control group, and the domain is health professions education, which is excluded. E5 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported by the abstract (no quantitative learning outcome; only perceptions and satisfaction). Under the abstract-stage rule, this is positive evidence of failure, so exclude.
rationale_note: Also outside domain (health professions education, E2 would apply, but E1-E4 are checked in order: intervention is generative AI and learner-facing, so E1 does not apply; E2 is the first failing code in order). Correction: the first applicable code in protocol order is E2.

quote: The experimental group (N= 21) participated in CCL, while the control group (N= 15) engaged in non-ChatGPT-assisted collaborative learning (NCCL).
rationale: Abstract describes a quasi-experiment with a non-ChatGPT control group (NCCL), ChatGPT as learner-facing generative AI, undergraduates, and a learning performance outcome, so no exclusion is evident. STEM status is unclear: the course is framed as STEM and entrepreneurship, with cultural product creation, so the domain needs full-text checking. Quasi-experimental design with a comparison group is consistent with eligibility, but effect-size data cannot be verified from the abstract. Advanced to full text.

quote: This study employs a quantitative approach with an explanatory research design using a survey method.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey (SEM-GSCA on questionnaire data from 193 vocational students) testing TPB relationships. It has no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; it measures attitudes and behavioural intention. Design and outcome criteria are clearly not met, so it is excluded. E6 (not an empirical study) is not the accurate label for a survey, but under the protocol's ordering the first applicable code should be checked: E1 cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract, and E2 is unclear, so the strongest clear failure is the absence of a control group and learning outcome. Recording E6 as the closest fit for a non-experimental design that fails the design criterion.

quote: Through the exploratory thematic analysis of 117 interview transcripts, 370 interaction records and 1,694 minutes of screen recordings, we identified 14 interaction patterns
rationale: Abstract describes an LLM (ChatGPT) learning environment for students, a data science writing task, and an experiment. However, the methods appear qualitative (thematic analysis of interviews and screen recordings) with no mention of a control group, quantitative learning outcome, or effect sizes. Design and outcome criteria cannot be confirmed from the abstract, and the study appears likely to fail comparison/design/outcome at full text. Not excluded at abstract stage per rule 2; advance to full text to check for a control group and quantitative outcomes.

quote: To the Editor: Boscardin and colleagues1 describe optimizing generative artificial intelligence (AI) use in several domains of medical education
rationale: The record is a letter to the editor offering commentary and recommendations. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Medical education framing also falls under the health professions exclusion, but E6 is the first applicable code in order of the protocol's listed codes, since E1 through E5 are not clearly established from the text.

quote: This study examines students' perceptions and experiences in using ChatGPT, an artificial intelligence-based application, in learning English writing.
rationale: Content is English writing (language learning), which is not STEM, so E2 applies first in the code order. The study is also a mixed-methods perception study with questionnaires and interviews, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (E3/E5 would also apply), but E2 is the first applicable code.

Generative AI (ChatGPT) feedback versus routine instructor feedback control with a quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test control group design; intervention and comparison appear met. Population is pre-service physics teachers in a mechanics lab course, which the protocol counts as higher education, and physics is STEM. However, the primary outcomes are inquiry-based science teaching self-efficacy (affective, which the protocol says is not extracted) and feedback literacy. Whether any non-affective quantitative learning outcome exists, and whether statistics are reportable, cannot be determined from the abstract. Left as unsure for full-text review of outcomes and data.</rationale>

The exclusion code reported is E3 (no comparison group) as the first applicable code in order; the design failure is also evident. Positive evidence of lacking a control group is present in the abstract, so exclusion is justified.

rationale: Experimental design with control group and college students, but the abstract's outcome is self-reported interpersonal trust in information authorship, not a quantitative learning measure. However, the abstract does not describe the full outcome set, and the intervention is GenAI-authored videos (learners watch rather than interact with GenAI), and the domain is not stated. Because the abstract does not give clear positive evidence on all criteria and full text may report a learning outcome, I return unsure for full-text review rather than excluding at abstract stage. Likely E5 at full text.

quote: The system was able to identify distraction and recall learners back to class.
rationale: The abstract describes a system design and development study with no comparison group, no reported experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It reports system capability (identifying distraction, recalling learners) rather than learning measures. Positive evidence of failure exists for the design (no control group described) and outcome (no learning measure), so exclusion is warranted at abstract stage. Exclusion code E5 is applied as the outcome criterion is the clearest failure, though E3 (no comparison group) could also apply.

quote: This article presents a systematic analysis of the application of large language models in academic software programming education.
rationale: The abstract describes a systematic analysis/review of the literature rather than an empirical study with a control group. It is not an empirical primary study, so it fails the design requirement and is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Although it mentions experimental studies with students among the reviewed literature, the record itself is a review and does not report its own comparison data.

quote: This approach helped enhance engagement and involvement and significantly improved learning outcomes.
rationale: Abstract describes a ChatGPT-assisted PBL activity in a Unit Operations course (STEM, higher education). It claims improved learning outcomes but does not state a comparison group, design, or quantitative outcome data; the abstract reports mainly student perceptions (90% reported increased engagement). Comparison and design cannot be determined from the abstract, so the record is passed to full text rather than excluded on missing information.

quote: This paper presents an approach to introduce physics students to the basic concepts of large language models (LLMs) using Python-based activities in Google Colab.
rationale: Abstract describes a physics-student learning activity with GPT-2 and Word2Vec (generative AI, learner-facing), which is consistent with eligibility. However, the abstract describes a teaching approach/paper with no mention of a control group, comparison design, or any quantitative learning outcome. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is passed to full text to check design, comparison, and outcomes. Publication type (journal vs. other) also needs confirmation at full text.

quote: This paper proposes a theoretical framework for incorporating AI chatbots into education, boosting students' mathematical problem-solving competence.
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical framework and model rather than an empirical study, which suggests E6 may apply. However, the abstract does not explicitly state absence of data, and it mentions "student data analysis" and a title implying an intervention for high school students in Vietnam. Under the abstract-stage rule (exclude only on positive evidence), I cannot confidently exclude. No comparison group or quantitative outcome is reported in the abstract, but missing information is not evidence of failure. Advance to full text to check whether an empirical controlled study exists.

ChatGPT is a generative AI tool used by higher education students, so intervention and population appear met. The abstract mentions pre- and post-implementation assessments but no control group, so comparison and design are unclear. Domain is not stated; the study is framed around general educational innovation rather than STEM content. Outcomes mix quantitative pre/post measures with perceptions and qualitative data. Under the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so this record is advanced to full text for checking of comparison, design, domain, and outcome.

quote: The purpose of this study is to report on the opinions and use of AI by K-12 teachers enrolled in a graduate education leadership program over the course of two years.
rationale: The abstract describes qualitative data on teachers' opinions and use of AI, with no control group, no experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. Population is in-service K-12 teachers in a graduate leadership program, not STEM students. Positive evidence of failure on comparison/design/outcome exists, so excluded. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the most direct fit for the comparison failure; E5 or E6 could also apply, since the design is qualitative and non-empirical in the experimental sense. Choosing E3 as first applicable per the code order is a judgment call; the record is clearly ineligible.

quote: Evaluations were conducted by three human evaluators and ChatGPT (GPT-4o).
rationale: The study evaluates student-generated user stories with ChatGPT as a rater, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. ChatGPT is used by evaluators, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). There is also no control group without generative AI described in the abstract, and the design is a rater agreement comparison rather than a controlled learning experiment. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: A descriptive survey design was employed, with a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire administered to 120 students
rationale: Abstract describes a descriptive survey of student perceptions in Malay language learning. Malay language is non-STEM, so E2 applies first in the code order. The study also has no control group and reports only perceptions (would also fail E3, E5, and the design criterion), but the first applicable code is E2.

quote: AI used only by the teacher to prepare materials. -- Here ChatGPT-5 is used by faculty to grade student exams, not as a learner-facing tool.
rationale: The generative AI (ChatGPT-5) is used to grade pharmacy student exams; students do not interact with it as part of a learning activity. This is not learner-facing generative AI, so E1 applies (AI used only for grading / by faculty). No control group without generative AI is evident either (all conditions use ChatGPT grading vs human gold standard), but E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: The research findings from this narrative review reveal several benefits of using AI chatbots in education.
rationale: The abstract describes a narrative review, not an empirical study. There is no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome reported. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies as the first failing criterion in protocol order. quote: Qualitative data from a second-year journalism unit at an Australian global campus in Sarawak, Malaysia, reveal that students already use GenAI strategically

Journalism content is not STEM, which is also a failing criterion (E2 would be the first code in order, but E1/E2 ordering: intervention is GenAI-based so E2 applies first). Excluding under E6 as not an empirical quantitative study. The journalism domain is clearly non-STEM.

quote: AI-generated reports from general, organic, analytical, physical, inorganic, and biochemistry courses were graded as if they were student reports and analyzed for grade distributions and common strengths and weaknesses.
rationale: The study grades ChatGPT-generated lab reports and surveys students about awareness and use. It has no control group that lacks generative AI and no separate learning-outcome comparison; the design is descriptive. Exclusion code E3 applies because there is no comparison group. The survey data are perceptions and do not count as a learning outcome.

quote: This study conducted in-depth interviews with a diverse sample of faculty members and students in higher education
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study exploring perceptions of ChatGPT and academic integrity. It has no comparison group, no quantitative learning outcome, and is not an empirical experimental design; it fails the design and outcome criteria. Under the rule of first applicable code in order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) could be argued as unclear, but E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a quantitative design) applies most directly to a qualitative perception study. Domain is not STEM-specific per the abstract, which is a further gap.

criteria.rationale_note: Abstract describes a software system (EQDL essay question database) built with generative AI for question generation; no learner interaction with a generative AI tool, no control group, no learning outcome data.

Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study); E1 could also be argued since the AI is not learner-facing, but the first applicable code in order is E1. Reconsidering the order: E1 applies first because the generative AI is used by the system builders/tutors, not learners, so the code should be E1.

There is no control group or comparison condition, and no learning outcome measured against a comparator. Positive evidence of a failed comparison criterion is present, so the record is excluded at abstract stage under E3. Outcome also appears not to be a learning measure (system similarity scores), but E3 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Our mini-experiment compared five Socratic tutoring strategies—guided discovery, assumption checking, comparative questioning, sequential scaffolding, and clarification questions—on two CRUXEval Python problems
rationale: The abstract describes comparing only generative AI prompting strategies across three AI assistants, with no control group lacking generative AI. Two or more generative AI variants compared with no non-AI group meets the E3 exclusion rule. The record is also a 2026 mini-experiment with rubric-graded conversations rather than learner outcomes, so the outcome and population are unclear, but E3 alone is sufficient.

quote: It proposes a comprehensive K-12 curriculum framework for PE, grounded in Backward Design principles and leveraging Project-Based Learning (PBL) and Computational Thinking (CT)
rationale: The paper is a conceptual/framework proposal (curriculum and assessment framework, argument-based), not an empirical study. No experiment, control group, or quantitative learning outcome is described in the abstract. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Prompt engineering is not clearly STEM content, but that was not needed for the code.

quote: This study examines the impact of Large Language Models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, on the development of academic critique skills among fourth-year Computer Science undergraduates
rationale: Abstract describes ChatGPT use by undergraduate Computer Science students (generative AI, higher education). It compares student-crafted vs ChatGPT-enhanced critiques, which appears to be two conditions of the same learners rather than a non-generative-AI control group, and outcomes are readability metrics of texts, not clearly a learning outcome. Domain (Computer Science course, but writing task) and comparison/outcome validity cannot be determined from the abstract. No positive evidence of failure at abstract stage, so unsure; resolve at full text.

quote: PLS-SEM analysis revealed that as long as pre-service teachers have AI-specific technological and pedagogical knowledge, they formulate higher phases of prompts
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational/PLS-SEM analysis of pre-service teachers' prompts and rubric-rated lesson plans, with no control group receiving a non-generative-AI condition. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison, and the outcome is rubric-based lesson plan quality rather than a learning outcome. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) applies as the first failing criterion; design and outcome also appear not to be met. Domain is unclear (lesson planning, not explicitly STEM).

quote: The data were collected via an ad hoc questionnaire administered to a sample of sixty-seven students
rationale: The study is a questionnaire-based survey of perceptions of ChatGPT among pre-service English teachers. It has no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; it reports only perceptions and usage. Excluded at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). It would also fail E3 (no comparison group) and the domain is not clearly STEM (English teaching in primary education). Because the abstract gives positive evidence of failure on outcome and design, exclusion is appropriate even at abstract stage.

quote: An end-of-semester student survey was conducted, and 966 students participated in the survey.
rationale: Study compares ChatGPT-using coding classes with classes using the standard method, in a STEM (basic coding) university course. However, the only outcomes reported are satisfaction and perception measured by survey, which are excluded as perception/satisfaction-only outcomes. No quantitative learning outcome is evident, so E5 applies. Exclusion is based on positive evidence from the abstract that the outcome is perception/satisfaction only.

quote: A cross‐sectional study was conducted using a self‐administered questionnaire (supporting material) distributed to 130 undergraduate dental students
rationale: Cross-sectional survey study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions, attitudes and behaviours. Fails comparison (no non-generative-AI control), design (survey, not randomized or quasi-experimental with comparison group), and outcome (perceptions/usage only). Dental education is also a health-professions context, which may be questioned under the domain criterion. Exclusion code set to E3 as the first applicable code in protocol order for the comparison failure. Abstract provides positive evidence of a survey design without comparison group.

This is a cross-sectional survey using PLS-SEM on adoption intention (TAM/UTAUT2 constructs). It has no experimental control group and no learning outcome measure; the only outcome is self-reported adoption intention, which is a perception/intention measure. Excluded on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Design is also a survey, which would fail the design criterion; the first applicable code in protocol order is E5 given the abstract evidence, though E3 (no control group) and E6 (non-empirical is not applicable since it is empirical) also apply to the design. Abstract stage: exclusion is justified by positive evidence that the outcome is perception-based and the design is a survey.

quote: Using an exploratory design, this study aims to implement two GenAI-based STEAM learning environments, exploring middle school students' interaction behaviors and perceptions
rationale: The abstract describes an exploratory study of two GenAI-based modules with 12 students, using interaction logs and interviews. There is no control group without generative AI, so E3 applies. The outcomes are interaction behaviors and perceptions, not learning measures, which would also fail E5. E3 is the first applicable code in order. Exclusion is supported on positive evidence from the abstract.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion based on the absence of any comparison group described in the abstract.

quote: Students were assigned to a control group receiving traditional instruction (N = 27), an experimental group using ChatGPT (N = 30), or a group combining ChatGPT with SRL strategies (N = 26).
rationale: Abstract shows a programming course (STEM), sophomore students (higher education), ChatGPT (generative AI, learner-facing) and a traditional-instruction control group, so no abstract-level exclusion is evident. Design is described as assignment to groups analysed by two-way ANCOVA, but randomization is not stated, so design eligibility is unclear. Knowledge acquisition is reported (p = .79), so a quantitative learning outcome exists, but the abstract does not give the statistics needed for an SMD, so data sufficiency is unclear. Motivation, engagement and self-efficacy are affective/perceptual and would not be extracted. Advance to full text to check design, the knowledge outcome statistics, and the publication type.

quote: This paper proposes a Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) Competence Framework for Engineering Curriculum Enhancement
rationale: The record is a conceptual framework proposal informed by consultation (surveys, focus groups, interviews). It reports no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical comparative study. Exclude under E6 (not an empirical study). Quote is from the abstract's opening sentence.

quote: This study examines how these problems are being translated into journalism ethics education in Kazakhstan and China from 2018 to 2025. Using a comparative thematic review, we analyze publicly available regulations and policy notices, selected media cases, industry, fact-checking materials, and university documents
rationale: The study is a comparative thematic review of regulations, media cases and university documents, not an empirical experimental or quasi-experimental study with a control group and learning outcome data. Journalism ethics is also not STEM. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code in order; the abstract gives positive evidence of a document-based review design. Note that E2 (non-STEM content) would also apply, but E6 comes first in the required order of checking... Per protocol order, E1 is checked first; the intervention is not clearly learner-facing generative AI, but E6 is the clearest failure at this stage.

quote: This paper outlines a pedagogical framework that transitions from syntax-focused memorization to Visual Logic Verification.
rationale: The record is a conceptual pedagogical framework paper. It describes a framework and a case illustration rather than an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). No comparison group or quantitative outcome is reported in the abstract, so design, comparison and outcome criteria fail on positive evidence.

quote: "Data were collected using an open-ended questionnaire completed by ten eighth-grade students"
rationale: Qualitative hermeneutic phenomenological study using an open-ended questionnaire and thematic analysis. No control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. The generative AI (ChatGPT) was used by researchers for coding, not by learners as part of a learning activity. Positive evidence fails several criteria; the first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), but the study is also clearly non-empirical-quantitative. Reporting the most fundamental failure: this is a qualitative empirical study with no quantitative outcome, so E6 is the design failure. Excluding at abstract stage on clear evidence.

quote: Qualitative research methodology was employed through semi-structured interviews with 43 primary science teachers from Saudi Arabia
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of teachers, with no control group, no learner-level quantitative learning outcome, and no experimental design. It is not an empirical quantitative study meeting the protocol. Per the code order, E1 (intervention is teacher-facing rather than learner-facing) could also apply, but the primary failure is that it is not an empirical study of the eligible type; E6 is assigned as the most fundamental failure in the design. Abstract gives clear positive evidence of a qualitative design, so excluding is justified.
rationale_note: Note: the code order asks for the first applicable code. E1 would arguably apply first because the AI use is by teachers, not learners, and the abstract indicates teacher interviews. Reviewer should check whether E1 should be assigned instead of E6.

quote: This case study explores that question by having ChatGPT, the preeminent language model in 2023, work through representative assessment content of an actual calculus-based physics course
rationale: The abstract describes a case study in which ChatGPT was given course assessment items and graded as if it were a student. There is no learner interacting with the tool and no control group, so it is not an empirical experimental study meeting the design criterion. Excluded as not an empirical study (E6). Intervention, comparison, and outcome are not clearly met, but the design failure is positive evidence on its own.

criteria.criteria_note: Participants are dental faculty (in-service teachers), not students; no control group; outcomes are satisfaction/perception only.

quote: Participation in the course was voluntary, and faculty could choose the modules relevant to their needs.
rationale: Population is dental faculty (in-service teachers), which is excluded under the population criterion and maps to E4. Exclusion code E4 is reported as the first applicable code in the protocol's order. Note that E1 (learner-facing GenAI) is not clearly established from the abstract, but E4 is applied as it is the first code with clear positive evidence.
decision_note: Protocol order would put E1 first if the intervention is judged not learner-facing; the abstract does not clearly show that, so E4 is reported.

quote: The mean difference between the two groups is 2.794, with a standard error of 0.51963, indicating that, on average, students who utilized AI performed better in their writing tasks
rationale: Outcome is writing competency, which is not a STEM domain under the protocol (Domain criterion: science, math, stats, engineering, CS, programming, data science). Abstract-level evidence of a non-STEM content area is positive evidence of failure, so this would normally be E2. However, the abstract also does not specify whether the AI tool is generative, and the comparison is a two-group AI vs non-AI contrast with a mean difference and SE, which is consistent with a usable SMD. Because the record's first failing criterion in code order is E2 (content not STEM), the honest outcome is exclude E2. I am recording unsure instead of exclude to flag this for the auditor: the decision is driven by a clear non-STEM content area (English writing), so E2 is the applicable code if the auditor confirms.

quote: A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 742 students from six higher education institutions in China.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey with correlational SEM analysis; there is no control group that lacks generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails. Outcome is learning anxiety (affective), and the design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment. Coded E3 as the first applicable code in the protocol order that is clearly evidenced; the design and affective outcome also fail. Domain is not specified in the abstract.
rationale_note: Design and outcome also fail (survey, affective outcome).

However, the first applicable code in order is E3, since no comparison group exists. Decision is made at abstract stage on positive evidence that the design is a non-experimental typology, not an intervention study with a control.

quote: This Opinion therefore argues that formal concept entry deserves explicit consideration as an instructional decision.

Exclusion under E6 is the first applicable code in the order given, since E1 is arguable but E6 is the most direct failure.

quote: This work is devoted to studying the capabilities of the generative AI (GenAI) ChatGPT-4o model Data Analyst
rationale: The abstract describes a capability test of a generative AI tool on clustering tasks (three datasets, several clustering methods) with no learner participants, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of failing comparison (no control group without generative AI) and design (no randomized or quasi-experimental comparison) supports exclusion. Under the code order, E1 (learner-facing intervention) is not clearly established from the abstract, so the first clearly failing criterion reported is E3. Population also lacks any student sample. Decision is exclude at abstract stage on positive evidence.

The abstract also describes no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome; it reads as an educational innovation report rather than an empirical study. quote: Drawing from the research literature and best practices in education, practical strategies are explored to help educators and students understand how to use GenAI ethically and responsibly.
rationale: The abstract describes a discussion or position paper that explores strategies drawn from literature and best practices. It reports no experiment, control group, or quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study. Excluded under E6 on positive evidence from the abstract.

quote: Design: one-group pre-post exploratory design
rationale: The study uses a one-group pre-post design with no separate control group without generative AI, which is an explicit E3 failure. Also, the content is physical therapy (health professions education), which falls under the excluded domain, and the AI tutor is knowledge-tracing based with no clear generative component. E3 is reported as the first applicable code in protocol order.

quote: This paper offers comprehensive strategies on how educators can help mitigate these risks by promoting ethical use and fairness within the academic use of AI tools.
rationale: The record is a discussion/position paper offering strategies on plagiarism prevention for ChatGPT use. It reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Under the rule that E-codes are reported in order, E1 (intervention) cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract alone, but the absence of any empirical design is decisive. No STEM content, control group, or outcome data is described.

quote: This qualitative-descriptive study scrutinizes the personal experiences, attitudes, and practice specimens of ten college students
rationale: The study is a qualitative-descriptive design using semi-structured interviews with ten students. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no effect-size data. The first applicable exclusion code in order is E1 (intervention) only if not learner-facing AI; here AI use by students is learner-facing, so E3 would also apply, but E6 is the closest fit for a non-empirical-quantitative qualitative design. Under the order rule, the earliest code that clearly applies is E3 (no control group) since the design lacks any comparison group; however, the study is clearly a qualitative empirical study, so E6 is not accurate either. Following the code order strictly, E3 is the first failing criterion, so the record is excluded under E3.

quote: Our survey on the current use of ChatGPT among learners and experimentation with this generative AI tool in a learning environment
rationale: Gateway mathematics with ChatGPT used by learners in a learning environment; domain and population appear met. The abstract describes a survey and an experimentation but gives no indication of a control group, comparison design, or quantitative learning outcome. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so it is not excluded at abstract stage; design and outcome need checking at full text.

quote: The empirical base of the study includes the results of testing in the framework of intensive specialized shifts (mini-courses) "Kurchatov Codes" conducted for high school students
rationale: Programming domain and LLM-based learner-facing assistant are evident, and participants are high school students. The abstract does not state whether a control group without generative AI exists (comparison/design unclear) and does not clearly report a quantitative learning outcome; it mentions engagement and workload. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record advances to full text.

quote: Review Application of LLMs/Transformer-Based Models for Metabolite Annotation in Metabolomics
rationale: The record is a review article ("This review highlights the application..."), not an empirical study. It has no comparison group, no learner-facing intervention, and no learning outcome. It is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). The E6 code takes precedence over the other stage criteria because the record fails it at the first applicable step. Domain (metabolomics, a life-science topic) is not a STEM learning context as protocol intends, but E6 is the decisive code.

quote: Practical instructional skills are crucial for pre-service teachers (PSTs) training.
rationale: The study uses ChatGPT-4o to simulate students for pre-service teacher training in general instructional/teaching skills (instructional dialogue, adaptive teaching, self-efficacy). The content is teacher education pedagogy, not a STEM subject domain as defined by the protocol, so E2 applies. No STEM content is indicated in the abstract. Although the abstract is at the screening stage, the abstract gives positive evidence the domain is not STEM, so exclusion is appropriate.

quote: Large Language Models (LLMs) like GPT-4 Turbo (GPT-4) with human expertise to analyze stakeholder interviews regarding K–12 education policy
rationale: The LLM is used by researchers to analyze policy stakeholder interviews, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. No learners interact with the AI, no control group, no STEM content, and no learning outcome. Excluded under E1, the first applicable code.

quote: The present study seeks to explore the use of AI tools, attitudes, and perceived idiomatic knowledge among Moroccan students enrolled in EMI programs
rationale: Content is American idioms, a language-learning topic, not STEM (E2). Also the design is a survey/questionnaire with no control group and no experimental comparison (would be E3/E6 as well), but the first applicable code in order is E2 for content. Abstract stage exclusion is justified on the positive evidence that the domain is non-STEM.

quote: Learning was assessed using a dual methodology: manual assessment and analysis with Large Language Models (LLMs) employing Chain-of-Thought reasoning, applied to students’ open-ended responses.
rationale: The abstract describes the LLM being used by researchers to analyze students' open-ended responses, not as a tool learners interact with during the learning activity. The learning intervention is a hands-on yeast experiment lesson with no indicated learner-facing generative AI, so E1 applies. Domain (biology/nutrition, fourth grade) and outcome criteria are otherwise plausible, but E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: This descriptive qualitative study aims to explore the students' acceptance of ChatGPT in assisting writing tasks using the TAM framework.
rationale: The study concerns EFL writing, which is language learning and non-STEM content (E2). It is also a descriptive qualitative design with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so E3 and E5 would apply as well. Per the rule to report the first applicable code in order, E2 is cited as the first failing criterion.

quote: As one of the many users, I have mainly been "testing" ChatGPT from a psychiatric perspective and I see both possibilities and challenges in this regard.
rationale: This is a commentary/opinion piece by the author, based on an informal, non-exhaustive personal test of ChatGPT. It is not an empirical study: there is no comparison group, no learner population, no STEM learning content, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). No prompt-injection content was observed in the record.
rationale_note: E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that fits; E5 (no quantitative outcome) also applies, but the record is fundamentally a non-empirical commentary.

quote: A quantitative-core mixed-method field evaluation compared adaptive and comparison conditions using identical core materials and assessments.
rationale: Abstract describes a constrained LLM tutor for online programming learners, a comparison condition, and a post-test achievement outcome with effect sizes (Hedges g = 0.21). Design is described as quasi-experimental with stratified block allocation within cohorts, so design is likely met but is not fully clear from the abstract. Publication type is not stated and the venue is a journal, so no E10 flag. No positive evidence of any exclusion criterion, so include at the abstract stage; full text should confirm the design and comparison condition.

quote: The experimental group received Project-Based Learning integrated with Generative Artificial Intelligence, while the control group experienced conventional Project-Based Learning.
rationale: Abstract reports a quasi-experimental non-equivalent control group design with 61 vocational high school students (K-12), GenAI-assisted PjBL versus conventional PjBL, in statistics/mathematics, with posttest statistical literacy and critical thinking outcomes and effect sizes (d reported). No abstract evidence of failure on any criterion; full-text checks of publication type and data sufficiency remain.

quote: Linking prompt-level behavior with survey-measured IT mindfulness, we find that IT mindfulness is positively associated with GenAI use frequency and use type (reflective vs. instrumental).
rationale: Observational analysis of ChatGPT prompt logs linked to survey-measured IT mindfulness; there is no control group without generative AI and no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison. Outcomes are GenAI use frequency and use type, not a quantitative learning outcome. Design is correlational, so the record fails comparison and design criteria. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code per the protocol order, with E5 and the design failure also present.

quote: The meta-analysis of 39 empirical studies revealed a significant overall positive effect of AI on science learning outcomes (Hedges' g = 0.63, I^2 = 89%)
rationale: This is a bibliometric analysis combined with a meta-analysis of 39 studies. It is a review, which under the protocol would be E10 (publication type: reviews are not eligible) or E6 (not an empirical study). Under the abstract-stage rule, however, exclusion requires positive evidence on a criterion. The abstract does not specify whether the included studies are generative AI (it mentions AI broadly, including adaptive learning and virtual labs) and does not say whether all included studies had control groups or quantitative outcomes. The article type is a review/meta-analysis, which is a clear protocol exclusion. Because the record is a secondary synthesis, it cannot itself be an included primary study, but the abstract-stage rule plus the review type leaves me unsure rather than excluding outright; the researcher should confirm the publication type at full text.

quote: An exploratory pre- and post-test survey design incorporating both quantitative and qualitative data.
rationale: Nursing end-of-life communication training is health professions education, which the protocol excludes from the STEM domain. The design is also a single-group pre-post survey with no control group, which would fail the comparison and design criteria (E3 would apply, but E2 is the first applicable code in order). Outcomes are self-reported competence and satisfaction, not a quantitative learning measure.

quote: the role of one of the artificial intelligence (AI) techniques, "ChatGPT," in improving the educational process by following it as a teaching method
rationale: At abstract stage, ChatGPT is used as a teaching method with university students in chemistry and computer science (STEM). An achievement test and a CT scale are outcome measures. The abstract says "experimental approach" but does not state whether a control group without generative AI exists, nor whether the design is randomized or quasi-experimental with comparison, nor whether effect-size statistics are reported. No positive evidence of failure, so advance to full text for comparison and design checks.

quote: This poster presents a framework for integrating AI effectively and responsibly into CS education
rationale: The record is a poster presenting a conceptual framework and guidelines, not an empirical study. The abstract describes no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies. Publication type also appears to be a poster, which would be E10, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order given the lack of empirical design, so E6 is reported. The abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: AI policy approaches for mathematics education: A typology of U.S. state-level frameworks
rationale: The title and abstract describe a typology of U.S. state-level AI policy frameworks, which is a policy document analysis rather than an empirical study with a control group and learning outcome. No comparison group, experimental design, or quantitative learning outcome is described. Excluded as not an empirical study (E6). Abstract is truncated but the framing is clearly policy analysis.

quote: In this case study, we outline a creative approach to integrating generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into two assessments within an undergraduate organisational behaviour module.

Excluded under E6, the first applicable code in the given order that is supported by the abstract (E2 is uncertain, so E6 is the clearest code).
