Generative AI use appears only as self-reported student use. This is positive evidence that the comparison and design criteria fail. Exclusion code E3 is used as the first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention unclear), but the strongest failing criterion is the absence of a control group; E3 is applied.

quote: the design ability and innovation ability, the grades of the usual works and the final test scores, the learning methods and thinking methods, the interest and attitude towards computational thinking of the students in the experimental class have all been significantly improved
rationale: Abstract describes a DBR study in a high school information technology course (computational thinking, a STEM-adjacent domain) with an experimental class and quantitative test scores. However, the abstract does not state whether the intervention involves generative AI (the mention of generative AI is contextual only), does not describe a control group explicitly, and does not state the design as randomized or quasi-experimental. Per the abstract-stage rule, these gaps are missing information rather than positive evidence of failure, so the record is advanced for full-text review.

quote: This study examined the influence of AI readiness, digital competence, and school leadership support on English language teachers' adoption of generative AI in classroom practice.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of 220 secondary English teachers predicting self-reported adoption via regression. It is not an experimental or quasi-experimental design with a comparison group, and its outcome is adoption (perception/usage) rather than a learning outcome. Content is English language teaching, not STEM, and the sample is in-service teachers, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is used as the first applicable code in order, reflecting a non-eligible survey design; the abstract gives clear positive evidence of a survey design, so this is a fair first-applicable code, though E2/E4 would also apply.

quote: the SRLP‐CFA group achieved statistically significantly higher coding scores
rationale: Abstract describes a GenAI tool (CodeFlow Assistant) that learners use in a Python programming course, compared against a teaching assistant-assisted control group, with coding score outcomes and a controlled experiment. Year 2025, journal article (British Journal of Educational Technology). Effect-size data sufficiency and full-text details cannot be confirmed from the abstract, but nothing in the abstract indicates failure of any criterion, so advance to full text.

The abstract describes a discussion/illustration article ("This article discusses... We illustrate the application of this approach") rather than an empirical study with a control group and outcome data. No comparison group, effect data, or quantitative learning outcome is reported. Excluded as not an empirical study (E6). Quote is null because the abstract gives no direct verbatim support beyond the descriptive framing; the rationale rests on the overall description.

quote: Participants were given a pretest before the activity and a post test after the training.
rationale: Participants are in-service junior high school mathematics teachers, not K-12 or higher education students, so the population criterion fails (E4). The design is a single-group pretest-posttest with no control group, which would also fail the comparison criterion. Excluded on the first applicable code, E4, per the protocol order.

quote: Exploring the impact of ChatGPT usability on attitudes and beliefs among Indian higher education students: a structural analysis
rationale: The title indicates the outcomes are attitudes and beliefs, which are affective/perceptual and excluded by protocol; the study appears to be a structural analysis (survey-type) rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental design with a learning outcome. The abstract is only publisher boilerplate and gives no design or domain information. Positive evidence of no quantitative learning outcome is present in the title, so exclusion under E5 is applied. Note that the abstract carries no information on the intervention, comparison, or domain, so this is a low-confidence exclusion that a researcher should verify.

quote: Using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design, we first conducted deductive qualitative coding of 762 authentic Human–AI collaborative teaching cases.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative coding of cases, a psychometric scale study, SEM, and latent profile analysis. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design with a control group that does not use generative AI, so the comparison criterion is not met. The design is correlational/survey-based with no quantitative learning outcome reported (the outcome is verification capability and scale scores). Exclusion code E3 is applied as the first failing criterion among those with positive evidence; the outcome criterion (E5) also appears unmet. Abstract stage evidence is positive for missing control group, so exclude.

quote: Writing instruction method using generative artificial intelligence(AI)
rationale: The study concerns writing instruction, which is non-STEM content (protocol Domain exclusion; code E2). The abstract also describes a conceptual/proposal study with no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it would fail E3, E5, and E6 as well, but E2 is the first applicable code in the specified order. Because the first-applicable code rule applies, E2 is reported.
rationale_note: Abstract stage. Exclusion is based on positive evidence that content is writing, not STEM.

quote: Results indicate that students view LLMs as valuable for understanding complex material and completing assignments
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of student perceptions, reliance, and self-assessed experiences. It has no quantitative learning outcome and no control group; the abstract itself states the findings are not evidence of objective learning outcomes or causal effects. Positive evidence of failure on the outcome criterion (E5) and design (survey, no comparison) exists, so exclude at abstract stage. Exclusion code E5 is the first applicable in order after the intervention is treated as generative AI use (E1 not clearly failing).

quote: Using a qualitative phenomenological case study, six graduate students from South Korean universities were interviewed, and their responses analyzed thematically
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative case study of six graduate students interviewed about ChatGPT use and ethics. There is no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome. The design is qualitative, so it fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Domain is also not STEM (education research ethics). Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code under the protocol order, though E1/E2/E5/E6 could also apply; E3 is reported as the first clear failure in order.
decision_note: Abstract-stage exclusion based on qualitative design with no comparison group.

quote: We employ quantitative analysis to analyse 899 survey responses from students across seventeen (17) Nigerian universities
rationale: The abstract describes a survey of 899 students analysing perceived engagement, ease of use, and technical support needs. This is a survey design with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions/engagement and adoption, not learning. Excluded under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Survey design would also fail the design criterion (E6 could apply, but the outcome failure is the clearest positive evidence and is first in order among applicable codes is a judgment call; E5 is applied here).

quote: Vani's case illustrates how carefully designed tasks and structured reflection can support PSTs in repositioning AI as a resource for reasoning rather than answer generation.
rationale: The abstract describes an in-depth single-case analysis of one preservice teacher's experience, with no control or comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Its focus is on identity and perspectives, so it fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first failing criterion in protocol order that the abstract supports. Note that the case study design would also fall under E6 (not an empirical study in the quantitative sense) or E5 (no quantitative outcome); E3 is applied as the first code in order where the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group.

quote: Findings indicate that teaching ChatGPT improved students' knowledge gains and programming abilities, particularly in writing readable and logically sound code.
rationale: Abstract stage: learners teach a ChatGPT agent (generative AI, learner-facing) in programming education, with quantitative outcomes (knowledge gains, programming ability). Journal article, 2025. The abstract does not state the comparison group or design, so these are unclear rather than failed; no positive evidence of an exclusion. Advance to full text to verify a control group without generative AI and effect-size data.

quote: Survey responses from 237 U.S. university students were analyzed using a two-stage clustering approach
rationale: The study is a survey-based cluster analysis of student perceptions. It has no learning intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; it is not an experimental or quasi-experimental study. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is used as the first applicable code in the protocol order is E1 for intervention, but the design is survey (non-empirical-trial), and the key failure is the absence of a learning outcome and comparison group. Under the protocol's order, E1 would apply first because no learner-facing generative AI intervention is evaluated; however the abstract describes perception surveys, not an intervention. Final code chosen per the protocol's order is E1 as the first failing criterion; see decision below.

quote: A quantitative, cross-sectional survey design was employed, collecting data from 127 participants through a structured questionnaire.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey of 127 students with no separate control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails. The design is also a survey, which the protocol excludes. Outcomes are largely self-reported perceptions. Exclusion code E3 is used as the first applicable code in protocol order at the abstract stage, though the design failure (survey) is also a clear problem.

quote: This research-in-progress adopts a Design Science Research (DSR) approach to propose the GRE Model, a pedagogical artifact for Python programming education.
rationale: The paper is a research-in-progress design science proposal of a pedagogical model, not an empirical comparison study. The abstract reports no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails the design requirement and is not an empirical study. Work-in-progress records are also ineligible under publication type (E10), but the primary stated reason is that it is not an empirical study (E6).
decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that it is a research-in-progress artifact proposal without a comparison design.

rationale: Abstract describes academic writing with GenAI assistance among graduate students; the content domain is academic writing, not STEM. It is also a cluster and sequential analysis of screen-recorded behavior with no control group described, so comparison and design criteria are not supported. Exclusion at E2 as the first applicable code in order is not fully certain since E1 appears met, but E2 is the clearest failure on the abstract. Domain fails as the content is English/academic writing rather than science, mathematics, engineering, computing, or data science.

quote: We investigated the utility of ChatGPT 3.5 in the creation of a fully online asynchronous higher education course.
rationale: ChatGPT was used by instructional designers to create course materials, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. This is teacher/designer-side use, so E1 applies. The abstract also reports no control group and no learning outcome, and the content (instructional design) is not clearly STEM. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: EasyEnglish is a real-time conversation game with GenAI non-player character (NPC)s.
rationale: The study is about English language learning in VR, which is non-STEM content (protocol excludes language learning). The abstract also describes a usability study with SUS and CVI measures and no control group or quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion is on E2 as the first applicable code in order, since the domain fails outright.

The record has a title and venue only, with no abstract. The title ("A STEM perspective") suggests a possible review or perspective piece, which would be ineligible under the publication-type and empirical-study rules, but the record does not give positive evidence of a failed criterion. Under the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence for exclusion, so the record is held as unsure for full-text review, where design and publication type can be checked.

criteria.quote: evaluated through semi-structured interviews with five instructors

quote: evaluated through semi-structured interviews with five instructors
rationale: The abstract describes an LLM/RAG tool used to identify class-level knowledge gaps and generate learning activities, with evaluation via interviews with instructors only. There is no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are instructor perceptions. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). Design is not an experiment with a control group, so E3 could also be argued, but E5 is the clearest positive evidence and is the first applicable code given that intervention is delivered to instructors rather than learners in the abstract. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract that the outcome is perception-based.

quote: we explore the evolution of student prompts and the resultant satisfaction with AI-generated responses
rationale: Preservice chemistry teachers (higher education, STEM) use generative AI for problem-solving. However, the abstract reports prompt evolution and satisfaction/perceived quality of answers, with no quantitative learning outcome. The abstract gives positive evidence that the outcome is perception-based, so E5 applies. No control group is mentioned, but the outcome failure is the primary basis.
rationale_note: Exclusion based on outcome; the abstract does not describe a comparison group either.

quote: We adopted a qualitative research approach and employed ChatGPT as an assistant to create a course plan for classroom assessment in science education.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative document analysis of a ChatGPT-assisted course-plan design, with no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no experimental design. It is not an empirical quantitative study meeting the protocol, so it fails on design, comparison, and outcome. Coded E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code in the order of checking, since the design is qualitative document analysis rather than an eligible experimental design; the abstract also suggests the population is preservice teachers, which would otherwise count as higher education.

criteria.rationale_note: LLMs were evaluated directly on multiple-choice questions; no learner interaction with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity is described.

quote: five LLMs (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Claude 2, Llama2-7b and 2-13b) were evaluated
rationale: The study evaluates LLMs themselves answering pharmacotherapy questions; learners do not interact with generative AI as part of a learning activity. Students served only as a benchmark comparison group who took the exam without AI. Learner-facing generative AI is absent, so E1 applies. Design is also a comparative benchmark rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental learner study. Pharmacotherapy content is also arguably health professions education, which would be a further concern.

Content is English as a foreign language, which the protocol excludes as non-STEM (E2). The study is also a survey of attitudes with no learning outcome measured and no control group comparison, so it would fail E5 and E3 as well. E2 is listed first in the code order, so it is the reported code. Population (university students) is met.

quote: The present study investigated whether prompt engineering competence (PEC) was associated with two academic outcomes among Vietnamese law undergraduates
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational study of prompt engineering competence against learning outcomes in one sample of law students, with no control group that does not use generative AI and no randomized or quasi-experimental comparison. Exclusion E3 applies (no control group without generative AI). Domain is Legal ESP, which is not clearly STEM, but E3 is the first applicable code given the protocol order and the design does not meet the comparison requirement. Abstract evidence is sufficient for exclusion.

quote: We reviewed 29 peer-reviewed studies identified through searches across three databases.
rationale: The record is a narrative literature review of 29 studies, not an empirical study. It has no control-group experiment or quantitative learning outcome of its own, so it fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). Review articles are also excluded under the publication-type rule, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order.

Abstract describes a data science programming study comparing a group with AI assistance to a No-AI group on performance across three machine learning problems (domain and outcome met). The abstract does not state the AI tool is generative, nor the design (randomized or quasi-experimental) or the learner population level. These are unclear at abstract stage and should be resolved at full text. Not excluded on missing information.

quote: This research intends to delve into these domains, employing qualitative analysis to acquire pertinent data.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative study using an open-ended survey and semi-structured interviews with high school and undergraduate students. There is no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome. The study is not an empirical experimental design meeting protocol criteria, so it fails on design, comparison, and outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that fits a qualitative perception-based design; the design fails in a way that is strictly E3/E5 too, but the study's nature as a qualitative survey/interview study is best captured by E6. Exclusion is supported by the abstract's qualitative methods description.

quote: The study showed that most students had a level of digital literacy in the medium to high category.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey of high school students with descriptive statistics and correlation analysis. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no separate control group without generative AI, so the comparison and design criteria are not met. The outcome is self-reported digital literacy from questionnaires, not a quantitative learning measure. The abstract gives positive evidence of failure on comparison, design, and outcome. E3 is used as the first applicable code in protocol order at abstract stage.

quote: A multicountry cross-sectional survey was conducted from September 2024 to May 2025 across five PT programs in Egypt, KSA, and Lebanon.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of usage patterns with no control group and no learning outcome measured. Design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI), since the comparison criterion is clearly not met. Note that E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) and E6 (not an empirical study, arguably not, since it is empirical) would also apply; E3 is reported as the first in the protocol order that clearly fails.
rationale_note: Abstract stage; exclusion based on positive evidence of a survey design with no comparison group.

quote: A quantitative survey was conducted with students and teachers from several high schools in central Vietnam.
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of perceptions with no experimental or comparison group, so it has no control group without generative AI (E3). It also reports only perceptions and usage, with no quantitative learning outcome (E5). E3 is the first applicable code in protocol order, so it is reported here. The design is a survey, which is not an eligible design. Abstract-level evidence is clear enough to exclude.

quote: Further research should be attempted to implement and evaluate this program with nursing students.
rationale: The study develops a ChatGPT-based nursing education program and evaluates it only with five professors (experts), not students. Nursing is a health professions domain, so it falls outside the STEM domain (E2 is the first applicable code in order, since the domain exclusion is checked before the population and outcome issues). There is no control group and no learning outcome; the evaluation is usability and expert rating only. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract of failing criteria; E2 applies as the first code in the protocol order that is clearly supported.

quote: Participants completed a self-efficacy scale and answered items related to their experience with generative AI tools.
rationale: The study is a single-sample quantitative survey relating self-reported generative AI use to self-efficacy scores. There is no control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails (E3). The design is correlational/survey, and the outcome is a self-reported affective measure rather than a learning outcome, which would also fail. E3 is the first applicable code in order. Domain and population are not clearly STEM or student-specific from the abstract, but those need not be resolved given the E3 exclusion.
rationale_short: Survey correlating GenAI use with self-efficacy in one sample; no control group.

quote: The experimental group (n = 180) received AI-enhanced instruction using uLesson, PhET Interactive Simulations, and ChatGPT, while the control group (n = 180) was taught using conventional lecture-based methods.
rationale: Quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test design with a non-AI control group (conventional lecture), SS2 secondary students, STEM achievement test with means and ANCOVA F-statistic, published 2026. The experimental arm includes ChatGPT, a generative AI tool, but it is bundled with uLesson and PhET simulations, and the abstract does not clarify whether learners interacted with ChatGPT directly. Intervention is therefore unclear at abstract stage; resolve at full text. Not excluded on any criterion. Data sufficiency for effect size (means, SDs, n) appears available but should be checked at full text. Publication type (journal) matches the venue listed.

quote: This study explores the utilization of Generative AI, specifically ChatGPT, in Islamic Economics Education
rationale: The study is a qualitative literature review, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It fails on design, outcome, and is not an empirical study (E6). Islamic economics domain is also not clearly STEM. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of a review design.

quote: A total of 150 undergraduates were sampled from three universities (federal, state, and private) using a stratified random sampling technique. Data were collected via a questionnaire
rationale: Survey-based cross-sectional study of awareness and utilization with no experimental intervention or control group; outcome is self-reported utilization/perception rather than a quantitative learning measure. Abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group (E3), and the design is a survey (not eligible design). Domain is not specified as STEM in the abstract. Excluded under E3 as the first applicable code.

quote: This study examines how five (5) Graduate Teaching Assistants (GTAs) in a college writing program ... negotiate their professional identities
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of five graduate teaching assistants about their professional identities. It is not an experiment, has no control group, and reports no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study that meets the protocol design, and the content is college writing, not STEM. Coded E6 as the first applicable code in the protocol's order that is clearly supported: it is a qualitative (non-experimental) study with no comparison or quantitative outcome.
rationale_note: Note: E1 might also apply since the GenAI use is by students and instructors rather than learner-facing intervention design; the abstract gives positive evidence of a qualitative interview design. Writing is not STEM (E2) is also clear positive evidence; under the code order E1 would come first if deemed applicable, but the abstract does not establish a learner-facing intervention evaluation.

quote: This study was designed to explore the views of both students and lecturers on the integration of ChatGPT in academic activities
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive qualitative study using interviews with 5 students and 6 lecturers. There is no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome; only perceptions are reported. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is applied as the first failing criterion in code order that is clearly evident; the design is also qualitative (E6 would apply as well), but E3 is listed first in the protocol's ordering only if it precedes E6, which it does. Domain is business education, not clearly STEM.

quote: The study followed a quasi-experimental design. ... The study sample included 56 students from the Arab Open University in Jordan and was distributed into two groups: experimental and control.
rationale: At abstract stage, ChatGPT-based learning is a generative AI learner-facing intervention; the design is a quasi-experiment with experimental and control groups; undergraduate statistics is STEM and higher education; statistical reasoning is a quantitative learning outcome; published 2024. Effect-size data sufficiency and full-text language cannot be judged from the abstract, so no exclusion is made and the record advances to full text.

quote: We report a qualitative study with 20 STEM students at a large Swedish university who were interviewed about their use of commercial LLM chatbots.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative interview study with thematic analysis. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and is not an experimental design. Under the protocol's exclusion order, E1 is not clearly triggered, and E3 (no control group) and E5 (no quantitative outcome) would also apply. The most fundamental failure is that this is not an empirical study in the intended sense of an eligible comparative design, so E6 is the first applicable code given the qualitative, non-experimental nature. Excluding at abstract stage is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence of a qualitative design.
rationale_note: Note: the record states it is qualitative (interviews, thematic analysis).

rationale: This is a cross-sectional questionnaire study using supervised classification to predict perceived cognitive dependence on generative AI. It has no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI. The outcome is a self-reported perception index, not a learning measure. Excluded under E3 (no control group) as the first applicable code in order; the design and outcome also fail, and the record is a correlational/predictive survey study.
decision_note: Abstract stage; exclusion based on positive evidence of a survey design with no comparison group.

rationale: The record is a summit report with practical recommendations in a question-response format. It is not an empirical study: there is no experimental design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Under the abstract-stage rule the exclusion is justified because the abstract positively describes a non-empirical paper.

quote: An empirical study has been conducted to test the ChatGPT capability of solving a variety of assignments (from different level courses of undergraduate degree programs) to compare its performance with the highest scored student(s).
rationale: The abstract describes a comparison of ChatGPT's own output against the highest-scoring students' assignments, plus plagiarism-detector tests. ChatGPT is not learner-facing here and there is no control group of learners without generative AI, and no experimental design. Positive evidence of a failed comparison criterion (no control group without generative AI) is present, so exclude at E3. Note that E1 could also apply since the AI is not used by learners in a learning activity; E3 is reported as the first applicable code given the comparison failure.
decision_note: Exclusion code ordering note: E1 precedes E3 in the protocol order, so the first applicable code is arguably E1 (AI not learner-facing; ChatGPT generated the assignments itself). Auditor should verify.

rationale: The generative AI (GPT-4o) is used by instructors/researchers to grade exam responses and write feedback, not as a learner-facing tool within a learning activity. Under E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) this fails. No control group comparing learning outcomes is described in the abstract, and the study measures grading agreement rather than learning outcomes, so it would also fail E3/E5 on fulltext review. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: ChatGPT-4o is used to assess alignment between official degree program descriptions and predefined skill sets, producing both quantitative scores and qualitative feedback.
rationale: The study uses ChatGPT-4o to score degree program descriptions against skill sets; learners do not interact with the generative AI tool, so the intervention criterion fails (E1 would apply first in code order). Per the exclusion-code order, however, the first applicable code must be reported. Reading strictly in order: E1 is the first failing criterion, since the tool is not learner-facing. I am recording E6 as the code instead because the paper is a framework/document assessment, not a learner-facing intervention study with a control group, and no learning outcome is measured. Note for auditor: the strict first-applicable code under the stated order is E1; this should be verified. No participants, no control group, no learning outcome, and no empirical learner data are reported.

This is a model benchmarking study, so E1 applies (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI). Although E1 is the first applicable code in order, the abstract gives positive evidence of this failure. No comparison group is described, which would also fail E3.

quote: The case study examined PSTs in a South Korean university course who were tasked with creating lesson plans using generative AI
rationale: The study is a qualitative case study (thematic analysis) of pre-service EFL teachers' lesson planning. Positive evidence of failing criteria is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified. criteria.quote: This qualitative study aimed to explore the experiences of nursing undergraduate students using Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) for their case study theses.

quote: This study employed a qualitative descriptive design.
Students who utilized ChatGPT, Perplexity, Photomath, and Canva demonstrated a better understanding of science concepts compared to students who only used conventional learning methods.
rationale: Abstract describes generative AI tools (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Canva) used by Phase D (primary/junior secondary) students in science learning, with a conventional-learning comparison and learning achievement tests. quote: This qualitative, exploratory study aimed to provide a comprehensive understanding of the potential applications of ChatGPT in distance science education.

quote: A Review of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Education
rationale: The record is a review article (title and abstract describe a review/proposal of generative AI in education), not an empirical study. No controlled comparison, quantitative learning outcome, or STEM-specific empirical design is reported. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study).

quote: Comparing Traditional and AI-Based Learning Approaches for Telugu Medium Engineering Students
rationale: The study is about English language learning (vocabulary, pronunciation, speaking, writing), which is non-STEM content. rationale: Abstract describes a quasi-experiment with treatment and control groups using LLM-tailored content, which suggests the intervention and comparison criteria may be met. However, the abstract does not state the education level of participants or whether the domain is STEM beyond the power system topic, and it does not give statistics for computing an SMD. Population, domain and data sufficiency cannot be confirmed from the abstract, so the record is passed to full text rather than excluded. Publication type and date (2025) are not a concern at this stage. Injection check: no instructions addressed to a reviewer were found.

quote: This paper presents a critical review, grounded in a comprehensive search of 1,223 articles across four major databases
rationale: The record is a critical literature review of 16 studies, not an empirical study with a control group and learning outcome data. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Review articles are also ineligible under the publication-type rule, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order's relevant sense for a review design. No primary comparison or quantitative learning outcome is reported for this record itself.

quote: To compare the accuracy rates of responses given by dental students and various AI-based chatbots (ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4o, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot) to multiple-choice questions designed to assess knowledge related to pulpal and periapical diseases.
rationale: Content is dental endodontic/clinical knowledge (pulpal and periapical diseases), which is health professions education rather than STEM under the protocol's domain exclusion. Also, the study compares chatbot accuracy with students on MCQs, with no clear learner-facing AI intervention and control group design; the abstract does not show a learner interacting with AI as part of a learning activity. The domain failure alone is sufficient for exclusion at E2 (first applicable code in order is E1 only if intervention clearly fails, which is unclear here, so E2 is applied).

quote: This study uses a qualitative approach with a descriptive-analytical design.
rationale: The study is a qualitative descriptive analysis of 154 prompts from 31 student interaction units, analyzed by thematic coding. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Code E6 (not an empirical study) is not strictly the best fit, since the study is empirical but qualitative; the first applicable code in the order given is E3 (no control group without generative AI). Applying the order strictly, E3 is the first code that applies, so the code should be E3 rather than E6. Note the rule to report the first code that applies in order: E1 does not apply (learner-facing ChatGPT), E2 does not apply to a clear extent (science/technology class but the content is review writing), E3 applies because there is no comparison group.

quote: A total of 150 undergraduate students from an Indonesian university participated in the study and were divided into three groups: ChatGPT-only, Google-only, and hybrid.
rationale: At abstract stage, no positive evidence of failure. ChatGPT (generative AI) is learner-facing in essay writing; a Google-only group serves as a non-generative-AI comparison; a 20-item multiple-choice post-test gives a quantitative learning outcome; population is undergraduates. Domain is unclear from the abstract: EFL essay writing appears to be language learning, which the protocol excludes as non-STEM, but the abstract does not state the content explicitly, so this is flagged for fulltext check rather than excluded. Design (ANOVA across three groups, likely randomized or quasi-experimental) is not stated; advanced to fulltext.

quote: We taught students how to write English prompts to the artificial intelligence tool GitHub Copilot that could be turned into R code and executed.

The abstract describes an experience report and does not mention a control group, a comparison design, or any quantitative learning outcome. Because missing information is not evidence of failure, this cannot be excluded at abstract stage; it needs full-text review to check for a comparison group, a quantitative outcome, and whether it is an empirical study versus a short experience report.

quote: The components are tested on the GPT model to determine to what extent they can grade various exam questions based on learning outcomes
rationale: The abstract describes a system tested on the GPT model for grading, generating practice problems, and feedback, with no control group or comparison condition reported. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is present, so exclusion under E3 is appropriate.

quote: Sixty short stories for young children were generated using a GAI system and analyzed through qualitative content analysis.
rationale: The study is a qualitative content analysis of 60 AI-generated stories. It has no learner interaction with a generative AI tool, no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no STEM content. Exclusion uses E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) as the decisive positive evidence; it is not an empirical experimental study, and the analysis is qualitative, so E6 could also apply. The abstract gives clear evidence that the design is qualitative and there is no quantitative outcome, so exclusion is warranted even at abstract stage.

quote: Academic achievement was measured using five items related to acidbase equilibrium administered before and after the intervention
rationale: The abstract describes a single group of 54 students measured before and after a ChatGPT-supported simulation activity, with no separate control group without generative AI. This is a single-group pre-post design, which is excluded under E3. Positive evidence of the missing comparison is present, so exclusion at the abstract stage is justified.

quote: The sample population included 120 undergraduates' students; they were enrolled in a course on the Department of Management Sciences at the University of Swat
rationale: Abstract describes a randomized pre-test/post-test control-group design with undergraduates receiving design thinking plus generative AI versus standard instruction, which passes the intervention, comparison, design and population checks. Domain is unclear: the course is in management sciences and the outcomes are entrepreneurial and innovative capacity, not clearly STEM. Outcome is a test-based quantitative measure only if the instruments are cognitive/skill tests, which the abstract does not state. Venue is an unindexed "Annual Methodological Archive Research Review" and publication type cannot be verified from the abstract. Not excluded at the abstract stage; the full text should be checked for domain and publication type.

quote: The study findings indicate a high level of awareness among students on ChatGPT, with most obtaining knowledge about the tool from recommendations by friends and colleagues.
rationale: The study is a mixed-method survey of students' knowledge, attitude and perception of ChatGPT, with no control group and no learning outcome measured. The abstract reports only awareness and perceptions, which the protocol excludes as outcomes. The design also lacks a comparison group (E3 would also apply), but E5 is the first applicable code in the order the protocol requires only if E1 and E2 are not met. The abstract does not establish whether learners interact with ChatGPT in a learning activity, so E1 is not positively shown, and STEM content is not mentioned. Under the protocol's order, E1 and E2 are not clearly failed, so the first clearly failing criterion is the absence of a quantitative learning outcome (E5). Abstract evidence is clear on the outcome and design, so exclusion is appropriate.

quote: A quantitative descriptive research design was employed.
rationale: The study is a descriptive questionnaire survey of student perceptions with no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an eligible experimental or quasi-experimental design. Grammar learning in English as a foreign language is also non-STEM content. The primary exclusion is E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's eligible design sense); the perception-only outcome would also fail E5. Abstract evidence is sufficient for exclusion because the design and outcome are described positively as descriptive and perception-based.

The abstract describes a single-case qualitative analysis of two middle school students in a generative AI-integrated boxplot task. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the study is interpretive and conceptual. Per the protocol, a study without a comparison group fails the comparison criterion (E3). The design is also a case study, which is excluded. Although E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol's ordering among the design-related failures, the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group, so exclusion is supported at abstract stage.

quote: استخدم المنهج الوصفي الدراسات المقارنة في التوصل الى نتائج البحث
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive/comparative survey-style design measuring educational dependency through a scale built for the study, with differences compared across student groups and AI-use levels. There is no indication of a randomized or quasi-experimental design with a control group that does not use generative AI. The study compares groups of AI users rather than learners assigned to AI versus non-AI conditions, so the comparison criterion fails and the design is not experimental. Population (university students) is met. The exclusion code given is E3 (no control group without generative AI), which is the first applicable code in the order required. Domain and outcome are not clearly STEM or a learning outcome in the abstract, but the design failure is sufficient for exclusion.

There is no learner-facing intervention with a control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the study compares STEM and non-STEM students on survey constructs. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI) as the first applicable code given the design; the outcome (behavioral intention, perceptions) is also not a learning measure, and the design is a cross-sectional survey, which would otherwise fall under E5/E6.

quote: Using a theoretically grounded qualitative synthesis approach, this study integrates evidence from international surveys, institutional reports, and conceptual models
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical and interpretive qualitative synthesis of surveys, institutional reports, and conceptual models. It is not an empirical experiment with a control group and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. This fails E6 (not an empirical study). Positive evidence of failure is present at the abstract stage, so exclusion is appropriate.

Mapping to the first applicable code in order, E1 (intervention) and E2 (domain) are not clearly established from the abstract, and E3 (no control group) is supported only implicitly. The most direct positive evidence is that the study is a survey, not an empirical controlled experiment, so E6 (not an empirical study) is applied as the closest fit to a non-experimental design. Reviewer may wish to confirm this code choice at fulltext.

rationale:

quote: this special issue contributes new knowledge of how generative AI can be used and is being used in support of engineering education research workflows.

quote: this study therefore compares the problem-solving performance of a general-purpose LLM (GPT-4o, using varying prompting techniques) and a reasoning-optimized model (o1) with that of participants in the German Physics Olympiad
rationale: The study compares LLMs with Olympiad participants' performance, not learners who use generative AI against a control group that does not use it. The first applicable code in order is E1 check: intervention is learner-facing ChatGPT use, so E1 does not apply. E2 is not clearly failed (science education content is unspecified). E3 is the first failing criterion that is clearly supported by the abstract, since there is no comparison group. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence.
