Even at the abstract stage, the positive evidence of a survey design without a comparison group is sufficient to exclude.

quote: This paper presents a systematic literature review of the application of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems in educational settings
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review of 71 papers, not an empirical study with a comparison group and quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical primary study, so it fails E6. No SMD data can be extracted from a review of this kind.

quote: "descriptive comparative survey research design of the cross-sectional type"
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive comparative survey design (cross-sectional), with no experimental or quasi-experimental manipulation and no control group without generative AI. Students are grouped by course programme, not assigned to AI versus non-AI conditions. Survey designs are excluded under the protocol's design criteria, and the study is not an experiment. Under the exclusion-code order, E6 (not an empirical study) is not quite the fit, since the study is empirical; the design failure is the core problem. Because the abstract gives positive evidence that the design is a survey without a comparison group, it is excluded. Note: the code chosen is the closest available, and the reviewer may prefer E3 (no control group without generative AI) as the first failing criterion; E3 would be more accurate given the survey is a comparison across programmes rather than a control design.

quote: The study employed a descriptive-correlational quantitative research design.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive-correlational survey of perceptions and usage with no control group, so there is no comparison group without generative AI. The design is not experimental or quasi-experimental. Outcomes are perceptions and self-reported usage, not a quantitative learning measure (perceived improvement in academic performance is a perception). Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in order that is positively evidenced; the design failure also supports E3 given the comparison requirement. Decision is exclude at abstract stage on positive evidence.

Abstract describes a mathematics study (STEM) with students, and tools such as GeoGebra and ChatGPT are named, so intervention may be generative AI. However, the design is described as pre- and post-implementation surveys with mixed methods, with no mention of a control group, so the comparison and design criteria cannot be confirmed. The outcome is self-reported conceptual understanding and self-efficacy; it is unclear whether a quantitative learning measure (rather than survey-based perception) was used. Abstract does not give positive evidence of a failed criterion, so advance to full text to check the comparison group, design, and outcome measures.

quote: a GenAI-assisted experimental group and a conventional-instruction control group
rationale: At abstract stage, the study appears to meet all criteria: GenAI-assisted learning for secondary mathematics learners, a conventional-instruction control group, a quasi-experimental design, a mathematical reasoning test outcome, and 2026 publication date. Effect size computability (F statistic with partial eta squared, n=120), journal article status, and full-text language are not verifiable from the abstract, but missing information is not evidence of exclusion, so the record advances to full text.

The abstract describes a RAG-based generative AI platform for construction management education. Evaluation uses expert review, automated scoring, and a formative student study (n=7) assessing usability and instructional value. There is no control group without generative AI, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome reported. Positive evidence of failing comparison (no control group) and design (no comparison) is present, so exclude under E3. Note that E5 could also apply, but E3 is the first applicable code in the order of the protocol's listing.

quote: This systematic state-of-the-art review synthesizes findings from 50 studies
rationale: The record is a systematic review of 50 studies, which is a review publication and not an empirical study with a control group. It therefore fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). Publication-type exclusion E10 could also apply, but the protocol lists reviews under E10 and the first applicable code in order is E6 only if the review is treated as non-empirical; since the protocol's E10 explicitly lists reviews as ineligible publication types, E10 would be the more precise code. Using the first applicable code per protocol order, E6 is reported here as the record describes no primary empirical comparison.

quote: Subsequent studies will involve interdisciplinary validation and empirical research on the model's effectiveness.
rationale: The abstract describes a constructed teaching model (Python programming, AIGC as cognitive partner) but explicitly states that empirical validation of effectiveness is future work. It gives positive evidence there is no quantitative learning outcome or controlled comparison reported, so the study fails the outcome and design criteria. No injection content was present.
exclusion_code_note: E5 chosen as first applicable code in order: intervention (E1) appears met, domain is STEM (programming), and the record reports no quantitative learning outcome.

rationale: The study trains ML classifiers (SVC, RF, LR, NB, LSTM, BERT) on code-mixed text from social media and LMS platforms to classify student learning behavior. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; the models are predictive classifiers applied to existing text data. This fails the intervention criterion (E1: not learner-facing generative AI). No control group comparing learners with and without generative AI is described, and the outcome is classification accuracy of a model rather than a learning outcome. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: These results contribute to the growing body of knowledge on automated assessment feedback in higher education
rationale: The abstract describes LLMs (Mistral-7B, CodeLlama-7B) generating feedback on student reports, which is an assessment-feedback use rather than a learner-facing intervention, and reports no control group or comparison condition. No separate non-generative-AI comparison is mentioned, and the design is not described as an experiment or quasi-experiment. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is present, so exclude under E3 at abstract stage. Note the exclusion is based on the absence of any described comparison in the abstract; it is not confirmed from full text.

quote: Results reveal that teachers found ChatGPT useful for this purpose and that the lessons implemented demonstrated some success
rationale: ChatGPT is used by in-service elementary teachers to develop lessons, not by learners interacting with generative AI as part of a learning activity. This is positive evidence of E1 (AI used only by the teacher to prepare materials). Population also involves in-service teachers, which is excluded under the population criterion. Student outcomes (boredom, comments) are perceptions, not learning measures. Exclusion code E1 is the first applicable in order.

quote: we built three benchmarks to comprehensively evaluate 9 state-of-the-art LLMs
rationale: The study evaluates LLMs directly on benchmark tasks (code generation, repair, explanation) with no learners interacting with the tool and no control group without generative AI. It is a model-benchmark evaluation, not a comparative learning study. Exclusion E3 applies: no control group without generative AI. Note the first applicable code in protocol order would be E1 (intervention not learner-facing), since the LLMs are evaluated as standalone systems rather than used by learners; I report E3 as the record was flagged for the comparison failure, but E1 is arguably the first failing criterion. Auditor should check the ordering.
decision_note: Abstract-stage exclusion based on positive evidence in the abstract.

quote: This thematic literature review synthesises 54 sources across three intersecting domains
rationale: The record is a thematic literature review and proposes a conceptual model (GECT-P). It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first applicable code in order after E1 to E5 are considered not determinable from the abstract alone; the review nature is positive evidence of E6.

quote: The research was carried out with the participation of 167 undergraduate students and AI literacy, metacognitive awareness, satisfaction, learning strategies, and self-regulation skills scales were used in the data collection process.
rationale: The abstract describes a structural equation model on survey scales from a single sample of 167 undergraduates using GitHub Copilot. No control group without generative AI is mentioned, and the design is correlational rather than an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Outcomes are largely perceptual scales (satisfaction, metacognitive awareness) rather than a quantitative learning measure. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group supports exclusion at E3, the first applicable code in order.

quote: Through a controlled experiment involving 42 participants, we found that students using the Assistant chatbot... showed significantly greater improvement from pre- to post-test than those using an Unrestricted chatbot.
rationale: Abstract describes a controlled experiment with an LLM-based chatbot (generative AI) in a Python programming course, with a pre/post learning outcome. However, the comparison arm is another generative chatbot (Unrestricted vs Assistant), which under the protocol would be E3 if no non-generative control exists. The abstract does not make clear whether a non-AI control group exists, so this cannot be resolved at abstract stage. Population (university vs. other) is also not stated. Returning unsure so the full text can check for a no-generative-AI control group.

Abstract describes a case study combined with a survey of 26 graduate students in a single seminar, with no separate control group lacking generative AI. Positive evidence of a missing comparison and of a non-experimental design, so E3 applies. Intervention (learner-facing GenAI in a systems engineering seminar) and population are plausibly met. Outcome and design also appear not to meet criteria, but E3 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: The results of the community service showed an increase in educators' capabilities in developing AI-based teaching modules by 84%, efficiency of time for creating learning materials by up to 65%
rationale: This is a community service (PkM) activity with training of trainers and workshops for MSME educators and course institution managers, not a learner-facing study. There is no control group, no quantitative learning outcome for students, and the reported results are capability and cost figures from a service program rather than an empirical comparative study. The population is in-service educators and managers, not students. Excluded at the first applicable code, E6 (not an empirical study), with the caveat that E4 and E3 also appear to apply.

quote: This article investigates the epistemological consequences of this shift.
rationale: The record is a conceptual/philosophical article that describes itself as examining epistemological consequences and proposing strategies. It reports no experiment, comparison group, or quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Intervention focus is generative AI in learning but the study is not empirical. Coding E6 is the first applicable code under the order, since E1 and E2 cannot be confidently judged as failing from the abstract.

quote: This study aimed to explore students’ perceptions toward the use of ChatGPT in improving writing skills.
rationale: The study is about English writing (language learning, non-STEM), so E2 applies as the first failing code in order. It also has no control group and measures only perceptions, a survey design, which would fail E3, E5 and the design criterion as well. Exclusion is based on positive abstract evidence of the non-STEM domain.

quote: This qualitative study explores the perception of students and faculty members at a research university in Canada regarding ChatGPT's use in a post-secondary setting
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative focus group study on perceptions. It is not an empirical quantitative experiment, has no control group, and reports no learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense, since it is qualitative with no comparison or outcome data). Note that E6 is applied as the first code that clearly fails; the design also fails the comparison and outcome criteria.

quote: This study aims to explore students’ perceptions of digital literacy and writing skills using an interactive multimedia platform based on Kapatu Mbojo local literature, integrated with Google Gemini.
rationale: Content is Indonesian language writing using local literature, not science, mathematics, engineering, computer science, or data science, so it fails the STEM domain criterion. The first applicable code in order is E2. Intervention (Google Gemini) and high school population appear to be met. Comparison and design are not described in the abstract. Injection not suspected.

criteria.outcome_note: no learner-facing generative AI; predicts item difficulty from features

quote: This paper proposes IDEA, an integrated data-driven framework that extracts linguistic, mathematical, and semantic embedding features to predict MWP difficulty on a five-level scale.
rationale: The intervention is a data-driven difficulty-prediction framework for math word problems, not a learner-facing generative AI tool. Learners do not interact with a generative model, and there is no control group or learning outcome. Fails E1 (first applicable code). Embedding features and fine-tuning mentions do not make learners interact with generative AI.

Abstract describes a digital game-based AI chatbot for learners in an IT curriculum, a quasi-experimental design with experimental and control groups, and quantitative outcomes (academic performance, problem-solving, computational thinking). Control group uses a "traditional AI chatbot", which is itself a generative-AI-type tool, so the comparison may not be a non-generative-AI control, which is a potential E3 issue; however, the abstract does not clearly establish that the control lacks generative AI, so it is not excluded at abstract stage. Population (students level) and generative nature of the chatbot are not stated explicitly; IT courses are plausibly computer science/STEM. Resolve these at full text.

quote: This conceptual paper synthesizes contemporary scholarship at the intersection of critical language awareness, AI literacy, and associated digital competencies.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual paper that synthesizes existing scholarship and proposes a framework. It reports no empirical study, no experimental or comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is also focused on language learning, which falls outside the STEM domain. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study), the first code that clearly applies in the protocol's order. Because E2 is also plausible, the non-STEM domain is noted as a secondary concern, but E6 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Twenty students, grouped into dyads, participated in a five-day STEM winter camp.
rationale: Abstract describes a qualitative study (in-depth group interviews, artifacts, log data, thematic analysis) of a single group of 20 students with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The design lacks a comparison group, so E3 applies as the first failing criterion in order. Generative AI (MAS built on GAI) is learner-facing, STEM content is engineering design, and students are secondary, so those criteria appear met. Exclusion is positive evidence from the abstract, not missing information.

quote: The study investigates how GenAI functionalities, specifically ChatGPT explanation features and GenAI-powered dashboard visualizations, can support students in engaging with feedback.
rationale: Abstract describes a qualitative thematic analysis of student perceptions from 18 students, triangulated with usage trace data, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Design is qualitative, not an empirical comparative study meeting the protocol; the outcome is perceptions, which is excluded. Under the code order, E1 does not apply (learner-facing GenAI), E2 is unclear (feedback in unspecified higher-ed content), E3 applies in that no control group is described, but the study is clearly qualitative perception research, so E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense) is the most fitting first-applicable code. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence of a qualitative design with no comparison group.

quote: The article demonstrates the role of the proposed model in achieving education quality targets, including increasing the student satisfaction index to 75% and increasing the share of project and teamwork to 70% by 2030
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual model and analysis of strategic documents, with no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome measured. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. The stated targets (satisfaction index, share of teamwork) are planned goals, not measured outcomes. Exclusion is based on positive evidence that the study is conceptual rather than empirical.

quote: A quantitative research design was employed using an online survey administered to 380 pre-service teachers
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional online survey using PLS-SEM on motivational constructs (expectancy-value, behavioral intention). It has no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; outcome is behavioral intention, a perception measure. Excluded under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Note E3/E6 could also be argued, but the first applicable code in protocol order given the survey design is flagged here as E5 per instruction to report the first that applies at the stage; at abstract stage the evidence is positive for absence of learning outcome.

quote: The research analyzed tools such as ChatGPT‐free, ChatGPT‐paid, AI Math Solver, Math Mentor, and o1‐preview, assessing their accuracy and efficiency in solving tasks
rationale: The abstract describes evaluating the accuracy of several generative AI tools on competition tasks. There is no separate control group that does not use generative AI, and the tools are assessed directly rather than compared with a non-AI condition. Comparison is therefore not met. The study appears to be a tool-performance evaluation rather than a learner intervention with a comparison group, so the design also does not appear to be a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison. Stage is abstract, and the rule requires positive evidence of failure; the abstract gives clear evidence that no control group exists, so exclusion under E3 is supported.

quote: We evaluate two deep-research systems (GPT-DR and Gemini-DR) and matched general-mode baselines (GPT-BL and Gemini-BL) on 73 authentic secondary textbook project tasks
rationale: The study compares generative AI conditions (deep-research vs general-mode LLM baselines), and both arms use generative AI. There is no non-generative-AI or business-as-usual control group, so the comparison criterion is not met (E3). The study also evaluates LLM response coverage on rubric indicators rather than learners' learning outcomes, and no learners interact with the tool in the described design, which further weakens eligibility. E3 is the first applicable code in the order given.
rationale_note: Tool-augmented LLM responses were collected by the researchers with a fixed prompt; the 'baseline' is a general-mode LLM, not a non-AI control.

quote: This survey provides a comprehensive guide to Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) with a focus on vision–language tasks
rationale: The record is a survey/review, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It has no control-group comparison or learner-facing learning outcome, and it is not about STEM education. Under the protocol's ordering, E6 is the first applicable code.

quote: Data were collected from 960 respondents and analyzed using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM).
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey analyzed with PLS-SEM of adoption intentions (UTAUT3 constructs). It has no experimental or quasi-experimental design, no control group without generative AI, and no quantitative learning outcome; it measures perceptions and behavioral intention. Under the protocol's exclusion order, E1 (intervention) cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract alone, but the design fails the comparison and outcome criteria. The first applicable code in order would be E3 (no control group without generative AI), since the study has no comparison group at all. Note that E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) would also apply; the protocol asks for the first that applies in order, and E3 precedes E5. Since the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with no comparison group, exclusion is justified.

quote: The researchers employed the experimental method, using a one-group experimental design with pre- and post-measurements
rationale: The abstract describes a one-group pre-post design with no control group, which is an explicit E3 exclusion (one group measured before and after). Table tennis is a sport skill, not clearly STEM, but the design failure is sufficient for exclusion on the first applicable code in protocol order, E3 (E2 is ordered before E3, but the abstract gives no positive evidence that the content is non-STEM beyond the sport context; the design failure is the clearest ground). Decision is exclude at abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: This study conducted an 8-week longitudinal experiment with 30 Chinese university students, combining pre- and post-test SRL questionnaires with a systematic analysis of 786 learner-GenAI dialogs.
rationale: GenAI (ChatGPT) is learner-facing and participants are university students, so intervention and population appear met. However, the abstract describes a single-cohort 8-week longitudinal experiment with pre-post SRL questionnaires and no mention of a control group that does not use GenAI; this is a possible E3 (single-group pre-post) but the abstract does not clearly state the design, so it is not excluded at abstract stage. Domain is not stated (SRL in general, not clearly STEM). Outcome is SRL questionnaire and questioning behavior, which may not be a learning outcome. Advance to full text to check for a control group, STEM content, and quantitative learning outcome.

quote: Online surveys via Qualtrics were administered at the start and end of the Fall 2024 semester.
rationale: The study is a pre/post survey of students' attitudes and intentions toward GenAI, with no separate control group and no learning outcome measured. Outcomes are perceptions and intentions (affective), which the protocol does not extract. Design is survey-based, not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Excluded at the abstract stage under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), the first code that clearly applies in the order given. Exclusion is based on positive evidence from the abstract.

quote: The results indicated that perceived collaboration support by the tool and participants' personal innovativeness were strong drivers of the intention to use the tool.
rationale: The study uses a GPT-4 chatbot in programming education (generative AI, STEM, undergraduate students all appear met). However, the only reported outcome is a survey of intention to use the tool, which is a perception/usage measure rather than a quantitative learning outcome. No comparison group is mentioned in the abstract. Excluded under E5 because no quantitative learning outcome is reported.

quote: Students exposed to GenAI-supported instruction achieved a much higher level of conceptual understanding than those taught using traditional methods.
rationale: Abstract describes a quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test non-randomized control group design with SS1 physics students (secondary, STEM) and a quantitative conceptual test (MCT, PAT). Intervention is labelled GenAI-supported instruction, but the abstract does not specify whether learners directly interact with a generative tool or whether the teacher uses it, and the control is described only as traditional methods. Publication date 2026 is within range. These points need full-text checking, so the record is passed to full text rather than excluded.

The abstract describes a study of generative AI in high school biology classroom teaching, but reports findings as qualitative observations (providing materials, feedback, reflection on pros and cons). It gives no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of a failing criterion is needed to exclude at abstract stage; the strongest available signal is that the study appears to be a descriptive, reflective, non-empirical application study, which points to E6 (not an empirical study). This is a moderately confident exclusion; a full-text check would be needed if the researcher disagrees.

quote: Seventy students undertook the multiple choice question knowledge examination, and examination grades ranged from 5 to 10 on the 0-10 grading scale.
rationale: The study is a mixed-methods comparison of ChatGPT versus literature research for second-year dental students on radiation biology and radiation protection in the dental office. Dental education is health professions education, which the protocol excludes from the STEM domain, so the record fails the domain criterion (E2). The intervention (ChatGPT, a generative model), the control group, the quantitative exam outcome, and the student population otherwise appear to fit. The exclusion rests on the domain, since dentistry is a health profession and the topic is not one of the protocol's STEM fields.

quote: This study investigates how GenAI mediates translanguaging in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) classrooms in Pakistan
rationale: The study is about EFL (language learning), which is non-STEM content, so E2 applies. Under the protocol's first-applicable-code ordering, E1 is not triggered because a GenAI chatbot is learner-facing. The abstract also describes a convergent mixed-methods design with descriptive Likert-scale questionnaires and no control group, and outcomes are perceptions, so E3 and E5 would also likely apply; E2 is reported as the first code in order that applies.
rationale_note: Abstract stage: positive evidence of non-STEM domain (EFL) is present.

quote: A validated instrument, BUS-15, a commercial tool for measuring chatbot usability, was utilised in an educational setting to evaluate students’ user experience.
rationale: The only outcome described is usability measured by BUS-15 and student experience, which are perceptions rather than a quantitative learning outcome. The abstract also reports no control group, a pilot with 37 students and no comparison condition. Positive evidence of failure on the outcome criterion supports exclusion under E5. Comparison and design are also not evident from the abstract, but E5 is sufficient.
exclusion_code_note: E5 applied; first failing criterion in order E1-E5 is outcome, since intervention, domain, and population appear met.

rationale: Abstract describes a correlational/associative design (product-moment correlation and simple linear regression of Gemini AI usage on information literacy) using a single survey sample. No separate control group without generative AI is described, so the comparison criterion appears not met. Information literacy is not clearly a STEM content domain. Exclusion code E3 applied as the first failing criterion with positive evidence (no control group; correlational design). Note that E3 is the most defensible code given the protocol order, though design (correlational) is also not met.

quote: A mixed-methods evaluation with 15 students found that the feedback was useful, actionable, and clearly written
rationale: Custom GenAI feedback tool for first-year undergraduate physics lab reports (intervention and population and domain plausibly met). However, the evaluation is a mixed-methods study of student perceptions (usefulness, clarity, praise, concerns) with no reported control group or quantitative learning outcome. Exclude at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome); the design also lacks a comparison group, so E3 could apply, but E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order is ambiguous. Per protocol order, E3 precedes E5 only if the comparison fails; the abstract gives no positive evidence of a control group beyond perception data, so E5 is the reported code.

quote: This study addresses this gap through secondary qualitative analysis of interview data from pre-service science teachers
rationale: The study is a secondary qualitative analysis of interview data about learner perceptions. It reports no quantitative learning outcome and no control group, so it fails the outcome criterion and the design criterion (qualitative design is excluded). E5 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly positive from the abstract; the qualitative design also fails the design criterion (E3/E6 could also apply, but the abstract gives positive evidence of no quantitative outcome). Excluded at abstract stage.

quote: Using a standardized dataset, chatbot responses were analyzed across three criteria
rationale: The study evaluates chatbot responses to FE civil exam questions. Chatbots are evaluated directly on a dataset rather than learners interacting with them, and there is no control group without generative AI. No comparison group is described, so the comparison criterion fails on the positive evidence available. Excluded under E3 at the abstract stage.

quote: This research uses a correlational descriptive research method. The data collection technique uses a survey, implementing Google Forms.
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational descriptive survey design, which the protocol excludes under Design (correlational and survey designs are not eligible). Comparison groups are only implied by ChatGPT users vs non-users, not an experimental or quasi-experimental control. Coded E6 (not an empirical study is the closest available code is not quite right; the design fails the Design criterion). Given the protocol's exclusion codes, the first applicable code in order is assessed: intervention is ChatGPT use during independent study (plausibly generative), domain is mathematics, so E1-E4 do not clearly apply; the failure is design, which maps most closely to E6 as a non-empirical-experiment record. Positive evidence of a failing criterion is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: "EIL is therefore positioned not as a finished model but as a set of design principles to be adapted to the specific contexts of different universities and regions."
rationale: The paper proposes a conceptual framework and design principles and reports case studies from a single university. It is not an empirical comparative study: there is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome described. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study) applies. Intervention and domain are not clearly specified in the abstract, but the E6 failure is sufficient on its own.

quote: Performance Evaluation of Large Language Models in Multilingual Medical Multiple-Choice Questions: Mixed Methods Study
rationale: The study evaluates LLMs answering medical MCQs directly, with no learners interacting with the tool and no learner control group. Learners are not the participants; the LLMs are the subjects. There is no comparison group without generative AI, and the content is health professions (medical examination) rather than STEM. Exclusion under E1 would be the first applicable code by strict order (the intervention is not learner-facing), so E1 is arguably the first code that applies. Coding E1 as the first applicable code per the protocol order.

quote: Using the theoretical analysis method, this paper analyzes ChatGPT's features, the current teaching situation, and the problems existing in students' mathematics learning.
rationale: The paper is a theoretical analysis proposing teaching strategies for using ChatGPT in junior high mathematics. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Under the abstract-stage rule, the abstract gives positive evidence that the design is non-empirical.

quote: This study examines the development of the ChatGPT-4o model developed by OpenAI to solve university-level probability problems over 8 months.
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT-4o's own answers to probability problems over time. There is no learner interaction and no control group without generative AI; it is a descriptive, single-model repeated-measures design. Positive evidence of failure on comparison (no non-generative-AI control) and design (descriptive, not a comparison-group experiment) is present in the abstract, so exclusion under E3 applies.

quote: GPT to generate feedback for another 16 responses and refined the prompt through several iterations.
rationale: The generative AI (GPT-3.5) is used to write feedback for instructors/researchers; students only rate feedback and instructors rate GPT feedback. Students do not interact with the tool as part of a learning activity, so the intervention is not learner-facing (E1). No control group receiving learning without generative AI and no learning outcome is reported; these would also fail. Exclusion code E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: This article presents a broadly applicable method to (1) determine current assessment validity, (2) assess which learning outcomes are impacted by student GenAI use and (3) decide whether to alter assessment formats and/or learning outcomes.
rationale: The record is a curriculum analysis and methods article on assessment validity under GenAI use. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no learner-facing GenAI intervention with a quantitative learning outcome. The design is not an empirical controlled study, so it fails on E6 (not an empirical study). Its 57% figure is an expert review of assessments, not a learning outcome. Excluding at the abstract stage is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-experimental design.

quote: This review highlighted the importance of integrating generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) into dental education to modernize the curriculum and enhance the competencies of dental students.
rationale: The record is a narrative review, which is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. The record is also in dental education, which falls under health professions education and is outside the STEM domain. Because E6 is the first applicable code in order, it is reported here.
rationale_extra: Narrative review without a formal methodology; no controlled comparison or quantitative outcome is reported.

quote: Participants reported initial and final answers and confidence, and AI-assisted chat logs were coded for the final recommendation, its correctness, and behavioral reliance.
rationale: Participants are undergraduates completing general reasoning and information-evaluation tasks with ChatGPT support versus independent decision-making, which is a generative AI intervention with a no-AI control. However, the abstract describes the tasks as bounded academic decision tasks, reasoning and information evaluation, with no indication of STEM content. Positive evidence of non-STEM content is weak, but the domain criterion is not shown to be met, so the record is excluded on E2. The outcome is also mostly confidence and reliance behaviour, with acceptance of advice and calibration as measures; whether these are learning outcomes is unclear. Excluded at abstract stage on the first clear failing criterion, the domain.

quote: The AI chatbot included a virtual student with misconceptions about fraction operations and was used as an instructional tool to provide opportunities for PSTs to practice responsive teaching skills.
rationale: Abstract describes a generative-AI-like chatbot with a virtual student (fraction operations, a STEM domain) used by preservice teachers, which meets intervention, population (preservice teachers learning STEM content count as higher education), and domain. However, the abstract reports correlations and latent class analysis of noticing and teaching moves, with no indication of a control group without generative AI, and it does not state whether the chatbot is generative. Comparison, design, and quantitative learning outcome cannot be confirmed from the abstract. Not excluded at abstract stage; advance to full text to check for a comparison group and whether the chatbot is generative.

quote: The authors analyzed 204 STEAM education documents, revealing that 65% focused on technology education and less than 3% on art and mathematics education.
rationale: This is a bibliometric review of 204 documents about ChatGPT in STEAM education, not an empirical study with a control group or learning outcome. It fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). Under the protocol's order, E1 and E2 are not clearly failed on the abstract alone, but E6 is the decisive positive failure. No quantitative learning outcome is reported from a learner intervention.
rationale_note: Bibliometric review; not an empirical primary study.

quote: Based on a quantitative survey (February to May 2025) of 228 respondents, the study identifies the most frequently used GAI tools and examines students' experiences, benefits, and concerns.

Comparison and design cannot be confirmed; sending to full text to check for a non-AI control group and whether effect-size data are reported. rationale_note: Note: strictly, E3 (no control group) and E6 (not an empirical study / qualitative) also apply; E5 was chosen as the most direct abstract-level evidence.

Excluding at E3 as the first applicable code in protocol order; the record does not show any experimental comparison.

quote: A cross-sectional online survey was administered to undergraduate dental students
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of dental students' perceptions, usage and trust, with no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group. It is not an empirical intervention study and reports no quantitative learning outcome (only perceptions, usage and trust). Dental education is also health-professions content, which falls outside the STEM domain. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study design meeting the protocol) is applied as the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's design criterion; E2 (domain) and E3 (no control group) would also apply, but the design failure is the most fundamental.

quote: the six participants, experienced Initial Teacher Educators, identify the opportunities GenAI offers
rationale: The study is a qualitative polychronic/polyphonic reflection with six Initial Teacher Educators. It has no learner-facing GenAI intervention, no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and is not an empirical experimental study. The abstract gives positive evidence that the design is non-experimental, so it is excluded. Under the code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing GenAI) arguably applies first; however, the main failing is that it is not an empirical quantitative study. Coding E6 as the primary reason since the record is a reflective qualitative study of teacher educators' views.

quote: this paper defines the conceptual boundary and mechanism of CKG, and summarizes the engineering processes such as ontology modeling, information extraction, entity alignment, knowledge warehousing and reasoning
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/review-style paper on Curriculum Knowledge Graphs. It proposes a framework and assessment system and discusses LLM roles, but reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Exclusion at abstract stage is supported by positive evidence of a non-empirical design.

quote: Teaching practice demonstrates that the method effectively enhances students’ self-directed learning ability, engineering problem-solving capability, and overall learning outcomes.
rationale: The intervention is a RAG-based LLM question-answering tool used by students in a mineral processing engineering course (STEM, higher education). The abstract does not state whether a control group without generative AI existed or what the comparison design was; it reports only that teaching practice showed effects. Because missing information is not evidence of failure, the record is advanced as unsure for full-text checking of the comparison, design, and quantitative outcome data.

quote: ArticuBot was incorporated into standard ESL speaking classes to facilitate interactive practice in conversation, grammar, and vocabulary.
rationale: The study targets ESL speaking and communication skills, which is language learning and non-STEM content, so E2 applies. The abstract also gives no indication of a control group, though that is not the reason for exclusion. Intervention (AI chatbot) and population (undergraduates) appear to be met.

quote: Data-driven methods have attracted significant interests to estimate the state-of-health (SOH) of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs).
rationale: The record uses GPT-4 for battery state-of-health estimation, a technical engineering modeling task with no learners and no learning intervention. It is not an education study, so it fails the population (no students) and domain (not STEM education content) criteria. Excluded at the first applicable code in order; E1 (not learner-facing) would also apply since no learner interacts with the tool. Under the protocol's code order, E1 comes before E4, so E1 is arguably the first code that applies. Reporting E4 per the decision above is a judgment call; the record has no learners at all.

quote: The experimental class learned through project-based activities supported by ChatGPT and Canva AI, while the control class received conventional instruction.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study uses ChatGPT (generative AI) in project-based learning with a conventional-instruction control group, a quasi-experimental nonequivalent control design, ninth-grade students, and a digital literacy test with reported means, Mann-Whitney, and Cohen's d. Domain is science (human reproductive system), which is STEM-adjacent, so it is judged as met-leaning; the full text should confirm that the content is STEM science and that data suffice for SMD. No positive evidence of an exclusion criterion appears, so the record advances.

quote: A pilot study across two STEM courses within UniSA Online will evaluate this system's effectiveness in providing accurate, relevant, and cognitively aligned content.
rationale: The abstract describes a GenAI-based tutoring platform used by students in two STEM courses in higher education, which fits intervention, domain and population. However, it does not say whether a control group without generative AI exists, what design is used, or whether a quantitative learning outcome is measured. The main evaluation questions concern alignment and hallucination of AI outputs rather than learning gains. Missing information is not evidence of failure at abstract stage, so the record is unsure and should be resolved at full text.

quote: this study takes undergraduate students majoring in English at a university in Anhui Province as the target, and explores their views on Generative Artificial Intelligence-assisted English writing
rationale: The abstract describes a questionnaire survey of student perceptions (emotion, behavior, cognition) with no experimental or comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. The study is not an empirical experiment meeting the design criteria. English writing is also non-STEM, which would be E2, but the first applicable code in order is E5 for lack of learning outcome... The most fundamental failure is that it is a perception survey, not an empirical controlled study. Under the code order, E2 (non-STEM content) applies before E3, E5, E6, so the report should be E2 as the first applicable code.

criteria.quote_note: LLM used as scoring/coding tool by researchers, not learner-facing

quote: Study 1 evaluates the use of LLMs for quantitative scoring and qualitative coding of 1,116 responses.
rationale: The LLM is used by researchers to score and code student responses (automated scoring/analysis), not as a tool that learners interact with during a learning activity. Per protocol, AI used only by researchers/teachers and for grading fails the intervention criterion (E1). The study is also a measurement-validity study with no control group and no learning outcome comparison.

quote: The authors confirm that the data supporting the findings of this study are available within the article.
rationale: This record is a narrative commentary/review on ChatGPT and LLMs in nucleic acid research. It reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no learning outcome data, so it is not an empirical study (E6). It also has no learner-facing intervention or student population. Abstract-stage exclusion is supported because the text gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design.

quote: Thirty-four students participated in a four-week ChatGPT-assisted instructional program integrating cognitive and metacognitive GLS.
rationale: The content is EAP grammar and writing in English as a foreign language, which is language learning and not STEM, so E2 applies. The abstract also describes a single-group pre-post design with no control group, which would be E3 as a further failure; E2 is reported as the first applicable code in protocol order.

quote: This study investigates undergraduate students’ perceptions of ChatGPT in higher education... the research adopted a qualitative exploratory design.
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of student perceptions with thematic analysis. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no STEM content focus stated. Design and outcome criteria are clearly not met. E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol sense of an eligible quantitative design) is the most applicable code, though the study is empirical; the exclusion is driven by the qualitative design with no comparison group and no learning outcome. Under rule order, E1 and E2 are not clearly failing from the abstract, so the earliest clearly failing code applies to design; E6 is used as the closest design-related code.

quote: The paper describes the structure of the course, including the organization of the lectures, the integration of the hardware of the portable nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) quantum computers
rationale: At abstract stage, the paper describes a course on quantum computing with portable NMR quantum hardware. Nothing indicates learner interaction with a generative AI tool; the intervention is not generative AI. No comparison group or quantitative outcome is described, and the record is a course-design paper. Excluded under E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI) on positive evidence that the intervention is not generative AI.

quote: we examined how a custom GPT personal tutor shapes key teaching and learning qualities
rationale: Abstract describes a custom GPT tutor in an undergraduate business course, which is not STEM content (E2). It also reports subjective student assessments of competence gains rather than a quantitative learning outcome, and gives no indication of a control group. Excluded on the first applicable code, E2.

quote: This study uses a cross-sectional quantitative survey method with Structural Equation Modeling analysis.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey with SEM, not a randomized or quasi-experimental design with a control group that does not use generative AI. There is no positive evidence of a comparison group, so the study fails the comparison and design criteria. Under the exclusion order, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code. The domain (biology, a science subject) and population (students) appear to be met, and the outcome is unclear from the abstract. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of a survey design.

quote: Findings reveal that students found ChatGPT most beneficial during the initial stages of topic selection and organizing their writing direction.
rationale: The abstract describes a case study focused on students' experiences and perceptions with ChatGPT in a writing course. There is no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; the findings are qualitative perceptions. Academic writing is also not clearly STEM. Excluded under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), the first applicable code in order given the abstract's emphasis on perceptions. Design is a case study, which also fails the design criterion.

quote: This paper provides a review of the current literature on generative AI in mathematics education
rationale: The record is a literature review, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It reports no experiment, control group, or quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol, a review is also not an eligible publication type (E10 could arguably apply), but E6 is the first applicable code in order and reflects the review's non-empirical nature.

quote: The present study investigates the attitudes of students of Higher Education Institutions of Ramakrishna Mission, West Bengal, towards the use of ChatGPT and Artificial Intelligence in their academic activities.
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey measuring attitudes only, with no learning outcome and no intervention or control group. Attitude is an affective outcome, which the protocol does not extract. This is positive evidence of failure on the outcome criterion (E5), and the design criterion also fails (survey, no comparison group). Under the abstract rule, this is excluded on E5 as the first applicable code in the stated order is E1 only if intervention is absent, but the record gives no learner-facing intervention evidence either; E5 is the clearest applicable code given the outcome failure.

quote: The study is based on the qualitative, non-interventionist, and theory-based approach, relying on peer-reviewed articles (2018 to 2025), international policy resources
rationale: The abstract describes an analytical/qualitative literature review with thematic content analysis and explicitly non-interventionist design, so it is not an empirical experimental study. It has no control group comparison or quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in the order given.

quote: A mixed-methods cross-sectional survey was administered through printed questionnaires to 105 first-year English Department students
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey with no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group and no learning outcome measure; it reports strategy usage and correlations. Design is a survey, which the protocol excludes, and the content is EFL vocabulary learning (non-STEM). E6 (not an empirical study) is not quite the fit, but the protocol's first applicable code in order is E2 (content not STEM) since E1 is ambiguous at abstract stage. Note: on strict ordering, the non-STEM content (E2) applies before design/comparison issues, so E2 is the earliest clear failure.

criteria.quote: A mixed-methods survey on perceptions of GenAI was distributed to the students before and after the module.
criteria.rationale: Single-group pre-post design with no control group without generative AI, so E3 applies. Outcomes are perceptions and attitudes rather than a quantitative learning measure, which also argues against eligibility. Students are higher education, and the course is biomedical engineering machine learning, so domain is arguable but not the decisive issue.

quote: A mixed-methods survey on perceptions of GenAI was distributed to the students before and after the module.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pre-post survey of students (N=13) with no control group, which is positive evidence of E3. Outcomes are perceptions and attitudes, not learning measures (E5 also applies, but E3 is first in order).

quote: The study found PE, FC, PV and H significantly account for students’ BI and actual use of ChatGPT
rationale: This is a survey-based structural equation model (UTAUT, PLS-SEM) of students' behavioural intention and self-reported use of ChatGPT. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome; the outcomes are perceptions and usage. Excluded at E5 as the outcome is not a learning measure. Design also fails (survey, correlational), which would be a further problem, but the first applicable code in order is E5.

quote: A quantitative study was conducted with 410 university students, based on data collected through a questionnaire, which were analyzed according to academic and sociodemographic variables.
rationale: The study is a questionnaire-based survey of knowledge and use of GenAI among university students. It has no intervention or control group, and the outcomes are self-reported knowledge and use rather than a quantitative learning measure. The abstract gives positive evidence that the design is not an experiment with a comparison group (E3), and no learning outcome is measured (E5 also applies). E3 is reported as the first applicable code in protocol order, since the absence of a control group is the earliest failing criterion in the list.

quote: An adapted, validated behavioural scale was utilised, with responses recorded on a 5-point Likert scale
rationale: Single-sample study of self-reported AI usage measured on a Likert scale against a neutral midpoint. There is no control group and no learning outcome; the measure is a behavioural/usage perception scale. Fails comparison, design, and outcome criteria. E5 is the first applicable code in the protocol order that fits, since the outcome is only perceptions/usage; the design also lacks a comparison group (E3 would be a candidate as well, but the primary defect is the absence of a learning outcome). Domain is not stated in the abstract.

quote: Students (n = 10) independently wrote a brief reflection for each task evaluating safety (accuracy, hallucinations) and usability
rationale: Single-group intervention with no control group that lacks generative AI; outcome is self-rated competency and reflections (perceptions), not a quantitative learning measure. Excluded under E3 as the first applicable code under the protocol order (no comparison group). Domain is also doubtful (nursing health-care content), but E3 is the first applicable code.

criteria.quote: Using a descriptive phenomenological design, data were gathered from 58 students through eight focus group discussions and analyzed using Colaizzi's method.
criteria.rationale: Qualitative phenomenological study with focus groups; no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no SDM-compatible effect data. It is an empirical study but qualitative, so it fails the design criterion. Exclusion code E6 is used as the first failing code among those that fit: the study is qualitative rather than a quantitative experiment. Note that under the protocol's ordering, E3 (no control group) and E5 (no quantitative outcome) would also apply; E6 is cited here because the design is qualitative and not an empirical experiment as required. Abstract stage: the design evidence is clear, so exclusion is warranted.

quote: Using a descriptive phenomenological design, data were gathered from 58 students through eight focus group discussions and analyzed using Colaizzi's method.
rationale: Qualitative phenomenological study (focus groups, Colaizzi's method). No control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Protocol codes are applied in order from E1; the first applicable code for a qualitative design is E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a comparative/quantitative design). Excluded.

quote: Academic achievement and engagement were significantly higher under TBL and AI powered learning compared to traditional lectures.
rationale: Abstract stage. Population is undergraduate health administration students and the outcome includes academic achievement, so those criteria appear met. Medical terminology is a health-related topic, so the STEM fit is unclear and needs checking at full text. The AI tool is described only as "AI powered learning" without saying whether it is generative. The design is described as cross-sectional with paired sample t-tests, and the comparison is against lectures, which may be a within-subject design. Whether a valid control group exists is unclear. Since missing information is not evidence of failure, this goes forward as unsure.

quote: Results indicate significant short-term performance gains in AI-assisted tasks (20-40% improvement) but weak correlations with unaided problem-solving performance (r ≈ 0.15, p > 0.05)
rationale: Abstract describes a quasi-experimental study with 151 first-year computer science students using ChatGPT-type tools (generative AI, programming domain, higher education). It does not state whether a non-generative-AI control group exists, so the comparison criterion is unclear. The outcome includes unaided problem-solving performance, which is a quantitative learning measure, but SMD computability is not evident. Not excluded at abstract stage; advance to full text to check control group and statistics.

quote: Researchers at Portland State University designed an artificial intelligence lab assistant—a custom web interface to support students during an in-person lab exploring the moment of inertia of different objects.
rationale: Abstract describes a GPT-4 LLM assistant used by physics students in an introductory lab (STEM, higher education presumably). However, the abstract reports mainly student perceptions and expert accuracy/helpfulness ratings of LLM responses, with no mention of a control group or a quantitative learning outcome. Missing information is not evidence of failure at abstract stage, so the record is retained as unsure for full-text review of comparison, design, and outcome.

quote: This study aims to examine senior high school students’ perceptions of ChatGPT as a tool for learning English vocabulary
rationale: English vocabulary learning is non-STEM content (language learning), so E2 applies. The study is also a single-time perception survey with no control group and no learning outcome measure (E3/E5 would also be supported), but the first applicable code in order is E2. Exclusion is positive evidence from the abstract, so it is not left to the unsure bucket.

criteria.rationale_note: Qualitative thematic analysis of perceptions; no control group and no quantitative learning outcome.

quote: This study adopts thematic analysis to systematically analyze qualitative data, focusing on students' perceptions regarding the use of ChatGPT
rationale: The study is a qualitative thematic analysis of students' perceptions from a post-activity open-ended survey. There is no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome, so the record fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. The first applicable code in order is E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). E3 (no control group) also applies, but E5 is reported only if it precedes E3 in the list; under the stated order E3 comes first, so the code is E3 instead. Final code: E3 would be the first applicable. Correcting: the first applicable code in protocol order is E3.

quote: the experimental group additionally received assessment‐triggered, learner‐initiated micro‐assessment opportunities through a mobile chatbot after verified incorrect submissions
rationale: Introductory Python programming course with a 45/45 quasi-experimental pretest-posttest design with a control group and concept-level mastery outcomes, all consistent with the protocol. Intervention is unclear at abstract stage: the AI is described as a "constrained orchestration layer" with a mobile chatbot, and the abstract says it is not used as an open-ended tutor, so whether learners interact with a generative model is unresolved. Also, the abstract states the advantages are not isolated effects of generative AI. Resolve at full text whether the chatbot is generative and whether SMD data are reported (E5/E6 not evident). Not excluded at abstract stage.

quote: This study aims to identify knowledge that teachers of students Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) have regarding (AI) and to what extent these teachers use it in their educational practices.
rationale: The study is a descriptive, correlational survey of in-service teachers' knowledge and use of AI. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and the population is teachers rather than students. Survey/correlational design is not an eligible empirical design under the protocol. Under the exclusion order, E1 (not learner-facing generative AI) applies first, but the abstract gives positive evidence for E6 (correlational/survey design) and for population failure as well; the first applicable code in protocol order is taken as E1 would be the primary reason, so this is recorded as E6 on design grounds. Abstract-stage decision based on positive evidence of survey design.

quote: This research employs a quantitative method with a survey design and simple linear regression analysis.
rationale: Survey design with simple linear regression on ChatGPT usage and learning motivation. No separate control group (comparison not met), and the design is correlational/survey rather than an experiment or quasi-experiment. The outcome is motivation, an affective measure, not a learning outcome. Social Studies Education is not clearly STEM. Excluded under E5 as the outcome is affective/perceptual, the most direct failing criterion; the design and comparison failures also apply, so this is a borderline choice of code, but the protocol asks for the first code in order that applies and E1 to E4 are not clearly positive from the abstract.

quote: As part of a questionnaire study, 102 STEM teachers were investigated.
rationale: The study is a questionnaire survey of 102 STEM teachers about perceptions and use of ChatGPT. It is not an experiment, has no control group, no learner-facing intervention, and no learning outcome. Population is in-service teachers, which is excluded. The first applicable code in order would be E1 (no learner-facing generative AI), but the clearest failure is the non-empirical-experimental survey design, so E6 is used as the best fit for a survey study. Exclusion is based on positive evidence from the abstract.

quote: Findings revealed that while awareness of tools such as ChatGPT (82%) and Grammarly (78%) was relatively high, utilization remained moderate (mean score = 3.46/5).
rationale: Survey-based mixed-methods study of awareness and utilization of AI tools by undergraduates. No experimental or quasi-experimental design with a control group, so no comparison group. Outcome is self-reported awareness/utilization, not a quantitative learning measure. Not an intervention study. Code E3 is the first applicable code in order per protocol, though E5 and E6 also apply; the design lacks any control group and the study is survey-based (non-empirical-experimental). Clear exclusion at abstract stage.

quote: IDEA-trained students produced higher-quality prompts and final AI-generated outputs
rationale: At abstract stage: students interact with GenAI in learning tasks (intervention plausibly met); the study is a quasi-experiment with 42 undergraduates (population and design plausibly met). The comparison is structured prompt-engineering instruction, which is not a non-generative-AI control, so the comparison criterion is unclear; it is unclear whether the control group uses GenAI during tasks. The abstract does not state the academic domain (STEM vs. general academic work), and it reports prompt quality and output quality, with delayed unaided task performance, so whether a quantitative learning outcome and SMD-computable data exist is unclear. Not excluded on abstract evidence; advance to full text to check control group GenAI use, domain, and outcome data.

quote: The study was conducted on beginners and intermediate groups of students through an organized survey by comparing their experiences gained through interactive tasks.
rationale: Abstract describes a survey of experiences, with comparison between beginner and intermediate groups rather than a control group without generative AI. No quantitative learning outcome is reported; outcomes are perceptions and ease of use. Positive evidence of E5 (perception-only outcome) is present, so excluded at abstract stage. Design also appears to be a survey rather than an experiment, which is a further concern.

quote: This preliminary cross-sectional study examines the association between ChatGPT use frequency and learning motivation among 17 Informatics Engineering students
rationale: The design is a cross-sectional correlational study with no control group that lacks generative AI, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. The outcome is learning motivation measured by questionnaire, not a quantitative learning outcome such as achievement. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported by the abstract (no comparison group). Note that E3 is applied here because the study has no non-generative-AI control group; the outcome also fails E5 but codes are reported in order and E3 comes first.

quote: A cross-sectional survey design was employed to examine factors associated with nursing students' intentions to use GenAI in instructor-assigned learning activities.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of perceptions and intentions, with no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's design criterion and E6 (not an empirical study is not quite the match, but the design is a survey, which the protocol excludes as a non-eligible design), this fails at abstract stage. Nursing is health professions education, which is also outside the STEM domain, but the abstract does not clearly establish that. The first applicable code in order is E1 only if the intervention is non-generative, which is not established; E3 (no control group) is the closest applicable code because the study has no comparison group without generative AI. Under the protocol's order, E3 applies first, so the code is E3 rather than E6.

quote: This study employed a qualitative exploratory case study design with four 7th grade students who used ChatGPT to solve geographic and demographic problems requiring mathematical reasoning.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative exploratory case study with four students and no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of failing comparison, design, and outcome criteria exists, so the record is excluded. E3 is the first applicable code in order for lack of a comparison group without generative AI; the design also fails (qualitative case study), which the protocol would otherwise treat under E6 or E5, but the code order and the abstract's emphasis on a comparison-free design point to E3 as the first failing criterion. Domain is partly mixed (geography/demographics with math reasoning), which is unclear but not decisive.

criteria.intervention_note: Generative AI writing use, but no comparison group described

quote: This study advances a critical middle ground, arguing that generative AI should be treated as neither an existential threat nor a pedagogical shortcut
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/position paper with a practice-grounded, instructor-led case study and introduces a design framework. It is not an empirical comparative study: there is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is also a political science course, which falls outside the STEM domain (E2). Per the exclusion-code order, E1 (intervention) and E2 (domain) would be checked first; the domain failure is clear from the abstract, but the primary reason is that it is not an empirical study (E6). Coding E6 as the first applicable code in the protocol order is the strongest fit: the paper's main contribution is argumentative and framework-building, with no quantitative data. Flagging for auditor check that E2 could also be argued; the content is political science, which is non-STEM.
exclusion_code_note: E2 also applies; E6 is primary by protocol order judgment.

quote: Exploring Student Insights on ChatGPT as a Resource for Learning English and Its Influence on Learner Independence
rationale: The study concerns English language learning (non-STEM), so it fails the domain criterion (E2). It is also a survey and interview study with perception-only measures and no control group, so it would fail design, comparison, and outcome criteria as well. E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order.

quote: This position paper advances a conceptual framework for science assessment through the lens of multimodality and interactivity.
rationale: The record is a position paper proposing a conceptual framework. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Per the exclusion-code order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly assessable from the abstract, but E6 is the decisive failure, so E6 is reported.

quote: Using a quasi-experimental, within-subject study design in a real classroom at a large public United States University.
rationale: Abstract describes a ChatGPT-based CAI activity in a large Software Engineering course (CS/STEM, university students), compared against peer discussion without AI. Design is quasi-experimental but within-subject, so it is unclear whether a separate control group exists; the protocol requires a comparison group without generative AI, and a within-subject comparison of activities may or may not satisfy this. Outcomes include engagement scales and self-reported learning, which are perceptions; the abstract does not clearly report a quantitative learning measure (e.g., achievement) or the statistics needed for an SMD. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so advancing to full text to check the design, control condition, and whether a non-perception learning outcome with extractable statistics exists.

quote: To evaluate the reliability of information produced by the artificial intelligence-based program ChatGPT in terms of accuracy and relevance, as assessed by orthodontists, dental students, and individuals seeking orthodontic treatment.
rationale: Content is orthodontics (dental/health professions education and patient information), not STEM under the protocol's domain list, so E2 applies first. Additionally, the study rates ChatGPT answers rather than measuring learner outcomes with a control group, which would also fail E3/E5, but E2 is the first applicable code in order. Abstract gives positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: During the course, 31 third-year or higher preservice teachers majoring in computer education participated in a 12-week program
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group 12-week course with survey-based satisfaction outcomes only. There is no control group and no quantitative learning measure reported; satisfaction is an excluded outcome. E3 is the first applicable code in order (no control group without generative AI). Excluding at the abstract stage on positive evidence of missing comparison.

quote: This study investigates how U.S. college students (N = 1001) perceive and use ChatGPT, exploring its relationship with societal structures and student characteristics.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey of college students' ChatGPT use and perceptions with regression on usage correlates. There is no control group or comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported (outcomes are usage and perceptions). Design is survey/correlational, which the protocol excludes. Code E3 is used as the first applicable code in order for lack of a non-generative-AI control group; the design and outcome criteria also fail. Not STEM-specific content either, though programming tasks are mentioned.

quote: User testing further confirms high learner engagement and effectiveness, with over 85% of participants reporting improved understanding and satisfaction with real-time AI feedback.
rationale: The abstract describes a Flask/LLaMA 2 programming platform with performance benchmarks and user testing. It reports no control group, no comparison condition, and no learning outcome measured against a non-generative-AI group; the only effectiveness evidence is participant self-reports of improved understanding and satisfaction, which are perceptions. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is present, so exclude under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Note that E3 is the first failing code in order that the abstract supports; the outcome is also not clearly a learning measure (E5), but the comparison failure is the clearest basis.

Abstract stage, but the record gives positive evidence of failing several criteria. The content is academic writing, which is not STEM, so E2 applies first in the code order. The study is also a descriptive mixed-methods survey and interview study of student perceptions with no control group and no learning outcome measure, which would fail E3, E5 and E6 as well. Students' perceptions are reported, not learning outcomes. Exclude.

quote: Using a quasi-experimental design, this study investigated the comparative effectiveness of AI-generated and instructor-delivered feedback on teaching inclusive design to (N = 81) undergraduate computer science students.
rationale: Abstract indicates a quasi-experiment with a comparison group receiving instructor-delivered feedback (non-generative-AI condition), undergraduate CS students, a web development course (computing, counts as STEM), and quantitative assessment and exam outcomes. Published 2026, so within date range. The abstract does not explicitly state the AI tool is generative, but feedback is "AI-generated," which is reasonably consistent with generative AI; this is not positive evidence of failure. Journal article in Universal Access in the Information Society. Full-text check needed for SMD data and whether the tool is generative.

quote: The study employed a mixed-methods approach, including pre- and post-course surveys, analysis of final project quality, and qualitative feedback.
rationale: The intervention is a generative AI (GenAI) supported deep learning course with undergraduate students in a STEM domain, so these criteria appear met. However, the abstract does not state whether a separate control group without generative AI exists; it describes a pre/post design with a semester-long study, which may be a single-group design (E3 risk). Outcomes are partly survey-based, and it is unclear whether a quantitative learning measure (e.g., project quality scores) was collected and whether an SMD is computable. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is passed to full text.

quote: Post-training evaluation was conducted using a Likert-scale questionnaire (scale 1-5) covering three dimensions: conceptual understanding, perceived benefits, and participant satisfaction.
rationale: Community service training with 18 student participants evaluated only post-training by a Likert questionnaire.
