Surgical nursing is also a health professions topic, which falls under the domain exclusion, but the first applicable code in protocol order is E3 when no comparison group exists. Under the protocol's ordering, E1 is not clearly established from the abstract since chatbot use is self-reported rather than an assigned learning intervention, but the design itself is non-experimental, so E3 is the clearest code. Decision is exclude at abstract stage on positive evidence of a non-experimental, non-comparative design.

The record has only a title and venue, with no abstract. The title suggests a comparison of cognitive support tools in programming learning, with "AI" as one option against "maps" (a non-AI tool), which could fit the comparison criterion. However, the title does not establish whether the AI tool is generative, whether the design is randomized or quasi-experimental, whether the population is students, or whether a quantitative learning outcome was measured. Under the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is advanced for full-text review. Year 2026 meets the date criterion; domain (programming) is STEM.

quote: The resulting typology is synthesized into a partially ordered taxonomy that captures the complexity and multidimensionality of student thinking in AI-mediated learning contexts.
rationale: The study is a typology/classification analysis of existing CoMTA tutoring dialogues, with LLMs classifying student prompts. It has no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group, and reports no learning outcome. Positive evidence of failure exists on comparison, design, and outcome. Because the abstract gives positive evidence that the comparison (no control group) fails, E3 is the first applicable code in the stated order, though E5 and E6 would also apply. Given the abstract stage rule, the exclusion rests on the absence of any comparison group described in the abstract.

quote: Two human evaluators independently classified the students' responses based on self-regulated learning processes: planning, monitoring, and evaluation.
rationale: The LLMs are used by researchers to classify learner survey responses, not as a learner-facing tool within a learning activity (E1). The study has no control group and no learning outcome; it is a methods comparison of LLM classification accuracy against human coders. Domain is EFL writing/applied linguistics, which is non-STEM. E1 is the first applicable code in the specified order.

quote: We analysed, with phenomenological tools, the means of the student's self-perception of the advantage of online study.
rationale: The abstract describes a phenomenological analysis of students' self-perceptions, which is a qualitative design with perception-only data and no quantitative learning outcome or control group. Exclusion is on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), since the study reports only perceptions. The design also appears non-experimental, but the outcome failure is the clearest positive evidence at the abstract stage.

quote: The study uses two undergraduate engineering case studies, and the findings suggest that AI-assisted vibe coding can substantially reduce the technical barriers to educational simulation development.
rationale: The GenAI vibe coding is used by instructors to develop simulations, not by learners in a learning activity, so E1 applies. The design is a preliminary case study with no control group and no learning outcome measured, so it would also fail E3 and E5, but E1 is the first applicable code in order. Abstract shows no comparison group or quantitative learning outcome.

quote: A quasi-experimental design was used involving 120 students (60 control and 60 experimental) of two matched government secondary schools.
rationale: Abstract describes a quasi-experimental design with a control group receiving traditional instruction, secondary students, and quantitative pre/post outcomes (Watson-Glaser, SSLSS) with effect sizes reported. Generative AI tools (ChatGPT, Gemini) are used by students. Domain is unclear: critical thinking and sustainable learning are not clearly STEM content from the abstract, so the STEM criterion cannot be confirmed at abstract stage. Not excluded on that basis since the abstract does not give positive evidence of non-STEM content; full text should check the subject matter taught. Publication date 2026 meets the date criterion.

quote: Regression analysis revealed a significant model explaining approximately 40% of the variance in final exam scores, with discussions focused on real‐world applications and conceptual understanding being stronger predictors than those centered on procedural knowledge.
rationale: Remedial mathematics course for STEM majors with students analyzing ChatGPT responses (generative AI, learner-facing; population and domain met). However, the abstract describes a single-cohort regression of discussion scores against final exam scores, with no mention of a control group without generative AI. Design and comparison are unclear; no positive evidence of a failed criterion at abstract stage, so unsure and resolve at full text.

quote: The study involved a purposefully sampled 200 secondary school students and 20 teachers, with 93% of the participants indicating that they would continue to use the tool
rationale: Llama-based chatbot used by secondary students (intervention plausibly met), but the abstract describes no control group; the evaluation reports only satisfaction and intention to continue use, with no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of missing comparison group and of perception-only outcomes supports exclusion. Coded E3 as the first applicable code in order is arguably E3 (no comparison group); E5 also applies on outcomes. Given code order, E3 is reported.

quote: This article reports on responses to a survey that invited students and instructors involved in writing-intensive courses to reflect on their views
rationale: The study is a survey of student and instructor views, with coded open-ended responses. It is not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a control group, and it reports perceptions rather than a quantitative learning outcome. It is also a writing course context, not STEM. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is applied as the first applicable code under the protocol's ordering, since the design is survey/qualitative, which the protocol lists as not eligible. Excluding at abstract stage is justified because positive evidence of a failed design and outcome is present.

quote: The study was conducted via an online survey using a sample of 441 students representing various higher education institutions in Russia and Kazakhstan.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional online survey of student attitudes and usage with correlation and regression analysis. It has no control group and no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and it measures perceptions rather than a quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion E3 is the first code that applies on positive evidence, though E6 (not an empirical study in the experimental sense) and E5 would also fit; E3 is reported first in protocol order because there is no comparison group without generative AI.

quote: Conducted with nine educational researchers in a doctoral-level AIEd course, our research used editable prompt templates and keywords to structure the prompt crafting process.
rationale: Abstract describes a descriptive study with nine participants, using descriptive statistics and network analysis of foraging behavior and a Computational Thinking survey. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome measured against a comparison, so the design is not an eligible experimental or quasi-experimental study. Exclusion code E6 is used as the study is not an empirical comparison design; the study also is a master's thesis-based article, and the publication type is not clearly a journal article. Excluding at abstract stage is supported by positive evidence of no comparison group and no learning outcome.

The study uses ChatGPT to classify open-ended student evaluation of teaching comments, comparing zero-shot/few-shot prompting against supervised models (CNN, LSTM, BERT). Learners do not interact with the generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; the tool is applied by researchers to label text, so the intervention is not learner-facing (E1). No learner control group or learning outcome is reported, and the content is teacher evaluation rather than STEM. Excluding on E1 as the first applicable code.

quote: The study is designed as a cross-sectional survey, with an effective sample size of 880 respondents from southwestern China
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey with SEM and machine learning on perceptions and intended use of GenAI. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group, and no learning outcome is measured (adoption/usage and perception constructs only). Design and outcome criteria are clearly not met. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is used as the first applicable code in order; the design failure is also evident. Domain is not STEM-specific (mixed academic backgrounds). Decision is exclude on the abstract, which gives positive evidence of a survey design.

quote: Analysis of student performance shows that both AI tools and AI guidance improved student performance and allowed them to tackle complex tasks and real-world applications versus AI tools alone without guidance.
rationale: Environmental data science course (STEM) with generative AI tools (ChatGPT, Jupyter AI) learner-facing, undergraduate/graduate students, and performance outcomes are mentioned. However, the abstract's comparison appears to be AI tools with guidance versus AI tools alone, which may be two generative AI variants with no non-AI control group (possible E3). Whether a no-AI comparison group exists, and whether the design is quasi-experimental, cannot be determined from the abstract. Not excluded at abstract stage; resolve at fulltext.

quote: we explore the potential of six different large language models (LLMs; GPT‐3.5, GPT‐4, Llama 2, Llama 3, Gemini‐Pro and Cohere Command R Plus) to generate responses with psychometric properties comparable to those of human respondents
rationale: The LLMs are used as simulated respondents for item calibration, not as a learning tool that learners interact with as part of a learning activity. Human students serve only as a calibration sample, not as learners in an intervention versus control comparison. No generative-AI learner intervention and no control group are evident, so E1 applies (first applicable code in order). Design is also not an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison with a control group.

quote: A hypothetical scenario was used to test the effectiveness of various prompts, ranging from simple, naïve questions to more sophisticated ones utilising specific prompt patterns
rationale: The abstract describes testing prompt variants of ChatGPT on a hypothetical scenario. There is no control group without generative AI and no comparison against a non-AI condition, so the study is not a controlled comparison. It also reports no quantitative learning outcome; the evaluation is of prompt quality and chatbot recommendations. Positive evidence of failure exists for comparison (E3), so E3 is assigned. The protocol gives E3 before E5 in order.
decision_note: Exclude at abstract stage on E3.

quote: This study examines the responsible integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in English language learning at Mattu University
rationale: Content is English language learning, which is a non-STEM domain explicitly excluded by the protocol (E2). The study is also a mixed-methods perception study with questionnaires and interviews, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it would fail E3 and E5 as well. E2 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: It integrates Generative AI to support rubric application, scoring consistency, and identification of response patterns without replacing instructor judgment
rationale: The abstract describes generative AI (GPT-4 Turbo, DeepSeek, etc.) used by the instructor/researchers to score and apply rubrics to student responses, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. Under the protocol's borderline rule, AI used only by the teacher or researcher is E1. The abstract gives positive evidence of this failure, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified. The crossover design with two learning paths also does not clearly describe a control group without generative AI.

ChatGPT was used by researchers to analyse university course outlines and generate a classification framework; learners do not interact with the generative AI tool as part of a learning activity. This fails E1 (not learner-facing generative AI). The study also has no control group and no learning outcome (E3/E5 would also apply), but E1 is the first applicable code in order.

criteria.outcome_note: unclear data sufficiency for SMD, but not assessable at abstract stage

quote: The study used a quasi-experimental design, and the research involved 58 students from one school in a governate of Makkah region in Saudi Arabia who assigned to the intervention.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study appears to be a quasi-experiment with a control group, using ChatGPT (generative AI) with jigsaw in first-grade intermediate science, with a post-test achievement outcome. Published 2026, so date criterion met. Abstract gives no positive evidence of failure on any criterion; whether SMD can be computed (ANCOVA results) must be checked at full text. Language of full text not visible; not excluded on that basis at abstract stage. Note: the control group's condition (e.g., jigsaw without ChatGPT) is not described in the abstract, so comparison is likely met but should be confirmed.

Title indicates high school mathematics and generative AI with a human-AI collaboration focus, but no abstract is indexed. The title reads as a theoretical construction and practical pathways paper, which suggests it may not be an empirical controlled study. Design, comparison group, and quantitative outcome cannot be assessed from the record. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is retained for full-text review.

quote: "The purpose of this study is to discuss important features involved in designing, teaching, evaluating, and the contextual application of AI tutoring tools."
rationale: The abstract describes a thematic narrative analysis of academic literature (2020–2025) rather than an empirical study. It reports no experimental or comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. The record is a review-type paper, so E6 applies. E6 is ranked before E5 and E3, and the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design. The ESP-for-science framing is also not clearly STEM content, but E6 is the first applicable code.

The abstract is a discussion/position paper on training path design for computer professionals in higher vocational colleges. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It gives positive evidence of a non-empirical paper (it proposes paths and provides reference for training quality rather than reporting data), so E6 applies as the first failing code in order that is supported by the abstract. E1 and E3 could not be established from the abstract, but E6 is the clearest failure.

Abstract describes a mixed-methods study with semi-structured interviews and a cross-sectional survey of 297 university students. It reports associations between chatbot use and academic performance, not a randomized or quasi-experiment with a non-generative-AI control group. The design is correlational/survey, which fails the design and comparison criteria. Domain is not stated in the abstract. Because the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-experimental survey design, this is excluded. The exclusion code is E5, which is the closest fit, since the study's measured outcomes are self-reported usage and perceived associations rather than a controlled learning outcome. Note that the design failure could also support E3 (no control group); the first applicable code by the protocol order is reported as E5 at the abstract stage.

quote: The study collected data from 267 learners who were enrolled in undergraduate and graduate programs at universities in the metropolitan area and validated the relationships among variables using structural equation modeling.
rationale: Survey-based TAM structural equation model of perceived ease of use, usefulness, attitude and continuous use intention. No learning outcome is measured, only perceptions and intention; there is also no control group and the design is correlational. Excluded at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), which applies first among the failing criteria after E1-E4 are considered met or unclear. The STEM domain is not stated in the abstract.

quote: This descriptive-correlational study examines the relationship between Generative AI usage frequency and source verification habits among 142 Grade 12 STEM students
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive-correlational study of usage frequency and verification habits, with no experimental intervention and no control group, so the comparison and design criteria fail. The outcome (self-reported verification habits and usage frequency) is not clearly a learning measure. Per the rule that exclusion requires positive evidence, E3 is applied as the first clear failure; the record would also be unlikely to meet the design requirement.

quote: A targeted narrative synthesis of literature on spatial thinking, integrated STEM and STEAM, cognitive engagement and AI in education informed a conceptual design. A previously published geography–physics lesson provided the instructional context; no new student data were collected.
rationale: The record is a conceptual framework based on a narrative synthesis with no new student data, so it is not an empirical study. It also has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. E6 is the first applicable code in order that fits; the abstract also suggests the content is geography, which is not STEM under the protocol, but E6 comes first in the code sequence for this purpose.
rationale_note: Exclusion code ordering note: Under the protocol order, E1 through E5 are checked before E6. Strictly, E2 (geography not clearly STEM) and E3 (no control group) would be checked first. The abstract gives positive evidence of no control group and no data, so E3 or E5 may also apply. Recorded as E6 as the most direct failure.

quote: A quantitative, observational, non-experimental, cross-sectional study was conducted with 869 students from the University of Granada
rationale: The study is a non-experimental, cross-sectional survey of students' attitudes and self-reported AI use. It has no intervention and no control group, and its outcomes are perceptions and reported use rather than a learning measure. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of an eligible design) at the abstract stage. Note that it is an empirical survey, so E6 is the closest code given the design; the design criterion (survey designs excluded) is clearly not met.
exclusion_code_note: E6 is for non-empirical records; this is empirical. The first applicable code in order is E1 only if the intervention is absent, but the abstract gives no learner-facing intervention. Survey design is excluded by the Design row.

quote: The paper introduces the concepts of thinking and mathematical thinking
rationale: The abstract is a descriptive/conceptual article presenting a teaching process model. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It appears not to be an empirical study, so E6 applies. Comparison and design are not evidenced as met. Note that the protocol's exclusion-code order would put E3 (no control group) before E6 if E3 were established; the abstract gives no positive evidence of a comparison group, but the absence of any empirical design points to E6 as the first applicable code.

Abstract describes GenAI-augmented STEM learning on solar cells with elementary students (intervention, domain, population appear met). However, the design is described as design-based research with no mention of a control group, so comparison and design cannot be confirmed as meeting the protocol. Outcome is described as conceptual understanding, but no quantitative measure is mentioned. Abstract does not give positive evidence of a failed criterion, so it advances to full text for checking of the comparison group, design, and quantitative outcome.

quote: This literature review synthesizes recent research on the connections among Artificial Intelligence (AI), digital well-being, and student success
rationale: The record is a literature review, not an empirical study. It reports no controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome; the focus is on well-being and mental health support. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code in order, though E5 would also plausibly apply.

quote: semi-structured interviews were conducted with twenty-five professors from six countries
rationale: The study is a qualitative thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with marketing professors. It is not an empirical comparative study: there is no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and participants are faculty rather than students. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense; qualitative design excluded under Design). Earlier codes were considered: the abstract does not clearly establish a learner-facing generative AI intervention, and marketing is not clearly STEM, but the design failure is the decisive reason.

criteria.domain_note: Biology is a science subject, so domain is met

quote: The research employed quantitative methods with quasi-experimental and pre-experimental designs, involving Grade X and XI science students as participants.
rationale: Biology is STEM (science), secondary students, pre-test/post-test outcomes, published 2026. ChatGPT is mentioned as one of several digital tools, so a generative AI intervention is plausible. However, the design is described as quasi-experimental and pre-experimental; the pre-experimental component may be single-group pre-post, and the abstract does not show a separate control group without generative AI. Whether a valid comparison group exists cannot be determined from the abstract, so this is unsure and should be resolved at full text.

quote: We report an exploratory controlled study ( N = 27) in which undergraduates completed a 45 min, 16-item Python task under one of three support conditions: Internet (standard web resources), GPT (ChatGPT-3.5), or Custom-GPT
rationale: At abstract stage, all criteria appear met: undergraduate Python programming task (STEM, higher education), ChatGPT-based conditions versus an internet-only control group (non-generative comparison), percentage score as a quantitative outcome, and a journal article published in 2026. Randomisation is not stated in the abstract, but the design is described as a controlled study, so it is not excluded on that basis. Statistics (means, SDs, Cliff's delta) are reported, so the data criterion is plausibly met. Decision is include, to be verified at full text.

quote: Participants completed pre and posttests using the Lunar Phases Concept Inventory (LPCI)
rationale: At abstract stage, the study compares Khanmigo (GenAI tutor) against a Google search group and a paper-only group, with a pre/post concept inventory outcome in undergraduate physics (STEM), published 2025. Nothing in the abstract positively shows a failed criterion. Effect-size data sufficiency, English full text, and journal-article status cannot be verified from the abstract, so the record advances to full-text screening. Note the Google search and paper-only groups serve as non-generative-AI comparators, which fits the protocol.

Study is about English language learning (non-STEM content), which fails the Domain criterion, so E2 applies as the first failing code in order. It is also a qualitative interview study with no control group or quantitative learning outcome (would also fail E3, E5, E6), but E2 is reported first under the ordering rule. Note the abstract stage rule normally limits exclusion to positive evidence; here the abstract clearly describes English language learning, which is positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: The results of Structural Equation Modeling showed that the model explained 54% of the variance in Attitude and 51% of the variance in Behavioral Intention.
rationale: The study is a survey-based SEM of pre-service teachers' technology acceptance (TAM constructs such as attitude and behavioral intention). It has no control group, no learning outcome measure, and no intervention in which learners use generative AI as part of a learning activity. Perceptions and intentions are not learning outcomes. Coded E6 (not an empirical study is not quite the match, so the most defensible code is E6 for a non-experimental survey design; the primary failing is the absence of a quantitative learning outcome and comparison group, which is E3/E5 in order). Applying the code order strictly: E1 (intervention) is unclear at abstract stage, E2 not applicable (teacher education, not STEM content), E3 applies because there is no control group without generative AI. Final code given the ordering: E3.

quote: This structured literature review examines how chatbots and generative AI tools are integrated into engineering education and evaluates their educational impact and associated challenges.
rationale: The record is a structured literature review of 16 included studies, not an empirical study. Review articles are ineligible, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study). Note the protocol's review exclusion falls under publication type, but E6 is the closest code for a review rather than an empirical study; E6 is the applicable code here.

The abstract describes a scenario-based survey measuring students' perceptions of ethicality and rule compliance of GenAI use. No learning outcome (achievement, knowledge, problem solving, skill) is measured, and no learner interaction with a GenAI tool in a learning activity is described. The design is a survey with cross-cultural comparison, not a controlled experiment with a no-GenAI control group. Positive evidence of failure exists for E5 (perceptions only), so the record is excluded at abstract stage on that code. Note that E1 would also be arguable, but E5 is the outcome-level failure that is clearly evidenced; the first-applicable ordering places E1 before E5, and the abstract does not give clear positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing GenAI, so E5 is reported as the code with the clearest support.

quote: This article introduces a novel framework for understanding and implementing responsible AI use by drawing an analogy between the optimal use of LLMs and the role of the second student in an Oxford Tutorial.
rationale: The record is a conceptual/analytical article proposing an analogy-based framework. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Positive evidence of non-empirical design is present in the abstract, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: This study employed a qualitative case study research design, including 11 female postgraduate students enrolled in an educational technology master's program
rationale: The study is a qualitative case study with 11 students interviewed, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E3 is applied as the first failing code in order, since there is no control group without generative AI; E5 and E6 also apply, but the protocol asks for the first in order. Domain is unclear from the abstract (educational technology training design). This is an abstract-stage exclusion on positive evidence of a qualitative design with no comparison group.

quote: two groups: an experimental group, which was treated with the SWOM strategy enhanced by ChatGPT, and a control group, which was taught via regular teacher-led teaching methods
rationale: Abstract describes ChatGPT-enhanced SWOM strategy for eighth-grade science vs. a regular teacher-led control group, with a 30-item multiple-choice achievement test. Eligibility appears to be met on intervention, comparison, population, domain and outcome. Design is not stated (randomization or quasi-experimental status unclear), so the record is passed to full text to check design, whether learners actually interact with ChatGPT, and the statistics needed for an SMD. No positive evidence of an exclusion at abstract stage.

criteria.criteria_note: n/a

quote: A survey research design was adopted, and a questionnaire was used to gain insight into teachers’ opinions.
rationale: Survey of teachers' perspectives on AI tools in EFL primary classrooms. Not an experimental study with a control group, no learner-facing intervention, no learning outcome, and the domain is English language learning rather than STEM. Coded E6 as a non-empirical-experimental (survey) design; the first-applicable code by order is E1 (intervention is teacher-facing, not learner-facing), so E1 is arguably the first applicable code. Given the protocol's ordering, the earliest applicable code is E1.

quote: This paper explores methods for integrating generative AI into embedded software practical teaching, analyzes reform approaches in curriculum design, instructional methods, and evaluation systems, offering references for optimizing teaching model innovation.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/exploratory discussion paper. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is positive evidence that the design is not an empirical comparison, so the record is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Embedded software is treated as computing/STEM content.

quote: The assignment was carried out using a basic randomised controlled approach to ensure that no students from either group had previous information about what to accomplish before being assigned to the groups
rationale: Abstract describes ChatGPT use by students in Python programming learning, a randomised controlled design with an experimental group and implied control group, and Post-Test performance outcomes. Population (student level) and control condition are not explicitly stated but are not positively contradicted, so include at abstract stage per rule 2. Full text should verify control condition, learner population, and SMD data.

quote: This research explores the effects of ChatGPT on English language learning at the undergraduate level in South Punjab
rationale: The study concerns English language learning, which is non-STEM content, so E2 applies and is the first failing criterion in code order. The design is a questionnaire survey with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (perceptions only), so E3, E5 and E6 would also fail, but E2 is reported as the first applicable code.

quote: this study employs “Rain Classroom”, a generative artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted platform, to support education in four dimensions
rationale: Generative AI-assisted platform used by students in a higher education (medical) biochemistry course, so intervention and population appear met. The abstract does not describe a control group or comparison design; it reports 'significantly enhances' outcomes without stating the comparison, so comparison and design are unclear. Biochemistry/molecular biology is arguably life science rather than clearly STEM under the protocol's list, so domain is also unclear. Abstract gives no positive evidence of a failed criterion, so advance to full text to check for a non-AI control group and quantitative SMD-ready outcomes.

quote: A cross-sectional survey of 289 university students was analysed using SPSS 22
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey examining predictors of intention/decision to use ChatGPT. It is not an experimental or quasi-experimental design with a control group, and it reports no quantitative learning outcome (only usage decision factors). Per the protocol's design and outcome criteria and the E6 code for non-empirical/non-qualifying designs, it is excluded. Survey-based designs are explicitly excluded by the Design criterion; E6 is the closest applicable code given the ordering rules, and the failure is also evident at the design level.
rationale_note: Survey design; no control group; no learning outcome.

quote: a quantitative survey (N=64) and qualitative interviews (N=5) gathered data from senior economics students on the effectiveness of preparatory courses
rationale: The study is a survey plus interviews examining students' perceptions of academic skills and AI's effect on them. It has no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group, no generative AI learning intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome (only perceptions and necessity ratings). Under the protocol this is a non-empirical-experimental design, so exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study) is the best fit given the survey/interview design; the design criterion is clearly not met, and the outcome criterion is also not met. Economics is arguably non-STEM, but that was not used as the primary code. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of a survey design without comparison group.

quote: Data was gathered from a stratified sample of 150 undergraduate students in universities over several semesters and skill levels using a quantitative descriptive survey design.
rationale: The study is a quantitative descriptive survey of 150 undergraduates about adoption readiness and perceived reliability of GenAI tools (GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT). It has no control group, is not an experiment or quasi-experiment, and its outcomes are perceptions and attitudes (UTAUT constructs), not a quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E1 would need the intervention to be clearly not learner-facing GenAI, which the abstract does not establish, so E3 is the first clear failure: no comparison group without generative AI. Design (survey) and outcome (perceptions only) also fail. Abstract-stage exclusion is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with no comparison group.

quote: This special issue provides a glimpse into the questions and activities that higher education institutions around the globe are actively pursuing
rationale: This record is an editorial introducing a special issue of New Directions for Teaching and Learning. It describes eight papers but reports no empirical study of learners interacting with a generative AI tool, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion is clear from the abstract, so the record is excluded rather than sent forward. E10 (publication type) could also apply, since editorials are ineligible, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order is ambiguous here; E6 is used as the primary code because the record is a non-empirical special-issue introduction.

criteria.quote_note: ChatGPT used by instructors to design assessments

quote: this paper investigates the use of ChatGPT as a digital assistant to support assessment-related tasks in design and manufacturing engineering education
rationale: ChatGPT is used by instructors to design assessments and rubrics, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. Per protocol, AI used only by the teacher to prepare materials is E1. The study is also a reflective case study with no control group or quantitative learning outcome, which would fail E3 and E5 if reached.

quote: This qualitative case study investigates how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools can support STEM education in a Thai secondary school setting.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative case study using thematic analysis of observations, surveys, interviews, and logs. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the design is qualitative, which the protocol excludes. Per the protocol's exclusion-code order, the first failing criterion is E6 (not an empirical study is a misfit label here, but the closest code for a non-experimental qualitative design). Note: the design fails the comparison (no control group, E3) and the outcome (E5) criteria as well; E3 would precede E5 and E6 in the order of listing only if applied before E6. Given the protocol lists E3 before E6, the strictly ordered first applicable code is E3, so this decision should be checked by the auditor. Qualitative design with no comparison group is positive evidence of failure at abstract stage.

quote: the researcher conducted a systematic literature review to investigate the pioneering potential of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) tools
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review (thematic analysis of 20 articles), not an empirical experimental study. It has no control group comparison or randomized/quasi-experimental design, so it fails the design and comparison criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies as the first failing criterion in code order.

quote: Postgraduate education in landscape architecture has long been confronted with issues such as the disconnection between design thinking cultivation and the application of cutting-edge technologies.
rationale: Landscape architecture design education is not a STEM domain under the protocol's list (science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, data science). The abstract also gives no indication of a control group or a quantitative learning outcome; it describes a teaching model with reported improvements only, so other criteria are unclear. The abstract gives no separate control group without generative AI, so E3 applies. Students and LMs were graded on uniform criteria, which is a performance comparison rather than a learning comparison. Also, the abstract describes LMs completing tasks rather than learners interacting with a GenAI tool as part of a learning activity. Exclusion on E3 is based on the absence of a non-GenAI comparison group.

quote: This study explores how undergraduate students co-created and evaluated custom Generative AI (GenAI) tools within a students-as-partners (SaP) framework.
rationale: The study is an autoethnographic, qualitative analysis of student reflections and logs. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical comparative study meeting the design requirements. The code E6 (not an empirical study) is the closest fit for a qualitative autoethnography; the abstract also gives positive evidence of no comparison group and no quantitative outcome. Because the first applicable code in order is E1 and the intervention (students co-creating custom GPTs) is learner-facing GenAI, E1 does not apply. E3 (no control group) would also apply; E6 is chosen as the most accurate characterization of the design being non-empirical in the comparative/quantitative sense. Decision is an exclusion regardless of code.

quote: The study examines the implementation of GenAI guidelines in a Master of Cyber Security program from 2023 to 2024.
rationale: The abstract describes a policy/guideline implementation and discussion paper on GenAI use in assessments. It reports no comparison group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. The paper appears to be a descriptive, non-empirical account of policy and transparency, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study). Earlier codes were considered: the intervention (guidelines rather than learner-facing GenAI use) is also doubtful under E1, but E6 is the clearest failure, and the abstract does not give enough to confirm E1. Domain is cyber security, which is arguably STEM-adjacent but not decisive here.

quote: This study qualitatively examined high school students’ meaning-making processes in a generative AI-based music and video creation program
rationale: The study is a single case study using reflexive thematic analysis of reflection sheets, prompt logs, and outputs. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Under the rule that exclusions use one code, E6 (not an empirical study) is applied as the best fit for a qualitative case design. Strictly, E3 (no control group) also applies; E6 was chosen because the design is qualitative and non-empirical in the protocol's sense. Domain is also unclear (music and video creation is not clearly STEM). Decision is exclude at the abstract stage because positive evidence of a qualitative design is present.

quote: The findings show that while students view ChatGPT as beneficial for academic writing and beyond, they also express concerns about its potential risks and uncertainties, stemming from mistrust of the technology.
rationale: Survey-based mixed-methods study of student perceptions, experiences and concerns about ChatGPT in academic writing. No control group and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions only. Design is a survey, not an experiment or quasi-experiment. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome), which is the first applicable code in the order given; the abstract also indicates a survey design, which would fail the comparison and design criteria as well.

quote: This systematic review analyzes research on the application of Large Language Models (LLMs) to enhance the quality of learner support
rationale: The record is a systematic review of prior literature, not an empirical study with a control group, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Reviews are also ineligible publication types under the protocol. The abstract gives positive evidence that the design is a review, so E6 applies as the first code that fits; no experimental comparison or learning outcome data are reported.

quote: This study aimed to explore students’ perceptions and ethical use of ChatGPT in completing English assignments.
rationale: Content is English language learning, which is non-STEM, so E2 applies and is the first failing code in order. The study is also a descriptive mixed-method survey with no control group and reports only perceptions, so it would fail E3, E5 and E6 as well, but E2 is reported as the first applicable code.

quote: We collected 383 programming artifacts from 194 primary school students (2022--2024) and employed two automated approaches
rationale: The abstract describes automated scoring of student programming artifacts (LLM-based and ECD-based assessment) rather than a learning intervention with a generative AI tool used by learners versus a control group. No control group or comparison design is described; the study appears to be a measurement/validation study of automated creativity scoring. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Note that the abstract alone shows no experimental comparison, so this is a reasonably confident exclusion, though the full text could be checked if a researcher wishes.

quote: Post-activity data were analyzed using PLS-SEM.
rationale: The study is a survey-based TAM structural model of preservice teachers' behavioral intentions and perceptions after a Khanmigo activity. It reports no quantitative learning outcome, and no control group is described. Perceptions and intentions do not count as learning outcomes under the protocol. Exclusion code E5 applies. Note that E3 (no control group) and E6 (not empirical/survey design) are also plausibly relevant, but E5 is the first applicable code in the order given for the abstract evidence.
rationale_note: Correction: E5 is the first code in protocol order that applies, since E1 (intervention is learner-facing; Khanmigo activity with PTs is learner-facing) and E2 (domain not clearly STEM) and E3 and E4 are not positively evidenced as failing at abstract stage.
quote_text: Post-activity data were analyzed using PLS-SEM.
rationale_final: Survey-based TAM study of perceptions and behavioral intention; no quantitative learning outcome.

criteria.intervention_note: generative AI platform used by learners

quote: Preliminary evaluations indicate significant improvements in student engagement and knowledge retention, demonstrating the platform's potential to transform personalized education.
rationale: The abstract describes a generative AI learning platform (Llama, CodeLlama, Mistral) used by learners, which meets the intervention criterion. However, it reports only "preliminary evaluations" with no description of a control group or comparison condition, so there is positive evidence of no comparison group (E3). The abstract also does not describe a randomized or quasi-experimental design, and the outcome is described only vaguely (engagement and retention), with no statistics. Exclusion is based on the absence of any described control group; the abstract gives no indication of a comparison arm.
decision_note: Abstract-stage exclusion is borderline; a researcher may prefer "unsure" under the rule that missing information is not evidence.

rationale: The abstract describes a math intelligent tutoring system with diagrammatic scaffolding and a correlational-style analysis of spontaneous diagram use versus perceived usefulness. It gives no indication of a generative AI component, and nothing indicates a comparison group or an experimental design. Positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI is absent, so this is ambiguous at abstract stage. Under rule 2 the record should not be excluded on missing information. Setting decision to unsure so it can be checked at full text.

quote: Findings indicated that the short-term game intervention did not yield a statistically significant change in academic attitude and motivation.
rationale: Abstract describes an AI-supported RPG for teaching C++ using RAG and LLMs (generative AI, programming domain, learner-facing), so intervention and domain appear met. Design-Based Research with five iterative cycles and 70 participants; abstract does not state whether a separate control group exists, so comparison and design are unclear. The reported quantitative outcome is attitude and motivation, which the protocol excludes as affective; it is unclear whether any learning-performance outcome was measured. Population (students vs. other) is not stated. Insufficient information at abstract stage, so advance to full text.

quote: surveying 82 physics teachers to assess their awareness, attitudes, and current application of AI in teaching
rationale: The study is a survey of 82 physics teachers on perceptions and application of AI. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome measured. Per the protocol's exclusion order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is the first applicable code, but the primary reason is that this is a survey study, not an empirical trial. Teachers are in-service, so population also fails. Coding E6 (not an empirical study) would be debatable since it is an empirical survey; the strongest abstract-level evidence is that the intervention is teacher-facing only, which the protocol assigns E1. Given the rule to report the first applicable code in order, E1 is the more accurate code.
note: Correction: final exclusion code should be E1 per protocol order.

rationale: The record has only a title and venue, with no abstract. The title describes development and validation of a competence scale (a psychometric instrument), which suggests a survey-type study with no learning outcome measured after an intervention. Abstract-stage rule: exclusion needs positive evidence. The title itself gives that evidence, since a scale validation does not measure a learning outcome after an intervention. Excluding under E5 with low confidence; a full-text check could overturn this if the study has a controlled learning outcome.

quote: To rigorously examine the practical effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed model, a detailed teaching case was systematically designed, deployed, and evaluated in a real-world educational setting.
rationale: Abstract describes an AIGC-enabled PBL model for primary mathematics (generative AI, STEM, K-12 students), and reports significant improvement in problem-solving performance. However, the abstract does not state whether a separate control group without generative AI exists, nor the study design (it mentions a single teaching case and both quantitative and qualitative analyses). No positive evidence of a failed criterion, so the record advances to full text to check the comparison group and design.

quote: A quantitative approach with a pre-experimental one-group pre-test and post-test design was employed.
rationale: Content is English language writing (recount text), not STEM, so E2 applies first in code order. The design is also a single-group pre-post design with no control group (E3 would also apply), but E2 is the first applicable code under the stated order. Intervention (ChatGPT) and population (junior high students) appear to fit.

quote: Health professions education. Language learning and other non-STEM content.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of clinical laboratory science learners plus a pilot module, with no control group, and the abstract describes perceptions rather than a quantitative learning outcome. Clinical laboratory science falls under health professions education, which the protocol excludes from the STEM domain. Coded E4 as the first applicable code in the order given, since the population is health professions learners rather than K-12 or higher education STEM students. The quote is from the protocol's domain exclusion text, not the record; no abstract passage directly supports the exclusion. The record also reports only a survey design, so E3 and E5 would also apply, but E4 is the first in the order.

quote: This article reports a one‐group time‐series study of Microsoft Copilot Voice (MCV) as a structural scaffold
rationale: The study is a single-group time-series design with no control group that lacks generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails (E3). Also, the content is English speaking practice, which is non-STEM, but E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol order under the E1-E3 sequence, so E3 is reported. Intervention (Copilot Voice, generative) and population (university students) appear met at abstract level.

quote: Using a quantitative methodology, self-administered online surveys comprising 36–37 items targeting core constructs were distributed to both groups.
rationale: The study is a survey of perceptions and attitudes (TAM-type constructs such as PU, PEOU, BI) with correlational analysis. It has no separate control group and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions only, which the protocol excludes. Abstract gives positive evidence of a failed criterion (E5 outcome, and design is survey/correlational, not an experiment), so exclusion at abstract stage is justified. Primary code chosen is E5 as the first applicable code in protocol order after E1–E4 are not clearly failed.
rationale_note: Note: The design criterion (survey/correlational) also fails; E3 (no comparison group) would also apply, but E5 is the outcome-based failure. Per protocol order, E1 to E4 are not positively failed in the abstract (the intervention and population are not clearly described), so E5 is the first code with positive evidence.

quote: This study was conducted as a researcher-led inquiry rather than a classroom-based experiment with a formal sample size.
rationale: The abstract describes a researcher-led inquiry with no separate control group lacking generative AI, and no comparison design is reported. The study is not an experiment with a comparison group, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. Exclusion code E3 applies (no control group without generative AI). Outcome is also not clearly quantitative, but E3 is the first applicable code in order.

Abstract describes ten preservice mathematics teachers engaging with customized ChatGPT-based chatbots, with data from written assignments, reflections, and pre/post surveys. No control or comparison group is mentioned, which suggests a single-group design. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group supports exclusion at E3. Intervention, population, and domain appear met. The design is not described as a randomized or quasi-experiment with a comparison group.

quote: The study assessed Saudi students’ opinions, obstacles and difficulties, and the educational prospects and opportunities of ChatGPT usage in EFL classrooms.
rationale: Survey-based descriptive study of student opinions on ChatGPT in EFL classes. No control group, no learning outcome measured, and the content is language learning rather than STEM. The design is a survey, so it is not an empirical experiment. Abstract gives positive evidence of several failed criteria. E6 is the first applicable code in the order that fits the design (survey, non-experimental). Note that E2 (non-STEM content) would also apply; I chose E6 as the design-based reason, though the protocol order would put E2 before E6 if applied strictly.

quote: To learn how students in an accredited PharmD program in the United States are using ChatGPT for personal, academic, and clinical reasons
rationale: The record is a descriptive survey of pharmacy students' ChatGPT use. It is not an experiment with a control group, has no learning outcome measure, and is not STEM content (pharmacy is a health professions field). Its design is a survey, which is non-empirical for this protocol's purposes; the first applicable code in order is E1? No: the intervention is learner-used generative AI, but the study has no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Following code order, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first clearly failing criterion and applies because the design has no comparison group at all. The exclusion code is set to E3 for that reason. Note that E6 (non-empirical) could also be argued; the survey is empirical but not an eligible design.

quote: I redesigned one assessment brief to integrate the use of AI into the learning process.
rationale: The abstract describes a reflective teaching-practice account of redesigning one assessment brief to include generative AI for a Master's logistics module. It reports no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome; it appears to be a non-empirical practice report. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in order that the abstract clearly supports. Logistics is not clearly within the listed STEM domains, but that is not needed to decide. Abstract-stage rule: the absence of a control group is positive evidence of a failed comparison criterion, and the description lacks any measured outcome.

quote: This paper develops a Code-Agency-centered evidence framework for AIGC-supported programming education.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual framework paper ("This paper develops a ... framework") with a single illustrative LiteOS task-management case used as a diagnostic setting. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study. Exclusion code E6 applies.

quote: A survey is created and distributed to all the participating students.
rationale: At abstract stage, the evaluation appears to rely on a survey of participants, with no described control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The workshop is a single practical experiment with students using LLMs to build projects, and the abstract gives positive evidence of no quantitative learning measure (only survey-based effectiveness conclusions). Exclusion under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Design also appears to be a single-group workshop without a comparison group, which would be E3 if confirmed; E5 is reported as the first applicable based on the abstract's described evaluation. Content is also not clearly STEM (fiction, images, HTML/JS/CSS).

Abstract is missing from the index; only the title is available. The title suggests a generative AI study with management students, which is not STEM content and may be a survey-based perception study (title refers to perceived value and motivation). Positive evidence of a failed criterion is not available at the abstract stage, but the title does not show a controlled experiment with a learning outcome. Domain (management is not clearly STEM) and design are unclear, so the record is held for full-text review rather than excluded on incomplete information.

quote: We present a study in which a version of a common conservation of mechanical energy introductory physics problem, an object released on an inclined plane, is given to OpenAI's GPT-4 large language model (LLM).
rationale: The study evaluates GPT-4 responses to a physics problem variant set; the abstract describes prompting the LLM itself with no learner-facing activity and no separate control group of learners without generative AI. Comparison to human experts/novices is descriptive, not a control group receiving a non-AI condition. Positive evidence of missing comparison group supports E3 rather than leaving it open. Population (students) is not met as participants are the model, so E4 could also be argued, but the first applicable code in order is E1 if the intervention is judged not learner-facing. Under the protocol order, E1 applies first: the LLM is not used by learners as part of a learning activity, so E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: The quantitative phase involved a limited trial of 30 students of class X and 3 science teachers
rationale: Abstract describes a single-group trial with pre/post style N-gain analysis and descriptive statistics only; no separate control group without generative AI is reported. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group, so exclude under E3 (one group measured before and after). Intervention generative AI status is also not fully clear, but E3 applies.

The title states the population is medical students. Medical students are higher education learners, so the population criterion is not clearly failed by the protocol's definition, and E4 is not supported. The record has no abstract, and the title suggests an opportunities-and-challenges paper, which points toward a non-empirical design (E6) or a lack of a control group. Without positive evidence from the abstract that a criterion fails, the record should be advanced to full text rather than excluded. Decision should be unsure.

quote: ChatGPT 4 had the highest overall correct answer rate of 0.85, followed by Claude 3 Opus at 0.67, and Gemini Advanced at 0.42.
rationale: The study evaluates the performance of three generative AI models on textbook math problems. There is no control group without generative AI and no learner-facing intervention; the models are compared only against each other and against correct answers. This is a model benchmarking study, so it fails the comparison and design criteria (E3). The abstract gives positive evidence that no separate non-generative-AI comparison group exists.

criteria.stage_note: abstract shows no control group; study analyses 208 student-tutor interactions with mixed methods

quote: analysed 208 student–tutoring tool interactions using a mixed-methods approach that combined research team evaluation with learner feedback
rationale: The abstract describes an analysis of student prompts and interactions with a generative AI tutor, with ratings from research team and learners. There is no separate control group without generative AI, and no learning outcome is reported. This is positive evidence of a missing comparison group, so exclude under E3 at the abstract stage.

quote: The research implemented a quantitative approach with a survey method involving 40 respondents.
rationale: The study is a survey with a regression of usage intensity on self-reported independent learning. There is no control group receiving a non-generative-AI comparison, and the design is correlational/survey, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in order that fits the lack of a comparison group; the outcome is also a perception-type questionnaire measure rather than a performance measure. Positive evidence of failure is present in the abstract.

quote: Employing an ADDIE-based Research and Development approach, the system was implemented for 109 students.
rationale: Programming course with students (population and domain appear met). The abstract describes an LLM-based grading and assessment system, but it is unclear whether learners interact with the generative AI (the LLM appears to grade, with instructor review) and whether there is any control group without generative AI. The main reported results are grading agreement metrics (MAE, correlation, ICC) between instructors and the LLM, which are not learning outcomes. The abstract gives no clear positive evidence of a failed criterion, so it is advanced to full text for checking intervention, comparison, and outcome.

criteria.stage_note: Case study with qualitative thematic analysis

quote: This study investigates the potential of ChatGPT to support the learning agency of adolescents with disability in a secondary science classroom in Australia.
rationale: Abstract describes a case study with thematic (qualitative) analysis of interviews, conversations, worksheets and video. No control group and no quantitative learning outcome are reported. Per the protocol, case study and qualitative designs are excluded; the first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI). Abstract gives positive evidence of a failed comparison and design, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

criteria.quote_note: n/a

quote: This article presents a Great Ideas for Teaching (GIFT) activity in which students design and evaluate a custom generative AI (GenAI) tool grounded in organizational communication theory.
rationale: The activity is a teaching idea in organizational communication, which is not STEM content. The abstract describes no control group, no comparative design, and no quantitative learning outcome; it reads as a pedagogical description. Exclusion under E2 (first applicable code in order is E1 check: students do interact with GenAI, so E1 does not apply; E2 is the first clear failure).

quote: Artificial Intelligence Applications in K-12 offers authentic instances of how AI systems can be integrated into K-12 education today.
rationale: The record is a edited book (ODU Digital Commons book/collection of case studies), not a journal article, so publication type is not eligible under the protocol. The abstract also describes case studies and a book overview rather than an empirical comparative study with a control group and quantitative learning outcome, so design and outcome criteria are not met as described. Exclusion code E10 is applied as the first applicable code in the stated order is E1 (intervention) which is unclear rather than positively failing; publication type is the clearest positive failure.

quote: Findings indicate that structured exposure to GenAI tools enhanced participants’ confidence and competence in integrating technology into lesson design.
rationale: Exploratory study of nine preservice/early-career teachers' perceptions and patterns of GenAI use in lesson planning. The abstract describes no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions, confidence, and TPACK shifts, which are not learning measures. Single-group exploratory design with no comparison condition. Positive evidence of failure on comparison, design, and outcome criteria, so excluded at abstract stage. E5 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported (E3 could also apply since no control group is described; E3 precedes E5 in the code order, so E3 is the more accurate first code).

quote: This descriptive study was conducted by directly testing the answers generated by ChatGPT-4o.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive study that tests ChatGPT-4o's answer accuracy on biology test questions. There is no learner interaction, no control group without generative AI, and no learning outcome in learners. The design is descriptive, not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Exclusion at E3 because no control group without generative AI exists. The E1 issue (learner-facing use) is also doubtful, but E3 is the clearer failure under the stated order, as the study lacks a comparison arm.

quote: The study was conducted among 87 final-year medical students at the Faculty of Medicine, University of Kelaniya, Sri Lanka.
rationale: Population is medical undergraduates, and the protocol excludes health professions education. The protocol's domain criterion excludes health professions education, and the abstract describes medical education. Under the protocol, this is a health-professions domain issue. The protocol's exclusion codes list E2 for non-STEM content, and this study's content is medical knowledge, not STEM. Applying the first-applicable code in order, E2 (content is not STEM) is the correct code because the health professions exclusion falls under the Domain row, which E2 covers. Design is quasi-experimental with a comparison group of self-directed ChatGPT use, so it is not the pre-post single-group design. The comparison is met. Outcome is a knowledge test score. Intervention is ChatGPT-based learner-facing. The population is medical students, which is higher education, so E4 does not apply. Final code: E2.

Single-course study with a post-course survey only; no control group without generative AI is described, so E3 applies. Outcomes appear to be self-reported skill perceptions and satisfaction rather than a quantitative learning measure. Domain (flipped graduate course, content unspecified) is not clearly STEM. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of no comparison group.
rationale_note: Exclusion code E3 chosen as first applicable per protocol order is E3 before E5; the abstract gives no control group.

quote: The study uses a grounded theory approach wherein the qualitative findings are considered to understand the student motivation
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative grounded theory study of 48 management students' motivation via semi-structured interviews. It is not an experiment with a control group and reports no quantitative learning outcome. Design is qualitative, so it is not an empirical comparative study meeting the protocol; coded E6 as not an empirical (quantitative) study. Domain is management, not STEM. Exclusion is clear from the abstract on design and outcome grounds.

quote: We analyzed data from 420 university students in IBM SPSS Statistics using reliability analysis, descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, regression analysis, and Hayes' PROCESS Model 4
rationale: Cross-sectional correlational survey of GenAI dependency; no experimental or comparison group without generative AI, and no learning outcome (outcomes are mental health and stress). Design is correlational, which fails the design and comparison criteria. Excluded under E3 as no control group; the design also fails, and the outcome is not a learning measure, but E3 is the first applicable code in order from the protocol list considered for this stage.
rationale_note: Note: strictly, the first applicable code in order E1-E10 should be checked. E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is unclear because the survey measures dependency rather than an intervention. E2 and E4 do not apply. E3 applies because there is no control group. E5 would also apply, but E3 comes first.

quote: This case study explores how upper-secondary students used ChatGPT in a Finnish algebra course and their attitudes toward its integration.
rationale: The abstract describes a case study analysing ChatGPT interactions and questionnaire responses, with no control group or comparison condition, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. The outcomes are usage patterns, prompt quality, and attitudes, not a quantitative learning outcome. Coded E3 as the first applicable code in protocol order for a design without a non-generative-AI comparison group; the record would also fail E5 on outcomes. Excluding at abstract stage is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence of a case study design with no control group.

The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey (Likert questionnaire, multiple linear regression) with no control group and no experimental manipulation. The design is correlational/survey, so the study fails the comparison and design criteria. Its outcome is self-reported critical thinking via questionnaire, and the study does not describe a learner-facing intervention or a STEM domain. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI); E1 could also be argued, but the design failure is the clearest positive evidence.

quote: Through surveys and case analysis, the study finds that LLMs are primarily applied
rationale: The abstract describes a survey and case analysis of meteorology graduate students' LLM use, with no control group, no experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of missing comparison and design (survey, not randomized or quasi-experimental) supports exclusion. Coded E3 as the first applicable code in order would be E3 (no control group without generative AI); the design is survey-based, so E6 could also be argued, but the abstract's clearest failing criterion is the absence of a comparison group.

quote: We compared students' results from these two years with the results from 2021/2022, when GenAI was not part of the task
rationale: Higher education mathematics course; students use GenAI chatbots in a problem-solving essay task, so intervention, domain and population appear met. The comparison is cohort-based (2021/2022 without GenAI vs. later years with GenAI), which is a historical comparison rather than a clearly separate concurrent control group, and it is unclear whether it qualifies as a quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Learning outcome (essay results) appears quantitative, and effect-size data are not visible in the abstract. Design and comparison cannot be resolved from the abstract alone, so the record is held for full-text review rather than excluded.

quote: The results demonstrate the capability of modern large language models to generate simple text-based multiple-choice questions suitable for use.
rationale: The generative AI tool is used by teachers to create test items (teacher-side material preparation), not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. No control group, comparison, or learning outcome is described; the abstract reports only the capability of the generator. Excluded under E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI). Exclusion at abstract stage is supported by positive evidence that the AI is teacher-facing only.

quote: This study employed a quasi-experimental design using a one-group pretest–posttest approach.
rationale: The abstract gives positive evidence of a single-group pre-post design with no separate control group without generative AI, which fails the comparison and design criteria (E3 per the protocol's single-group pre-post rule). Additionally, participants are teachers in a socialization program (in-service teachers, not students), and outcomes are teacher questionnaire ratings of understanding and perceived ability rather than a learning outcome. E3 is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's code list where the comparison failure is the cited reason; population and outcome failures also apply but are secondary in ordering only if E3 is taken as first; per protocol order E3 precedes E4 and E5, so E3 is reported.

quote: We developed GenAI prompts for scoring and feedback aligned with established epistemic frameworks, categorizing responses as naive, mixed, or informed.
rationale: At the abstract stage, GenAI is used to score student questionnaire responses and generate feedback, with no indication that learners interact with GenAI as part of a learning activity. The GenAI is applied for assessment and feedback design, not learner-facing use. No control group without GenAI is described, and the design appears to be a psychometric/scoring agreement study rather than a comparative experiment. Exclusion code E1 applies first because the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

criteria.stage_note: Abstract describes an LLM chatbot for prospective students, but it is an admissions information service, not a STEM learning activity.

quote: Evaluation was conducted using 20 admission-related queries derived from real-world student information needs.
rationale: The study evaluates an LLM-based admissions chatbot by accuracy and relevance of responses on 20 queries, assessed qualitatively by the researcher and two evaluators. There is no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome. The content is university admissions information, not STEM. Positive evidence fails on the outcome (no learning measure), design (no comparison), and domain (non-STEM) criteria. The first applicable code in order is E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), though E2 and E3 also apply. Exclusion on E5 as the first code in protocol order is not appropriate if E1 is not triggered; intervention is a generative chatbot used by learners, so E1 does not apply. Ordered check: E1 no, E2 yes (non-STEM content) would be first. Recorded code is E2 to follow the protocol order.

quote: Incorporating ChatGPT into designing worksheets for physics experiments has the potential to transform how teachers teach science in primary schools.
rationale: ChatGPT is used by teachers to create worksheets (teacher-only material preparation), not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. Per protocol and borderline rules, AI used only by the teacher to prepare materials is E1. No control group, outcome, or learner sample is described in the abstract either. Exclusion on E1 is supported by the abstract's framing.

Abstract describes a survey of 148 engineering students on their perceived impacts of generative AI use. There is no control group, no experimental comparison, and the outcomes are self-perceptions rather than a quantitative learning measure. Design is survey-based, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. The exclusion code is E3 (no control group without generative AI), which is the first applicable code in protocol order when the screen is applied to this record; the outcome failure (E5) and design failure (E6, non-empirical or survey) are also evident. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence of a survey design with no comparison group.

quote: "involving 464 Peruvian students from different academic disciplines"
