Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is kept for full-text review rather than excluded. Publication year 2026 meets the date criterion.

quote: The study employed a quantitative approach using a quasi-experimental design with a Nonequivalent Control Group Design.
rationale: At abstract stage, the record describes ChatGPT integration (generative AI, learner-facing implied by 'integration' into learning) versus a control group in a quasi-experimental nonequivalent control group design, with twelfth-grade students in genetics (STEM, biology), a Toulmin-based argumentation test (quantitative outcome), published 2026. Effect size (Cohen's d = 0.96) is reported, so data appear sufficient. Venue is a journal (Science and Education Journal), though the abstract alone does not fully confirm publication type. No positive evidence of any failed criterion; include for full-text check.

quote: Statistical analysis using MANOVA and ANOVA confirmed that these differences across the student, NLP, and LLM groups were statistically significant (p < 0.001).
rationale: Abstract compares a fine-tuned LLM (generative) with a rule-based NLP pipeline and mentions student, NLP and LLM groups, so a non-generative comparison group may exist. However, it is unclear whether students interact with the LLM as learners (the LLM may generate diagrams for groups rather than learner-facing use), whether the population is higher-education students, and whether the outcomes are quantitative learning measures (fidelity and correction effort are tool-output metrics, not learning). UML modeling is software engineering, which plausibly falls within the computer science domain. Insufficient evidence to exclude at abstract stage; advance to full text to check learner interaction, population, and outcomes.

quote: Developing Prompt Engineering as a 21st-Century Skill: The Impact of Structured ChatGPT Instruction in EFL Education
rationale: The study concerns EFL (English as a foreign language) learning, which is non-STEM content, so E2 applies. The abstract also describes a three-phase within-group intervention with no clear control group, and perceptions are among the outcomes, which would support further exclusions, but the first applicable code in order is E2. Language learning is explicitly excluded by the protocol's domain criterion.

quote: A 15-week curriculum applying the model was implemented for 41 juniors and seniors(17 teams) enrolled in a Spatial Design studio course at a four-year university in Korea.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group implementation with learner surveys and expert evaluations, with no control group that avoids generative AI. Outcomes are self-reported awareness and expert ratings, not a clear quantitative learning measure. Spatial design is also not clearly within the protocol's STEM domain. The positive evidence of no comparison group (E3) is sufficient for exclusion.

quote: In this article, our panel of experts delve into the various ways ChatGPT can be applied in clinical chemistry and medicine.
rationale: The record is an expert panel discussion/commentary in Clinical Chemistry, not an empirical study. It has no control group, no learner population, no STEM learning domain, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order that fits best; it also fails the other criteria.

The record has no abstract and only a title and venue (AI & Society, 2026). The title ("the problem of evidence of understanding in education in the age of generative AI") suggests a conceptual or philosophical essay, which would likely fail the empirical-study requirement (E6). However, this is inferred from the title alone, and missing information is not evidence of exclusion at the abstract stage. Retain for full-text review to check whether any experimental comparison with a control group and quantitative learning outcome exists.

quote: This paper showcases work in progress currently being carried out to explore ways generative artificial intelligence (gen AI) can support post-secondary instructors.
rationale: The record is a work-in-progress participatory action research design with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Gen AI is used by the instructor to redesign course materials, not learner-facing, and the domain is education/UDL rather than STEM. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study yet, work in progress) is the best fit; the design also lacks a control group and quantitative outcome, so it would fail E3 and E5 as well, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order from the perspective of the work being an in-progress study. Note: the strict order would place E1 first since the AI is used by the instructor, not learners; applying the order strictly, E1 applies first.

quote: Our evaluation involving 113 students showed that the course design might help students to understand GenAI characteristics and change their behaviour.
rationale: Abstract describes a GenAI-integrated data science course for non-computing students (higher education, STEM domain). It does not state whether there is a control group without GenAI, and the reported outcomes (understanding of GenAI characteristics, behaviour, misuse, course objectives) do not clearly indicate a quantitative learning measure or effect-size data. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so advance to full text to check comparison design, outcome measures, and statistics.

quote: The quantitative research method was adopted with the help of the structured survey that was conducted in 300 students
rationale: The study is a structured Likert survey of 300 students about perceptions of AI tools, with no control group and no learning outcome measured as a quantitative performance measure (academic success is self-reported perception). Design is survey, not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Abstract gives positive evidence that the comparison and design criteria fail, so excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Note the design failure could also be read as E6 (not an empirical experimental study); E3 is applied as the first failing comparison criterion.

quote: This cross-sectional study assessed awareness, attitudes, and utilization of LLMs among healthcare students across Saudi Arabian universities using a self-administered online questionnaire
rationale: The design is a cross-sectional survey with no control group and no learning outcome; it measures only awareness, attitudes and use. Positive evidence fails the comparison and design criteria. Under the code order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly the first failure, so the first applicable code is E3, since no comparison group without generative AI exists. Domain is also health professions rather than STEM, which would be a further failure. Given the abstract, exclusion is supported.

The study concerns English language learning, which is non-STEM content, so E2 applies as the first failing code in order. It is also a descriptive questionnaire study with perception-based measures and no control group (E3/E5/E6 would also apply), but E2 is reported as the first applicable code.

Exploratory mixed-methods comparison of student think-aloud responses and ChatGPT-generated solutions to physics problems. There is no control group that does not use generative AI, and no quantitative learning outcome or intervention comparison is described; the study compares responses qualitatively through sensemaking and mechanistic reasoning lenses. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI) as the first applicable code; the design also appears non-experimental. The abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group.

quote: A qualitative document analysis was used to analyse 30 preservice teachers' written assignments
rationale: The study is a qualitative document analysis with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Design is qualitative, so it fails the comparison and design criteria; it is excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI) as the first applicable code, with the absence of quantitative outcomes (E5) also present. Abstract-stage evidence is clear that the design is qualitative and has no comparison group.

quote: These tools align with Generation Z learning preferences and can be integrated into existing curricula to transform text heavy content into multimodal engaging content.
rationale: The abstract is a narrative/commentary piece on generative AI for multimodal content in health professions education. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Health professions education is also outside the STEM domain. Coded E6 as not an empirical study, which is the first applicable code in order that is supported by the text; the domain issue (E2) is also present but E6 is the primary basis. Note that under the strict ordering E1 does not apply since the intervention is learner-facing generative AI.

quote: Findings show that students generally view ChatGPT positively for increasing engagement, stimulating creativity, and supporting personalised learning
rationale: The abstract describes a survey plus focus groups on student perceptions. There is no control group, no experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome; the outcomes are perceptions. The design is survey/qualitative, which the protocol excludes. E3 is the first applicable code in the stated order, since there is no comparison group without generative AI. Domain is also unclear as the discipline is not specified. Excluding at abstract stage is justified because positive evidence of failed comparison and outcome criteria is present.

quote: "A cross-sectional, questionnaire-based study was conducted (January-March 2026) among 324 MBBS students"
rationale: Cross-sectional questionnaire survey of perceptions and awareness with no learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Also health professions (MBBS) education, which the protocol excludes from STEM domain. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study eligible under the design criteria) is the first applicable code in the order given in the protocol is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), but the abstract gives no evidence that students used a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; it describes usage patterns and perceptions. Strictly, the first applicable code is E1 since the intervention is not a learner-facing AI learning activity. Final code: E1.

quote: A quantitative design was employed using a structured questionnaire completed by 506 students from several higher education institutions in the UAE.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional questionnaire of 506 students on ChatGPT usage differences by demographics. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI, so the comparison and design criteria are not met. The outcome is self-reported usage and perceptions rather than a quantitative learning measure. The abstract also gives no evidence of a STEM focus (fields are non-technical vs. other). Exclusion is based on E3 as the first clear failure per the protocol's ordering, and the study has no comparison group; it is a survey design, which would also fail E6-type criteria, but the first applicable code in order is E3.

quote: We introduce and demonstrate a methodology for setting up a designed sequence of prompts and apply text analytic methods, such as latent semantic analysis to analyze responses.
rationale: The abstract describes a methodology for designing prompts to query an LLM and analyze responses with text analytics. It involves no learners, no learning activity, and no control group; the 'learning' refers to researchers learning about LLM outputs. Not an empirical study of learners with a quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E5 is applied as the first clearly failing criterion, with E1 or E4 also plausible; the design lacks a comparison group entirely (E3 would also apply). Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that no learner-facing intervention or learning outcome is present.

quote: A questionnaire was administered to university students, considering dimensions of usability, satisfaction and usefulness, and accessibility and interaction, to understand the perception of the system and improvements.
rationale: At the abstract stage, the evaluation relies on student perception questionnaires (usability, satisfaction, usefulness) and a simulated case study of system behavior. No quantitative learning outcome is reported, and no control group using or not using generative AI is described. The paper is a system architecture with perception and system-efficiency evaluation, so E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). Domain is also unclear (not STEM content specified). Excluded on the outcome criterion, with the design also appearing not to be a comparison experiment.

quote: This review examines the potential benefits of AI in biological education
rationale: The record is a review article (title: "a review of the use of AI tools"; abstract: "This review examines..."), not an empirical study. Under the protocol, reviews are ineligible and fall under E6 (not an empirical study). It also lacks any comparison-group experiment described in the abstract. Biology is also not clearly within the STEM domain list, but the E6 exclusion is decisive.

quote: A multimethod analysis combining structural equation modeling (SEM) and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) was conducted.
rationale: Abstract stage. Higher education students and 2026 publication fit. The abstract describes an SEM/fsQCA association study of GAI-supported teaching, which does not clearly show a controlled comparison group with a non-generative-AI condition, a randomized or quasi-experimental design, or an STEM-specific domain (disciplinary context is mentioned but not specified). Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record goes to full text to check design, comparison, domain, and whether HOT performance is a quantitative learning outcome.

quote: Using AI Applications to Enhance EFL Learners' Writing Skills
rationale: The study concerns EFL (English as a foreign language) writing skills using the generative AI assistant Monica. English language learning is non-STEM content, which fails the Domain criterion, so exclusion code E2 applies. Other criteria (random assignment with control group, writing outcome) appear met, but the population (in-service program adults aged 26-36) also raises doubt; the domain failure is decisive as the first applicable code in order is E2 under the protocol's ordering, since E4 is checked after E2 only if E1 and E2 do not apply... E2 is checked before E4 and applies.

quote: The study involved 25 physics education students who completed these tests independently and with ChatGPT's assistance.
rationale: Abstract describes a within-subject design in which the same 25 students took the tests both independently and with ChatGPT. There is no separate control group without generative AI, and the design appears to be a single-group comparison, so the comparison criterion fails (E3). The abstract also describes a case study, with no quantitative effect statistics reported. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of the missing control group at the abstract stage.

quote: 모든 프로젝트는 창의성·실현 가능성·도구 활용도를 기준으로 루브릭 평가 및 비교 분석을 실시하였으며, 대표 사례로 선정된 세 팀을 대상으로 질적 분석을 추가로 수행하였다.
rationale: The abstract describes a single course with 8 team project outputs, evaluated by rubric and qualitative analysis of three teams. There is no described control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion appears not met (E3). The study looks like a single-group outcome analysis of student projects. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of no comparison group in the abstract.
rationale_note: Abstract stage; the rule says exclude only on positive evidence. Here the abstract describes one course and no comparison, which is a positive indication of E3. Also, the domain (non-CS students learning generative AI use, no-code/vibe coding) is borderline for STEM, and the outcome (rubric scores of project outputs) is not clearly a learning measure.

quote: The research employed an online questionnaire survey (273 students) and semi-structured interviews (11 faculty members).
rationale: The abstract describes a survey and interviews on ChatGPT use and attitudes. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design, no control group, and no learning outcome measured. Under the protocol, this fails the comparison and design criteria. E3 is the first applicable code in order (no control group without generative AI), and the study also fails E5 and E6. Because the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-comparative survey design, exclusion is appropriate.

criteria.criteria_note: n/a

quote: The study employed a Research and Development (R&D) method using the 4D model (Define, Design, Develop, Disseminate) involving 94 eighth-grade students.
rationale: Abstract describes Gemini Veo 3 generative video used in student worksheets for eighth-grade science (elements and compounds), with an inquiry skill outcome (N-Gain). Generative AI intervention, STEM domain, K-12 population and quantitative outcome appear met. However, the abstract reports only an N-Gain from what appears to be a single-group pre-post effectiveness test, with no mention of a control group. Per the rules, a single-group pre-post design is E3, but the abstract does not clearly rule out a comparison group, and the design is not described. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record advances to full text to check for a control group and effect size data. Journal article status is also not confirmed from the abstract, though the venue suggests a journal.

quote: A structured questionnaire was administered to 294 students from three Moroccan engineering schools in order to collect data on their use of these tools.
rationale: The study is a questionnaire-based survey with predictive modeling of grades from self-reported GAIT use. There is no control group without generative AI and no experimental comparison, so the design and comparison criteria fail (E3). Survey/correlational designs also fail the design criterion. Exclusion code E3 is applied as the first clear failing criterion in order after E1/E2 were not positively shown to fail.

quote: A quantitative, cross-sectional research design was employed, and data were collected from 300 undergraduate and postgraduate students
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional structured-questionnaire survey with regression and mediation analysis of self-reported GenAI adoption. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI, so the study fails the comparison and design criteria (E3 applies as the first failing code given the protocol's order; the design also fails the Design criterion). Outcomes are self-reported competencies and readiness rather than measured learning. Domain is not clearly STEM. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of a non-comparative cross-sectional design.

quote: professors blindly evaluated the responses on a 0-10 scale, considering quality, depth, and personalization
rationale: The study compares a customised GPT (BSVP) with ChatGPT-4 Turbo, both generative AI, and the outcome is professor ratings of response quality rather than a learner outcome. No quantitative learning measure is reported, and the comparison is between two generative AI variants with no non-AI control, which would also fail E3. Coded E5 as the first applicable code in order; the abstract gives positive evidence that no learning outcome is measured. Note that E3 could also apply, but E5 is listed first in the order of checks needed here, and the abstract-stage evidence is clear on the outcome.

quote: A cross-sectional survey design was employed in this quantitative study.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey design with structural equation modelling and path analysis, with no separate control group that avoids generative AI. Outcomes are largely perceived conceptual understanding and affective factors (self-efficacy, motivation, satisfaction), and there is no sign of a comparison group. Positive evidence of a missing control group supports exclusion under E3. Design also fails the survey exclusion, but the first applicable code in order is E3.

quote: This study synthesized 19 experimental and quasi-experimental studies conducted in different contexts (k = 68), involving 2,347 participants.
rationale: This is a meta-analysis, which is a review and would normally be excluded as E6 (not an empirical study) under the protocol's publication-type/empirical criteria. However, the rule for abstract-stage decisions says to exclude only on positive evidence and the protocol's exclusion list for review articles is under publication type (E10: reviews). Because the record is a meta-analysis of primary studies rather than a primary study, it does not itself meet the eligibility of a primary empirical study; the abstract provides positive evidence of a review design. Given the audit context and the rule that wrongly excluded studies are lost, I mark it unsure for the researcher to confirm whether meta-analyses should be excluded (E6 or E10) or whether the included primary studies should be sought from its reference list. Intervention (Gen-AI), outcome (HOT), and experimental design are described in the abstract but cannot be verified for individual primary studies here.

quote: evaluating the performance of several LLMs in generating Python code and answering basic computer science and programming questions
rationale: The study evaluates LLMs' own performance on programming exercises and MCQs; no learners interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). No control group or learner sample is described. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that learner-facing generative AI is absent.

criteria.quote: This study employed a qualitative approach using a descriptive phenomenological research design.

quote: This study employed a qualitative approach using a descriptive phenomenological research design.
rationale: The study is a qualitative phenomenological design on students' experiences, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Arabic language writing is also non-STEM (E2), but the first applicable code in order is E3 for missing control... Applying the order strictly: E1 does not apply (learner-facing ChatGPT feedback). E2 applies because Arabic writing is language learning, not STEM, which precedes the other codes in the protocol order. Non-STEM content is therefore the first failing criterion.

quote: An overall framework is proposed, which centers on "human-machine collaboration", with "pre-class, in-class, post-class" as the main line
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual framework and analysis of how GenAI might be integrated into a Systems Engineering course. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is a position or conceptual paper, so E6 applies as the first failing criterion in code order.

quote: The study explored student and faculty perspectives on using Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools, like ChatGPT, in eLearning.
rationale: The abstract describes a perspective/survey-style study of student and faculty views on GenAI. It reports no controlled comparison and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions and views, which the protocol excludes. Positive evidence of failing the outcome and design criteria is present, so exclude. E5 is the first applicable code in order that fits (no quantitative learning outcome), with the design also not meeting a comparison-group requirement.

quote: The study employed a single-group pretest–posttest design without a control condition.
rationale: The abstract explicitly describes a single-group pretest-posttest design with no control condition. Per protocol, single-group pre-post designs and one group measured before and after are E3. The other criteria appear met (generative AI chatbots, secondary physics/electrical engineering, quantitative pre-post outcomes), but the comparison requirement fails on positive evidence.

quote: This session will introduce you to generative AI, AI literacy, and ways to incorporate AI in your daily life.
rationale: The record is a webinar session description, not an empirical study. It describes no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not a journal article. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in order; the record also fails other criteria (no control group, no outcome data, not STEM-specific, not a journal article), but E6 is the earliest applicable code.
rationale_note: Exclusion at abstract stage is justified by positive evidence that the record is a non-empirical webinar description.

quote: A bibliometric analysis of 412 journal articles from Web of Science provided the initial step to identify major themes and relationships in the LLSE literature.
rationale: This is a meta-synthesis and bibliometric review of LLSE literature with conceptual recommendations. It is not an empirical study with a control group or learning outcome, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study). No learner-facing GenAI intervention or comparison group is reported.

quote: LLM feedback outperformed novice feedback and, in the categories explanation, questions, and specificity, even surpassed expert feedback in quality
rationale: The study evaluates the quality of LLM-generated feedback as rated by researchers, not a quantitative learning outcome of learners exposed to the AI. Feedback quality ratings of generated text are not learner achievement, so E5 applies. Also, learners do not interact with the LLM in a learning activity here; the LLM generates feedback for teacher education texts, and the population is preservice teachers in a non-STEM (feedback/teaching) context, which is also doubtful. The first applicable code in order is E1 possibly, but the intervention is LLM-generated feedback for evaluation rather than learner-facing use; E5 is the clearest positive failure shown in the abstract.

quote: The research critically examines the impact of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) on educational assessment by highlighting both its transformative potential and associated risks.
rationale: The abstract describes a critical/narrative analysis and stakeholder analysis, with no experimental design, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study with a comparison group, so it fails the design and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is applied as the first code that applies on the evidence available; the record is a review-type analysis.

The abstract describes a survey-based observational study of awareness, academic use, and perceived instructor encouragement among 938 undergraduates. It reports no control group, no experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are usage and perceptions. Design and outcome criteria are not met on positive evidence, so the record is excluded at the abstract stage under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), the first applicable code in the order given. Quote field is null because no single passage states the design or lack of outcome directly; the decision rests on the overall description.

quote: In this SoTEL Symposium presentation/discussion with the ASCILITE MLSIG I propose a move away from a humanist world view
rationale: The record is a symposium presentation/discussion proposing a conceptual, post-human perspective on generative AI in art and design education. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Other criteria are also unmet or unclear, but E6 applies first in the code order that is relevant here; E5 (no quantitative outcome) would also apply.

quote: The scope of this research was descriptive, and the design was nonexperimental.
rationale: The study is a descriptive, nonexperimental design with teachers as the population (60 English teachers), so it has no control group, no learner outcome, and English language content rather than STEM. Under the protocol's code order, E2 (non-STEM content) is the first code that applies; the design and population failures would also be disqualifying. Abstract gives positive evidence of non-STEM content (English reading and writing).
rationale_note: Exclusion chosen on domain as first applicable in order E1-E10 check; E1 not clearly applicable since intervention is teacher-facing design work, but E1 would be an alternative. Ordering: E1 is checked first; the abstract does not establish learner interaction with generative AI, so E1 is arguably the first applicable code. Reporting E2 per content domain.

quote: A pilot implementation of this system involving 200 computer science students successfully demonstrated the effectiveness of this technology.
rationale: Abstract describes a hybrid gamification framework using AI, ML, and ANFIS with a pilot involving 200 computer science students. It does not state whether a generative model is used (ANFIS and ML are not generative), and it gives no information on a control group, design, or quantitative learning outcome. These are not positive evidence of failure, so the record is passed to full text as unsure rather than excluded.

quote: Using qualitative analyses, workflow modeling, and simulated performance assessments, the research highlights improved operational efficiency
rationale: The paper concerns GenAI integrated into ERP systems for administrative operations, not a learner-facing generative AI learning activity. It uses qualitative analyses and simulated assessments, with no control group and no learner quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E1 as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI for learning; the other failures (no comparison group, non-empirical design, non-STEM learning content) also apply.

quote: A quantitative research design was adopted, and data were collected through a structured questionnaire from 350 undergraduate and postgraduate students
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional questionnaire with SEM mediation analysis. It has no control group without generative AI, so it is not a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison design. The abstract gives positive evidence of a correlational/survey design, so E3 applies. The domain is also not stated as STEM. The outcome is self-perceived performance, not a clearly quantitative learning measure. Because the first applicable code in order is E3, that code is reported.

quote: We iteratively designed prompts for the generation of specific feedback types (as part of existing feedback taxonomies) in response to authentic student programs.
rationale: Abstract describes prompt design and evaluation of LLM-generated feedback quality against feedback taxonomies, with no control group, no comparison condition, and no learner-outcome measure. Positive evidence of missing comparison group and missing quantitative learning outcome; exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code in order that is supported by the abstract. Design is not an experiment comparing learners, so this is an exclusion rather than unsure.

quote: The purpose of this article is to explore how artificial intelligence (AI) tools can be leveraged within this structure-building process
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/discussion article on using AI assistant tools for curriculum design (backward design) in nursing education. It presents no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Also, AI is used by faculty for curriculum development rather than learner-facing, which would independently trigger E1, but E6 is the first applicable code given the ordering rule is applied to the primary failure; E1 is earlier in order, so the strictly first applicable code is arguably E1 since AI is used only by educators. Nursing is also health professions education, outside the STEM domain (E2 would apply before E6 in order). Given the rule to report the first applicable code in order, the exclusion should be E1 because the AI is used only by faculty to prepare curriculum materials.

quote: This article proposes an optimization of guiding feedback involving the integration of pedagogical agents to provide the feedback to students and the use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) to support the generation of error-specific information.
rationale: The article is a conceptual proposal that "introduces the concept" and "illustrates it through examples." It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no outcome data, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion is based on positive evidence from the abstract that the paper is non-empirical.

quote: Students were mandated to use GenAI (e.g. ChatGPT) in their assignment, reflect on its ethical implications, and draw parallels to its use in marketing practice.
rationale: Content is marketing ethics, not science, mathematics, engineering, computer science, programming, or data science, so E2 applies (first failing code in order after E1 check, which is met since students use GenAI directly). The abstract also describes no control group (E3) and analyses student self-reflections, which are perceptions rather than a quantitative learning outcome (E5); E2 is reported as the first applicable code.

quote: The article presents the results of an analysis of the academic integrity policies of all six Singapore universities in the context of using artificial intelligence (AI) in education.
rationale: This is a policy document analysis of institutional academic integrity policies, not an empirical study with a learner-facing generative AI intervention, a control group, or a quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Exclusion is based on positive evidence from the abstract, which describes a policy review rather than an experiment.

quote: A survey of 539 engineering students from 12 leading Chinese universities, using the UTAUT framework
rationale: The study is a survey of engineering students' LLM tool use with no experimental or comparison group, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. It also reports perceptions and usage rather than a quantitative learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI), though E5 and E6 (non-empirical is arguable, since it is a survey) would also apply. Excluded on the abstract alone since the design is clearly a survey.
rationale_note: Stated design is a cross-sectional survey, so no control group exists.

criteria.quote: This mixed-methods survey study investigates dual study students’ use of GenAI, their perceptions of curricular preparedness
criteria.rationale: Survey-based study of student perceptions and adoption; no control group, no intervention comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. Fails comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Coded E6 as a non-experimental survey, which is not an empirical experiment meeting the design criteria. Although E6 is typically reserved for non-empirical records, the design is a survey and the first applicable code by protocol order here would be E1 or E3; however the study is clearly not an intervention study, so E3 (no control group) is the most direct first failing criterion among those ordered. Note: decision follows the protocol's ordered codes; see rationale for the basis.

quote: This mixed-methods survey study investigates dual study students’ use of GenAI, their perceptions of curricular preparedness for AI-supported work
rationale: Survey study of perceptions and adoption with no intervention comparison and no learning outcome. Fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. Per the protocol's code order, E1 (learner-facing GenAI intervention) is the first code that applies, since no GenAI learning activity is evaluated. Correcting my initial code: the first applicable exclusion in order is E1 because the study does not evaluate a learner-facing GenAI intervention. Domain is also not clearly STEM (business/dual study programs unspecified in abstract), but that is not the first failing code.

quote: We describe an assignment in which Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) students learned to use generative text AI.
rationale: Educational description of an assignment with no comparison group, no quantitative learning outcome (only faculty debrief and student reception), and the domain is nursing informatics/health professions rather than STEM. Excluded under E6 as a non-empirical descriptive report; the abstract gives positive evidence of no control group and no quantitative outcome. Health professions education is also outside the STEM domain, which would be a further failure.

The abstract is a narrative overview of ChatGPT's potential in education, with no described study design, sample, comparison group, or quantitative learning outcome. It gives positive evidence of no empirical study (E6). Domain and population are not described. Excluded at abstract stage on E6 because it reads as a discussion or review piece rather than an empirical study.

quote: This study explores the arrival of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) technologies in a collaborative Problem-Based Learning (PBL) environment from the perspective of students.

Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in the order given (no comparison group), with E5 also applicable. Design is survey/exploratory, not an experiment. Abstract-stage evidence is positive for failure of comparison, so excluded.

quote: a manuscript cannot report model performance as observed when no empirical response corpus has been collected
rationale: The record is a Monte Carlo simulation study with synthetic outputs and no empirical data collected from learners. quote: We evaluated three LLMs – ChatGPT 4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Gemini 1.5 Pro – on 120 multiple-choice questions and compared their performance to that of over 139,000 high-school students.

Human students' exam scores are a historical comparison, not a control group that lacks generative AI. No learner-facing generative AI intervention is present, so E1 applies (first applicable code). Design is a benchmark evaluation rather than a randomized or quasi-experiment with a comparison group.

quote: After this implementation, we analyzed students’ opinions on the application of AI in selected areas.
rationale: Generative AI (ChatGPT) is used by preservice mathematics teachers, a higher education population in a STEM-related domain. Perception-only outcomes and a case-study design fail the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E5 is applied as the first failing criterion among the outcome-related failures; the design also appears non-experimental. Decision is made at abstract stage on positive evidence of the case-study, opinion-based design.

quote: The study involved 102 middle school students who played an online game with the provision of ChatGPT and sought help from ChatGPT while solving physics problems.
rationale: Learners interact with ChatGPT in a physics game-based learning activity, and participants are middle school students, which is consistent with the protocol. The abstract does not state whether there is a control group without generative AI; it describes profiles and correlations, which suggests a correlational design (exclusion E3 or E6 likely at full text). Outcome is game performance/engagement and attempts, which may be quantitative learning measures. Abstract does not give positive evidence of failure, so advance to full text to check comparison and design.

quote: This cross-sectional study aimed to explore the use and perceptions of ChatGPT among students and faculty in North American genetic counseling programs.
rationale: Cross-sectional online survey of use and perceptions. Survey design is not an empirical experiment eligible under the protocol design criteria; the first applicable code in order is E1 only if the intervention were not learner-facing, which is unclear, so E6 is used as the closest code for a non-experimental survey study. Abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with no learning outcome and no control group.

Abstract describes an evaluation exploration of generative AI tools' capability for generating teaching materials. No control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported; findings concern tool capabilities. Positive evidence of missing comparison group supports E3 (no control group without generative AI). Would also fail E5 and E6 possibly, but the first applicable code in order is E1 check: the tools are used to generate materials, not clearly learner-facing, so E1 could apply; however the clearest failure is the absence of a control group, so E3 is reported. Note: at abstract stage, the evidence is that no comparison exists.

quote: Method: This study employed a quantitative correlational design using PLS-SEM.

The outcome is self-reported motivation (perception-based), not a quantitative learning measure. The protocol lists E3 (no control group) as the first applicable code in the order given, so E3 is reported. Population (university students) is met; domain is unclear from the abstract. Excluding at abstract stage is justified by positive evidence of correlational design with no comparison group.

quote: Bu araştırma, Kırklareli Üniversitesi Yazılım Mühendisliği Bölümü’nde öğrenim gören ... lisans öğrencileri ile gerçekleştirilmiş olup, veriler ilişkisel tarama modeli esas alınarak toplanmış ve Yapısal Eşitlik Modellemesi ile analiz edilmiştir.

Excluded on the first applicable code in order, E1 being unclear at abstract stage; E3 is the clearest positive failure.

Excluded as not an empirical study meeting design criteria; the first applicable code in order is E1 check (intervention not clearly learner-facing GenAI) but the study fails on design/outcome, and the most fundamental failure is that it is a survey, coded E6 as non-experimental empirical study.
