quote: Immediate feedback on open-ended questions enhanced learning outcomes, enabling students to address knowledge gaps effectively.
rationale: Abstract describes LLM-based grading and feedback tools used with geotechnics students (generative AI, STEM domain met). It does not state whether a control group without generative AI exists, so comparison and design cannot be confirmed. The abstract also says the study is mixed-methods with synthetic and real student data, and the outcome claim about learning enhancement is not clearly backed by a quantitative comparison. Missing information is not grounds for exclusion at abstract stage, so advance to full text to check the comparison, design, and outcome.

quote: Development and implementation of an elementary English writing program using image-generative AI
rationale: The study concerns English writing instruction for sixth-graders, which is language learning and not STEM (E2). Although image-generative AI is used by learners and writing outcomes are quantitative, the content domain fails the protocol's STEM requirement. Coded E2 as the first applicable exclusion in order (E1 does not apply since the tool is learner-facing generative AI).

quote: ChatGPT-3.5 scoring an average of 35%, ChatGPT-4 47% and ChatGPT-4 with Wolfram plugin 78%
rationale: The study has ChatGPT answering online quizzes itself, not learners interacting with generative AI in a learning activity. There is no control group without generative AI; the comparisons are only between ChatGPT variants and a corrected-arithmetic version of the same outputs. This fails the comparison and design criteria. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Other criteria (STEM-adjacent quantitative modules, outcome as quiz scores of the AI) are not clearly met either.

quote: The method used is a systematic study of 26 relevant articles from 2016 to 2025
rationale: The record is a systematic review of 26 articles, not an empirical primary study with a control group. It is therefore not an empirical study (E6). Its design criterion is not met, and the review does not report its own learning outcome data.

The record has only a title and venue; no abstract is available. The title suggests graduate students in higher education and a writing-process focus, but it describes perceived appropriateness, utility, and self-reported use, which points toward perception/usage outcomes that the protocol excludes. Writing is also not obviously STEM. Nothing in the record gives positive evidence of a failed criterion, and the title alone does not establish whether a control group or quantitative learning outcome exists, so the record is advanced to full text for checking.

quote: The paper presents a case study that applies the 5Es model to test personalized learning for students using ChatGPT.
rationale: ChatGPT (generative AI) used by learners in a data science (Deep Learning) learning activity, so intervention, domain and population appear met. The abstract describes a "case study", which suggests a non-experimental design, but it also says ChatGPT was compared against "traditional teaching methods", so a comparison group may exist. Whether there is a control group and a quantitative learning outcome cannot be determined from the abstract. Not excluded on missing information; advance to full text to check design, comparison and outcome.

quote: This narrative review explains the technical principles of large language models and examines their use in vocational undergraduate finance and accounting education.
rationale: The record is a narrative review, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It reports no controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome. Finance and accounting is also not clearly within the STEM domain in the protocol, but the review-design failure is the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported. E6 is the first applicable code given the record is a review rather than an empirical study.

criteria.rationale: placeholder

quote: English language learning and teaching; "Language learning and other non-STEM content" is excluded by protocol.
rationale: The study concerns English language learning and teaching with ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot. English language learning is non-STEM content, so the Domain criterion fails (E2). The abstract also describes a perspective/overview paper rather than an empirical study with a control group, which would separately fail E3/E6. Coded E2 as the first applicable code in protocol order per the domain failure.

quote: Results reveal that educators employing the language model-assisted system stated that preparation time declined and provided students with individual feedback more frequently
rationale: The study concerns English language teaching, which the protocol excludes as non-STEM (language learning and other non-STEM content). The intervention is also mainly teacher-facing (18 English teachers using LLM materials), which would raise E1 as well, but E2 is the first applicable code in the specified order. Abstract gives positive evidence of non-STEM content, so exclusion is supported.

quote: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among Years 1–5 medical undergraduates at SUSL in May 2025.
rationale: Cross-sectional survey with no experimental or comparison group. Outcomes are usage, self-rated competence, and attitudes, not quantitative learning outcomes. Positive evidence of design failure (survey, not a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison) is present, so E3 is applied (no control group without generative AI). Note that E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) also applies, but E3 is listed first in the protocol order, so E3 is reported. Domain is medical education, which is not clearly STEM and may also fail E2.

quote: School is conceived as a place for learning knowledge and developing skills through curricula that address, on the one hand, administrative aspects and on the other, aspects that concern the individual
rationale: The abstract is a general position/essay about school innovation and teacher roles. It describes no empirical study, no learner interaction with a generative AI tool, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It appears to be a non-empirical discussion piece, so E6 applies. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract that the record is not an empirical study.

Content is an English debate course (EFL/language content), which falls under the protocol's non-STEM exclusion (language learning). The study is qualitative (focus group interviews and open-ended questionnaires), with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Generative AI use is not described as learner-facing in the abstract; the only mention is a generic 'particularly in the context of generative artificial intelligence.' E2 is the first applicable code in order, so it is reported.
rationale_quote: Data were collected through semi-structured focus group interviews and open-ended questionnaires.

rationale: Abstract describes a qualitative examination of GPT models' understanding of graphical representations compared with students' strengths and limitations. No control group receiving a non-generative-AI condition is described, and the study is qualitative rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison. No quantitative learning outcome with SMD-computable statistics is evident. Coded E3 as the first applicable code in order is E3 (no comparison group without generative AI); E5 would also plausibly apply. The abstract gives positive evidence of no control group, so exclusion is supported.

quote: we benchmark GPT-4.1 and GPT-5 models on a corpus of 601 undergraduate physics exam problems
rationale: The study benchmarks LLMs directly on exam problems by marking model answers against official solutions. No learners interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, and there is no control group or experimental design. This fails the intervention criterion (E1). Also no comparison group exists (E3 would also apply), but E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: The study evaluates the AI assistant's impact across four key areas: teaching preparation efficiency, active learning support, data analysis process enhancement, and the promotion of advanced learning activities.
rationale: Custom GPT-based RAG teaching assistant for university data science, so generative AI learner-facing intervention, STEM domain and higher-education population appear met. However, the abstract does not state a control group or any comparison, and the evaluation reads as perception/workflow-focused ("findings indicate significant improvements", "fostering self-directed learning") with no clear quantitative learning measure. Abstract does not positively show a failure, so advance to full text to check for a control group and quantitative learning outcome.

quote: Data were collected via comparative testing, post-interaction surveys, and informal student interviews.
rationale: Abstract describes LLM-based (GPT) chatbots for undergraduate CS/engineering, which meets population and domain. It is unclear whether a control group without generative AI exists: the comparison is described as "direct-answer AI tools" and "comparative testing", and the abstract says controlled comparative studies are future work. Outcomes are mixed with perceptions (engagement, confidence, perceived usefulness), and it is unclear whether a quantitative learning measure with SMD-usable data was reported. Abstract gives no clear positive evidence of failure, so the record advances to full text.

quote: Employing a quasi-experimental design, we implemented a 16-week dual-track instructional intervention (incorporating AI-integrated pedagogy and ethical scaffolding) for 148 computer science students.
rationale: Abstract reports a quasi-experiment with computer science students and GenAI integration, but the outcomes reported are UTAUT2 constructs (performance expectancy, hedonic motivation, behavioral intention, habit), i.e., perceptions/adoption measures rather than a quantitative learning outcome. Affective/perception outcomes are excluded by protocol, so E5 applies. No learning achievement measure is evident in the abstract.

quote: The methodological framework rests on synthetic causal analysis conducted on the basis of a systematic review of empirical studies from 2020?2025.
rationale: The abstract describes a "synthetic causal analysis" based on a systematic review of prior empirical studies, not a primary randomized or quasi-experiment with its own control group and learner data. This is not an empirical study of the protocol's design type, so it fails E6. No new trial with a control group is described. Intervention, domain, and population are not clearly stated, but the design alone is a positive exclusion at the abstract stage.

The record has a title and venue only, with no abstract. The title suggests generative AI use in an introductory science course, which fits the topic, but nothing in the record shows whether there is a control group, a learning outcome, or an eligible design. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is kept for full-text review rather than excluded.

quote: Using a one-group pretest-posttest design, 34 pre-/in-service teachers completed the module in 2025
rationale: The abstract describes a one-group pretest-posttest design with no control group that does not use generative AI, which is positive evidence of E3. Population is also teachers (pre-/in-service), which would be an additional concern, but the first applicable code in order is E3 for the design/comparison failure.

quote: The paper is conceptual. It follows a theory adaptation design
rationale: The abstract states the paper is conceptual and that no data were analysed, so it is not an empirical study and has no control group or quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order that the abstract supports. E1 to E5 are not assessed separately because the abstract gives positive evidence of E6 and no empirical comparison exists.

quote: The pronunciation of regular past tense /-ed/ endings remain a challenging skill for Thai learners in an EFL context.
rationale: The study is English-as-a-foreign-language pronunciation practice, which is language learning and non-STEM content, so it fails the Domain criterion (E2). The abstract also describes a single-group pre-test/post-test design with no control group, which would independently fail the comparison criterion (E3). E2 is listed first in the code order, so it is the code reported. The record is not ambiguous on domain, so exclusion is justified even at the abstract stage.
rationale_note: Abstract describes pre-test and post-test on one group of 62 students with no comparison group.

quote: The main objective was to implement and evaluate the impact of a multilingual AR resource (in Moldovan, English, Russian, and Spanish) in educational settings
rationale: Content is multiword expressions in language learning (Moldovan, English, Russian, Spanish), which is non-STEM, so E2 applies. Also, the abstract reports only satisfaction and perception surveys with no quantitative learning outcome or control group, and AR is not shown to be generative AI (LLMs were used only for coding data, not learner-facing). Multiple criteria fail; E2 is the first applicable code in the stated order.

quote: This study explores students' reflective and selective use of Chatgpt in academic essay writing in Islamic-based higher education. Using a qualitative approach of the phenomenological type
rationale: The study is a qualitative phenomenological design with interviews and document analysis, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Essay writing in Islamic education is not clearly STEM. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of no comparison group and qualitative design; E3 is the first applicable code in protocol order for the missing comparison, though E5 and E2 also apply.

quote: This scoping review maps recent journal literature from 2021 onward, anchored in a Scopus export searched on 22 February 2026.
rationale: This is a scoping review of literature, not an empirical study, so it fails E6 (the first applicable code given the protocol's ordering; E1 cannot be assessed as the review does not describe a single intervention). Its focus is academic writing, which is not STEM content, so it also fails the domain criterion. Review publication type is also not eligible under the protocol.

quote: This study examined teachers’ readiness for the use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in classroom pedagogy in Jolo III District, Division of Sulu.
rationale: The study is a descriptive-exploratory survey of in-service elementary teachers' readiness. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; it is a survey (non-experimental). Exclusion at E6 (not an empirical experimental study) is the first applicable code given the design. Note: under the ordering rule E1 (intervention not learner-facing) also applies; E1 would be the first code in the protocol order. The protocol says report the first that applies in order, so the code should be E1.

quote: "本文探讨了该模式对师范生的工具应用能力、协同设计能力以及创新引领能力的提升作用"
rationale: Abstract describes a generative AI agent (AI智能体) used by learners in a Mathematical Analysis course (STEM, preservice math teachers in higher education). It does not state whether a control group exists or what study design is used, and does not report a quantitative learning outcome; it mentions capability improvements without indicating measurement. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is kept for full-text review rather than excluded.

quote: The study involved 150 PSTs enrolled in a master's-level mathematics course at a German university who worked collaboratively on three authentic modeling tasks.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive, qualitative-style study (worksheets, open-ended surveys, interviews) of PSTs using LLMs for modeling tasks. There is no control group without generative AI and no quantitative learning outcome reported. Positive evidence of failure on comparison and design/outcome is present, so exclude. Coded E3 as the first applicable code in the order of checking, since no comparison group is evident; E5 would also apply on outcome.

Abstract describes a cross-sectional Likert questionnaire on perceived awareness, use, and benefits of GenAI across gender, study level, and delivery mode. No separate control group receiving a non-GenAI condition and no learning outcome measured; outcomes are perceptions and self-reported use, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion is positive evidence on outcome (perceptions only) and design (survey, not experimental). Coded E5 as the outcome failure; E3 and E6 would also apply on design grounds. Abstract-stage exclusion is justified because the abstract explicitly describes perception-only survey data.

quote: It introduces a conceptual Input-Mediator-Outcome framework with strong research potential
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual framework and aims to lay groundwork for future research. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is a non-empirical (conceptual) paper, so E6 applies. Under the rules, E6 is the first applicable code for this record at the abstract stage, since the absence of an empirical design is positive evidence against eligibility.

criteria.population_note: Students implied but level not stated in abstract

quote: We observed that students relying solely on ChatGPT for learning resulted in lower performance compared to those receiving instruction from teachers, either alone or supported by ChatGPT.
rationale: Abstract describes a ChatGPT (generative AI) learner-facing condition, a mathematics domain, and a three-group comparison with a teacher-instruction group that does not use generative AI, which suggests a control group. However, the abstract does not state the study design (it is labeled a case study, which would be excluded if it lacks a comparison group), the education level of the students, or whether a quantitative learning outcome with extractable statistics is reported. These points cannot be confirmed from the abstract, so the record is passed to full text rather than excluded.

quote: ChatGPT was used to generate answers to homework assignments and tests used to measure student performance in an intermediate accounting course
rationale: Content is intermediate accounting, which is not STEM under the protocol's domain list (science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, data science). The abstract also describes ChatGPT-generated answers compared with a prior course section, not a concurrent control group of learners using non-generative-AI, so the comparison is doubtful. E2 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported by the abstract.

quote: A qualitative case study approach was employed, with focus group discussions conducted to collect data from six first-year students
rationale: The study is a qualitative case study using focus groups with six students, with no control group, no generative AI intervention evaluated, and no quantitative learning outcome. The design is not an eligible empirical comparison; coded E6 as a non-empirical-comparison (qualitative) study. Exclusion is supported by the explicit qualitative design, though the code E6 is the closest fit for a non-quantitative study rather than a strict "not empirical" finding.

Abstract is absent from the index; only the title is available. The title indicates the outcome is students' earning expectations, which is an attitudinal/expectation measure rather than a quantitative learning outcome, and the topic is labor market economics rather than STEM content. Positive evidence of failure exists on outcome (E5) and domain (E2 would also apply), but the protocol's exclusion codes are applied in order, and E1 (intervention) and E2 (content) are checked before E5. Because the title does not establish whether the intervention is learner-facing generative AI, the E1 check is unresolved, so this exclusion is a best judgment from limited information and should be verified by the auditor. Given the rule that abstract-stage exclusions require positive evidence, this record could alternatively be marked unsure.

quote: Using a mixed-methods research approach, this study employed a CSE-based questionnaire and focus group interviews
rationale: Abstract describes an EFL academic writing study (English language content, non-STEM), so E2 applies as the first failing criterion in code order. The design is a questionnaire and focus-group study with no control group or learning outcome, which would also fail E3/E5 but E2 is reported first.

quote: an investigation of the need and opportunities of AI in chemical engineering education. The latter is achieved through quantitative and qualitative analyses of the responses given by both Master's students and academia/industry practitioners on the introduction and use of AI in education.
rationale: Abstract describes a chatbot overview and survey-style analyses of student and practitioner responses on perceptions, expectations and concerns. No controlled comparison group or quantitative learning outcome is indicated; the study appears to be a perception/survey and descriptive work. Excluded at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Design also appears non-experimental, but the abstract is not explicit enough to make E3 or E6 the first applicable code with certainty; E5 is the most direct positive evidence.

decision_note: Survey of academic staff; not an empirical experiment with a comparison group.
quote: In 2023, we administered a survey to academic staff at our Australian-based University to explore their perspectives, attitudes and experiences regarding GenAI in learning and teaching.
rationale: The study is a survey of university staff perspectives. It is not an intervention study with learners, has no control group, and reports no learning outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion codes, the first applicable code is E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's intended sense of a comparative/quantitative design); the survey design fails the Design criterion and the population is staff rather than students, so the record is excluded at abstract stage.

quote: Practice has shown that this framework significantly improves students’ instructional design efficiency, resource integration skills, and confidence in technology application
rationale: The abstract describes a course-level implementation framework ("Practice has shown") with no described control group or comparison condition, which points to a practice report rather than a controlled empirical study. The outcomes named (instructional design efficiency, confidence) are largely perceptual or unmeasured in the abstract, and no quantitative learning measure or comparison is described. Educational Psychology is also not clearly STEM content. On the positive evidence available, the study does not appear to be an empirical comparison design, so it is excluded under E6. Confidence is moderate; a full-text check could confirm whether any controlled comparison exists.

quote: Using a mixed-method research design, we explore students’ performance, preferences, mental workload, and emotional responses across various problem sources from the manufacturing domain in mechanical engineering, specifically traditional textbook-based problems and Gen-AI-generated problems.
rationale: Mechanical engineering (STEM) with Gen-AI-generated problems vs. textbook problems suggests a possible comparison group without generative AI. However, the abstract does not clarify whether students interact with the Gen-AI tool (versus only the teacher or researcher generating problems), whether the design is a controlled comparison, whether the population is students, or whether a quantitative learning outcome is reported (performance is mentioned but mixed with perceptions and emotional responses). Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is held for full-text review.

quote: Ninety-eight nursing students enrolled in the Nursing Care and Services Management course
rationale: The content is nursing care and services management, a health professions topic, which the protocol excludes from the STEM domain (E2). The design is a cross-sectional survey with no evident control group, and the study does not clearly meet the comparison or design criteria, but the domain failure is the first applicable code in order.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on domain is positive evidence: health professions education is explicitly excluded.

quote: This study aims to investigate English as a Foreign Language students’ perceptions and attitudes towards using ChatGPT to enhance their English-speaking skills
rationale: Content is English language learning (speaking skills), which is non-STEM, so E2 applies as the first failing code in order. The study also uses a single-group questionnaire on perceptions with no control group and no learning outcome (would fail E3 and E5 as well), but E2 is the first applicable code. Positive evidence of failure is present at the abstract stage.

quote: The participants were divided into two groups: the control group (107 students), where traditional feedback was used, and the experimental group (106 students) involving an improved GAI-based feedback system.
rationale: Abstract describes a control group and a GAI-based feedback experimental group with students in teacher training programmes (higher education). However, the primary reported outcome is satisfaction with feedback and perceptions, which is excluded under the outcome criterion unless a quantitative learning measure exists. The abstract does not name a STEM content area beyond mathematics and computer studies faculty, and does not show a learning outcome measure. Missing information is not evidence of failure at abstract stage, so the record is unsure and should be checked at full text for a quantitative learning outcome and STEM content.

quote: Perceived usefulness was evaluated through post-course student feedback across two independent markets with identical game mechanics.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study is an exploratory case study evaluating perceived usefulness through survey feedback. The abstract explicitly states the chatbot functioned as a support mechanism rather than a driver of performance outcomes, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. Exclusion under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) applies; the design also appears to be a case study rather than a comparative experiment. The rule for abstract stage is to exclude only on positive evidence, and the abstract gives positive evidence that only perceptions were measured.

quote: This interpretive study examines how seventy preservice teachers engaged with GenAI through structured learning experiences
rationale: The abstract describes an interpretive study using thematic analysis of reflections and prompt documentation, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Design is qualitative, so it is not an empirical design meeting the protocol. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of comparative quantitative design); E3 (no comparison group) and E5 (no quantitative outcome) would also apply. Domain is also unclear since the seminar covers general lesson planning across subjects. The abstract gives clear positive evidence of a qualitative design lacking a control group, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

The title describes a "Case Study", which signals a case study design. The protocol excludes case study designs (Design criterion), and case studies are not controlled experiments with a comparison group. No abstract is available, so the title is the only evidence. This is a non-empirical-experiment design, coded E6 as the closest fit. Confidence is moderate because the title alone is limited; a full-text check would confirm the design.

quote: Experimental validation was carried out using a Yahboom DOFBOT educational manipulator robot, an accessible platform for academic and research experiments.
rationale: The abstract describes a system implementation with experimental validation of a robot interface. It gives no learner population, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of a failed criterion is lacking for comparison and design, but the abstract describes a technical system validation rather than a learning outcome study. Excluding on E5 since no quantitative learning outcome is evident. This is a judgment call; a full-text check would confirm whether any learning measure exists.

quote: The paper adopts a review-based methodology, particularly a systematic qualitative review approach, to examine and synthesize existing research from peer-reviewed sources.
rationale: The abstract describes a review-based, qualitative synthesis and a conceptual framework proposal, not an empirical study. There is no control group or quantitative learning outcome reported. Exclude under E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first applicable code in order of the stated rules for this design.
rationale_note: Abstract stage; positive evidence that the paper is a review/framework rather than an empirical experiment.

quote: This study employs a descriptive qualitative approach, involving eighth-grade junior high school students selected through purposive sampling
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive qualitative study with no control or comparison group, so the comparison and design criteria are not met. Data come from questionnaire, essay test, and interviews analysed qualitatively. The protocol excludes qualitative designs; the first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI), since E1 to E2 and E4 are met on the abstract. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of a non-comparative qualitative design.
exclusion_code_note: E6 could also apply (qualitative, not an empirical comparison); E3 chosen as the first applicable code per the protocol's listed order.

quote: Participants included 32 PLTs in an English Language Teaching (ELT) program in Türkiye.
rationale: The study concerns preservice English language teachers learning grammar methodology, which is language teaching content and not STEM (E2). It is also a qualitative reflexive thematic analysis with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so E3, E5 and E6 would apply too. Per the rule to report the first applicable code in order, E2 is the code, and it is the earliest-ordered failure that is clearly positive from the abstract. Intervention is arguably met (GenAI used by learners), but domain fails.

quote: This research aims to examine students’ attitudes toward using ChatGPT as a learning tool using a quantitative approach with a descriptive study design.
rationale: Descriptive survey study of attitudes toward ChatGPT among undergraduates with no comparison group and no learning outcome measured. Design is a survey, and outcomes are perceptions only. Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly failed at abstract stage, but E3 (no control group) is positive evidence of failure. Exclusion code E3 is applied as the first clearly failing criterion; E5 and E6 would also apply.

quote: The study employed a sequential exploratory mixed-methods strategy, starting with a systematic survey and followed by detailed interviews.
rationale: The study is a survey of mathematics teachers' awareness and perceptions of ChatGPT, not a learner-facing intervention with a control group. It has no quantitative learning outcome among students, and population is in-service teachers, not students. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is not strictly correct since it is empirical; however, the first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI, since teachers only are surveyed and AI is not used by learners). Correcting to the first applicable code in order: E1.

quote: This article presents a theory-informed framework for using ChatGPT to enhance instructional feedback to K–12 teachers for teaching engineering terminology.
rationale: The article is a conceptual framework paper that proposes theory-based prompt design for ChatGPT feedback to teachers. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome. The intervention is teacher-facing (AI used by teachers to prepare instruction), which also falls under E1, but the primary failure is that it is not an empirical study (E6). Per rule 4 and the order of codes, E6 is the first applicable code given the design is conceptual; E1 would also apply, so this is a judgment call that the auditor may wish to check.

The study is a PLS-SEM survey of behavioral intention to use ChatGPT (TAM extension). There is no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; the measured outcome is behavioral intention, an attitudinal measure. Although the abstract gives positive evidence that the design is a survey and the outcome is not learning, the first applicable code in order would be E1 only if intervention failed; since the intervention is ChatGPT use by learners, the failing criteria are design/comparison and outcome. Per the code order, E3 (no control group) would be checked before E5, and the abstract shows no control group, so the first applicable code is E3. Note the design is correlational/survey, which is grounds for E6 as well; the earliest applicable code in the protocol order is E3.

quote: A descriptive survey design was adopted, involving 300 undergraduate Business Education students
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive survey with a single sample and correlational analysis (Pearson correlation between AI usage and performance). There is no control group without generative AI, and the design is not experimental or quasi-experimental. Business Education is not clearly STEM. Exclusion code E3 applies first in order that is clearly evidenced by the absence of a comparison group; E3 is the first code that positively fails here given the protocol's order (E1 and E2 are not clearly failed on the abstract alone).

quote: Analysing User Interaction with AI Chatbots in Academic Libraries
rationale: The study concerns AI chatbots for academic library information services, which is not STEM content (E2). It also reports correlational/questionnaire analyses (satisfaction, trust, r values) with no separate non-generative-AI control group and no learning outcome, so it would fail E3, E5 and E6 as well. E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order.
rationale_note: Code E2 is listed first in order of applicability.

quote: In a randomized controlled experiment, 60 non-mathematics majors solved series convergence proof problems under either dynamic scaffolding or static prompting conditions.
rationale: Abstract describes a randomized experiment with an LLM-based scaffolding system versus static prompting (a generative AI comparison arm, so the comparison criterion is unclear rather than clearly met, since the control also uses LLM prompting). Mathematical proof learning is STEM, the population is university-level (non-math majors), and far-transfer performance is a quantitative outcome. Effect-size data, publication type, and language cannot be verified from the abstract. Because the comparison may be two generative AI variants (which would be E3), the study is advanced to full text for verification rather than excluded at abstract stage.

quote: In this paper, we investigated the role of generative AI in education in academic publications extracted from Web of Science (3506 records; 2019–2024).
rationale: x

quote: We evaluated 1000 Computer Science answers from 100 students across six student-history conditions and eight open-weight LLMs.
rationale: The LLM is used as an automated grader; students do not interact with the generative AI as part of a learning activity, so the intervention is not learner-facing (E1). The study is also a controlled measurement of score drift across conditions with no learner-outcome comparison group without generative AI, so it does not meet the comparison or outcome criteria. Exclusion code E1 is reported as the first applicable code.

quote: Our data source for this project was previous exam questions from an introductory biology course at a large, Southern, research-intensive university.
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT's answers to past exam questions rather than learners interacting with generative AI in a learning activity, and it reports no control group. The abstract gives no comparison group, so the comparison criterion appears not met. Biology is a science domain, so domain is met. Exclusion is based on the absence of a control group, which is positive evidence of failure; the abstract describes a single-source accuracy analysis with no comparison condition.

quote: We applied a mixed‐method survey approach to explore STEM teachers' perceptions, familiarity, and the support needed for integrating generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in K‐12 education.
rationale: The study is a survey of in-service STEM teachers' perceptions and familiarity, with no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. It is not an empirical intervention study eligible under the protocol. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is applied as the first failing criterion in the ordering; E1 would also apply since there is no learner-facing intervention, but the survey design is the primary issue. Abstract gives positive evidence of survey design.

quote: by combining modern embedding models with powerful unsupervised clustering methods, we were able to group student solutions into remarkably well-defined clusters
rationale: The study uses LLM embeddings as an analysis tool on student code submissions to cluster solutions. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). The design is unsupervised clustering analysis with no control group and no learning outcome measured, so the comparison, design, and outcome criteria also fail. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract that the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

quote: An exploratory qualitative research design was employed. A focus group interview was conducted with five female first-year undergraduate students
rationale: Qualitative focus-group study with five students and no control group or quantitative learning outcome. Not an empirical comparative study eligible under the protocol. quote: The proposed approach is studied on two examples. The study showed that the use of Arduino platforms in combination with the Excel Data Streamer data streaming tool makes it possible to create measuring complexes accessible to a wide range of teachers and students
rationale: The abstract describes an approach for creating measuring complexes with ChatGPT-generated code, studied on two examples. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is present, so exclusion under E3 is applied at abstract stage, with the caveat that ChatGPT here is used to write code (arguably by teachers/researchers rather than learners), which could alternatively be E1.

quote: This study examined the operationalization of GenAI within child-focused pedagogy and assessed teacher perspectives on its efficacy.
rationale: The abstract describes a case study of three classrooms using GenAI in STEM projects, with videotaped observations, interviews, and artifacts. The design is also a case study, and the outcomes are teacher perspectives and observations rather than a quantitative learning measure. Under the code order, E3 is the first applicable code. Exclusion is positive evidence based on the abstract's description of the design.

quote: This research aims to understand undergraduate business students’ Generative AI (GenAI) usage and perception by analyzing survey data collected in August 2024 and January 2025.
rationale: The record is a survey study of business students' GenAI usage and perceptions. It is not an experiment or quasi-experiment, has no control group, and reports no learning outcome. Business content is not clearly within the STEM domain. Excluded as a non-empirical-learning design under E6 (survey design, not an eligible empirical study); the primary failure is design and outcome, and the survey design is not one of the protocol's included designs.

quote: This study introduces a methodological framework for instructor-designed generative AI in dental hygiene education, aiming to establish a theoretical structure that supports self-regulated learning (SRL)
rationale: The record describes a conceptual/methodological framework with design principles and a proposed model. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome data. Dental hygiene education is also a health professions domain, which falls under the protocol's domain exclusion. The primary exclusion is E6 (not an empirical study), as the paper is a conceptual framework proposal.

quote: The article analyzes the data from a survey conducted in 2025 among students enrolled in programs for highly qualified personnel

Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study design eligible under the protocol's design criteria). Note: the protocol's design exclusions list correlational and survey designs; E6 is the closest available code. Domain is also not STEM (publishing practices). quote: Using a quasi-experimental approach, two high school classes of students from China were divided into an experimental class (N = 40) and a control class (N = 40).
rationale: At abstract stage, the study appears to meet all criteria: a quasi-experiment with a traditional-teaching control class, high school students, physics (STEM), a generative AI-based chatbot as part of the intervention, and measured scientific reasoning/modeling/questioning outcomes. Publication year 2025 meets the date rule. Data sufficiency for SMD and the journal-article type cannot be confirmed from the abstract, but no positive evidence of failure is present, so it advances to full text.

quote: We provide an example application using GPT-4, observing a range of precision and recall scores depending on the topic and experimental setup
rationale: The study is a benchmark dataset evaluating GPT-4's ability to detect misconceptions (precision/recall), not a learner-facing intervention with a control group. There is no comparison group and no learning outcome measured in students. Excluded at the abstract stage on positive evidence: no learner interaction with generative AI and no quantitative learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), since the GPT-4 use is a model evaluation rather than learner interaction; I am recording E1 as the first applicable code.

quote: A quantitative cross-sectional research design was adopted.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey with regression analysis of self-reported generative AI usage. There is no control group that avoids generative AI and no experimental assignment, so the comparison and design criteria fail. Exclusion code E3 is used as the first applicable code in the protocol's order. Note that the code order places E1 and E2 before E3; the abstract does not give enough detail to confirm those, but E3 is clearly evidenced here. Outcomes are self-reported and the domain is not stated as STEM.

quote: Results revealed a significant group effect on posttest attitude scores, F(2,129) = 27.630, p < .001, partial η² = .300.
rationale: The only outcome is attitudes toward calculus measured with the Calculus Attitude Questionnaire. Affective outcomes are not extracted for any study under the protocol, and no quantitative learning outcome (achievement, conceptual knowledge, problem solving, skill) is reported. Other criteria appear met: ChatGPT-enriched intervention, conventional-teaching control, quasi-experimental design, preservice mathematics teachers (higher education), and calculus as STEM content. Excluded at E5 as the first applicable code.
decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that the outcome is affective only.

quote: Survey data from 189 students with varying levels of LLM use in educational and coding-related contexts were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM).
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey analyzed with PLS-SEM, not a randomized or quasi-experiment with a control group that lacks generative AI. Outcomes are self-reported perceived competence, not a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code in the order given; the design also fails the Design criterion and the outcome is perception-based (E5 would also apply), but E3 is reported as the first applicable code per the ordering. Positive evidence of failure is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

The study concerns English pronunciation for vocational students in an A1 English course. English language learning is explicitly excluded from the STEM domain, so E2 applies at the first failing criterion. Other criteria (whether the chatbot is generative, and the control group) are not needed to decide. Abstract stage exclusion is justified because the content is clearly non-STEM language learning.

quote: This study determined the levels of learning satisfaction of nursing students in selected higher education institutions (HEIs) in Sulu with the use of Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer (ChatGPT)
rationale: The abstract describes a satisfaction survey (Likert-scale perceptions) of nursing students using ChatGPT. The domain is nursing, which is a health professions field, not STEM, and there is no control group, so the comparison and design criteria also appear unmet. Exclusion is based on E5 as the first clearly applicable code in order; the abstract gives positive evidence the outcome fails.

quote: Maker Education, which combines hands-on projects with STEAM content (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics)
rationale: The study concerns CLIL language learning integrated with Maker Education. The protocol excludes language learning and other non-STEM content. The abstract gives no generative AI intervention, and the focus is language learning with maker projects, so it fails on content (E2). Generative AI is only mentioned as background concern. Only a title, venue, and year are available; there is no abstract. The title suggests a comparison of students with GPT-3.5 and Gemini on SBA (situational judgement/single best answer) items, which may be medical education rather than STEM and may not have a non-AI control group. Nothing in the record gives positive evidence of a failed criterion, so the record is passed to full-text screening rather than excluded. Year 2024 satisfies the date criterion.

quote: This paper introduces the leapfrogging effect hypothesis, proposing that generative AI significantly expands students’ Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD)
rationale: The paper is a theoretical/conceptual argument ("introduces a hypothesis", "argues", "advocates"). It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6).

quote: generation of the task bank took about hours instead of the typical several days
rationale: The generative AI (LLM) is used by teachers to produce assessment tasks, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails (E1 would be the first applicable code under the protocol order). However, the protocol order requires reporting the first applicable code; E1 is checked first. Note: the abstract shows AI used to generate test items for the instructor's assessment fund, with no control group comparison described, and no quantitative learning outcome against a comparison. Given the first-applicable-code rule, E1 is the correct code: generative AI is used only by instructors to prepare materials. Decision is exclude at abstract stage on positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing.

quote: The study is based on data from representative questionnaires of students of technical universities in Russia (KGEU, SSU, Bauman Moscow State Technical University) conducted by Drach and Torkunova (2025)
rationale: The record is a theoretical/review-style synthesis built on questionnaire data and secondary results from other studies. It reports no experimental comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical comparative study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); the design criterion also fails since the data are correlational/survey-based.

Abstract describes a survey-based latent profile analysis of motivational appraisals (enjoyment, pressure, choice, competence, value) about chatbot use among upper secondary maths students. No control group or experimental comparison; the gender comparison is of profile prevalence. Design is correlational/survey and outcomes are perceptions/affect, not a quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI), the first applicable code in order that is positively evidenced; the design (E6-type survey) also fails. Per protocol order, E3 is reported first since there is no comparison group. No quote supports a control group; the abstract's described design is a questionnaire study.

quote: Using thematic analysis, survey responses from teachers across two suburban public school districts were examined.
rationale: The study is a survey-based thematic analysis of in-service K-12 teachers' use of generative AI. It has no learner-facing intervention, no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no experimental design. It is not an empirical study with eligible design; it is a survey/qualitative study, so E6 applies as the first code that fits. Teachers are also not students (E4), but E1 is the first applicable code in order since AI use is teacher-only (E1 applies first per the ordering rule).
decision_note: Exclusion code should be E1 by order: AI used only by teachers to plan materials is not learner-facing.

quote: employ a quantitative approach by conducting pre- and post-course surveys to measure changes in students' knowledge, skills, and attitudes across approximately 1,000 undergraduates
rationale: The abstract describes a pre-post survey of one group of undergraduates with no mention of a control group that does not use generative AI, which is positive evidence of a failed comparison criterion (single-group pre-post design). Content is a general digital skills course on generative AI, not clearly STEM, and outcomes are largely self-reported knowledge/attitudes. Excluded on E3 as the first applicable code in the order given; the design criterion also appears not met.

quote: The research surveyed 300 educators and 1,000 students, supplemented by interviews and focus group discussions.
rationale: The abstract describes a mixed-methods survey, interviews and focus groups, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The claim that ChatGPT 'significantly enhances' understanding rests on perception-based survey data, not a comparative experiment. Under the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E1 (intervention) and E2 (domain) are not clearly failed, E3 (no control group) is positive evidence from the design description, but the design itself is non-empirical-experimental; I select E6 as the primary code because the study is survey/qualitative and not an empirical comparative study. Exclusion is supported by positive abstract evidence of survey-based design without a control group.

quote: Thirty-two undergraduate students at Sultan Qaboos University were divided into experimental and control groups.
rationale: At abstract stage, no positive evidence of failure. Learners use GenAI within a structured programming assignment approach; control group used GenAI without restrictions, which is a generative-AI control, so the comparison requirement (separate group without generative AI) is not clearly met. This is a positive signal of possible E3, but the abstract is ambiguous about whether the control is truly without GenAI, so I cannot exclude at this stage. Experimental vs control on programming assessments with p-value suggests quantitative outcome. Publication type and full-text data sufficiency to be checked at full text. Journal publication year 2026 meets date criterion.

rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive mixed-methods study using questionnaires and interviews with 98 students. quote: Large Language Models (LLMs), such as GPT-4, to automate content generation

quote: The results of this research suggest that using ChatGPT in the process of teaching mathematics can provide a range of benefits, including personalized learning, increased engagement, and improved outcomes.

Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record advances to full text for checking comparison, design, and outcome.

quote: This study reviews literature on how structured GenAI prompting frameworks can improve the quality, accuracy and ethical grounding of AI-generated feedback in large accounting classes. Using PRISMA 2020 guideline, 26 reviewed articles were extracted from Scopus and ScienceDirect.
rationale: The record is a literature review (PRISMA, 26 reviewed articles) that proposes a framework and template. It is not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. Accounting is also not a protocol STEM domain. Excluded on E6 as not an empirical study, the first applicable code in order.
rationale_extra: Domain: accounting is not listed in the protocol's STEM domains, which would be a further failure, but E6 is applied first in the code order.

Publication date 2026 is within the window and the venue is a journal article. Effect-size data are not visible in the abstract, so that is left to full text. rationale: The study is about English speaking skills, which is language learning and not STEM, so E2 applies as the first failing code in order. quote: A 30-item cross-sectional email-based survey was distributed at two US medical schools.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of medical students reporting perceptions and self-reported usage. quote: Although direct trials involving students were deliberately avoided, the platform's technical feasibility was validated through multidimensional benchmarking against established models
rationale: The study is a technical benchmarking of a Llama 3 system against BERT-base and GPT-2 models, with no student participants and no learner outcome. quote: The results show that the browser extension is feasible to use and can provide personalized explanations, potentially enhancing students' comprehension of academic terminology during independent study.
rationale: The abstract describes an R&D study with software development and white-box/black-box functional testing of a browser extension using an LLM. quote: In this conceptual paper we build on Blackie's work on knowledge-building and assessment practices
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual paper with no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. quote: Experimental results based on the effectiveness of undergraduate courses show that students spend less time debugging code in the course, the accuracy of solutions is improved

rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of knowledge, attitudes, and practices about ChatGPT. It has no learner interaction with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is a survey design, so it fails the design criterion. The first applicable exclusion code is E1 in strict order, but the abstract gives positive evidence that the study is a non-empirical-learning survey; I report E6 as the closest fit for a survey without a learning intervention or comparison. Note that the code order means a reviewer may prefer E1 or E3 instead; the design failure is the most direct reason.

quote: The study employs a cross-sectional quantitative design to examine the relationships between SDL, AL, and CT in the context of adult learners' use of GenAI tools like ChatGPT.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey of perceptions (281 survey responses) with SEM and ANOVA. There is no control group comparing GenAI use to non-AI use, and the outcomes (self-directed learning, active learning, critical thinking) are perceived and self-reported rather than quantitative learning measures. Exclusion is based on positive evidence: the design is correlational/survey, so there is no comparison group (E3 would also apply), but the first applicable code in order is E5 because outcomes are perceptions only. Under the abstract-stage rule this is a clear exclusion on the design and outcome criteria.

quote: Sections were randomly assigned to treatment (engagement with the learning modules between pre- and post-tests) or control (no learning modules between assessments).
rationale: Randomized experiment with a no-module control group, undergraduate and graduate students, and pre/post knowledge and skill measures. The abstract does not state whether the modules involve learner interaction with a generative AI tool (they teach genAI competency, with practice and feedback), and it does not establish a STEM content domain (genAI literacy, prompt engineering, and fact-checking are not clearly STEM). Missing information is not grounds for exclusion at abstract stage, so this is unsure pending full text. Publication type and language are not assessable from the abstract.

Abstract describes an R&D (ADDIE) development study with expert validation and practicality questionnaires on 6 students. There is no comparison group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are validity and practicality ratings. The study is not an empirical comparative design, so it fails the design, comparison and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is used as the primary code under the protocol's order, though the more precise reason is absence of a control group (E3) and no learning outcome (E5). Abstract-stage evidence is positive enough to exclude.

quote: The objective of this study was to assess the perceptions of these students regarding the use of generative AI in their reflective reports over the course of two academic years.
rationale: The study compares two annual cohorts (2023 vs 2024) on Likert-scale perceptions and preference proportions. Outcomes are affective/perception-based only, with no quantitative learning measure, so E5 applies. The design is a cohort comparison with no separate non-generative-AI control group, which would also fail E3. Domain (reflective art-based reports in medical education) is not clearly STEM. Exclusion under E5 as the first applicable code in the protocol order is reasonable at the abstract stage given the abstract's clear positive evidence of perception-only outcomes.

quote: Data were collected via a Google Forms-based survey using Likert-scale items
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional perception survey of students (perceived impact of ChatGPT, Grammarly, QuillBot) with one-way ANOVA across disciplines and no control group receiving a non-generative-AI condition. There is no quantitative learning outcome; the measures are self-perceptions. Exclusion E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). Design also lacks a comparison group (E3 could be argued), but the first applicable code in order is E5... Note: E3 precedes E5 in order, and the absence of a control group without generative AI is positively indicated by the survey design, so the first applicable code is E3.

quote: Then, in this Scoping Review (ScR) based on 146 studies retrieved from the databases SCOPUS, Web of Science (WoS), and ERIC
rationale: The record is a scoping review of 146 studies, not an empirical study. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). The protocol also excludes reviews under publication type, but E6 is the code that applies to this record.

quote: Employing a qualitative phenomenological approach, this study involved eight teachers utilizing platforms such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Canva AI.
rationale: The study is a qualitative phenomenological inquiry of eight in-service secondary school teachers. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and participants are teachers rather than learners. It is not an empirical quantitative study meeting the protocol design, so it fails on E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense). Population (in-service teachers) and outcome also fail, but the first applicable code in order is E1 check: the intervention is teacher-use, not learner-facing, which would be E1 earlier in the order. Given code order, the first applicable code is E1 because AI was used by teachers for their own planning, not as a learner-facing learning activity.

quote: Students in the AI-assisted group demonstrated significantly higher accuracy compared to the traditional group
rationale: At abstract stage, the study appears to meet all criteria: ChatGPT (generative AI) used by undergraduate students in a mathematics task (sum to infinity of a geometric series), randomized two-group design with a traditional-resources control, and a quantitative accuracy outcome, published 2025. Effect-size statistics, language, and publication type (journal vs. other) cannot be verified from the abstract, so no exclusion is warranted; the record advances to full text for those checks.

quote: A structured questionnaire was administered to 53 diploma students.
rationale: The study is a single questionnaire survey of student perceptions and awareness of AI in chemistry learning. There is no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions and behavioural intentions only, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). Although the design is survey-based (which would also fail the design criterion), E5 is the first applicable code in the order given for an outcome failure. Abstract-stage evidence is positive for the failure, so exclusion is appropriate.

quote: A cross-sectional survey design was employed with 214 mathematics lecturers from 49 public Colleges of Education in Ghana.
rationale: Cross-sectional survey of mathematics lecturers with no learner intervention or control group; no learning outcome measured. Design is a survey, not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Participants are teachers/lecturers rather than students, and the study measures readiness and self-reported integration. Exclusion coded E3 as the first criterion failing that is clearly positive per the abstract (no control group without generative AI). Note that E6 (not an empirical study) does not apply since this is empirical survey work.

Abstract describes LLM use by journalism bachelor's students in a "Modern Information Technologies" course and the content is media/text processing, not STEM (protocol Domain excludes non-STEM content). Also the abstract gives no evidence of a control group without generative AI (single experiment with chi-squared on qualitative changes), but the domain failure is the first applicable code in order. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of non-STEM content.

Record is a bibliometric analysis (per title) of AI and machine learning approaches for predicting student achievement. Bibliometric analysis is not an empirical study of learner interaction with generative AI, and predictive analytics is excluded by protocol. No abstract is available. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); the title alone gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design. Note the protocol's intervention exclusion for predictive analytics would also apply.

quote: Data were collected via a survey of 1101 German secondary students
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of resource use among German secondary students. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Generative AI is mentioned only as one resource students might access. Under the E1-first ordering, the intervention criterion also fails, but the design is a survey, which is non-empirical-experimental; the first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI). Note: strictly applying the order, E1 applies first, so the code should be E1.

quote: "Survey data was triangulated with the learners' emotional responses towards the combination of three AI feedback types"
rationale: Generative AI chatbot feedback to engineering students (population and intervention plausibly met). However, the outcome is emotional responses (affective), and the abstract reports survey-based data with no learning measure. Affective outcomes are not extracted under the protocol, so no quantitative learning outcome exists. Exclude under E5. Comparison group and design are not described in the abstract, but the outcome failure is sufficient.

quote: Using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses framework, this study reviewed 79 peer-reviewed articles
rationale: This is a systematic review of 79 articles (PRISMA), not an empirical study. It has no control group, no learner-facing intervention evaluated, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order that is positively evidenced at abstract stage. Stage is abstract-level; the review nature is explicit.

quote: We then share our findings from a year of design-based implementation research during the 2023–2024 academic year.
rationale: The abstract describes a design-based implementation study with framework discussion and emerging best practices, with no mention of a control group, comparison condition, or quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of a failing criterion is needed at abstract stage, but the abstract's framing (design framework, instructional resources, best practices, future directions) reads as a descriptive/design paper rather than a comparative empirical experiment. Coding E6 (not an empirical study) is a judgment that may be overturned at full text; the cleaner reading under rule 2 would be unsure, since the abstract does not explicitly show absence of a control group. I am flagging this as exclude per E6 with low confidence and recommend the full-text reviewer verify it.

quote: Virtual patient simulations using social robotics combined with large language models for clinical reasoning training in medical education
rationale: Participants are medical students completing clinical reasoning training with virtual patients. Health professions education is explicitly excluded from the Domain criterion, so the study fails on domain (clinical medicine, not STEM content). Medical students are higher education students, so population is not the failing point; the domain failure is the decisive reason. Code E2 (content not STEM) is the applicable code. Correction: the first applicable code in order is E2 since E1 is not clearly failing at abstract stage, so I report E2 as the decision basis.

quote: This editor's introduction provides an overview of the interdisciplinary goals for an ongoing series in Critical AI devoted to the topic of “Generative AI” and writing in higher education.
rationale: The record is an editor's introduction to a journal issue, not an empirical study. It presents critical assumptions and summarizes articles, with no intervention, control group, or quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Publication type (editorial) also falls outside eligibility (E10 could apply), but E6 is the first applicable code in order and is used here.

quote: The questionnaire was filled out by 70 EFL teachers.
rationale: The study surveys in-service EFL teachers about perceptions and intention to use ChatGPT (TAM questionnaire). This is a survey design with no learner-facing intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and English language teaching rather than STEM. Abstract gives positive evidence of failure on outcome (perceptions only) and population (in-service teachers). Under the code order, E1 (not learner-facing) would be the first applicable code since teachers are the users, but the abstract does not clearly show learner interaction. Excluding at E1 is the first applicable code, so I use E1 instead of E5.

quote: This review examines the ethical incorporation of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in higher education
rationale: The record is a review/conceptual paper drawing on institutional case studies and expert testimony, with no empirical comparison group or quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). It is also not STEM-specific. Per the abstract, no experimental design is described, so E6 is the first applicable code in protocol order given the review nature.
rationale_note: Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that it is a review.

quote: The findings indicate that 72% of surveyed students utilize GenAI on a weekly basis
rationale: Survey study of GenAI usage and perceptions among secondary students; there is no intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome measured. Positive evidence of failing the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code in protocol order for the design/comparison failure; the study is also a survey without a learning outcome (E5 would apply under a strict reading). Coded E3 as the first failing criterion among the protocol's code ordering with the intervention not evaluated.

quote: We used a dataset of student-written text in comparison with LLM-written text.
rationale: The study is a machine learning classifier that detects whether text was written by humans or by LLMs. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). No learner-facing generative AI, no control group receiving a learning comparison, and no learning outcome are described. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: The solutions to the problem as well as the class proposals built by both teachers and chatbots were compared in terms of a number of proposed categories
rationale: At abstract stage there is positive evidence of failure. The study compares outputs of in-service teachers and chatbots (productions, solutions, class proposals) rather than learners' quantitative learning outcomes after an intervention. No learner-facing intervention or control group is described, and the population is in-service teachers, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion code E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first applicable code in the order given, since the study is not a learner-outcome study. The population concern (E4) is also present but E5 is reported as the primary code given the protocol order. Note that E1 could arguably apply first; the abstract does not indicate learners interacting with GenAI, so E1 is not asserted outright.

quote: This exploratory study analyzes the institutional strategies adopted for the integration of generative artificial intelligence (generative AI) in leading universities
rationale: The study is a documentary analysis of institutional policies from 15 universities, not an empirical learning study. It has no learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in the order given, since E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract and the design is clearly non-experimental.

quote: In this paper, we focus on the qualitative analysis of three key stages experienced by the teachers
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative analysis of prompts, responses, and reflections of 15 pre-service teachers, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E5 is applied as the first code that clearly fails on the abstract's evidence. The design is qualitative and no comparison group is mentioned, so the design criterion also appears unmet. Under the abstract-stage rule this is positive evidence of failure, so exclusion is appropriate.

quote: A one-group pretest-posttest experimental design, the experiment involved 58 university students
rationale: The study uses a one-group pretest-posttest design with no separate control group without generative AI, which fails the comparison and design criteria. This is a positive abstract-stage signal of E3 (single group pre-post), so the record is excluded. Other criteria appear met: ChatGPT-integrated programming environment, university students, web programming, and learning performance outcomes.

quote: the study employed a single-group pre-test–post-test quantitative design with 32 undergraduate students
rationale: The abstract explicitly describes a single-group pre-test–post-test design with no control or comparison group, which the protocol excludes under E3 (and the design criterion is not met). Financial literacy is also arguably non-STEM, but E3 is the first applicable code in order of the protocol's listed sequence given the design failure is positively evidenced. Note: E2 is checked before E3 in the code order; financial literacy is not clearly STEM from the abstract, so the domain judgment is uncertain, but the design failure is unambiguous.

quote: Singapore secondary school students were surveyed on their perceptions on completing a computing task with a GenAI Chatbot.
rationale: The study is a survey of perceptions (TAM constructs) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Outcomes are perceptions and intentions only, which the protocol excludes. Excluded at abstract stage on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome); the design also lacks a comparison group, which would independently fail the criteria.
rationale_note: Positive evidence is clear from the abstract.

quote: Higher education students trust and use of ChatGPT: empirical evidence
rationale: The abstract is a publisher boilerplate and does not describe the study design, comparison group, domain, or outcomes. The title suggests higher education students and ChatGPT (generative AI), but it reports trust and use, which points toward perception/usage outcomes and a survey-type design. No positive evidence of a failed criterion appears in the abstract, so the record is passed to full text to check for a control group, STEM content, and a quantitative learning outcome.

Abstract describes engineering drawing (STEM) taught with AI including an LLM, and students' spatial and drawing skills are mentioned as strengthened. However, the abstract does not state whether there is a control group, whether the design is randomized or quasi-experimental, or whether a quantitative outcome with extractable statistics was collected. It reads as a review or summary of implementation effects, so design and comparison cannot be confirmed as met. Missing information is not evidence of failure at abstract stage, so the record is passed to full text.

quote: The research instruments were two questionnaires.
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey using two questionnaires on current and desired situations and needs for AI use. There is no control group, no experimental comparison, and no learning outcome measured. Survey designs and perception-only measures fail the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Under the protocol's exclusion codes, the first applicable code is E3 (no control group without generative AI), so it is coded E3. The STEM domain is also not clear from the abstract.

quote: The study employed a 2 (student status: domestic vs. international EFL) x 2 (inoculation status: inoculated vs. non-inoculated) x 2 (time: pre-test vs. post-test) mixed factorial design.
rationale: Abstract suggests a comparison between inoculated and non-inoculated students, which may be a control group, and the population is higher education students (EFL students, domestic students). However, the abstract does not clearly establish whether the intervention is learner-facing generative AI use within a learning activity (the inoculation message is about ChatGPT, and tasks include academic-source summaries and math problems), whether the outcome is a quantitative learning measure (verification behavior and intentions may be behavioral/affective rather than learning achievement), or whether SMD data are available. Math problem verification is STEM-adjacent. No positive evidence of exclusion is present, so the record is advanced for full-text review.

quote: "80 teachers of public schools in Ma'an Governorate, Jordan were used."
rationale: The participants are in-service public school teachers receiving professional development, which the protocol excludes (population: in-service teachers are not students). The abstract gives positive evidence of this failure, so exclusion under E4 is made at the abstract stage. Intervention, domain, and outcome are not clearly assessable from the abstract but do not need to be resolved given the population exclusion.

quote: we conducted a study to examine the extent to which GPT models hold the potential to advance the existing knowledge of LA-supported feedback systems
rationale: At abstract stage, the study compares GPT-generated feedback against human instructors' feedback on student writing, rated for readability, effectiveness, and reliability. It is an evaluation of feedback text quality, not a learner-facing intervention with a learning outcome measured in students. No student learning outcome or control group of learners is described. Exclude under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome); the feedback-quality ratings are not learning measures. Design is an evaluation study with no randomized or quasi-experimental learner comparison. Given the abstract, positive evidence exists that the outcome is not a learning measure, so exclusion is supported.

quote: we share our exploratory interactions with ChatGPT relevant to issues of plagiarism and academic integrity, hoping to shed light on how writing instructors can use the tool
rationale: The record is about academic writing and academic integrity, not STEM content, so it fails the domain criterion (E2). It also describes exploratory interactions with no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and an essay-style piece rather than an empirical study. E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order for the abstract-stage evidence; the abstract gives clear positive evidence that the content is writing/ethics rather than STEM.

quote: GAMAI enables teachers to effortlessly apply storytelling to describe a gamified scenario
