rationale: The LLM-based tool (GAMAI) is used by teachers to author gamified programming exercises, not as a learner-facing tool within a learning activity. Per protocol, AI used only by the teacher to prepare materials is E1. The abstract reports student positive assessments but no controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion on E1 is applied since the abstract gives positive evidence the intervention is teacher-facing.

quote: A quasi-experimental design was employed, dividing participants into two groups: a control group utilizing traditional scaffolding methods and an experimental group integrating GAI tools alongside scaffolding techniques.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study is a quasi-experiment with a control group using traditional scaffolding (no GAI), in programming courses for first-year university students. Outcomes include coursework performance and final project scores, which appear to be quantitative learning measures. Tools named (Kahoot!, Slido, NotebookLM, VS Code) are not explicitly described as generative in the abstract, though GAI is stated as the category; the generative nature is plausibly met. Data sufficiency for SMD cannot be judged from the abstract. No positive evidence of exclusion, so include for full-text check.

The study concerns EFL (English as a foreign language) learning, which is non-STEM content, so E2 applies first in the order. It is also a descriptive-correlational questionnaire study with no control group and no learning outcome measure, which would fail E3, E5, and the design criteria. Excluding on E2 as the first applicable code; the abstract's EFL framing is positive evidence of non-STEM content.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: Utilizing a systematic literature review following PRISMA guidelines, the research identifies current trends and practical applications of AI in physics education.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review plus personal experience and an interview, not an empirical controlled study. It has no separate control group and no quantitative learning outcome data. Reviews are not empirical studies, so E6 applies. The protocol's ordering would place E1 and E2 first only if they clearly failed; the abstract gives no positive evidence for those, and E6 is the first clear failure in order of applicability.

quote: The article reports on a case study of an early-adopter classroom writing experiment utilizing generative AI
rationale: The abstract describes a case study with reflections and student feedback via survey and video statements. There is no separate control group that avoids generative AI, and the outcomes are perceptions rather than quantitative learning measures. Positive evidence of failing comparison, design, and outcome criteria is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified. E3 is the first applicable code in order given no control group; E5 would also apply.

quote: The work is of a review and analytical nature and can serve as a starting point for further research in the field of digitalization of educational assessment and integration of LLM into the educational process.
rationale: The abstract describes the work as review and analytical, with a qualitative analysis of ChatGPT outputs compared with teacher assessments. It has no learner-facing AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical experimental study, so E6 applies. The quote is taken from the abstract and supports the review nature of the work. Quote is verbatim, but the criteria field was filled as a string summary rather than a structured value.

quote: We observe varied approaches among students and point to further research needed regarding how to teach students to integrate AI tools in their modelling practices.
rationale: The abstract describes a preliminary observational analysis of students' engagement with a modelling activity. It reports no comparison group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. This points to a non-experimental, descriptive study, so it fails the design and outcome criteria and is not an empirical experimental study. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code, with the caveat that the abstract is sparse and the full text could clarify the design.

quote: The objective of this work was to assess students' perceptions of the widely diffused chatbot ChatGPT and its use as a learning tool.
rationale: The abstract describes students' perceptions and satisfaction with ChatGPT in a repeated cross-sectional study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of failure exists on outcome (perceptions only, which are excluded) and design (no comparison group described). Per the protocol, perceptions-only studies fail the outcome criterion, so E5 applies. Note the design also appears to lack a control group, which would be E3 if coded first, but the ordering rule points to E5 only when E1-E4 do not apply; E1 and E2 are not triggered, and E3 is not positively evidenced in the abstract, so E5 is the first code with positive evidence.

Menu planning in dietetic training is not STEM content (health/nutrition education falls under health professions, excluded by the protocol). The outcome is anxiety, an affective measure that the protocol does not extract, and the design appears to be a pre-post survey without a non-AI control group (E3 also plausible). Exclusion uses E2 as the first applicable code in protocol order for the domain failure.

quote: A quasi-experimental design was employed, involving 59 fifth-grade students from a primary school in northern Taiwan.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study appears to be a quasi-experiment with a control group receiving traditional instruction, with learners analyzing GPT-4 solutions (generative AI, learner-facing via error analysis activity). Mathematics domain, K-12 population (fifth graders), quantitative tests and confidence scale outcomes, published 2024. Whether the SMD can be computed and whether the intervention involves learners interacting with GPT-4 directly (versus only reviewing its outputs) can be resolved at full text. No positive evidence of failure, so include.

quote: Chatbot users achieved higher essay scores than non-users.
rationale: Abstract reports university students using a genAI chatbot (ChatGPT) during a reading and essay task, with quantitative performance measures (essay scores, knowledge and transfer tests). Chatbot users versus non-users comparison is mentioned, but the abstract does not state whether a randomized or quasi-experimental control group without genAI exists; it describes an exploratory study with trace-based analysis, so the design may be observational. The domain (reading/essay writing) is not clearly STEM. These points cannot be resolved from the abstract, so the record is passed to full text.

quote: Using screen recording software, we recorded the writing process of 40 mostly French-speaking students when they produced a 300-word essay in English.
rationale: The study concerns L2 (English) essay writing with GenAI tools, which is language learning and non-STEM content. It is also a descriptive, observational study of writing processes with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E2 (content not STEM). Also a presentation abstract with no evidence of a journal article.

quote: A mixed-methods design was employed with 98 middle school students. Quantitative data were collected through pre and post-tests
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pre-post design with pre and post-tests and no control group; per protocol, single-group pre-post designs fail the comparison criterion (E3). Intervention (ChatGPT for learners) and middle school population are met; STEM content is plausible (computational thinking, data literacy) but not needed for the decision.

quote: A quantitative correlational research design was employed, involving 273 undergraduate students from three teacher education programs.
rationale: The study is a correlational, self-report questionnaire design (PLS-SEM) with no control group, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. Its measured constructs (computational thinking, deep learning skills, AI use) are not a quantitative learning outcome after an intervention. Under the code order, E1 and E2 are not clearly failed from the abstract, but E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the clearest positive failure. Exclusion is based on the abstract's correlational, survey-based design; the abstract gives no evidence of a learner-facing intervention with a control group.

quote: This paper harnessed the experiences of using LLM (AI code generating tools) for teaching and learning computer programming at the introductory level
rationale: The abstract describes a position/review paper that draws on experiences, existing literature, position papers and workshops, and offers recommendations. It reports no experimental design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Exclusion is based on positive evidence from the abstract that the paper is a non-empirical review/position piece.

Abstract describes an LLM-based tutoring system for primary (Grade 5) mathematics word problems, which meets intervention, population and domain criteria. However, the abstract does not state whether there is a control group without generative AI; it reports simulated dialogues and a classroom pilot of 40 students, and mentions outcomes like interactional consistency and engagement without clear quantitative learning measures. Comparison, design, and outcome are unclear, so the record is passed to full text.

quote: Employing GPT-4o, a total of 321 distractors were generated based on five error types
rationale: The LLM (GPT-4o) is used to generate test distractors for item banks, not as a tool that learners interact with during a learning activity. No control group, no learner outcome measured. Excluded under E1 as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. Design is a content-generation study, not an experiment.

decision_note: Umbrella review, not an empirical study.
rationale: The record is an umbrella review of 11 included reviews, not a primary empirical study with its own learner-level comparison group. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Its evidence comes from secondary synthesis, so no primary experiment is eligible. Although the review also falls under publication-type concerns, E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order for this design.

quote: This study explores Korean physics educators' perceptions of the educational use of ChatGPT and future changes in society and the educational environment.
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of physics educators' perceptions (semi-structured interviews, consensus qualitative analysis). It is not an empirical experiment with a control group and has no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible designs); it also fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Under the first-applicable-code rule, E1 is not clearly positive from the abstract since the intervention is not learner-facing use, so E6 is the best-fitting first code.

quote: The sample consisted of 200 teachers from public and private institutions in Zone 6 of the Ministry of Education, who participated through online surveys.
rationale: Participants are in-service teachers surveyed online, not K-12 or higher education students (E4). The study is survey-based with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; it is also about curriculum planning rather than learner-facing use. Positive evidence of population failure is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified. Coded E4 as the first applicable code in protocol order would be E1 only if learner-facing use were clearly absent; the teacher-only use is also grounds for E1, but the population failure is the clearest and is stated explicitly.

The abstract describes ChatGPT generating assessment tasks for instructors. It reports no comparison group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no learning outcome measured in learners. The teacher-only use suggests E1 as well, but the protocol requires exactly one code. Using the first applicable code in order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing) applies before E3. Correction: the first applicable code is E1, so the exclusion should be E1 rather than E3.

criteria.domain_note: Dental/health professions education on infective endocarditis prophylaxis

quote: The use of large language models (LLMs) in healthcare is expanding.
rationale: The content is infective endocarditis prophylaxis in dental procedures, which is health professions education and therefore not STEM under the protocol's domain exclusion. The study is also a model-benchmarking evaluation with a pilot comparing LLM-assisted versus unaided answering, with no clear separate non-generative-AI control group described in the abstract. Excluded on E2 as the first applicable code in order.

quote: It analyzes opportunities such as enhanced learning efficiency and assistance in complex tasks, alongside severe challenges like academic integrity crises, deviations in students' skill development, and dilemmas in adapting teaching methods.
rationale: The abstract describes a discussion/analysis paper on GAI in university programming courses. It gives no indication of a controlled comparison group, an experimental design, or a quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of failure on design/comparison/outcome is not explicit in the abstract, so it cannot be excluded at this stage; it appears to be a non-empirical review-style paper, which would likely be E6 at full text. Advancing as unsure for full-text check.

quote: The ability and pedagogical potential of ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Claude AI to create study notes and practice questions were evaluated
rationale: The abstract describes an evaluation of three generative AI tools' outputs against each other (comparisons of AI variants) with no non-generative-AI control group and no learner-facing learning outcome; the study appears to assess AI-generated study materials quality rather than learners' learning. Positive evidence of missing control group supports E3 at abstract stage.

quote: a comparison group (learner-centered instruction) and an experimental group (AI-assisted collaborative learning) were formed with 49 undergraduate students
rationale: Abstract describes a comparison group and an experimental group using generative AI tools with undergraduates, so intervention, comparison, and population appear met. However, the course is a general education creativity course (Creativity and Future Problem Solving), which is not clearly STEM content. Outcomes are analyzed mainly by qualitative content analysis of creative products and reflection journals, and it is unclear whether any quantitative learning outcome or SMD-computable data exist. Reserving judgment for full text to check domain, quantitative outcomes, and design.

quote: This study developed and validated a novel scale, grounded in the Interactive‐Constructive‐Active‐Passive (ICAP) framework, to measure the integration of GenAI in academic research by graduate students.
rationale: Psychometric scale development study using survey data from 1216 graduate students. It has no experimental or comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical intervention study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study of the protocol's design type); it also fails the design and outcome criteria. Note that E6 is applied as the closest code, since the record is a survey-based validation rather than an intervention study.

quote: Using a sequential mixed-methods and cross-over quasi-experimental design, quantitative analyses showed improvements in self-efficacy, motivation, higher-order thinking, collaboration, learning experience, satisfaction, and project performance.
rationale: Abstract describes a generative AI (GAI) scaffold used by learners in a flipped model, and a quasi-experimental design with project performance and higher-order thinking outcomes, so no abstract-level exclusion is evident. However, the comparison group is not stated (a cross-over design may lack a clean non-AI control), the subject domain is not named (flipped higher-education course, possibly non-STEM), and the abstract mentions affective outcomes (self-efficacy, motivation, satisfaction) that are not to be extracted. These need full-text verification.

quote: Pre- and post-experiment questionnaires were administered to examine the impact of ChatGPT on students' perceptions of progress and sense of agency.
rationale: The study examines student perceptions and sense of agency using pre/post questionnaires in a single translation course cohort, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Outcomes are perceptions only, which the protocol excludes (E5). The design also lacks a comparison group (E3 would apply too), but E5 is the outcome-based reason and the protocol asks for the first applicable code in order, so E3 (comparison) is checked before E5. Given the protocol order E1, E2, E3, E4, E5, the first applicable code is E3 because there is no control group. Correction: the first applicable code is E3.

quote: A preliminary literature review identified significant factors requiring attention, further refined through interviews with 14 students and 13 faculty members, and expanded upon via a survey involving 54 students and 42 faculty members.
rationale: The study is a survey/interview study rating factors by Relative Importance Index. It is not an experimental design with a control group and reports no learning outcome. Positive evidence shows it is not an empirical comparative study: design is survey-based, so it fails the design criterion and the outcome criterion (perceptions only). Excluded under E6 as not an eligible empirical study (survey-based perception research). Note that E6 is applied here as the closest code; the abstract gives no comparison group or learning measure.

quote: This literature review explores faculty perceptions of generative AI, and ChatGPT in particular, in English as a Medium of Instruction (EMI) undergraduate education.
rationale: The record is a literature review, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It also focuses on faculty perceptions rather than learner-facing use with a control group and a quantitative learning outcome, and it is not STEM-specific. The first applicable code in order is E1, but the abstract gives no evidence of learner-facing AI use, so E6 is the clearest failing criterion; the review design is the decisive factor.

quote: Qualitative phenomenological study.
rationale: The study is a qualitative phenomenological design using semi-structured interviews with nursing students and faculty. It is not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense, as the design is qualitative and not a comparative experiment); the record also lacks any comparison group or quantitative outcome, so it fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Nursing is also outside the STEM domain, which would be a further failing criterion, but the first applicable code in order is taken as E1 check first: intervention is generative AI use by learners, so E1 is not triggered; E2 (nursing is health professions, not STEM) would come before E6 in the code order, so the most appropriate code is E2.

quote: The dissertation conducts a user study with 19 undergraduate students working on nine programming exercises.
rationale: Record is a doctoral dissertation (Utah State Digital Commons), which is not an eligible publication type (journal articles only). Abstract also gives no indication of a control group or a quantitative learning outcome; the user study appears to be a single-system study with analytics, but the publication type alone is a clear exclusion under E10.

quote: Qualitative analysis of the data revealed that students recognize the potential of generative AI for ideation and conceptual development
rationale: Abstract describes a qualitative study of ten art students using observation and a questionnaire on perceptions. No control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the design is qualitative, so E6 (not an empirical study is closest) — however it is an empirical study, so the stronger exclusion is E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) or E3 (no control group). Applying the code order, E3 applies first because there is no control group without generative AI.

quote: Using a case study approach, 21 students from two high schools interacted with DST to explore socioscientific issues as they learned physics, chemistry, and biology.
rationale: The abstract describes a case study of 21 students interacting with a generative AI chatbot (DST) with qualitative chatlog analysis and no comparison group. This is positive evidence of a design lacking a control group and of a non-experimental, case-study design, so the study fails the comparison and design criteria. Exclusion code E3 is used as the first applicable code for the missing control group; the design also fails on the non-experimental case-study approach. The outcome is argumentation and dialogic characteristics from chatlogs, not clearly a quantitative learning outcome.

quote: A mixed-methods case study was conducted of a scientific computing course in a Mechanical Engineering Master's program
rationale: The abstract describes a mixed-methods case study using questionnaires, interviews and grades, with no separate control group lacking generative AI. This is a case study design with no comparison group, so the comparison and design criteria fail. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code in the order given. The intervention (student ChatGPT use in a STEM programming course) and population (graduate engineering students) appear to be met.

quote: This report is based on a systematic literature review.
rationale: The record is a rapid literature review of 112 sources, not an empirical study with a control group or learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. It also reports no quantitative learning outcome and has no comparison group. Since E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol order that is clearly met, it is used here. Not a primary study and not a journal article per se (grey-literature report), so it would also be ineligible on publication type.

quote: The method used is a systematic review using the PRISMA method.
rationale: The record is a systematic review, which is not an empirical study, so it fails the eligibility criteria. Systematic reviews are not primary studies with a control group, so the design and comparison criteria are also not met. Under the protocol, the first applicable code is E6 (not an empirical study). The review's scope includes ChatGPT among other media, but that does not change the outcome.

quote: The study involved 78 trainee teachers from three intact classes.
rationale: At abstract stage all criteria appear met. ChatGPT-based flipped classroom is learner-facing generative AI; there is a conventional (non-AI) control group and a video-based flipped group; design is quasi-experimental with intact classes; trainee teachers learning programming count as higher education STEM (computer science); outcome is a programming achievement test score. Published 2025, journal venue (Asia Pacific Journal of Curriculum & Teaching). Data sufficiency for SMD and full-text language to be checked at full text, but nothing in the abstract excludes it. Abstract is in English while title is Malay; full text language to be judged later.

quote: This quantitative cross-sectional study was conducted in 197 undergraduate nursing students
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional questionnaire survey of perceptions of AI chatbot use. It has no control group without generative AI, and its outcomes are perceived benefits and self-directed learning scores from questionnaires rather than a quantitative learning measure from an intervention. Design is survey-based, so it fails the design criterion. Nursing is health professions education, which is excluded from the STEM domain. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol order, since no comparison group exists. The abstract gives clear positive evidence of a non-comparative survey design.

quote: The study employed a survey research design, utilizing questionnaires as the primary data collection method.
rationale: The study is a survey of design students' perceptions of ChatGPT (n=149), with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The design is survey-based, so it is not an empirical experimental study meeting eligibility; coded E6 as a non-empirical-eligible design. Abstract gives positive evidence of survey design, failing the design and outcome criteria (perception-only). Design domain (product/UX design) is also questionable as STEM. Excluding on E6 is the closest fit given survey design; the outcome failure (perceptions only) would also apply.

quote: The research assesses the relative effectiveness of DeepSeek and ChatGPT tools for social science postgraduate education
rationale: Content is social science teaching (not science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, or data science), so E2 applies. Also, the abstract describes a comparison of two generative AI tools (DeepSeek vs ChatGPT) with no clear non-AI control group, which would be a further concern (E3), but the first applicable code in order is E2. Note the wording "post-test" and "students scored" suggests a possible single-group pre-post design. Domain failure is sufficient for exclusion.

quote: using a quantitative correlational design with 40 students (60% female, 40% male) selected through purposive sampling.
rationale: The abstract describes a quantitative correlational design with a single sample of 40 students and no control group, so there is no comparison group without generative AI (E3). Correlational designs also fail the design criterion. The outcome is learning motivation, an affective measure, which the protocol excludes from extraction. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that the abstract supports; the design and outcome failures are noted but the single code is E3.

quote: Eighty-three second-year MBBS students ... participated in a single-center pre-post interventional trial using a within-subject crossover design.
rationale: The study uses a within-subject crossover design in which every student completes both a standard SDL assignment and an AI-assisted one. There is no separate control group without generative AI, and the abstract describes it as a pre-post design, which the protocol excludes under E3. Domain (medical microbiology) and population (medical students) are not clearly STEM-or-not under the protocol, but the design failure is sufficient on its own. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract.

The abstract describes an exploratory article that "explores the potential" of generative AI in nursing continuing professional development, focusing on design strategies, implementation, and challenges. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Nursing CPD is also health-professions education, which the protocol excludes from the STEM domain. Positive evidence that the design is not empirical is present, so E6 applies as the first failing code in order. Note that E1 (learner-facing AI) is not clearly established from the abstract, but E6 is the first code with positive evidence of failure. Excluding at abstract stage on E6 is justified because the abstract explicitly frames the article as a discussion of potential rather than a study.

quote: In this demo, we will outline the inner-workings of the tool, focusing on the pipeline steps.
rationale: The record is a conference demo paper (GI venue, "In this demo"), which is an ineligible publication type under the protocol (E10). It also describes a system design/demo with no evidence of a comparison group or quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical comparative study. E10 is the first applicable code in the order used for this record's publication type. Abstract stage exclusion is justified by positive evidence of publication type being a demo/conference item.

quote: This paper proposes PlacementPro AI, a community-driven intelligent placement preparation platform that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to deliver personalized placement guidance.
rationale: The abstract describes a system proposal/development paper with no evaluation, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome reported. It reads as a system description rather than an empirical study, so it is not an empirical study (E6). It also gives no comparison group or learning measure, which would fail E3 and E5 if read further. Domain (placement preparation covering aptitude and coding) is not clearly STEM. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that it is not an empirical study.

quote: This study employs a quantitative approach with a correlational survey design.
rationale: The study is a correlational survey with no control or comparison group, which fails the comparison and design criteria. It also measures students' technological knowledge and digital ethics awareness via questionnaire, not a quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E3 is used as the first applicable code under the protocol's ordering that reflects the missing control group; the design failure is clear from the abstract.

quote: Drawing on a grounded theory methodology from an interpretivist standpoint, this paper develops a grounded framework for the enactment of GenAI use in learning routine.
rationale: The study is a grounded theory, interpretivist qualitative study with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Qualitative design fails the Design criterion and there is no quantitative outcome; the first applicable code in order is E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a comparative quantitative design). Domain and population are not specified in the abstract.

quote: This paper presents an analysis of documents produced by 116 US universities classified as as high research activity or R1 institutions
rationale: The study is a document analysis of institutional GenAI policies and guidelines, not an empirical learner-facing intervention study. It has no control group, no learner intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code in the protocol's order that fits; E1 could also be argued since no learner interacts with a GenAI tool, but the design is a policy document analysis, so E6 is the most direct fit.

quote: A single-case study methodology was used to analyze extensive interaction logs between students and both AI systems in simulated STEM learning experiences.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-case study analyzing interaction logs, with no separate control group that avoids generative AI. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group and a non-experimental design means the record fails the comparison and design criteria. Exclusion code E3 is used because the absence of a control group without generative AI is the failure that applies first in the ordering; the case-study design is also not an eligible design.

Abstract describes four case studies with 119 students and a mixed-methods design using grades, surveys, and interviews, with no mention of a separate control group without generative AI. Multiple-case study with no comparison group suggests E3 applies. Generative AI is one of several technologies integrated, and the design is not described as randomized or quasi-experimental. Positive evidence of missing comparison group is present, so exclude at abstract stage.

criteria.quote: analyzing the lesson plans developed by 29 pre-service elementary teachers and assessing how they integrated ChatGPT into science learning activities
criteria.rationale: The study is a descriptive analysis of lesson plans and perceptions from 29 pre-service teachers with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the design is not an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI), the first applicable code in order is E1 only if learner-facing use fails, but the lesson-plan design lacks any comparison group, which is the primary failure. Note the outcome (rubric scores of lesson plans) is not a learning outcome either.

quote: analyzing the lesson plans developed by 29 pre-service elementary teachers and assessing how they integrated ChatGPT into science learning activities
A comprehensive literature review was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar.
rationale: The record is a narrative literature review, not an empirical study. It has no comparison group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. E6 is the first applicable code in protocol order that is supported by the abstract. Domain is medical education, which may also fall under the health professions exclusion.
rationale_note: Review article; E6 applies. Medical education may also trigger E2 (health professions), but E6 is listed first in the required order only if E1 is not applicable; E1 is not positively shown, so E6 is reported as the first applicable code.

quote: Through an exploratory study involving 26 medical students, we investigate the efficacy of natural language dialogue for learning and operating RIS.
rationale: The study concerns a chat-based interface for radiological information systems, used by medical students. Radiology/medical imaging informatics is health professions education, which the protocol excludes from the STEM domain. This is a clear domain failure, so exclusion under E2 applies. The abstract also gives no sign of a control group without generative AI or a quantitative learning outcome, but the domain failure is the first code in order.

quote: This case study examines changes introduced in an undergraduate statistics course following the release of ChatGPT in November 2022.
rationale: The abstract describes a case study with survey data and no separate control group without generative AI, so the comparison and design criteria are not met. Outcomes are mainly perceptions and attitudes (anxiety, confidence, withdrawal rates), with no clear quantitative learning measure. Positive evidence of failure exists for comparison (E3), so E3 is the code applied as the first failing criterion in order. Note that E3 is applied per protocol order: intervention (E1) is not clearly failing at abstract stage, and E3 is the clearest positive failure.

criteria.quote: Participants advocated for a hybrid model of feedback that would pair the technical efficacy of AI and the human insight of instructors.

quote: The study included one writing task evaluated by ChatGPT-4o. After receiving the feedback, students completed a perception-based survey comprising seven Likert-scale items and two open-ended questions.
rationale: The abstract describes a perception-only survey with Likert items and open-ended questions analyzed descriptively and thematically. There is no quantitative learning outcome and no control group, so the study fails on outcome and comparison. The E5 code is used as the first applicable failure in the protocol's order that is clearly evidenced; the design also appears to be a single-group perception study with no comparison. Domain is ESP for medical students, which is not clearly STEM, so it is also unclear. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of no learning outcome.

quote: Generative AI was employed to summarize research topics, methods, and subjects, demonstrating high accuracy and effectiveness
rationale: The study uses generative AI as a research tool to analyze journal papers on corporate education; no learners interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, and there is no control group or learning outcome. Excluded under E1 as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. Also not a STEM content study and not an intervention study, but E1 is the first applicable code in order.

The record has only a title and venue, with no abstract. The title describes a cross-sectional study of nursing students' perceptions and ethical considerations of ChatGPT use. This is a survey-type design measuring perceptions, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Health professions education (nursing) is also excluded by the Domain criterion. Exclusion is based on the title alone, which describes a perception-based cross-sectional design. Coded E6 as a non-empirical-trial design; the primary reason is that the study is a cross-sectional perception survey, not an eligible comparison study. Because the abstract stage requires positive evidence of failure and the title gives it (cross-sectional, perceptions), this is an exclusion, but a reviewer may wish to confirm at full text.

quote: This paper is also provides some of the major issues with data integrity, ethical considerations, and faculty awareness and suggests ways to advance responsible AI use in higher education.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual framework and discussion paper on GenAI in outcome-based education, with no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract that the paper is a non-empirical framework.

quote: This quantitative study examines the impact of these AI tools on fostering inclusive education in Kenya, Nigeria, and South Africa. It involves 322 university students, using purposive sampling and online questionnaires.
rationale: The study is a questionnaire survey of student perceptions and attitudes, with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. The abstract describes attitudes, motivations, and perceived equity impact, which are perception outcomes that do not count. Design is survey-based and no control group is described, so it fails on outcome and design. Excluded at the abstract stage on E5, the first applicable code in the stated order, because the abstract gives positive evidence that no learning outcome was measured.

quote: This essay explores the diverse applications of artificial intelligence (AI) methods in the assessment and quantification of educational outcomes.
rationale: The abstract describes an essay/discussion piece on AI in educational assessment, not an empirical study. No randomized or quasi-experimental design, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome are reported. Excluded as not an empirical study (E6), which is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's rules for this record type.

quote: A four-week case study was conducted with 60 undergraduate students, comparing a control group using textbooks and an experimental group using AlgoLLM.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study describes an LLM-based system (AlgoLLM) used by undergraduates for algorithm learning, compared against a textbook control group, with post-test learning gains and Cohen's d reported. Design (randomization vs. quasi-experiment) and the sufficiency of statistics are not clear from the abstract, but nothing gives positive evidence of a failed criterion. Publication type and journal-article status are not evident from the record beyond venue name; no exclusion is supported. Advance to full text to check design and data.

quote: A small pilot study with senior nursing students indicated that the simulator improved students' confidence, preparedness, and understanding of ethical considerations.
rationale: The tool is a generative AI (GPT-4o, Claude) interview simulator for learners, but the content is research interviewing with older adults in a Science of Aging/biology course and nursing students, not STEM learning content per the protocol's domain list. The abstract also reports a pilot with confidence/preparedness/understanding outcomes, which are perceptual, and gives no comparison group, so E3 and E5 are also doubtful. Excluded on E2 as the first applicable code, since the domain is not STEM content (health/nursing-oriented interview skills).

quote: thirty-two experienced instructors engaged in dialogues with the LLMs, simulating learners with this misconception
rationale: Participants are experienced instructors, not K-12 or higher education students; they role-play learners with a misconception. The study evaluates LLM responses rated by instructors, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome from students. Exclusion under E4 is the first applicable code in order that is positively evidenced; the design also lacks a comparison group (E3) and a learning outcome (E5), but the population failure is the first in sequence.
decision_note: Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract.

quote: The study compares the impact of ChatGPT on academic performance between these two groups.
rationale: Abstract describes ChatGPT use by university Python programming students with an academic performance outcome, which fits the protocol. The abstract does not say whether there is a control group without generative AI; it compares beginners and intermediate students using ChatGPT. The design (randomized or quasi-experimental with a non-AI comparison) and the data needed for an SMD cannot be confirmed from the abstract. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record goes to full text.

quote: Using cross-sectional data from 200 undergraduate mathematics education students at Universitas Negeri Makassar who used conversational AI during a differential calculus course
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey analysed with psychometric network analysis of CoI survey items. There is no control group without generative AI, and no quantitative learning outcome; the items are perceptions/behaviours. Positive evidence of design failure (cross-sectional, no comparison) is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified. E3 is the first applicable code in order that fits the lack of a comparison group; E5 would also apply since outcomes are survey-based perceptions.

quote: this study analyses the technical, organisational, and personal viewpoints of 50 CE educators working in higher education institutions in the MENA area
rationale: The study is an interview-based thematic analysis of 50 computer engineering educators (in-service teachers), with no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an experimental study. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical comparative study), the first clearly applicable code in the protocol's order is E1 since the intervention is not learner-facing, but the design is qualitative interview research, so E6 best fits the evidence. Note: strictly, the first applicable code in order is E1 because AI use is not learner-facing; flagging for auditor review.

quote: A conversational AI assistant helps students debug code and clarify concepts from their notes, providing personalized, on-demand guidance.
rationale: The abstract describes a platform with a conversational AI assistant for programming students, which plausibly is a generative LLM-based tool, and the domain is programming. However, it describes a system and features, with no mention of a control group, study design, or any learning outcome measured. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so it is not excluded at abstract stage. Needs full text to check for a comparison group, design, and quantitative outcome, and to confirm the AI is generative.

criteria.rationale_note: LLM is used by researchers to code student chat logs, not as a learner-facing tool

quote: Using LLMs to Identify Indicators of Persistence from Students' Dialogues with a Pedagogical Agent
rationale: The LLMs (ChatGPT4o) are used by researchers to automatically code student chat logs from a conversation-based assessment; learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of the learning activity. This is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI). No control group or learning outcome is described; the study evaluates coding reliability against human coders.

quote: The results suggest that ChatGPT is able to solve some physics calculation problems, explain solutions, and generate new exercises at a human level.
rationale: Exploratory study demonstrating ChatGPT's problem-solving ability in physics; the abstract describes no control group and no learner comparison, which is positive evidence that the comparison criterion fails. Excluded under E3. Design and outcome are not described as a controlled experiment with learning measures.

quote: the study adopts a within-subjects quasi-experimental design, with a sample involving N=50 undergraduate students
rationale: The abstract describes a within-subjects design in which the same 50 students' self-crafted prompts are compared with meta-prompts. There is no separate control group without generative AI, and the design is a single-group pre-post comparison, which the protocol excludes under E3. The domain (prompt engineering in education) is also not clearly STEM, but E3 is the first applicable code.

quote: This study aims to analyze the students' perspectives on using ChatGPT in the field of programming and programming learning.
rationale: Abstract describes a single-cohort study (41 undergraduates) using open-ended form data analyzed by content analysis on student perspectives. No control group and no quantitative learning outcome is reported; outcomes are perceptions. Positive evidence of failure on comparison/design and outcome criteria. Coded E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) as the first applicable code after intervention and population/domain checks; E3 would also fit since no comparison group is described. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: Data were collected from undergraduate students using an online survey and analysed through descriptive and inferential statistics, including chi-squared tests and regression analyses.
rationale: Abstract describes a cross-sectional online survey of arts and design students on GenAI attitudes, with regression on perceptions. This is not a controlled comparison, has no learning outcome, and the content is arts and design rather than STEM. Exclusion is on the first code that applies in order: E1 is unclear from the abstract, so E2 (content not STEM) is the first clear failure. Design and outcome failures also apply.

quote: A mixed-methods approach, employing a survey of 68 students at a business-focused university in the United States
rationale: The abstract describes a survey of 68 university students on GenAI use and self-perceived expertise. This is a survey design with no control group and no learning outcome measured after an intervention, so it fails comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Per the protocol's exclusion code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing GenAI) is not clearly established from the abstract, so the first clearly applicable code is E3 (no control group without generative AI). Domain is not clearly STEM from the abstract. Excluding at the abstract stage on positive evidence of a survey design with no comparison group.

quote: We input 3357 questions into GPT-4o, GPT-4-Turbo, o1 and o3-mini via Microsoft's Azure OpenAI Service using zero-shot and chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting.
rationale: The study evaluates LLMs answering exam questions themselves; no learner interacts with the generative AI tool as part of a learning activity. The residents are only a historical benchmark, not an intervention or control group. This fails the learner-facing intervention criterion (E1). It is also medical/ophthalmology content, not STEM (E2), though E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: Results indicate that students hold moderately positive views of Generative AI's impact on critical thinking and creativity.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of perceptions with no experimental control group. Its outcomes are self-reported perceptions of critical thinking and creativity, not a quantitative measure of learning, so it fails E5. Design also fails (survey), but E5 is the first applicable code in the order given as it is the earliest code in the protocol list that the abstract clearly supports (E3 is also arguably applicable since there is no control group without generative AI; per the protocol order E3 precedes E5, so the code should be E3). Correcting: the first applicable code in protocol order is E3 because no control group without generative AI exists.

quote: in-depth interviews were conducted with eight Chinese students at a Korean university, and the data were analyzed using the constant comparative method.
rationale: Qualitative interview study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of failure on comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Per the protocol's exclusion code order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly failed, so the first applicable code is E3 (no comparison group without generative AI). Domain is not stated in the abstract. Excluded at abstract stage.

The record has only a title and no abstract. The title ("Generative AI Use Among Students in CPED Doctor of Education Programs") suggests a study of students' use and perceptions of generative AI, not a comparative experiment with a control group and a quantitative learning outcome. The population (Doctor of Education students) is also not STEM content. Exclusion is based on the title alone, which is weak evidence, so the researcher should check the full text if desired. Code E5 is used because the title points to a descriptive use/perception study with no quantitative learning outcome; the STEM domain and design criteria are also doubtful, but no single code is clearly established from the record.

Abstract describes GenAI (ChatGPT-type) integrated into an organic chemistry course with an AI teaching assistant, which fits the intervention, domain (chemistry, STEM), and population (university students). However, the abstract gives no description of a control group, comparison design, or quantitative outcome data; it reads as a teaching-practice description. Missing information is not positive evidence of failure, so the record is passed to full text to check comparison, design, and outcome measurement.

quote: A lesson case analysis was conducted to examine how preservice teachers developed digital competencies throughout this process.
rationale: The abstract describes a lesson case analysis with qualitative data (lesson plans, activities, self-assessment reflections) and no control or comparison group. This is positive evidence of a non-comparative design, so E3 applies (no control group without generative AI). Outcomes are described as reflective growth rather than a quantitative learning measure, which is also not supported.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on positive evidence of no comparison group.

quote: A correlational research design was employed, with data collected from 442 undergraduate students using a structured questionnaire.
rationale: The study is correlational and survey-based, with no comparison group receiving or not receiving generative AI, so there is no control group (E3). The outcome is self-reported awareness and usage, not a quantitative learning outcome. Domain is also not clearly STEM. Under the protocol's exclusion order, E1 (intervention) is unclear from the abstract, so E3 is the first clear failure I can cite from the abstract; the design criterion is also not met.
rationale_note: Ordering note: the protocol lists codes E1 to E10 in order and says to report the first that applies. E1 cannot be confirmed as applying from the abstract, so E3 is used here. Design (correlational) and outcome (usage/awareness, no learning measure) are clear failures.

quote: The study employs a quantitative cross-sectional research design. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire on a sample of 433 students
rationale: Cross-sectional survey of 433 students relating perceived GenAI use to cognitive engagement and learning experiences. There is no control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails. The design is correlational/survey, not an experiment or quasi-experiment, and the outcomes are perceptions rather than quantitative learning measures. Coded E3 as the first applicable code in the protocol's order, though E6 (not an empirical experiment) would also fit. Abstract gives positive evidence of failure, so exclude.

quote: A descriptive-correlational design was employed, utilizing a survey questionnaire and interviews with 464 respondents
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive-correlational survey study with no experimental or comparison group, so no control group without generative AI is evident (E3). It also reports only usage and perceptions, with no quantitative learning outcome. Population (senior high school students) is met. Coding E3 as the first applicable code in the protocol order is a judgment call; the design failure is clear from the abstract even though E3 is listed before E5 and E6.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion based on positive evidence of a non-experimental, survey design with no comparison group.

quote: This paper proposes stewardship as a necessary fourth paradigm of educational data science.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/position paper proposing a framework ("stewardship") for educational data science. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Other criteria cannot be assessed from the abstract but are moot given E6.

quote: Methods: In April–May 2025, a cross-sectional questionnaire survey was conducted in all third-‐ and final‐year BDS students
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional questionnaire survey with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome (only knowledge/attitude/practice self-report and frequencies). It fails on design (survey), comparison (no control group without generative AI), and outcome (perceptions/usage only). Dental education is also arguably health professions education, which the protocol excludes. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI).

quote: The study demonstrates a promising replicable model for integrating AI literacy into foundational courses
rationale: The abstract describes a case study of a single pedagogical intervention with 120 business students, analyzing a final assessment artifact (digital magazine). There is no mention of a control group or comparison condition, and the design is described as a case study/pilot implementation. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group and a non-experimental design supports exclusion under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Intervention (ChatGPT use in a learning activity) and population (college students) appear met, and the course is mathematics-related, though the abstract frames it as business AI literacy.

The LLM is used offline by researchers to automatically design heuristic dispatching rules for a scheduling problem; no learner interacts with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity. This fails the intervention criterion (E1). Population is also not students. Coded E1 as the first applicable exclusion in order.

quote: A quasi‐experimental study was conducted in an undergraduate Operating System course involving cohorts from 2020 to 2022.
rationale: Abstract describes a quasi-experimental study in an undergraduate computer science (operating systems) course with a generative AI-supported BOPPPS model, and reports significant academic performance gains. The abstract does not state the control condition (whether it lacks generative AI) or give effect-size statistics, so eligibility on comparison and data cannot be confirmed. Publication date (2025) and journal venue are consistent with eligibility. No positive evidence of failure at abstract stage, so advance to full text.

quote: This study aims to analyze publication trends, collaboration patterns, knowledge structures, and future development directions of e-assessment in physics and science education through a bibliometric approach.
rationale: The record is a bibliometric analysis of 190 Scopus documents, not an empirical study of learners. It has no intervention group, comparison group, or learning outcome. It fails on E6 (not an empirical study). Its publication type is also doubtful, but E6 is the primary code. Note the record's own stage is abstract, and it is clearly a review-type work, so exclusion is supported by positive evidence.

quote: examine the knowledge, perceptions, and practices of 214 Bhutanese in-service teachers regarding the use of ChatGPT in education
rationale: The population is in-service teachers, which the protocol excludes (E4). The design is a mixed-method survey with no control group and no learning outcome measure, so it also fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. E4 is the first applicable code in order, so it is reported. Domain is not clearly STEM from the abstract.
rationale_note: Multiple criteria fail; E4 is reported as the first applicable code under the stated order of checking, with E3, E5 and E6 also applicable in substance.

quote: students who used ChatGPT scored significantly lower on average than their non-GPT-using peers
rationale: At abstract stage, the record shows a mid-term mathematics exam with students who used ChatGPT compared with students who did not, and total exam scores as an outcome. Design (randomized or quasi-experimental versus observational comparison) and population level (K-12 vs higher education) are not stated in the abstract, so they are not excluded on those grounds. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record advances to full text for checking design, population, and effect-size data.

quote: This study investigates the potential of generative AI, specifically GPT-4, in classifying course learning outcomes according to their respective cognitive levels
rationale: GPT-4 is used to classify learning outcomes (an instructor/researcher task). No learner interacts with the generative AI tool, so the intervention is not learner-facing (E1). Also no learner sample or learning outcome is evident; the study is a model-performance comparison against annotated labels. Excluded on E1 as the first applicable code.

quote: Using a convenience sampling approach, data were collected from 1,295 university students with programming learning experiences involving generative AI.
rationale: The study is a scale development and validation study (survey-based psychometric design: item analysis, EFA, CFA, correlations). It has no control group, no learning outcome measured, and no experimental or quasi-experimental design, so it fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Because it is a non-experimental survey study with no learning outcome, it is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of an eligible design) as the first applicable code at this stage. Domain (programming) and population (university students) appear to be met.

quote: The study employed a qualitative descriptive approach involving 19 fifth-grade students.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative descriptive study of a single fifth-grade classroom with no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome (only engagement percentages and qualitative observations). Positive evidence of design failure (qualitative, no comparison group) is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified. E3 is the first applicable code in protocol order for the missing comparison group; the qualitative design also fails the design criterion.

quote: this exploratory instrumental case study, we examined how pre-service teachers in an upper-level ESOL Foundations course
rationale: The study is a qualitative instrumental case study analyzing coursework artifacts. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and is not an STEM domain (ESOL/multilingual learner teaching with media and AI literacy). It is not an empirical quantitative study meeting the protocol. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol sense of eligible design) is applied; the most fitting first-applicable code given the order is E1 only if AI were not learner-facing, which is not clearly stated, so E6 is used for the qualitative case-study design. Note the domain is also non-STEM (E2 would apply by content), but codes are applied in order and E1 is not clearly met at abstract stage.

quote: This study ... used a cross-sectional research design. The data were collected via questionnaire, with 486 undergraduates from a Chinese university participating.
rationale: The record is a cross-sectional questionnaire survey of GenAI usage with no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. Under the code order, E1 and E2 are not clearly failed at the abstract stage, but the study is a survey, which is not an empirical experiment of an intervention, so E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense) is the best fit. Note that E6 is applied here because the design is a survey, not an experiment.

quote: The study involved 91 undergraduate computer science students, with 37 assigned to the experimental AI-assisted group.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study is a quasi-experiment with an experimental GPT-4o-mini-based feedback group and implied comparison group, in undergraduate computer science (programming), with programming performance measured, published 2025. The abstract does not show that the comparison group lacks generative AI or that effect-size statistics are reported, but none of this is positive evidence of failure. Full text needed to confirm the control condition, the data for SMD computation, and publication type (the venue name is a journal, but verification is needed). Advance to full text.

quote: I develop the “mismatch vulnerability,” a design flaw in assignments that occurs when students can pass the assignment without exercising the skills or capacities it is intended to assess

It is not an empirical study (E6). Also not a STEM-specific context by abstract (criminal justice education journal).

quote: "the error diagnosis and feedback performance of ChatGPT was evaluated"
rationale: The abstract describes evaluating ChatGPT's error diagnosis and feedback on constructed student scenarios, not an experiment with a control group of learners. rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of educators, not an empirical experiment with learners. Under the protocol order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing) could also be argued, but the core failure is the qualitative, non-experimental design and population of educators.

Abstract describes a reflective teaching-experience account of student-designed political simulations in a political science course, not an empirical comparative study. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study) is the first code that clearly applies; E1 and E2 would also apply, but the record is primarily a non-empirical experience report. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence that no empirical study with a control group and quantitative outcome is reported.

There is no learner intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome data; it is a corpus/framework mapping study (E6-like), but E1 is the first applicable code in order.

Outcome is perceived transdisciplinary awareness from interviews, not a quantitative learning measure.

Code E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense) is the first applicable code for a qualitative perception study; E5 would also apply since there is no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion is clear from the abstract.

rationale: Abstract stage. The record has only a title and venue; no abstract is available.
