quote: The effectiveness and limitations of Chat-GPT are exemplified through two case studies, showcasing the importance of manual calculations and established simulation software
rationale: The abstract describes a methodology/case-study paper on using ChatGPT in a distillation design course. It reports no control group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. The study appears to be a non-empirical methodological or pedagogical discussion, so E6 applies. Note that E1 through E5 are not clearly triggered on positive evidence, but the design is not an empirical comparison.

Abstract describes a single inquiry-based workshop with no mention of a control group or comparison condition, and no learning outcome or design is reported. Positive evidence of a failing criterion is lacking for most criteria, but the abstract gives no indication of a comparison group, and the description reads as a single-arm workshop report (a descriptive teaching-innovation paper). Because the abstract stage requires positive evidence to exclude, this should strictly be unsure. Correcting: the decision is unsure, not exclude, since missing information is not evidence of failure.

quote: Through a cross-sectional correlational design, the data were collected from 147 tertiary-level EFL students across four cities in Türkiye.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional correlational design with no control group, which fails the comparison and design criteria. The study is also about EFL (language learning, non-STEM) and measures ChatGPT literacy and sustainability perceptions rather than a learning outcome. Exclusion code E3 is used as the first applicable code in the protocol's ordering of the E1 to E10 codes; the domain failure (non-STEM) would also apply. Note: strictly by code order, E1 (intervention) is unclear, and E2 (content not STEM) is positive evidence of failure and comes before E3, so the correct first code is E2.

quote: Results show that 65–77.5% of students found the system "quite helpful" or "very helpful"
rationale: Abstract describes a generative RAG chatbot used by university students, but evaluation relies on student questionnaires and free-response feedback about helpfulness, which are perceptions only. No quantitative learning outcome or control group is described, so the study fails E5 (and the design appears non-comparative). Domain is partly STEM (software engineering, information networks) but not needed for the decision. Exclusion is positive evidence from the abstract rather than missing information.

quote: the proposed model with four suggested hypotheses was developed from past theories based on technology adoption.
rationale: The study is a PLS-SEM survey of 300 responses on technology-adoption constructs (performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating conditions, behaviour intention). It reports perceptions and behavioural intention, not a quantitative learning outcome, and has no control group. Per the abstract it is a survey design, so it fails the outcome and design criteria. Although E1 through E4 are not clearly failed on the abstract alone, the first applicable code in order would be E1 or E3 if checked; however, the abstract gives positive evidence of no learning outcome and a survey design, so E5 is the most evident failure. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract.

quote: The study adopted mix method research approach design. A quasi experimental-control group design with intact class involving pretest, post-test with one experimental group and one control group
rationale: Quasi-experimental design with a control group and undergraduate participants fit the criteria. The abstract does not say whether the AI tutor is generative, so intervention is unclear. Domain is integrated science (biology course), which is arguably STEM but unclear. The outcome is a cognitive load questionnaire, which is self-report, so it may not count as a learning measure. Per the abstract-stage rule, these unresolved points go to full text rather than exclusion.

quote: This study evaluates ChatGPT's effectiveness on intermediate and advanced Hungarian high school mathematics exams and KöMaL competition tasks
rationale: The abstract describes ChatGPT's performance on exam and competition tasks scored by researchers, plus a questionnaire on student attitudes. There is no indication of a separate control group that does not use generative AI, so the comparison criterion appears to fail. The design also looks non-experimental. Abstract shows positive evidence of no control group, so exclude under E3.

quote: The study investigated the influence of ChatGPT-generated feedback on the writing skills of ESL leaners of Pakistani high school students.
rationale: The intervention is ChatGPT feedback on ESL writing skills. Writing/language learning is not a protocol STEM domain, and the protocol explicitly excludes language learning and other non-STEM content. Exclude at E2 (first applicable code; the E1 check passes since ChatGPT is a generative, learner-facing tool). Other criteria appear plausibly met from the abstract, but the domain failure is clear positive evidence.

Abstract is missing from the index, so no criterion can be checked against positive evidence. Title describes middle school mathematics and learning outcomes, which fits domain and population, but it does not show whether the teachable agent uses a generative model, whether a non-generative-AI control exists, or the design. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not grounds for exclusion, so advance to full text.

quote: Data were collected from 109 Chinese high school students who engaged in programming tasks using either ChatGPT-driven dialogic interaction or traditional pair programming.
rationale: Abstract indicates ChatGPT-based programming with high school students, versus pair programming control (non-generative-AI comparison), so intervention, comparison, population and domain appear met. Described as quasi-experimental with a comparison, which fits the design criterion. Outcomes are mainly engagement (behavioral, cognitive, emotional) and self-efficacy/anxiety, which are partly affective; the abstract does not clearly report a quantitative learning outcome such as achievement or problem-solving, so the outcome criterion is unclear. Affective outcomes must not be extracted. Full text needed to check whether any cognitive/skill performance measure exists and whether SMD data are reported.

quote: Data were gathered through questionnaires (students n = 115; staff n = 17), two student focus groups, and five semi-structured staff interviews.
rationale: The study is a mixed-methods perception study (questionnaires, focus groups, interviews) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group and only perception data, so it fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is not quite the best fit, but the first applicable code in order is E1 only if intervention is non-learner-facing, which is not clearly established; the decisive failure is absence of a control group and learning outcome (E3/E5). Following the protocol's order, E1 is unclear, E2 not applicable (chemical engineering is STEM), E3 applies: no control group without generative AI. Rationale corrected: the first applicable code is E3.

quote: This study adopted a within-subjects experimental design to compare students' performance in science learning under TSI and GSI conditions
rationale: Abstract describes a science learning study with GAI-Student Interaction (GSI) vs Teacher-Student Interaction (TSI) in a within-subjects design. The protocol requires a separate control group without generative AI; a within-subjects design where both conditions involve students may be a two-condition comparison, which could be E3 if no non-AI group exists in the design. Abstract also reports academic performance and engagement outcomes, but whether the TSI condition counts as a non-generative-AI comparison (a human teacher is an eligible comparison per protocol) and whether the design is randomized or quasi-experimental cannot be determined from the abstract. Advance to full text to check the comparison structure, the quantitative performance data, and the population (education level).

quote: Structured surveys were administered to measure ethical perception, academic performance, and responsible use of AI.
rationale: The abstract describes a methodological proposal (CLASES framework) developed from a survey-based quantitative study. Surveys measure perceptions and self-reported use, with no described control group or experimental comparison, so the design is not an eligible experiment or quasi-experiment and the outcome is not a learning measure. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense, since it is a framework proposal with survey data) is the best fit at abstract stage. Note that E3 (no control group) would also apply; E6 is reported as the first applicable code given the framework-proposal nature. The abstract gives positive evidence that the design is survey-based and not a comparative experiment.

criteria.domain_note: design/multimedia animation content; STEM status unclear
criteria.intervention_note: Generative AI for design implied but not explicit in abstract

quote: The learning achievement of the Active Learning group was significantly higher than that of the Traditional Learning group at the .05 level.
rationale: Abstract reports a Traditional vs Active Learning comparison of learning achievement with 20 undergraduates using AI for design. Whether the tool is generative, whether the content is STEM (design/multimedia/animation seems outside the protocol's STEM list), and whether the design is a true comparison with a non-generative-AI control are not clear from the abstract. No positive evidence of failure on any criterion is given, so the record is kept for full-text review rather than excluded. Title is in Thai; the abstract is in English. Language is not judged at abstract stage.
rationale_note: Full text should check the domain (STEM vs. design) and whether the Traditional group avoided generative AI.

quote: Based on questionnaire data collected from 394 college students after they engaged in programming tasks using an AI-Agent developed by the research team
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional questionnaire study using fsQCA on learning beliefs and self-efficacy (psychological/affective dispositions), with no control group and no quantitative learning achievement outcome. Excluded at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome); it also lacks a comparison group (E3 would apply, but E5 is the first code that clearly applies on the outcome measures named). Design is correlational/survey-based, which fails the design criterion as well. Since the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-eligible outcome and design, exclusion is justified.

quote: The research involved 260 Teacher Training students (170 males, 90 females)
rationale: The abstract describes a pre-test post-test two-way equivalent group design examining associations between time, environmental patterns, psychosocial factors and students' use of ChatGPT and "technology integration". The outcome is use/adoption of the tool, not a quantitative learning outcome such as achievement or problem solving, and the abstract gives no learning measure. This is positive evidence that the outcome criterion fails, so exclude under E5. Domain is also not clearly STEM from the abstract, but E5 is the first applicable code given the stated outcome.

quote: The study adopted a mixed methods approach. Survey data were collected from online communities on social media.
rationale: Study concerns foreign language learning, which is non-STEM, so E2 applies first in the code order. It is also a survey study with perceptions only and no control group, which would fail E3, E5 and E6 as well, but E2 is the first applicable code.

quote: This study examines the perceived utility of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), particularly ChatGPT, in the development of final degree projects across diverse academic disciplines.
rationale: The study measures perceived utility (perceptions), not a quantitative learning outcome, and reports no control group; eleven students in a mixed-methods design with no comparison condition. Perceptions-only outcomes fail E5. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that the outcome and design criteria fail. Domain is mixed across disciplines (including Computer Science, Chemical Engineering, Psychology, Philosophy), so STEM status is not the deciding factor.

quote: We outline six ready-to-apply undergraduate assignments based on active learning pedagogical practices that emphasize process, reflection, and engagement over product alone.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/position article proposing assignments and a scaffolding model. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails the empirical design requirement (E6). Domain is also unclear (science communication), but E6 is the first applicable code given the order and the nature of the record.

quote: This study included 20 nursing students ... A qualitative research approach with purposive and snowball sampling was employed
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Nursing content is also health professions education, which falls outside the STEM domain. Per the protocol's exclusion order, the first applicable code is E2 (content is not STEM) since health professions education is explicitly excluded from the domain, but the design is also non-empirical in the protocol sense of quantitative comparison. Abstract clearly shows qualitative design, so E6 is the best fit for a non-eligible empirical design, with domain and outcome also failing.

quote: Student feedback indicated that generative AI could enhance their understanding of disease-specific lifestyle management
rationale: The abstract describes a single-cohort course using ChatGPT with only a post-course satisfaction survey. There is no control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion is not met. The design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. The only outcome is satisfaction and perceptions, which is not a quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in order, since the lack of a control group is the first failing criterion reached after E1 and E2 are considered met or unclear. Domain is also unclear because Korean medicine clinical education is not clearly STEM. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence of no control group and no learning outcome.

This is a system-description paper presenting NexusAI, a platform with a Gemini-driven tutoring feature. The abstract reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no learning outcome data; it describes architecture and features only. Positive evidence that the comparison criterion fails is lacking in the abstract, but the record reads as a non-empirical architecture or design paper with no control group. Under the abstract rule, the design and outcome are not positively shown to meet criteria, so the strict reading would be unsure. However, the abstract gives no indication of a control group without generative AI or any quantitative learning measure, and the paper appears to be a system description. Excluding on E3 (no control group) is the best-supported code, though the basis is absence of evidence rather than a stated design, so a reviewer should confirm at full text if there is doubt.

quote: The study develops a four-module framework for a learner-centric personalization learning path enabled by LLMs
rationale: The study is a secondary analysis of the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset comparing High vs Low Adaptation groups defined by VLE interaction patterns. No learner interaction with a generative AI tool is described; the LLM is only a conceptual framework component. Intervention is not learner-facing generative AI (E1). Also no separate non-generative-AI control group in the sense required; design is observational grouping rather than an experiment. E1 applied as first failing code.

quote: A scoping review was performed following PRISMA-ScR and JBI guidelines to identify the empirical literature regarding the use of LLMs in UGME.
rationale: The record is a scoping review, which is a review article and not an empirical study (E6). It also concerns medical education (health professions), which falls under the domain exclusion, though the first applicable code in order is E2 for non-STEM content. Rule-ordered coding: E1 is unclear from the abstract (the review mixes LLM uses, some faculty-facing such as MCQ generation), E2 applies because medical education is a health-professions domain, not STEM. Given the code order requires the first applicable, E2 would be the first code that applies in the ordering from E1 onward only if E1 does not apply; since E1 is unclear rather than clearly met, the coding is E2 as the earliest clear failure. Note: the paper is a review, so E6 is also clearly met; the sequence rule places E2 first.

quote: Results indicated that no substantial differences were identified in students' programming knowledge acquisition and group-level programming product quality when both instructor manual feedback and ChatGPT intelligent feedback were provided.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study compares ChatGPT intelligent feedback with instructor manual feedback in collaborative programming in higher education, with programming knowledge acquisition as an outcome. The comparison group receives a non-generative-AI feedback condition (instructor manual feedback), which meets the comparison criterion. Design (randomized or quasi-experimental) is not stated in the abstract, so it is unclear and is to be checked at full text. No positive evidence of any failed criterion, so include.

criteria.criteria_note: Emergency medicine clerkship MCQs; domain is medical/health professions education, which the protocol excludes.

quote: Comparative analysis was conducted using 160 MCQs from an EM clerkship curriculum
rationale: The study compares ChatGPT, Gemini, and final-year emergency medicine clerkship students answering MCQs from an EM curriculum. Emergency medicine is a health professions domain, which the protocol excludes as non-STEM. The study also does not appear to have a learner-facing AI intervention; AI was tested as an answering system rather than used by learners in a learning activity, and there is no control group that lacks generative AI. Several criteria fail on the abstract, and the domain exclusion is the clearest.

quote: Two case studies conducted in Russian middle schools provide empirical grounding
rationale: Abstract describes generative AI use by middle school students in programming and project-based learning, with computational thinking as the target, which fits intervention, population, and domain. However, it describes "two case studies," which suggests a case-study design rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison with a control group, and it gives no indication of a comparison group or effect statistics. The design and comparison are therefore not clear from the abstract. Given the rule that missing information is not evidence for exclusion, this is passed to full text to check whether a control group and quantitative CT outcome exist.

quote: A comprehensive literature search identified four studies for inclusion.
rationale: This is a scoping review, which the protocol treats as a review rather than an empirical study. The abstract describes it as a scoping review of four included studies, so it is not an empirical study and fails E6. Under the code order, E1 through E5 are not clearly established from the abstract, so E6 is the first applicable code. Note that the included studies are described as case studies, not randomized or comparison-group designs, which would also be unlikely to meet the design criterion.

quote: Knowledge assessment results showed modest but non-significant changes in students’ conceptual AI knowledge
rationale: placeholder

quote: General Chemistry students who evaluated AI-generated content showed strong gains in their knowledge about report structure and the capabilities and deficiencies of LLMs in chemistry.
rationale: Abstract describes ChatGPT (generative LLM) used by undergraduate chemistry students in assignments, which meets intervention, population and domain. The abstract does not state whether a control group without generative AI exists; it reads as a single-cohort course assignment with pre/post knowledge gains, which would be E3 if no comparison group exists. Cannot determine from abstract, so advance to full text to check the comparison and design.

quote: Qualitative feedback from students and instructor observations indicate that the framework aids in reducing cognitive barriers
rationale: The abstract describes a proof-of-concept classroom implementation evaluated through feasibility, perceived utility, and qualitative feedback. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome reported. Positive evidence that the outcome and design criteria fail is present, so exclude at abstract stage. E5 is the first applicable code in order that fits: no quantitative learning outcome. The design also lacks a comparison group, which would support E3, but E5 is applied as the stated primary failure in the reported evaluation; the earlier-ordered codes E1-E4 do not apply.

quote: Frequency of use was moderately associated with perceiving GenAI as an interactional participant.
rationale: Survey-based mixed-methods study of perceptions with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the content is English language learning, which is non-STEM. Exclusion code set to E3 (no control group without generative AI) as the first applicable code in order is arguably E2 for non-STEM content; however, the protocol says report the first that applies in order E1 to E10. Applying order: E1 intervention is arguably learner-facing GenAI use, so not clearly E1; E2 applies because the content is English language learning, not STEM. Correct code should be E2.

quote: we leveraged a fine-tuned large language model (LLM) to automate the encoding of classroom discourse
rationale: The LLM is used to automate coding of classroom discourse for researchers, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. Pre-service and expert teachers analysed observed dialogue; there is no learner interaction with generative AI, no control group, and no learning outcome measured. Excluded under E1 as the first applicable code. The abstract gives positive evidence the intervention is not learner-facing.

quote: The reflective exercises submitted by the students indicated that working with a nonprofit gave students valuable hands-on experience applying marketing concepts in real-world settings.
rationale: Case study of an experiential learning marketing project. Evidence is student reflective exercises and a debriefing, not an empirical comparative study. No control group and no quantitative learning outcome reported. Domain (marketing) is not STEM. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in the order given; E2 (non-STEM content) would also apply but E6 is reported as the primary designation for a case study with no empirical design. Note that the protocol orders codes E1 through E10 and asks for the first that applies; under strict ordering, E1 (intervention) is unclear because GenAI tool use is only mentioned in passing, and E2 precedes E6 as a content failure. Auditor should review whether E2 should be the reported code instead.

quote: Using a within-subjects design, N = 107 students solved a real-world task, first unaided and then with ChatGPT.
rationale: The study uses a within-subjects design where all students solve the task unaided and then with ChatGPT. There is no separate control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails. Pre-post within a single group is explicitly E3. Intervention (ChatGPT, learner-facing), STEM domain (probability), and population (engineering students) appear met, but the design lacks a comparison group.

quote: The study employed a descriptive research design with a quantitative approach.
rationale: Language courses (English) are non-STEM content, so E2 applies first in the code order. The study is also a descriptive survey with no control group (would be E3/E6 under other criteria), but E2 is the first applicable code. Abstract gives positive evidence of non-STEM content and a descriptive, non-comparative design.

quote: A comparative design with a mixed-methods approach was used, involving 30 respondents: 15 early-stage students (Semester 4) and 15 advanced-stage students (Semester 6).
rationale: The study compares two student groups by experience level, both using vibe coding (generative AI). No control group without generative AI is described, and the outcomes are Likert-scale questionnaire perceptions plus a prompt quality rubric, not a clearly quantitative learning measure. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI) on the abstract's evidence; the abstract gives positive evidence that the comparison is between AI-using groups only.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion based on comparison design.

quote: The study analysed 1287 utterances from middle school science classes using a mixed‐method approach.
rationale: ChatGPT is used by the researcher as a qualitative coding tool for analysing classroom dialogue, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity (E1). There is no control group, no learning outcome (kappa measures inter-rater agreement), and it is a single-researcher case study. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: This article is the second in a series examining the way in which generative artificial intelligence is changing practice and training in the health and medical sciences.
rationale: The record is a narrative/review-style article in the health sciences (nursing and clinical decision-making). It is not STEM content under the protocol, which excludes health professions education. It also describes no controlled study or quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E2 as the first applicable code in order; E1 was considered but the abstract does not clearly describe a learner-facing tool, so E2 is the most direct ground. No injection content observed.

criteria.quote: This paper proposes the AI-Resilient Teaching Innovation Framework (ARTIF), an integrative and vaue-grounded model
criteria.rationale: The record is a conceptual framework paper that proposes a model and gives an illustrative case. It reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study. Exclusion code E6 applies as the first failing criterion in order.

quote: This research is a quantitative study that utilises primary data through a survey method.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey (TAM/UGT structural equation modelling of behavioural intention and perceptions). It has no control group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; only perceptions and intentions are measured. Excluded as a non-empirical-experimental design under E6 (not an empirical study eligible under the design criterion). Note the first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group) or E5 (no learning outcome); the protocol's first applicable code in sequence is E3 given no comparison group exists. Reporting E6 as the closest fit for a correlational survey design.

quote: "This work establishes a proof of concept for state‐grounded virtual instruction and provides a foundation for evaluating skill transfer and learning outcomes in future large‐scale studies."
rationale: The study is a pilot with n=6 students observed in a design-based approach, with no control group and no learning outcome measured; the abstract explicitly defers learning outcome evaluation to future studies. Positive evidence of no comparison group supports E3 (no control group without generative AI). Exclusion is at the abstract stage based on this positive evidence.

Abstract describes entrepreneurship education, which is not a STEM domain under the protocol. The study also appears to be a survey-based correlational/mediation analysis of 203 students (no control group, no experimental comparison described), so design and comparison criteria are not met on the abstract. Exclusion code E2 is the first applicable code in order, since content is not STEM. Quote is unavailable as a verbatim passage supporting a clear STEM-domain statement; the abstract does state "data were collected from 203 students enrolled in entrepreneurship programs" and "Mediation and moderation analyses with bootstrapping," which supports the non-experimental nature.

quote: This qualitative study investigates how 29 undergraduate CS students used LLMs while developing open-ended AI applications in a project-based course.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative study of 29 undergraduate CS students using LLMs in a project course, analyzing documentation, reflection logs, and transcripts. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the design is qualitative, so it is not an empirical experiment meeting the criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in the order given, reflecting a non-experimental qualitative design. Since the abstract gives clear positive evidence of a qualitative design with no comparison group, exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: The study employs fuzzy-Delphi and fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (f-AHP) techniques with the 15 expert panel and 4 considered cases of HEIs to prioritize depicted implications.
rationale: The paper is a fuzzy-Delphi and f-AHP expert-panel prioritization study, not an empirical controlled experiment. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the design is not an eligible study design. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol sense). Domain and population are also not STEM-specific or learner-based in the abstract, but the design failure is decisive.
rationale_note: Exclusion under E6 reflects a non-experimental expert-judgement design.

quote: Using OpenAI Copilot as a large language model, we create programming exercises (including sample solutions and test cases), evaluating them qualitatively and quantitatively.
rationale: The abstract describes ChatGPT/Copilot used to generate programming exercises for teachers ("a tool for teachers"), not a learner-facing learning activity. Content is evaluated qualitatively and quantitatively as generated output; there is no learner group, no control group, and no learning outcome. Exclusion under E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI) is the first code that applies. Design is clearly not an experiment with a comparison group.

quote: A phenomenological approach was adopted within the qualitative research framework, utilising a semi-structured interview form and researcher diaries as data collection tools.
rationale: The study is a qualitative phenomenological study of 18 teachers' perspectives, with no control group, no learner outcome, and teachers (not students) as participants. Exclusion code E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first clearly applicable code under the protocol's ordering, though the design also fails E3 and E4. Under the abstract-stage rule, the exclusion is supported by positive evidence of a qualitative design with no quantitative outcome.

quote: The study investigated the effect of utilizing AI chatbots to develop the ability of Jordanian grade 8 students to speak English properly.
rationale: The intervention is an AI chatbot for English speaking skills, which is language learning, not STEM. The domain criterion fails on positive evidence, so E2 applies first in the code order. Other criteria appear plausible from the abstract (control group, pretest-posttest, student population), but the STEM exclusion is sufficient.

quote: We present an evaluation of state-of-the-art (SOTA) LLMs on PhD-level to research-level computational physics problems.
rationale: The study evaluates GPT-4 zero-shot on physics simulation problems. There is no learner population; the subject is the LLM itself. There is no control group, no learning outcome (performance is scored by soft error-count metrics), and the design is a model evaluation rather than a randomized or quasi-experiment. Under the coded exclusion order, E1 (learner-facing use) is not clearly established from the abstract, but the main failure is population: no students are involved. Coding E4 as the first clear failure, with E3/E5 also present.

Community service program on IELTS and TOEFL (language test) preparation, a non-STEM content area, which fails the domain criterion (E2). The design appears to be a participatory action research program with pre/post gains and no described control group, so E3 and E6 are also likely, but E2 is the first applicable code in order. Exclusion made at abstract stage on positive evidence that content is language learning, not STEM.

quote: This study aimed to analyze the effect of the Gemini AI Chatbot on the academic achievement and motivation of 11th-grade high school students. The research employed a quasi-experimental design.
rationale: Gemini is a generative AI chatbot used by high school students, the design is quasi-experimental, and achievement is measured by tests. The abstract does not state a control group, so comparison is unclear. The subject area is also not named (the outcomes are general academic achievement), so STEM domain is unclear. Neither is clear enough to exclude at the abstract stage, so this goes to full text to check the control group and the subject.

quote: This conceptual review examines how young learners can use generative AI without outsourcing retrieval, reasoning, argumentation, verification, and transfer.
rationale: The record is a conceptual review, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. The field experiment it describes is a secondary citation of other work, not an study reported by this article. Exclusion is based on the article's own design being non-empirical.

quote: our randomized controlled trial (RCT; N = 95) investigated whether a structured, SRL-aligned scaffolding training session could improve students' AI-assisted revision performance in electromagnetism problems
rationale: Abstract reports an RCT with a control group (no AI-specific training) in electromagnetism (STEM), with students interacting with the LLM Doubao for revision, a quantitative conceptual-test outcome, and d = 0.81 reported, published 2026. Population (students vs. higher-ed/K-12) is not stated in the abstract, so it is not excluded; data sufficiency and language are to be checked at full text.

quote: The methodological framework consisted of a comparative analysis of 21 scientific publications from 2021–2026, systematization, structural-functional analysis, and secondary analysis of open statistical data
rationale: The record is a narrative/review-style analysis of 21 publications plus secondary analysis of a faculty survey (Digital Education Council 2025). It is not an empirical experiment with a learner-facing generative AI intervention, a control group, or a learning outcome. It fails the design, comparison and outcome criteria; the faculty survey reports readiness perceptions, not learning outcomes. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies as the first failing code in the protocol's order that is evident from the abstract.

quote: This exploratory inquiry consolidates recent scholarly works to discuss the potential benefits and downsides of ChatGPT in terms of increasing teaching and learning.
rationale: The abstract describes a narrative review/consolidation of prior scholarly works, not an empirical study. It has no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Domain and population are not specified in the abstract, but the E6 failure is sufficient.

quote: This cross-sectional study explored relationships between high school students' ability to complete programming activities when permitted to use generative AI, their interest and attitude towards programming, and foundational mathematical knowledge.
rationale: The study is described as cross-sectional, examining relationships between programming performance with generative AI permitted, interest, and math scores. There is no described control group without generative AI, and no comparison group is evident. Design is cross-sectional rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison, so the comparison criterion fails on positive evidence. Exclusion code E3 applied as the first failing criterion in order (E1 does not apply since learners use generative AI; E2 and E4 do not apply).

quote: Using a cross-sectional self-report design, this study examined the statistical associations among AI-enabled course development, AI proficiency, academic adjustment, and a composite indicator of self-reported psychological adjustment.
rationale: Cross-sectional self-report survey with no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group, so no control group without generative AI exists (E3). Outcomes are self-reported psychological adjustment and perceptions rather than a quantitative learning measure, and the domain is not clearly STEM. E3 is the first applicable code in protocol order given the absence of any comparison group design.

criteria.outcome_note: no quantitative learning outcome; perceptions only

quote: A descriptive cross-sectional study was done in all the 198 female students enrolled in the four years BSc Nursing program.
rationale: Exclusion code should be the first that applies in order. The study is a descriptive cross-sectional survey with no control group without generative AI (E3 applies). Domain is nursing, which is health professions education, not STEM (E2) and the outcome is self-perceived, not a quantitative learning measure (E5). quote: This article describes a two-year teaching experience (2024/2025 and 2025/2026) integrating the free, responsible, and critical use of GenAI into a coordinated, complex software development project
rationale: The abstract describes a two-year teaching experience with an exploratory phase followed by a revised implementation, with no separate control group without generative AI. Reported findings are largely perceptual (frustration, usage patterns), with no quantitative learning comparison. Positive evidence of no control group supports E3 at the abstract stage.
rationale_note: Exclusion based on absence of a comparison group described in the abstract; the design appears to be a sequential single-cohort course evaluation.

quote: This study evaluated how 56 undergraduate university students in Ecuador viewed GenAI use in academic writing in English as a foreign language.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey of student perceptions with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Perceptions-only outcomes are excluded by protocol. Design is a survey, not an experiment or quasi-experiment. Domain is EFL academic writing, which is non-STEM despite the mention of STEM classes. Exclusion code E5 is the first applicable code in the order given that is clearly supported by the abstract; the abstract gives positive evidence of a perceptions-only survey.

quote: GPT-4 can be used as an adjunctive tool in creating multi-choice question medical examinations
rationale: GPT-4 was used by specialist physicians/faculty to write exam questions, not by learners in a learning activity. Learner-facing generative AI is absent, so E1 applies. No control group or learner outcome is described either, and the domain is medical education, which is health professions education.

quote: English-speaking instruction has long been plagued by insufficient input, lack of interaction, delayed feedback, and emotional anxiety
rationale: The study concerns English-speaking learning, which is language learning and not STEM content, so it fails the domain criterion (E2). The abstract also describes a mixed-methods study with pre- and post-tests and no clearly stated control group, but the domain failure is sufficient for exclusion on its own.

quote: The research developed an AI-Agent system based on large language models and employed a quasi-experimental design
rationale: At abstract stage all criteria appear met: an LLM-based AI-agent is learner-facing in a collaborative programming course; there is a CSCL control group without generative AI; the design is a quasi-experiment with random assignment; the population is university students; the domain is programming; learning achievement is measured. Journal article in 2025. Data sufficiency for SMD cannot be confirmed from the abstract, but missing information is not grounds for exclusion at this stage.

quote: A questionnaire addressing students' perceptions about the work and ChatGPT usage was performed after delivering the task.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-cohort course task with ChatGPT required, evaluated via student perception questionnaire and teacher acknowledgement. There is no control group without generative AI, so E3 applies. The outcome also appears to be perceptions only (E5 would also be arguable), but E3 is the first applicable code in order. Domain is computer science degree, but the abstract is focused on critical thinking and ethics rather than STEM content learning.

quote: A quantitative, cross-sectional research design was employed. Using convenience sampling, a total of 535 undergraduate students
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of students' perceptions of ChatGPT, with chi-square associations between demographics and perceptions. It has no control group, no learning outcome, and no STEM content indicated. Under the protocol, the study fails on outcome (E5) and design; E5 is reported as the first applicable code in order. Reporting only perceptions meets the E5 exclusion directly.

criteria.criteria_note: Survey of perceptions; no control group or learning outcome described

quote: The research has provided insight into the perception of Business Administration students regarding these applications.
rationale: The abstract describes an exploratory perception survey of university students about generative AI. It reports no control group, no experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. Only perceptions are measured, and the protocol excludes perception-only studies. Domain (business administration) is also not STEM. Exclusion code E5 is the first applicable code in the order that fits best, though the design failure (no comparison group, survey design) is also evident.
exclusion_code_note: Domain is business/economics, not STEM (E2) and design is survey (E6) may also apply; reported first applicable per order E1-E10 would be E2 since E1 is unclear.

quote: The study results showed that the group receiving AI convergence education using generative AI significantly improved their computational thinking. The improvement in computational thinking was also significant compared to the control group
rationale: Abstract reports high school students in an experimental group using generative AI (ChatGPT) versus a control group, with computational thinking measured by a test tool. Computational thinking is a STEM-related (computing) domain. Design appears to be a group comparison with a control group; randomization is not stated, so design is not confirmed. Publication date 2024 and journal venue are consistent with eligibility. No positive evidence of failure on any criterion, so include at abstract stage; full text should confirm randomization/quasi-experimental design, effect size data, and journal article status.

The record's title names attitudes toward ChatGPT on medical topics, but the abstract describes a neural identifier for parameter identification of a DC motor. It does not describe learners interacting with a generative AI tool, and it is not a learning study. The abstract contradicts the title, so the record appears mismatched. Under the protocol's exclusion code order, E1 applies first because the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. Domain (E2) and outcome issues also appear, but E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: This conceptual paper positions prompt engineering as a twenty-first-century learning competency
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual paper that synthesizes literature and proposes frameworks, with no empirical design, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Under the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly failed at abstract stage, so E6 is the first code that positively applies.

quote: This paper is a conceptual and argumentative contribution grounded in an extensive review of recent international and African literature
rationale: The record is a conceptual and argumentative paper based on a literature review, not an empirical study. It has no comparison group, no original design, and no quantitative learning outcome from participants. It fails E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first applicable code in order given that E1 through E5 cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract alone but the non-empirical nature is clear.

quote: "The current study uses a cross-sectional empirical survey design with a sample of N = 917 respondents"
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey measuring self-reported stakeholder perceptions, not learning outcomes. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, and the design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment. Under the protocol, survey designs and studies reporting only perceptions are excluded. The abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with no learning measure, so the record is excluded. The protocol lists survey designs under E6 (not an empirical study is the closest code) but this is a survey, which is empirical; the strongest positive evidence is the absence of a learning outcome, which would be E5. Since the rule asks for the first applicable code in order, E3 (no control group) also applies first in order. Applying the order strictly: E1 is unclear, E2 is unclear, E3 applies because there is no comparison group without generative AI.

criteria.criteria_note: Health professions education is excluded under Domain; population is healthcare students

quote: A cross-sectional survey was conducted to evaluate the knowledge, attitudes, and practices of healthcare university students in Saudi Arabia regarding the academic use of ChatGPT.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey, not a controlled experiment, so there is no comparison group (E3 would also apply). Under the protocol's order, E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract, but the design is not empirical learning-outcome research: it measures knowledge, attitudes and practices via questionnaire, with no quantitative learning outcome (E5). Health professions education is also excluded in the Domain row. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract that the study is a survey with no learning outcome.
rationale_note: Abstract stage; survey design with no learning outcome. Note E3 and domain (health professions) also fail.

quote: In case of incorrect solutions, a Large Language Model, contextualized with sample solutions and task classification results, offers auxiliary support for students struggling to initiate or complete tasks.
rationale: The platform embeds an LLM that students interact with during MATLAB/Simulink programming exercises in control engineering, so intervention and STEM domain appear met, and students are presumably university learners. However, the abstract describes a system and project without any comparison group, study design, or quantitative learning outcome. Missing information is not positive evidence of failure, so the record is kept for full-text review of design, comparison, and outcome.

quote: This glossary serves as a comprehensive terminological resource to understand generative artificial intelligence (AI) in educational contexts.
rationale: The record is a glossary/conceptual framework built from a literature review, NLP analysis, and Delphi validation. It is not an empirical study with a control group or learning outcome, so it fails the design and outcome requirements. Under the protocol's exclusion order, E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract, and E6 (not an empirical study) is the applicable code. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that it is not empirical.

quote: This integrative review synthesizes recent research to identify key trends, opportunities, and challenges associated with AI integration in mathematics teacher education.
rationale: The record is an integrative review, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It reports no controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion is based on positive evidence from the abstract that the design is a review. The quote is from the abstract, so it is set at the abstract location.

quote: A cohort of 34 introductory-physics students generated and attempted 543 practice problems during exam preparation.
rationale: The abstract describes a single cohort of 34 students generating and attempting LLM-produced physics problems, with students comparing items in pairs for preference and expert/LLM judge benchmarking. There is no separate control group without generative AI, and the study is exploratory with preference and judge-agreement outcomes rather than a learning outcome. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is present, so exclude under E3 at abstract stage.

quote: This research intends to evaluate the usage and impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in engineering education through a cross-sectional study using a web-based questionnaire distributed to 290 undergraduate and graduate students.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional web survey measuring perceptions and self-reported use of AI tools. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions and usage only, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). Design is also a survey, which is outside the eligible designs, but the first applicable code in order is E5 as the abstract stage gives positive evidence that no learning outcome is measured.

quote: Notably
rationale: At abstract stage, the study is a difference-in-differences/triple-difference comparison of a genAI-built ECG app (intervention site vs five control sites) in first-year medical students, which appears to fit intervention, comparison, design, and population. However, the only learning outcome is exam performance on ECG-focused vs non-ECG items, and the abstract reports the effect as null/inconsistent without giving statistics. The E5 code is applied tentatively because the abstract does not show a clear quantitative outcome suitable for SMD extraction; however, exam scores are quantitative, so this is not clear positive evidence of failure. Given the rule that abstract-stage exclusion requires positive evidence, this should be reconsidered. Domain is also ambiguous: ECG interpretation is medical education, which falls under health professions education and is excluded by the Domain criterion (E2 would apply as non-STEM). Because the record's exclusion rests on a health-professions domain, the most defensible code is E2, not E5.

quote: Student feedback is shown and a general positive and motivational impact is noted during and after the workshop.
rationale: The abstract describes a workshop application of LLM tools in software engineering courses, with student feedback and perceived positive impact as the reported results. It gives no separate control group without generative AI and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of failure exists for comparison (no control described) and outcome (only feedback/perceptions), so exclusion is warranted at abstract stage. Code E3 is applied as the first failing criterion in protocol order given the absence of any comparison group; E5 would also apply.

criteria.quote: we will conduct a qualitative research and observation of a class of mainly master's degree students
criteria.rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative research and observation of one class of 14 master's students giving weekly feedback. There is no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome; it is a qualitative design. Exclusion on E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported, though E5 (no quantitative outcome) and E6 (not an empirical study framing) would also apply. Abstract clearly lacks a comparison group, so E3 is the reported code.

quote: we will conduct a qualitative research and observation of a class of mainly master's degree students

We developed a five-step method to evaluate and address the impact of GenAI. Together with the respective lecturers, all assessments in the courses comprising a curriculum are analysed and subsequently adapted
rationale: The record is a curriculum/assessment analysis method paper with a case study. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no learner outcome data; assessments were analysed by lecturers, not learners interacting with GenAI in a learning activity. It is not an empirical comparison study, so it fails design, comparison, and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first clearly applicable code in the protocol order.

quote: Following IRB approval, the researchers examined world language instructors’ perceptions of using artificial intelligence for a variety of purposes
rationale: Record is a dissertation (publication type not eligible, E10), but the first applicable code in order is E2 is not STEM... Following protocol order, the earliest-applicable code: E1 is unclear. The study examines instructors' perceptions (survey-type, not an experiment with learner outcomes) and is in world language learning, which is non-STEM. Applying codes in order, E1 cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract, E2 applies because the content is world language (non-STEM). Therefore E2 is the first code that applies.

quote: Mixed-method and reflexive thematic analysis of the results showed that structured instructional exposure increased students’ confidence in using AI
rationale: Fashion design curriculum is not a STEM domain under the protocol (science, math, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, data science), so E2 applies first in code order. The study also uses mixed-method/thematic analysis with confidence and perception outcomes and no described control group, which would raise further concerns (E3, E5), but E2 is the first applicable code.

quote: This conceptual article examines resources for facilitating computational thinking (CT) in Massachusetts schools
rationale: The record is a conceptual article that argues for generative AI use in computational thinking instruction. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Other criteria are not reached because E6 is the first applicable code in the order listed.

quote: Adopting a quantitative, cross-sectional design, data were collected from MBA students using a structured Likert-scale questionnaire.
rationale: The design is a cross-sectional questionnaire study with correlation, regression, and mediation analysis, with no control group that avoids generative AI. Per the protocol, correlational and survey designs are excluded. Outcomes are self-reported Likert-scale perceptions, not a quantitative learning measure. MBA business content is also non-STEM. The primary exclusion is design (not an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison), which I coded as E6 (not an empirical study is the closest available code for a non-eligible design), but the strongest grounds are the absence of a comparison group and the non-STEM domain.

quote: The analysis of quantitative information was performed through descriptive statistics, reliability test, correlation and regression analysis
rationale: The abstract describes a questionnaire-based correlational/regression design on ChatGPT usage levels, with no control group that avoids generative AI and no experimental comparison. Design and comparison criteria fail on positive evidence. Domain is also not clearly STEM (critical thinking and academic writing). Excluded under E3 as the first applicable code in the ordering concerned with the comparison group; the design failure is equally evident.

quote: Title: Generative Artificial Intelligence in Health Care; Venue: The Journal of Urology; article type: Editorials
rationale: The record is an editorial (per its listed article type) on generative AI in health care. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no learning outcome. Under the protocol the appropriate code is E6 (not an empirical study). Editorials are also an ineligible publication type (E10), but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order's spirit as an empirical-study failure; the record is clearly not a primary study. The domain is health/urology, which is also outside STEM education scope.

quote: In a quasi-experimental design, participants with varying SRLs were assigned to either a tutor-feedback or GenAI-feedback group.
rationale: Abstract suggests a quasi-experiment with a human-tutor feedback comparison group, higher education, published 2026. GenAI feedback is delivered to learners, so intervention plausibly met. Domain is a nine-week statistics course, which fits STEM. The outcome includes self-regulation skills (goal-setting, overall SRL levels) and it is unclear whether these are quantitative learning measures or process/behavioural measures. Not enough to exclude; full text needed to check whether the outcome is a learning measure and whether GenAI feedback is learner-facing and the stats are reportable.

quote: The study used a pre-experimental, one-group pretest-posttest design with a cohort of 47 tenth-grade students
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pretest-posttest design with no separate control group that avoids generative AI, which fails the comparison and design criteria. This is positive evidence of E3 (one group measured before and after). Intervention generativity is also unclear (Canva AI), but the exclusion rests on the design. Note the abstract-stage rule was applied: the design is explicitly stated, so exclusion is justified.

quote: ChatGPT's KPSS knowledge and interpretation skills are significantly lower than the university graduate candidates who took the exam.
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT's answers to KPSS questions in Biology, History, Geography, Turkish Literature, and Social Studies, i.e., non-STEM content (E2). ChatGPT is evaluated directly rather than learners interacting with it in a learning activity, and there is no control group of learners. E2 is the first code that applies in order of the protocol's code list, given the domain failure is clear from the abstract.

quote: Undergraduates from two disciplines—Early Childhood Education (n = 32) and Computer Science (n = 34)—participated in this study
rationale: The abstract describes two groups from different disciplines that both undergo the same generative AI experimental condition ("both groups ... undergoing the same experimental condition"). There is no non-generative-AI control group, so the comparison criterion appears to fail (E3). Domain is also unclear given Early Childhood Education content, but E3 is the first applicable code given the positive evidence of a single AI condition for both groups.

quote: This study examines how upper secondary students engage with generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in science learning
rationale: The study is a constructivist grounded theory design based on semi-structured interviews with 21 students. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no effect-size data. It is qualitative, so it is not an empirical study in the quantitative sense the protocol requires. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study) at the abstract stage, since the abstract gives positive evidence of a qualitative design. The first applicable code in order would be E3 (no control group) or E5 (no quantitative outcome), but the qualitative design is the most direct failure. Study is upper secondary science, so domain and population are met.

quote: a survey was conducted among teaching staff at the Faculty of Computer Science and Engineering (FCSE) in Skopje to assess their ability to identify AI-generated essays
rationale: The study is a survey of teaching staff (in-service faculty judging AI-generated essays), not a controlled experiment with learners. There is no control group, no learner-facing generative AI intervention, and no learning outcome; the design is survey-based. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study is the closest fit, but the study is a survey, i.e. empirical; the first applicable code in order is E1 since AI is not used by learners in a learning activity). Judging strictly by protocol order, E1 applies first: no learner-facing generative AI intervention is described. Because the abstract gives clear positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing and the population is staff, this is excluded.

quote: The sample group comprised 32 lower secondary school students
rationale: The abstract describes a single group of 32 students measured with a paired t-test before and after the intervention, with no control group. This is a single-group pre-post design, which the protocol excludes under E3. Digital media literacy is also not clearly STEM content. E3 is applied as the first failing criterion in code order that the abstract gives positive evidence for.

quote: User acceptance was evaluated by first-year mechanical engineering students (N = 108) using an expanded Technology Acceptance Model instrument, and the results were analyzed via PLS-SEM.
rationale: The abstract reports only user acceptance and perceptions (TAM, PLS-SEM) with no quantitative learning outcome and no control group described. Evidence of a failed outcome criterion is positive here: the only outcome is perception-based, so it is excluded at E5. The design also appears to be a single-group acceptance survey, which would be E3/E6 at most, but E5 is the first applicable code in order of the protocol's listing that the abstract clearly supports.

quote: We used ChatGPT to solve all our coding assignments for the semester from our UPB Functional Programming course.
rationale: Abstract describes the authors using ChatGPT to solve coding assignments and assessing its outputs for correctness (68%). No control group of students or comparison condition is described, and no learning outcome from a comparison design is reported. This appears to be a descriptive evaluation of the tool's outputs rather than a controlled comparison, so the comparison and design criteria are not met. Exclusion code E3 applies, since there is no control group without generative AI.
rationale_note: Exclusion stated at abstract stage based on positive evidence of no control group.

quote: We conducted a mixed-methods study with 114 senior computer science and software engineering students
rationale: Abstract describes a single-group mixed-methods study of GitHub Copilot use by students, with descriptive statistics on acceptance perceptions. No control group without generative AI is described, so the comparison criterion fails (E3). Outcomes are perceptions/acceptance rather than a quantitative learning measure, which would also fail E5. Using the first applicable code in order, E3 is reported. Note the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group.

quote: A survey was conducted with 141 teachers as participants.
rationale: The study is a survey of 141 in-service teachers about their perceptions of ChatGPT. It is not an empirical experiment with a control group, has no learner participants, and reports no quantitative learning outcome. It is a survey design, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is used as the first applicable code in the order given; E4 (participants not students) would also apply, but the design failure is the more fundamental reason. Positive evidence of failure is present in the abstract.

quote: This quantitative descriptive study involved student nurses from Saint Louis University, Baguio City, selected through proportionate random sampling in February 2024.
rationale: Cross-sectional descriptive survey of ChatGPT use among student nurses with no control group and no learning outcome measured; the design is a survey, not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Nursing is a health profession, not STEM under the protocol's domain list. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code per the ordering of the protocol (no control group without generative AI); the study also lacks a quantitative learning outcome and is not a comparison design. Abstract evidence is clear enough to exclude.
rationale_note: Note: E2 (nursing is a health profession, not STEM) may arguably come first in code order; see note in the decision.

quote: Data were collected via pre- and post-tests and analyzed using Rasch analysis, ANCOVA, t-test, and DIF
rationale: Abstract describes ChatGPT-assisted PBL in physics vs a control class (quasi-experimental, with pre/post achievement tests), which passes intervention, comparison, design, domain, and outcome at abstract stage. Population is implied as students (65 students in classes) but school level is not stated; no positive evidence of failure, so include. Publication year 2025 meets date criterion. Full-text checks needed for data sufficiency and publication type.

quote: This study employed qualitative research methods.
rationale: The study is a qualitative survey of in-service high school teachers measuring ICT usage, satisfaction, and perceived impacts. It has no control group, no learner-outcome measure, and the sample is teachers rather than students. Exclusion is on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) since only perceptions and usage are reported; the design and population also fail the protocol, but E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order that is clearly evidenced at the abstract stage. Decision is clear from the abstract.

quote: This study investigates the use of ChatGPT among FCIC students through a descriptive-correlational research design
rationale: The study is a descriptive-correlational design examining usage and perceptions. It has no control group, no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome; the outcomes are usage extent and perceptions. Under the protocol this fails design, comparison, and outcome criteria. The code is E6 (not an empirical study) under the rule for the first applicable code is not quite the right fit, but the closest fit given the design is a non-experimental survey-type study. Note the protocol order puts E3 (no control group) before E5 and E6; the strongest positive evidence is the absence of a comparison group, which is E3, so the code should be reconsidered by the auditor. Decision is firm on exclusion.

quote: Practical teaching research conducted in two consecutive "C Language Programming" courses shows that this mode can significantly improve students' algorithm design and problem-solving abilities without the aid of AI
rationale: Programming course (STEM) in university students, with a claimed improvement in problem-solving ability. The abstract does not state whether a control group without generative AI exists (the design of the two consecutive courses is unclear, possibly sequential cohorts or a pre-post comparison). The intervention is a teaching-mode reform involving AI tools, and whether learners directly interact with a generative AI tool is not clear. Not clear-cut exclusion at the abstract stage, so advance to full text for checking of comparison, design, and intervention.

quote: "This study proposes a four-phase teaching framework ("rule-driven methods—statistical learning—deep learning—large model applications") tailored for application-oriented undergraduate institutions"
rationale: The abstract describes a curriculum/teaching framework proposal for NLP courses without any controlled comparison, experimental design, or quantitative learning outcome. It reads as a non-empirical reform proposal. Exclusion is based on positive evidence that the study is not an empirical comparison (E6). No quantitative outcome or control group is described. Exclusion is for E6 as the first applicable code in the order given; E5 would also plausibly apply.
rationale_note: Note: E6 is applied, though a design-based check at fulltext would confirm.

quote: We discuss two surveys conducted with pre-service teachers at two colleges in Israel, where students share experiences using ChatGPT.
rationale: The abstract describes two surveys of pre-service teachers about their ChatGPT experiences, which is a survey design with no control group lacking generative AI. The claim that ChatGPT use enhances learning performance is not based on a comparison group in the abstract. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI). The design is survey-based, so E6 (not an empirical study) could also be argued; E3 is applied as the first code that clearly fits the comparison requirement.

quote: A qualitative methodology, utilizing narrative inquiry, was employed to gather data from three university-level English educators
rationale: Study is about English language teaching (non-STEM content), so E2 applies as the first failing code in order that is clearly evidenced. It is also a qualitative design with no control group or quantitative learning outcome (E3/E5/E6 would also apply), but E2 is the first in protocol order that the abstract clearly shows. Note the ordering: E1 is not triggered since AI is used by learners/teachers, and population concerns university educators rather than students, which is a further mismatch.

quote: Educators (n=20) were purposively sampled to be interviewed about their experiences in using AI in their classrooms.
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of educators, not an experimental or quasi-experimental study with a control group and learning outcomes. It has no quantitative learning outcome and the participants are in-service educators rather than students. Excluded under E6 as a non-empirical-comparative (qualitative) design; the population criterion also fails since participants are teachers, not students.

quote: The purpose of this study is to analyze topics of media reports regarding generative artificial intellignece and education.
rationale: The study is a topic-model analysis of newspaper articles, not an empirical learner-facing intervention study. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study of the eligible type (E6). Abstract gives positive evidence of failure, so exclude.

quote: Using a qualitative and analytical research approach based on secondary data, the study reviews scholarly literature, educational reports, policy documents, and recent developments in AI-assisted learning.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative, secondary-data literature review, not an empirical experiment. There is no control group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. The study is not an empirical study (E6). Its STEM domain and population are not specified. Under the rule that exclusion requires positive evidence, the abstract's design statement is sufficient for E6.

quote: The survey for this study was created by a library student team and vetted through focus groups.
rationale: The study is a survey of student perspectives on generative AI. It is not an empirical experiment with a control group and reports only perceptions and attitudes, not a quantitative learning outcome. The design is a survey, which is not eligible, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible designs). No STEM content is described and no comparison group exists, so the record fails multiple criteria; E6 is applied as the first code that clearly applies in order of the protocol's ordering, since E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract.

criteria.quote: Using qualitative methods, the study explores how students develop debugging skills
criteria.rationale: Dissertation (not a journal article) using qualitative methods; evaluation is anonymous student feedback on confidence, with no quantitative learning outcome or control group described. Abstract gives positive evidence of non-empirical-eligible design (qualitative) and no comparison group. Coded E6 as the most fitting first-applicable reason; the publication-type issue (dissertation, E10) would also apply. Intervention generative nature is also not stated in the abstract.

quote: Using qualitative methods, the study explores how students develop debugging skills in a CS program
rationale: Record is a dissertation with qualitative methods and feedback-based evaluation (perceptions of confidence). No control group and no quantitative learning outcome are described. Coded E6 (not an empirical study eligible under the design) — note it is also a dissertation, which falls under E10 publication-type exclusion. Protocol says report the first code that applies in order; E1 cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract because generative AI use by learners is not mentioned, but the intervention is not described as generative. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of qualitative design and perception-only outcomes.

quote: Through an action research study situated in a Grade 10 English classroom, the study examines the key conditions that facilitated students' critical questioning with GenAI.
rationale: The abstract describes an action research study with ethnographic methods (observations, interviews, chatlogs) in a Grade 10 English classroom. It reports no control group or comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome. The content is English language, which is non-STEM. Positive evidence of failure exists for comparison/design (no comparison group), so exclude. Under the protocol order, E1 does not apply (students do interact with GenAI), E2 would also apply because the content is English, but the first applicable code in order is E2 (content not STEM) before E3. Coding as E2 is the correct first code.

quote: This paper attempts to describe the advances and applications of three large language models: ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and Grok.
rationale: The record is a review study describing LLM chatbots, not an empirical study with a control group or learning outcome. It is also framed around English education, which falls outside the STEM domain. Positive evidence of failure on E6 (not an empirical study) is present in the abstract, so it is excluded at the abstract stage. Domain (English education is non-STEM) also appears to fail, but the first applicable code in protocol order is E2 only if E6 were not applicable; per the rule of reporting the first code in order, E6 is listed first because the review nature is the earliest decisive failure.

quote: Experiments are conducted on three few-shot settings across six biomedical benchmark datasets.
rationale: The study is about biomedical NLP model training (few-shot text classification/extraction with LLM-derived explanations used as training supervision), not learners interacting with generative AI in a STEM learning activity. Content is biomedical text mining, not science/math/engineering/CS education, so it fails the Domain criterion (E2). Also, no learner population is evident. Excluded at abstract stage on the clear positive evidence of non-STEM, non-learner content; first applicable code in order would be E1 (the intervention is not learner-facing), but the clearest failure is domain.
