quote: Scoutlier EngagEd, a digital teaching assistant that embeds in existing Learning Management Systems (LMS) to automatically and invisibly gather multidimensional data on student engagement and performance
rationale: The LLM generates recommendations for teachers; the tool is not described as learner-facing. The abstract says the LLM produces actionable recommendations "for teachers," and the system gathers engagement data invisibly. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, so E1 applies. No comparison group or learning outcome is described in the abstract either, and the study appears to be a development paper.
rationale_note: Teacher-facing LLM recommendations; E1 applies at the first failing criterion.

quote: The results reveal that AI tools such as ChatGPT have revolutionized personalized learning by offering tailored feedback, enhancing critical thinking, and improving student engagement.
rationale: The record is a bibliometric analysis (co-citation, keyword analysis, trend mapping), not an empirical learner study. It has no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome data for an SMD. Under E6 (not an empirical study) it is excluded. E6 is the first applicable code in the order that is supported by the abstract; the earlier codes (E1, E2) are not clearly failed on the abstract alone, since it is about STEM and generative AI, so E6 is the primary reason.

quote: We tested the LLMs on 14 progressively complex C programming tasks.
rationale: The study evaluates LLMs directly on programming tasks and compares their success rates with students' solutions from an assessment system. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; the LLMs are benchmarked as standalone performers. There is no control group of learners without generative AI. This fails the intervention criterion (E1) and the comparison criterion. Exclusion code E1 is reported first in order since it applies.

criteria.comparison_note: no learner-facing GenAI use with a control group evident

quote: We use a large language model (LLM) to solve ten standard textbook exercises 100 times for each question and analyse the answers
rationale: The study has the LLM solve textbook problems itself, 100 times per question, to compare its answers with students' answers. There is no learner interacting with the LLM and no control group. The abstract gives no quantitative learning outcome for learners. Exclusion code is E5 as the first clearly failing criterion under the code order. Strictly, the intervention criterion (E1) also fails, since the LLM is not used by learners. The code order puts E1 first, so the code should arguably be E1. Recording E1 as the first applicable code under the rules.

quote: Design – Survey research. Setting – A university library in Nigeria.
rationale: The study is a survey of students' perceptions of ChatGPT versus reference librarians, with no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an eligible design. Per the protocol's exclusion order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly established as failing from the abstract alone, so the first clearly applicable code is E3 (no control group without generative AI). Domain (library reference consultation) is also not STEM and the outcome is perception/usage only, so E2 and E5 would also apply; E3 is reported as the first code in the order that is unambiguous for the design. Given the abstract's positive evidence of a survey design, exclusion is appropriate.
quote_final: Design – Survey research. Setting – A university library in Nigeria.

quote: The article deals with the description of an experiment, a kind of empirical study, which was carried out in one of the Polytechnic Universities of Ukraine.
rationale: The study uses ChatGPT to explain English grammar articles to Ukrainian students, which is language learning, not STEM content. The abstract gives positive evidence of a non-STEM domain, so it is excluded under E2. The mention of engineering students does not make the content STEM. Comparison, design, and outcome are not reported in the abstract, but the domain failure is sufficient.

quote: This TREO talk presents a mixed-methods learning analytics study of a custom Socratic AI tutor in an introductory Python course.
rationale: The record is a TREO talk, not a journal article reporting a comparative empirical design. The abstract describes a mixed-methods learning analytics study that correlates survey measures with chat-log behavior (correlational, no control group evident). It reports no control condition without generative AI, so the design does not appear to meet the randomized or quasi-experimental requirement. The record is also not clearly an empirical journal article, so E6 is the first applicable code at abstract stage under the protocol ordering. Intervention (generative LLM tutor) and domain (Python programming) and population (introductory students) appear to be met. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of a correlational, non-comparative design. Note: the publication type (TREO talk in a journal venue) may also warrant checking against E10.

quote: the experimental class with a total of 26 people, and ordinary treatment (learning using conventional models) to the control class with a total of 25 students
rationale: Abstract describes Gemini AI (generative LLM) learning media used by learners in an experimental class versus a conventional-learning control class, with pre/post test of mathematical concept understanding in 2025 (secondary vocational school students). All criteria appear met at abstract stage; SMD computability, journal status and full-text language are not verifiable from the abstract, so no exclusion is made. Advance to full text.

quote: Our approach leverages chatGPT's capabilities to optimize client-side scripts for server-side implementation efficiently
rationale: ChatGPT is used by developers/teachers to write Roblox game code, not as a learner-facing tool in the learning activity. Students only provided feedback on the resulting experience. This fails E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI). The study also reports feedback/engagement rather than a clear quantitative learning outcome with a control group, and no comparison group is described in the abstract.

quote: I argue that linguistic analysis is essential for understanding how GenAI constructs agency
rationale: The article is a position/argument piece ("I argue", "In this article, I posit") drawing on a research program, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Domain is also not clearly STEM. No eligible comparison or outcome is reported in the abstract.

quote: The study employed a qualitative descriptive research design involving 36 fifth-grade students
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative descriptive design with a single group of 36 students and no control group, so no comparison without generative AI is evident. Design is qualitative, not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. News writing is also a language/literacy topic rather than STEM. Exclusion code E3 is applied as the first failing criterion in the ordered list for the comparison and design failure. The abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted with 262 undergraduate and postgraduate students from nine Nigerian higher education institutions.
rationale: Cross-sectional survey with no experimental or quasi-experimental control group; there is no comparison condition and no learning outcome measured (perceptions and self-reported behavior only). Design and outcome criteria are clearly not met, and the absence of a control group is the first applicable code in the protocol's order (E3 precedes E5 and E6 for this purpose, though E6 - not an empirical study in the experimental sense - would also apply since it is a survey). Per the code order, E3 is reported. Domain is also not clearly STEM at abstract stage.

quote: The study evaluates the impact of four key variables—perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, information seeking, and novelty—on students’ intention to use ChatGPT for learning activities.
rationale: The study is a survey-based SEM analysis of perceptions and intention to use ChatGPT. It has no control group and no learning outcome measure; the outcome is behavioral intention (a perception measure), which is not a quantitative learning outcome. Design is correlational/survey, and the domain (office administration) is not clearly STEM. The exclusion code E5 is applied as the first failing criterion checked in order that is positively evidenced by the abstract; E3 (no control group) also applies, but the protocol requires the first applicable code in order, and E3 precedes E5, so the code should be reconsidered: E3 is the first applicable code in the sequence. On reflection, the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group, so E3 is the correct first code.
exclusion_code_note: Corrected: E3 is the first applicable code.

quote: Results showed that the AI chatbot and the tiered support system were associated with significantly lower perceived intrinsic and extraneous cognitive load than textual support.
rationale: The study uses a cluster randomized design with a non-AI control (textual support) and ninth-grade STEM (physics) participants, and the chatbot is learner-facing generative AI. However, the outcomes are perceived cognitive load and affective-motivational measures (enjoyment, hope, hopelessness, self-efficacy, interest) only. No quantitative learning outcome such as achievement, conceptual knowledge, or problem-solving performance is reported, and affective outcomes are not extracted under the protocol. Perceived cognitive load is a self-report, not a learning measure. Excluded under E5. Intervention being generative is stated only as "AI chatbot" in the abstract; the custom-configured chatbot is presumably LLM-based, but this is not confirmed at abstract stage, and the exclusion rests on the outcome criterion.

The abstract describes a comparison of three LLMs (ChatGPT, Bard, Llama 2) on tutoring tasks, judged by a human tutor. There is no control group without generative AI, and the comparison is only between generative AI variants, which the protocol excludes under E3. The study also appears to evaluate model outputs rather than learner outcomes, so it is not a learner-facing learning study with a quantitative learning outcome. E3 is the first applicable code in order that the abstract supports. Middle school math (STEM) and the population are met.

quote: The study investigates the acceptance level of AI chatbots among college students
rationale: The study is a quantitative survey of acceptance of AI chatbots among college students. It reports perceptions/acceptance rather than a quantitative learning outcome, and it has no control group or comparison design (E5 applies). Domain is not STEM-specific per abstract (major disciplines only as a moderator). Exclusion on E5 is the first applicable code given the abstract: the outcome is perception-only, which the protocol excludes.
rationale_note: Exclusion code E3 (no control group) would also be supported by the design; E5 is reported as the first code applicable in the protocol's order that is clearly evidenced.

rationale: The abstract describes a proposed framework for a generative AI-based adaptive learning system and says the research will analyze existing tutoring systems to propose a framework. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome data. This is a design/conceptual proposal, so E6 (not an empirical study) applies. Abstract gives positive evidence of non-empirical nature, so exclusion is warranted.

quote: Using openAI's flagship gpt-3.5-turbo large language model (LLM), we assessed its ability to answer 1337 physics exam questions
rationale: The study evaluates the LLM's answers to exam questions directly rather than learners interacting with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity. There is no control group without generative AI; the design is a benchmark evaluation of model performance. Excluded at E3 (no comparison group). Strictly, the first applicable code in order would be E1 (intervention is not learner-facing), since the LLM is not used by learners; however, the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group as well. Coding E1 as the first applicable code in order.

quote: An exploratory qualitative design was employed with 12 Informatics teachers from a college specializing in Informatics education.
rationale: The study is an exploratory qualitative interview study of teachers' perceptions, not an empirical comparative study with a control group or a quantitative learning outcome. It is not an eligible design. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is applied as the first code that clearly fits, since the design is qualitative. Note that E6 is applied on the basis of qualitative design; the protocol's design exclusion for qualitative designs is also clearly failed. No quantitative learning outcome is reported.

quote: The study uses a descriptive qualitative approach with documentation study methods, observation, and interactive analysis.
rationale: ChatGPT is used by teachers as a supervision tool to analyze RPP and LKPD documents, not as a learner-facing intervention (E1). The design is a descriptive qualitative study with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it would also fail E3, E5 and E6 on the abstract. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Through a questionnaire survey conducted at the Hunan Institute of Technology, the study uncovers a majority inclination to incorporate generative AI as an auxiliary tool in education.
rationale: The abstract describes a questionnaire survey of perceptions, use, and attitudes among undergraduates. This is a survey design, not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a control group, and it reports no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of failure on design and outcome criteria supports exclusion. E6 (not an empirical study) is the closest code, since survey designs are excluded as non-experimental; the protocol's exclusion list for design explicitly names surveys.

quote: The present study synthesizes published systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and bibliometric studies to examine six central concerns
rationale: This is an evidence synthesis (review of reviews and bibliometric studies), not an empirical primary study with a control group. It fails the eligibility requirement for an empirical design (E6). It also does not report its own effect sizes; the generative AI effect size it cites (g ≈ 1.02) comes from other reviews, so it cannot count as an eligible primary study.

quote: A total of 100 cases of school-age children aged 6–12 were collected from the standardized intervention archive of our institution
rationale: Abstract-stage screening. The study is a retrospective archive-based comparison of two intervention groups, not a randomized or quasi-experimental design with a comparison group in the protocol sense; it is a retrospective control study with groups formed by the intervention plan actually accepted. Participants are children aged 6–12 (school-age, reading-focused early literacy), and the reading content is not clearly STEM. Strictly, the design criterion is doubtful and the population/domain fit is questionable, but the abstract does not present a clear control without generative AI (both groups use generative AI), which is the first ordered exclusion code applicable: E3 (both arms receive generative AI; the comparison is between two generative AI-based interventions). Note the abstract gives positive evidence that the comparison is between two generative AI variants, so E3 is the best-fitting code. Reviewer may wish to confirm at full text if reconsidered.

quote: This article examines the opportunities, challenges, and ethical considerations associated with the use of Generative AI in higher education.
rationale: The abstract describes a discussion/review article on opportunities, challenges and ethics of generative AI in higher education. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. The E1 check was considered first, but the abstract gives no learner-facing intervention details; E6 is the first code that clearly applies to the stated content. No injection was observed.

criteria.rationale_note: Survey-based correlational study of use and attitudes

quote: The study aimed to shed light on the relationship between the use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) by student teachers
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive, analytical, comparative questionnaire study examining self-reported use, ethical awareness and attitudes toward generative AI. There is no experimental intervention in which learners use a GAI tool as part of a learning activity, and no control group without GAI. Outcomes are perceptions and usage, not a quantitative learning measure. Under the protocol, the correlational survey design fails the comparison and design criteria; the first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI). Note the abstract-stage rule allows exclusion only on positive evidence, and the abstract gives clear evidence of a survey design with no intervention or learning outcome.

quote: Questionnaires from 86 students across three majors indicated generally high satisfaction.
rationale: The intervention is LLM use by medical students, and the population is undergraduate medical students. However, the content domain is bioethics training within a medical cell biology laboratory course, which is not science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, or programming. Under the protocol's domain criterion and exclusion code order, E2 applies first (content not STEM). Positive evidence of non-STEM content is present in the abstract, so exclusion at the abstract stage is justified. Additional concerns: the design is described as quasi-experimental but the comparison appears to be between LLMs and satisfaction ratings, with outcomes mostly perceptions, which may also fail E3/E5.

quote: This study investigates EFL learners’ perceptions of using ChatGPT as a supporting tool for academic writing
rationale: Descriptive survey study of student perceptions only. No control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and the domain is EFL academic writing, which is non-STEM. Excluded at abstract stage on the first applicable code in order. E5 is the first code that applies to the outcome failure, but E2 (non-STEM content) and E3 (no control group) also apply on the abstract's positive evidence; E2 comes earlier in the code order, so E2 is the correct first code. Recording E2 as the primary exclusion.

quote: Medical schools of South Asian countries need to incorporate artificial intelligence-powered chatbots in existing undergraduate medical curricula
rationale: The record is a commentary/editorial-style piece arguing that medical schools should incorporate chatbots. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Medical education is also health-related, but E6 is decisive as the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's logic for non-empirical records.

quote: Thematic analysis of 258 students' reflection, triangulated with academic performance data, revealed four key themes
rationale: The study is a qualitative thematic analysis of student reflections with no control group and no experimental comparison, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. Students use GenAI in a business data analysis assessment, a higher-education context with a data-analysis (STEM-adjacent) focus. Coding E3 as the first failing criterion in the order used is a judgment call; the design is best described as non-experimental, which may also be E6 (not an empirical study is not quite right, since it is empirical). Exclusion is clear from the abstract because the design is described as qualitative with no comparison group. Injection not suspected.

quote: A cross‐sectional survey was administered to 1039 undergraduate medical students across Saudi Arabia.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey measuring perceptions and attitudes only, with no learner interaction with a generative AI tool, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical experimental study of learning. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is used as the design is survey-based, which fits the protocol's exclusion of survey designs; E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) would also apply. The abstract itself states findings reflect perceptions, not measured educational effectiveness. Medical education is health professions education, which is also outside the STEM domain.

criteria.stage_note: Mixed-methods case study; no control group described in abstract

quote: Across all assessments, GenAI users achieved slightly higher scores, although differences were not statistically significant
rationale: The abstract describes a mixed-methods case study examining how students used GenAI across three assessments, comparing GenAI users with non-users only on scores. It gives no separate control group design, and the design is described as a case study, which points to no comparison group that meets the protocol. Positive evidence of a missing control condition is present (case study framing, comparison is between users of GenAI within one unit), so E3 is applied. Population (undergraduate physics) and domain are met; the intervention is learner-facing GenAI use. Although the comparison is between GenAI users and non-users, this is observational use-based grouping within a single case study rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison group, so the design criterion is not met.

criteria.quote: A literature review and analysis of AI applications in education focused on adaptive learning technologies, interactive simulations, and AI-driven feedback systems.
criteria.rationale: Abstract describes a literature review and conceptual analysis, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. Exclude at E6 (not an empirical study). The abstract gives positive evidence of a review design, so exclusion is warranted even under the abstract-stage rule.

quote: A literature review and analysis of AI applications in education focused on adaptive learning technologies, interactive simulations, and AI-driven feedback systems.
rationale: The abstract describes a literature review and analysis rather than an empirical study. There is no described control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Coded E6 as the first applicable code in order that is supported by the text. Note that E3 and E5 would also likely apply, but E6 comes first in the code list only if ordered before them; per the protocol order E1 and E2 do not apply (ChatGPT is mentioned and physics is STEM), so E3 would precede E6 by number. Given the protocol's stated order (E1 to E10), the strictly first applicable code is E3 (no control group without generative AI), since the paper reports no comparison group. Reviewing for the stated order, E3 is the correct code.

quote: A quantitative cross-sectional survey involving 430 students who had used ChatGPT for physics learning was conducted.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of students' perceptions with no control group, so no comparison without generative AI exists (E3). It also reports only perceptions and usage with a correlation, not a quantitative learning outcome collected after an intervention. Under the rule of first applicable code, E3 is reported. Design is a survey, which the protocol excludes.

criteria.stage_note: EFL writing task; no comparison group evident

quote: This study examines the content and sequencing of prompts that English as a foreign language (EFL) secondary students used with no prior instruction to complete a writing task using ChatGPT.
rationale: The study concerns EFL writing, which is language learning and not STEM content, so E2 applies. The abstract also describes a qualitative case-based study of prompt content with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so E3 and E5 would apply as well; E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order.

quote: The study used a Research and Development approach organized with the ADDIE framework and a one-group pretest-posttest evaluation involving 60 fourth-grade students.
rationale: The study is a one-group pretest-posttest design with no separate control group that does not use generative AI, which the protocol explicitly excludes (E3). The abstract also states the design had no comparison group or randomization. Other criteria appear met (LLM chatbot, elementary fractions, quantitative pre/post scores), but the comparison failure is decisive.

criteria.domain_note: science education implied but not explicit

quote: A total of 62 primary school students participated in a four-week experiment, in which the quantitative and qualitative data were collected
rationale: Primary school students (K-12) with quantitative outcomes (critical thinking, inquisitiveness, motivation) are reported. The abstract describes an AR-based embodied conversational agent called Virtual Scientist, but does not state whether the agent is built on a generative model; the title says Generative AI, so this is plausibly met but not confirmed. The abstract does not describe a control group, so comparison and design cannot be judged. The domain is hinted at as science education but not stated explicitly. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so this stays unsure for full-text review. Note: the outcome is affective-leaning (motivation, inquisitiveness); the protocol excludes affective outcomes from extraction, which should be checked at full text along with critical thinking.

quote: Los resultados indican que los estudiantes valoraron positivamente la utilidad, precisión y facilidad de uso de ChatGPT
rationale: The abstract reports only student and faculty perceptions (utility, ease of use, attitudes) and faculty survey use; there is no quantitative learning outcome and no control group described. Exclude on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), since perceptions-only studies fail the outcome criterion. Design also appears to be survey-based, with no comparison group evident.

quote: directly assess student learning outcomes
rationale: The study scores LLM response quality via a rubric by reviewers; it does not measure student learning outcomes, and the authors state that assessing student learning is future work. There is no learner-facing comparison with a control group. Excluded under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). The abstract gives positive evidence of no student learning measure, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: we systematically screen 5309268 articles from key journals up to 2024, and accurately extract 124021 papers related to batteries
rationale: The study evaluates LLMs for literature screening, data extraction, and database construction in battery research. It involves no learners interacting with generative AI, no control group, no learning outcome, and no students or participants. It is not an empirical learning intervention study meeting the protocol. Excluded under E6 as not an empirical study of learner-facing generative AI; E1 (intervention not learner-facing) would also apply, and the first applicable code in order is E1, so E1 is arguably the correct first code.

quote: The personalized LLM approach achieves 89.7% accuracy compared to 91.4% for human instructors while reducing response time from 1,248 seconds to 12.3 seconds.
rationale: Abstract describes an LLM feedback framework in STEM education with effect sizes reported, which suggests a comparison and quantitative outcome. However, the abstract does not state the control condition, the study design (randomized or quasi-experimental), or the learner population level, so these cannot be confirmed. Abstract-stage rule: do not exclude on missing information; advance to full text to check the comparison group, design, and whether the outcomes are learning measures rather than engagement or accuracy of feedback.

quote: A descriptive survey research design was adopted, with a population comprising students from eight public and private universities.
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of students' awareness and adoption of AI tools, with no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group and no learning outcome measured. Survey designs are excluded and the study reports perceptions and usage only. The code E6 (not an empirical study) is not strictly accurate because the study is empirical, but the design fails the Design and Outcome criteria. Under the rule that the first applicable code in order is reported, E1 and E2 could not be confirmed as applying from the abstract, E3 is the next in sequence and applies to the absence of a control group, so E3 is the more precise first failing code. Note: applying the order strictly, E3 is the first code that applies, so the exclusion code should be E3, not E6.

quote: We also conducted surveys and discussions with mathematics and statistics students and staff at the University of Warwick.
rationale: The abstract describes genAI performance on assignments, plus surveys and discussions. There is no control group comparing learners with and without genAI, and no quantitative learning outcome measured after an intervention. Design appears to be survey/investigative rather than experimental. Per the code order, E1 is not clearly applicable (intervention unclear), so E3 is the first clear failure (no comparison group). Note that E5 or E6 could also apply; E3 is reported as the first clearly failing criterion in order. The record is excluded on positive evidence of absent comparison.

quote: Five LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, Grok3.0, Claude4Sonnet, Gemini2.5 Flash, DeepSeekR1) were used to generate responses to six frequently asked questions about body donation in Turkish.
rationale: The LLMs generate materials evaluated by anatomists; learners do not interact with the LLM as part of a learning activity, so intervention is not learner-facing (arguably E1). No learner population is described (participants are expert raters, and the topic is body donation communication, not STEM learning). The study compares LLMs with each other and reports expert-rated quality and readability, not a learning outcome from students. Under the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E1 would apply first because the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI. Correct code is E1, not E5, given the order rule.

quote: This conceptual paper proposes the Dialogue-to-Depth model as a theory-building framework
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual paper proposing a theoretical model with a research agenda; it reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. The quote is from the abstract and supports the conceptual, non-empirical nature of the paper.

quote: The study employed a qualitative approach using a dual-case study design
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative dual-case study with interviews, observation, and document analysis. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Design is qualitative, so the record fails the comparison and design criteria. Under the rule that the first applicable code is reported, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first failing criterion in order. The study also has no quantitative outcome (E5), but E3 comes first. Domain is unclear from the abstract, as it does not name a STEM subject.
decision_note: Abstract-stage exclusion based on positive evidence of qualitative design with no comparison group.

quote: Participants (N = 84) from EFL academic writing classes responded to a prompt on how they perceive the impacts of AI on English education.
rationale: The study concerns English as a foreign language education (non-STEM content), so E2 applies. It is also a perception-based prompt response study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, which would fail E3 and E5 as well. The first applicable code in order is E2, since E1 is not clearly established at abstract stage.

quote: The study employs a qualitative embedded case study design involving AI prompt writing, lesson planning, classroom observations, a focus group discussion, and a semi-structured interview.
rationale: English language learning (ESL) is non-STEM content, so E2 applies first in the protocol order. The design is also a qualitative embedded case study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (E3/E5 would also apply), but the first applicable code in order is E2. The teacher uses ChatGPT to adapt materials, which additionally suggests E1.

quote: The study was conducted using the general survey model, and the participant group consisted of 468 middle school students.
rationale: Abstract describes a general survey model examining relationships between technology-related variables and self-regulation/SDL. No intervention in which learners interact with generative AI is described; no experimental or comparison group is present. Survey/correlational design with no control group fails the comparison and design criteria. Under the abstract rule, exclusion is supported by positive evidence of a survey design (not an experiment), and the protocol excludes survey designs. Coded E3 (no control group without generative AI) as the first applicable code in order given the absence of any intervention-comparison structure; AI usage competence is a correlational variable, not an intervention.

criteria.outcome_note: pilot compared with static platforms; control design not described in abstract

quote: A 60-day pilot study involving 120 undergraduate students demonstrated a 34.7% improvement in problem acceptance rates
rationale: Programming domain, undergraduate population, and ChatGPT API-based platform appear to meet criteria. The abstract mentions comparison with static platforms, but it is unclear whether this is a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison group or a pre-post pilot; the 34.7% improvement may be a pre-post change, which would be E3. Not excluded at abstract stage because the design is not positively shown to fail. Needs full text to check the comparison design and whether the problem acceptance outcome is a learning measure.

quote: The participants of this training were 35 EFL teachers of state and private vocational high schools located in Eastern Jakarta, Indonesia.
rationale: Study concerns English as a foreign language (non-STEM content) and involves in-service teachers. It is a descriptive community service training with questionnaire data only, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion is based on the first applicable code in order; E2 (non-STEM content) applies first on the abstract's positive evidence of English learning content.

quote: This research aims to analyze the development of the ChatGPT topic in the context of its utilization and the challenges in supporting 21st-century education and learning programs
rationale: The abstract describes a literature review (method: "a literature review related to ChatGPT"), not an empirical study with a comparison group or quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies as the first failing code in order (E1 through E5 cannot be confirmed from the abstract, but E6 is the decisive positive evidence).

quote: Doctrinal and comparative legal analysis methods to evaluate the efficacy of the EU AI Act and China's Interim Measures for the Management of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services
rationale: The study is a doctrinal and comparative legal analysis of regulations, not an empirical study. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first code that applies in the protocol order, since E1 (intervention) is arguably not met either but the study does not evaluate any learner-facing tool empirically.
decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of non-empirical legal design.
quote_verbatim: Doctrinal and comparative legal analysis methods

quote: the experimental group received AI-guided training, and the control group was taught through traditional instruction
rationale: The study concerns English-Arabic translation training, which is a language/humanities domain and not STEM. Protocol explicitly excludes language learning and other non-STEM content, so E2 applies. Other criteria appear plausibly met at abstract level, but the domain failure is determinative.

quote: Outputs produced by two GenAI models, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o, were assessed for reliability with a human coder.
rationale: The study evaluates GenAI model output reliability against a human coder, not learners' learning outcomes. There is no learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome measured. It is not a learner study. Exclusion on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the best fit at abstract stage, since the reported measure is model classification reliability rather than student learning. Positive evidence of failure is present for the outcome criterion and the comparison criterion (only two GenAI models compared).

Outcomes are described qualitatively (manual work satisfactory, reflections), with no clear quantitative learning measure or effect-size data.
decision_note: Exclusion code E3 applied at abstract stage on positive evidence of no control group.

The record is not an empirical learning study meeting the protocol; E6 is applied as the design is a comparison of chatbot outputs rather than a learning study. Under the rule that the first applicable code is reported, E1 (not learner-facing) could also be argued, but the record is best captured as non-empirical for learning purposes. Abstract-stage exclusion is supported by positive evidence on several criteria.

Excluded on the first applicable code in order; E5 is the earliest-listed code that clearly applies from the abstract (E2 also applies on domain, but is listed earlier, so the ordering matters: E2 precedes E5). Correcting: the first applicable code in protocol order is E2 because the content is EFL language learning, not STEM.

Whether the neutral-feedback control is a non-generative comparison is also unclear, since it may also be generative AI. Venue is a Korean society and the record does not confirm journal-article status. No positive evidence of failure at abstract stage, so advance to full text.

quote: Each question included eight human-generated responses and two from GPT-4.

This is positive evidence that the comparison criterion fails, so E3 applies. Note the abstract also suggests the GPT-4 responses were rated rather than used by learners, which would be E1, but the first applicable code in the protocol order is E1 only if intervention clearly fails; since learner-facing use is not clearly absent from the abstract alone, E3 is given as the clearest failing criterion.

There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design with a control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the study is not an empirical intervention study. Entrepreneurship education is also not clearly STEM. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study of the eligible type); the survey-based design fails the design and outcome criteria regardless. Generative AI appears only as a suggested supportive tool, not a tested intervention.

quote: this paper looks at three case studies of genAI use in education representing different levels of disruptiveness
rationale: The paper is about language education (TESOL), which is non-STEM content and is excluded by the protocol. It also describes three case studies and a conceptual analysis, not a controlled experiment with a comparison group or a quantitative learning outcome. E2 is the first applicable code in order for this abstract-stage exclusion.

quote: A Likert-scale survey was used to obtain data on frequency of usage, perception of use, perception of utility, prompt effort, and ethical awareness when using ChatGPT.
rationale: The study is a descriptive quantitative survey of student perceptions with no control group and no learning outcome measured; outcomes are perceptions and usage only. It fails the comparison and design criteria (E3 would also apply), but E5 is the first code applicable after the E1-E4 checks pass (ChatGPT is learner-facing, organic chemistry is STEM, students are higher education). Under the protocol's ordering, E3 precedes E5, so the first applicable code is E3 — noted here: the no-control-group failure is the earliest applicable code.

quote: Pre- and post-intervention data were collected using validated instruments that measured digital technology self-efficacy and AI-integrated teaching competence.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pre-post design with 16 preservice teachers and paired-sample t-tests, with no control group. Per the protocol and borderline rule ("One group measured before and after: E3"), this fails the comparison and design criteria. Exclusion code E3 applies. Intervention, population, and outcome are not clearly contradictory but the design failure is decisive.

quote: This study takes the application of generative artificial intelligence technology in high school geography teaching as the research object, aiming to explore its value, limitations and improvement strategies.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/discussion paper: it compares mainstream AI systems and proposes strategies, with no experimental design, no comparison group, and no learning outcome measured. Positive evidence of a non-empirical study, so E6. Geography is also not clearly STEM (E2 would be an alternative, but E6 applies first in the code order given the nature of the paper is non-empirical... note: E2 precedes E6 in order; geography is a social/earth science with ambiguous STEM status, so this exclusion rests mainly on E6 as the abstract gives no evidence of STEM content beyond geography).

quote: Employing a phenomenological approach within the qualitative paradigm and guided by Diffusion of Innovations (DOI) theory, this study explored the lived experiences of seven purposively selected secondary school STEM teachers
rationale: Qualitative phenomenological study of in-service teachers' perceptions; no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no quantitative learning outcome. Not an empirical study meeting the design requirements; the ChatGPT use is for analysing transcripts by researchers, not learner-facing. Under the code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) applies first because the only AI use is researcher-side transcript analysis.
rationale_note: Correction: first applicable code in order is E1, not E6. Decision recorded as exclude with E1 below.

quote: A grounded theory design was adopted.
rationale: The study is a grounded theory qualitative design using interviews, artifacts, and stimulated-recall discussions. It has no control group without generative AI, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. It also reports no quantitative learning outcome. Under the code order, E1 does not apply (learners use GenAI), and E3 is the first failing criterion that applies to a design with no comparison group. Note that the protocol lists E5 (no quantitative outcome) and E6 (not an empirical study) too; the qualitative design is empirical, so E3 is chosen as the first applicable code in order on comparison grounds.

quote: The experimental group used SRLbot to maintain a regular study habit and facilitate their SRL, while the control group utilized rule‐based AI chatbots.
rationale: At abstract stage, a generative AI chatbot (SRLbot, ChatGPT-based) is compared with a rule-based chatbot control, which is a non-generative comparison and qualifies under the protocol. Secondary 4 science students, with knowledge outcomes reported. Design (randomized or quasi-experimental status) and effect-size data are not stated in the abstract, so these are left unclear for full-text verification; the paper is also described as a "case study", which needs checking against the design criterion. Advancing to full text.

quote: Specifically, we utilized Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), a prominent PEFT technique, to fine-tune three state-of-the-art LLMs—Llama-3.2-3B, Gemma-2-9B, and Mistral-7B-v0.3—targeting the analysis of both teachers' and students' dialogic moves within K12 mathematics lessons.
rationale: The study fine-tunes LLMs to classify dialogue moves in classroom transcripts; the LLMs are used as analysis tools by researchers, not as a learner-facing generative AI tool in a learning activity. No learner interaction with generative AI is described, and no control group without generative AI is evident (comparisons are against BERT/RoBERTa and prompting, which are not learning-condition controls). Excluded under E1 at the abstract stage on positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing.

quote: A mixed-methods approach was used. First, Gemini's feedback on students' assignments was analyzed using specific rubrics. Second, a questionnaire was used to survey students' perceptions
rationale: Study analyzes Gemini feedback on student writing and surveys perceptions. No control group without generative AI is described, and the design is descriptive/mixed-methods rather than a comparative experiment. Outcome is perception-based and feedback-content analysis, not a quantitative learning outcome. Writing (English-language writing proficiency) is not clearly STEM content, though the population is science and engineering track students. Excluded on E3 as the first applicable code in order (no comparison group); the abstract gives positive evidence of no control group.

quote: This review analyses five key studies that offer explicit structures for prompting.
rationale: The record is a narrative/integrative review of five existing studies, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It has no comparison group and no learning outcome data, so it fails the design, comparison and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that fits; the abstract gives positive evidence that the paper is a review.

quote: This paper approaches the ASSURE model and proposes a teaching process utilizing AI Chatbots combined with gamification in a self-regulated learning framework
rationale: Mathematics domain is met. The abstract describes a conceptual paper proposing a teaching process ("approaches the ASSURE model and proposes"). It states that research findings indicate benefits, but gives no design, control group, or quantitative outcome details. Whether this is an empirical study with a comparison group cannot be determined from the abstract, and AI chatbots are not clearly generative. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so it is unsure and should be checked at full text, where E6 (not empirical) is a likely outcome.

quote: This exploratory study, conducted between February and April 2025 with n. 1,072 pre-service teachers enrolled in qualification programs in Italy, examines perceptions and practices related to AI-assisted writing tools for student self-assessment.
rationale: The study is a survey of pre-service teachers' perceptions and practices, not a controlled experiment. It has no control group and no learner learning outcome; it measures perceptions. It is also writing (language) rather than STEM content. Exclusion under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the clearest positive failure shown by the abstract; the design is a survey, and the domain is not STEM, so E2 would also apply, but the protocol asks for the first code in order, which is E1 only if the intervention is not learner-facing. The abstract does not clearly show E1, so E2 would be the first applicable code by order. Correcting: the first applicable code in order is E2 (content not STEM), which I record here.

quote: Assessing the Ability of a Large Language Model to Score Free-Text Medical Student Clinical Notes
rationale: ChatGPT is used by the scorer (teacher/assessor side) to grade student notes, not as a learner-facing tool within a learning activity. Students do not interact with generative AI. Also, there is no control group without generative AI; the comparison is between AI scoring and standardized patient scoring of accuracy. Health professions/medical education context also raises domain concern (protocol excludes health professions education). Excluded under E1 as the first applicable code.

quote: We administered a questionnaire to 87 full-time faculty at the school via email.
rationale: The study is a faculty usage survey, not an empirical learning study. Learners do not interact with generative AI, there is no control group, no learning outcome, and the population is faculty and not students. Also health professions education and not STEM. Excluded at the first applicable code in order, E1 would be arguable, but the core failure is that it is a survey (not an empirical intervention study), so E6 is the most fitting single code.

criteria.criteria_note: survey of perceptions

quote: this study explored the perspectives and experiences of secondary mathematics pre-service teachers with the tool
rationale: The study is a mixed-method survey and interview study of perceptions (ease of use, intention to use). It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first code that clearly applies; the design also lacks a comparison group (E3), but the protocol asks for the first applicable code in order, and E3 precedes E5. Reporting the first applicable code in order gives E3 instead.

quote: The textbook was deployed in the 2024/2025 academic year, and the data was compared with the summary results from 2021 to 2024.
rationale: At abstract stage, the intervention is a GPT-4-based intelligent textbook used by students in Electrical Engineering (STEM), with mid-term and final assessment outcomes. However, the comparison is partly against historical cohorts (2021-2024) and a between-group comparison in one year is mentioned, so it is unclear whether a concurrent control group without generative AI exists and whether the design is a quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is passed to full text to check the comparison and design, and whether SMD-computable data are reported.

The study uses generative chatbots to paraphrase and synthesize training data for ML scoring models. Learners do not interact with the generative AI as part of a learning activity; the chatbot is used by researchers for data augmentation to build an automated scorer. This fails the learner-facing intervention requirement (E1). The abstract gives no indication of a learner-facing generative tool or a control group without generative AI. Chemistry is STEM and participants are undergraduates, so those criteria appear met.

quote: The present scoping review synthesizes literature from 2020 to 2025 to explore the integration of generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in higher education
rationale: The record is a scoping review of literature, not an empirical study. It has no control-group experiment and no quantitative learning outcome. It is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Review articles are also outside the eligible design.

quote: Using PRISMA principles, 44 articles were selected for review. Grounded coding was then used to reveal trends in the data.
rationale: This is a systematic review of the literature (state-of-the-field), not an empirical study with a control group or a quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Reviews are also ineligible under the publication-type rule, but the protocol's exclusion code for this case is E6 as the first applicable code for a non-empirical design.

quote: This case study explored graduate students’ uses and attitudes toward generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) for academic purposes at an iSchool.
rationale: Abstract describes a case study using a questionnaire and focus groups with descriptive statistics and content analysis. There is no control group or comparison condition, so the design is not a comparative experiment or quasi-experiment. Outcomes are attitudes and use patterns, not a quantitative learning measure. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI), the first applicable code in order; E5 would also apply to the outcome, but E3 is the first failing criterion in the code order as the design lacks any comparison group.

quote: The study discusses the technical principles underlying ChatGPT and identifies factors that contribute to incorrect responses.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/analytical discussion of ChatGPT errors with illustrative examples and recommendations. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Exclusion at abstract stage is justified by positive evidence of non-empirical design.

The record is a legal education discussion paper proposing AI integration into law curricula. Law is non-STEM content, so E2 applies. It also reads as a position/conceptual paper with no comparison group or quantitative learning outcome, but the first applicable code in order is E2 (content is not STEM); E1 and E2 are checked first and E2 is the earliest that clearly applies on positive evidence.

quote: A total of 92 students from Emmanuel Alayande University of Education, Oyo, were randomly assigned to one of the two groups: one used traditional resources (e.g., textbooks and class notes), while the other used ChatGPT
rationale: Abstract describes a randomized experiment with a traditional-resources control group and ChatGPT (generative AI) group, undergraduate students, mathematics (geometric series), with an accuracy outcome (3-point rubric) published 2025. No abstract-level evidence of failure on any criterion. Data sufficiency and publication type (journal vs. other venue) cannot be confirmed from the abstract, so the record advances to full text rather than being excluded.

quote: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 301 postgraduate students at a public healthcare university in Central Vietnam
rationale: The design is a cross-sectional survey with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the measured variable is self-reported academic use of ChatGPT. Domain is health professions education, which is excluded by the protocol. Under the ordering rule, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first code that clearly applies on the abstract's evidence. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of design failure.
rationale_note: Domain (health professions) would also fail, but E2 is listed before E3 in the protocol; however, health professions education is not clearly "not STEM" in the abstract's terms, so E3 is applied as the clearest positive failure.

quote: The study involved 46 learners in the experimental group using GAI-assisted learning and 46 in the control group using traditional methods.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study describes a generative AI (GAI)-assisted programming course with a traditional-methods control group, a programming domain, vocational school students, and learning outcomes (achievement). Published 2025, so date criterion met. Design is implied as a comparison of groups but randomization/quasi-experimental status, SMD data availability, and article type are not stated in the abstract; no positive evidence of failure, so include and verify at full text.

quote: The participants of this study were 60 eleventh-grade students, 30 students from class XI-D (control class), and 30 students from class XI-E (experimental class).
rationale: The study uses ChatGPT with a control class, quantitative pre/post test, and secondary students, so most criteria appear met. However, the content is English as a foreign language writing ability, which is language learning and not STEM. Per the protocol, language learning is excluded, so E2 applies as the first failing code in order (E1 does not apply since ChatGPT is learner-facing).

quote: This study investigates the readiness of higher education students in Indonesia to use ChatGPT for learning and explores its perceived benefits in academic settings.
rationale: The study is a mixed-methods survey/perception study with Rasch analysis of readiness and perceptions. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions and readiness only. Excluded under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Domain is not specified as STEM in the abstract, but the exclusion rests on the outcome. Design also lacks a comparison group, which would be a further failure.

quote: We used them with zero, one, two, three and four shots.
rationale: The LLMs (GPT-3, BLOOM, YOU) are used to classify fourth-grade math answers as incoherent, i.e., an automated grading/review task performed by the system rather than a learner interacting with generative AI as part of a learning activity. This is not learner-facing generative AI, so E1 applies. No control group without generative AI is evident either, but E1 is the first applicable code. Excluding at abstract stage is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence the intervention is not learner-facing.

quote: This study explores the use of a GPT-5.4–based system to support the evaluation of introductory physics laboratory reports
rationale: The generative AI system is used for grading lab reports (AI used only for grading / instructor-facing evaluation), not as a learner-facing tool within a learning activity. Per protocol, AI used only for grading is excluded, and E1 applies as the first failing code. No control group of learners or learner outcome is described; the study compares AI scores to instructor grading.

However, the decisive failure is the non-experimental survey design, which is a non-empirical-study type of problem; E6 is chosen as the single code reflecting the survey (non-experimental) nature. The abstract gives clear positive evidence of survey design, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: this conceptual study proposes the Reflective Instrumental Genesis (RIG) model
rationale: The paper is a conceptual/theoretical reconstruction that explicitly states it is a conceptual study using primary theory texts and published literature. Exclusion code E6 is applied as the first failing criterion in the order given; E1 is not clearly failing from the abstract alone, so E6 is the first code that clearly applies.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on positive evidence of a non-empirical design.

quote: A between-group mixed-methods experiment was conducted amongst 124 undergraduate students (62 in the control group and 62 in the experimental group) over 7 weeks.
rationale: Abstract describes a between-group experiment with a control group among undergraduates in Java programming (STEM), with GenAI-based learner interaction and posttest HOTS and programming logic outcomes with adjusted Hedges' g reported; 2026 publication date meets the date rule. Effect sizes are reported in the abstract, so data sufficiency is likely. The control condition's nature (whether it uses GenAI) is not stated in the abstract, and publication type and full-text language cannot be verified from the abstract alone. No positive evidence of exclusion, so advance to full text.

quote: This study used a descriptive, qualitative method.

It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical comparison of the kind the protocol requires. Excluded at E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense). Translation courses are also questionable as STEM content, but E6 is the first applicable code given the design. Coded E6 at abstract stage on the qualitative design evidence.

quote: This article proposes a similar framework for navigating generative AI in writing instruction
rationale: The record is a theoretical/pedagogical essay in College Composition and Communication. quote: Through an in-depth analysis of the technical characteristics of generative AI, its code generation capabilities, and its current applications in the educational field

quote: This scoping review explores the evolving landscape of GenAI applications and introduces prompt engineering as a critical competency
rationale: The record is a scoping literature review, not an empirical study. It reports no primary intervention, control group, or quantitative learning outcome of its own. It is not clear whether learners interact with a generative AI tool as part of the activity (the training seems to be about evaluating AI-generated images rather than using a generative tool), and the abstract does not mention a control group, so the comparison criterion cannot be judged. Because the abstract does not give positive evidence of a failed criterion, it is passed to full text for checking of intervention, comparison, and domain.

rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual framework paper ("This paper proposes a pedagogically grounded framework") with structured exemplars, not an empirical study. Positive evidence of non-empirical design is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

There is no control group and no learning outcome measured; it is not an experiment. Although the protocol's E3 (no control group) is the natural code, the first failing criterion in code order is E1 only if the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI, which is arguably met here (students use ChatGPT). E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) also clearly applies, since outcomes are perceptions and intentions. Following the first-applicable order, the study lacks a comparison group and a learning outcome; E3 is reported as the first clear design failure, with E5 also applicable. Reviewer should verify code choice.

quote: A qualitative descriptive approach was employed, using semi-structured interviews with five participants.

rationale: Abstract describes a cross-sectional, correlational design with a single sample of 357 undergraduates measured on ChatGPT usage intensity, anxiety and perceived problem-solving. Whether the GenAI tool is learner-facing, whether a non-GenAI control exists in the sense required, and whether SMD-computable statistics are reported cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone; none of these show positive evidence of failure, so advance to full text.

Secondary school mathematics students in a quasi-experiment with a traditional-instruction comparison group and an N-Gain achievement outcome, published 2025. The abstract does not state whether the AI LMS contains a generative model (it mentions AI personalization, adaptive difficulty and an AI tutor, which could be non-generative), so intervention is unclear. Per the abstract-stage rule, this is sent to full text rather than excluded. quote: Study 2 ... a 22 item instrument was pilot tested and then administered to 642 students for confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey with SEM and interviews; there is no control group or experimental comparison, and the outcome is perceived transfer gains (self-report perception), not a quantitative learning measure. Design is correlational/survey, which the protocol excludes. Per the protocol's exclusion order, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code in sequence after E1/E2 are not triggered; the outcome (E5) and design (E6 - not empirical experiment) problems also apply, but the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group, so E3 is reported. Domain is not stated in the abstract (general higher education), so it is not excluded on domain.

quote: Descriptive statistics and comparative analysis revealed that both groups perceived ChatGPT positively as a tool that improves writing quality, coherence, and confidence.
rationale: The study is a questionnaire survey of perceptions of ChatGPT in academic writing among EFL students. It reports no learning outcome measured after an intervention and no control group, so it fails the outcome criterion (perceptions only). Domain is also non-STEM (EFL academic writing). Exclusion code E5 is the first applicable code in order that fits; E2 (non-STEM) would also apply, but the protocol asks for the first in order, and E2 precedes E5 in the list, so the code should be E2. Correcting: the first applicable code in protocol order is E2 because the content is English language writing, not STEM.

Abstract stage. The title refers to programming education and computational thinking, and the study compares an edtech platform with AI-assisted responses against an LMS group in college courses. However, the abstract reports outcomes only as interaction levels and academic interest (affective), with no quantitative learning measure such as achievement or problem solving. Interaction and interest are perception/affective outcomes, which the protocol excludes. Positive evidence of a failed outcome criterion is present, so exclusion under E5 is applied. The title's mention of computational thinking skills is not supported by the abstract's reported outcomes. Note: the abstract is in Korean; the rule against language exclusion at abstract stage was respected, and E9 is not applied here.

quote: The present study does not compare clustering against alternative exemplar-selection strategies, and therefore conclusions should be interpreted as evidence of feasibility rather than comparative superiority.
