There is no control group without generative AI, and the outcome is instructor usability ratings rather than a learning measure. Positive evidence of E3 (no comparison group) and E5 (no learning outcome) is present; E3 is the first applicable code in order. Not an empirical learner study with a comparison group, so the record fails the protocol.

quote: A quantitative survey was conducted with 166 respondents, and the data were analysed using descriptive statistics, analysis of variance (ANOVA), and independent t-tests.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of perceptions and adoption among Malaysian undergraduates. It has no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no separate control group without generative AI, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. It also reports perceptions and usage rather than a quantitative learning outcome. Under the abstract-stage rule the abstract gives positive evidence of failure on comparison and design, so it is excluded. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI); the survey design would also support E5 or E6, but E3 is the first listed failure that the protocol order gives.

quote: Data from expert validation, practicality questionnaires, and product assessments were analyzed using Aiken's V and descriptive statistics.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study reports development and validation via expert validation, practicality questionnaires (perceptions), and product assessments analyzed with Aiken's V and descriptive statistics. There is no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome such as achievement or skill performance measured against a control. Abstract gives positive evidence that the outcome criterion fails (only perceptions and validity ratings) and that no control-group comparison is reported, so exclusion under E5 is applied. Note: the venue name "Journal of Paddisengeng Technology" is not a recognized venue and the design appears to be a single-group development study; the record should be verified at full text if the reviewer disagrees.

quote: pre-training LLMs on authentic K-12 mathematical dialogue datasets
rationale: The abstract describes pre-training LLMs on K-12 math dialogue data and NLP task performance (downstream NLP tasks, text generation). No learner interacts with the generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, so the intervention criterion appears not met (E1). No control group with learners is described. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing.

The abstract describes an LLM-based tutoring system using RAG and prompt engineering, so the intervention appears to be generative AI. However, the abstract does not state a control group, a comparison design, a STEM domain, a student population, or a learning outcome. It reports evaluation on accuracy, clarity and similar metrics of responses, which may be response-quality ratings rather than learning outcomes. Missing information is not grounds for exclusion at the abstract stage, so the record is advanced for full-text review.

The record has only a title and venue, with no abstract. The title describes LLM-based role-playing agents simulating student learning behaviors, which suggests a simulation study rather than a learner-facing intervention with a control group. Nothing in the record gives positive evidence that a criterion fails, and the design, population, and outcome cannot be judged from the title alone. Per rule 2, it is not excluded at the abstract stage and should be resolved at full text.

criteria.stage_note: Abstract describes a single-group ChatGPT activity with perception-based results (confidence, perceptions) and no control group mentioned

quote: The study implemented a ChatGPT-based activity in introductory chemistry courses, where students engaged with ChatGPT in three stages
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group implementation of a ChatGPT activity in introductory chemistry, with no mention of a comparison group that does not use generative AI. Results are largely self-reported confidence and perceptions, which would also fail the outcome criterion. Positive evidence of a missing control group supports E3 at abstract stage.
rationale_note: Single-group design apparent from abstract; no control condition described.

quote: As part of the study, a literature review and a survey of 86 first-and second-year students in the areas of biotechnology, information systems and pedagogy of dual-degree programs were conducted.
rationale: Abstract describes a survey study (descriptive, no control group) and a literature review; no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Design is survey-based, so the record fails the comparison and design criteria. Domain also appears non-STEM (ethics, English language classes), though the abstract does not state this fully. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code in order that fits the lack of comparison; the survey design would also support E5/E6. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence of a non-comparative survey design.

quote: we surveyed 300 undergraduate students from public and private institutions in Mexico
rationale: This is a perception survey of undergraduate programming students with t-tests and ANOVA across groups. It has no control group receiving a comparison condition and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions of support, trust, and engagement, which the protocol excludes. Design is survey-based, not an experiment. Exclusion code E5 is the first applicable code in the order given that fits the positive evidence (perceptions only, no learning measure). Note that E3 (no control) and E6 (not an empirical study, arguably) could also apply; E5 is reported as the cleanest match for the perception-only outcome.

quote: A quantitative instrumental case study explores ChatGPT’s impact on early adopters in education. A survey of undergraduate computer science students
rationale: The study is a survey of satisfaction and opinions with ChatGPT, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; only perceptions and satisfaction are measured. Exclusion code E5 applies, since the abstract gives positive evidence that the outcome is perception-based rather than learning. Design also appears to be a survey, not an experiment, but E5 is the first applicable code in order for this record.

quote: 通过实证研究，验证了AIGC在职业教育中的有效性
rationale: Abstract describes AIGC (generative AI) in vocational education and mentions an empirical study verifying effectiveness. However, it gives no details on control group, design, STEM content (title mentions "Mathematical" but abstract is generic), or quantitative outcomes. No positive evidence of an exclusion criterion failing, so cannot exclude at abstract stage; advance to full text to check design, comparison, domain and outcome.

This is a review/critical analysis of grey literature claims about ChatGPT in higher education, not an empirical study. It has no learner-facing intervention, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), but the abstract describes claims analysis rather than a tool given to learners, so E6 (not an empirical study) is the most accurate primary code. Not STEM-specific either. Exclusion is based on positive evidence that the study is not empirical.

quote: A quantitative pre-experimental approach employing a one-group pretest-posttest design was implemented with 25 participants selected through purposive sampling.
rationale: The abstract explicitly describes a one-group pretest-posttest design with no separate control group that avoids generative AI. Single-group pre-post designs fail the comparison and design criteria, so the record is excluded under E3 (one group measured before and after). The domain (elementary arithmetic) and population (second-grade students) appear to fit, and the outcome is a quantitative achievement test, but the comparison failure alone is decisive.
rationale_note: Intervention generative status (ChatGPT, Canva AI) is plausible but not needed for the decision.

rationale: Abstract describes a convenience survey analysed with reticular analysis of coincidences, examining perceptions (TAM attitudes, confidence) and usage. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions and attitudes. This is a survey-based, non-experimental study, so it fails the design, comparison and outcome criteria. The first applicable code in protocol order is E3 (no control group without generative AI), but the more fundamental failure is that the study is not an empirical trial with a learning outcome; per the protocol's order, E3 is the first code that applies on the exclusion list, so the code assigned should be E3 rather than E6. Final code: E3.

quote: We produced responses from three generative AI chatbots (ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4, and Bard) to two WTL assignments developed to elicit students' mechanistic reasoning.
rationale: The study compares chatbot-generated responses with previously collected authentic student responses; no learner interacts with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, and there is no control group receiving a non-generative-AI condition with a learning outcome. Chatbot outputs are scored by an existing ML model, not a learning measure. Per the protocol's comparison requirement (no control group without generative AI), this fails at E3. Note that the abstract gives positive evidence the design is not a learner-facing experiment.

quote: This study explores university students’ perceptions of DeepSeek, an AI-powered chatbot, as a supporting tool in English language learning.
rationale: Content is English language learning, which is non-STEM, so E2 applies (first failing code in order that is positively evidenced; E1 not clearly failing since DeepSeek is a learner-facing chatbot). Study is qualitative interviews of perceptions with no control group or quantitative learning outcome, so E3 and E5 also fail, but E2 is reported as the first applicable code in order.

quote: Our three-stage study showed that a significant portion of computing-related students currently lack security awareness toward the use of AI assistants.
rationale: Abstract indicates a computing-education study of students using generative AI assistants (ChatGPT, Copilot) for coding, which fits domain and intervention. However, the abstract does not show whether there is a control group without generative AI, the study design (it describes a "three-stage study" with a security-mindset factor, which may be correlational), or whether a quantitative learning outcome is measured (the outcome reported is code security). None of these is positive evidence of failure at abstract stage, so the record is kept for full-text review rather than excluded.

quote: Using a qualitative interpretive approach, interviews with nine academics reveal key themes
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of nine design educators about their views. It is not an empirical trial with a control group and has no quantitative learning outcome. It fails the design, comparison and outcome criteria. Qualitative design is the first applicable exclusion in code order at E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a comparative quantitative study); the participants are educators, not learners, but E4 is not used because E6 is the earliest applicable code in the order given. Abstract-stage exclusion is justified by explicit positive evidence of a qualitative, non-experimental design.

criteria.criteria_note: no control group; correlational/mediation analysis of survey data

quote: Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, ANOVA, regression analysis, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), and mediation analysis (model with bootstrapping).
rationale: The abstract describes a mixed-methods survey-based study of ChatGPT use and academic dependency with regression and mediation analysis. There is no separate control group without generative AI, and no quantitative learning outcome (dependency and engagement are self-report constructs). Abstract gives positive evidence of comparison and design failure, so exclude under E3 (first applicable code in order would be E5 or E6 for some aspects, but E3 is the clearest failure for a correlational design without a comparison group).

quote: The study adopts a mixed-methods design, drawing on survey data and qualitative insights from semi-structured interviews and focus groups with pre-service primary and secondary teachers.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey and qualitative interviews/focus groups on trainee perceptions and usage of GenAI. There is no control group, no experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. Design is survey/qualitative, which fails the design and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported; E3 (no control group) would also apply. Per the protocol's code order, E3 precedes E5, so the first applicable code is E3 given the absence of any comparison group. Note the abstract does not explicitly describe a control group, and the design is non-experimental.

quote: This paper examines the ethical, legal, and social issues (ELSI) arising from the integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in educational settings in Japan.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/policy analysis of ELSI issues and proposes response strategies. It reports no experiment, comparison group, or quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). No intervention or comparison is described.

quote: A qualitative approach was employed using semi-structured interviews with 12 Thai university students selected through purposive sampling.
rationale: Qualitative interview study of perceptions with no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and writing in English is not STEM content. Abstract gives positive evidence of design and outcome failure. Coded E5 as the first clearly applicable outcome failure; the design (no comparison group, qualitative) and domain (English writing, non-STEM) also fail, but E3 and E2 would be applied first in protocol order only if they were the first failing criterion; given the protocol order, E2 (non-STEM) is actually the first applicable code.

quote: The population of this study was all 165 sixth-grade elementary school students.
rationale: The study is about Problem-Based Learning and writing skills in elementary school, which is language/writing content and not STEM. The abstract also gives no indication that learners interact with a generative AI tool; AI and ChatGPT are mentioned only as background to declining writing skills. Excluded on E2 (content not STEM), the first applicable code in order.

quote: University Students' Perspectives on ChatGPT as an Educational Tool
rationale: The title frames the study as students' perspectives, which suggests perception-based outcomes. The abstract is only publisher boilerplate and gives no description of the design, comparison group, or learning outcome. Positive evidence of a failed criterion is limited to the title's perception framing, so the exclusion rests on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). This is a weak basis at abstract stage; the rule favours advancing when evidence is missing. Consider changing to unsure and checking the full text for a learning measure.

quote: This article explores the incorporation of Generative AI (GenAI) into IB curricula, examining course fit and faculty readiness, while presenting actional recommendations
rationale: The record is a non-empirical commentary/perspective article proposing recommendations for international business curricula. It reports no study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is also outside STEM (international business education). Excluded under E6 as not an empirical study; the first applicable code in order is E1 only if intervention is judged, but the abstract gives no learner-facing empirical evaluation, so E6 is the best-supported code.

quote: The data were collected from 50 undergraduate translation students by using structured questionnaire.
rationale: The study is a descriptive quantitative questionnaire survey of student perceptions, with no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions of speed, accuracy and quality. Translation is also not clearly STEM. Excluded under E5 as the first clearly applicable code at abstract stage; the design also lacks a comparison group (E3) and translation is a non-STEM domain (E2), but the primary failure is the absence of a learning outcome measure.
rationale_note: Exclusion codes are reported in order; E2 would precede E5 in the protocol order. See note below.

quote: This study investigates how Gemini AI uniquely facilitates speaking fluency through Task-Based Learning in self-directed learning and its impact on students’ speaking performance.
rationale: The study concerns EFL speaking fluency, which is language learning and not STEM, so E2 applies. The abstract also describes a single cohort of 19 participants in a mixed-methods intervention with no control group, which would independently raise E3 (no comparison group). Under the protocol's ordering, E2 is the first applicable code and is reported. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract.

quote: Here we evaluated whether LLMs can assess human creativity in Physics Playground, an educational physics game where students design playable levels.
rationale: The LLMs are used to automatically assess student-created game levels (rater/scoring use), not as a learner-facing generative AI tool within a learning activity. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool, and there is no control group comparing learning outcomes with and without generative AI. This fails the intervention criterion (E1). Other criteria cannot be assessed from the abstract alone, but E1 applies first.

The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey (physical surveys, 5-point Likert scales, SmartPLS structural analysis) of 378 design students, with GAI interaction measured as a self-reported scale rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison against a non-GAI control group. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group and a non-experimental design supports E3 (no control group without generative AI). Domain (design students) is also not clearly STEM, but E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol order that is supported by the abstract.

quote: Research approach uses associative descriptive quantitative methods through surveys at Al-Falah As-Sunniyah University Kencong Jember.
rationale: The study is a survey-based associative/correlational design with no control group that does not use generative AI, so comparison and design criteria fail. Outcomes are self-reported independent behavior and plagiarism categories from a questionnaire, not a quantitative learning measure. Under the exclusion-code order, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first clear failure I can cite from the abstract; E5 would also apply. Domain is not stated in the abstract (Islamic religious education), which is not STEM, but the record is excluded on the first applicable code as ordered.

criteria.quote: pre- and post-tests were conducted on a single group
criteria.rationale: The abstract states the study used pre- and post-tests on a single group, which is a single-group pre-post design with no separate control group without generative AI, so E3 applies. Domain (technology education, digital citizenship) is not clearly STEM, but E3 is the first applicable code in order from the protocol's perspective given the design evidence. Outcome is a digital citizenship measure, which is not clearly a learning outcome, but the design failure is sufficient.

quote: pre- and post-tests were conducted on a single group
rationale: Abstract gives positive evidence of a single-group pre-post design with no control group without generative AI, so the comparison and design criteria fail (E3). Exclusion code E3 applies.

quote: through collaborative multi case studies supported with other data collection sources (eg surveys/questionnaires), we explore gaps and uncertainty in the existing knowledge of students
rationale: The abstract describes a collaborative multi-case study with surveys and questionnaires exploring student understanding. This is a qualitative/case-study design with no control group, which fails the comparison and design criteria. Legal education is also not STEM, so the domain criterion fails. The exclusion code is E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code under the protocol's ordering is E2 for non-STEM content; however, the design is a case study, so I report E6 as the primary reason as the study is not an experimental comparison. Abstract-stage evidence of non-STEM content (law) is clear, so E2 is the earlier-ordered code that applies.

quote: The LLM achieved a B-grade performance (82.24%), approaching but not exceeding the class average (84.99%)
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT's own performance on course deliverables under a minimal-effort protocol, compared against the class average rather than a separate control group of learners without generative AI. No randomized or quasi-experimental comparison group is described, so the comparison and design criteria are not met. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) applies as the first failing criterion in order that is clearly evidenced; the design is an AI-performance evaluation rather than a learner-facing controlled comparison.

quote: Using adverse event data from early childhood incubators as a case study, it integrates multi-source standards to construct a three-layer risk knowledge system.
rationale: The record is about LLM-based knowledge graph construction for medical electrical equipment risk management. It is not a learning study, and the content is medical device regulation rather than STEM education. The abstract gives no learner-facing intervention, control group, or learning outcome. Excluded on E2 (content not STEM education) as the first applicable code; the domain is clearly outside the protocol's STEM scope.

criteria.comparison_note: GenAI user vs non-GenAI user groups; control status unclear

quote: the differences in measured academic performance and study efficiency between the GenAI user and non-GenAI user groups were not statistically significant
rationale: University plant physiology course (higher education; plant science is plausibly STEM, though horticulture is borderline). The abstract compares GenAI user and non-user groups on academic performance, which may satisfy a comparison and a quantitative outcome. However, the groups appear to be self-selected user vs non-user categories from surveys and LMS data, so it is unclear whether this is a true controlled comparison, and the design (quasi-experiment vs correlational/survey) is not clear. Abstract does not give positive evidence of failure, so advance to full text for checking design, comparison, and STEM status.

quote: This qualitative case study explores master students' perceptions of using ChatGPT to support critical thinking in academic writing
rationale: The study is a qualitative case study of student perceptions, with no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no effect data. It is not an empirical study that meets the design criteria. Domain is academic writing in English language education, which is non-STEM. E6 is the earliest applicable code given the design (qualitative case study, not an experimental/quasi-experimental empirical design). Note that E2 (non-STEM content) would also apply; under the code order, E1 does not apply since ChatGPT is learner-facing, and E2 precedes E6 in the list, so the first applicable code by order is E2. Correcting: exclusion code should be E2 since E2 precedes E6.

quote: generative artificial intelligence was used as a teacher-facing instructional co-design tool, not as a real-time intelligent tutor
rationale: At abstract stage, generative AI is used as a teacher-facing co-design tool, which is E1 (not learner-facing). However, the reasoning should follow protocol order: E1 applies first. The abstract explicitly says generative AI was a teacher-facing co-design tool, not a real-time tutor, so learners did not interact with it. Additionally, there is no control group and outcomes are perceptions/feasibility only, not learning measures. Per code order, the first applicable code is E1.

quote: Through a qualitative case study, 11 secondary science teachers used GenAI embedded in AIMS to design novel sweetener molecules.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative case study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Design is qualitative, so comparison and outcome criteria are not met. Participants are in-service secondary science teachers, which is also outside the population criteria. Exclusion coded to E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) as the primary reason; the design failure (no comparison group, E3) would also apply, but the protocol asks for the first code in order, and E3 precedes E5, so E3 is arguably the first applicable code. Given the evidence, E3 applies first in the order.

quote: The article, originating from a conference presentation by Tsinghua University and NTHU, Taiwan, provides a nuanced overview of Generative AI.
rationale: The abstract describes an overview/discussion article based on a conference presentation, with no experimental design, control group, or quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Although the abstract mentions a high school language course illustration, that is a classroom application description, not a controlled comparison. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of a non-empirical overview.

quote: This exploratory cross-sectional study was conducted via an online questionnaire from January to March 2025.
rationale: Cross-sectional survey with descriptive statistics only; no control group, no intervention comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. Design is a survey, which is non-empirical-experimental and fails the design and outcome criteria. Per the first-applicable-code order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly failed at abstract stage, E2 and E3 are also not clearly positive, and E4 is not positively shown; E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) applies since outcomes are perceptions and usage. Coded E6 as the survey is a non-experimental empirical design; the record is clearly ineligible.

quote: A total of 112 third-year undergraduate students majoring in hydraulic engineering were assigned to traditional and AI-assisted groups.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study compares a Gen AI-assisted group with a traditional group (non-AI control) of undergraduates in soil mechanics lab (engineering, STEM). Outcomes are grade-based performance measures (experimental operation, data analysis, report scores), which are quantitative. Randomization/quasi-experimental status and SMD-computable statistics are not stated in the abstract, so design and data criteria are unclear rather than failed. No positive evidence of exclusion; advance to full text.

Abstract describes a qualitative study (unobtrusive observations and stimulated recall interviews) of 16 undergraduates engaging with ChatGPT feedback on IELTS writing. No control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and the domain is language learning rather than STEM. Coded E6 as an empirical qualitative study without a comparison or quantitative outcome; the first applicable code in order would arguably be E2 (IELTS writing is non-STEM), but the design itself is non-eligible, so E6 is reported as the primary reason. Clear exclusion at abstract stage.

quote: This study explores the potential of the large language model GPT-4 as an automated tool for qualitative data analysis by educational researchers
rationale: GPT-4 is used by educational researchers as a qualitative coding tool for analyzing existing datasets, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. This fails E1. No control group or learning outcome is described; the study is an evaluation of coding agreement with human coders, not a learning outcome. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Study design Cross-sectional survey
rationale: The record is a cross-sectional survey of health science undergraduates about perceptions and use of generative AI. It has no intervention arm and no control group without generative AI, and it reports perceptions rather than a quantitative learning outcome. Domain is health sciences, not STEM. Under the protocol's exclusion ordering, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) could be argued, but the clearest positive evidence is the absence of any control group (E3), so E3 is reported. Design is also not an eligible experimental or quasi-experimental design. Exclusion is clear from the abstract alone.

quote: The experimental group used a Meta AI chatbot integrated with WhatsApp as a learning companion during four instructional sessions, while the control group received conventional instruction.
rationale: Abstract stage: learners interact with a Meta AI chatbot (LLM-based, generative) as part of instruction; control group receives conventional instruction (non-AI), quasi-experimental with non-equivalent control group, 10th-grade vocational students, critical thinking test with t, d, and N-gain reported so SMD computable. Domain is automotive engineering basic subjects, which plausibly falls under engineering, so domain is treated as likely met but not fully confirmed from the abstract. No positive evidence of failure on any criterion, so include. Journal article status and English full text to be checked at fulltext stage.

quote: This study investigated how Preservice Elementary Teachers (PETs) collaborated with ChatGPT on Analyzing and Interpreting Student Responses (AISR) tasks.
rationale: The abstract describes a study of PETs collaborating with ChatGPT, with findings from qualitative analysis of prompts and task responses (e.g., "developed more positive views", "prompt-engineering strategies"). No separate control group without generative AI is described, and no quantitative learning outcome or comparison is evident. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group supports E3 at the abstract stage.
rationale_note: Exclusion on E3 is based on the abstract showing no control condition; full text could be checked if the researcher disagrees.

quote: A qualitative research design was adopted in this study to arrive at in-depth perceptions of IT programming instructors
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of programming instructors' perceptions. It has no learner-facing intervention, no comparison group, no quantitative learning outcome, and participants are teachers rather than students. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's quantitative sense, i.e. the design does not meet the eligible design criteria) is the most applicable code as the first failing criterion for a qualitative perception study; the record gives positive evidence the design is qualitative, so it is excluded at the abstract stage.
rationale_detail: Qualitative design only; no experimental comparison or quantitative learning outcome.
exclusion_code_note: E6 chosen; first applicable in order would be E1 only if intervention is clearly not learner-facing, which the abstract does not establish.

criteria.stage_note: single-group case study with pre/post self-efficacy surveys and Likert ratings of AI modes; no control group without generative AI

quote: "a mixed-methods case study examines the effectiveness of ChatGPT's adaptive learning modes" and "Pre/post paired analysis demonstrated significant improvements in self-efficacy"
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group mixed-methods case study with no separate control group that avoids generative AI; the only comparisons are between AI modes and pre/post within one group, which is E3 per protocol. Outcomes are largely self-reported self-efficacy and Likert ratings, which also weigh against a quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion is positive evidence based on the abstract's design description, so E3 is applied as the first failing code.

criteria.rationale_note: Chatbots compared against IUPAC definitions; descriptive qualitative design with no control group

quote: This study aims to explore the performance and accuracy of three chatbots (ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot) in defining five basic chemistry concepts compared to the definitions described in the IUPAC's Compendium of Chemical Terminology.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive qualitative study comparing chatbot outputs against IUPAC definitions. There is no control group of learners without generative AI, and no quantitative learning outcome in learners. Evidence of failure on comparison (E3) is positive: the comparison is chatbot output versus a reference text, not a learner control group. Design is qualitative, and no learner outcome is measured. E3 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Qualitative analysis of the GAI application in teaching yielded positive comments, as students perceived the activity as helpful, motivating, and engaging
rationale: The abstract describes a generative AI activity in a Business Decision Analysis course, but reports no control group and no comparison design. The only outcomes described are student perceptions (qualitative comments) and correlations between predicted and achieved scores, not a learning outcome compared against a control. Positive evidence of failure on comparison (no control group mentioned) and on outcome (perceptions only) supports exclusion. Domain is business/decision analysis, which is arguably not STEM, but I did not rely on that. Exclusion coded E5 as the first clearly applicable code in protocol order after intervention (met) and population (met); E3 could also apply since no control group is described, but the abstract does not explicitly state the absence of a control, so E5 is the most directly evidenced failure.

quote: Because the comparison cohort is historical, the findings are interpreted as preliminary rather than causal.
rationale: The study is a design-based course reform with generative-AI-assisted feedback for graduate vehicle engineering students (STEM). However, the only comparison is a historical cohort, and the abstract reports descriptive course records and survey data. There is no concurrent control group without generative AI, so E3 applies. Outcome measurement (project scores) is unclear but not needed for the code decision.

quote: Two teachers, each with over eight years of educational experience, graded answers from 204 students and compared these with the results from GPT-4 based ChatGPT.
rationale: GPT-4 is used to score student answers, and teachers grade them; learners do not interact with the generative AI tool as part of a learning activity. AI used only for grading/teacher-side work is not learner-facing (E1). No control group without generative AI is described, and the study compares teacher vs. AI scoring agreement rather than a learning outcome (E3/E5 also apply but E1 is first in order).

quote: This one-group pretest-posttest mixed-methods study examined a week-long, GenAI-integrated informal cybersecurity summer camp
rationale: The abstract describes a one-group pretest-posttest design with no control group without generative AI, which is a positive indication of E3 (single-group pre-post designs are excluded by the protocol). Other criteria appear plausibly met, but the comparison and design failure is sufficient for exclusion.

quote: A descriptive survey research design was adopted, with a population comprising students from eight public and private universities.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive survey study of students' awareness and adoption of AI tools, with no experimental or comparison-group design and no learning outcome measured. Survey designs are not empirical experiments eligible under the protocol, so E6 applies as the first failing criterion in order (E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract; E3 would also fail since there is no control group). Note that E6 is applied here as the non-experimental survey design fails the design criterion.

quote: "Structured questionnaires and surveys were used to evaluate the course's impact on prompting skills, academic English proficiency, and overall learning experiences."
rationale: The abstract describes a case study evaluated through questionnaires and surveys, with no mention of a control group or comparison condition. This is positive evidence of a non-experimental design lacking a comparison group, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. Domain is also unclear (prompt engineering and academic English, not clearly STEM). The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI). Exclusion is supported by the abstract's case-study framing and absence of any control group.

quote: The present study proposes a formative assessment approach to compare the comprehension level of selected fundamental engineering concepts for a group of eight students
rationale: The study involves a single group of eight students who take a proctored test without AI and then an open-book test with AI permitted. There is no separate control group without generative AI, and the design is within-subject, not a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison group design. This fails the comparison and design criteria. Under the exclusion code order, E3 (no control group without generative AI) applies first, as the abstract gives positive evidence of a single-group design.

quote: Adaptive AI-Tutor focused specifically on teaching theatre and drama by improving the skills of performance, interpreting scripts, expressing emotions, and being present on the stage
rationale: The content domain is theatre and drama, which is not STEM under the protocol (science, math, statistics, engineering, CS, programming, data science). The abstract itself states the focus is creative arts. This is a clear positive failure of the domain criterion, so exclude with E2. Other criteria (generative model use, control group, design) are not clearly stated in the abstract and are not the basis for exclusion.

quote: The research involved 18 participants, consisting of 11 fifth-grade students and 7 sixth-grade students
rationale: The abstract describes a single small group of 18 students in a science talent program with no control or comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. It is a descriptive/discussion paper about chatbot design. Abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group, so exclude under E3 (the first applicable code in order would arguably be E5/E6, but the lack of control group is the clearest failing criterion; the paper also appears to be a non-empirical discussion piece, which would be E6). Note that E6 may be the more accurate first-applicable code given the discussion-style content; flagged for auditor review.

quote: Exploring Learners' Perceptions of Learning Support and Job Readiness in a Generative Artificial Intelligence-Integrated Marketing Technology Data Analytics Vocational Training Program
rationale: The title indicates the study explores learners' perceptions of learning support and job readiness, which points to perception-based outcomes rather than a quantitative learning measure. The abstract field contains only the text "補正完畢" (roughly "correction completed") with no usable abstract, so the other criteria cannot be assessed. Exclusion is based on positive evidence from the title that the outcome is perceptual; E5 is applied. The rule-based exclusion is at the abstract stage, so this could be revisited if a full text shows a quantitative learning outcome.

quote: The students' pre- and post-tests indicate statistically significant learning gains in school mathematics and modelling competencies
rationale: Abstract describes a GenAI platform generating modelling problems used with 49 secondary students (STEM: mathematics, secondary population, quantitative pre/post test outcomes). However, the abstract describes a single focal intervention with pre- and post-tests and no mentioned control group, which suggests a single-group pre-post design (E3 likely). Abstract does not explicitly state absence of a control group, so unsure; resolve at full text. Also the study is labelled a case study with mixed methods, and the learner-facing nature of the GenAI tool is not explicit (the platform generates resources; students' interaction unclear).

quote: This conceptual review integrates recent literature (2022-2025) to develop a theoretical framework
rationale: The record is a conceptual review that develops a theoretical framework and reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). The exclusion code is set to E3 below per my reading; the code order favors E1 and the audit should check this.

quote: Survey data were collected from 153 undergraduate students.
rationale: Survey of undergraduate perceptions about AI and employment; no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E1 applies first in protocol order because no learner-facing generative AI intervention is evaluated.

The study is a qualitative focus-group analysis (critical discourse analysis, concordance and thematic analysis) of student conceptions of GenAI. quote: Purposive sampling was used to select 11 participants from the state of Kerala, India, in higher education.
rationale: Qualitative phenomenological study using semi-structured interviews with 11 students. No control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no STEM content is evident. The design and outcome criteria fail on positive evidence from the abstract. Excluded under E5, the first applicable code in the protocol's sequence that is supported by the abstract (E3 would also apply, but the qualitative design is the clearer failure; E6 could also be argued as the study is not a quantitative empirical experiment).

quote: This study employed a quantitative research design. Data was gathered from 385 mathematics teachers in Metro Manila using a structured questionnaire
rationale: The study is a questionnaire survey of in-service mathematics teachers about perceptions and TAM constructs of generative AI. It has no learner-facing AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. Per the protocol, it is a survey design and fails the eligibility criteria. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing), but the study's primary nature is a non-empirical-intervention perception survey; I chose E6 as the design is a survey rather than an empirical experiment. Note: strictly by code order, E1 applies first since no learner interacts with the AI tool.

quote: This study employed an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design using a purposive sample of 45 school nurses from primary, secondary, and higher education institutions in Taiwan.
rationale: Abstract stage exclusion. The study is a survey plus focus-group mixed-methods study of school nurses (in-service professionals, not students), with no control group, no learning outcome, and no STEM content. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical comparison study by design, descriptive survey/qualitative) as the first clearly applicable code; positive evidence also fails population (in-service nurses, not students) and domain (health education), but the protocol's first-applicable ordering places E4 before E6 for population, so the code should be E4 under strict ordering.

quote: Phase 2 conducted a quasi-experimental activity (n = 24), in which students solved a normative design task using ChatGPT (GPT-Vanilla) without prior instruction.
rationale: Learners use ChatGPT (generative AI) in a design activity; the population is higher education (AEC students). The abstract describes a quasi-experiment but does not state a separate control group without generative AI; the only described condition is GPT-Vanilla, so E3 may apply but cannot be confirmed from the abstract. Domain (AEC/architecture design) is borderline for STEM and engineering content. Missing information is not evidence of failure at abstract stage, so the record is passed to full text to check the comparison group, the STEM classification of the design task, and whether the outcome yields SMD-computable statistics.

quote: This study aims to examine the experiences and perspectives of pre-service teachers regarding the educational digital games they developed using Claude
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative case study of 27 pre-service teachers' experiences and perspectives, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E3 (no control group) is the first code that applies in the protocol's order after intervention and population checks; the qualitative design and absence of quantitative outcomes would also fail other criteria. Positive evidence of failure is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: A class of 12 female students participated in two work sessions: in the first, the students interacted with ChatGPT without pretraining; in the second, the chatbot was trained with a structured prompt
rationale: The abstract describes a single class of 12 students who completed two sessions, both using ChatGPT (untrained vs. structured prompt). There is no control group without generative AI, and the study is described as qualitative analysis, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. Exclusion code E3 applies because there is no comparison group without generative AI. Exclusion is justified at the abstract stage because the abstract gives positive evidence of the missing comparison.

quote: Data was collected from 80 teachers and school principals selected purposefully from public primary, secondary, and high schools.
rationale: The study samples in-service teachers and school principals, not K-12 or higher education students, which is an explicit population failure. It is also a qualitative case study with perception data only and no control group or quantitative learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E1, but the abstract does not give positive evidence that the intervention is learner-facing (it concerns perceptions of ChatGPT), so E1 is not clearly established. E4 is the first clearly supported code given the abstract evidence. No STEM content is described, but that is not the first failing criterion in order.

quote: A validated digital survey grounded in established technology-acceptance frameworks—the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) was administered to 94% of the student population
rationale: Cross-sectional survey study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; students report perceptions only (perceived improvements). Positive evidence of failing comparison (no control), design (survey, cross-sectional), and outcome (perceptions only). Under the protocol's codes, the first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI). Domain is not clearly STEM from the abstract. Excluded.
rationale_note: Note: E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) also applies; E3 listed as first in protocol order.

quote: The study explores The influence of artificial intelligence on English language skills and particularly speaking one.
rationale: The study targets English language speaking skills, which is non-STEM content (language learning), so E2 applies. Note the rule that abstract-stage exclusions require positive evidence; here the abstract clearly states the content is English language speaking, so the exclusion is supported.

quote: A qualitative investigation of Tanzanian primary school mathematics teachers' perceptions of contextualised intelligent social robots.

It is excluded at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Although it may also fail E6 (not an empirical study is not the case here, since it is empirical; E3 also plausibly applies), E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order that is clearly supported by the abstract.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on positive evidence: design is qualitative with teacher perception outcomes only.

Domain (engineering design) is plausibly STEM and outcomes include design performance, but the abstract does not show a quantitative comparison group or SMD-ready data. Unsure at abstract stage; full text needed to check the comparison design.

Missing information is not evidence of failure at the abstract stage, so the record is passed to full text to check for a comparison group. Reporting the first applicable code: E1 would also arguably fit since GenAI use is teacher-side for lesson preparation, but E6 captures the core design failure.
