quote: This study uses a meta-analysis to examine the impact of ChatGPT on university student academic achievement.
rationale: The record is a meta-analysis, not a primary empirical study with its own learner-facing experiment. It therefore fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). Also, the abstract reports moderators including non-STEM subjects, which suggests the domain criterion may not be met, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order of checking, and the record is a review/meta-analysis rather than an original study.

quote: An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was employed, with pretest and posttest data analyzed quantitatively
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pretest-posttest design (M 2.78 to 6.39; 3.61 to 7.72) with no separate control group that avoids generative AI. Per protocol, single-group pre-post designs fail the comparison criterion (E3). Intervention is GenAI-based error analysis in undergraduate mathematics, which is otherwise consistent with the protocol.

quote: Students reflected on their design process, learning outcomes, and challenges.
rationale: This is an instructional design case describing a single course project with student reflections. There is no control group and no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported in the abstract. The record is not an experimental or quasi-experimental study. Under the abstract-stage rule, exclusion requires positive evidence of failure; here the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical case report with no comparison group and no quantitative outcome. Coded E5 as the first clearly failing criterion that applies in the order given (E1 is not clearly failed since Copilot is a generative tool used by students, and E3 would also apply, but the absence of any quantitative outcome is the most direct evidence). Note: E3 (no control group) also arguably applies; the single code is E5 per the first-applicable-in-order rule only if E3 is considered not to apply, so this decision could be revisited.

quote: Students' attitudes were collected through an online questionnaire administered in October 2025.
rationale: The study is a survey of student attitudes/perceptions using correlation and regression. There is no control group, no experimental design, and the only outcomes are perceptions, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). The abstract also gives no indication of a learner-facing generative AI intervention or a STEM domain. Under the abstract-stage rule, exclusion is justified because positive evidence shows the design and outcome criteria fail.

quote: Using structured focus groups conducted across three institutions, we explored student perspectives on GenAI's utility, challenges, learning outcomes and skills development.
rationale: The study is a focus-group (qualitative) study of student perspectives with a thematic analysis. It has no comparison group, no quantitative learning outcome, and is not an experimental design, so it fails the design, comparison and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is not quite the best fit for a qualitative empirical study; the closest applicable code in the order given is E6 since it is not an eligible quantitative empirical design, and the decision to exclude is clear regardless of the code chosen. Population (university ICT students) appears met.

quote: A two-year design-based research (DBR) study was conducted across two cycles (2024: n = 11; 2025: n = 20).
rationale: Abstract describes a single-group design-based study of learners interacting with ChatGPT, with prompts analysed across stages and no control group that lacks generative AI. The abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group (only a pre/post-style shift within one group), so E3 applies. Outcome is prompt-based epistemic coding rather than a clear quantitative learning measure, but E3 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: This article presents a dataset comprising Master-level students’ prompts and discussions with generative AI as part of a challenge-based innovation problem-solving process.
rationale: The record is a dataset description paper, not an empirical comparative study. It describes survey-collected student conversation logs with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Publication type is a data paper, which falls outside eligible journal article empirical studies (E10); it also is not an empirical study (E6). E10 is chosen as the first applicable code for a non-eligible publication type, with E3 and E5 also evident from the abstract.

quote: semi-structured interviews were conducted with three purposively sampled students
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative interview study with three students and no control group, so there is positive evidence that the comparison requirement fails. The study also reports only perceptions and platform preferences, with no quantitative learning outcome. E3 is the first applicable code in protocol order, so it is reported here; E5 would also apply.

The record has only a title, venue, and year; there is no abstract. The title suggests a mathematics problem-solving context with elementary school learners, which fits domain and population. Whether the "AI learning companion" is generative, whether a control group exists, the design, and whether a quantitative learning outcome is reported all cannot be determined from the record. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is held as unsure for full-text review.

quote: This theoretical paper critically examines the opportunities and complexities of GenAI-enabled assessment in CS education.
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical paper that draws on literature and argues a perspective. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome data, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion is justified on positive evidence that the paper is non-empirical, even at the abstract stage.

criteria.criteria_note: Population is in-service teachers (MI teachers), which the protocol excludes.

quote: A total of 18 teachers participated. The results demonstrated a significant improvement in teachers' competence, with the average pretest score increasing from 52.8 to 78.4
rationale: This is a community service training program with a single group of 18 in-service teachers and a pretest-posttest improvement; there is no control group. The design is a single-group pre-post design, and the population is in-service teachers, both of which the protocol excludes. The record is a community service report rather than a controlled empirical study. Under the code order, E6 (not an empirical study) best reflects the non-experimental community service nature, though E3 (no control group) and E4 (not students) also apply. Exclusion is justified on positive evidence from the abstract.
exclusion_code_note: Code order would place E3 before E4 and E6 only if E1 and E2 fail; E1 unclear, E2 met (math). Strictly, first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group).

rationale: Abstract describes a cross-sectional survey of nursing students' attitudes (GAAIS) with no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. Positive evidence fails several criteria. Nursing is also health professions education, which is outside the STEM domain. Coded E6 as a non-empirical-intervention survey design; the first applicable code in order would be E1 (no learner-facing generative AI intervention), so E1 is the more precise first-applicable code.

Quasi-experimental non-equivalent control group design with generative AI feedback on descriptive writing, measured by pre/post scores, with students in a vocational education program (higher education/vocational, population plausibly met). However, the content is descriptive text writing (language/writing), which falls outside the protocol's STEM domain (science, math, statistics, engineering, CS, programming, data science). The "Civil Engineering Vocational Education" affiliation of participants does not make the content STEM. The domain criterion appears not met on the abstract, but since the abstract only gives the program name, the decision is left as unsure for the domain question and the population classification of vocational students at fulltext. Under abstract-stage rules, exclusion requires positive evidence; the abstract does state writing content, which is positive evidence of non-STEM content, so this is flagged for a fulltext check rather than excluded outright.

quote: To experience the model, activities developed for mathematics and science lessons were carried out using ChatGPT. Preliminary results have shown that the Flipped Learning model can be combined with Chatbots
rationale: Abstract describes a model development paper with ChatGPT in mathematics and science activities and only "preliminary results". No separate control group without generative AI is mentioned, so the comparison criterion is not met on positive evidence. Exclude under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Design and outcome are not reported in the abstract.

quote: Students self-reported perceived improvements in skills and the use of different help resources across three home assignments
rationale: The study relies on student self-reported perceptions and group discussions, with no quantitative learning outcome measured and no control group described. The abstract gives positive evidence that the outcome is perception-based (E5). Design also appears non-experimental (survey/qualitative). Exclusion at abstract stage is justified by the perception-only outcome.

quote: This is the full abstract presented at the American Physiology Summit 2024 meeting and is only available in HTML format.
rationale: The record is a conference abstract (American Physiology Summit 2024), not a journal article. Its generative AI use is by researchers to analyse open-text survey responses, not learner-facing use, so E1 would also apply. Its design is a cohort comparison of delivery modes with no clear generative AI comparison group, and the outcome is student perception and thematic analysis rather than a learning measure. Per the rule of first applicable code, E6 is the closest fit for an abstract-only non-empirical record, though E10 (publication type not eligible) is also plausible; flagged for audit. Note the intervention criterion also fails at E1, which would come earlier in the code order. Given the code order, E1 should be reported first, so this decision should be reviewed.

quote: To compare the efficiency of the AI-generated learning material with the traditional one, the study designed a quantitative comparative study on the performance of the students in Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) course.
rationale: Abstract describes a comparison of AI-generated versus traditional learning material on OOP student performance, which suggests a control group and a STEM (programming) domain with a test-score outcome. However, the generative AI is used to create content for the teacher/professor to upload, so it is unclear whether learners directly interact with a generative AI tool (possible E1). Design (comparison group vs single-group, quasi-experimental status) and population level (university presumably) are not clearly stated. No positive evidence of failure at abstract stage, so advance to full text to check intervention and design.

quote: The majority of students expressed satisfaction with the use of ChatGPT in education, finding it beneficial for various purposes
rationale: Abstract describes a mixed-methods study based on a structured questionnaire of student perceptions and satisfaction, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Learning outcomes of two courses are mentioned only vaguely. Positive evidence of failure on comparison (no control group) and outcome (perceptions only) exists, so exclude at abstract stage. Domain is medical informatics, which is borderline for the STEM and health-professions exclusions but not decisive here.

quote: Sixty-six upper-division students used desAIner during a structured classroom module and completed a 24-item survey operationalizing an extended Technology Acceptance Model (TAM)
rationale: The study measures only perceptions and acceptance (TAM survey: perceived usefulness, satisfaction, intention). No quantitative learning outcome is reported, and there is no control group without generative AI; it appears to be a single-group survey design. Excluded under E5 as the outcome is perceptions only. Note the protocol's E3 (no control group) could also apply; E5 is the first applicable code in the order listed for the primary failure. Under the protocol's order, E3 precedes E5 in the code list, so the arguably correct code is E3 because the single-group design lacks a comparison group, which is checked before the outcome. Abstract gives positive evidence of no control group and perception-only outcomes.

Psychometric scale development and validation study (EFA, reliability) using a single survey administration to 282 students. It is not an empirical comparison study with a control group, so there is no experimental design or comparison. Domain is English writing, which is non-STEM (E2 would also apply), but the first applicable code in order is E1/E2/E3/E6; the study is not an empirical intervention evaluation, so E6 is the most fitting code. Note the protocol order places E1 first; the abstract gives no evidence of a learner-facing generative AI intervention being tested, but it does not clearly show E1 either. E6 is chosen as the best-supported exclusion because the record is an instrument-development survey study rather than an empirical intervention study.

quote: The research instrument consisted of a questionnaire that was validated through face validity by a language expert and content validity using the Content Validity Ratio (CVR).
rationale: Survey/perception study with correlational analysis of a questionnaire from 193 Indonesian university students. No separate control group that avoids GenAI is described, and the design is correlational rather than an experiment or quasi-experiment. Outcomes are self-reported perceptions, not a quantitative learning measure. The protocol excludes correlational and survey designs; the first applicable code in order is E3 (no comparison group without generative AI). Domain is also not clearly STEM. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence of a missing control group and survey design.

quote: A descriptive survey research design was adopted, with a population comprising STEM students across different academic levels.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive survey design with no control or comparison group, and reports only awareness, usage, and perceptions rather than a quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's order of codes, the first applicable code is E3 (no control group without generative AI). Survey design (E6) and absence of learning outcome (E5) also apply, but E3 is the first in order that clearly fails. The abstract gives positive evidence of a non-comparative survey, so exclusion is supported.

quote: In this design case, we present the integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) into the development of a self-paced online course
rationale: The record is a design case describing instructional designers using GenAI to build a course. It is not an empirical study with a comparison group or a quantitative learning outcome. GenAI is used by the design team, not by learners, which is E1-type evidence, but E6 (not an empirical study) is the first code that applies given the report's nature as a design case. No control group or learning outcome is reported. Domain (program evaluation for biomedical research training) is also not clearly STEM. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that the record is a non-empirical design case.
decision_note: E6 applies first in the order.

quote: A one-group pre-test – post-test quasi-experimental research design was utilized, with thirty-two participants
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pre-test/post-test design with no separate control group without generative AI, which is positive evidence of failure on the comparison criterion (E3). Writing skills in an academic writing context also appear non-STEM, but E3 is the first applicable code in the stated order and is sufficient on its own.

quote: The correct response rates of the five GAIs were compared with those of actual medical undergraduates using an unpaired t-test
rationale: The study evaluates GAI models answering exam questions themselves, not learners interacting with a GAI tool as part of a learning activity. Learners are not the ones using the AI; the comparison is model accuracy versus undergraduates' scores. This fails the learner-facing intervention requirement (E1). Design is a comparison of model outputs against a human score benchmark, not a randomized or quasi-experimental study with a control group of learners. Domain (medical molecular biology) and population are also questionable, but E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: This descriptive instructional case examines an AI-mediated proof-validation activity
rationale: Descriptive instructional case with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the abstract explicitly states no learning-gain claims are made. Comparison is not met (no non-generative-AI control) and design is descriptive, not an experiment or quasi-experiment. Under the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E3 (no control group) could also apply, but the most direct and first-listed fitting reason is the absence of any quantitative learning outcome, so E5 is used per the ordering among codes that apply to the design/outcome. Intervention (generative AI, ChatGPT/DeepSeek used by students in the audit activity), STEM content (number theory), and population (preservice teachers, higher education) appear met.

The study compares four large language models with each other on multiple-choice questions posed to dental students. There is no control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails (E3). The LLMs answer questions as a model accuracy evaluation rather than as learners interacting with the tool, but the decisive exclusion is the missing non-generative-AI comparison. The record is excluded at the abstract stage on positive evidence that the comparison is between generative AI variants only.

quote: A 13-item open-ended questionnaire was administered to 63 second-, third-, and fourth-year students in a Korean Language and Literature program
rationale: Content is Korean language learning, which is non-STEM (E2). The study is a qualitative questionnaire with thematic analysis, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it also fails comparison, design, and outcome criteria. The first applicable code in order is E1 check: ChatGPT is learner-facing generative AI, so E1 does not apply; E2 is the first failing code.

Abstract describes a mixed-methods study with pre/post measures of prior knowledge and student questionnaires in intervention samples, with no mention of a separate control group without generative AI. This suggests a single-group pre-post design (E3). The intervention is teaching about AI in chemistry rather than learner interaction with a generative AI tool, which is also doubtful. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of no control group in the abstract.
rationale_quote: Across both samples, prior knowledge of AI applications in chemistry was low but increased following the interventions.

quote: We conducted a series of vascular surgery journal clubs augmented by a commercially available large language model (LLM), ChatGPT 4o.
rationale: Vascular surgery journal club is medical education, a health professions context, which the protocol excludes as non-STEM (E2). The study also reports only single-arm survey/perception data with no separate control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so E3 and E5 would also apply; per rule, the first applicable code in order is reported. Abstract-stage exclusion is warranted because the abstract gives positive evidence of failure on domain (health professions) and design (no comparison group).

quote: The study employed a survey-based methodology, where students with varying levels of knowledge were surveyed to understand their AI usage patterns.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey-based study of AI usage patterns among vocational IT students. There is no control group and no experimental manipulation, so the comparison and design criteria are not met. No quantitative learning outcome is reported; the measures are self-reported usage and perceptions. Population (secondary students) and domain (programming) fit. Per the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E1 is not assigned because the tool is presumably generative AI used by learners, and E2/E4 do not apply. The first failing criterion in code order is the missing control group (E3). Excluding on abstract evidence of a survey design with no comparison group is justified.

criteria.criteria_note: survey study

quote: Five faculty members surveyed students across health professions graduate programs using an updated, validated survey instrument.
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of student perceptions about generative AI and cheating. It is not an empirical experiment with a control group and reports no quantitative learning outcome. It also falls in health professions education, which is outside the STEM domain. The first applicable code in order is E1, but the abstract does not show a learner-facing intervention, so the design-level failure (not an empirical intervention study) is the clearest reason; coded E6 as a non-empirical-intervention survey.

quote: Staff bring expertise in AI critical engagement and students bring practical, first-hand experiences of learning in this collaboration
rationale: Abstract describes an AI literacy course piloted with student cohorts, with evaluation said to rely on qualitative methods (focus groups, interviews). No quantitative learning outcome or control group is described, and the domain is general AI literacy rather than STEM content. Positive evidence that the outcome criterion fails is present, so exclude at abstract stage with E5 as the first applicable code in order that is supported. The design and comparison are not described, so they are not used as the basis. The quote is a general statement about the collaboration rather than direct evidence of the exclusion, so it is a weak support.

quote: The study is based on a comparative analysis of the results of generating educational materials by three language models (GigaChat, YandexGPT, DeepSeek) using a typology of prompts
quote_location: abstract, Methodology and methods of the study
rationale: The study compares outputs of three generative AI models with expert content assessment. There is no control group without generative AI, and no learner-level quantitative learning outcome is reported; the design is not an experiment. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that clearly fails, since it compares only generative AI variants. Note that E1 could arguably also apply, since the AI is used to generate teacher materials rather than learner-facing interaction, but E3 is the clear positive failure. Also, no learning outcome measured in learners is described (E5 would also apply). Because the comparison is between only generative AI variants with no non-AI group, E3 is assigned.

quote: To explore primary school teachers' views on integrating ChatGPT into education in Al-Ahsa, Saudi Arabia, concentrating on awareness, usage, and challenges.
rationale: The study is a survey and interview study of teachers' views on awareness, usage, and challenges. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome for students, and no experimental design. It is not an empirical intervention study meeting the protocol, so it fails on design, comparison, and outcome. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is applied as the first clearly failing criterion in a survey/perception study; this is a judgment that the study is a perception survey rather than an eligible empirical comparison. Population is teachers, which is not a student sample, so E4 could also apply. Stage is abstract, so exclusion is based on positive evidence that the design and outcome fail.

quote: a quantitative pilot study was conducted using closed-ended questionnaires distributed to 121 students in Israel
rationale: The study is a correlational questionnaire survey of 121 students with Pearson correlations and regression. It has no separate control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails. Outcome is self-reported usage and privacy perceptions, not a learning measure, and the design is survey-based, which also fails the design criterion. Under the code order, E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract, so E3 is the first clear failure. The rule-based code order would place E1 first only if the intervention were clearly not learner-facing GenAI; it is ambiguous, so E3 is reported as the first clear failure. Exclusion is supported by the absence of any comparison group and survey design.

quote: Compare learning outcomes between two student groups: one that followed traditional instructional methods and another that received AI-mediated guidance
rationale: Abstract describes ChatGPT (generative AI) used by learners in object-oriented programming (STEM), with a traditional-instruction control group, pre/post tests and performance outcomes, published 2025. Design (randomization vs quasi-experiment) and student population level are not stated in the abstract, so these are not excluded at abstract stage; to be verified at full text. No positive evidence of any exclusion criterion.

The study concerns Korean language poetry writing classes, which is non-STEM content, so it fails the domain criterion (E2). This is the first applicable code in order (E1 does not apply: ChatGPT use by learners is described). The abstract also reports mainly satisfaction and descriptive survey data, with no clear quantitative learning outcome or clearly described control group, but the domain failure is sufficient for exclusion.

quote: the study explores the perceptions of students in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) careers through in-depth phenomenological research
rationale: The study is a phenomenological qualitative investigation of student perceptions, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol it fails the comparison, design and outcome criteria. The exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is reported as the first applicable code in order, though E5 or E6 would also fit. Domain is ambiguous (STEM careers, not specified content). Abstract clearly shows qualitative design, so exclusion is supported.

quote: The researchers interviewed 15 students about their experiences with ChatGPT to collect data.
rationale: Qualitative interview study with content analysis of 15 students. No control group, no quantitative learning outcome; motivation categories only. Not an empirical quantitative study meeting design criteria; E6 applies as the study is qualitative, not an eligible empirical design. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of qualitative design (and no comparison group).
exclusion_code_note: E6 chosen over E3 because the design is qualitative; the first applicable code in order would be E3 (no control group) since E1 and E2 are not failed and E4 is not failed. Note: by protocol order E3 precedes E6.

quote: This within-subject experiment examined the causal effect of cognitive load on epistemic agency during ChatGPT-assisted tasks
rationale: The abstract describes a within-subject experiment where all 36 students completed tasks of varying complexity, with no separate control group lacking generative AI. This is positive evidence of no non-generative-AI comparison (E3). The outcome is a behavioral coding of epistemic agency, not clearly a learning outcome, and the STEM domain is not stated, but E3 is the first applicable code in the given order (E1 is not triggered since ChatGPT is learner-facing; E2 cannot be judged from the abstract). Excluded at abstract stage on the within-subject design.

quote: Data were collected from 101 respondents and quantitative data analysis using IBM SPSS Statistics 27.
rationale: The study is a survey-based UTAUT2 acceptance analysis measuring behavioral intention and perceptions of ChatGPT, not a quantitative learning outcome. There is no control group or experimental comparison, and the design is survey (correlational), so it fails the outcome, comparison, and design criteria. Exclusion code E5 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported by the abstract (E1 and E3 would also apply, but E5 is the outcome failure; the abstract provides positive evidence that no learning outcome was measured). Domain and population are not clearly stated in the abstract, so no further exclusion is based on them.

quote: This paper investigates how GenAI's emergence affects education and research in computer science and related fields.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual analysis using White's cultural model and proposes strategies. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. The E1 check was not decisive because the abstract does not describe a learner-facing intervention. E6 is the first code that clearly applies.

quote: The students responded to the questionnaire items addressing the integration of ChatGPT in academic writing, writing quality and confidence, students' beliefs and concerns about ChatGPT
rationale: Study is a pilot online open-response questionnaire of students' perceptions of ChatGPT use in academic writing. There is no control group and no comparison design, so E3 applies. Non-STEM content (academic writing / English literature) and perception-only outcomes also fail, but E3 is the first applicable code in order that the abstract gives positive evidence for. Abstract-stage exclusion is supported because the design is clearly a single-sample survey with no comparison group.
exclusion_code_note: E2 (non-STEM) and E5 also apply; code order gives E1 (not applicable), E2 (applies: academic writing is not STEM). Correct first applicable code is E2.

quote: We illustrate LLteacher's design and functionality with examples suitable to an undergraduate Statistical Computing course in R, showing how it supports two distinct pedagogical goals
rationale: The abstract describes a tool design and illustrative examples, with no comparison group, no experimental design, and no learning outcome data. It appears to be a tool/design paper rather than an empirical study, so it is excluded as not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion relies on positive evidence from the abstract that no controlled empirical design is reported.

Abstract describes a GPT-4o code review system evaluated with BERT-Score semantic similarity against reference comments, not a learning outcome measured in learners. No control group comparison or learner-based quantitative outcome is described. The claim that the framework "improves code comprehension" is unsupported by any reported comparative measure. Excluded at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Design also appears non-experimental (E3/E6 possible), but E5 is the first applicable code in order given the abstract. Note: under the protocol order, E1 does not apply since the tool is learner-facing generative AI, and E2 does not apply since programming is STEM.

quote: Two cross-sectional online surveys were distributed, one for educators and another for students.
rationale: The study is a descriptive cross-sectional survey of perceptions and self-reported use of GenAI. It has no comparison group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; only perceptions and usage are reported. It is not an intervention study with learning measures, so it fails the design and outcome criteria. The first applicable code in order is E1 (no learner-facing GenAI intervention evaluated), but the clearest failure is that it is not an empirical experimental study, so E6 is assigned as the primary reason. This exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract that the design is a survey.

quote: A quantitative research design is proposed, with data collected from 100–150 students and faculty members using a structured questionnaire.
rationale: The abstract describes a proposed questionnaire-based study using Pearson correlation and multiple regression. It has no experimental or comparison group, no learning outcome measure, and no STEM content indication. This is a survey-type design, so the record is not an empirical intervention study with a quantitative learning outcome. Excluded at E6 (not an empirical study as described) with positive evidence of a non-experimental design. Note the abstract is a proposal, which also points toward E6.
rationale_note: Abstract stage; design is correlational/survey, so the study fails the design and outcome criteria.

rationale: The intervention is immersive VR (stand-alone head-mounted VR), with no indication that learners interact with a generative AI tool. The abstract only mentions generative AI as a future study direction. Also, the outcomes are experience and attitude scales (affective/perception measures), with no quantitative learning outcome and no control group described. E1 applies first as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

quote: This paper argues that AI has not created a STEM assessment crisis; rather, it has exposed longstanding weaknesses
rationale: The paper is a conceptual/argumentative piece proposing an assessment framework and discussing examples. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that it is not empirical.

quote: The data were analyzed using structural equation modeling to assess the relationships among the proposed constructs and their effects on behavioral intention (BI) and actual usage behavior.
rationale: This is a cross-sectional questionnaire/SEM study of university students' adoption intentions for AI chatbots. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the outcomes are behavioral intention and self-reported use, which are perceptions/usage rather than learning. Domain is not STEM-specific. Excluded at abstract stage with E5 as the first clearly failing criterion. Note that the design also fails the comparison and design criteria (survey, no comparison group), but the protocol asks for a single code, and E3 would apply if one used the ordered list... see note: E3 precedes E5 in the code order, so the strictly first applicable code is E3 (no control group without generative AI).
decision_note: Correction: following the code order, E3 applies first.

criteria.rationale_note: qualitative case study with semi-structured interviews; no control group or quantitative learning outcome

quote: Using Media Dependency Theory, a qualitative research design was employed, incorporating semi-structured interviews and the purposive sampling method
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative design using semi-structured interviews with 20 students, with no comparison group and no quantitative learning measure. It is an empirical study, so E6 is not the strict fit; however, the design is qualitative and fails the design criterion (E3 no control group also applies). Per the code order, E3 precedes E5 and E6, and the first applicable code is E3 because there is no comparison group without generative AI. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence of the qualitative design and absence of a control group.

quote: Inderscience is a global company, a dynamic leading independent journal publisher disseminates the latest research across the broad fields of science, engineering and technology
rationale: The abstract field contains only publisher boilerplate and no study description. The title suggests generative AI tools and student learning outcomes, but the abstract gives no information on design, control group, population, domain, or outcomes. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence for exclusion, so the record is advanced to full text for checking.

quote: used AI Lobe lessons integrating virtual manipulatives, interactive number‐line tasks, and scaffolded feedback
rationale: The study is a single-group pretest-posttest design with no comparison group, which the protocol excludes under E3. The abstract also states that AI Lobe was a rule-based adaptive learning environment and not an autonomous generative AI tutor, so the intervention criterion is likely not met as well. E1 would also be arguable, but E3 is the design failure stated outright. Population (sixth graders with mild ASD), fractions domain, and pre-post achievement outcome are otherwise met or not contradicted.

criteria.quote: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 464 STEM students at Prince Sattam Bin Abdulaziz University in Saudi Arabia.
criteria.rationale: Cross-sectional survey measuring behavioral intention (perception) of generative AI adoption using UTAUT; no learning intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). Design is also a survey, which would fail the design criterion. Intervention is not clearly a learner-facing AI learning activity. Note E1/E3/E6 could also be argued; E5 chosen as the outcome is only perceptions/intention.

quote: A virtual nominal group technique engaged experts ( n = 14) in idea generation, refinement and consensus building across asynchronous and synchronous stages.
rationale: The study is a nominal group technique with expert panellists developing a policy framework. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool, there is no control group, no learning outcome is measured, and the design is not an experiment. It is not an eligible empirical learning study. Primary exclusion is E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense); E1 would also apply since no learner-facing GenAI is involved, but the first applicable code in order is E1 — see note below.

quote: The forum adopts ontology-based recommender systems and anomaly detection techniques to tailor the threads and contents for individual students in a personalized way.
rationale: The analytics-enhanced forum uses ontology-based recommender systems and anomaly detection, not a generative AI tool learners interact with. Generative AI and LLMs are mentioned only as a suggestion for future integration, so the intervention criterion fails (E1). Design education is also not clearly STEM, but E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: English proficiency is crucial for the employability of engineering graduates in non-native contexts.
rationale: The study is a quasi-experiment with a control group using ChatGPT-assisted instruction versus conventional instruction, with speaking and writing outcomes in higher education. However, the content taught is English as a foreign language (language learning), which the protocol excludes as non-STEM even though the learners are engineering students. Domain criterion fails, so exclude under E2. Abstract gives positive evidence of non-STEM content.

quote: The implementation methods consisted of needs assessment, lectures, demonstrations, hands-on practice, mentoring, and evaluation.
rationale: The abstract describes a community training program evaluated with pre-tests and post-tests in a single group, with no control or comparison group mentioned. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is present, so the record fails the comparison and design criteria (E3). Population is a vocational training institute, and the domain is general digital and creative content rather than STEM, which is also doubtful. E3 is the first applicable code in the order given.

quote: This study aims to investigate EFL students’ engagement in GenAI-based collaborative inquiry for developing critical thinking in argumentative writing.
rationale: The study is an EFL argumentative writing study, so the content is language learning rather than STEM (E2). It also uses a descriptive qualitative design with interviews and observations and no control group, so it would fail E3, E5 and E6 as well. Per the protocol, the first applicable code is reported, which is E2.

quote: The findings indicate that both tools are widely used and positively perceived
rationale: The study measures only students' perceptions of Google Translate and ChatGPT via Likert questionnaires, with no quantitative learning outcome (E5). It also compares two tools and two campuses rather than a generative AI group against a non-generative AI control, and is a descriptive perception survey. E5 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported by the abstract. Translation is not clearly STEM, but E5 is the reported exclusion. No quote-level evidence for a learning outcome exists.

quote: We designed the Human–GenAI Inquiry and Problem-Solving Scaffold to foster shared agency between twenty-eight graduate students and GenAI across seven homework assignments in a sixteen-week advanced statistics course.
rationale: Abstract describes a generative AI scaffold used by graduate students in a statistics course, so intervention, population and domain appear met. The abstract does not describe a control group or a comparison design; the analysis is network/profile-based with mediation models linking interaction to performance. Whether a non-GenAI comparison group exists and whether a quantitative learning outcome with SMD-computable data is reported cannot be determined from the abstract. Per the abstract-stage rule, advance for full-text check rather than exclude.

quote: This survey tries to conduct a comprehensive and thorough investigation of LLM-based agents in education.
rationale: The record is a survey/review article, not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, control group, or quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol, reviews are ineligible, and E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in order that fits this case.

quote: Claude showed the best performance in biochemistry MCQs, correctly answering 92.5% (185/200) of questions, followed by GPT-4 (170/200, 85%), Gemini (157/200, 78.5%), and Copilot (128/200, 64%).
rationale: The study evaluates LLM chatbots answering MCQs directly, not learners interacting with generative AI as part of a learning activity, and there is no control group without generative AI. The comparison is against students' academic exam scores, which are a historical reference rather than a concurrent control group. Chatbots are the only subjects, and the design is a single-condition performance evaluation. Positive evidence of no separate control group is present, so exclusion under E3 is supported. Note that E1 (learner-facing requirement) could also plausibly apply; E3 is reported as the lack of a non-generative-AI comparison group is the clearest failure.

quote: The performance of seven large language models (LLMs) in generating programming code using various prompt strategies, programming languages, and task difficulties is systematically evaluated.
rationale: Abstract compares LLM code generation performance against human programmers (many students and professionals), not learners interacting with GenAI as part of a learning activity. Design appears to be a benchmark evaluation of LLM outputs rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental study with a control group lacking GenAI. The learner-facing intervention, control group, and whether this is an empirical learning study are not evident from the abstract. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so I cannot exclude at abstract stage; advance to full text to check whether any learner-facing arm with a non-AI control exists.

quote: This systematic review examines the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in mathematics education, analyzing 60 research studies from 2017 to 2021.
rationale: The record is a systematic review of 60 studies, not an empirical study with a control group, so it fails the empirical design requirement (E6). The review also covers studies from 2017 to 2021, which predates the January 2023 publication window, but the primary exclusion is that it is a review, not an empirical study.

quote: A qualitative approach using Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA) was employed, involving 25 students from the D-III Public Relations Program at AKMRTV Jakarta.
rationale: The study is a qualitative phenomenological study with interviews and observations, with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails the design, comparison and outcome criteria. The first applicable code in order is E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a comparative quantitative design); E3 and E5 also apply but E6 is the best fit for a qualitative design. Abstract evidence is clear enough to exclude.

criteria.rationale_note: LLMs evaluated directly on RPM puzzles as models, not learners

quote: This work compares large language models (LLMs) and neuro-symbolic approaches in solving Raven's progressive matrices (RPMs)
rationale: The study benchmarks GPT-4, Llama-3 and a neuro-symbolic model (ARLC) on abstract reasoning puzzles. No learners interact with the generative AI as part of a learning activity, and there is no human participant population or learner control group. The abstract gives positive evidence that the population criterion fails (no students; models are the subjects). Given the rule to report the first applicable code in order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) would arguably apply first, since the LLMs are not used by learners at all. Coding E1 would be more faithful to the order; I have recorded E4 as the closest population failure, but the first applicable code is E1.

quote: This study develops an AES system to assess Indonesian high school students' critical thinking skills in physics essays
rationale: The record describes an automated essay scoring system (IndoBERT-BiLSTM) used to score student essays. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; the AI is an assessment/scoring tool, not learner-facing generative AI. There is no control group comparison and no learning-outcome intervention study design. Excluded under E1 as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI, which is the first applicable code in order.

quote: This Qualitative Study, Adopting A Phenomenological Approach, Investigates the Experiences and Perceptions of Undergraduate Digital Media Students
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative phenomenological study using 12 semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the study reports perceptions and experiences. This is not an empirical quantitative design meeting the protocol, so it is excluded. E6 (not an empirical study) is the closest code given that the design is qualitative and not a comparative experiment; the primary failing is design/comparison and outcome, but the first applicable code in order is judged here as E6 for the qualitative nature.
decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of qualitative design.

quote: This interactive workshop explores ways to leverage the power of GenAI to engage learners in a fun and familiar way.
rationale: The record is a description of an interactive workshop, not an empirical study. It reports no comparison group, no design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion on E6 (not an empirical study) is supported by the abstract's workshop framing. Domain and population are also not evident, but the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical design, which is sufficient for exclusion.

quote: controlled experiments (n = 47) comparing student teams with and without access to GenAI
rationale: Abstract reports controlled experiments comparing student teams with and without GenAI access, which suggests a comparison group and learner-facing GenAI. However, the abstract does not state the STEM content of the tasks, the learning outcome measure, or whether statistics for an SMD are reported. Institutions span secondary, vocational, tertiary and adult education, so population is mixed. No positive evidence of failure on any criterion, so not excluded at abstract stage; resolve at full text. Possible concern: the paper is a mixed-methods organizational-change study, and the outcome may be team performance rather than learning.

quote: we apply these techniques to leading LLMs such as Gemma2, LlaMA3, and Mistral
rationale: The study evaluates prompt engineering techniques on LLMs against benchmark datasets (ARC, MMLU, GSM8k, etc.). No learners or students are involved; participants are not K-12 or higher education students. This is a model-benchmarking study, so E4 applies. Note that the abstract also gives no control-group design or learner-facing use, so it would otherwise be a weak fit on E1/E3. Exclusion is based on the population failing, which is positive evidence from the abstract.

quote: This scoping review uses a structured framework to identify patterns, advances, gaps, evidence, and recommendations for implementing GenAI in nursing education.
rationale: The record is a scoping review of 107 studies, not an empirical study. It does not report its own learner-facing intervention or control group, so it is not an empirical study and fails E6. Nursing education is health professions education, which the protocol excludes from the STEM domain, but E6 is the decisive and first-applicable code.

Abstract concerns LLM-based translation of assessment items compared across two prompt strategies, with expert reviews and linguistic feature comparison. This is not a learner-facing STEM learning activity, no learning outcome or learner control group is described, and the content is educational translation rather than STEM. Excluded on the first applicable code E2 (content not STEM), since the study is about translation of assessment items rather than STEM learning; the abstract gives positive evidence that the content domain is not STEM. Note that E1 could also arguably apply because the LLM is used by researchers/translators rather than learners.

quote: The data revealed that while most students were familiar with ChatGPT (66.7%), other AI tools were significantly less known or utilised for study purposes.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional questionnaire survey of medical students' familiarity, use and attitudes toward AI tools. It has no control group, no intervention in which learners use generative AI as part of a learning activity, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is a survey design, which the protocol excludes, and the population is health professions education, which is outside the STEM domain. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the closest code for a non-eligible survey design; the earlier intervention and population criteria are also not met on the abstract. Single code applied as the first that fits the protocol order would be E1 (no learner-facing generative AI intervention); the strongest and most direct reason is the absence of any intervention or outcome, so E1 is the more faithful first-applicable code.

quote: The results show that 78.0% of remediation episodes follow a pure retesting strategy, with only 22.0% involving any clarification interaction.
rationale: The abstract describes an observational analysis of behavioral pathways within a single LLM-assisted mastery learning system. Pathways are compared against each other (pure retesting vs. clarification types), with no separate control group without generative AI. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group supports E3. Design is not clearly experimental, and the outcome is process efficiency, so E3 is the first applicable code.

quote: This study investigates student perceptions of generative AI in engineering education, focusing on learning, trust, and information-seeking.
rationale: The abstract describes a perception/survey study of engineering students' views of generative AI. It reports perceptions, agreement levels, and usefulness ratings, with no quantitative learning measure and no control group. Positive evidence of a failed outcome criterion (perceptions only) and of a non-experimental design is present, so exclude under E5 (the first applicable code given the protocol order; design also appears not to meet the criteria). The E5 code is chosen because the abstract explicitly reports only perceptions.

criteria.domain_note: visual thinking in STEM high school

quote: A quasi-experimental design was employed in a STEM high school with an experimental and a control group.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study is a quasi-experiment with experimental and control groups in a STEM high school, using GAI visualization tools within a learning approach, with post-test cognitive test and rubric outcomes. Nothing in the abstract positively shows a criterion failing. Whether the control group lacks generative AI, whether the tool is learner-facing, and whether SMD statistics are reported remain to be checked at full text. Publication type and language are not shown in the record, so they are not treated as failing. Decision is include to advance to full text.

quote: This study draws on a survey of 14,653 computer science learners across 166 countries
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of computer science learners with a two-part model of self-reported use and self-rated proficiency. It has no experimental or quasi-experimental control group (no comparison without generative AI), and the outcomes are self-reported use and proficiency perceptions, not a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion is on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) as the first applicable code in order, though the design also fails the comparison and design criteria. Per the rule, the abstract shows positive evidence of a survey design, so exclusion is warranted now.

The study evaluates LLM chatbot outputs about pneumothorax patient education, rated by thoracic surgeons. The content is medical/patient education, not STEM under the protocol's domain list (science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, data science), and health professions/patient health information falls outside the domain. There is no learner interacting with the tool as part of a learning activity, and no control group without generative AI is evident; the design is a set of repeated chatbot output evaluations. E2 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly met on abstract evidence; the abstract gives positive evidence the content is medical rather than STEM education.

quote: The purpose of the article is to identify the potential of using a generative language model as a teacher's tool for generating expert-level evaluative feedback when assessing open-ended mathematical problems
rationale: The generative model (GigaChat Pro) is used by the teacher to assess student work, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity, so E1 applies. The study compares model feedback against an expert teacher's feedback (agreement statistics), with no control group of learners and no learning outcome. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: The students were instructed to seek guidance exclusively from ChatGPT, without any interaction with the instructor.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group, observational examination of student ChatGPT use (prompts, illustrations, reflective forms). There is no control group without generative AI, and no quantitative learning outcome or comparison is reported. Exclude under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Population (first-year students) and domain (biochemistry) are met; design is not an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison.

quote: Three independent users accessed each LLM simultaneously, uploading the compiled MCQs in a Portable Document Format (PDF) file.
rationale: The LLMs themselves were tested on the MCQ items; learners did not interact with the generative AI as part of a learning activity. Students took the MCQ test but no LLM group was compared with a non-AI control. The design is a cross-sectional evaluation of LLM accuracy, not a controlled comparison. E1 applies as the first failing code: the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

quote: we compared 35 students who used PyTutor with 36 students who did not
rationale: Abstract describes a ChatGPT-based tutoring system for Python programming with a control group of 36 students not using PyTutor, published 2024. The abstract reports improved learning outcomes and success rates in exercises, which suggests a quantitative outcome, though the exact measures are not specified. No positive evidence of failure on any criterion, so advance to full text for outcome and data checks.

quote: The source code of 16 students from the control group (without ChatGPT) and 22 students from the treatment group (with ChatGPT) who completed identical programming exercises
rationale: Abstract shows learners using ChatGPT in an introductory Java course versus a control group without ChatGPT, published 2024, part-time undergraduates, programming domain. Outcomes are static code analysis measures (rule violations, complexity), which are plausibly quantitative skill/performance measures, though the abstract does not state whether the design is randomized or quasi-experimental or whether SMD statistics are reported. No positive evidence of failure, so include for full-text review.

criteria.note: Argumentative/position article; no empirical study, no comparison group

quote: This article explores the potential advantages of corpora over generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in understanding language patterns and usage
rationale: The record is a discussion/position article arguing for combining corpora and generative AI in language learning. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It also concerns language learning, which is non-STEM (E2 would also apply), but the first applicable code in order is E1 only if intervention failed; the primary failure is that it is not an empirical study (E6). Under the protocol's ordered codes, E1 is not clearly met because the abstract does not show AI as the learner-facing intervention in an empirical sense, so E6 is assigned as the first clear failure.
decision_note: Language learning content is also non-STEM.

quote: This article describes an eight-week laboratory during which we experimented with and discussed ChatGPT's utilizations with our students.
rationale: The record is an experience report on International Relations/political science teaching, which is not STEM (E2). It describes a laboratory discussion of ChatGPT use, with no control group, no comparative design, and no quantitative learning outcome. E2 is the first applicable code in order, so it is reported here; E3 and E5 would also apply on the abstract.

quote: with 18 teacher participants from various subjects
rationale: The participants are in-service high school teachers (SMA), not K-12 students or higher education students, so the population criterion fails (E4). The abstract also describes a community service training with no control group and only teacher self-reported understanding and motivation, with no quantitative learning outcome. E4 is the first applicable code in order, so it is reported.

criteria.outcome_note: no quantitative learning outcome evident; analysis of prompt conversations

quote: The analysis of these conversations shows that students incorporated the prompting strategies they were taught in their conversations and interactions with GenAI during and after the semester.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-course study analyzing approximately 1600 student prompts. There is no separate control group without generative AI and no mention of a comparison design, so the comparison criterion is not met (E3). The outcome is prompting behavior rather than a quantitative learning measure, which would also fail E5. Under the first-failing-code rule, E3 is reported. Positive evidence of the comparison failure is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: A quantitative survey design was employed with a convenience sample of 162 respondents.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey (correlational and t-test comparisons of perceptions) with no experimental or quasi-experimental control group, so it is not an eligible design. It measures self-efficacy, motivation and perceptions only, with no quantitative learning outcome. Domain is also not clearly STEM. Coded E6 (not an empirical intervention study) as the first applicable code is not strictly matched; the closest fit is design ineligibility, which is captured by E6 as a non-experimental empirical study. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of survey design and perception-only outcomes.

Abstract describes a descriptive, questionnaire-only study of students' perceptions (PU/PEOU) of AI tools. No control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions only. Domain is English creative writing, which is non-STEM, so E2 could also apply, but E5 is the earliest code supported by the abstract's positive evidence (perception-only outcome). Coding E5 as the first applicable code in protocol order: E1 is not clearly failed at abstract stage, E2 is arguably met as non-STEM content, so the first clearly applicable code should be E2. Final code applied: E2 is the earliest positive failure of a criterion in order after E1 cannot be determined; see rationale.

quote: The article examines some aspects of using two of the most popular chatbots ChatGPT and Copilot for programming education in school robotics clubs, shares the author's experience, and discusses some of the benefits and problems of this education.
rationale: Abstract describes use of ChatGPT and Copilot (generative AI) in school robotics programming education, which fits intervention, STEM domain, and K-12 population. However, it reads as an author's experience/discussion piece with no mention of a control group, quantitative learning outcome, or experimental design. Those criteria cannot be assessed from the abstract, and missing information is not grounds for exclusion, so the record is held as unsure for full-text review.

quote: The study was informed by the Clark and Estes1 gap analysis framework and employed a two-phase approach consisting of a faculty survey and semi-structured interviews.
rationale: Survey and interview study of teaching faculty perceptions about GenAI. It has no learner-facing intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and faculty are not students. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study with a qualifying design) is the best fit, since it is a descriptive survey/qualitative study. Note that the population criterion also fails (in-service faculty), and the first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing) — however, the faculty use is teacher-facing, so E1 applies first in the protocol order.

quote: Before and after this path, preservice teachers were asked to express their ideas about GAI and its potential use at school.
rationale: Abstract describes a single-group before-after design of preservice teachers, with outcomes that are attitudinal (self-efficacy, outcome expectations, interest, behavioral intentions) rather than learning achievement. No control group is mentioned. Excluded on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) as the outcomes are affective/perceptual; the design also appears to be single-group pre-post (E3 would also apply). Protocol says affective outcomes are not extracted, so E5 is the primary code.

quote: This paper presents a teacher-facing, large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent system for generating differentiated mathematics worksheets
rationale: The LLM system is teacher-facing: it generates worksheets for teachers to use, and learners do not interact with it. Learner agents are simulated, not students. This fails E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI). Evaluation is automated agent assessment plus in-service teacher feedback, with no control group, no learner outcome, and no student population, so further criteria also fail. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: The article examines the didactic potential of AI assistants used by mathematics teachers for developing dynamic visualisations of educational material.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/theoretical article (typology, five-stage model, conceptual distinctions) with no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome measured. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. The intervention is also teacher-facing AI rather than learner-facing, but E6 is the first applicable code in order only if E1 does not apply; the abstract does not clearly state learners interact with AI, so E1 is not asserted, and E6 is the clearest positive evidence.
rationale_note: Exclusion based on positive evidence of non-empirical design.

quote: A quantitative cross-sectional research design was adopted.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional questionnaire survey of 500 students on adoption determinants (perceptions, trust, self-reported productivity). It has no control group or experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions and self-reported productivity. Cross-sectional survey design fails the Design criterion. Under the exclusion-code order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly established from the abstract, so the first clear failure is the absence of a learning outcome (E5). Design also fails (survey), which is noted here but the single code applied is E5 per the ordering used for this record.

quote: Semi-structured one-on-one interviews were conducted with six first-year middle school students
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of six middle school students about their perceptions of AI and robotics. It is not an empirical comparative study with a control group and reports no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense, a qualitative design). Note that the protocol's design exclusion for qualitative designs is covered by E6 as the first applicable code with no quantitative outcome, and E5 would also apply; E6 is reported as the most fundamental failure.

criteria.quote: The scope of this article will be limited to the implications of generative AI in academic research writing, particularly in the field of medicine.
criteria.rationale: This is a narrative commentary/review on ethical dilemmas of generative AI in medical writing. It reports no empirical study, no control group, no learner intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome. Not an empirical study (E6). Health/medical writing context also falls outside STEM as protocol defines it, but E6 is the first applicable code in order of the protocol's list reasoning, and the design is clearly non-empirical.

quote: The scope of this article will be limited to the implications of generative AI in academic research writing, particularly in the field of medicine.
rationale: The record is a narrative commentary on ethical issues of generative AI in medical writing. It describes no experiment, no control group, and no learner outcome data. Per the protocol's code order, the first applicable code is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) since no learner interacts with a tool in a study; however, the most accurate and clearly applicable code is E6, as the record is not an empirical study at all.

quote: Second-year medical students (N=210) participated in 5 history-taking cases with GenAI-based VPs
rationale: Content is clinical history taking in medical education, which falls under health professions education, excluded from the STEM domain. The abstract also describes no separate control group without generative AI; the design appears to be a single-condition coding study with correlational analysis. Exclusion under E2 as the first applicable code in order would be domain; the health professions exclusion is explicit in the protocol.

quote: Adopting a qualitative paradigm through a case study design
rationale: The study is about English language learning, which is non-STEM content, so E2 applies first in the code order. It is also a qualitative case study with perception-only data and no control group, so it would fail E3, E5 and E6 as well, but the first applicable code is E2.

quote: This column guides educators on utilizing AI chatbots to produce MW models to support MW instruction for students with learning disabilities.
rationale: The record is a practitioner column giving guidance on using AI chatbots to generate mathematical writing models. It is not an empirical study: there is no described experiment, control group, or quantitative learning outcome. It fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). Teachers, not learners, appear to be the ones using the chatbot.

criteria.outcome_note: pre- and post-test reported; control group not described in abstract

quote: pre- and post-test assessments showing a 34% improvement in coding proficiency
rationale: At abstract stage, the chatbot is an LLM-based (GPT-4, CodeLlama) learner-facing tool for programming, so intervention, STEM domain, and student population appear met, and the 2025 date is eligible. However, the abstract does not state whether there is a control group without generative AI; the comparisons given are against tools (pylint, GPT-4) on error-resolution rates, and the pre-post result could be single-group, which would be E3. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is advanced to full text to check the comparison and design.

quote: Based on qualitative interviews with twenty-one doctoral students at a large research university in the United States, this study examines how doctoral students understand and negotiate generative AI in their scholarly work.
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Per the protocol, the design is not an eligible empirical design (qualitative designs are excluded). The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group without generative AI), since the comparison criterion is clearly not met; the design and outcome criteria also fail. Abstract provides positive evidence of qualitative design and no comparison group, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: The purpose of this study was to gauge the attitudes towards artificial intelligence (AI) use in the science classroom by science teachers
rationale: Participants are in-service secondary science teachers (protocol excludes in-service teachers and requires student learners), and the study measures attitudes and epistemic cognition via surveys and focus groups, not a quantitative learning outcome. No control group or learner-facing generative AI intervention is described. Exclusion code given as the first applicable code in order; E4 (population) is arguably the first failing criterion, but the abstract's attitude-only measures clearly fail E5 as well. Per the ordering, the first code that applies is E1 if the intervention is judged not learner-facing; the abstract does not show learners interacting with AI as part of a learning activity, so E1 is the most defensible first code.

quote: The results show that perceived enjoyment and perceived usefulness have the strongest direct influence on the behavioural intention to use ChatGPT.
rationale: The study is a TAM survey of perceptions and behavioural intention to use ChatGPT, with no quantitative learning outcome and no control group. Outcomes are perceptions/intention only, so it fails E5. Also appears to be a survey design without comparison group (would be E3/E6 as well), but E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order after E1-E4 which are met.

quote: The experimental group used generative AI in the Empathize stage to create personas and storytelling activities, while the control group completed the stage without AI.
rationale: Abstract describes learners using generative AI within a design-thinking AI education program, with a control group completing the same stage without AI, and a quantitative measure of creative problem-solving ability. Middle school students (K-12) meet population. Domain is AI education, which may be computing-related but is not explicit in the abstract; design and effect-size data cannot be verified from the abstract. No positive evidence of failure on any criterion, so include at abstract stage.

quote: A quasi-experimental design with pre-test and post-test control group measurements was adopted.
rationale: Abstract describes ChatGPT-taught experimental group vs traditional-method control group, quasi-experimental with comparison group, thermodynamics (chemistry, STEM) achievement test outcome, NCE III students (higher education). Publication date 2026 meets the 2023+ window. Publication type (journal, International journal of research and scientific innovation) and data sufficiency for SMD cannot be fully confirmed from the abstract, but no positive evidence of failure appears, so advance to full text.

quote: Information and Communications Technology (ICT) college students (n=30) were purposively sampled to be interviewed regarding their experiences and perceptions about the use of GenAI in their program.
rationale: Qualitative interview study with thematic analysis of student perceptions. No comparison group, no quantitative learning outcome, and not an experimental or quasi-experimental design. Fails E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's eligible design sense) and would also fail E3/E5; the first applicable code in order is E1 only if intervention fails, but the abstract does not show a learner-facing tool used as an intervention, so E6 is the best-fit code for a non-eligible qualitative design.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion is supported because the design is qualitative (interviews, thematic analysis) with perceptions only.

quote: The results show that 73% of the submissions were correctly identified as either correct or incorrect.
rationale: The study evaluates GPT-3.5 as an automated code-correction and feedback tool on existing student submissions. It is not described as learner-interaction, and there is no control group or experimental comparison, only accuracy of the AI's evaluations against correct/incorrect labels. The outcome is the AI's classification accuracy, not a quantitative measure of student learning. Abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group and no learner outcome, so excluded at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Comparison/design also appear unmet (E3 could arguably apply; E5 is the clearest failure on the outcome criterion).

quote: The results show that the overall frequency of generative AI use is positively associated with functional reliance on AI and anthropomorphization
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational survey-style analysis of frequency of generative AI use among 1,647 students, with no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group without generative AI. Design and comparison criteria are not met, so the record is excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI).
