Generative nature of the custom chatbot is implied by ChatGPT comparison but should be confirmed at full text. Publication type and data sufficiency cannot be judged from the abstract. Unsure pending full text.

quote: A vast majority of participants indicated that AI enhances their sense of confidence, productivity, and learning independence
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-cultural survey of student perceptions about generative AI use and academic integrity. Outcomes are perceptions and self-reported confidence and productivity, not a quantitative learning measure, and there is no indication of a control group or experimental comparison. Design is survey-based, which the protocol excludes. Under the abstract-stage rule, the strongest positive evidence is that the study is a perception survey without a learning outcome, so it is excluded on E5 (the design also fails, but the code order gives E5 as the first clear failure for an empirical study with no learning outcome).

quote: We introduce a novel LLM-driven process and application, called ItemForge, tailored specifically for the automatic generation of e-assessment items in mathematics.
rationale: The LLM is used to generate assessment items for instructors/materials production; no learner interacts with the tool as part of a learning activity. Evaluation is by three mathematical experts reviewing 240 items, with no learner outcome and no control group. Excluded at E1 (not learner-facing generative AI), which is the first applicable code in order. Abstract evidence is sufficient for exclusion.

quote: Six open-source LLMs and GPT-4 (as expert reference) independently scored each response using two predefined rubrics.
rationale: The LLMs are used for automated scoring of student responses, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. Learners do not interact with the generative AI. There is also no control group without generative AI, and the study compares LLM graders against GPT-4 rather than a learning outcome. E1 applies as the first failing code in order.

criteria.stage_note: qualitative coding of student written responses; no control group

quote: Using a deductive qualitative approach, 192 written responses were coded against a 32-item taxonomy of ethical and professional considerations.
rationale: The study is a deductive qualitative analysis of student perceptions of GenAI failure case studies. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; it reports perceptions and ethical considerations only. Design (qualitative, not an experiment) also fails. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group), but E5 is also clearly met as a failure. Per the protocol's order, E3 applies first because the absence of a comparison group is positive evidence stated by the design. Note: the abstract does not explicitly describe a control group, so the exclusion is based on the qualitative design and perception-only outcomes.

quote: The combination of these tools resulted in a significant reduction in analysis time by 89.1% compared to manual methods.
rationale: The study is an R&D development of an automated assessment framework (Whisper plus GPT-4o) used to evaluate children's communication. The AI is used for transcription and analysis of recorded speech, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity, and there is no control group without generative AI; the comparison is against manual assessment by teachers, and the design is a framework evaluation rather than a comparison experiment. Positive evidence of no separate non-generative-AI control group is present, so E3 is applied. Domain (autism communication assessment) is not STEM, which is also a failing criterion, but the first applicable code in order is E1 if intervention is judged not learner-facing; I applied E3 as the comparison failure is the clearest positive evidence. No outcome is a learning measure in the protocol sense either.

quote: Data were collected using a survey instrument designed to gather information on educators’ experiences, practices, and concerns related to generative AI integration.
rationale: The record is a survey of in-service K-12 educators about perceptions and practices. It is not an empirical experiment with learners, has no control group, and reports no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded as not an empirical study of the eligible design (E6); E4 also applies because the sample is educators rather than students, but E6 is the primary design failure. Under the code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing) is the first code that could apply since learners do not interact with a GenAI tool, but the abstract gives no learner-facing intervention; the clearest positive failure is the survey design.

quote: This paper therefore reconceptualizes CoI in the age of GenAI by positioning GenAI as an epistemic condition.
rationale: The record is a conceptual/theoretical paper that reconceptualizes the Community of Inquiry framework and proposes a heuristic. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Per the first-applicable-code rule, E1 (intervention) is not positively ruled out by the abstract alone, but E6 is the clear, earlier-ordered failure only if E1 is not met; since the abstract gives no learner-facing GenAI intervention evidence either way, E6 is the most defensible code given the design is non-empirical.

quote: The study employed a quantitative research method to analyze the data gathered through a cross-sectional survey using a purposive sampling technique.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey measuring attitudes and behavioral intentions, with no learning outcome and no control group. Perceptions-only outcomes fail the outcome criterion (E5). Exclusion is based on the survey design and perception-only outcomes, and the abstract gives positive evidence of this.
rationale_note: Ordering note: E5 applied first in code order where E1 (intervention) is unclear; the survey design also fails E6-like empirical-design criteria but the protocol's listed codes for a survey without learning outcome best match E5.

quote: This single-group, pretest–posttest mixed-methods feasibility study included 35 first-year students
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pretest-posttest feasibility design with no separate control group without generative AI, which fails the comparison and design criteria. Under the protocol's borderline rule, one group measured before and after is E3. Evidence-based nursing is also not clearly STEM, but E3 is the first applicable code in order for this record given the abstract evidence.

quote: ChatGPT and Legal Education in Indonesia: Examining Readiness and Implications
rationale: Legal education is not STEM (domain fails, E2). The abstract also describes an empirical survey-style study of law schools' readiness and perceptions, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, so it would fail other criteria too. E2 is the first applicable code in order, as the protocol requires reporting the first code that applies.

quote: Forty-six students participated, with 30 completing the TAM questionnaire.
rationale: At abstract stage there is positive evidence of no control group: the study reports a single-group deployment of MoodleBot with TAM questionnaire and accuracy measures, with no comparison condition described. Outcomes are perceptions (TAM acceptance) and response accuracy rather than a quantitative learning outcome, which also points away from eligibility. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI); E5 is a secondary concern. Note the abstract stage rule is to exclude only on positive evidence; the absence of any comparison group described is the basis here.

quote: Quantitative data were collected using the System Usability Scale (SUS), while qualitative data were obtained through semi-structured interviews
rationale: The study measures only perceived usability (SUS) and interview perceptions in a single-sample mixed-methods design with no control group. The domain is English language education, which is non-STEM. No quantitative learning outcome is reported. Exclusion code E5 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order after E1 (the intervention is generative AI used by learners, so E1 does not apply), and E2 (non-STEM) would also apply; under the protocol's order E2 precedes E5, so the code should be E2 rather than E5. Correcting: the first applicable code in order is E2.

quote: Classical machine learning models, including logistic regression, XGBoost, and support vector machine, are used to distinguish between AI-generated and student-written essays.
rationale: The study is a detection-classifier evaluation: models classify essays as AI-generated or student-written. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; generative models are only the objects being detected. This fails the learner-facing intervention requirement (E1). No control group without generative AI in the learning sense is described either, and the outcome is classifier accuracy rather than learning. E1 is reported as the first applicable code.

quote: The findings revealed that the chatbot was highly successful, achieving an expert validation score of 91.11% ("Very Valid") and a user practicality score of 84.42% ("Very Practical").
rationale: Abstract describes a fine-tuned Mistral (generative LLM) chatbot for Grade VII algebra, with a post-test outcome. However, the abstract reports no control or comparison group; the design appears to be R&D with validation, practicality and a single-group mastery threshold. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group is not explicit in the abstract, so the design cannot be confirmed as failing. Advancing to full text to check for a comparison group.

quote: Using narrative review, critical review, concept analysis, and theory synthesis on 2021-2026 literature, it combines Conceptual Change theory, Interactive Engagement, Modeling Instruction, Vygotsky-Piaget constructivism, and TPACK
rationale: The abstract describes a theoretical framework and development roadmap based on narrative review and concept analysis. No empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome are reported; the Design-Based Research validation is only proposed as future work. Not an empirical study (E6). Note that the criteria object above has a non-protocol key 't' which should be disregarded.

quote: The study recommends integrating generative AI applications into English language instruction and teacher-training programs
rationale: The study targets oral communication skills taught in English language instruction, which is language learning, not STEM. Per the protocol, language learning is excluded (E2). The abstract also does not clearly state the learner's interaction with a generative AI tool, but the domain failure alone is sufficient. Population (middle school) and quasi-experimental control group with a quantitative post-test appear to be met.

quote: we conducted a qualitative exploratory study that employed semi-structured interviews
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of in-service Norwegian teachers about LLM use. It is not an empirical experimental study with a control group or learner learning outcome, and participants are teachers rather than students. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense) applies, as the design is qualitative and does not measure learning outcomes. Coded as E6 since the qualitative design is non-eligible per the design criterion; population (in-service teachers) would also fail.

quote: Fifteen students participated in this study from mathematics-oriented courses e.g., engineering, statistics, and education. Interviews were conducted on how students used AI chat models
rationale: Qualitative interview study of 15 students with no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of missing comparison (E3) applies; design is also non-experimental. Under the code order, E3 is the first failing criterion that applies on the abstract's evidence.

quote: Data collection and processing were conducted during professional development courses for education professionals in the Chernihiv region (Ukraine) through pedagogical observation of course participants and their work with AI.
rationale: The study is a descriptive observational/retrospective analysis of teachers' use of ChatGPT 3.5 during professional development courses. It has no control group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome for students. The participants are in-service teachers, which is outside the population criteria. The main reason is that it is not an empirical comparative study, so E6 is applied. Under the first-applicable-code rule, E1 (learner-facing intervention) is not clearly established, and E3 would also apply, but E6 best captures the non-empirical, observational nature.
decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: This conceptual paper introduces phonocentrism in GenAI as a theoretical lens
rationale: The paper self-describes as a conceptual paper that reviews literature and proposes a theoretical model. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion is supported by positive evidence in the abstract.

quote: Therefore, this perspective article aims to discuss the opportunities and cautions associated with GenAI in dental education
rationale: The record is a perspective article that explicitly states no evidence exists on GenAI effects on critical thinking in dental students. It is not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It also has no control group or quantitative learning outcome. Dental education is health-professions content, which would also fail the domain criterion, but E6 is the first applicable code in the order given (E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract).

quote: By analyzing artificially generated data sets, the capabilities and limitations of ChatGPT in performing statistical analyses are demonstrated.
rationale: The abstract describes an evaluation of ChatGPT's performance on artificially generated datasets, not a learner-facing intervention with a control group. There is no comparison group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome for learners. Excluded at E5 as the abstract gives positive evidence of no learning outcome measure. Note that the design also appears non-experimental (E3/E6 could apply), but E5 is the first applicable code given the protocol order and the evidence in the abstract.

quote: This paper explores the transformative impact of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) on teachers' roles and agencies in education, presenting a comprehensive framework
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual framework paper (four teacher roles) rather than an empirical study. No experimental design, comparison group, or quantitative learning outcome is described, and the population is teachers (pre- and in-service) rather than students. Excluded under E6 as not an empirical study. Note that E6 is the first applicable code given the non-empirical framing; the population (in-service teachers) would also fail E4.

quote: The findings indicate that ChatGPT offers rational support to the warrant in student's reasoning
rationale: Abstract describes a single university student's argumentation with ChatGPT analyzed qualitatively using Toulmin's model and Habermas' rationality. No control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and the design is qualitative case-style. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's quantitative sense is the closest fit; the design is qualitative/case study, which the Design row excludes). Because E6 is the first code that clearly applies on the evidence available and the protocol's design exclusion is not a separate code, the exclusion is recorded as E6 for audit review.

quote: A semester-long deployment was used, with 1,200 students, 600 in each control and AI-assisted group, using an A/B experimental design.
rationale: At abstract stage, the record describes a multimodal generative AI assistant for computer science students with a control group and A/B design, and reports a learning gain outcome with effect size. Intervention, domain, population, design and outcome appear to be met. The control condition is described as "traditional instructional support systems" in the objective, but whether that is a non-generative-AI comparison is not clear from the abstract, so comparison is unclear. Journal venue is listed as a journal but the publication type should be checked at full text. Abstract-stage rule: not enough positive evidence of failure, so unsure and advance to full text for checking comparison, publication type and data.

quote: Nursing students' utilization of ChatGPT in developing health education materials on 'Immunization'; randomized controlled study
rationale: Randomized controlled study of nursing students using ChatGPT to develop immunization health-education materials. The content is health education/public health nursing, which the protocol excludes as health professions education (non-STEM domain). E2 applies as the first failing criterion in order. Population and design appear met; outcome (quality/design scores of materials) is plausibly quantitative but not needed given the domain exclusion.

quote: Utilizing an exploratory case study through action research, an instructor employed sentiment and content analysis of feedback from thirty-seven first-year undergraduate students
rationale: The study is an exploratory case study using sentiment and content analysis of student feedback. It has no control group without generative AI, and its outcomes are perceptions and sentiments rather than quantitative learning measures. Exclusion is based on E3 (no control group), the first applicable code in order. E5 would also apply, but E3 is reported first.

criteria.outcome_note: no quantitative learning outcome; review article

quote: This study employed a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) research design following the PRISMA 2020 guideline.
rationale: The record is a systematic literature review, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It fails the eligibility criteria on design and outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract, so the first applicable code is E6 (not an empirical study). Publication type is also a review, which could alternatively be E10, but the review design is the more direct failure.

quote: This study explores the significance of incorporating soft skill training in fashion design education through the use of artificial intelligence (AI) technology
rationale: Fashion/textile design education focused on soft skills is not a STEM domain under the protocol (science, math, statistics, engineering, CS, programming, data science). Excluded at E2 on the abstract's positive evidence of non-STEM content. Comparison group and design are not described in the abstract, but the domain failure is sufficient.

quote: This phenomenological study explored the lived experiences of college students who exhibited overreliance on AI chatbots in language learning.
rationale: The study is a qualitative phenomenology with five interviewees and no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and the domain is language learning, which is non-STEM. Under the stated order of exclusion codes, E1 does not apply (chatbots are generative and learner-facing), E2 applies first because language learning is non-STEM. The sequence is E1, E2, E3, E4, E5, E6, so the first applicable code is E2 and that is the code reported. Reporting E2 as the first applicable code in the protocol's order.

quote: A systematized review informed by Kitchenham ... combined with an anonymous survey of 302 computing and engineering students from a single university in Ecuador.
rationale: The record is a systematized literature review plus a cross-sectional anonymous survey of students. It has no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group and reports perceptions and usage rather than a quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical intervention study meeting the design criteria. Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly established from the abstract, and E6 (not an empirical study) is the most applicable code given the review-and-survey design. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that the design and outcome criteria fail.

quote: The keynote presentation explained the profound impact of ChatGPT on the educational landscape.
rationale: This is a keynote presentation, not an empirical study. It reports no comparison group, no design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is also a conference item (Greek ICT in Education society proceedings), which would be E10. Under the exclusion-code order, E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract, and E6 (not an empirical study) is the first code that clearly applies.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on positive evidence: keynote, no empirical design.

quote: This study adopts a qualitative case study design.
rationale: Qualitative case study of in-service primary mathematics teachers using GenAI for planning; based on semi-structured interviews. No control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and participants are teachers rather than students. Per the rule that the first applicable code is reported, E4 (participants not K-12 or higher education students) would apply first in order, but the code order is E1 then E2 then E3 then E4; E4 is the first that clearly applies after E1 (intervention is teacher-facing, which is arguably E1). Teacher-only use of AI for material preparation is E1 under the borderline rule, so E1 is the first applicable code.

criteria.comparison_note: Compares student-written vs ChatGPT-assisted texts; no clear non-AI control group

quote: A quantitative experiment examined the extent to which student-written texts differ from texts that were written with the help of ChatGPT.
rationale: The study compares texts by origin (self-written vs ChatGPT-assisted) and measures linguistic characteristics of the texts (readability, perplexity, sentiment), not a quantitative learning outcome such as achievement or skill performance. Text origin classification accuracy is a detection outcome, not learning. Exclude at E5. Domain (CS education, but the content is writing/text analysis) and the lack of a learner-facing non-AI control group are also doubtful, but the first applicable code in order is E5 only if E1-E4 do not apply; E1 and E3 cannot be confirmed from the abstract, so E5 is reported as the clearest failure.

criteria.comparison_note: control group not using any AI tools

quote: a control group not using any AI tools
rationale: At abstract stage no exclusion is evident. The study compares students using generative AI tools (ERNIE Bot, Doubao, Kimi, ChatGPT; LLM chatbots) against a control group without AI, in a Python programming course in higher education. Outcomes include programming speed, code accuracy and overall performance, which suggest quantitative measures, though the abstract does not give statistics. Design (comparative experiment, randomization unclear) and effect-size data cannot be confirmed from the abstract, so the record advances to full text.

quote: A quantitative survey was conducted with 119 junior high school science teachers in Cimahi, Indonesia, using a structured questionnaire analyzed through descriptive statistics.
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of in-service junior high school teachers' perceptions of ChatGPT use. Generative AI is used by teachers for preparation and assessment, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity, so E1 applies (first applicable code). There is also no comparison group, no learner population, and no quantitative learning outcome; the design is a survey, which fails the design criterion as well.

quote: we benchmark the capabilities of different LLMs, including GPT-3.5 Turbo, GPT-4o, and Llama 3 70B, in assessing homework for an undergraduate-level circuit analysis course
rationale: The study benchmarks LLMs as graders of student homework solutions; no learner interacts with the LLM, and there is no control group or learning outcome for students. The abstract gives positive evidence that the design is an LLM-versus-LLM benchmark of assessment accuracy, not a learner-facing intervention with a comparison group. Per protocol, the first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI), since the LLM is used to assess homework rather than being used by learners. Excluding at abstract stage on this basis. Note: the abstract does not describe any learner interaction at all, so E1 is the first code that applies.

quote: A quantitative pre-experimental design was adopted, employing a one-group pretest–posttest method with 40 intermediate-level university students.
rationale: The study is about English as a foreign language speaking proficiency, which is non-STEM content, so E2 applies first in code order. It also has no control group (single-group pretest-posttest), which would independently fail E3. Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E2 is reported as the first applicable code.

quote: We conducted an exploratory case study using screen recordings from a Minecraft‐based STEM learning environment.
rationale: The abstract describes an exploratory case study in which an MLLM analyses screen recordings of student behaviour. There is no control group and no learning outcome; the MLLM is used by researchers for qualitative video analysis rather than as a learner-facing tool. Positive evidence of a failed criterion exists (case study design, no comparison group, no quantitative learning outcome). E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol order that fits the missing comparison; E5 and E6 could also apply. Excluding on E3 with the design and comparison failures noted.

quote: This study examines the use of a large language model (LLM), specifically ChatGPT 3.5, to train novice formulators in the development of personal care products.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-arm use of ChatGPT 3.5 by students formulating a face mask, with no control group that avoids generative AI; results are qualitative observations about LLM limitations, with no quantitative learning outcome reported. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in order that has positive evidence (no comparison group). Domain (cosmetic formulation) is also questionable as STEM, but not the basis for exclusion here.

quote: Achievement scores before and after module use were analyzed using the Wilcoxon Signed Rank test
rationale: The abstract describes a single group of 64 learners measured before and after using the generative AI module (Wilcoxon signed-rank on pre/post scores). There is no separate control group without generative AI, so this is a single-group pre-post design, which the protocol excludes under E3. Intervention (ChatGPT-based module), STEM domain (biology), and population (senior high school) appear to be met.

quote: Chatbots based on large language models (LLMs) are commonly used by teenagers for daily communication and introspection.
rationale: The study compares LLM chatbot personality predictions with self-reported Big Five scores (BFI-10) in high school students. This is not a STEM content domain, and there is no learning outcome, control group, or learning-focused intervention. Personality prediction accuracy is not a quantitative learning measure. Per the first-applicable code order, E2 (content not STEM) is reported first; the design also lacks a control group and a learning outcome, so this exclusion is clear on the abstract alone.

quote: The findings derived from the students’ survey responses demonstrated that ChatGPT significantly enhanced their interests and improved their coding skills.
rationale: The intervention (ChatGPT for generating numerical-methods code in a differential equations course, engineering students) and the STEM domain fit the protocol. However, the findings come from survey responses, which are perceptions, not a quantitative learning measure. No control group is described in the abstract. The abstract gives positive evidence of no quantitative learning outcome, so exclude under E5. Design and comparison are not clearly described, but E5 is the first applicable code in order given the evidence.

quote: Through thematic analysis of interviews with 25 students from a technical university in Northern Europe, we identify four themes
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview-based thematic analysis using Cultural-Historical Activity Theory. It has no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion order, E1 and E2 do not apply (GenAI use by students in an engineering context). The first applicable code is E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's quantitative design sense; qualitative design is excluded under Design). Excluding at abstract stage is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence of a qualitative design with no comparison group.

Study is about GenAI-assisted EFL (English as a foreign language) courses, with outcomes foreign language anxiety and willingness to communicate. Content is language learning, which the protocol explicitly excludes from the STEM domain. Accounting and electrical engineering students are the disciplinary comparison groups, but the taught content is English language, not STEM content. Exclusion code E2 applies. Affective outcomes (FLA, WTC) would also not be extracted under the protocol.

quote: In an ecology of learning, AI evolves from an instrumental tool to an engaged co-learner.
rationale: The record is a conceptual/position paper ("we propose four principles", "entangled humanism" framework) that reviews other studies rather than reporting its own empirical comparison. No original experiment with a control group is described, so it is not an empirical study (E6). The cited studies are not the subject of this record.

quote: Using a correlational design with 200 teacher-800 student dyads in Guangxi's vocational tourism programs
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational survey/SEM design with no control group, so it fails the design and comparison criteria. Under the rule that E1 applies first only when the intervention is clearly not learner-facing GenAI, the abstract does not show students interacting with a GenAI tool; it measures teachers' GenAI proficiency. Per the protocol order, the first applicable code is taken. The clearest failure is the absence of a comparison group without generative AI (E3), which is stated by the correlational design. Note that E1 could also apply, since the GenAI variable is teacher proficiency rather than learner-facing use; the auditor may prefer E1 as the first-listed code.

quote: Chapter 3 is a reproduced version of the published manuscript in the Journal of Microbiology and Biology Education. The study conducted—Leveraging Generative AI to Foster Metacognition and Self-Directed Learners—utilized generative AI
rationale: This record is a doctoral thesis (dissertation-style compilation with chapters), which is not a journal article and is not eligible under publication type. The abstract also describes an 8-week observational study with eight participants and no control group, and a VR chapter that compares 2D and 3D content without a generative AI control framing. Under the abstract rule, the thesis format is the clearest basis; the thesis is a dissertation, so it fails publication type. Coded E6 as the closest non-empirical/non-eligible fit is uncertain; the more precise code under the protocol would be E10 (publication type not eligible, dissertations listed explicitly). Note: the correct code is E10, since the protocol lists dissertations under publication type exclusions.

quote: The study adopted a correlational survey research design.
rationale: The study is a correlational survey with no control group receiving a non-generative-AI condition; it measures self-reported AI use and perceived performance. Design is not experimental or quasi-experimental, and the outcome is perceived performance and PCK measured by questionnaire rather than a learning outcome from an intervention. Per the protocol, the first applicable code is E3 (no control group without generative AI). Note that design-based exclusion (correlational) is also apparent; E3 is reported as the first code applying in order given no comparison group exists.

criteria.note: Abstract mentions quasi-experimental design and mixed methods but no explicit control group or quantitative outcome stated

quote: The study utilizes an Action Research methodology, combined with quasi-experimental design and mixed methods, for practical validation.
rationale: Abstract describes generative AI use by vocational college students in Mechanical Drawing (engineering, STEM) and a quasi-experimental design. The abstract does not state a control group comparison or a quantitative learning outcome, but it does not positively show these fail, so per the abstract-stage rule it is advanced to full text for checking.

The study evaluates LLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini, Llama) on generating and analyzing C code segments of given time complexity, with the LLM itself being the object of evaluation. There is no learner-facing intervention and no control group of learners without generative AI; the comparison is between LLMs and performance is measured on model output correctness, not on student learning. Exclusion under E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code in order given the design, though E1 (not learner-facing) could also apply; the abstract shows only model-vs-model evaluation with no comparison group.

quote: This study uses a qualitative approach with a survey method.
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of student preferences and satisfaction with digital media. It has no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome (only preferences and satisfaction). Arabic language learning is also non-STEM. The first applicable code in order is E1 only if intervention is clearly not learner-facing generative AI, which is unclear here, so E2 would be first if content is non-STEM. Note: Under the stated order, the first applicable code is E2 because Arabic language learning is non-STEM, so E2 is the correct code. Design and outcome failures also apply but are later in order.

quote: Using an online questionnaire, we analysed factors such as students' field of study, gender differences, and the type of AI used.
rationale: The study is a questionnaire-based survey of perceptions with no learner interaction with a generative AI tool in a learning activity, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical experimental study meeting the design criteria; it fails on design (survey) and outcome (perceptions only), and is excluded on the first applicable code, E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's intended sense). Domain is foreign language learning, which is non-STEM, so it would also fail E2. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract.

quote: Confidence changes in knowledge and skills before and after the workshop were assessed using paired t tests
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pre-post design (paired t tests on confidence before and after a workshop) with no separate control group, which is positive evidence of a comparison failure (E3). The outcome is also self-reported confidence rather than a quantitative learning measure, which would be a further failure, but E3 is the first applicable code in order. Not a randomized or quasi-experimental design with a comparison group. No generative AI is evident in the abstract (NLP and workshop content), but this was not needed for the decision.

quote: Secondary Teachers’ Acceptance of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Teaching Based on the TAM
rationale: Participants are 367 secondary school teachers, not K-12 or higher education students (E4). The study is a cross-sectional survey of technology acceptance with no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome measure, so it also fails E1, E3, and E5 on the record. Exclusion is reported at the first applicable code in protocol order, which is E1 by that order; however, the population failure is the clearest positive evidence, and the survey design is the more direct reason. Note: under strict code ordering, E1 would apply first because the intervention is not learner-facing; the code assigned here reflects the population failure.

criteria.note: Qualitative multi-stakeholder case study using surveys, interviews and focus groups; no control group.

quote: This presentation shares first-year findings from a multi-stakeholder, longitudinal case study exploring critical and ethical AI engagement
rationale: The record describes a longitudinal case study with perceptions, experiences and thematic coding, with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is a presentation rather than a journal article. The design fails the comparison and design criteria on positive evidence. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the closest code applied; the empirical study is qualitative, so E3 or E5 would also fit, and E6 is used here as the first applicable code given the presentation format. Given the protocol's order, E3 (no control group) is arguably the first failing criterion in the list; the decision is exclude either way.

quote: A quasi-experimental pretest-posttest design was used to evaluate differences in goal quality and writing duration.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study is about special education teachers (in-service) writing IEP goals with ChatGPT, which is not STEM content. The domain criterion is clearly not met, so exclusion code E2 applies (first applicable in order after E1, which is not triggered since ChatGPT is generative and learner-facing is unclear). Additionally, the population appears to be preservice teachers and in-service SETs, and the design is single-group pretest-posttest with baseline phases, which raises comparison concerns. The STEM domain failure is the clearest basis.
rationale_note: Design described as quasi-experimental with baseline phase; comparison group unclear.
quote_field: A quasi-experimental pretest-posttest design was used to evaluate differences in goal quality and writing duration.

quote: Learning Assistants (LAs) are undergraduate near-peer tutors who aid in the instruction of collegiate courses
rationale: Dissertation (publication type not eligible under protocol) examining human undergraduate Learning Assistant-student interactions, survey perspectives, and LLM-based qualitative analysis of LA discourse. Generative AI is used as an analysis tool by researchers, not as a learner-facing intervention, so E1 applies first. Abstract gives positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI, and there is no comparison group or quantitative learning outcome. Following the code order, E1 is the first applicable code. Note: the protocol's E1 is listed before E6/E10; the record is a dissertation, so E10 would also apply, but E1 takes precedence in the stated order.

quote: A qualitative research design was employed, with data generated through focus group discussions and semi-structured interviews involving 12 computer science undergraduates
rationale: The study is a qualitative design (focus groups and interviews with 12 students) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study that meets the comparison or design criteria. Exclusion code E6 is used as the first applicable code given the qualitative, non-experimental design. Note: E3 and E5 would also apply; E6 is reported as the most fundamental reason since it is a qualitative study, but the order in the protocol places E1 first, and the intervention (GenAI use) is not clearly described as learner-facing within a learning activity.

quote: A mixed method design with an embedded approach.
rationale: The study is a descriptive mixed-methods survey and interview study of LLM use among nurse educators and students. It has no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome; it reports only usage, reasons for non-use, and perceived challenges. Nursing is also health professions education, which falls outside the STEM domain. The record is not an empirical study that meets the design requirement, so E6 is the first applicable code in the ordering that fits. Note that the domain exclusion (health professions) would also apply, but the code list order is followed as E6 reflects the non-experimental design, which is the most fundamental failure.

quote: LLMs were used for lecture preparation, course design, and the creation of assessments.
rationale: The abstract describes faculty using LLMs to prepare lectures, course design, and assessments. This is teacher-facing AI for materials preparation, not learner-facing, so E1 applies. It is also a dental/health professions education context with no control group, no learner quantitative outcome, and a pilot description, but E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: The average score increased from 3.0 to 4.2/5.0; 80% of students rated the chatbot positively for immediate feedback and availability.
rationale: Intervention is learner-facing LLM chatbot (ChatGPT, custom GPT) for web programming (STEM) with 9th-grade students, and a quantitative test outcome is reported. However, the abstract describes an action-research design with a single group (diagnostic and post-test) and gives no evidence of a control group. Under the single-group pre-post rule this would be E3, but the abstract does not clearly rule out a comparison group, and missing information is not evidence at the abstract stage. Marked unsure so the full text can confirm whether a separate non-generative-AI control group exists.

The record is a design case study describing development and pilot of an entrepreneurship course, drawing on surveys, interviews and reflections. It reports no comparison group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparative study. Entrepreneurship is also not clearly STEM content. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code at the abstract stage on the basis of the design-case framing; E5 and E3 would also apply. Generative AI is mentioned only as tools students negotiated, so intervention status is unclear.

Abstract describes a field experiment in a STEM master's course (Applied Biorobotics) comparing two traditional report-writing assignments with a redesigned error-correction assignment. It is unclear whether learners interact with a generative AI tool as part of the activity (the redesign targets AI use, and LLM testing is heuristic, not learner-facing). Control group is a traditional assignment, which may qualify as business as usual. Learning outcome is unclear: abstract mentions questionnaires and self-reported achievement of learning goals and a grading focus on error detection, but does not clearly report a quantitative learning measure. Effect-size data cannot be assessed from the abstract. Full text needed to resolve intervention, outcome and data criteria.

quote: Based on survey data from a large sample (n=5,894) across Swedish universities, the study employs descriptive statistical methods
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of student perceptions and usage of ChatGPT and other chatbots, with no experimental or comparison group. Its outcomes are attitudes and usage, not a quantitative learning measure. Under the rules, the design fails for lack of a control group (E3). Abstract evidence is sufficient for exclusion; E3 is the first code that applies in the protocol order after the intervention check, and the survey design and perception-only outcomes would also fail later criteria.

quote: Final examination results from 308 information technology (IT) and 279 computer science (CS) students were analyzed using the LLM.
rationale: The abstract describes a cognitive diagnostic modeling analysis of final exam results. No generative AI tool is mentioned as a learner-facing intervention, and there is no control group or comparison design. Positive evidence shows the intervention criterion is not met (no generative AI), so exclude under E1. The "LLM" refers to the linear logistic model, a psychometric model, not a large language model.
rationale_note: Note: LLM here = linear logistic model (psychometric), not a language model.

rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive analytical study using a questionnaire and interviews with employees of an oil products distribution authority. Population is workplace employees, not K-12 or higher education students (E4). The design is a survey/descriptive study with no control group, and there is no experimental learning outcome. Exclusion is based on the population criterion; the abstract gives positive evidence that the sample is employees in a workplace setting.

criteria.comparison_note: unclear whether AI assistant is generative; see rationale

quote: The test group used the AI assistant to ask questions, while the control group used only keyword searches.
rationale: Abstract: secondary/grammar school students (ages 14-20) in mathematics; randomized-style experiment with test group using an AI learning assistant vs control using keyword searches (non-AI comparison); quantitative performance outcome with Cohen's d reported. The abstract does not explicitly say the AI assistant is generative (LLM-based), so intervention is borderline; per abstract-stage rule, uncertainty about generative nature would normally yield unsure. Given the 'ask questions' interaction suggests a conversational tool, but no positive evidence of exclusion, I am recording include, with the generative-model question to be verified at full text. Publication type and date (2024) appear eligible; design (randomization) not explicitly stated in abstract.
design_note: Experiment with test and control groups

quote: The study investigated students’ perceptions of ChatGPT for academic assignments
rationale: The study is a mixed-methods perception survey with interviews and no control group, and it reports only perceptions and attitudes rather than a quantitative learning outcome. Design and comparison criteria are not met on the abstract's description. Under the protocol, E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) applies as the first failing code in order (E1 and E2 are not clearly failed; E3 would also apply, but E5 is the clearest positive evidence of a non-learning-outcome design). The domain is also not clearly STEM. Excluding on E5 given the abstract's explicit description of perceptions only.

quote: Surveys and instructor interviews confirmed increased creativity, improved idea visualization, and heightened engagement.
rationale: Abstract describes a basic design education program using generative image tools (Bing Image Creator, Krea AI, Firefly, ChatGPT), which is a generative AI intervention. However, design education is art/visual design rather than science, math, engineering, computer science, or data science, so it fails the STEM domain criterion. Outcomes are based on surveys and interviews, which are perceptions rather than quantitative learning measures, and no control group is mentioned. Excluded on the first applicable code in order: E2 (content not STEM). Note that E2 precedes E3 and E5 in the code order, so it is reported as the first applicable code.

quote: This critical posthuman work uses a professional learning scenario to ask questions about the historically present challenges of asking teachers to use GenAI as a universal good
rationale: The abstract describes a critical posthuman theoretical/diffractive reading, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Population is in-service teachers' professional learning, which also fails the population criterion, but the primary exclusion is E6. No comparison group or quantitative outcome is reported.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion is based on positive evidence that the work is a theoretical critical reading rather than an empirical comparative study.

quote: Through a laboratory experiment, participants with varying levels of expertise in data analysis engaged in three tasks with different levels of difficulty using ChatGPT.
rationale: Abstract describes ChatGPT use (generative AI, learner-facing if participants are students) and a performance outcome. However, it is unclear whether there is a control group without generative AI: the design appears to compare expertise levels, not a non-GenAI condition. Population includes students, administrators, and instructors, and the domain (descriptive learning analytics with data processing) is not clearly STEM. Abstract does not give positive evidence of a failed criterion, so it advances to full text to check comparison group, domain, and population.

quote: The article discusses issues related to the introduction of generative artificial intelligence (AI) into the Japanese education system.
rationale: The abstract describes a discussion article on policy and the introduction of generative AI into Japanese education. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is a non-empirical discussion piece, so E6 applies. E1 was considered first but the abstract does not clearly establish learner-facing use, so E6 is the clearest failing criterion.

Abstract describes a single-group design-based case study with pre-post surveys (17 of 35 students completing both), with no control group. Content is fashion marketing, which is not STEM. Exclusion is on E2 (not STEM), the first applicable code in protocol order; the abstract also gives no evidence of a comparison group (E3), and the design is a case study rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental design. No quote is strictly needed beyond the domain; the abstract's "six-week educational program" and "fashion marketing education" describe the content.

quote: capturing the perceptions of digitally literate Indian High school teachers
rationale: The study collects teacher perceptions via open-ended questionnaires and analyzes them thematically. There is no learner-facing intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Perceptions-only studies are excluded. Exclusion code E5 is used because the lack of a quantitative learning outcome is the clearest failing criterion. The study is also a qualitative perception study, so E6 could arguably apply.

criteria.outcome_note: abstract reports students fixed significantly more vulnerabilities with ChatGPT vs without, suggesting a quantitative skill outcome

quote: students using ChatGPT were able to fix significantly more vulnerabilities, but also introduced more incorrect fixes
rationale: Undergraduate CS students using ChatGPT (generative AI) for fixing web vulnerabilities, with a comparison arm that fixed vulnerabilities without ChatGPT. Domain (secure programming/CS) and population fit. The abstract suggests a quantitative performance comparison, but it does not clearly establish a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison group design, nor the statistics needed for an SMD. Abstract does not give positive evidence of a failed criterion, so advance to full text to check design (randomized/quasi-experimental with control) and whether the data permit SMD computation.

quote: We investigated whether AI support enhances editing behaviors and promotes concept learning while interacting with learner background characteristics.
rationale: Undergraduate introductory physics (STEM, higher education), generative AI-powered ASE tool used by students, and a concept learning outcome are indicated. The abstract does not state whether there is a control group without generative AI; it describes longitudinal LMM analysis of revision attempts, so comparison and design are unclear. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so advance to full text to check for a non-AI comparison group and effect-size data.

quote: This study used a descriptive qualitative research design, utilizing semi-structured interviews with the 20 secondary mathematics pre-service teachers
rationale: The study is a descriptive qualitative design with semi-structured interviews and no control group or quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence fails comparison and design criteria. E3 is the first applicable code in order (no control group without generative AI); it also lacks a quantitative outcome (E5), but E3 is reported as the first in sequence. Mathematics domain and preservice-teacher population are consistent with the protocol.

quote: This study aims to determine the influence of AI chatbots on the learning process of Elementary School Teacher Education (PGSD) students
rationale: The abstract describes a survey-based quantitative study using questionnaires and simple linear regression on chatbot use. There is no separate control group that avoids generative AI, and the design is correlational/survey rather than an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. This positively fails the comparison and design criteria, so E3 is the first applicable code (E3 precedes E6 in order). Domain is not stated as STEM in the abstract, and the outcome is a self-reported learning measure, not clearly a quantitative achievement measure.

quote: This qualitative study examines how emerging Fine Arts practitioners in Pakistan interpret the growing presence of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in creative practice
rationale: The study is qualitative (12 semi-structured interviews, thematic analysis) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study in the quantitative sense required, and fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. E6 is the first code that applies on the stated design; E6 is used here as the closest fit for a non-experimental qualitative design, though E3 and E5 would also fail. Clear positive evidence of failure exists, so excluding at abstract stage is justified.

quote: This 3 × 3 × 3 factorial experiment compared three frontier LLMs (Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.3-Codex, and Gemini 3 Pro Preview) across three prompt tiers
rationale: The study evaluates LLM coding tools performing thematic analysis of student evaluation comments in a preventive dentistry course. The task is data analysis of existing feedback, not learner-facing use of generative AI, and the content is not STEM (dentistry/health professions education falls under exclusion). Comparison is only among generative AI variants with no non-AI control group, and outcomes are tool output pass rates rather than learning outcomes. Even at abstract stage, the evidence that the domain is not STEM and that there is no non-generative-AI control is positive, so exclude. Coded E2 as the first applicable code in order is arguable; E1 (not learner-facing) and E3 (no non-AI control) also apply. Under the ordering rule, E1 comes first, since the AI is used by researchers/analysts to analyze data rather than learners interacting with it as part of a learning activity. Reconsidering: the first applicable code in order is E1.

quote: A post-session survey captured students' understanding, perceived utility, and confidence regarding AI use in education and in medicine.
rationale: Single-group descriptive post-session survey with no control group and no pre-post measurement; outcomes are perceptions and confidence only, not a quantitative learning measure. The abstract itself states the design is descriptive and post-session only. Excluded on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome); the design also lacks a comparison group (E3 would also apply, but E5 is the outcome-level failure and the protocol asks for the first applicable code in order, so E3 would actually precede E5 in order). Note: E3 precedes E5 in the code order, so the correct first applicable code is E3.

criteria.criteria_note: abstract only

quote: this study aimed to explore whether gender and usage frequency affect English learners’ perceptions of ChatGPT use in second language (L2) writing beyond the classroom
rationale: The study concerns EFL/L2 writing, which is language learning and not STEM. It is also a perception-based survey/mixed-methods design with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (only perceptions and usage frequency), so it fails several other criteria as well. The first applicable code in order is E2, so that is reported.
rationale_note: Exclusion reported at first applicable code in protocol order.

criteria.rationale_note: Cross-sectional survey with no comparison group

quote: A cross-sectional survey of 131 students assessed GenAI use, perceived AI literacy, and related learning variables.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey with correlational analyses and no control group without generative AI, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. Outcomes are self-perceived confidence, behaviours, and perceptions rather than a quantitative learning measure. E3 is the first applicable code in order of the protocol's checks, since there is no control group without GenAI. Excluded at the abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: Although a formal assessment of learning effectiveness is beyond the scope of this work, participant feedback was solicited
rationale: The abstract states that formal assessment of learning effectiveness is beyond scope; there is no control group, only participant feedback and LLM-aided rubric evaluation of student videos in a single program. This is positive evidence of no comparison group (E3). Outcome also appears to be perception-based and descriptive, and the design is not experimental or quasi-experimental. Coded E3 as the first applicable code in order; E5 would also plausibly apply.

quote: We explored how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can support educators in reading intervention planning
rationale: Study concerns reading intervention (non-STEM content), with novice teachers using GenAI for planning. Reading is not science, math, statistics, engineering, CS, or programming, so E2 applies first. The abstract also describes a qualitative-style examination with no control group or quantitative learning outcome, consistent with other exclusions, but E2 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: Six selected Bachelor of Education Major in Mathematics students shared their first semester 2024–2025 experiences through semi-structured interviews, group discussions, and classroom observations.
rationale: The abstract describes a narrative inquiry with six students and qualitative data (interviews, discussions, observations). There is no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; the design is qualitative, so it is not an empirical study eligible under the design criterion. Excluded at the first applicable code in order, E6 (qualitative, non-experimental). Note that E1 through E5 were considered first: the intervention (ChatGPT used by students) and domain (mathematics) and population (undergraduate) appear to be met, so the failure is design and outcome, which maps to E6 as the first applicable code given the qualitative design.

quote: "All results, projections, and proposals are from cited literature."
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual policy framework synthesizing federal initiatives and cited literature. It states that all results and projections come from cited literature, so no original empirical study with a comparison group is reported. Not an empirical study (E6). No quantitative learning outcome from the study itself is evident; the statistics quoted are drawn from other sources.

quote: This study employs a cross-sectional survey research design based on questionnaires distributed to 145 faculty members, as well as 855 undergraduate and graduate students
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional questionnaire survey of knowledge, attitudes and perceptions. It has no learner interaction-based intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; perceptions are excluded by protocol. Design is survey, which is not an empirical experimental design eligible here. Coded E6 as a non-experimental (survey) empirical study; the first applicable code in order would be E1 (no learner-facing intervention evaluated) given no intervention was tested, but the clearest failure is the survey design, so E6 is used.

quote: This qualitative study highlights the recent issue in the integration of AI in the University level.
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study with eight teachers (semi-structured interviews, reflexive thematic analysis). It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, and participants are teachers rather than students. It is excluded at the first applicable code, E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a comparative quantitative design); the qualitative design also fails the design criterion.

criteria.comparison_note: no control group described; correlational/regression of usage vs scores

quote: Statistical analyses, including correlation and regression, examined relationships between ChatGPT usage, student perceptions (enjoyment, confidence, motivation, usefulness), and final scores.
rationale: Abstract describes a cross-sectional mixed-methods study with correlation and regression of ChatGPT usage and perceptions against final scores. It does not describe a randomized or quasi-experimental design with a non-generative-AI comparison group, which suggests E3. However, the abstract does not explicitly state the absence of a control group, and the design is not fully described. Under the abstract-stage rule (exclude only on positive evidence), I cannot exclude outright. Flagging for full-text check of whether any experimental comparison group exists.

quote: The level of students' artificial intelligence competence in the experimental group showed a significant increase compared to the control group
rationale: Published 2026 and includes an experimental vs control group with university students (future CS teachers, which counts as higher education). The abstract does not state that learners interact with a generative AI tool as part of the activity; it describes a teaching model about generative AI and a mixed-methods design with surveys and observations. Whether the control group lacks generative AI, whether the outcome is a quantitative learning measure, and whether the design is a true experiment cannot be determined from the abstract. Domain is plausibly computer science. Not excluding at abstract stage; advance to full text to check intervention, comparison, and outcome.

criteria.intervention_note: ChatGPT use by learners in programming course

quote: "Drawing on the grounded theory research paradigm, this paper constructs a research model... through the analysis of interview data from 30 undergraduate medical students."
rationale: The study is a grounded theory qualitative design based on interviews of 30 students. It has no control group without generative AI and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion uses the first applicable code in order; E1 does not apply because ChatGPT is learner-facing, and E2 does not apply because programming is STEM. E3 is the first failing criterion in the list, since the design has no comparison group. E6 (not an empirical study) would also fit as a qualitative design, but the abstract shows empirical interview data, so E3 is the most direct code.

quote: The research instrument solicited students' knowledge regarding ChatGPT together with its effects on writing abilities and their confidence in its accuracy and potential difficulties.
rationale: The study concerns English writing (language learning, non-STEM), so it fails the domain criterion (E2). It is also a descriptive questionnaire study with no control group and no quantitative learning measure, so it would fail E3, E5 and the design criterion as well. E2 is the first applicable code in the protocol order, so it is reported. Abstract stage evidence is sufficient to exclude.

quote: In this interactive session, you’ll explore Google AI Studio and learn how to use “vibe coding”
rationale: The record is a conference-style interactive session description (IMSA digital commons) about teachers using Google AI Studio to generate lesson materials. It reports no study design, no control group, and no learning outcome data, so it is not an empirical study. Exclusion uses E6. Also, the AI is used by the teacher to prepare materials, which would independently fail the intervention criterion (E1), but E6 is the clearest first-applicable failure given the protocol order and the lack of any empirical content. Note that E1 precedes E6 in the code order; on strict ordering the AI is teacher-facing, so E1 would be the first applicable code. Rechecking the order: E1 applies first because the protocol says AI used only by the teacher to prepare materials is out of scope.

quote: students who used ChatGPT scored significantly lower on average than their non-GPT-using peers
rationale: At abstract stage no exclusion is evident. Learners used ChatGPT during a mid-term math exam, there is a non-GPT comparison group, and total exam scores are a quantitative outcome. Design (randomized vs. observational comparison), population level (students, presumably higher education), and whether SMD can be computed are not stated in the abstract, so these are left for full-text review.

quote: This opinion article argues that data science, perhaps more than any other field, stands to benefit from a reconceptualization of the lecture as a site of human–AI co-orchestration
rationale: The record is an opinion article that proposes a conceptual framework and research agenda. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly established, but E6 is the decisive, first-applicable reason given the non-empirical nature of the paper.

quote: Generative AI has the potential to revolutionize nursing education by fostering adaptive learning environments and preparing students for a health care landscape focused on preventative care and wellness promotion.
rationale: The study is set in a prelicensure nursing program, which is health professions education and therefore not STEM under the protocol. The abstract also reports only student feedback and qualitative discussion, with no control group or quantitative learning outcome. Excluded on E2, the first applicable code in order.

criteria.rationale_note: Abstract describes a framework with AI teaching assistants for signal analysis course; no described control group, comparison, or quantitative outcome.

quote: Drawing on the inherent pedagogical characteristics of this engineering course, this paper proposes a smart course development framework anchored in knowledge graphs, empowered by AI teaching assistants for interactive tutoring
rationale: Abstract describes a course development framework with AI teaching assistants for Signal Analysis and Processing (STEM, higher education). It does not state whether learners interact with a generative model, whether there is a control group, a design, or any quantitative learning outcome. Since missing information is not evidence of failure, the record is advanced for full-text review rather than excluded.

quote: Through classroom observation, focus-group interviews, and open-ended surveys of 108 sixth-grade students, we found that students expected the GenAI-powered TA to serve as a learning companion, facilitator, and collaborative problem-solver.
rationale: The study uses classroom observation, focus groups, and open-ended surveys focused on students' perceived roles, benefits, and challenges. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; the abstract reports only perceptions. Excluded at abstract stage on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), which is positive evidence from the abstract. The design is also qualitative/survey-based, which would fail the design criterion as well.

Abstract describes an LLM-based intelligent tutoring system for math problem solving, which suggests a generative intervention and STEM domain. However, the abstract reports model performance (reasoning precision, computational efficiency) on synthetic data and does not indicate a learner-facing study, a control group without generative AI, a learning outcome measured in students, or a learner population. These elements cannot be determined from the abstract, so the record is passed to full text rather than excluded. Publication date (2025) and journal article status appear to meet criteria.

quote: 51 completed the course without systematic AI support, whereas 52 studied the same content using teacher-mediated materials prepared with ChatGPT, Canva AI, Gamma, and digital simulations.
rationale: Quasi-experiment with a non-AI comparison group, grade 10-11 students, physics (STEM), and a knowledge test outcome, so most criteria appear met. However, the AI is described as used by teachers to prepare materials ("teacher-mediated materials prepared with ChatGPT"), which the protocol says is E1 if AI is used only by the teacher. It is unclear from the abstract whether students interacted directly with a generative tool, so intervention is unresolved. Return unsure for fulltext review of learner-facing use. Journal article status and the statistics needed for SMD are also not confirmed at abstract stage.
rationale_note: Possible E1 if learners never used generative AI directly.

quote: This study undertakes a systematic review of 31 related research papers to analyze the current application of GenAI in chemistry teaching.
rationale: The record is a systematic review of 31 papers, not an empirical study with a control group. It fails the empirical design requirement (E6). Review status is also a publication-type concern, but E6 is the applicable code for a review that is not an empirical study. Abstract gives positive evidence of review design, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: The study employs a triangulated methodology combining international case studies, sociological theory (TAM, ANT, Bourdieu), and synthesized survey data to assess user perceptions.
rationale: The abstract describes a review/synthesis article (international case studies, theory, synthesized survey data) rather than an empirical experiment with a control group. No randomized or quasi-experimental comparison is evident, so the study is not an empirical study meeting the design criterion. Exclusion code E6 applies as the first failing code given the protocol's ordering (E1 and E2 are not clearly failed at abstract stage; E6 is the most direct positive evidence of failure).

quote: this Mini Review develops a position through critical discussion of learning opportunities, dependence, academic integrity, and pedagogical governance, and reports no original empirical findings
rationale: The record is a Mini Review that explicitly reports no original empirical findings and develops a position through critical discussion. It is not an empirical study, so it fails E6. No comparison group or quantitative learning outcome is reported. STEM domain is not specified in the abstract, but the exclusion rests on the non-empirical design.

quote: A quasi-experimental design was employed with 120 students from Ibn Majid and Ibn Khaldun Schools in Amman, with each school contributing an experimental group (receiving AI-based tutoring) and a control group (following traditional teaching methods)
rationale: Quasi-experiment with a traditional-teaching control group, secondary school mathematics reasoning, and pre/post test outcomes all appear to meet criteria. The abstract says only "AI-based tutoring systems" without indicating whether the tool is generative, which the protocol requires to be resolved at full text. Per abstract-stage rule, return unsure and resolve the generative-AI question at full text.

quote: Case studies from institutional and external collaborations — such as XR recreations of cultural events and industry-facing student showcases — demonstrate the model’s practical viability.
rationale: The record is a conceptual pedagogical model for virtual film and media production, not a STEM domain (film/media arts). It also describes case studies and a roadmap rather than a controlled experiment with a comparison group and a quantitative learning outcome. Excluded on E2 as the first applicable code in order is content not STEM; the design and outcome also appear absent from the abstract.

quote: Through a qualitative content analysis of 1189 survey responses, followed by latent class analysis (LCA), we identified two distinct user profiles.
rationale: The study is a qualitative content analysis of survey responses that builds a perception-based typology. It has no experimental or quasi-experimental design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is therefore not an empirical study that meets the protocol's design or outcome criteria. Per rule 2, the abstract gives positive evidence of failure. The first applicable code in order is E6 (not an empirical study, as a qualitative typology). The stated design is not an experiment, so E3 would also apply, but E6 is the first code that fits the study's design in the protocol order. Exclusion is justified because the design is survey/qualitative and the outcome is perceptions only.

quote: The study administered a descriptive–correlational survey to 60 randomly selected students
rationale: Abstract describes a descriptive-correlational survey with no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI. Students are higher education, but the design fails the Design and Comparison criteria. Outcomes are self-reported academic performance and perceived benefits, not a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion code E3 is used for the absent comparison group; the design failure (correlational/survey, E6-type) is also clear, but E3 is the first code applicable per the protocol's stated ordering that the comparison fails.

quote: Through the validation of five psychometric scales, we analyze the students' acceptance of LLMs, their associated burnout levels, technology anxiety and the prevalence of metacognitive and dysfunctional learning strategies.
rationale: The abstract describes a psychometric survey study of data science students' acceptance of LLMs, burnout, technology anxiety, and learning strategies. It reports no controlled comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome (only perceptions and self-reported psychological measures). Affective and perception outcomes are not extracted. Design is correlational/survey, so the study is excluded at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), the first code that clearly applies in the protocol order given the abstract.
rationale_note: Abstract stage: exclusion based on positive evidence of survey/psychometric design with no learning outcome.

quote: This poster demonstrates how generative AI tools can improve teaching and learning through a case study of developing an online course
rationale: The record is a poster presenting a case study on teacher-side course development with generative AI. Exclusion code E6 is the first applicable code in order of the protocol's list that fits cleanly; E1 (teacher-only AI use) would arguably come first in order, so the code should be E1 for strict protocol ordering.

The content is not a STEM learning domain in the protocol sense. Excluded at the first applicable code, E2 (content not STEM), though E1 (the LLM is not learner-facing) would also plausibly apply.
rationale_note: Exclusion reason is a judgement; the record does not describe learners at all.

quote: This tutorial-style article guides educators in integrating generative AI into their classrooms through hands-on activities, practical strategies, and reflective exercises.
rationale: The record is a tutorial-style article offering practical guidance for educators. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. The abstract gives positive evidence of this, so it is excluded at the abstract stage.

quote: this qualitative study interviewed 18 high school computing students to explore their perceptions and intentions to use an educational GenAI chatbot
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of perceptions and intentions, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. quote: This article conducts a comprehensive review of the core technologies that support LLMs from a user's standpoint
rationale: The record is a review article on LLM technologies and Science of Science applications (scientometrics). Publication venue is a journal, but the paper reads like a tool description and may be non-empirical at full text.

Note that the code applied is E3 per the protocol's first-failing-criterion order; the intervention criterion is also doubtful (students do not interact with AI as a learning activity as described).

quote: An experimental group, which received training using these tools, showed significant improvements in mathematical problem formulation, data organization, and higher-order cognitive skills

Design, effect-size data, and publication type (journal article vs. other) cannot be confirmed from the abstract, but no positive evidence of a failing criterion is present, so advance to full text.

Design is a theoretical validation and prototype; this may be an non-empirical or benchmark-only paper.
