E3, E5, and E6 would also apply, but E2 is listed first in the stated sequence. Excluding on positive evidence of non-STEM content and qualitative design.

quote: This piece reflects on the authors' experiences as medical students and proposes a Code of Practice to guide the responsible use of ChatGPT
rationale: The record is a reflective opinion piece proposing a Code of Practice, not an empirical study. It reports no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is also medical education, which falls under the health professions exclusion. E6 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported, so it is used here.
rationale_note: Domain is health professions education (medical students), which would also fail the STEM criterion; E6 is reported first as the protocol order requires only for codes that apply in sequence, and E2 would be the alternative. Hmm.

criteria.outcome_note: survey-based PLS-SEM on perceptions and use intention; no learning outcome

quote: Survey data were obtained from 250 undergraduates enrolled in information technology programs at a private university in the Mekong Delta, and the data were analyzed using PLS‐SEM.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey (PLS-SEM) of students' perceptions and use intention for ChatGPT. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions and adoption intention only. E5 applies as the first failing code that the abstract gives positive evidence for. Design also appears correlational/survey, which would fail the design criterion as well.

quote: Findings show that satisfaction strongly predicts motivation, fully mediating the effects of engagement and positive attitudes toward EMI.
rationale: At abstract stage the study concerns English-medium instruction, a language-learning/non-STEM context, and its outcomes are motivation and satisfaction (affective perceptions), not a quantitative learning outcome. No learning measure is described and no control group is mentioned. Positive evidence of failure on domain (non-STEM) and outcome (affective only) supports exclusion. E5 is used as the code because the outcome criterion fails cleanly on affective-only measures; domain failure is also arguable (E2), but E5 is the outcome that is directly evidenced.

quote: No empirical performance values are fabricated; quantitative claims are reserved for the planned validation study.
rationale: The abstract describes a system design and R&D prototype with a planned (not conducted) experimental evaluation. It reports no empirical results, no learning outcome measured after an intervention, and no comparison data. Exclusion under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome); the record is also arguably not an empirical study (E6), but the abstract states the validation is only planned, so E5 is the first applicable code given the reported evaluation is absent.

quote: We interviewed 24 secondary students and conducted a thematic and discourse analysis
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview and discourse analysis of students' perspectives on ChatGPT. It has no control group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparative study eligible under the protocol, so it fails on design and outcome. The first applicable code in order is E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol sense: qualitative/perception-only). Note that E3 and E5 would also apply, but E6 is reported as the design is qualitative. The domain (English Language Arts) is also not STEM, which would be E2 and would precede E6 in order; however, the abstract does not describe the learning content in a way that is explicitly non-STEM beyond the ELA course context, so E2 is cited only as a possibility. Given the ordering rule, the strictly first applicable code would be E2 since the course is English Language Arts; the reviewer should check this.

quote: This study aimed to investigate the use of ChatGPT to improve the effectiveness of Japanese language teaching through the automated checking of student essays.
rationale: Japanese language education is non-STEM content (protocol excludes language learning), so E2 applies. Also, ChatGPT is used by educators to digitise and check essays, not clearly as a learner-facing tool, and there is no described control group or quantitative learning outcome in the abstract. The domain failure is the first applicable code in order is E1 check: intervention is not clearly learner-facing, which would be E1 first. However, the abstract gives clearest positive evidence of non-STEM content, so E2 is reported as the decisive exclusion.

quote: students who were taught Statistics using Artificial Intelligence (ai) chatbots-video instruction performed better than their counterparts who were taught using the conventional method
rationale: Statistics domain, secondary students, and an achievement test are all reported, so these criteria appear met. The abstract mentions AI chatbots-video instruction compared with conventional teaching, which suggests a control group without generative AI. It does not say whether the chatbot is generative, nor whether the design is randomized or quasi-experimental, and ANCOVA with 53 students is reported without detail. Since none of these is clear negative evidence, the record goes to full text to check whether the chatbot is generative and whether the design has a comparison group.

quote: The authors generated 646 definition refinements for two geometric objects (ray and quadrilateral) using structured feedback prompts in 216 simulated conversations
rationale: The study uses simulated conversations generated by LLMs rather than real students, so no learner population is present (E4). It also has no separate non-generative-AI control group: it compares LLM feedback variants only (E3 would also apply). The first applicable code in order is E1 check: the intervention is LLM-mediated but simulated, so learner-facing status is unclear; under the ordering, E1 is not clearly met, so E4 is reported as the first clear failure.

quote: This study shows a review of previous research, exploring and understanding the ideas behind a learning management system powered by GenAI.
rationale: The record is a review of previous research and describes a conceptual platform without any empirical study, control group, or quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Under the protocol's ordering, E6 is the first applicable code that is clearly supported by the abstract.

quote: we conducted a case study with a cohort of 59 participants among students and professionals without computational thinking skills
rationale: Abstract describes learners using ChatGPT and LIDA with GPT (generative AI) for data analytics/coding, and students/professionals as participants. However, the study is described as a "case study" with participant perceptions emphasized; the abstract does not clearly show a control group without generative AI (it compares traditional tools vs LLM tools, which may be a comparison group) nor a quantitative learning outcome (preference and perspectives are mentioned, and performance is mentioned without statistics). Design and outcome are unclear at abstract stage, so the record is advanced to full text for checking.

quote: The current research aims to "develop the perceptions of Northern Technical University instructors regarding the use of generative artificial intelligence technology in laboratory teaching."
rationale: The study is a descriptive analytical survey of instructors' perceptions. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and the participants are teachers rather than students. It is not an experimental empirical study of learning. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol sense of an eligible design) is applied; E6 is the closest fit because the design is a perception survey, although E1 and E4 also apply on the abstract. The protocol asks for the first code in order, so E1 would strictly apply first, since the intervention is not learner-facing. Rechecking: E1 is first in order and the abstract describes no learner interaction with generative AI, so the code should be E1.

quote: The final study revealed a bigger significant knowledge improvement in students who used ALTER‐Math compared to the control group
rationale: Abstract describes a generative AI-powered teachable agent (ALTER-Math) used by middle school students in math, with a quasi-experimental control group and pre/post knowledge tests, published 2025 in a journal. The abstract does not report the statistics needed for an SMD, but missing information is not grounds for exclusion at abstract stage; full text should check data sufficiency.

quote: The results indicated a clear recognition of the relevance of these technological tools for teaching and learning.
rationale: The study analyzes student perceptions via a mixed-method survey-style design, with no control group or quantitative learning outcome. Outcomes are perceptions, which the protocol excludes. Domain is also not clearly STEM (teacher training in early childhood and primary education). Exclusion code E5 is the first applicable code given the perception-only outcome; the abstract gives positive evidence that no learning outcome was measured, and no comparison group is mentioned.
rationale_note: Perceptions-only study; no control group reported.

quote: data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered to 300 undergraduate students
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational/regression survey of undergraduates' self-reported GPT use, with no separate control group that avoids generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails. The design is also correlational rather than an experiment or quasi-experiment. Outcomes are self-perceived skill development from a questionnaire, not a quantitative learning measure. Domain is not clearly STEM. Exclusion code E3 is applied as the first failing criterion for the no-control-group problem, which is positive evidence from the abstract.
rationale_note: Coded E3 as the first applicable code; E5 and design failures also apply.

quote: This was a qualitative descriptive study to explore experiences of medical students
rationale: The study is a qualitative descriptive design using focus groups and interviews. It has no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study that meets the protocol's design criteria, so it fails at E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a comparative quantitative design). Exclusion is based on positive abstract evidence of a qualitative design with no control group or quantitative outcome.

quote: Data were collected from 688 university students who used ChatGPT in higher-education institutions on the island of Java, Indonesia.
rationale: Survey-based cross-sectional study using PLS-SEM on continuance intention. No randomized or quasi-experimental design with a non-generative-AI control group, and no quantitative learning outcome (continuance intention is a perception/usage measure). Excluded at first applicable code E3 (no control group without generative AI). The protocol's design and outcome criteria also fail, but E3 is the first code in order that applies. Domain is not stated in the abstract, so it is not assessed as a basis for exclusion.

quote: This study examines the effect of the GenAI writing tools on the academic integrity and the writing proficiency of students using a quantitative cross-sectional survey design.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of 400 undergraduates who are all active GenAI users, with no control group that avoids generative AI, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. Writing proficiency is not a STEM domain. Under the exclusion order, the first applicable code would be E3 (no control group), but the abstract gives clear evidence of a survey/correlational design, which is not an empirical experiment. I am recording E6 as the primary reason: a cross-sectional survey with SEM on self-reported data is not an eligible empirical intervention study. Note the strict ordering rule would place E2 (non-STEM) and E3 before E6; the reviewer should verify the code choice.

quote: Revolutionizing Medical Education: Can ChatGPT Boost Subjective Learning and Expression?
rationale: Abstract is not in the index, so only the title is available. The title places the study in medical education, which falls under the health professions exclusion in the Domain row. Under the protocol, health professions education is excluded from the STEM domain, so this is coded E2 (content not STEM), which is the first applicable code in order. Note: the protocol's first code that applies in order would be E2 for non-STEM content, and E4 was an error in the initial coding; the decision is an exclude with code E2. Population is not clearly non-student from the title alone. Other criteria cannot be confirmed from the title.

quote: This systematic review synthesizes findings from 131 empirical and technical studies published between January 2022 and February 2025.
rationale: The record is a systematic review (secondary synthesis of 131 studies), not an empirical study with a control group, so it fails the protocol's design and comparison criteria and is not an empirical study (E6). Review articles are also an ineligible publication type, but E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order for this record's nature.

quote: This paper proposes an AI-assisted, task-driven reform framework for a computer vision course.
rationale: The abstract describes a proposed reform framework and practical model, with no comparison group, no experimental design, and no learning outcome data reported. This reads as a conceptual/framework paper rather than an empirical study, so it fails E6. Abstract gives positive evidence of non-empirical design.

This is a mixed-methods survey study of computing students' perceptions and trust in ChatGPT. It reports no learning outcome, only perceptions and usage, and has no control group. Design is a survey, not an experiment. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome); the abstract gives positive evidence of perception-only measures. Although E3 and E6 might also apply, E5 is the first code in the protocol order that clearly fails on the abstract.

quote: After surveying what they experienced, some declared that this was their first time using ChatGPT, while others had already used the tool.
rationale: The abstract describes a pilot study in which students used ChatGPT and then surveyed perceptions. There is no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome reported. Positive evidence of design (no comparison) and outcome (perceptions only) failure is present, so this is excluded. The most fitting code under the protocol order is E6 (not an empirical study in the sense of a comparative trial); however, the study is an empirical pilot with survey data, so the code is a judgment call. Under the stated order, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the clearest positive failure because no comparison group is described. Given the ordering, E3 is the more accurate primary code.
decision_note: Corrected code: E3 preferred over E6.

quote: This study adopted a collaborative action research approach to explore how educators supported students with disabilities in engaging with ChatGPT in the classroom.
rationale: The abstract describes a collaborative action research study with video-based analysis producing a qualitative taxonomy. There is no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. The first applicable code in order is E1 check: the intervention is learner-facing ChatGPT use, so E1 does not apply. E2 does not apply (science classroom). E3 applies because there is no control group without generative AI. Under the protocol order, E3 is the first applicable code after E1 and E2, so the exclusion code should be E3 rather than E6. The qualitative design is also evident, but the report must use the first applicable code in order.

quote: Science communication in the AI era must actively counteract bias to remain inclusive.
rationale: The record is a conceptual/position piece on co-designing science education for critical AI literacy. It describes no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It cites other studies but reports no data of its own. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies as the first failing code in order. Note that E1 could also be argued, but the paper is not an empirical study so E6 is the primary reason.

quote: The framework integrates deep learning architectures, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and Transformer-based multimodal fusion, to analyze temporal and heterogeneous learning data.
rationale: The abstract describes a predictive analytics framework (LSTM/Transformer) modelling student performance from learning data; it is unclear whether learners directly interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, or whether a separate non-generative-AI control group exists. Comparison design is not described in the abstract ("comparative analysis" is mentioned but without a clear control condition). Engineering education is STEM and students are higher education, so those criteria appear met. Not excluded at abstract stage because positive evidence of failure is absent; advance to full text to check intervention, comparison, and design.

quote: A qualitative research design was employed involving twenty-four social science educators from higher education institutions in Northern Luzon, Philippines.
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of educators' ethical concerns, not an empirical comparison with a control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is also social science, not STEM. Under the rule for E-code ordering, the first applicable code is E1 for intervention, but the intervention is not an experimental learner-facing tool; the clearest failure is that it is not an empirical quantitative study, so E6 is assigned.
rationale_note: Note: the domain (social science, non-STEM) also fails, but codes are applied in order; E2 (not STEM) precedes E6 in the list and would be the first applicable code. See corrected decision below.

quote: The experimental group (n = 30) used Generative AI tools (ChatGPT/GitHub Copilot) during practicum sessions, while the control group (n = 30) relied on conventional resources.
rationale: Abstract reports a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control design with 60 undergraduates in a Deep Learning course (computing/STEM). The experimental group used generative AI coding assistants (ChatGPT/Copilot) and the control group used conventional resources. Outcomes include a conceptual understanding test and code quality rubric, with t-statistics and Cohen's d reported, so SMD is computable. Journal venue and 2025 date fit. No abstract-level evidence of failure; include, with full-text verification of the data and journal status still needed.

quote: The results showed improvements in programming self-efficacy, media-art production self-efficacy, AI literacy, and creative self-efficacy.
rationale: The abstract describes a guided-practice educational program with pre-post style improvements in self-efficacy and literacy measures, with no mention of a separate control group that does not use generative AI. This is positive evidence of a missing comparison group, so E3 applies. The outcomes are also self-report perceptions, which would raise E5 at full text.
rationale_note: Abstract stage: exclusion based on positive evidence of no control group.

quote: This review evaluates the current applications of AI in neurodegenerative disease research, including drug discovery, biomarker identification, and multi-omics integration.
rationale: The record is a review article, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It also concerns neurodegenerative disease research rather than STEM learning, with no learner-facing intervention, control group, or learning outcome. Under the abstract-stage rule this exclusion is supported by positive evidence that the record is a review.

quote: the system utilizes a graphic interface to process student submissions, allowing instructors to select an LLM and customize the grading rubric
rationale: The LLMs are used for automated grading of student programming assignments, and the instructor selects the model and rubric. Learners do not interact with the generative AI tool, so the intervention is not learner-facing (E1). The abstract also reports agreement between LLM and human grades, not a learning outcome, and shows no control group. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: The authors examine the potential of applying artificial intelligence for personalized mathematics education, using Yandex products as a case study
rationale: The abstract describes an analytical/discussion paper examining opportunities and limitations of Yandex AI tutors, with no experimental design, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It appears to be a non-empirical analysis (E6). Coding E6 as the first applicable exclusion in order is reasonable, though E3 and E5 would also apply since no control group or outcome is reported.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion is supported by positive evidence: the abstract describes analysis and outlining of directions, not an empirical comparison.

criteria.quote: A case study methodology was employed, focusing on 17 fourth-year science teacher candidates and 6 graduate students
criteria.rationale: Qualitative case study on teacher candidates' opinions and prompting approaches; no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Not an empirical experimental design meeting eligibility.

quote: A case study methodology was employed, focusing on 17 fourth-year science teacher candidates and 6 graduate students in a science education master's program
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative case study (interview form and conversation images, content analysis) of teacher candidates' opinions and question-preparation approaches. There is no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. This is a non-experimental qualitative design, so it fails the design, comparison and outcome criteria. Coded E6 (not an empirical study meeting the design requirement), with E3 and E5 also applicable; E6 is the closest fit for a qualitative case study, but the first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group), which is the strictly ordered choice.

quote: Utilizing a quantitative cross-sectional approach, data were collected from 68 diploma-level LIM students
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey-based PLS-SEM analysis of association between RAIL literacy and academic integrity, with no experimental intervention and no control group without generative AI. The outcome is a self-reported/perceptual construct rather than a quantitative learning measure. Fails comparison and design criteria; E3 is the first applicable code in order given no control group. Abstract-stage evidence is positive for the absence of a comparison group and a non-experimental design.

quote: Large language models (LLMs) have shown great potential in automatic scoring.
rationale: The study uses LLMs to score constructed responses (automatic scoring), not learner-facing use of generative AI in a learning activity. Learners do not interact with the tool, so E1 applies. No control group or learning outcome is evident; the design is a measurement/consistency study rather than an experiment.

quote: We, thus, have designed and prototyped a generative artificial intelligence chatbot application (GAIA), named TeacherGAIA
rationale: The abstract describes design and prototyping of a generative AI chatbot with preliminary design, prompt engineering and prototyping evidence only. No controlled comparison, no learning outcome measured, and no empirical experimental design is reported. Fails design and outcome criteria on positive evidence. Intervention is generative AI and the population is K-12, but these do not rescue the exclusion. Exclusion code E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first applicable in the code order given the design is a prototype without measured outcomes; E6 (not an empirical study) could also be argued, but the record describes a design/prototyping paper.

quote: This study examined engineering faculty perceptions of GenAI and its influence on teaching and learning through three semi-structured focus groups with n = 16 faculty
rationale: The study is a qualitative focus-group study of engineering faculty perceptions, not an experiment with learners using generative AI and a control group. It is not an empirical quantitative study of learning outcomes, and participants are faculty rather than students. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a quantitative comparative design); E6 is the closest code given the qualitative design, though the population (faculty, not students) also fails E4.

quote: The participants were 62 newly qualified nurses with less than one year of clinical experience in Taiwan, who needed to learn to interpret electrocardiograms (ECGs) as part of their professional training.
rationale: Participants are newly qualified nurses in professional training, not K-12 or higher education students; this is workplace/professional training. The content (ECG interpretation) is health professions education, which is also outside the STEM domain as defined by the protocol. Exclusion under E4 is the first applicable code in order (E1-E3 do not apply: a generative AI tool is learner-facing, and a conventional PP control exists; E4 precedes E2 in the code order).

quote: two groups, one control group, and one experimental group, subjected to a curricular educational program for one month
rationale: Abstract describes a quasi-experiment with a control group and mathematics content, so design and domain appear met. The experimental program uses "AI and gamification" with Scratch programming, but it is not stated whether the AI is generative, so intervention is unclear. Outcomes include school performance and anxiety; a quantitative achievement measure is likely but not explicit, and population (school level) is not stated. No positive evidence of exclusion at abstract stage, so unsure; resolve at full text for generative AI use, learner interaction, outcome data, and population.

quote: This paper details our reflections on experiencing collaborative learning and collective sensemaking through a discussion-focused event
rationale: The abstract describes a reflective experience report of a facilitated discussion event, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). No comparison group or learning measure is described, so the exclusion is based on positive evidence of a non-empirical reflection paper.

quote: found that the intervention had a positive impact on students’ perceptions of ChatGPT, with an increase in agreement with statements related to its benefits and incorporation into their daily lives.
rationale: Secondary-school physics study using ChatGPT, but the only reported outcome is students' perceptions, which the protocol excludes as a non-learning outcome. No quantitative learning measure is described in the abstract. Excluded at abstract stage on E5 because positive evidence shows the outcome criterion fails.

quote: This study examines the prospective uses of GenAI for NLP synthesis as well as its potential role as a conversational agent in the classroom business.
rationale: The abstract describes a discursive/conceptual examination of prospective uses of generative AI in education. It reports no empirical design, no control group, no sample, and no quantitative learning outcome, so the record appears not to be an empirical study. Positive evidence of a failed criterion is present (no empirical design), so exclusion at abstract stage is justified under E6. No STEM content, population, or comparison is specified.

criteria.rationale_note: Title suggests generative AI-powered VR simulation with science and mathematics preservice teachers, which may fit population and domain. However, the title emphasizes perceptions and experiences, which points toward a perception-only outcome that would fail the quantitative outcome criterion. No abstract is available to confirm a control group, quantitative learning outcome, or effect data.

rationale: No abstract is in the index, so the abstract stage cannot establish any criterion failure. The title describes preservice science and mathematics teachers' perceptions and experiences with a generative AI-powered VR simulation. Perception-focused designs would fail the outcome criterion (E5), but this cannot be confirmed without the full text. Population (preservice teachers learning STEM content count as higher education) and domain appear plausibly met. Advance to full text to check for a control group, a quantitative learning outcome, and SMD-ready statistics.

quote: Using qualitative content analysis, six interrelated themes were generated that describe how students experienced ChatGPT as a learning scaffold
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative content analysis of student narratives with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Design and outcome criteria fail on positive evidence. Chemistry (redox) is STEM and the participants are university students, so those criteria appear met. Coded E5 as the first failing criterion in order is E3 for comparison, but the rule asks for the first code that applies; the lack of any comparison group is also positive evidence. Using E3 would be the first in order since comparison precedes outcome in the protocol's listing; however, the most decisive failure is design/no quantitative outcome. Recording E5 as the outcome failure per the study's qualitative nature.

quote: This study aimed to enhance pre-service teachers' understanding of pedagogical key ideas by integrating ChatGPT in the open and distance learning (ODL) pedagogy course tutorials.
rationale: The abstract describes a case study of nine pre-service teachers with only pre/post and within-subject comparisons (Friedman test, Wilcoxon tests), and no separate control group without generative AI. This fails the comparison and design criteria (single-group pre-post, case study), so E3 applies. Domain is also unclear: pedagogical key ideas in an education course is not clearly STEM. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of no control group and a case-study design.

quote: The study sample consisted of 30 college students who were randomly assigned to two groups.
rationale: Abstract describes ChatGPT use by college students in programming, randomly assigned to a prompt-based vs unprompted ChatGPT learning condition. Both arms use generative AI, so the comparison may fail E3 (no non-generative-AI control), though the UL group may be a usage-only comparison; the abstract does not make this clear. Outcomes emphasize behaviors, interaction quality and perceptions; it is unclear whether a quantitative learning performance measure (achievement/skill) was collected. Perceptions are excluded by protocol. Abstract does not give positive evidence of exclusion, so unsure for full-text review of comparison and outcome.

quote: This paper examines the current use of generative AI in higher education and gathers stakeholder perspectives
rationale: The abstract describes a literature review and stakeholder perspective gathering, not an empirical comparative experiment. No control group or quantitative learning outcome is reported. It is not an empirical study in the protocol sense, so E6 applies. Domain is not specified as STEM either, but E6 is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's logic for this non-empirical paper.
rationale_note: Abstract-stage exclusion on positive evidence of non-empirical design.
rationale_full: The record is a review and perspective paper. The abstract gives positive evidence that it is not an empirical comparative study: it reports a literature review and stakeholder perspectives, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome.

quote: Descriptive statistics for each survey item are presented in Table 1.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional online survey in which practicing audiologists or AuD students rated ChatGPT-generated audiology texts on Likert items. There is no learner interacting with generative AI as part of a learning activity, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; the only outcomes are perceptions of quality and accuracy. Audiology is also not STEM content in the protocol's sense. Excluded at the first applicable code, E1 is arguable since the learner does not interact with the tool, but E5 is the clearest failing criterion. Decision made at abstract stage on positive evidence of a survey design with rating-only outcomes and no control group.

quote: By employing collaborative poetic autoethnography, we argue that ChatGPT is more than just a tool or assistant
rationale: The study is a qualitative poetic autoethnography of one teacher and two students, drawing on poems, reflections and freewriting. It is not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. Domain is academic writing in EFL, not STEM. Excluded on the first applicable code in order; E1 does not apply because ChatGPT is learner-facing, and E2 (non-STEM content) would also apply, but E6 (not an empirical study in the quantitative sense) is the most fundamental failure. Note: under the strict ordering, E2 precedes E6 in the code list only by number, not by order of application; the protocol says report the first that applies in the listed order, which is E1, E2, E3, E4, E5, E6. Non-STEM content (E2) is the first applicable code in that order and should be used instead.

quote: This article empirically explores the usage of ChatGPT 3.5 in database administration education through a case study conducted with 40 computer science students.
rationale: Abstract describes a case study of 40 students using ChatGPT and examines correlation between ChatGPT usage and grades. No control group without generative AI is described, and the design appears observational/correlational rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison. Positive evidence of missing comparison group supports E3 at abstract stage.

quote: Student translators’ cognitive demands and translation behaviors in GenAI-assisted legal translation
rationale: Title indicates legal translation by student translators, which is language/translation content and not STEM. The domain criterion fails on positive evidence, so the record is excluded under E2 (first applicable code, checked in order; E1 could not be assessed from the title alone). No abstract is available, so other criteria were not judged.

Descriptive-quantitative study of student perceptions and self-regulation with descriptive statistics, ANOVA and Pearson correlation; no control group without generative AI is described, so the comparison and design criteria fail. Outcomes are perceptions and usage rather than a quantitative learning measure (E5 also plausible). Per the order of codes, E1 is not clearly established from the abstract, and E3 is the first clearly applicable code since no comparison group exists. Population (senior high STE students) and domain (science) appear met.

quote: Using cross-sectional survey data from a nationally stratified sample of 2,307 students, we estimated structural equation models predicting IRT-scaled achievement
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey with structural equation models linking self-reported GenAI use to achievement. There is no learner-facing intervention and no control group without GenAI, so it is not an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison. Design is correlational/survey, which the protocol excludes. E3 is the code that best fits the missing comparison group, but the design failure is the more fundamental issue; the record is excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of a non-experimental design.

Record has no abstract. Title indicates a business school management course context (management education, feedback literacy, judgment-oriented learning), which is not STEM content under the protocol. Exclusion on domain is supported by the title alone; no quote is available from an abstract. Note that the protocol's E1 code is checked first, but the record gives no evidence about whether the AI is learner-facing or generative, so E2 is the first code with positive evidence of failure. Flagging for researcher review given the thin record.

quote: This quasi-experimental study investigated generative AI (GenAI) tools—Copilot for chemistry and GitHub Copilot for mathematics—on academic achievement
rationale: At abstract stage, all criteria appear met: GenAI tools (Copilot, GitHub Copilot) used by undergraduates, quasi-experimental design with experimental and control groups, STEM content (chemistry, mathematics), pre/post achievement tests with effect size reported. Journal is iJEP, published 2026 (within date range). Publication type and data sufficiency cannot be fully verified from the abstract, but no positive evidence of failure is present, so include and check at full text.

quote: The introduction of neural network technologies into the educational process is shown to significantly reduce calculation time and shift students' focus from mathematical derivations to the physico-chemical analysis of processes.
rationale: The abstract describes illustrative examples of using Microsoft Copilot in chemical engineering courses, with no mention of a control group or comparison condition. quote: a Human-LLM Collaborative Framework (HLCF) for the automatic generation of university course slides
rationale: The LLM is used by educators to generate course slides (teacher-side material preparation), not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity, so E1 applies. The case study measures slide preparation time and qualitative quality, with no control group of learners and no learning outcome, so the design and outcome criteria also appear unmet. E1 is the first applicable code in order.
rationale_note: Abstract stage; exclusion based on positive evidence that the AI is used only by educators.

criteria.stage_note: abstract reads as a conceptual/review article about LLM-based relevance measurement in e-commerce

quote: This article addresses fundamental trade-offs between coverage, quality, and cost that have long constrained traditional relevance measurement methodologies
rationale: The abstract describes an e-commerce search relevance application with no learners, no STEM learning context, no control group, and no learning outcome. It reads as a discursive or review article rather than an empirical study. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study). Domain (e-commerce, not STEM education) and population (no students) also fail, but the first applicable code in order that is most clearly supported is E1 for intervention; however the intervention is not learner-facing, so E1 applies first. Note: per the protocol order, E1 applies first since the LLM is used to assess relevance by system designers rather than learners.

quote: This mixed methods study explores EFL students' experiences and perceptions as they learn to write a composition with ChatGPT's support
rationale: The content is English language writing (EFL), which is non-STEM, so E2 applies. The study also has no control group, uses a single-group pre-post and mixed-methods perception design, and reports only perceptions, satisfaction, and cognitive load, so E3, E5 and design concerns would also apply. E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order.

quote: This survey investigates the integration of ChatGPT into mathematics education
rationale: The record is a survey/review article, not an empirical study. The abstract describes no experimental or comparison-group design and no quantitative learning outcome measure. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Positive evidence of the review nature is given by the word "survey" and the absence of any primary data.

quote: A qualitative study design. METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were conducted among 16 nursing postgraduates.
rationale: Qualitative interview study on perceptions (UTAUT framework). It has no comparison group, no quantitative learning outcome, and is not an empirical study with eligible design. Nursing content is also outside the STEM domain. Excluded under E6 as the first applicable code in the order of the protocol is E1 (intervention not clearly learner-facing GenAI), but the abstract does not establish a learning activity; the decisive failure is the non-empirical-quantitative qualitative design. Note: strictly, the first code in protocol order that applies with positive evidence is E2 (nursing is health professions education, not STEM).

quote: Implementation and Educational Impact of a Story-Centered Curriculum Using a Large Language Model: A Class on Internal Disorders for Physiotherapy Students
rationale: Students are physiotherapy students learning internal disorders/respiratory clinical cases, a health professions education context. Protocol excludes health professions education, which is not STEM content (E2). Intervention (ChatGPT GPT-4 narrative cases) and comparison (historical control) are otherwise plausible. Exclusion is based on domain, the first applicable code in order before design concerns.

quote: The present investigation employed an educational design research (EDR) methodology in which the researchers incorporate ChatGPT into our Math+CT lessons to assist students in accomplishing the task.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group educational design research study with qualitative analysis of prompts and conversations. There is no control group without generative AI, and the design is qualitative rather than an experimental or quasi-experimental comparison. Exclude under E3 (no control group without generative AI); the design also fails the study-design criterion. This is positive evidence from the abstract, so exclusion is appropriate.
rationale_note: Only one code is reported (first applicable in order).

quote: Using a mixed descriptive–experimental design with 40 undergraduate computer science students, two simulation phases were conducted: (1) unrestricted submission where ChatGPT use was possible and (2) instructor-guided submission with supervised ChatGPT interactions and oral defenses.
rationale: ChatGPT is a generative AI tool and the population (undergraduate CS) and domain (programming) fit. However, the design appears to be a single-group two-phase comparison (same 40 students, unrestricted then guided), with no evident separate control group without generative AI. That would point to E3, but the abstract is not explicit enough to exclude at this stage, and the outcome (65% vs 90% 'AI generation indicators' and 'comprehension') is ambiguous as a quantitative learning measure. Rule 2 requires positive evidence of failure, so this is unsure for full-text review.

quote: Using a qualitative descriptive approach, data were collected from three students in semester six or above, each submitting five naturally composed prompts.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative descriptive study of prompt syntax from three students, with no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of failure exists for comparison/design and for outcome (E5 is the code for no quantitative learning outcome). Domain is ambiguous (Morphology and Syntax course, linguistics rather than STEM), but E5 is applied as the first clearly failing code in protocol order for this stage. Note that E3 (no control group) would also apply; under the code ordering E1 and E2 are not clearly met, so E2 could be argued for the linguistics content, but E3 comes before E5 in the protocol order and the study has no control group, so E3 is the first applicable code.

quote: Students were randomly divided into experimental (n = 21) and control (n = 24) groups. While the experimental group students benefited from the ChatGPT during the weekly programming practices, the control group students did not use this tool.
rationale: Randomized experiment with ChatGPT (generative AI) used by university learners in programming practice, versus a control group without the tool. Outcomes include computational thinking skills, a quantitative scale measure of learning. Published 2023, journal article (Computers and Education: Artificial Intelligence). Data sufficiency for SMD cannot be fully confirmed from the abstract, but no positive evidence of failure is given, so advance to full text.

The abstract describes a position/reform-proposal paper ("this paper proposes comprehensive reform suggestions"). It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Under rule 2, exclusion requires positive evidence of failure; here the abstract itself indicates a non-empirical discussion paper, so E6 applies. Note that E6 is the first applicable code in order only if E1 is not clearly failing; the abstract does not clearly show a learner-facing tool, so E1 was not assigned.

quote: we compare the application of various models for conducting a large-scale analysis of written text
rationale: The LLMs (BERT, LLaMA) are used by researchers as text classifiers to label students' lab notes, not as a learner-facing tool that students interact with during a learning activity. This fails the intervention criterion (E1). No learning outcome or control-group experiment is described; the study is a methods comparison of classifiers.

quote: Because no student-outcome data were collected, the paper reports instructional implementation and practitioner observations rather than causal effects on engagement or learning.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive teaching case with no student-outcome data and no control group. Explicitly no quantitative learning outcome is reported, so E5 applies. Design also lacks a comparison group (E3 could be argued), but E5 is the clearest positive evidence and the first applicable code per the protocol's order is E3 before E5; however, the abstract gives no comparison group either, so the earliest code that positively applies is E3. Given the protocol order, E3 applies first: no control group is described and the design is a descriptive case.

quote: The results indicated that the students were positive toward the artificial intelligence ChatGPT.
rationale: At abstract stage, the only reported result is student positivity toward ChatGPT, which is a perception outcome, not a quantitative learning measure. The abstract gives positive evidence that no learning outcome is measured (the t-test is not linked to any achievement result). Per protocol, perception-only outcomes fail the outcome criterion, so E5 applies. Domain and comparison are not stated in the abstract; those are unclear but not needed given the E5 exclusion.
decision_rationale: Excluded at abstract stage for no quantitative learning outcome.

quote: This study was conducted with master's and doctoral students in the field of public health nursing at a university.
rationale: Descriptive qualitative study of nursing graduate students' ChatGPT experiences via semi-structured interviews. Content is public health nursing, which is health professions education, not STEM, so E2 applies. It also has no control group (E3) and no quantitative learning outcome (E5); E2 is the first applicable code in order. Abstract evidence is sufficient to exclude.

criteria.domain_note: NMR chemistry is a science domain
criteria.note: Main study evaluates LLMs as test-takers on benchmark problems rather than learners interacting with generative AI in a learning activity

quote: We evaluated 10 LLMs (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, o1, o1 mini, o3 mini, Claude-3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 2.0 Flash, Meta Llama 3, ChemDFM-R, and ether0)
rationale: The study mainly benchmarks LLMs on NMR problems; learners do not interact with generative AI as part of a learning activity. Human students were evaluated in a controlled setting, but there is no control group that lacks generative AI and no learner-facing AI intervention. The primary exclusion is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI). Design is also a benchmark evaluation, not a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison. Decision made at abstract stage on positive evidence.
rationale_note: Exclusion is clear from the abstract.

quote: A cross-sectional survey design was used in this research among 836 school students in Kathmandu, Nepal.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey with structural equation modeling, not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. There is no control group without generative AI, so the study fails the comparison and design criteria. E3 is the first applicable code in order that is supported by the abstract; E6 (not empirical) does not apply since it is an empirical survey. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of a non-experimental design.
exclusion_code_note: E3 used; design failure is the closest code.

quote: The study of the experience of using AI tools among applicants for higher education in the medical field during the "Molecular Biology" course revealed that 70.3% of respondents utilize AI for learning.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey-based study of student experience and usage of AI tools (70.3% utilize AI). There is no control group, no experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is a survey/descriptive design, so it is not an empirical comparative study meeting protocol design or outcome criteria. The first applicable code is E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense). Domain (molecular biology in medical education) is arguably STEM but the population is higher education, so this is not the deciding issue.

quote: Student survey responses indicated substantial adoption and generally positive perceptions; peer-led supplemental instruction attendance and course-grade data are presented only as contextual information.
rationale: Technology report describing a custom GPT chatbot in undergraduate biochemistry. The abstract reports only survey perceptions and adoption, with course-grade data presented only as context, and no control group or learning measure. Excluded on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). The design also appears to be a descriptive report rather than a controlled comparison, but the abstract gives no explicit design statement, so E5 is the primary code given the positive evidence of perception-only outcomes.

quote: eleven models solving problems from the Bulgarian National External Assessment (NEA) for 10th grade are empirically evaluated
rationale: The study evaluates LLMs solving NEA problems directly (model accuracy), with no learner-facing comparison group. The second strand is qualitative observation of teachers. No control group without generative AI and no learning outcome for students is described, so the record fails comparison, design and outcome. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is applied as the first failing criterion in the stated order. The abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group.

quote: This study examined the difficulties students experience when learning syntactic tree diagrams
rationale: Syntax tree diagrams in English Education are linguistics content, not STEM, so E2 applies first. The study is also a descriptive qualitative/questionnaire design with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (perception means only), so it would fail E3, E5 and E6 as well. E2 is reported as the first applicable code in the protocol order.
intervention_note: ChatGPT used as a self-selected strategy, not a studied intervention

quote: this research investigated integrating ChatGPT into mathematics education, focusing on the familiarity, perceptions, and training needs of 110 mathematics teachers
rationale: The study surveys in-service mathematics teachers about familiarity, perceptions, and training needs. Participants are teachers, not K-12 or higher education students, and there is no control group, no experiment, and no quantitative learning outcome. The record fails several criteria on positive evidence. E4 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that clearly applies (participants are not students). Since the design is a survey, E6 (not an empirical study) would also apply, but E4 is reported as it comes first in the listed order. Intervention and comparison are also not met (learner interaction with GenAI and control group absent). The primary exclusion is population, so E4 is recorded.

quote: The study reviewed the literature semi-systematically. This approach searched for and overviewed the research area and the progress made.
rationale: The abstract describes a semi-systematic literature review, not an empirical study. No control group, learning outcome, or primary data are reported. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E1 and E2 are not clearly evidenced from the abstract, so E6 is the first applicable code on the positive evidence available.
rationale_extra: Publication type also appears to be a review, which the protocol excludes under E10, but the abstract's primary description is a literature review, so E6 is applied.

quote: No formal student learning assessment is reported; the purpose is to share a practical, adaptable approach to AI-assisted study-guide development.
rationale: The article is a Tips and Tools instructor workflow in which generative AI is used by the instructor to draft study guides, not by learners; the abstract states no student learning assessment is reported and there is no control group. Under the protocol, teacher-only AI use is E1, but the record is a practice article with no empirical study, so E6 is the first clearly applicable code in the protocol's ordering given it is not an empirical study at all. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence.

criteria.criteria_note: Survey and interview study of teachers

quote: Through the survey and interview on 40 English primary teachers in Kuta, it is found that 9 teachers were using generative AI
rationale: The study is a survey and interview of 40 primary English teachers about their use of and perspectives on generative AI. It is not an empirical comparative study: there is no control group, no learner-facing intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome. The design is survey/qualitative, so it is not an eligible empirical study. Population (in-service teachers) and domain (English language learning) also fail. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention not learner-facing), but the abstract shows teachers as the users, which fits E1 as well. Because the protocol requires the first applicable code in order, E1 is the correct code.

quote: This Community Service Program (PKM) aims to enhance the technological literacy of students at SMKN 1 Duduksampeyan
rationale: This is a community service program report (Jurnal Pengabdian Masyarakat) describing a training activity with pre-test questionnaire descriptives only. It has no control group, no comparison design, no quantitative learning outcome computable as an SMD, and the content (LLM use for school assignments, accounting-focused) is not clearly STEM. Publication type is a community service report rather than an empirical journal article. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence of failed comparison/design/outcome; the first applicable code in order would be E1/E2, but the abstract does not clearly establish those, so E10 (publication type not eligible) is used as the most evident failure given the record is a community service program report, not an empirical study. Note: strictly, E3 (no control group) and E5 (no learning outcome) are also evident; the code list order places E3 before E10, so E3 is arguably the first applicable code.

quote: Participants experienced either GenAI-supported or traditional instructions while learning the same concept.
rationale: Controlled experiment with 96 undergraduate computer science students (Database Management) comparing GenAI-supported learning with traditional instruction; quizzes give achievement outcomes; published 2025 in Education Sciences (journal). Effect-size data sufficiency cannot be verified from the abstract, so the record is advanced to full text rather than excluded. Abstract gives no positive evidence of any failed criterion.

quote: Designed as a qualitative classroom-based case study, the research was conducted over a seven-week module.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative case study with diaries, journals and interviews, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It concerns collaborative academic writing, which is not clearly STEM. Positive evidence that the comparison and design criteria fail supports exclusion. E3 is the first applicable code in order, since there is no control group without generative AI; the design is also qualitative.

quote: Using KLAP, we conducted an empirical evaluation on a sample consisting of 312 computer science students from three courses at the undergraduate level.
rationale: Abstract reports an empirical evaluation with 312 undergraduate computer science students and a learning-effectiveness effect size (Cohen's d = 0.74), with comparison against traditional adaptive learning path systems. Record is a mix of a systematic review and an empirical study. Whether the KLAP intervention is learner-facing generative AI (fine-tuned LLM plus KG) is plausible but the abstract does not clearly describe learner interaction. The comparison is with adaptive systems, which may or may not lack a generative component, and the design (randomized or quasi-experimental) is not stated. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record goes to full text. Publication venue "Technical Annals" and the 2026 date should also be checked for journal-article status.

quote: by combining generative artificial intelligence technology, it tailors precise mathematics learning strategies for students with different learning styles
rationale: Junior high school mathematics with generative AI tailoring learning strategies; learner-facing use is implied. The abstract does not describe a control group, an experimental design, or a quantitative learning outcome, so these cannot be confirmed as met or as failed. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is held for full-text review rather than excluded.

quote: This paper investigates the potential of GPT-4o to support theory-informed codebook development across two educational contexts.
rationale: The study uses GPT-4o as a research tool by researchers to develop qualitative codebooks from think-aloud data. Learners do not interact with the generative AI as part of a learning activity, so E1 applies. There is no control group comparing generative AI against a non-AI condition; the second study compares prompting strategies for the researchers' codebook development. Outcome is codebook quality, not a learning measure. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing.

criteria.comparison_note: control group of 30 students described; whether control used no generative AI is not stated

quote: the researcher used a quasi-experimental design with two groups; a control group of 30students and an experimental group of 30students
rationale: Quasi-experimental design with a control group and an achievement test in functional writing skills, with students at a university, so design, outcome, and population appear met. Functional writing is not clearly STEM, so the domain is unclear; the abstract does not say what the control group received, and the training program's use of generative AI is only implied by its title. Missing information is not evidence of failure at abstract stage, so the record goes to full text for checks on domain (E2) and the control condition (E3).

quote: this study develops an exploratory Monte Carlo simulation framework for quantifying perception-based student success in the context of GenAI use
rationale: The record is a Monte Carlo simulation using synthetic observations parameterised from literature summary statistics, not an empirical study with learners. It has no control group comparison and its outcome is perception-based, not a quantitative learning measure. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code in order is E1 or E2 unclear, but the abstract gives positive evidence that the study is a simulation rather than empirical research.

quote: The study involved 19 third-year students from G University of Education who used ChatGPT to create lesson plans.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group qualitative study of 19 pre-service teachers using ChatGPT, with findings based on feedback and comparative analysis of lesson plans and reports. There is no control group without generative AI, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. Excluded under E3 (no comparison group); the design is also not an experiment. Domain (clothing life/practical arts) is also not clearly STEM. The first applicable code in order is E3, since E1 does not apply (learners do use ChatGPT).

quote: those qualitative reflection responses were analyzed for themes
rationale: The study analyzes qualitative student reflections only, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Epidemiology is also arguably not STEM under the protocol's listed domains. Exclusion is on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), the first code that clearly applies in the protocol's order after intervention (ChatGPT used by students, met) and population (undergraduates, met). Design is qualitative, which also fails the design criterion, but the abstract's explicit evidence is the absence of a quantitative outcome.

quote: This study used descriptive statistics and linear regression analysis using the data collected randomly from 216 students’ responses on the Twitter website
rationale: The study is a survey-style analysis of 216 students' social media posts about ChatGPT use, using descriptive statistics and regression. There is no control group without generative AI, no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome (outcomes are usage, cost, preference, and perceived task completion). Domain is not STEM-specific. Excluded on E3 as the first applicable code in order (no comparison group without generative AI); the design and outcome problems also independently fail the criteria.

criteria.criteria_note: Narrative paper on ChatGPT in medical education; no comparison group or outcome data

quote: This paper examines the potential applications, limitations, and strategies for using ChatGPT.
rationale: The record is a narrative/perspective paper (examines potential applications, limitations and strategies) with no empirical design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is also focused on medical education, which falls under the health professions exclusion for domain. The primary exclusion is E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported by the abstract. Note that the domain also appears to be health professions education, which would be excluded, but E6 is the first code reached in the protocol's stated order.

quote: survey data were collected from 117 students during February–March 2025
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey using SEM/ANN on perceptions and intention to use, with no separate control group that avoids generative AI. Outcome is perception/intention (usage-type), not a quantitative learning measure. Although the abstract claims AI improves problem-solving and self-efficacy, the design gives no comparison group, so the first applicable code is E3 (no control group without generative AI). Abstract-stage exclusion is justified by positive evidence of a survey design without a control group.
rationale_note: Exclusion at abstract stage based on survey design; no comparison group evident.

quote: Adaptive Heterogeneous Multi-Agent Debate (A-HMAD), a novel framework that extends multi-agent debate with (i) diverse specialized agents, (ii) dynamic debate routing, and (iii) a learned consensus mechanism.
rationale: The study is a multi-agent LLM debate framework evaluated on benchmarks (arithmetic QA, GSM8K, MMLU, biography generation, chess strategy). No students or learners are described; the agents are the LLMs themselves. Participants are therefore not K-12 or higher education students, so E4 applies. The "educational" framing does not establish a learner population. Exclusion is based on positive evidence that the population criterion fails.

quote: First, our literature review shows key challenges and considerations linked to infrastructure and resource requirements, digital inequality, data privacy, copyright
rationale: The abstract describes a literature review and theoretical contextualization of ChatGPT in engineering education. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Per the protocol's order, E6 is the first code that applies after checking E1 (intervention not clearly ruled out at abstract, but the design itself fails).
rationale_detail: Not an empirical primary study; review/theoretical paper.

quote: Assessment of learning outcomes, student self-efficacy, group dynamics, and stakeholder feedback are required to measure the effects of ChatGPT in the PBL curriculum.
rationale: The abstract describes a perspective/commentary on using ChatGPT in problem-based learning medical education. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome data; it explicitly states that outcomes are yet to be assessed. Positive evidence of non-empirical design (E6) applies. Medical education also raises a domain concern (health professions, not STEM), but the first applicable code in order is E6 given the order rule would place E2 earlier; however, the domain is not clearly STEM or non-STEM from the abstract alone, so E6 is the clearest positive failure. Note: strictly by code order, E2 precedes E6 if the domain failure is confirmed; the health-professions context suggests E2 may apply at fulltext.

quote: A visual content analysis of AI generated images (N = 291) representing STEM-related occupations (e.g., scientist, mathematician).
rationale: The study is a visual content analysis of AI-generated images, not an empirical study with learners. It has no control group, no learner-facing intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome. The bias and disfigurement percentages are image characteristics, not learning measures. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study of learners); E1 or E3 would also apply, but E6 reflects the design best. Note that E1 comes first in the code order, so the strictly first applicable code could be argued as E1; the study is not learner-facing at all.

quote: A cross-sectional study was conducted with 235 Computer Science students.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional path analysis of students' perceptions of ChatGPT and plagiarism threshold. There is no experimental intervention or control group, so the design and comparison criteria are not met. The outcome is a self-reported attitude (plagiarism threshold), not a quantitative measure of learning. Excluded at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). Per the code order, E1 (intervention) and E3 (comparison) would also arguably apply, but the first clear failure on the outcome is recorded here; the design failure (cross-sectional, non-experimental) is a further basis for exclusion.

quote: Using a descriptive cross-sectional survey design and non-probability convenience sampling, data were collected from 451 Malaysian university students (Generation Z).
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey (PLS-SEM) with no control group, no experimental manipulation, and no learning outcome; it measures perceptions, intention and self-reported usage. Under the protocol's first applicable code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing GenAI) is not clearly established from the abstract, and E3 (no control group) and E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) also apply. The best-fitting code for a non-empirical-experimental survey that fails design is E6 (not an empirical study is arguably wrong since it is empirical); given the code order, E3 would be the first clear failure after E1/E2 are not positively shown to fail. Decision recorded as exclude on design grounds.

criteria.population_note: participants are in-service secondary physics teachers, not students

quote: Data were collected from 12 secondary school physics teachers in Beijing.
rationale: The participants are in-service secondary school physics teachers, not K-12 or higher education students, so the population criterion fails (E4). The study also reports teacher perceptions via TAM and question-type analysis, with no clear controlled learning outcome and no control group described, but E4 is the first applicable code in order. Excluding at abstract stage is justified because the positive evidence (teacher participants) is explicit.

quote: Rather than delivering a fully integrated production system, WENDY develops and evaluates complementary prototypes, design frameworks, and validation procedures to inform future implementation
rationale: The abstract describes a methodology and prototypes/design frameworks for building concept maps with LLMs and embeddings. It reports no controlled comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome for learners. The work reads as a design/methods project rather than an empirical comparative study, so it fails the design and outcome criteria and is not an empirical study. Exclude at E6 (the first applicable code in order that is clearly supported; E1 is not clearly positive since the LLM use may be teacher/researcher-side for building maps, and E3/E5 are also likely but the abstract does not state them explicitly).

quote: This study aims to examine the influence of ChatGPT as a digital learning media on students' learning motivation and achievement in English
rationale: The study is about English language learning, which the protocol excludes as non-STEM (E2). It also uses a one-group pretest-posttest design with no control group, which would be E3. Per the protocol's exclusion code order, E2 is reported first. Exclusion is justified on the abstract alone because the content domain is explicitly English.

quote: This meta-review synthesizes existing systematic reviews on AI in mathematics education
rationale: The record is a meta-review of 13 systematic reviews, not an empirical study with a control group or learning outcome. It fails the design, comparison and outcome criteria. Per the protocol's E6 code (not an empirical study), it is excluded at the abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: The purpose of this exploratory qualitative case study is to gain a deeper understanding of teacher experiences and perspectives of ChatGPT as a pedagogical tool.
rationale: The study is a qualitative case study of teacher perspectives (survey and focus groups). It is not an empirical quantitative experiment with a control group, no learner outcome is measured, and participants are in-service teachers rather than students. Excluded at E6 as a non-empirical-quantitative (qualitative case study) design; the first applicable code in order would be E1 (teachers using ChatGPT for materials, not learner-facing), but the design failure is the clearest and most fundamental reason. Coded E6 per the qualitative design.

quote: A comprehensive survey was conducted with 57 college students at an online survey platform SurveyMonkey.com.
rationale: The study is a survey of perceptions and acceptance (UTAUT2/Diffusion of innovations), with no experimental or comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E5 applies: only perceptions and intentions are measured. Design also fails (survey design, no comparison group), but E5 is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's listed codes for this record's abstract-level evidence, since the survey design is evidenced as a non-experimental perception study.

quote: This study was guided by Arksey and O'Malley's framework for scoping reviews
rationale: The record is a scoping review, which is a review article and not an empirical study with a comparison group or learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). It also reports no experimental comparison or quantitative learning outcome. Domain is not specified in the abstract.

quote: A customised chatbot was developed leveraging ChatGPT to provide step-by-step assistance through a structured problem-solving algorithm.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study appears to meet all criteria: a ChatGPT-based LLM chatbot used by 12th-grade physics students, randomly assigned to a teacher-guided comparison group, with a problem-solving competency outcome, published 2024. Data sufficiency for SMD, journal article status, and language cannot be confirmed from the abstract (Mann-Whitney result reported without descriptive statistics), so these are deferred to full text. No positive evidence of failure, so include.

quote: By integrating AI tools into the course, it aims to enhance the efficiency and innovation of students' programming practice
rationale: Abstract describes a programming practice course in higher education that integrates AI tools, so domain and population appear met. However, it is a curriculum reform framework; the abstract gives no indication of a control group, a comparative design, a learner-facing generative AI tool specifically, or any quantitative learning outcome. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so it passes to full text for checking of design, comparison, and outcome.

quote: A self-designed online questionnaire featuring items on a 5-point Likert scale was utilised to gather data from 264 students pursuing PGDM.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group survey of student perceptions with no control group and no learning measure; the outcomes are self-reported perceptions (Likert items) and the design is survey-based, not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Positive evidence of failure on comparison/design and outcome criteria exists, so exclusion is warranted. Under the protocol's coding order, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code at this stage, though E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) and E6 (not an empirical design as specified) could also apply.

quote: The integration of GenAI into creative mathematics learning is particularly important because it enables students to explore multiple solution strategies
rationale: Abstract describes a correlational analysis between prompt quality and logical reasoning of student teachers using LLM tools (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude) in mathematics.
