The abstract describes ChatGPT-4o used by a university teacher to generate test materials (tasks, test questions, synopses). This is teacher-facing use of generative AI to prepare materials, not learner-facing use, so E1 applies. There is no indication of a learner-interaction intervention or a control group with learning outcomes. Excluding at the abstract stage is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing.

quote: we conducted semi-structured interviews with 42 instructors from 33 institutions in nine countries
rationale: The record is a qualitative interview study of instructors. It is not an empirical experiment with a control group and has no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible designs), which is the first applicable code after the intervention and domain checks, since the intervention is instructor-level and not learner-facing generative AI with a comparison group. Stated quote supports qualitative interview design.

quote: students who had access to a combination of video-based Q&A and multi-agent debates performed significantly better on quizzes compared to those who only had access to the video or video-based Q&A
rationale: At abstract stage, the intervention uses LLM-simulated debates with learners (generative AI, learner-facing), CS university students (STEM, higher education), control groups with video-only or video Q&A without debates (non-generative-AI comparison), and quiz performance as a learning outcome. Randomization and effect-size statistics are not stated in the abstract, so design and data sufficiency are unclear and warrant full-text checking. No exclusion criterion is positively evident.

quote: A quantitative survey design was employed involving 20 seventh-semester students from the English Education Department.
rationale: Survey design measuring perceptions of ChatGPT use for thesis proposal writing in an English Education department; content is language/academic writing, not STEM. No control group, and outcomes are perceptions only. Exclusion code E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order that the abstract clearly supports (non-STEM content). Note that E2 is checked before E3 and E5 per the order given; the design also fails E3/E6 and outcome E5.

quote: This study compared ChatGPT adoption among university students in Indonesia and Malaysia using a quantitative cross-sectional survey.
rationale: Cross-sectional survey comparing adoption across two country samples, with no experimental or quasi-experimental control group without generative AI. Outcomes are self-reported adoption, self-efficacy, and perceived benefits, not a quantitative learning outcome. The abstract gives positive evidence of failure on outcome (E5) and design (survey, not an eligible design). E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order of the protocol's exclusion list. STEM content is not evident from the abstract. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: The results demonstrate that well-structured prompts significantly improve the accuracy and relevance of AI-generated solutions
rationale: The abstract describes a methodology and best-practices paper about prompt engineering in a C++ cloud training ecosystem. It reports no comparison group, no controlled design, and no learning outcome measured as a quantitative effect; it reads as a descriptive or position paper rather than an empirical controlled study. Positive evidence of design failure (no control group described) supports exclusion as not an empirical study (E6). Note that the code E6 is applied on the basis of the abstract's descriptive framing; a full-text check could revise this if the paper reports a controlled experiment.

quote: The study found that a personalized counseling program, intelligent emotion recognition and instant feedback constituted the three core elements of GenAI support
rationale: Abstract describes a GenAI-supported mental health resilience intervention with normal university students (population met). However, the abstract gives no indication of a control group, the design (mixed methods, unclear whether randomized or quasi-experimental), or quantitative learning outcomes. Domain is mental health resilience, not clearly STEM. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so unsure at abstract stage; the domain fit is a concern to resolve at full text.

quote: This study investigated the effect of AI chatbot-assisted instruction on the entrepreneurial learning engagement of ABM Senior High School students
rationale: The content is entrepreneurial learning in an ABM (Accountancy, Business and Management) strand, which is business/entrepreneurship content and not STEM under the protocol's domain list. This is a positive abstract-level failure of the domain criterion, so exclude under E2. Intervention type (chatbot, possibly generative) and outcome (engagement questionnaires, which may be perception-based) are also unclear, but the domain failure is sufficient on its own.

quote: An online survey was distributed, garnering responses from 37 students at several institutions.
rationale: The study is a survey of 37 students with self-reported impact of ChatGPT on academic performance. There is no control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails. The design is a survey (correlational/survey), not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Abstract gives positive evidence of the failed comparison and design criteria, so exclude at abstract stage with E3 as the first applicable code in order (no control group).

quote: This qualitative case study involved three intermediate EFL university students at Institut Pendidikan Indonesia Garut, West Java.
rationale: The study is an EFL speaking practice study, so content is non-STEM (E2). It is also a qualitative case study with no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no SMD-capable data. The first applicable code in order is E2, since the content criterion fails first.
rationale_note: Multiple criteria fail; E2 is the first in protocol order.

quote: This study examined public sentiment regarding ChatGPT's influence on education by utilizing web mining and natural language processing (NLP) techniques.
rationale: The study mines 2003 web articles on public sentiment about ChatGPT in education. It has no learners interacting with a generative AI tool, no control group, and no learning outcome measure. It is not an empirical study of learners in the protocol's sense, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study) as the first applicable code. Other criteria also fail, but E6 is the earliest code that clearly applies from the abstract.

quote: this paper constructs an AI-PBL implementation framework. Taking the teaching of "Exponential Function" as an example, it explores the specific application
rationale: The abstract describes a framework and a single teaching example in a case study. It reports no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome, so the study appears non-empirical (case study/framework). Code E6 is used because the paper is a conceptual framework and case study rather than an empirical comparison. Domain (high school mathematics) and population (high school) are met.

quote: We propose an agent-based approach to question generation and scoring
rationale: The LLM agents generate questions and score answers; learners do not interact with the generative AI as part of a learning activity. The generative tool is used by instructors for question creation and grading (AI used only by teacher / for grading), so intervention is not learner-facing. No learner learning outcome or control group is described in the abstract. Excluded under E1.

quote: "ChatGPT: the future of discharge summaries?" and "The question for the future will be how, not if, we adopt this technology."
rationale: The record is a Lancet Digital Health commentary/viewpoint on using ChatGPT to write hospital discharge summaries. It reports no empirical study, no control group, no learners, and no outcome data. It is not an empirical study (E6). It is also not about STEM learning and involves clinicians rather than students, but E6 is the first applicable code in order from E1 onward only if E1 and earlier do not apply. The intervention is clinician-facing rather than learner-facing, which would technically be E1 first; however, the record is not an empirical study at all, so E6 is the most fundamental reason. Decision is exclude at abstract stage with positive evidence of no empirical design.

quote: A cross-sectional quantitative design was employed, involving academic staff ( n = 52) and students ( n = 513)
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey design with correlational and chi-square analyses of AI use frequency against academic performance. There is no randomized or quasi-experimental design and no control group without generative AI, so the study fails the comparison and design criteria. Exclusion code E3 is applied as the first failing criterion; E3 is the code for no control group without generative AI. Domain is not stated in the abstract, and the study is not clearly STEM. Because the abstract gives positive evidence of a non-experimental design, exclusion is appropriate even at the abstract stage.

quote: The scenarios aim to introduce students to programming through low-code software development.
rationale: At abstract stage, the intervention is low-code programming scenarios for mobile apps; no learner-facing generative AI tool is described. The abstract mentions generative AI only as background motivation. Positive evidence that the intervention is not generative AI supports exclusion under E1. Results rely on educator perceptions and surveys, with no clear quantitative learning outcome (E5 also a possible concern). Control classes are mentioned but the abstract does not describe a comparison of learning outcomes.

quote: This exploratory study examines how first-year engineering students at a Korean university autonomously used AI tools in a writing-based English grammar course
rationale: Abstract describes an exploratory survey/reflection study of autonomous AI use in an English grammar course, with no control group and no experimental comparison. Content is English grammar (language learning), not STEM, and the outcome is perceived achievement via survey. Design is survey/correlational, not an experiment. Exclusion code assigned as E3 (no control group without generative AI) per the first applicable code order as the clearest failing criterion; the domain (E2) also fails and would be an alternative. Note: the protocol's code order places E2 before E3, so on strict first-applicable ordering this should arguably be E2. Correcting to E2 in the decision below.

quote: A subgroup of 170 students received a formative assessment with varying difficulty levels of ChatGPT-generated questions.
rationale: Abstract describes a university mathematics course (number base conversion, STEM) with a ChatGPT-generated-questions group versus students who did not receive them, and post-test performance as an outcome. Positive evidence of exclusion is absent. However, it is unclear whether learners interact with ChatGPT themselves (the questions may be teacher-used material, which would be E1) and whether the comparison is a true control with extractable SMD statistics. Resolve at full text.

quote: generative AI technologies – such as large language models, visual content generators, and educational chatbots – that are increasingly assisting teachers in preparing and delivering mathematics instruction
rationale: The abstract describes generative AI used by teachers to prepare materials and deliver instruction, not learner-facing interaction. No comparison group, no empirical design, and no learning outcome are described. E1 applies as the first failing code.

The abstract describes a survey-style study of knowledge, attitudes, and practices toward ChatGPT among senior high school mathematics learners. It reports group differences in perceptions and self-reported use, not a learning outcome, and there is no experimental or comparison group with a learning intervention. Design is a survey and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. Coding the first applicable exclusion in order: E1 is not clearly applicable since the abstract does not state whether the tool is learner-facing in a learning activity, but the decisive failure is the absence of a control group and a learning outcome. Per the protocol order, the first code that applies from E1 onward would be E1 only if intervention failure is evident; the abstract gives no positive evidence that the intervention is non-generative, so the strongest positive evidence is the lack of a control group (E3) and of a learning outcome (E5). Using E3 as the first clearly evidenced failure. Note that the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with no comparison group, so exclusion is supported.

Domain is also not clearly STEM (English education). Exclusion on E5 as the first clearly failing criterion reflects that the only outcomes are perceptions, which the protocol excludes. Design also fails the comparison requirement (survey, not an experiment with a control), but the code was assigned per the order given, so E5 is applied as the first failure among those evident from the abstract.

quote: Harnessing Generative Artificial Intelligence to Improve Efficiency Among Urologists: Welcome ChatGPT
rationale: This is a JU Forum opinion piece (editorial-style commentary) on using ChatGPT for urologist efficiency. quote: this position paper argues that it has significant implications for various aspects of the educational sector

It is not an empirical learner study with a control group; there is no comparison group without generative AI, and no learner intervention. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that the abstract gives positive evidence for. Note that the abstract does not clearly show E1 or E3 first, but E6 is the most direct positive evidence. Rule 2 is applied with positive evidence from the abstract.

quote: The results of this study show that the overall suitability of the development of the architecture of the educational guidance platform via AI Chatbot is at strongly agree level.

quote: The study examined... data were collected through a survey questionnaire administered to 30 English teachers from various private institutions.

Population (university students) is met; domain and outcome are unclear from the abstract but not needed for the decision.

quote: The purpose of this "how-to" guide is to assist pharmacy educators and training program leaders with practical strategies and examples for integrating GenAI into teaching and assessment across pharmacy education.

E6 is the first applicable code in the stated order that is clearly supported by the abstract; the stated order would place E2 first if domain is weighed, but the abstract's clear nature as a non-empirical guide makes E6 the most direct reason.

Exclusion is E3 because there is no comparison group; the case study design also fails the design criterion, but E3 is the first applicable code given the protocol's ordering and the lack of any control condition evident in the abstract.

rationale: The abstract describes a survey of students' use, trust, satisfaction and perceptions of ChatGPT. There is no control group and no experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported. Survey design and perception-only outcomes both fail the protocol. Exclusion code E3 is applied as the first failing criterion in the order given (no control group without generative AI). Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract that the design is a survey without a comparison group.

quote: An explanation layer translated model outputs into structured, teacher-facing natural language linked to key risk indicators and intervention cues.
rationale: The study uses predictive ML models (Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost) on public datasets. The LLM component produces teacher-facing explanations only; learners do not interact with any generative AI tool. No learner-facing generative AI intervention and no control group comparing generative AI use. Excluded under E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI), the first applicable code in order.

quote: The experimental group engaged in Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) Strategy for six weeks, while the control group received traditional classroom instruction.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study appears to meet most criteria: a generative AI strategy (ChatGPT, DALL·E, Codex named) with a control group receiving traditional instruction, a quantitative achievement test (30-item MCQ), and undergraduate participants. Published 2025 in a journal. Not excluded on any criterion with positive evidence. Domain is Biology, which is not in the protocol's STEM list (science is listed, so biology plausibly counts as science; left for fulltext). Design is described as quasi-experimental non-randomized with a control group, which fits the protocol's quasi-experiment inclusion, but the abstract does not give enough to confirm the comparison-group design or effect-size data. Sending to full text to verify design, STEM classification, and whether means/SDs/variance permit SMD computation.

quote: This paper reports an inductive thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with 48 engineering students across year levels at three Australian universities.
rationale: The study is a qualitative thematic analysis of interviews, not an empirical experiment with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion codes, E1 (intervention) is not clearly the first failure. The first applicable code in order is E1 only if the intervention fails; since the intervention is perception-based and no learner-facing GenAI intervention is evaluated, E1 could apply, but the more direct and defining failure is that the study is not an empirical quantitative study (E6, qualitative design). Chosen E6 as the defensible primary code, recognizing that E3 and E5 also fail.

The study is a survey of perceptions of ChatGPT use, with descriptive and comparative statistics. It has no control group and no learning outcome measure; it reports perceptions only. Design is survey, not an experiment or quasi-experiment, so it fails the design and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is not strictly the right fit, but the closest first-applicable code given the protocol's ordering would be E3 for no comparison group. Per the protocol order, E1 does not clearly apply (ChatGPT use is learner-facing in classroom), E2 unclear. The first clearly failing criterion is the absence of a control group (E3). Reporting E3 as the primary code is the more accurate ordering-based choice.

quote: University students were given a structured survey to complete in order to get data on their motivation and level of involvement after utilizing ChatGPT for their statistics assignment.
rationale: The study uses a regression analysis of a survey measuring motivation and engagement after ChatGPT use, with no described control group. The outcomes are affective/perceptual (motivation, engagement), which the protocol does not extract, and there is no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E5 at the abstract stage on positive evidence that the outcome criterion fails; the design also appears to be single-group survey-based, not a controlled comparison.

quote: 44 college students participated in progressive prompt-assisted programming learning.
rationale: Abstract describes generative prompt-assisted programming learning with college students and CT outcomes (met at abstract level). Abstract does not state whether a separate control group without generative AI exists; it reports paired t-tests and microgenetic/sequential analyses, which may suggest a single-group pre-post design (E3). Cannot tell from abstract; full text needed to check for a comparison group.

quote: A qualitative case study methodology was adopted which facilitated an in-depth exploration within a real-world context
rationale: The study is a qualitative case study of course coordinators' views, not an empirical controlled study with a learning outcome. It has no comparison group, no learner-facing GenAI intervention, and no quantitative learning outcome. Coded E6 as not an empirical study in the protocol's sense (qualitative perception study); the first applicable code in order would be E1 (no learner-facing GenAI intervention), but E6 is the design-defining reason, so I report E6.

quote: A quasi-experimental design was conducted with 30 undergraduate students enrolled in an object-oriented programming course
rationale: Programming domain, undergraduate population, and Generative AI intervention are indicated. The abstract describes a quasi-experiment but does not state a separate control group without generative AI; the two tools appear compared against each other, which could trigger E3. Outcomes are described as task performance and perception surveys, so whether a quantitative learning measure exists with usable statistics is unclear. Not excluded at abstract stage; resolve at full text.

quote: This research approach uses a qualitative method with observation, in-depth interviews, and focus group discussions (FGD) as the primary instruments for data collection.
rationale: The study is about literacy (reading and writing), which is non-STEM content, so E2 applies. It also uses a qualitative design with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome, but E2 is the first code in order that applies. Only the abstract was available, and it gives positive evidence of a qualitative, non-comparative design.

quote: Using qualitative Grounded Theory methodology, this study explored how teachers perceive the opportunities, challenges, and implications of integrating GenAI
rationale: Qualitative grounded theory study of teacher perceptions (N=7 interviews). It has no learner-facing GenAI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Participants are teachers, not students. Per the protocol, qualitative designs are excluded; E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in the order given, though the study is empirical, so E6 reflects its non-eligible design. Exclusion is clear at abstract stage because the abstract positively shows a qualitative, teacher-perception design with no quantitative learning outcome.

quote: this paper proposes two frameworks for the uses of generative AI to support academic writing
rationale: The record is a conceptual paper proposing two frameworks for acceptable use of generative AI in academic writing. It is not an empirical study: there is no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It also does not address STEM content. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) is the first code that applies in protocol order, since E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone.

Abstract describes a mixed-methods correlational design (path analysis and latent profile analysis of reflection reports from 181 undergraduates) with no described control group receiving a non-generative-AI condition. Positive evidence that the comparison criterion fails: no comparison group is described, and the design is correlational/qualitative rather than an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Excluded under E3 at abstract stage.

quote: Through a qualitative, multi-site investigation grounded in constructivist and connectivist theories
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative, multi-site investigation with pilot programs and classroom observations, with no control group or quantitative learning outcome. Design is qualitative, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. The protocol lists E3 (no control group without generative AI) as the first applicable code in the ordering, but the design also fails on E5/E6 grounds. Applying the codes in order, E1 does not apply (ChatGPT is learner-facing in classrooms), E2 is unclear, so E3 is the first code that clearly applies on the positive evidence of no comparison group.

quote: Findings indicate that students did not adopt GenAI uncritically or as a substitute for professional judgement.
rationale: The abstract describes a thematic analysis of student reflective entries and perceptions, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Forensic science is arguably not in the protocol's STEM domain list, but the exclusion rests on the design and outcome failures. Excluded at abstract stage on E5 as the first code that applies in the protocol's order for this record (the design also lacks a comparison group).

quote: The study compares results from a pre-AI period (2021–2022) with results from a post-AI period (2023–2025)
rationale: The abstract describes a retrospective pre/post comparison across time periods (pre-AI vs post-AI cohorts) rather than a separate concurrent control group without generative AI. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group and a single-group historical design fails the comparison and design criteria, so E3 applies. Students' actual use of generative AI is also not clearly described as a learner-facing intervention. Domain (programming) and outcome (project scores) appear to be met.

quote: Our pedagogical design based on the SAM model of pedagogical engineering explores the contributions of AGI as a catalyst for learning towards an agile and iterative modelling in favour of the development of the argumentative competence and critical thinking of the writing student.
rationale: The study concerns argumentative writing skills in secondary school writing, a non-STEM content area (language/writing). The abstract gives positive evidence the content is not STEM, so E2 applies. Intervention is a generative AI conversational agent, and the population is secondary students, but no comparison group or quantitative outcome is reported.

quote: A survey involving 44 Computer Science students revealed a diverse range of preferences between original and reframed problems
rationale: The study uses ChatGPT to reframe problems and evaluates them via expert review and a student preference survey. There is no control group comparing learning outcomes, and no quantitative learning measure (expert ratings and preferences are not learning outcomes). Design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). Because the abstract gives positive evidence of no learning outcome, exclusion is appropriate even at abstract stage. Note: the first-applicable ordering would place E1 (intervention is researcher-generated content, not learner-facing) as arguably earlier, but the abstract does not clearly establish that learners did not interact with the tool, so E5 is reported.

quote: Identical course-specific rubrics were provided to an instructor and the LLM.
rationale: The LLM is used for grading of student work, and the abstract describes the instructor and LLM as graders. Learners do not interact with the generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, so the intervention fails E1 (AI used only for grading / not learner-facing). Exclusion under E1 is applied first in the code order; the study also lacks a clear control group of learners without generative AI.

quote: The study involved a pedagogical experiment in which authors described how ChatGPT generates solutions to math problems and what mistakes it makes.
rationale: Abstract describes a learner-facing ChatGPT task (pre-service math teachers checking ChatGPT answers), STEM content, and a pedagogical experiment with a critical thinking outcome. However, the abstract does not state whether a separate control group without generative AI exists, nor whether quantitative data for an SMD are reported. These are unclear rather than positively failing, so the record is passed to full text under rule 2.

quote: This study examines the impact of structured instruction on artificial intelligence (AI) use for improving academic writing in a non-English context.
rationale: The study concerns academic writing in a teacher education program, which is not STEM content (E2). The abstract gives positive evidence of a non-STEM domain, so it is excluded at abstract stage. The repeated-measures design with no clear control group is also a concern, but E2 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: The aim of this study is to determine students' perceptions about the integration of artificial intelligence into science courses.
rationale: The study is a qualitative phenomenology based on semi-structured interviews with 8 secondary students. It reports only perceptions, has no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion order, E1 (intervention not clearly learner-facing generative AI) is not positively shown, and the decisive failure is the design/outcome, so E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible quantitative design) is assigned. Note that the qualitative design more directly fails the Design criterion; E6 is the closest code available for a non-quantitative, non-comparative study.

quote: This study provides empirical insights into how STEM students, use Gen AI in academic design-oriented project work through semi-structured interviews conducted at a UK university.
rationale: The study is a semi-structured interview study, a qualitative design with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the ordered codes, the first applicable code is E3 (no control group without generative AI), since the design has no comparison group at all. Abstract-stage exclusion is justified by positive evidence of the design (interviews only), not by missing information. Could alternatively be read as E5/E6 but E3 is the first in order that clearly applies.
rationale_detail: Interview design is not an eligible design; no comparison group; no quantitative outcome.

quote: A quantitative survey design was employed involving students who had prior experience using GenAI-based tools for academic learning.
rationale: The study is a survey of students' perceptions (usefulness, trust, autonomy) with no experimental or comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the ordered codes, E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract, and E3 would also apply, but the design is a non-empirical-learning survey. Coding as E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's intended sense of a controlled learning evaluation) is the best fit; the survey design also fails the Design and Outcome rows outright. Positive evidence of failure exists for design (survey, no comparison) and outcome (perceptions only), so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

quote: This paper reviews current trends in the integration of AI into smart classrooms within higher education, drawing on recent industry reports, market analyses, and peer-reviewed literature from 2025 and 2026.
rationale: The record is a trend review drawing on industry reports and market analyses, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). No STEM domain or control group is described, but the review nature is sufficient for exclusion. Note that the criteria object above uses fields beyond the schema labels; the decision itself is what matters.

quote: Using a mixed-methods quasi-experimental design, 72 students participated (37 experimental, 35 control).
rationale: At abstract stage, the record shows a GenAI (ChatGPT) learning framework, a control group, a quasi-experimental design with a comparison group, prospective mathematics teachers (higher education), and statistical literacy as the STEM content (mathematics/statistics). Published 2026, so the date criterion is met. Quantitative outcome (test scores) is implied but the abstract does not give statistics for computing an SMD, so data sufficiency is undetermined and must be checked at full text. Abstract is in English, so no language exclusion. Publication type (journal article, Mosharafa Jurnal Pendidikan Matematika) cannot be fully confirmed from the record. No positive evidence of failure, so include for full-text review.

quote: The data analyzed consist of policy texts on the use of GenAI in higher education. The analyses were conducted through thematic coding to identify the main topics, followed by hermeneutic interpretation
rationale: The study is a hermeneutic-phenomenological interpretation of GenAI policy documents. It has no learners interacting with GenAI, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study of the type the protocol requires (E6 applies first in the code order that is relevant; E1 is also arguably unmet since no learner-facing tool is studied, but the design is clearly non-empirical in the qualitative-interpretive sense). Exclusion is supported on positive evidence from the abstract.
rationale_note: Codes checked in order: E1 (no learner-facing GenAI tool evident; policy texts only) would apply first under the strict order. Given the protocol order, the first applicable code is E1, not E6. See note.

quote: Seventy second-grade students participated in a short-term writing program in which ChatGPT was used as a support tool during English writing tasks.
rationale: The content is EFL English writing, which is non-STEM (language learning), so E2 applies first in the code order. The abstract also shows only a single-group pre-post survey design with affective outcomes only (motivation, interest, anxiety, self-efficacy), with no control group, which would independently fail E3 and E5. Exclusion on E2 is the first applicable code.

quote: This paper presents a meta-analysis of literature examining the dark side of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in higher education
rationale: The record is a literature synthesis (described as a meta-analysis but using thematic coding of 300 articles, not a pooled effect-size analysis). It is not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome, so it fails E6. It also has no comparison group or learning outcome measure, and it is not a STEM-specific study. Excluding at E6 as the first applicable code.

quote: This article explores the role of AI and ChatGPT in health sciences and nursing education and the challenges it poses regarding academic integrity
rationale: The abstract describes an exploratory article about ChatGPT and academic integrity in health sciences and nursing education. It reports no empirical design, no comparison group, and no learning outcome. It is not an empirical study. Health sciences and nursing education also falls under the protocol's excluded health professions domain, though E6 is the first applicable code in order on the abstract evidence.

quote: A quantitative survey was conducted with a sample of 125 Tamil-based research students from public and private universities across Malaysia.
rationale: Cross-sectional survey using correlation analysis; no control group and no experimental comparison, so no eligible comparison or experimental design. Outcome is perceived research quality and attitudes (self-report), not a quantitative learning measure. Domain (Tamil-language academic research) is not clearly STEM. Excluded on the first clearly failing criterion: no control group without generative AI (E3). Note the protocol lists E1-E10 in order; E3 is applied here as the design/comparison failure, and the survey design also fails E6 (not an empirical experiment) but E3 is the first code in the order that applies to a design with no comparison group.

quote: Finally, a statistical comparison of the systems' performance was conducted.
rationale: Abstract describes a customised GPT (BSVP) compared with ChatGPT-4 Turbo, two generative AI variants, with no non-generative-AI control group, which fails the comparison criterion (E3). Outcomes are professor ratings of response quality (0-10) on generated answers, not a learner learning outcome, so E5 also plausibly applies. Per the rule to report the first applicable code in order, E3 would be the primary code; however, the abstract is ambiguous on whether any student-learning group exists. Given the abstract shows positive evidence of two-generative-AI comparison, E3 is the more accurate first code. Correcting the code: E3.

quote: This book provides a theoretical framework to allow educators, researchers, and policymakers to better understand computer-generated writing
rationale: The record is a book, not a journal article, so it fails the publication type criterion (E10). It is also a theoretical framework rather than an empirical study with a control group, and its topic is writing education rather than STEM. Under the rule that the first applicable code is reported, E10 is the first code that applies on the evidence given, since the publication-type failure is positive evidence in the record itself.

quote: In this overview, we present three examples for physics lab courses, in which generative AI integrated at different points into existing sequence of inquiry-based learning
rationale: The record is an overview/editorial-style piece presenting examples, not an empirical study. It reports no comparison group, no design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Note the publication venue is a magazine (Europhysics news), which may also be ineligible, but E6 is the first applicable code in order from the protocol's perspective given the abstract.

quote: The research involved 30 science teachers from different-sized schools in Thailand, utilizing surveys, interviews, and document analysis.
rationale: Study surveys science teachers about readiness and adoption factors; no learners interact with a generative AI tool, there is no control group, and no learning outcome is measured. Design is survey/mixed-method descriptive, not an experiment. Participants are in-service teachers, which is outside the population criteria. Positive evidence of failure on intervention, comparison, design and outcome, so excluded at abstract stage. The first applicable code in order is E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI), but the more direct reason is absence of a control group; I report E3 as the design/comparison failure is the clearest positive evidence.

criteria.domain_note: assessment of learning course, not clearly STEM

quote: The purpose of this study was to interpret and describe the perceptions of a group of pedagogy students on the use of ChatGPT as an assistant in a learning experience
rationale: The study is a mixed-methods description of student perceptions in a single course of 26 pedagogy students, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not a controlled comparison, so it fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol sense of an eligible design); the abstract's perception-focused, descriptive, single-group nature is the first failing criterion in code order that applies, with E3 (no control group) being an alternative basis. Coding E6 as first-applicable for a non-experimental perception study is the closest fit available, though E3 would also be defensible since there is no comparison group at all. Abstract also does not clearly indicate STEM content.

The abstract reads as a narrative or conceptual discussion of ChatGPT in computer science education ("This paper explores the role...", "The paper concludes..."). It gives no description of an empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative outcome. Positive evidence of a non-empirical paper is present, so it is excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Design, comparison, and outcome are not reported in the abstract.

Abstract is missing from the index; only the title and venue are available. The title indicates middle school STEM education and students' interactions with AI (likely generative, given prompt engineering skills), but it suggests a correlational/process-focused study (shaping collaboration via dispositions and skills), so a control group, quantitative learning outcome, and design cannot be confirmed. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of exclusion, so the record is held as unsure for full-text review.

criteria.quote: Using a qualitative research design, 31 undergraduate students aged 18~23 with diverse majors and sports backgrounds were selected as subjects.
criteria.rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative design using questionnaires, semi-structured interviews, and text mining, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Sports skill learning is also not clearly STEM. The earliest positive failure is the design: it is qualitative, not an experimental or quasi-experimental study with a comparison group. Per the exclusion order, E1 (intervention) does not clearly fail, E2 is doubtful, so E3 would also apply, but the qualitative non-empirical-quantitative design is best captured as E6 because the study is not a comparative empirical quantitative study. Coding chosen: E6 because the design is qualitative and reports no learning measure.

quote: Using a qualitative research design, 31 undergraduate students aged 18~23 with diverse majors and sports backgrounds were selected as subjects.
rationale: Qualitative design (questionnaires, interviews, text mining) with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; sports skill learning is not STEM. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical quantitative study). Stated positively in abstract, so exclusion is justified at abstract stage.

quote: Through a combination of quantitative survey data and qualitative open-ended responses collected via Google Forms
rationale: The abstract describes a survey of engineering students' perceptions and ethical views of GAI use, with no experimental or control group and no learning outcome measured. Design is survey-based, and outcomes are perceptions only. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). Note that E5 is listed after E1-E4; the design failure (no comparison group, E3 by criterion) is also present, but the study's core failure is the absence of any learning outcome. Under the abstract-stage rule, this is positive evidence of failure on the outcome and design.

Abstract describes a conceptual framework plus an "exemplary case study" of a chemistry STEM project with three layers, including LLM (ChatGPT) use. No control group, comparison design, or quantitative learning outcome is reported; the study appears to be a conceptual/case description rather than an empirical experiment. Positive evidence that the design fails (no comparison group, case study) supports exclusion. Coded E6 as not an empirical study, though the design-based exclusion (no control group) is also a plausible reading; the abstract gives no comparison group.

quote: The responses of each student to the five questions were graded by six different Bing Chat accounts and six faculty members.
rationale: Bing Chat is used by faculty/researchers to grade student answers, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. Students only wrote answers; the AI is used for grading only, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion code E1 applies as the first failing criterion. The study also does not measure a learning outcome (grading consistency is the outcome), which would be E5 but E1 comes first.

quote: The results of this study show that this course not only facilitates students' mastery and application of chemistry knowledge but also effectively enhances students' inquiry and discussion skills
rationale: Abstract describes a high school chemistry course that introduces generative AI (GAI) technology, so the intervention may qualify, but the abstract does not state whether a control group exists or the study design. It reports learning outcomes (mastery of chemistry knowledge, inquiry skills) but gives no statistics. Also the abstract mentions self-efficacy and identity (affective outcomes, which are not extracted). No positive evidence of a failed criterion, so advance to full text to check design, control group, GAI role for learners, and data.

quote: The breakthrough in generative artificial intelligence (AI) has unlocked new possibilities for higher education.
rationale: The study builds a generative-AI chatbot (PMTutor) for project management training. Project management is not a STEM domain under the protocol (science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, data science), so E2 applies. The abstract also emphasises usability and feedback rather than a controlled comparison with a learning outcome, but the domain failure alone is sufficient for exclusion.

quote: Empirical analysis indicates that the effects of AI-assisted assessment are selective.
rationale: Secondary school mathematics, empirical evaluation with comparisons (Mann-Whitney U, Cohen's d) suggest a comparison against traditional assessment. However, the abstract is focused on automated assessment by ChatGPT integrated into a platform; it is unclear whether learners directly interact with a generative AI tool (the ChatGPT component may be teacher/system-facing for assessment), and it is unclear whether the comparison is a true control group with statistics sufficient for SMD. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so this is unsure for fulltext review of intervention, design, and outcome details. Published 2026, so date criterion met; journal article per venue. Not excluded at abstract stage.

quote: Students demonstrated the ability to differentiate quality in AI-assisted writing and provided structured evaluations of their peers’ work.
rationale: Abstract reports a peer-assessment study with comparative judgment and LCT analysis of students' perceptions; no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome is described. Domain is Academic English/professional communication, not clearly STEM despite engineering students. Excluded under E5 as the abstract gives positive evidence that no quantitative learning outcome is measured (findings are evaluations and perceptions). Note that E3 (no control group) could also apply; E5 is reported as the first applicable code in the order given only on the basis of the outcome evidence available.

quote: This paper presents the architecture and workflow of SATGPT, showcases its performance through flood map examples, and discusses the advantages, limitations, and future directions
rationale: The paper presents a tool architecture and illustrative flood map examples, with no learner population, control group, or quantitative learning outcome described. It is a tool/system description rather than a controlled learning study, so it fails the outcome and design criteria on positive evidence. Coded E5 as the first failing criterion with clear evidence in the abstract; the E1 (learner-facing) and E4 (population) checks are not clearly failed from the abstract alone. The developed course is mentioned but no learner outcome data are reported.

quote: In this commentary, we argue that many current GenAI applications conflate learning with performance and feedback
rationale: The record is a commentary (argumentative piece), not an empirical study. It reports no experiment, comparison group, or quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order after E1 and E2 which do not clearly apply at abstract stage.

The abstract describes a convergent mixed-methods study using a descriptive survey and semi-structured interviews on student attitudes and perceived impact on critical thinking. It reports no separate control group, no experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning measure; outcomes are perceptions. Exclusion at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the first applicable code in order that is supported by positive evidence; the design also lacks a comparison group (E3), but E5 is listed earlier in the code order only after E1-E4 are checked, and E3 would apply first. Note: per protocol order, the first applicable code is E3 because no control group is described. Since the protocol requires the first applicable code in order, the code is E3.

quote: Rather than evaluating effectiveness, this review provides an overview of research trends, identifies concentrations and gaps in the literature
rationale: This is a systematic mapping review of 30 studies, not an empirical intervention study. The abstract states it does not evaluate effectiveness. Under the protocol this is not an empirical study, so E6 applies.

criteria.criteria_note: Descriptive survey of teachers; no control group or learner outcome

quote: This study examined elementary school teachers’ perceptions of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of teachers' perceptions, with no learner interaction with GenAI, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence shows it is a survey design (non-empirical-experimental), so E6 applies as the first failing code given the design. Note that strictly, the population (in-service teachers) and outcome (perceptions only) also fail, but the design failure is the primary issue; E4 would apply on population as well, but E6 is the most direct since the study is a survey of perceptions rather than an intervention study.

Abstract describes a qualitative study of participant feedback (in-class discussions, annotated tasks, final survey) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Domain is EFL academic writing, not STEM content, and the abstract does not show a comparison. Exclusion code E3 is used as the first applicable code under the order given, since there is no control group without generative AI. Hard to say whether E2 would be preferred, but E3 is the first clear failure in the code order that is supported by the abstract (qualitative design, no comparison group).

quote: The study examined the websites of twelve universities in the UK and other English-speaking countries to retrieve documents providing guidance to students on the use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
rationale: The study is a document analysis of university website guidance on ethics, not an experiment with a control group or a learning outcome. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. E6 applies as the first code in order that fits: it is not an empirical intervention study. Note that E1 (intervention not learner-facing) would also plausibly apply; I chose E6 as the more fundamental failure of the design, but the record is clearly ineligible either way.

quote: This study investigates the use of ChatGPT by students as foreign language (EFL) learners in doing English homework
rationale: Content is English as a foreign language, which is non-STEM (language learning), so E2 applies and is the first failing code in order. The study is also a questionnaire-based TAM survey with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (perceptions and usage only), which would fail E3 and E5 as well, but E2 is reported as the first applicable code.
rationale_note: Order check: E1 does not apply (ChatGPT is learner-facing generative AI). E2 applies first.

quote: The research employed a qualitative paradigm with a phenomenological-hermeneutical design.
rationale: The study is a qualitative, questionnaire-based perception study of faculty (teachers), not an experimental study with a control group or a learner-level quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparison design eligible under the protocol. Population is also teachers rather than students, which fails E4 as well, but the primary failure is design/empirical-study status (E6) with no control group or quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E6 applied as the first applicable code is a judgement call; the record contains positive evidence of a qualitative design, and it is a non-experimental study.

quote: This study aimed to investigate the perceptions, experiences, and ethical awareness of undergraduate Speech and Language Therapy (SLT) students in Türkiye
rationale: Cross-sectional survey of perceptions with no control group, no learning outcome measured, and speech and language therapy is a health professions domain, not STEM. Per the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E1 would not apply because ChatGPT is learner-used, so the first applicable code is E5 (no quantitative learning outcome; only perceptions and usage reported). Design criterion also fails (survey). Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence.

Abstract describes an experiment on GenAI use in programming learning, with learning outcomes. Abstract does not state whether there is a control group without GenAI (comparison unclear), the learner population level (unclear), or whether the outcome is quantitative and provides SMD-computable data (unclear). No positive evidence of exclusion at abstract stage, so unsure; resolve at full text.

quote: this paper proposes a comprehensive framework for the responsible and ethical application of Gen-AI in science education
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/framework paper on generative AI in science education. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion is based on positive evidence that the paper is non-empirical.

quote: Overall, the conference papers revealed that generative AI had not changed everything, even though it was clear that much remains to be learned
rationale: The record is an editorial/commentary piece (Modern Language Journal "this issue" framing, discussion of prior conversations and a conference overview) rather than an empirical study. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is also a language-learning/applied linguistics commentary, not STEM content. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order that is supported by the text; the record is not an empirical study regardless of the other criteria.
rationale_note: Code E6 is the first applicable code, as the record is not empirical. Domain (language learning, not STEM) would also fail but E2 precedes nothing relevant; per code order E1 and E2 were considered first: intervention is not a specific learner-facing tool evaluation and content is language learning, which is non-STEM (E2). Under strict order of codes, E2 precedes E6.

quote: students were assigned to experimental groups (allowed to use ChatGPT) or control groups (restricted to traditional, non-GenAI resources)
rationale: At abstract stage, the study appears to compare ChatGPT-using students against a control group without GenAI, with higher education students and a quantitative performance outcome. Intervention and population look met. Domain is mixed: it includes engineering and informatics/computer systems courses, but also childhood disorders, which is not STEM, so the STEM status of the analysed content is unclear. Design (assignment method, whether it is a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison) and the data needed for an SMD are not stated. No positive evidence of an exclusion, so advance to full text.

quote: A one-group repeated measures quasi-experimental design was applied to 15 undergraduate social welfare students.
rationale: The study uses a single-group repeated measures design with no separate control group that avoids generative AI, so E3 applies. The domain is also not STEM (motivational interviewing training for social work students), but E3 is the first applicable code in protocol order only if E2 does not come first; since the protocol says to report the first code in order from E1, E2 would be checked before E3. Content is motivational interviewing for social work, which is not science, mathematics, engineering, computer science, or data science, so E2 is the first applicable code and is reported here.

quote: Few studies have explored using LLMs to generate data for qualitative engineering education research.
rationale: The study uses ChatGPT to generate research data for qualitative analysis, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. Participants are researchers generating data, not learners interacting with AI. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. The abstract gives positive evidence that the intervention criterion fails (E1), which is the first applicable code in order.

The abstract describes an assessment of ChatGPT-4 solving physics problems and comparing its performance with student performance. The generative AI is evaluated as a problem solver, not used by learners as part of a learning activity, so the intervention criterion is not met (E1). There is no indication of a control group receiving instruction without generative AI, and the design appears to be a performance benchmark rather than a randomized or quasi-experiment. Positive evidence of failure exists on intervention, so the decision is exclude with code E1 as the first applicable code.

quote: We first validated the EduDesignEval framework through metric definitions and demonstrated its utility by employing ten publicly available LLM models
rationale: The study proposes an evaluation framework for LLM-generated educational content and compares LLMs on text generation and classification. No learners interact with the generative AI as part of a learning activity, so the intervention is not learner-facing (E1). No control group or learning outcome is described either.

quote: The empirical part of the study consisted of the results of a survey of 194 students from three leading universities in the South Kazakhstan region, aimed at studying the perception and experience of using AI in the process of studying chemistry.
rationale: Abstract describes a systematic literature analysis plus a student survey on perceptions and experience. No comparison group, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions only. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). Design also lacks a comparison group, but the first applicable code in order is E3 for no control group... Per protocol order, E3 precedes E5 in code order, so the strictly first applicable code is E3. Final code given the protocol's ordering is E3.

Abstract describes a conceptual framing and a "proposed quantitative model" of prompt engineering literacy's influence on English communication, technical writing, and problem-solving among engineering students. It does not describe a learner-facing generative AI intervention with a control group, nor an experimental or quasi-experimental design. Domain is ambiguous (English language teaching for engineering students, which is not clearly STEM content). Nothing in the abstract gives positive evidence of a failed criterion, so the record is held for full-text review to check design, comparison, and whether the outcomes are quantitative learning measures.

quote: The sample group consisted of 18 senior students enrolled in the "Computer and Social Media Use" course at the University of the Third Age
rationale: The topic is awareness of call center scams, a consumer-safety/digital literacy subject, not a STEM content domain. The study also reports a single group with no control group (pre-post style awareness assessment), and the outcome is awareness/opinion rather than a clear quantitative learning measure. Exclusion under E2 (first applicable code in order is E1 only if the AI intervention is not learner-facing, which is unclear here; the domain failure is the clearest positive evidence).

quote: The framework enables patients to perform both predefined and non-predefined operation tasks with hand exoskeletons
rationale: The study concerns LLM-based control of a hand exoskeleton for patients with motor impairment, not learners in a learning activity. Participants are patients, not K-12 or higher education students, and the content is not STEM learning. Excluded at the abstract stage on population (E4), which is positive evidence from the abstract. The intervention is an LLM control framework rather than a learner-facing learning tool, so E1 could also apply, but the population failure is clear and the protocol asks for the first applicable code in order; E1 precedes E4 in order, so E1 is arguably the first code. Given the order rule, the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI for learning, which is E1.

quote: Students reported increased efficiency in completing tasks, citing improved grammar, idea generation, and understanding of complex subjects.
rationale: The abstract describes a usage and perception survey of Filipino engineering undergraduates. It reports only perceptions and self-reported efficiency, with no control group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded at E5 as the first applicable code (E3 for missing control would also apply, but the no-outcome failure is the clearest positive evidence; the design is clearly non-experimental). Given the rule to exclude only on positive evidence, the absence of any comparison group and the survey-based perception outcomes are explicit in the abstract.

quote: we conducted a controlled experiment with 20 students learning a programming language
rationale: Abstract describes an LLM-based personalized programming learning system (generative AI, learner-facing) with programming as STEM content, and a controlled experiment with 20 students. Control group composition, outcome measures, and effect-size data are not stated in the abstract, so eligibility on comparison, design, outcome and data cannot be confirmed. Not excluded at abstract stage; advance to full text to check the control condition and quantitative learning outcome.

quote: This study analyzed the factors influencing their use of GAI by applying the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT)
rationale: The study is a PLS-SEM survey of 331 college students on factors predicting intention and use of generative AI in math learning. It has no control group receiving a non-generative-AI condition and no learning outcome measure; it is correlational/survey research with perception and usage constructs only. Excluded under E3 (no control group) as the first applicable code in protocol order; E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) and E6 (not an empirical intervention study) would also apply. Under the rule to report only the first applicable code, E3 is given. Abstract stage, so the decision is exclude based on positive evidence that comparison and outcome criteria fail.

quote: Through quantitative analysis of university students' survey responses, three distinct clusters of GenAI users' re indentified
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of 226 university students about GenAI adoption, ethical concerns and perceptions. It has no comparison group, no intervention, and no learning outcome measure, so it is not an empirical experiment meeting the design criteria. Survey and perception-only designs are excluded. Under the ordered codes, E1 (intervention not learner-facing GenAI) could also be argued since no learner interaction in a learning activity is described, but the primary reason is that this is a survey-based, non-experimental study (E6 as not an empirical study meeting eligibility design). Exclusion is based on positive evidence from the abstract.

quote: the absence of a non-scaffolded control precludes causal attribution
rationale: The cross-cohort task-effectiveness study reports large pre-to-post gains but explicitly lacks a non-scaffolded control group, so it is a single-group pre-post design without a comparison group (E3). The perception and interaction-pattern studies are not learning-outcome comparisons (perceptions/usage only). No eligible comparison group is reported. Excluded under E3 as the first applicable code in order for the learning-outcome evidence presented.

quote: This research employed an exploratory study design with a regular course setting, and there were no experimental treatments involved.
rationale: The abstract states an exploratory correlational design in a regular course with no experimental treatment, so there is no control group without generative AI. The design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Exclusion code E3 applies (no control group without generative AI). Note that E3 is the first applicable code in protocol order only if no earlier code applies; the intervention and domain are not clearly resolved from the abstract, but the comparison failure is positive evidence and is sufficient for exclusion.

criteria.population_note: preservice teachers in math methods courses

quote: This is a practitioner reflection described three uses of AI chatbots in two mathematics methods course for middle grades and elementary education majors.
rationale: The abstract describes a practitioner reflection, not an empirical study. It reports no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's ordering, E6 (not an empirical study) is the first code that applies. Exclusion is positive evidence based on the abstract's own description of the piece.

quote: Data was collected from six fifth-grade students, including worksheets, AI-student chat logs, observation notes, interview transcripts, and student reflection essays.
rationale: Six fifth-grade students interacting with generative AI, with qualitative data sources (chat logs, observation notes, interviews, reflections) and no mention of a control group or quantitative learning outcome. The abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group (single-group, qualitative case-style study), so E3 applies. Note that the design also appears qualitative, which would fall under E5/E6 at a fuller review.

quote: The study explored the Generative AI tool usage of 29 in-service EFL teachers who were currently following a Master of TESOL program in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. Data were collected via an online questionnaire.
rationale: Survey-based descriptive study of usage and perceptions of 29 EFL teachers. No control group, no quantitative learning outcome, not STEM (language teaching), and population is in-service teachers. Primary exclusion is E6 (not an empirical experimental study; survey design), as it is a survey without an intervention comparison. Criteria marked not_met reflect positive evidence from the abstract; the first applicable code in protocol order is E1 only if intervention is judged non-learner-facing, which is unclear, so E6 is applied as the design is a survey rather than an eligible empirical comparison.

quote: Methods From September 2024 to February 2025, we conducted a cross-sectional survey among Bachelor and Master students.
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional survey of medical informatics students on GenAI usage, competencies, and attitudes. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group, so the comparison and design criteria fail. There is no quantitative learning outcome; the measures are self-assessed competencies and perceptions. Per the exclusion-code order, E1 (intervention) is not clearly failed, but the design fails. Under the stated order, the first applicable code would be E1 only if intervention failed; since it is a survey of usage, E3 (no control group) is the most direct failing criterion and is reported here. Abstract-stage exclusion is supported by the positive evidence of a cross-sectional survey design with no comparison group.

criteria.comparison_note: Abstract describes AES with ChatGPT vs AES without ChatGPT; a control with a non-generative-AI condition is implied but not fully explicit.

quote: The results indicated that the AES with ChatGPT led to better outcomes and higher learning satisfaction than the AES without ChatGPT.
rationale:
Abstract reports a controlled experiment teaching Java programming (STEM) with 54 first-year undergraduates, comparing an AES with ChatGPT to an AES without ChatGPT, with learning outcomes measured. The comparison group (AES without ChatGPT) appears to lack generative AI, so E3 is not clearly triggered. Whether the ChatGPT component is learner-facing and whether the design is a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison, and whether the data allow an SMD, cannot be determined from the abstract. Advance to full text to verify the design, intervention, and effect-size data.</rationale>

decision_note: Abstract describes a multi-component framework with R² attendance association, multi-semester tracking, and hardware speedup; no separate control group without generative AI is evident.
quote: Analysis across 14 semesters shows that underperforming students were found to benefit most from attending score clarification sessions, a relationship validated by an R² value of 0.83
rationale: The abstract describes a framework with observational analysis across semesters and hardware benchmarks (3.41× speedup vs gzip), not a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison with a control group lacking generative AI. No comparison group is mentioned. Positive evidence of no control group supports E3. However, at abstract stage the rule says exclude only on positive evidence; the abstract reports an R² association and no control condition, which is fairly clear evidence of design failure. Also the record is a journal-type venue with a non-STEM-oriented title, but that is not decisive.

criteria.criteria_note: Commentary/editorial on AI in medical education; no experiment

quote: Artificial intelligence (AI) is fast getting integrated into clinical medicine and has received a lot of attention recently
rationale: The record is a commentary/viewpoint arguing for introducing AI into undergraduate medical curricula, citing the Gartner cycle. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no learning outcome data. It is not an empirical study (E6). Domain is also health professions education, which is outside the STEM scope, but E6 is the first applicable code under the stated order of checking E1 through E10 only where they apply; E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract alone, so E6 is reported as the primary reason.

quote: A questionnaire survey was conducted among 758 undergraduates enrolled in online mathematics courses
rationale: The abstract describes a cross-sectional questionnaire survey with structural equation modeling of perceived teacher support, AI literacy, and cognitive tool use. This is a correlational/survey design with no experimental or quasi-experimental comparison group, so it fails the design and comparison criteria. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is applied as the first failing criterion available in the ordered list; the outcome is a self-reported learning power scale, not a clearly quantitative learning measure. Population (undergraduates) is met.

quote: The authors implemented the GAI innovation in the graduate-level "Teaching 100" course (enrollment n = 27) at Harvard Medical School
rationale: Participants are health professions educators (in-service faculty development), not K-12 or higher education students in STEM, and the domain is health professions education, which is excluded. The study is also a single-group pre-post design with no control group (E3 would also apply), but the first applicable code in order is E4 because the population is not students. Abstract gives positive evidence of population failure, so excluded.

quote: This manuscript proposes a new framework, critical trust, to help university students balance trust and mistrust in the validity of information in GenAI outputs.
rationale: The record is a conceptual/framework manuscript that proposes a framework and suggests a future scale to be developed. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). The abstract gives positive evidence that the design is not an experiment; E6 is the first applicable code in the order given, since E1 through E5 cannot be confirmed as failing from the abstract alone and E6 is the clearest failure.

quote: Three approaches-machine learning (ML), a pre-trained language model (BERT), and a large language model (LLM)-were applied to 2,080 peer feedback data
rationale: The study uses AI models (ML, BERT, LLM) to automatically classify peer feedback levels against human raters. The AI is used for classification/assessment of text, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. No control group of learners using generative AI versus a comparison condition is described, and no learning outcome is measured. Excluded under E1 (intervention is not learner-facing generative AI), the first applicable code in order.

The abstract describes a study of parents' views and attitudes about AI chatbots in high school STEM education. It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Parents' attitudes are not a learning outcome and the study is not a learner-facing intervention. Excluding on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), which is the clearest positive failure visible in the abstract. Design also appears to be a perspective/survey-type study, which would fail the design criterion as well.

quote: This study used a survey method through a questionnaire to obtain data.
rationale: The study is a questionnaire-based survey of student perceptions about ChatGPT as teaching material. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome (only motivation perceptions), and the content is Pancasila and citizenship education, which is not STEM. The primary failing is that it is not an empirical comparative study; it is a survey design, so E6 is the first applicable code in the ordering that fits best. Under strict order E2 (non-STEM) would be checked first and also applies; however, the abstract clearly shows a non-STEM course, so E2 is the first applicable code in the protocol order.
decision_note: Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: Effectiveness was examined through a single-group pretest–posttest design in one Civic Education class.
rationale: The study uses a single-group pretest-posttest design with no control group that avoids generative AI, which fails the comparison and design criteria (E3). Civic Education is also a social-science topic rather than STEM, but the first applicable code in order is E1/E2 checks: intervention is learner-facing generative AI (met), so E2 would apply before E3 on the protocol's order. Content is civic education, not science, mathematics, engineering, computing, or data science, so E2 is the first code that applies. The exclusion is recorded as E2 for that reason.

quote: A structured questionnaire was administered to 184 design students aged 18 to 25 in Kerala
rationale: The study is a mixed-methods survey with descriptive statistics and qualitative interviews/focus group, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (only perceptions and usage). Exclusion uses E3 as the first applicable code in order (no comparison group without GenAI); E5 and E6 also apply, but E3 is the first that fits the protocol order. Design students' domain is not clearly STEM, which is noted as unclear.

Abstract describes a feasibility/technical evaluation of an open-source LLM generating feedback. It reports classification accuracy of the LLM against GPT-4o and quality ratings of feedback, with no separate control group of learners without generative AI and no learning outcome measured on students. Positive evidence of missing comparison group and learning outcome supports exclusion under E3 (no control group without generative AI); E5 would also apply, so E3 is the first applicable code in the listed order only if the comparison failure is ranked first. Given the protocol order, the comparison failure is cited first.

quote: This study reviews research from 2014 to 2024, examining AI's impact on science education. It proposes a structured framework for integrating AI
rationale: The record is a review and framework proposal, not an empirical study. It reports no controlled comparison or quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first applicable code in order that the abstract supports.

quote: This study asks whether generative AI can be adopted in Japanese grammar education
rationale: Content is Japanese grammar (language learning), which is non-STEM, so E2 applies. The study also evaluates output quality of three commercial models on probe items rather than a learner-facing intervention with a control group, with no quantitative learning outcome from learners, so E1/E3/E5 are also doubtful. E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order that the abstract clearly supports.

The title indicates a technology acceptance model study of high school students' acceptance of GenAI for physics learning. Acceptance/attitude constructs are perceptions, not quantitative learning outcomes, so the study appears to fail the outcome criterion. No abstract is available in the index, but the title alone gives positive evidence that the outcome is perceptual (TAM constructs), which is sufficient for exclusion under E5.</rationale>
