quote: This article describes three approaches to differentiation science educators can take to reap the benefits of GenAI tools when addressing the needs of multiple, diverse learners in middle-grade science classrooms.
rationale: The record is a practitioner-oriented article describing approaches to differentiation using UDL principles. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Exclusion is positive at the abstract stage because the abstract describes a conceptual/practice piece rather than a study with data.

quote: a chatbot providing adaptive, contextualised advice and feedback, supported by Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI)
rationale: At abstract stage, the study is a 2x2 experimental design with 160 seventh-grade students in a science DGBL context. A GenAI-supported chatbot is a learner-facing intervention, and the four groups include groups without GenAI access, so a control comparison appears present. The outcome is science learning, which is quantitative (F statistics reported). No positive evidence of failure on any criterion. Journal article per venue. Data sufficiency for SMD and full-text details (language, publication type) to be confirmed at full text.

This is a survey study (PLS-SEM on 251 questionnaire responses) of adoption intentions using UTAUT. There is no learning outcome, no control group, and no intervention in which learners use a GAI tool as part of a learning activity. Exclusion is on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), since the only measures are perceptions and intentions. Because the design is a survey, E6 (not an empirical study) would also be defensible, but the protocol's first-applicable ordering places E5 earlier only in terms of the listed codes; the core failure is the absence of a learning outcome. Abstract evidence is clear enough to exclude.

quote: Metacognitive analysis showed improvements in conditional knowledge (33%-50%), planning (76%-88%), and depuration (76%-88%).
rationale: Abstract describes a generative AI assistant (RAG-supported) in a mobile game-based anatomy app with undergraduates, but reports no control group; outcomes are pre/post questionnaires and logs in what appears to be a single-group design, with improvements in metacognitive measures reported as percentages. No positive evidence of a separate non-generative-AI comparison group, so E3 applies. Anatomy is also arguably health professions education, which would be a further concern at full text (E2 would be considered first only if clearly non-STEM; kept as E3 per abstract evidence).

quote: This study investigates the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) writing tools, particularly ChatGPT, on the writing skills of English as a Second Language (ESL) students in Pakistani universities.
rationale: Content is ESL writing, which is language learning and non-STEM, so E2 applies. The design is a questionnaire-based correlation/regression study with no control group described, so it also appears not to meet the design and comparison criteria. Excluding on the first applicable code, E2.

quote: This quantitative study examines ChatGPT usage intensity, AI dependency, content understanding, interaction quality, and student happiness using structural models.
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational/structural-model study of ChatGPT usage intensity and perceptions in online discussions. It reports no separate control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails (E3). Outcomes are interaction quality and satisfaction (perception-based), with no clear quantitative learning measure, and the design is correlational rather than experimental. Using the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E1 does not apply (ChatGPT is learner-facing), so E3 is the first failing criterion reported here. Domain (mechatronics) is plausibly STEM but not stated explicitly.

quote: The experimental group received four weeks of teacher-guided ChatGPT-assisted inquiry learning, while the control group received conventional instruction.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study appears to meet all criteria: ChatGPT-assisted inquiry learning by fifth-grade students (generative AI, learner-facing), a control group receiving conventional instruction, a quasi-experimental design with comparison group, science content, and a critical thinking outcome measured after the intervention. Means and SDs are reported, so an SMD is computable. Publication type (journal vs. other) and full-text language are not verifiable from the abstract, so they are left for full-text review. Note the criteria field includes keys beyond the schema's listed values; the decision itself is what matters.

quote: LLMs embedded as adaptive scaffolding in one experimental condition. A total of 120 Grade 6 students from rural schools were randomly assigned at the class level to three conditions
rationale: Abstract stage: LLM-embedded scaffolding is learner-facing generative AI; comparison groups without AI (4C/ID without AI, traditional instruction) exist; randomized class-level assignment; Grade 6 students; Earth systems STEM content; CPS performance tasks and conceptual quizzes are quantitative learning outcomes. Journal article in 2026 with Interactive Learning Environments venue. Data sufficiency for SMD cannot be confirmed from abstract, but no positive evidence of failure, so include.

quote: The purpose of this study was to explore the perceptions of university students who used ChatGPT for English learning
rationale: The study concerns English language learning, which is non-STEM content (protocol Domain exclusion). It is also a perception-based mixed-methods study with no evident control group, so it would fail on design/comparison and outcome as well. The first applicable code in order is E2, since the content check comes before the comparison and design checks.

quote: Three nursing faculty members independently reviewed 126 AI-generated responses using a 5-point scale based on clarity, relevance, and educational appropriateness.
rationale: Nursing reflective record writing is health professions education, not STEM, so E2 applies first in the code order. The abstract also shows no control group, no learner-facing study (faculty rated simulated outputs), and no quantitative learning outcome; those would be further failures (E1/E3/E5) but E2 is the first applicable code. Positive evidence of the domain failure is clear from the abstract.

quote: A systematic scoping review was conducted, synthesizing foundational literature to establish a robust proof-of-concept.
rationale: The record is a systematic scoping review and conceptual framework proposal, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It fails the design and outcome criteria, and E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in order that fits. Domain is agricultural education, which is not clearly STEM. Injection not suspected.

quote: Adopting a qualitative research design, the study links iterative prompt engineering with a systematic thematic analysis of AI-generated outputs.
rationale: Abstract describes a qualitative design with prompt engineering and thematic analysis of AI outputs, with pilot feedback from middle school students. There is no control group without generative AI and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E3 is the first applicable code in the order given, since the lack of a comparison group is the first failing criterion in the protocol order that applies. Positive evidence of a qualitative design and no comparison group supports exclusion at the abstract stage.

The course is "Professional Communication in the Field" for sport master's students. Its content is professional communication (communicative competence), not a STEM discipline such as science, mathematics, engineering, computer science, or data science. The protocol's domain criterion is not met on positive evidence in the abstract, so the record is excluded under E2. ChatGPT is listed among tools, but the domain exclusion applies first in code order. Population (master's students) is consistent with eligibility. Design and control group are not clearly described in the abstract.

quote: Empirical studies across 42 institutions confirm that the optimized framework elevates:STEM problem-solving accuracy to >90% (Δ+21.8% vs. generic models)
rationale: The abstract describes DeepSeek (an LLM) used in K-12 to tertiary settings with STEM problem-solving outcomes, so intervention, population, and domain do not show failure. However, the comparison is ambiguous: the abstract references "generic models" and a "mixed-methods approach (technical benchmarking + empirical field trials)" without clearly stating a control group without generative AI. The design is unclear, and the reported effects (accuracy, retention, SUS adoption) may include non-learning or benchmark measures. Abstract does not give positive evidence of a failed criterion, so advance to full text to check comparison group, design, and whether outcomes are learning measures with extractable statistics.

quote: Using interpretive description, we conducted focus group interviews with undergraduate nursing students.
rationale: The study is a qualitative focus-group interview study examining student perspectives. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and is not an experimental design. Nursing is a health profession, which the protocol excludes from the STEM domain. The qualitative design is not an empirical study that meets the protocol's design criteria, so E6 applies as the first code in order that fits (the protocol's first-applicable ordering starts with E1 for intervention, but the abstract gives no learner-facing AI intervention evaluated, so E6 is the clearest positive failure reflecting a non-experimental qualitative design).

quote: We present a scaffolded approach using centralized GenAI support and a step-by-step guide for developing novel experiments and supporting faculty GenAI literacy.
rationale: The abstract describes a course design and instructional guide ("we present a scaffolded approach... step-by-step guide") with no comparison group, no described experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. This reads as an educator experience/practice report rather than an empirical study. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study) is the first code that applies on the abstract's positive evidence. No injection detected.

criteria.comparison_note: No control group described in abstract; study appears to be a single-cohort TTF-TAM/SEM study with 21 students

quote: The research was conducted with 21 final‐year undergraduate students who used GenAI tools such as ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Gemini, and Tabnine to develop a full‐stack application
rationale: Generative AI use by undergraduates in software engineering (STEM, higher education) is met. However, the abstract describes a single group of 21 students analyzed with SEM on perceptions (satisfaction, readiness, alignment) and a vaguely described learning outcome; there is no mention of a control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion is possibly failed. Abstract does not give positive evidence of a failed criterion, so retain as unsure for full-text check of whether a comparison group exists and whether a quantitative learning measure with SMD-computable statistics is reported.

quote: covers diverse areas such as English as a Second Language (ESL), English as a Foreign Language (EFL), foreign language learning
rationale: The record describes an edited book (a book description/review), not an empirical study. It covers language education, which is non-STEM (domain exclusion applies too), but the protocol's exclusion code order places E1 and E2 before E6. Under the order, the first applicable code is E1 only if the intervention is clearly not learner-facing generative AI, which the abstract does not establish; E2 is positively evidenced by language-education content (ESL/EFL/foreign language). Since the protocol requires the first applicable code in order, E2 would be the first applicable code with positive evidence. Therefore the correct code is E2, not E6. Note: the record is a book description, so it is also not an empirical study (E6), but E2 precedes E6 in the ordering.

Abstract gives no positive evidence of a failing criterion. It describes a ChatGPT-based flipped interactive learning model versus a conventional flipped learning control group (non-generative-AI) in an undergraduate programming course (STEM), with a semi-experimental design comparing groups of 36 and 38 students and a programming skills outcome. Journal article, 2024. Data sufficiency for SMD and full-text language cannot be judged from the abstract, so these are left for fulltext.

quote: A sample of 616 students from a key high school in northern China was randomly assigned to an experimental group (LLM personalized instruction, n=308) or a control group (traditional instruction, n=308).
rationale: At abstract stage, the study appears to be a randomized comparison of LLM-based instruction versus traditional instruction in high school computer science, with reported performance gains (t-tests). Outcome quantitative data and SMD computability cannot be confirmed from the abstract, but no positive evidence of failure is present, so per rule 2 it is advanced to full text. Journal venue listed as Individual Differences in Language Education; publication type and full-text details should be checked at full text.

quote: The empirical study was conducted at Derzhavin Tambov State University and included interaction with ChatGPT in order to compile on its basis fragments of research work
rationale: Abstract describes an empirical test of ChatGPT use in research writing with no control group or comparison condition, so the comparison criterion fails (E3). The study is also a qualitative-style exploration of outputs rather than a comparative design, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported (E5 would also apply, but E3 is the first applicable code in order). Domain is foreign-language teaching methods, which is non-STEM (E2) and would also apply; under the order rule E2 comes before E3, so the first applicable code is E2. Correcting: the first applicable code in order is E2.

Abstract describes a correlational survey of 307 graduate teacher education students (perceptions, motivation, research attitudes) with descriptive statistics and Pearson's r. There is no control group without generative AI, no experimental or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; attitudes and perceptions are affective and not extracted. Exclusion code E3 (no control group) is the first code that clearly applies; the design also fails and the outcome is not a learning measure.

quote: Qualitative findings were generated from an anonymized review of 51 student submissions assessed using readability, FILA accuracy and solution correctness.
rationale: The abstract describes a pedagogical case study with a single class of 51 students and no separate control group without generative AI. Results are descriptive (mean and median scores) and qualitative, with no comparison condition. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group supports E3. Coded E3 as the first applicable code after E1 and E2, which do not apply (generative AI is learner-facing and the domain is Engineering Dynamics, which is STEM).

The intervention is GenAI-generated narratives in LA dashboards, but the learners interacting are teachers, not students (in-service teachers fall outside the population). Outcomes are teachers' understanding, perceptions, decision-making and willingness to adopt, measured by questionnaires and interviews, with no quantitative learning outcome for students or learners. No control group is described. The record fails on outcome (no quantitative learning measure) and on population (teachers, not students). Exclusion code E5 is applied as the first clear failure in order that is supported by the abstract; E4 could also apply since participants are in-service teachers. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence that the outcome criterion fails.</rationale>

quote: The pilot demonstrated high usability, curricular alignment, and perceived value for classroom application.
rationale: Framework/system design paper with a pilot of N=8 primary educators. Outcomes are usability and perceived value, not a quantitative learning outcome. No control group or learner-level comparison is described. Literary text adaptation is not STEM content, so E2 could also apply, but the protocol asks for the first applicable code in order; E1 is not clearly established (the tool is used by educators), and E2 precedes E5 in order. Applying the order strictly: the content is literary education, which is not STEM, so E2 is the first code that clearly applies.

quote: We conducted a cross-sectional online survey with purposive sampling.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of perceptions (TAM constructs such as usefulness, ease of use, intention) with no experimental intervention or control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's ordering, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is arguably not the first failure to report, and the survey design is not an experiment; the clearest failure is the absence of a learning outcome (E5). Design also fails the randomized/quasi-experimental requirement, but E5 is reported as the outcome failure evident from the abstract. Exclusion is supported by positive evidence in the abstract.
decision_note: Abstract-stage exclusion based on positive evidence of survey design and perception-only outcomes.

quote: comparative analysis of four AI large language models, ChatGPT (now GPT-4o), Bard (now Gemini), Copilot, and Auto-GPT
rationale: The abstract describes LLMs being evaluated on generating curriculum content, with experts providing feedback. Learners do not interact with the generative AI as part of a learning activity, so the intervention is not learner-facing (E1). No control group or learning outcome in learners is described. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing.

quote: We conducted an experimental application involving university students, and the results suggest that GenAI can serve as a suitable guide for learners in the initial stages of each QCP
rationale: Abstract describes learners using GenAI (guided quiz creation) in programming education with university students, which fits intervention, population, and domain. The abstract does not state whether a control group without GenAI exists: it compares GenAI with prompts against "general GenAI", which may be a two-GenAI-variant comparison (E3 risk). Learning outcome is also unclear, since the abstract emphasizes learner evaluations. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so this is unsure pending full text to check for a non-GenAI control group and a quantitative learning outcome.

quote: Using a mixed-methods, survey-based approach, undergraduate students completed two phases of data collection.
rationale: Abstract describes a survey-based study of perceived learning and engagement with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome (perceptions only). Design is survey/mixed-methods, not a comparison experiment. Excluded at E5 as the first applicable code in order of the protocol; the design also lacks a comparison group (E3 would be a further concern), but E5 is the first failing code reported by the rules is E5 before E6 at this stage. Positive evidence of failure is present from the abstract.

quote: Applying the AIEPE framework to a faculty development program evaluation, we analyzed 3361 qualitative comments.
rationale: Generative AI is used by evaluators to analyze program evaluation data, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity (E1). There is no control group, no learning outcome, and the design is a framework application, so it also fails comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Population is faculty (in-service), which further fails the population criterion. Exclusion code E1 is reported first per the ordering rule.

quote: Data were collected from 716 students via a structured self-reported questionnaire.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional self-report survey modeling behavioral intention, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Behavioral intention is a perception/affective-type measure, not learning achievement. Excluded at abstract stage on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome); design is also a survey, not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group.

quote: An online questionnaire was completed by 58 students from seven faculties, and data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlations, t-tests, ANOVA, and multiple regression.
rationale: Survey-based correlational study of self-reported generative AI use among university students with no control group that avoids generative AI. Outcomes are perceived understanding and perceived academic performance, not a quantitative learning measure. Abstract gives positive evidence of a non-experimental design lacking a comparison group, so E3 is applied as the first failing criterion in code order is E3 (no control group) before E5 (perceptions only), with design also not met.

quote: This paper presents a design-based research (DBR) contribution and a theoretically grounded pedagogical framework
rationale: The paper is a conceptual framework and design contribution. It explicitly states that empirical validation with student participants is still to come, so there is no empirical study, no control group, and no learning outcome data. E6 applies (not an empirical study). Intervention, domain and population appear to fit, but the study design is not empirical.

quote: With a group of 60 students, the study investigates how AI, especially ChatGPT, enhances project development, problem-solving, and knowledge dissemination.
rationale: Undergraduate engineering students using ChatGPT in projects (generative AI, learner-facing, STEM, higher education). The abstract does not state whether a control group without generative AI exists, which design was used (appears to be a case study, which would be excluded), or whether quantitative learning outcomes with SMD-ready statistics are reported. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so unsure is returned for full-text review.

quote: we propose a novel distillation framework that extracts intermediate reasoning steps, such as pseudocode, from LLMs and transfers them to smaller models
rationale: The study distills LLM reasoning into smaller code-generation models (student models such as CodeT5). No learners interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity; the LLM is used as a teacher for model training. This fails the learner-facing intervention requirement, so E1 applies. Other criteria are not assessable from the abstract and are not needed given E1.

quote: This design case covers the design decisions made throughout the design, development, and implementation processes of four iterations of this course.
rationale: The abstract describes a design case about developing an asynchronous AI course for L&D practitioners. It reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is a design case, not an empirical comparative study, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study). Coded E6 as the first applicable code that is clearly supported by the text.

quote: The study employed a quantitative method, collecting 295 valid responses covering variables such as AI usage frequency, AI literacy levels, learning engagement, and creativity.
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational survey design (correlation and multiple regression on 295 responses, measuring AI usage frequency and AI literacy levels) with no experimental or quasi-experimental manipulation and no control group without generative AI. This fails the comparison and design criteria. Under the protocol's order, the first applicable code is E3 (no control group without generative AI), so this is excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence.

quote: A structured survey was administered to 135 students across IT and business programs, examining demographics, language skills, learning habits, AI tool exposure, perceptions, concerns, and self-assessed learning confidence.
rationale: The study is a structured perception survey of 135 students with no experimental or comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome measured after an intervention. Design is a survey, so it is not an empirical experimental study eligible under the protocol. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's eligible sense) is applied as the first failing code that fits; the design is survey-based, and the outcome is self-assessed confidence/perceptions only, which would also fail E5. Under the protocol's ordering, E1 and E2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract, and E3 is not positively evidenced because the abstract does not describe a comparison, so E6 is the best-supported code.

criteria.intervention_note: ChatGPT-assisted instruction is generative AI, learner-facing presumably
criteria.population_note: students level not stated in abstract

quote: The study's findings reveal a significant improvement in students' HOTS within the experimental group that utilized ChatGPT, as compared to the control group.
rationale: Abstract describes a quasi-experimental study with an experimental group using ChatGPT and a control group, in the domain of DC physics (STEM). ChatGPT is a generative AI tool. Abstract does not state whether students are K-12 or higher education, nor whether the control group received a non-AI alternative, and the HOTS outcome is described as a measured improvement, which likely qualifies as a quantitative outcome. No positive evidence of failure at abstract stage, so unsure; resolve at full text for population, comparison, and effect-size data.

quote: Utilizing two years of educational data from Prairie View A&M University, it applied data augmentation with tabular generative artificial intelligence models.
rationale: Generative AI is used to create synthetic tabular training data for a Deep Knowledge Tracing model. Learners do not interact with a generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, so the intervention criterion fails and the record is excluded under E1. The abstract also reports model performance (AUC, accuracy), not a learner learning outcome, but E1 is the first applicable code.

quote: The literature on using large language models to teach programming is just getting started, but software development is going to fundamentally change
rationale: The record is a magazine-style news/feature piece (Engineering & Technology "Influence" column) discussing generative AI in education, quoting a researcher and describing tools. It reports no study, no comparison group, and no learning outcome data, so it is not an empirical study. Exclusion code E6 applies.

quote: We reviewed 50 relevant empirical articles published from January 2023 to April 2025 on GenAI in higher education.
rationale: This is a literature review of 50 articles, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It fails the design and outcome criteria, and the review type makes it ineligible under E6 (not an empirical study). Abstract evidence is clear enough to exclude at this stage.

quote: The findings indicate that LLMs are especially beneficial in organizations where data analytics is crucial
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT-generated code and deep learning models' performance on an HR dataset. There is no evident separate control group without generative AI; the comparison is only against prior studies' accuracy, and the design is a single-pipeline evaluation rather than a learner-facing randomized or quasi-experiment. Learners are not clearly students, and the context is organizational/employee attrition rather than STEM education. Excluded at E3 as no control group without generative AI is described; the abstract does not give positive evidence of a qualifying comparison.

The record has only a title and venue; there is no abstract. The title suggests undergraduate computer science learning with knowledge graphs created via generative AI, which is consistent with the protocol's domain and population criteria. However, whether learners interact with a generative AI tool, whether a non-generative-AI control group exists, the study design, and whether a quantitative learning outcome is reported cannot be determined from the title alone. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is advanced for full-text review rather than excluded.

quote: compared to the baseline, MindScratch more effectively helps students achieve high-quality projects aligned with learning objectives
rationale: Abstract stage: a multimodal generative AI visual programming tool is learner-facing, programming is STEM (computer science), and it compares against a baseline with outcomes on project quality and computational thinking. Design (randomized or quasi-experimental) and K-12/higher-ed population are not stated in the abstract, so these are unclear rather than failed. Per the abstract-stage rule, include for full-text check.

quote: Results from the study shows that students are able to make significant improvements to their proofs using the feedback from the autograder
rationale: Domain is STEM (mathematical induction proofs). The abstract describes an LLM-based autograder giving feedback to students, which plausibly meets the generative AI intervention, but it is unclear whether the user study has a control group without generative AI, what the design is, or whether a quantitative learning outcome with SMD-computable statistics is reported. Abstract does not give positive evidence of failure, so unsure; resolve at full text. Population (students) not clearly stated in abstract but not excluded.

quote: This study explored the perceptions of sixth-semester students from the English Education Study Program at Sriwijaya University regarding the use of ChatGPT as a translation tool.
rationale: Content is translation in an English education program, which is language learning and not STEM, so E2 applies. The study is also a descriptive perception survey with no control group and no learning outcome (E3/E5 would also apply), but E2 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: By harnessing the capabilities of ChatGPT, we aim to provide a solution that can alleviate the burden on educators
rationale: The abstract describes ChatGPT used by educators to create problem sets, i.e., AI used only by the teacher to prepare materials, not learner-facing generative AI. This fails the intervention criterion (E1). No learner interaction or control group is described, and the paper appears to be a tool-use exposition without a learning outcome.

quote: A validated and trial-tested Artificial Intelligence Chatbots and Research Questionnaire for Undergraduates (AICRQU) with a Cronbach Alpha reliability index of 0.85 was used for data collection.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive survey design with a single sample and no control group. Outcomes are self-reported perceptions of self-efficacy and attitude, not quantitative learning measures. Exclusion is on E3 (no control group without generative AI) as the first code that applies; E5 (perceived outcomes only) also applies. Per the protocol's order, E3 is reported first.

quote: This paper presents an updated tutorial on using PyPI for counting disaggregated objects such as bugs and pests
rationale: The abstract describes a tutorial/introduction to PyPI and a motivation-focused tool with no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome reported. Positive evidence of a missing quantitative learning outcome supports E5. Generative AI is mentioned only as an assistant, and no empirical study is described. Excluded at abstract stage on E5 as the first clearly applicable code, with the design and comparison also appearing absent.

quote: The study aimed to investigate the effectiveness of using an educational program based on ChatGPT in developing English grammar skills among tenth-grade female students
rationale: The intervention is a ChatGPT-based program (generative AI, learner-facing) with a control group taught traditionally, a quasi-experimental design, and an achievement test. However, the content is English grammar, which is language learning and not STEM. Excluded under E2. The record is also dated 2026, so the date criterion is met.

quote: In an online survey, 105 undergraduates answered questions on their preferences, engagement barriers, selection criteria, and use of lifestyle management apps.
rationale: The study is a survey of undergraduates' use and retention of well-being/lifestyle apps, with descriptive statistics only. It has no generative AI learning intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; the title's ChatGPT framing is not supported by the abstract's content. Exclusion uses the first applicable code in order. E1 (not learner-facing generative AI) would arguably apply first, since the intervention described is not generative AI, but the abstract gives positive evidence of the survey design and absence of a learning outcome. I am recording E5 as the most direct failure. Also noted: the design is a survey, which fails the design criterion, and the domain is not STEM.
decision_note: Note: the protocol's exclusion order makes E1 the first applicable code here; see rationale.

quote: Eigenvector centrality of the peer collaboration network was identified as the best predictor of student achievement.
rationale: The study predicts achievement from peer network centrality and uses generative AI to build tailored scenarios, but the abstract describes no randomized or comparison design with a control group that lacks generative AI. Outcomes are predictive classification accuracy and perceptions, not a learning outcome compared across groups. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Note that the decision is made at the abstract stage on positive evidence of no comparison group; the abstract gives no evidence of one.

The abstract describes a correlational, questionnaire-based study (Likert-scale usage survey with correlation and R² between ChatGPT use and achievement). There is no separate control group without generative AI, and the design is not experimental or quasi-experimental. Exclude at E3 (no control group). Design also fails the eligible-design criterion, but the first applicable code in order is E3, per protocol's no-comparison-group requirement. Note: at abstract stage, the positive evidence of a non-experimental design with no comparison group supports exclusion.

criteria.stage_note: abstract lacks any comparison group or learning outcome measure

quote: The present research analyses the language of texts generated by ChatGPT when solving mathematical problems related to the quadratic equation.
rationale: The study is a discourse/linguistic analysis of ChatGPT-generated texts (functional grammar framework). It reports no control group and no quantitative learning outcome measured on learners; it is not an experimental comparison. Under the protocol, the design and outcome criteria fail on positive evidence from the abstract, so exclusion is warranted. Coded E5 as the outcome is absent; the design also lacks a comparison group (E3 would be a plausible alternative code, but E5 is the first applicable criterion in the stated order per the abstract's content analysis of text).

quote: This study examines the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Education, mainly focusing on its impact on student achievement in the Pancasila and Citizenship Education Program at STKIP Pasundan.
rationale: Content is Pancasila and Citizenship Education (civic education), which is not STEM. This is a clear positive failure of the domain criterion, so exclude under E2 at abstract stage. The design appears to be a regression-based quantitative study without a clearly described control group, but this is not needed for the decision. Note that the first applicable code in order is E1 only if the intervention fails; the abstract does not clearly show that, so E2 is the first code that positively applies.

criteria.population_note: students in physics classroom, level not stated

quote: Integrating ChatGPT in the classroom may improve student learning outcomes in physics by developing critical thinking abilities
rationale: Abstract describes learners using ChatGPT in a physics classroom to correct misconceptions, so intervention and STEM domain appear met. The abstract does not state whether a control group exists, the study design, or whether a quantitative outcome was measured, so these cannot be judged. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not grounds for exclusion, so the record is advanced to full text for checking.

quote: The analysis reviews existing GenAI mentoring platforms, including MentorAI and Thunai, demonstrating their capabilities in delivering personalized career guidance and overcoming geographical and resource barriers.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/review analysis of GenAI mentoring platforms and calls for future longitudinal research. It reports no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence that the paper is not an empirical study (E6) is present, so it is excluded at abstract stage. The code E6 is the first applicable one in the order when design is assessed; E5 would also apply, but E6 comes first in the protocol's listed sequence for non-empirical work.

quote: The proposed system uses Optical Character Recognition (OCR) to recognize handwritten characters and convert them into machine-readable text.
rationale: This is a system description for converting handwritten notes to digital text with an LLM cleanup step. The abstract reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome; it describes a tool and its features only. Under the abstract-stage rule, exclusion needs positive evidence of failure. The abstract does show no learning outcome and no control group, so it is excluded on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) as the first clearly applicable code. Not an empirical evaluation is also plausible (E6), but E5 is the first clear failure cited here.

quote: This scoping review analyzes 24 empirical articles published between 1 January 2022 and 5 September 2023 on students’ perceptions and use of AI chatbots in higher education.
rationale: This is a scoping review, which the protocol excludes as a review (E6, not an empirical study). It also reports only students' perceptions and use, with no quantitative learning outcome or control group. Exclusion code E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order; the review type is the clearest ground.
rationale_note: Scoping review of perceptions; not an empirical primary study.

quote: "The research adopts a deductive/inductive approach, combining conceptualization and empirical evidence analysis."
rationale: The abstract describes an in-depth case study with essay assessment, detector testing, and a questionnaire on technology acceptance. It reports no separate control group without generative AI, no randomized or quasi-experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome (the results are described as qualitative). Exclusion code E3 is applied as the first failing criterion in order that is clearly evidenced; the design is a case study, so E6 (not an empirical study) could also be argued, but the abstract does describe empirical data collection. Decision is made on positive evidence of no comparison group.

quote: The study used a quantitative approach. Data were gathered from 163 respondents in the Secretarial and Records Management departments via a structured online survey and analysed using descriptive statistics.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-sample structured online survey with descriptive statistics on learners' perceptions. There is no control group, so the comparison criterion fails (E3). The outcomes are perceptions of cognitive load and usage, not a quantitative learning measure (E5 would also apply), and the design is a survey, not an experiment or quasi-experiment. Under the code order, E3 is the first that applies because no comparison group exists. The domain (Secretarial and Records Management) is not clearly STEM.

quote: it was effective in improving their computational thinking generally but not their problem-solving skills
rationale: Programming education with a ChatGPT-based scaffolding system and a computational thinking outcome; domain and intervention appear met. The abstract does not state whether a control group without generative AI exists (mixed-method design unclear), nor the participant level or whether SMD-computable statistics are reported. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so advance to full text for the comparison and design check.

quote: The article concludes that the use of Generative AI can contribute to the development of in-demand skills among students who have experience working with these technologies
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/review-style article that discusses generative AI capabilities and compares chatbot assistants, and gives a case description of the Walter+ assistant with institutional achievement indicators. There is no described comparison group, no randomized or quasi-experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome measured against a control. This appears to be a non-empirical discussion article, so E6 applies. Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract that the design is not an empirical comparative study.
rationale_short: Discussion/conceptual article with a single institutional case; no control group or learning outcome described.

quote: Perception of students in the use of ChatGPT Questionnaire and Students Satisfaction on ChatGPT Questionnaire was used as instruments for data collection.
rationale: The study measures only perceptions and satisfaction with ChatGPT, using a correlational/survey design with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Excluded under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome); it would also fail the comparison and design criteria. Biology is STEM-adjacent, so domain was not the deciding factor.
rationale_note: Abstract gives positive evidence of perception/satisfaction-only outcomes and a correlational survey design.

quote: Our results reveal systematic and statistically significant differences between LLM and human coding across structural, transitional, and code-level metrics for binary and ordered tasks.
rationale: The study compares LLM coding against human coding of qualitative learner text, i.e., the LLM is used as a coding tool by researchers, not as a learner-facing intervention with a control group receiving no generative AI. There is no learning outcome measured; the outcomes are agreement/accuracy metrics of coding. Exclusion for E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the most applicable code, though E1 (not learner-facing generative AI) also fits; following the protocol's rule of reporting the first applicable code in order, E1 precedes E3 and should be the code applied. Correcting: the first applicable code is E1.

quote: This paper explores three introductory physics examples related to 1-D motion, and employs ChatGPT 3.5 to generate scripts that will produce graphs from raw data.
rationale: The abstract describes an illustrative, example-based paper on using ChatGPT to generate plotting scripts. It reports no controlled comparison, no participants, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is not an empirical comparative study, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study). Exclusion is supported on the abstract alone because the paper presents examples and a tool demonstration rather than an experiment with a control group.

quote: This article proposes an approach for using the AI chatbot ChatGPT to create educational games.
rationale: The abstract describes a methodological/approach proposal for educators using ChatGPT to create games, with no empirical comparison group, no learner interaction with the tool, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. Ordering: E1 (intervention not learner-facing, since educators are the ones using ChatGPT) could arguably apply first; however, the abstract gives no evidence of a learner-facing intervention either way, and the clearest failing criterion is the absence of an empirical design. Exclusion is based on positive evidence that the study is not empirical.

quote: Empowering STEM teachers' professional learning through GenAI
rationale: The title indicates the participants are STEM teachers engaged in professional learning, which the protocol excludes as in-service teachers (population criterion). No abstract is available. The title gives positive evidence that the population is in-service teachers, so the record is excluded at the abstract stage under E4. Other criteria cannot be assessed from the title alone. The study's focus on task-technology fit, cognitive appraisal, and emotions also suggests a perception-based design, which would point to E5 or E6 as well, but the first applicable code in order is E4.

quote: This study examines how Generative AI tools, specifically ChatGPT and Gemini, can enhance English for Specific Purposes (ESP) learning and education.
rationale: The study is about English for Specific Purposes, a language-learning context, which is non-STEM content (E2). Although vocational departments such as Nursing and IT are mentioned, the instructional content is ESP English. The abstract also reports only a single sample with pre-post tests and no control group described, which would separately raise E3. E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order.

criteria.domain_note: Classroom management course in Islamic Religious Education; not clearly STEM

quote: A quantitative approach was applied using a quasi-experimental method with a one-group pretest–posttest design.
rationale: The abstract describes a one-group pretest–posttest design with no control group that does not use generative AI, which is positive evidence of a failed comparison criterion (E3). Also, the content (classroom management in Islamic Religious Education) does not appear to be STEM, but E3 is the applicable first-listed code given the design. Single-group pre-post designs are explicitly excluded.

quote: This quasi-experimental study investigated the effects of targeted GenAI prompt engineering instruction on knowledge acquisition, prompt writing skills, and confidence levels among undergraduate and graduate students in business analytics courses at a research university.
rationale: Abstract describes a quasi-experiment with GenAI prompt engineering instruction among undergraduate and graduate students, with knowledge and prompt-writing outcomes, so intervention, population and outcome plausibly met. However, the abstract describes a pre-test/post-test design with no clearly stated control group, so comparison is unclear. Business analytics is not clearly STEM under the protocol's list (it may count as data science, but this is not stated). Missing information is not grounds for exclusion at the abstract stage, so the record is sent to full text to check for a comparison group and domain.

quote: Three LLMs (ChatGPT, GPT-4o, and DS R1) were used to assess the responses using two prompting strategies
rationale: The LLMs are used by evaluators to score student responses and generate feedback; learners do not interact with the generative AI tool as part of a learning activity, so E1 applies. The study also compares only generative AI prompting variants with human scorers as benchmark, with no non-generative-AI control group, and reports agreement metrics rather than a learning outcome. E1 is the first applicable code in the protocol order.

quote: We piloted this instructional syntax in 17 classes with 215 primary students and examined implementation fidelity using LLM-supported transcript analysis.
rationale: The generative AI (LLM) is used by researchers to analyze lesson transcripts, not as a learner-facing tool in the learning activity. The intervention is a pedagogical syntax with written reflection, not a generative AI tool learners interact with. Abstract gives positive evidence the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI, so E1 applies. No control group or learning outcome is described either.

quote: The study underscores the importance of demonstrating practical benefits and providing adequate support to enhance AI chatbot adoption in educational settings
rationale: The study is a survey of 385 students on intention to use Gemini (a technology acceptance model study). It has no control group, no randomized or quasi-experimental comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome; only perceptions and intentions are measured. Exclusion is on E3 as the first criterion that clearly fails at abstract stage, with the design and outcome also failing. Design/outcome failure would also support exclusion. Positive evidence is clear from the abstract.

quote: A descriptive, quantitative survey design was employed, with the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM)
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey with no control group and no experimental manipulation, so no comparison group without generative AI exists. Outcomes are perceptions (usefulness, ease of use, attitudes) rather than a quantitative learning measure, although a "student learning" construct is modeled. Design is survey, which the protocol excludes. E3 is the first applicable code in order that is clearly evidenced by the abstract (no control group); the survey design and perception-only outcomes would also fail other criteria.

quote: Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the chatbot in delivering accurate career advice and phishing detection
rationale: The abstract describes a chatbot evaluated by experimental results, but gives no indication of a control group that does not use generative AI. The chatbot is built on NLP and machine learning, with no mention of a generative model. Its evaluation appears to be accuracy of the system itself, not a learner comparison against a control group. This is positive evidence of a missing comparison group, so exclude under E3. Learner interaction, generative nature, and outcome type are also unclear from the abstract.

quote: This scoping review synthesizes 32 studies (2023–2025) purposively sampled from 259 records to map personalization mechanisms and effectiveness signals in higher-education CS contexts.
rationale: The record is a scoping review, which is a review rather than an empirical study. Under the protocol's publication-type rule, reviews are excluded; the closest fitting code is E6 (not an empirical study). The review synthesizes other studies and reports no primary comparison-group data of its own. Exclusion is based on positive evidence from the abstract that the paper is a review. No prompt-like text was found in the record.
rationale_note: Note: the protocol lists reviews under publication type (E10) as well as not-empirical (E6). I chose E6 because the review type is not an empirical study; E10 could also apply if the researcher prefers that mapping.

quote: Pilot studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework in improving participation, retention, and learning outcomes for students with disabilities.
rationale:
Abstract describes a generative AI adaptive learning system (ALGA-Ed) for students with disabilities, which may meet the intervention criterion. However, the abstract does not state a control group, a comparison design, the STEM domain, or the statistics needed for an SMD. The pilot studies could be single-group, which would be E3, but the abstract does not say so. quote: A mixedmethods approach evaluated students’ awareness, perceptions, and practical experiences pre- and post- intervention.
rationale: The abstract describes a case study with pre- and post-intervention measurement of a single cohort of pre-service mechanical engineering educators, with no control group that avoids generative AI. The abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group, so exclude at abstract stage.

Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing GenAI) would be the first code that applies, but the abstract gives no evidence of a learner-facing tool, so E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense, i.e., qualitative non-experimental design) is the most accurate single code. The decision is clear-cut exclusion, not a borderline case.
exclusion_code_note: E6 is used here for a qualitative design; the study is empirical, so the stricter reading would be non-eligible design. Considered E4 too, since participants are staff not students.

rationale: Abstract describes a text-mining pipeline using Gemini 1.5 Pro to analyze public news and enterprise records, plus expert validation surveys. quote: this investigation reports student responses to an e-questionnaire investigating their perspectives on it

quote: Due to the limited sample size (n = 43), exploratory or confirmatory factor analysis was not conducted.

The design appears to be a model-performance evaluation rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental study with a comparison group.

rationale: Cross-sectional survey of 275 participants on perceptions and awareness of generative AI, analysed with descriptive statistics and chi-square. Abstract-stage exclusion is justified because the abstract positively describes a survey of perceptions rather than a learning outcome.

Abstract describes ChatGPT-3.5 answers to assessment problems graded by tutors against past student responses, not learners interacting with generative AI as part of a learning activity, and there is no separate control group using generative AI. Population is medical students in a health professions program (pre-clerkship medical education), which falls under the health professions exclusion for domain/population. Exclusion code E4 is selected as the first clearly applicable code at abstract stage per the protocol ordering concern, but the strongest reasons are the absence of a learner-facing intervention and of a generative-AI-free comparison group (E1/E3 would apply first in the protocol order). Because the code order places E1 before E4, the code should be considered E1 rather than E4 if the auditor prefers the strict ordering: the record is not learner-facing generative AI use, since ChatGPT produced answers that were then graded, not a learning activity with learners.

quote: A quantitative, cross-sectional, descriptive-correlational survey was conducted among 472 senior high school and higher education students
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional descriptive-correlational survey with no control or comparison group, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. Exclusion code E3 is applied as the first failing criterion for a design without a non-generative-AI control group; E5 (no learning outcome) also applies. Under the protocol's order, E3 is reported first, although the abstract gives clear positive evidence of no comparison group, which is the strongest reason for exclusion.

quote: "Methodologically, the study adopts a qualitative analytical framework grounded in comparative literature synthesis, theoretical modeling, and interpretive reasoning."
rationale: The abstract states the study is a qualitative, theoretical literature synthesis with no experiments or numerical metrics ("Rather than relying on numerical simulation or experimental metrics"). Under the protocol's code order, E1 and E2 are not clearly failed from the abstract, but E6 is the decisive positive failure.

quote: Findings reveal that students primarily used AI tools, especially ChatGPT, for improving writing quality, generating ideas, and proofreading content

It reports usage and perceived motivations, not a quantitative learning outcome, and it has no control group. Business is also not a protocol STEM domain. Exclusion is on E5 as the first clear failure in the protocol order at this stage; E2 and E3 would also apply, but E5 is the first listed for the reported usage-only design.

quote: Comparing ChatGPT and DeepSeek in Addressing Misconceptions about Physics Concepts
rationale: Abstract describes generative AI tools (ChatGPT, DeepSeek) addressing physics misconceptions, so intervention and domain appear met. However, the abstract does not state whether a non-generative-AI control group exists (it appears to compare two generative tools, which would be E3 if no control), does not describe the design, and does not report a quantitative learning outcome. These are not positive evidence of failure at abstract stage, so unsure and defer to full text.

quote: "Employing a qualitative approach with an action research design"
rationale: Abstract describes a qualitative action research design with reconnaissance, intervention, and post-intervention phases in one school, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of failure on comparison (no control group), design (qualitative, not an experiment or quasi-experiment), and outcome (no quantitative measure). Exclusion code E3 (no comparison group without generative AI) is the first applicable code in protocol order to be assigned at abstract stage; E5 would also apply. Coded E3 as the primary design/comparison failure.

quote: Survey data from 378 Bangladeshi engineering students were analysed using PLS-SEM and multi-group comparisons
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey using PLS-SEM on technology acceptance constructs (intention, perceived usefulness, ease of use). It has no experimental or quasi-experimental design with a control group, and no quantitative learning outcome such as achievement or skill performance; outcomes are perceptions and usage intention. Excluded at abstract stage on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), with the survey design also failing the design criterion (E6 would be the code for non-empirical, but this is an empirical survey so E5 is the first applicable code given the outcome failure).

quote: Based on primary data collected from 78 students participating in post-graduate management and commerce programs and 25 faculty members, the study finds a strong and convergent preference for applied learning in both groups.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey-based study of student and faculty perceptions with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Outcomes are preferences, self-rated engagement, and grading-method favour, which are perception measures. Exclusion under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). The design also appears to be a survey, not an eligible design, and the domain (management and commerce) is not clearly STEM, but E5 is the first applicable code in order from the abstract evidence.
rationale_note: Exclusion code is the first applicable in the protocol order based on abstract evidence.

quote: This master's thesis represents a meticulous scholarly endeavor
rationale: The record is a master's thesis using surveys and interviews (mixed methods) on student perceptions of ChatGPT. It reports perceptions, satisfaction and usability rather than a quantitative learning outcome, and has no control group. It is not an empirical comparison study meeting the design criteria. The thesis format is also not an eligible publication type (E10 would also apply), but the first applicable code in order is E3 for the missing control group; however, the more directly applicable reading is that this is a non-experimental perception study. Coded E6 as not an empirical experimental study, with the absence of a comparison and outcome also evident from the abstract.

quote: The aim is to evaluate the effectiveness of generative artificial intelligence (GAI) in enhancing student engagement, personalising learning, and improving teaching practices. rationale: The design is a mixed-methods survey, interview and observation study with no comparison group, so the comparison criterion is not met. The outcomes are perceptions and ratings of integration rather than a quantitative learning measure. Under the abstract-stage rule, exclusion is justified only where the abstract gives positive evidence of failure. Here the abstract describes surveys, interviews and observations with no control group and no learning outcome, which is positive evidence of E3 (no control group without generative AI). E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) would also apply; E3 is reported first in the protocol order.

Outcomes include self-efficacy, higher-order thinking, and project performance (CPAM evaluation), which appear to be quantitative learning measures. Journal article in Education and Information Technologies, 2025. No abstract-level evidence of a failed criterion; full-text check needed for SMD data availability.

rationale: The abstract describes a ChatGPT-based interview education program evaluated with pre-post tests (paired-sample t-tests) on speech ability, speech metacognition, and AI digital literacy, plus learner interviews. No control or comparison group is mentioned, so this reads as a single-group pre-post design, which the protocol excludes (E3). The content is interview/speech training, not STEM (E2 would also apply, but E3 is the first applicable code given the protocol's order is E1 then E2... see note). Per the code order, E2 (not STEM) comes before E3; the domain is clearly non-STEM (interview and speech skills), so the first applicable code is E2.

However, the abstract does not state a control group without generative AI; it appears to compare two generative AI tools, which would be E3 if confirmed. Outcomes mention task completion speed and soft skills, with no clear quantitative learning measure stated, and no explicit design details. Since the abstract does not give positive evidence of a failed criterion, advancing to full text to check whether a non-generative-AI comparison group exists.

quote: A descriptive qualitative approach with a case study design was employed.

Exclusion coded E3 (no control group without generative AI), the first clearly applicable code in order after intervention and domain checks. Positive evidence of a failing criterion is present, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified.

E5 is applied as the first code that clearly applies on the outcome, consistent with the survey-only design; the abstract gives positive evidence the outcome is perception/experience rather than learning.

Abstract describes a thematic analysis of 112 Mathematics Stack Exchange posts referencing ChatGPT. Given the abstract gives positive evidence of a qualitative design with no comparison group, exclusion is warranted.

quote: submitting five versions of short essays about criminological topics generated from ChatGPT to the TurnItIn software

quote: The study revealed that most respondents are enrolled in the College of Arts and Sciences, aged 22 to 23, female, and full-time first-year students

quote: The paper empirically evaluates how well various configurations of generative LLMs can grade student short answer responses compared to expert human raters.

quote: The study involved 189 parents of school-age children. Data were collected through an online survey using a structured questionnaire
rationale: The study is a survey of parents about family regulation practices. It involves no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. quote: We developed a 13-question survey using the REDCap application to explore participants' educational background, year in school, preferred medical specialty, and perception of current or potential use of GenAI within residency applications.

rationale: The study is a survey comparing attitudes of students and teachers toward ChatGPT in English for engineering classes. It reports only perceptions and attitudes, with no quantitative learning outcome and no control group without generative AI. Excluded under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome). The design is a survey, which also fails the protocol's design criterion, but E5 is the first applicable code in order and the abstract gives clear positive evidence of it.

quote: the experiment's results showed that students' learning rates increased by LLMs as model interpretation assistants
rationale: An LLM is used as a learner-facing assistant for interpreting UML models, which suggests the intervention criterion is met. The abstract does not state whether there is a control group without generative AI, the experimental design, or the quantitative outcome measure. UML modeling is plausibly computer science/software engineering content, and the participants are described as junior engineers, so population eligibility is unclear. Because missing information is not evidence of failure, the record is passed to full text.

quote: The main stages of the study consisted of expert validation and empirical testing.
rationale: The study is an instrument validation (CVI and item validity/reliability of a questionnaire on generative AI use). It reports no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome; the measures are questionnaire items about use, which are perceptions rather than learning. It is not an intervention study with an eligible design, so it fails on design, comparison, and outcome. Because it is not an empirical study of learning effects, E6 is the most fitting code, though E3 or E5 could also apply. Exclusion is supported on positive evidence from the abstract.

quote: The purpose of this qualitative case study was to explore how college students described their use of these tools in academic courses
rationale: The study is a qualitative single case study using semistructured interviews and document analysis. It is not an empirical comparison with a control group and reports no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's design and outcome criteria, it fails. E6 (not an empirical study) is the closest code. The abstract does describe an empirical qualitative study, so the code is a judgment call, but no quantitative outcome or control group exists, and the study cannot meet the design criterion regardless of the code chosen. Exclusion is justified on the abstract alone, since the abstract gives positive evidence of a qualitative design with no comparison group.
rationale_note: Ordering note: E1 through E5 were checked first. Domain and intervention are not clearly stated in the abstract, so E1/E2 could not be confirmed. E3 applies (no control group), and E5 (no quantitative outcome) also applies. Per the protocol's order, E3 should be reported before E5/E6 if the record is re-screened at fulltext. The code is E6 here as the design is qualitative and non-empirical in the comparative sense.

quote: This was a cross-sectional, online survey.
rationale: Cross-sectional survey with no control group and no learning outcome; it measures self-reported generative AI use. Design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment, and the outcome is usage and perceptions, not learning. Physical therapy DPT education is health professions, which falls outside the STEM domain. The most fitting code is E3, since no comparison group without generative AI exists; the abstract gives clear positive evidence that the comparison criterion fails.

quote: A survey approach was employed, involving 220 respondents, and data were analyzed across four key areas
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of student readiness, with no experimental or comparison group and no learning outcome measured. It is not an empirical intervention study, so E6 applies. Survey designs and perception-only measures also fail the design and outcome criteria. Under the exclusion-order rule, E1 and E2 are not clearly established from the abstract, so E6 is the first applicable code given the survey design.

quote: two Hispanic literature survey courses at the University of Delaware during the Spring 2023 semester
rationale: Content is Hispanic literature, a non-STEM subject, so E2 applies and is the first failing criterion in code order. The abstract also reports only a perception survey of 21 students and no control group, so E3 and E5 would apply as well, but E2 is reported as the first that applies.

The study is a survey of perceptions and attitudes (ease of use, ethics, perceived impact on learning). There is no experimental intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; only perceptions and usage are reported. This fails the outcome criterion and the design criterion (survey design is excluded). Exclusion code E5 is the first applicable code in the stated order that is positively evidenced by the abstract; the study is also not an experiment (E3 would also apply), but E5 is reported as the outcome failure is explicit. Abstract gives positive evidence of a survey-only design, so exclusion is warranted.

quote: In the study, a case study, which is a qualitative research method, was used.
rationale: The study is a qualitative case study of early childhood teachers' views, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Participants are in-service teachers, not students. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study is broader, but the design is qualitative empirical work); the first applicable code by order is E4 for population, but E1 (teacher-only use of ChatGPT) and E3 (no control group) also apply. Under the protocol's order, E1 is checked first: ChatGPT was used in teacher training, not as a learner-facing tool, so E1 applies first.

quote: Simulation-based education plays a critical role in paramedic education by enabling learners to develop both clinical and non-technical skills in a safe, realistic environment.
rationale: The record is a continuing professional development article on paramedic simulation design with Gen AI, not an empirical study. It reports no comparison group or quantitative learning outcome, and paramedic education is health professions education, which the protocol excludes from STEM. The protocol's first exclusion code that applies, in order, is E1 (intervention not learner-facing), but the abstract describes AI used for facilitator prompt design, so E1 is plausibly met too. Because the rules require one code and the first applicable one in order, the decision is recorded as E4 on population grounds, which is a weaker fit than E6 (not an empirical study). An auditor should check this code choice. The abstract gives clear evidence the study is not an empirical trial, which is the most direct failure.

quote: Questionnaire results and thesis evaluations indicate increased interest in and engagement with graduation research, improved self-evaluations of mathematical thinking and data analysis skills
rationale: The abstract describes a learning design with GenAI and image analysis for undergraduate research, with no mention of a control or comparison group. Outcomes are questionnaire self-evaluations and thesis evaluations, which are perception-based. Positive evidence of a missing comparison group supports E3. Exclusion is based on the abstract's description of a single-arm design with no control group.

quote: We provide a brief introduction to diffusion models for applied mathematicians and statisticians.
rationale: This is a tutorial/expository article on diffusion models. It describes no learner interacting with a generative AI tool, no control group, no comparison design, and no learning outcome measured. It is not an empirical study. E1 would also technically apply (no learner-facing generative AI intervention), but the first-applicable code in order is E1; however, the core failure is that it is not an empirical study. Per the protocol order, E1 comes first: the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI, so the code reported is E1.

Abstract describes evaluating Gemma 3 LLM-generated solutions to calculus exam problems, with comparison against student cohort performance. This is an evaluation of LLM outputs rather than a learner-facing intervention with a separate control group that does not use generative AI. No control group without generative AI is described, so E3 applies. Abstract stage exclusion is based on positive evidence: the design is a model-benchmarking framework, not a comparison of learners with and without generative AI.

quote: This reflective autoethnography offers unique insights into multiple factors of interest.
rationale: The study is a reflective autoethnography with a prompt engineering experiment in which ChatGPT designs quiz questions. It involves no learner interaction with generative AI and no control group, and it reports no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E5 is applied as the first clearly failing criterion that is evidenced in the abstract. Under the abstract-stage rule, this is a positive exclusion, and the design is also not an experimental comparison. Note that E1 (AI not learner-facing) could also plausibly apply, since ChatGPT is used by lecturers/researchers to produce assessments; E1 precedes E5 in the code order, so the strictly correct code may be E1. Given that the first-applicable rule in order is E1, I'm recording E1 below instead.

quote: This study examines how university students enrolled in social science programs at two Spanish universities ethically evaluate a typical misuse of GenAI
rationale: The study is a survey-based, correlational PLS-SEM and fsQCA analysis of students' ethical perceptions and intentions. It has no experimental or comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome, and the content is social science rather than STEM. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study design eligible under the protocol) is the best fit; E2 (non-STEM content) would also apply, and the protocol orders E2 before E5/E6 but the first applicable code is E2 by order. Reporting E2 as the first applicable code in protocol order.

The abstract describes GPT-4o used by teaching assistants to grade quizzes and project reports, i.e., AI used for grading and not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity. This fails the intervention criterion (E1). There is also no described control group without generative AI and no learning outcome measured; the scores compared are AI grades versus human grades, not learner outcomes. The abstract gives positive evidence of E1, so it is excluded at the abstract stage.

quote: This review compiles research from 2019 to 2025 on the use of AI—especially ITS—in college-level differential calculus.
rationale: The record is a review of prior literature, not an empirical study with its own control-group comparison, so it fails the empirical-study requirement (E6). Its title also marks it as a global review. Domain (calculus) and population (college) are consistent with eligibility, but the review design rules it out.

quote: Thematic analysis of the qualitative data yielded eight primary themes
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study with thematic analysis, not an empirical experiment with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. Design is qualitative, so it fails the comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Under the exclusion-code order, E1 and E2 do not clearly apply at abstract stage (ChatGPT is generative; domain is unspecified, graduate curriculum and instruction). The primary reason is that it is not an empirical quantitative study, so E6 is used.

quote: Research involved nursing students, educators, and clinical practitioners from various institutions and healthcare settings, with a total of 820 participants gathered.
rationale: Nursing education is health professions education, which the protocol explicitly excludes from the STEM domain (E2). The abstract also describes a mixed-methods study with pre/post tests and no clearly described separate control group without generative AI, so design and comparison are doubtful. The first applicable code in order is E2. Nursing/health content is a clear positive indication of failure at the abstract stage, so exclusion is justified.

quote: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of ChatGPT as an educational tool for business administration students in Nueva Ecija, Philippines
rationale: Business administration students; content is not STEM (E2). Also the abstract describes a descriptive/quantitative survey-style design using percentages, weighted means and Pearson's r with no control group and perception-based outcomes, so E3/E5/E6 likely also apply. Only one code can be reported; E2 is the first applicable code in protocol order that is positively evidenced by the abstract.

quote: We conduct an A/B test among 60 undergraduate students in a programming course and collect their feedback through a questionnaire.
rationale: Abstract describes an LLM-based system for generating programming projects, used by lecturers to create content; it is unclear whether learners interact with the generative tool. An A/B test with 60 undergraduates is reported, but the outcomes appear to be expert grading of projects and student ratings/questionnaire feedback, which may be perceptions rather than learning measures. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so return unsure for full-text review of whether students use the LLM and whether a learning outcome with extractable statistics exists.

The record has only a title, venue, and year; no abstract is available. The title suggests GenAI-supported self-regulated game-based science learning (STEM domain, 2026 publication, so date criterion appears met), but the title does not show whether there is a control group without generative AI, the study design, the population level, or a quantitative learning outcome. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is advanced for full-text review rather than excluded.

quote: This article presents a secondary data analysis of existing empirical research, systematic reviews, and policy documents to examine how GenAI is reshaping the relational dynamics
rationale: The record is a secondary synthesis of existing studies, systematic reviews and policy documents with a sociological framework, not an empirical primary study with a control group. It has no comparison group or quantitative learning outcome, so it fails the design, comparison and outcome criteria. Not an empirical study (E6) is the first applicable code in order at the abstract stage, since E1 and E2 cannot be assessed from the abstract. Excluded.

quote: A mixed-methods, quasi-experimental design was employed to compare two naturally occurring undergraduate cohorts at a Gulf-region university.
rationale: Abstract describes a quasi-experimental comparison of two undergraduate cohorts (Python-based vs GenAI-supported pathways) in a computing course, which fits population and design.
