However, the abstract does not clarify whether the control cohort lacks generative AI in a way that meets the comparison requirement (it appears to be a Python pathway, which may qualify as a non-AI comparator). Outcomes include project satisfaction and perceived ease of use (perceptions, excluded) alongside creativity and professional output, and it is unclear whether a quantitative learning outcome with SMD-computable statistics is reported. Insufficient to exclude at abstract stage; advance to full text to check outcomes and statistics.

quote: We would like to comment on “Comparing ChatGPT and Dental Students' Performance in an Introduction to Dental Anatomy Examination: A Cross-Sectional Study.”
rationale: The record is a journal comment/letter responding to a cross-sectional study, not an empirical study with a control group. It has no eligible comparison design (ChatGPT vs students is a comparison of performance, not a learner-facing intervention with a control group), and it is an editorial-type commentary, so it is not an eligible publication type. Excluded under E10 (publication type not eligible); E3 and E6 would also plausibly apply, but E10 is the best fit for a commentary piece. The abstract-stage rule is satisfied because positive evidence shows the item is a commentary rather than an eligible article.

quote: This paper explores the potential of using Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer (ChatGPT), a powerful language model, as an innovative tool to enhance education in the classroom.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/experience-based paper ("Drawing from firsthand experience", "demonstrates how ChatGPT can be integrated") with no comparison group, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparative study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study); E5 would also apply since no quantitative learning outcome is reported.
decision_rationale: Abstract gives positive evidence of a non-empirical, experience-based paper.

quote: The present systematic literature review investigates the ethical integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in Islamic Religious Education (IRE).
rationale: This is a systematic literature review, which the protocol excludes as a review and as a non-empirical study (E6). The abstract states the evidence base is predominantly conceptual, exploratory, or perception-based, with few intervention or comparative studies, so no control-group quantitative learning study is reported. Islamic Religious Education is also not clearly within STEM. E6 is the first applicable code in order for this non-empirical review.

quote: This study adopts a conceptual research approach based on a systematic review of literature published between 2019 and 2025.
rationale: The record is a conceptual framework paper built on a systematic literature review and content analysis. It is not an empirical study: there is no experimental or quasi-experimental design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion under E6 (not an empirical study) is the first applicable code in protocol order; E1 was considered but the abstract does not clearly establish the intervention, so E6 is the decisive ground.

quote: Inderscience is a global company, a dynamic leading independent journal publisher disseminates the latest research across the broad fields of science, engineering and technology
rationale: The title refers to an AI tutoring system with adaptive learning on mobile technology for Gen Z university students, but the abstract is only publisher boilerplate and gives no details on whether the AI is generative, whether a control group exists, the design, the STEM domain, or any learning outcome. No positive evidence of a failed criterion is present, so the record is advanced to full text for checking. Population appears to be university students, which is consistent with the title. The title's "adaptive learning" wording raises a possible E1 concern that should be resolved at full text.

quote: A survey-based methodology was employed to evaluate the system's projected effectiveness.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey-based evaluation of projected effectiveness, with no quantitative learning outcome or control group reported. Survey-only evaluation fails the design and outcome criteria. Exclusion code E5 is applied as the first failing criterion after the intervention (MLLM-based system, C++ domain) is judged met. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of a survey-only design rather than missing information.

quote: A systematic research method allowed comprehensive coverage of peer reviewed literature using two databases: Web of Science and SciFinder.
rationale: This is a literature review (systematic review of 245 articles), not an empirical study with a control group and learning outcome data. It fails the design, comparison and outcome requirements. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies as the first failing criterion for a review. Generative AI is mentioned only as an opportunity in the discussion of findings.

Abstract is missing from the index; only title and venue are available. The title suggests a professional development study with pre-service teachers in mathematics and generative AI acceptance, but it does not show whether there is a control group, whether a learning outcome was measured (the title points to acceptance, which is an affective/perception measure), or the study design. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is held as unsure for full-text review, where the methods and outcomes can be checked.

quote: Synergizing Hybrid Ensemble Learning and Generative AI For Robust and Explainable Student Placement Prediction
rationale: The title describes hybrid ensemble learning for student placement prediction, which is predictive analytics rather than learner-facing generative AI. The abstract also describes a waste management teaching program among women, which is not STEM content and does not match the title. Positive evidence fails on intervention (predictive, not learner-facing generative AI) and domain (waste management knowledge is not STEM). The record is internally inconsistent, but the abstract gives positive evidence against the intervention and domain criteria, so it is excluded under E1, the first applicable code.

The study compares emotional content of ChatGPT answers and human Stack Overflow answers. It is not a learner-facing intervention with a control group, and it has no quantitative learning outcome; emotion/tone measures are affective and do not count as learning outcomes. Although the abstract's first criteria checks are ambiguous, the record gives positive evidence that the outcome (emotional tone of text) is not a learning measure, so E5 applies. No verbatim quote is needed beyond the abstract's description of emotional tone; quote set to null as no single passage establishes the code cleanly. Note: the abstract does not describe an experimental design with learners, so the design criterion also appears unmet.

quote: This study aims to reconstruct adab al-‘ilm as a conceptual framework for learning ethics in Islamic education in the GenAI era. It employs an integrative literature review combined with conceptual reconstruction.
rationale: The record is an integrative literature review with conceptual reconstruction, not an empirical study. It has no control group, no learner outcome data, and no quantitative measure. E6 applies as the first failing code in order, since E1 through E5 cannot be assessed as met from the abstract but the design fails outright on E6.

quote: Overall, 59.80 % of the students reported substantial use of GenAI in their design projects, and 40.20 % showed limited or no use.
rationale: The study is described as a natural experiment, but it compares students who chose to use GenAI with those who did not, based on self-reported use and reasons (perceptions/qualitative themes). The abstract reports no quantitative learning outcome, only usage shares and reported reasons. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome). At abstract stage, the design is also not clearly a randomized or comparison-group quasi-experiment, but E5 is the first applicable code given the abstract's focus on perceptions and usage.
decision_note: Exclude is based on positive evidence that no quantitative learning outcome is reported.

quote: 50 academicians from Türkiye participated in the study within the scope of snowball sampling.
rationale: The study surveys academicians' views with a semi-structured interview and descriptive statistics. It has no control group, no learner sample, and no quantitative learning outcome. Exclusion code E5 applies (no quantitative learning outcome); E3 and population criteria also fail on the abstract, but E5 is the outcome-level failure and the study is a perceptions study. Note the abstract gives positive evidence of perception-only design, so exclusion is appropriate.

criteria.comparison_note: Control group taught with traditional method (non-AI) per abstract

quote: A quasi-experimental design was employed, with a sample of 55 students divided into two groups
rationale: Quasi-experiment with a control group taught by traditional method (non-AI), biology achievement test (quantitative outcome), second-year intermediate students (K-12), published 2026. The intervention is described as generative AI-based visual aids made with ChatGPT per the title, but the abstract does not clarify whether learners themselves interact with the generative tool versus the teacher using AI-generated visuals, which is an E1 question to resolve at full text. Biology is a science domain. Publication type and full-text data sufficiency cannot be checked from the abstract. Retained as unsure for full-text review.

University physics course (STEM, higher education) using LLM-based inquiry learning for projectile motion. The abstract describes a methodology and rubric development using data mining and explainable AI, with no mention of a control group, comparison design, or quantitative learning outcome comparison. Missing information is not evidence of failure at the abstract stage, so the record is held for full-text review to check for a comparison group and effect data.

quote: This qualitative study examines the perceptions, experiences, and usage patterns of BS Applied Mathematics students
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative study of perceptions, experiences, and usage patterns using interviews, focus groups, and observations. There is no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's ordering, E1 and E2 do not apply (generative tools and mathematics content are present), and the first applicable code is E6, since the design is not an empirical experiment with a comparison. Note that the design is qualitative, so E6 is applied as the closest fit for a non-eligible empirical design; E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) would also apply. Decision is exclusion at abstract stage based on positive evidence of a qualitative design.

quote: The study is based on a review of international literature and UNESCO guidance on generative AI in education.
rationale: The abstract describes a narrative literature review and policy guidance analysis, not an empirical study. No experimental or comparison group and no learning outcome are reported. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), which is the first applicable code in order here since E1 to E5 cannot be confirmed as the decisive failure from the abstract alone.

quote: The study followed a descriptive research design in which a customized version of ChatGPT served as a self-learning assistant for students in a programming class for one semester.
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive design with a questionnaire and interview of a single class, with no control group that lacks generative AI. Outcomes are perceptions only, not a quantitative learning measure. Exclusion is based on positive evidence of no comparison group (E3). Outcome perceptions-only would also be E5, but E3 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: This study examines the lived experiences and perceptions of secondary-level students in Nepal
rationale: Abstract describes a phenomenological qualitative design (Google Forms and semi-structured interviews with 15 students) examining perceptions and lived experiences. There is no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical quantitative study meeting the design criteria. The STEM domain is also not indicated. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of qualitative design and perception-only outcomes; the first applicable code in order is E3 for no control group, but the qualitative nature (E6, not an empirical study of the eligible kind) is the most fitting primary reason. Coding follows the protocol order: E1 not applicable (ChatGPT is learner-facing), E2 domain not clearly STEM, E3 no control group is positively evident.

Abstract is not available in the index, so no positive evidence of any criterion failure exists. The title indicates ChatGPT (a generative LLM) used by undergraduate students, published 2024, which fits intervention, population and date. Whether there is a non-ChatGPT control group, whether the content is STEM (interdisciplinary learning), and whether a quantitative learning outcome and SMD-computable data exist cannot be determined from the title alone. Per rule 2, not excluded at abstract stage; advance to full text for these checks.

Abstract describes a proposed approach to decision support in information protection subsystems using a generative network. It is not a learner-facing generative AI intervention in a learning activity, has no control group, no learning outcome, and no participants. It reads as a conceptual/methodological proposal rather than an empirical study. Under the code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing) would be the first applicable code; however the primary failure is that it is not an empirical study. Applying the first-applicable rule strictly: the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI for learning, so E1 is the first code that applies. Excluding with E1 is the strictly correct code under the ordering.

quote: Here, we show various ways in which high school students use ChatGPT during a physics laboratory session
rationale: The title and abstract describe a case study of high school students using ChatGPT in a physics lab session, with no mention of a control group or comparison condition. Positive evidence of a failed comparison criterion is present: the design is a case study, which the protocol excludes. Exclusion code E3 (no control group without generative AI) is applied as the first failing criterion in order that is evidenced at abstract stage; the case-study design also fails the design criterion. Intervention, population (high school), and domain (physics) are met.

criteria.criteria_note: Gamified PBL e-learning game; no indication of a generative AI tool learners interact with. GenAI is mentioned only as background motivation.

quote: Quantitative questionnaires of student motivation and experiences with e-learning were evaluated.
rationale: The intervention is a gamified problem-based e-learning game on startup processes. The abstract gives no evidence that learners interact with a generative AI tool; GenAI is mentioned only as background motivation for the teaching design. The study also reports only perceptions and survey opinions, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Following the code order, E1 applies first because the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

quote: Generative AI-Supported Task-Based Instruction among Chinese EFL Undergraduates
rationale: The study concerns English vocabulary instruction (EFL), which is language learning and not STEM content. Per protocol, language learning is excluded from the domain criterion, so E2 applies as the first failing criterion in code order (E1 does not apply since learners interact with GAI). Other criteria (control group, design) are not clearly stated in the abstract but the decision rests on E2.

quote: This opinion piece argues that as AI eventually becomes ubiquitous in education, educators should aim to use the technology to challenge students
rationale: The record is an opinion piece with use-case descriptions, not an empirical study. It reports no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome; the reported feedback is survey-based perception only. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies as the first failing criterion in code order.

quote: Data (n = 25) were analyzed, and free-response answers were thematically coded.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-cohort assignment (n = 25) with a survey and rubric-based assessment, with no control group that does not use generative AI. This is positive evidence of no comparison group, so E3 applies. Domain (immunology course) and outcome measurement are not further assessed, since the first failing criterion governs.

quote: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted with 495 undergraduate, master's, and doctoral students
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey examining associations between AI acceptance, self-efficacy and well-being. It has no intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome (self-efficacy and well-being are perceptual/affective measures). Design is correlational, so it fails the comparison and design criteria. E3 is the first applicable code in order that fits the lack of a control group without generative AI; the record would also fail E5 and E6 on the same evidence.

The record has a title only and no abstract. The title describes a generative AI utilization education program for gifted students, which suggests a learner-facing generative AI intervention and a K-12 population, and it reports creative problem-solving skills as an outcome. However, the title does not show whether there is a control group, whether the design is randomized or quasi-experimental, or whether the domain is STEM. The protocol excludes only on positive evidence at the abstract stage, so the record is held as unsure for full-text review.

quote: This study investigates the comparative impact of three instructional conditions: traditional instruction (TI), LLM-assisted learning (LLM-AL), and human-AI collaborative learning (HAICL) on 240 secondary school students
rationale: Abstract describes an LLM-assisted learning condition with a traditional instruction control group, quasi-experimental pretest-posttest design with comparison group, secondary school students, mathematical reasoning and critical thinking outcomes (quantitative). Nothing in the abstract gives positive evidence of failure on any criterion. Effect-size data and publication type cannot be verified at abstract stage, so include and check at full text.

criteria.rationale_note: Survey of perceptions and satisfaction; no control group; no learning outcome.

quote: The study contributes to a better understanding of AI tool integration in diverse academic disciplines
rationale: The abstract describes a questionnaire-based survey of students' perceptions and satisfaction with ChatGPT (business, engineering, IT). It reports no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; outcomes are perceptions and satisfaction only. The design is survey, which is also ineligible. Exclusion is on E5 (no quantitative learning outcome), the first code that clearly applies after the intervention and population checks. Note that the design also fails the comparison and design criteria, and the STEM domain is unclear given that the disciplines include Business.

Abstract describes a continuous extension of Bayesian Knowledge Tracing evaluated through controlled simulations and mastery-estimation error, not an empirical learner-facing intervention with a control group and learning outcome. The study has no comparison group of learners without generative AI and no quantitative learning outcome measured on students. Excluded on E5 as the primary failing; design is also not a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison. Abstract positively shows simulation-based model evaluation, so exclusion is justified despite the abstract-stage rule.

quote: this paper examines the conceptual underpinnings and empirical evidence for rethinking teacher preparation programs
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/review-style paper discussing teacher education innovations, including generative AI practicums only in passing. It reports no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study. Excluded at abstract stage on E6 based on positive evidence that it is a conceptual paper, not an empirical study.

Title describes an AI teaching assistant used in college chemical engineering education (STEM domain, higher education population), and the venue is a journal. However, there is no abstract, so the intervention type (whether generative AI), the presence of a control group, the design, and the learning outcome cannot be assessed. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is advanced to full text.

quote: A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 300 undergraduate nursing students using the developed questionnaire.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey examining predictors of GenAI-supported learning behavior, with no experimental or comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. Nursing is a health professions domain, which the protocol excludes, so the record fails on domain as well. Exclusion code E3 is used as the first applicable code under the protocol order for the missing control group; the design is in fact correlational (survey), so the record would also fail on design.

quote: stratified randomization of AI access across the 16-week semester
rationale: At abstract stage all criteria appear plausibly met: ChatGPT-4o (generative) used by engineering undergraduates, an AI vs non-AI comparison via Mann-Whitney U tests, randomized AI access, and academic performance as outcome. Published 2026 journal article. Design, outcome measurement, and effect-size data cannot be fully verified from the abstract, so advance to full text rather than exclude. No exclusion evidence found.

quote: Compared to traditional teacher-led instruction, AI Chatbots significantly enhance students' PSE in programming skill
rationale: Fifth-grade students in a Chinese primary school with a control group receiving traditional teacher-led instruction; programming domain, journal article, 2025. The abstract does not state whether the AI chatbot is generative (intervention unclear) and the outcome is self-efficacy, which is a perception-type measure; whether any quantitative learning outcome (e.g., programming skill performance) was collected is unclear. Advancing to full text to check whether the chatbot is LLM-based and whether a non-self-efficacy performance outcome exists. Note: the outcome measure is self-efficacy; the protocol's affective-outcome exclusion may apply at full text.

quote: Employing the descriptive survey method, the study's sample comprised graduate and post graduate students
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive survey of students' ChatGPT usage and perceptions, with no experimental or quasi-experimental design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Survey design is not an empirical experiment meeting the protocol's design criteria, so it is excluded as not an eligible empirical study (E6). Exclusion is supported by positive evidence in the abstract, not missing information.
rationale_note: Survey-based; no comparison group; outcomes are perceptions and usage.

criteria.rationale_note: Descriptive survey design with no comparison group

quote: A descriptive survey research design was adopted.
rationale: The abstract reports a descriptive survey design using a questionnaire with mean and standard deviation analysis. There is no control or comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome is measured; the outcomes are perceived accessibility, utilization, and challenges. Under the protocol, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first applicable code in order, since the design fails the comparison requirement. Survey design also fails the Design criterion and the outcome is perception-based, but the exclusion code order places E3 first among applicable codes.

quote: One hundred ninety-eight students responded to a survey developed to collect their opinions on how they see the use of AI in schools.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey of student opinions only, with no experimental or quasi-experimental design and no control group. Outcomes are perceptions and self-reported productivity, not a quantitative learning measure. No comparison group without generative AI is described, so the study fails the comparison and design criteria. Exclusion E3 is applied as the first failing criterion in code order that is positively evidenced; the design is a survey, which under the protocol would also be non-eligible (E5/E6 could apply). Coded E3 because the absence of a control group is the clearest failing element at abstract stage.

quote: A cross-sectional survey design involving 384 teachers from various educational institutions across Indonesia was employed.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of teachers (not learners interacting with generative AI), with no control group and no learning outcome. Positive evidence of failure exists for intervention (teachers' readiness, not learner-facing GenAI), population (in-service teachers), design (survey), and outcome (perceptions/readiness, not learning). Per protocol the first applicable code is E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI), so E1 is the code that should be reported, not E3.

quote: Therefore, this study used semi-structured interviews (N = 9) to investigate how university English instructors in Japan are currently addressing the use of MT and AI tools in their courses.
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of English instructors about their policies. It is not an empirical learning experiment, has no control group, no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no quantitative learning outcome, and the domain is English language learning (non-STEM). Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the eligible sense) is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that fits; E1 and E2 could also apply, but the design is qualitative interview research, so E6 is the most direct fit.

criteria.intervention_note: LLM-powered learning environment suggested by title; no abstract available

rationale: Abstract stage with no abstract in the index; only the title and venue are available. The title indicates an LLM-powered creative project-based learning study with children, which may meet the intervention and population criteria, but the title does not show a control group, quantitative learning outcome, STEM domain, or design. Per rule 2, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is kept for full-text review rather than excluded.

criteria.quote: Without a pre-exposure baseline, a comparison group, or direct learning-outcome measures, the study cannot establish educational effectiveness or GenAI's independent effect.
criteria.rationale: Repeated Q-methodology study of learner perceptions (viewpoints) with no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; the abstract itself states no learning-outcome measures. Design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. Also E3 (no control group) would apply, but E5 is listed first in the order used by the protocol? Per the code order, E3 precedes E5; however the abstract gives positive evidence of no comparison group, so E3 is the first applicable code. Coding E3 as the first failing criterion.

quote: We propose a solution using agents to orchestrate specialised large language models and to demonstrate its applicability in graduate level cybersecurity topics
rationale: Generative AI (LLM-based agents) tutoring system in graduate cybersecurity education, so intervention and population appear met. The abstract does not state a control group or design, and it mentions only subjective factors as outcomes, so comparison, design, and outcome are unclear. Cybersecurity domain fit is also not fully settled from the abstract. Abstract does not give positive evidence of exclusion, so advancing to full text.

quote: This paper explores the potential of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in revolutionizing engineering education by designing and offering up-to-date content.
rationale: The abstract describes an exploratory/discussion paper on the potential of generative AI in engineering education. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Exclusion is based on positive evidence of a non-empirical design in the abstract.

quote: A survey is conducted among 430 students of an MSc degree in computer science at the University of Hertfordshire, UK, and their opinions about the tool are studied.
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of student opinions about ChatGPT. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome; it measures only perceptions. Under the rule that exclusion codes are reported in order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing) is not clearly indicated, since students are described as using the tool only in general terms, so E5 is the first clear failure on the outcome. Design is a survey, which is also ineligible. Exclusion is supported by the abstract's positive evidence that the study is perception-only.

quote: This paper offers a reflective analysis based on the author's first-hand teaching experience at a Chinese university
rationale: The abstract describes a reflective analysis based on first-hand teaching experience, not an empirical comparative study. There is no control group and no quantitative learning outcome reported. This is not an empirical study under E6. Earlier codes (E1, E2) are not clearly positively failed from the abstract, so E6 is the first code that clearly applies in the protocol order given the evidence is a reflective essay; abstract-stage evidence is positive for the absence of an empirical design.

quote: This review critically examines the emerging role of AI in civil engineering education and proposes an integrated framework
rationale: The record is a narrative review that proposes a conceptual framework (AI-CEEIF). It reports no experiment, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so E6 applies. E6 is the first applicable code in order here, since the review's non-empirical nature is the primary failure; E1 and E3 are not assessable from the abstract alone. The quote is verbatim from the abstract, which describes the paper as a review.

quote: A quasi-experimental pretest-posttest design was employed.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study appears to meet all criteria: ChatGPT-supported AI instruction vs conventional lecture control (quasi-experimental with comparison group), undergraduate mathematics (ODEs), 2026 publication, and a quantitative achievement test (ANCOVA, F and partial eta-squared reported). Effect-size computability (means/SDs) is not visible in the abstract, and full text is not yet checked, so this is an include for advancement to full text. No evidence of failure of any criterion in the abstract. Publication type (journal) appears met from venue name.

quote: The study used a self-constructed questionnaire for data collection; this questionnaire comprised the positive and negative effects of using ChatGPT on working memory performance.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-sample survey of university students' perceptions of ChatGPT effects. There is no control group or comparison condition, and the design is survey-based, not an experiment or quasi-experiment. Outcomes are self-reported perceptions rather than a quantitative learning measure. Positive evidence of failure on comparison, design, and outcome criteria is present, so exclude. E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol order that fits the missing control group; E5 and E6 would also apply.

quote: The three predictor variables had a positive and significant effect on students' perception of Generative AI-based learning
rationale: The study is a single-survey PLS-SEM model of students' perceptions of generative AI-based learning. It has no control group and no learning outcome measure; the only outcome is perception, which is excluded. Coding E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) as the first applicable code; the design also lacks a comparison group (E3 would also apply, but E5 is reached first in order only if E3 is not prioritized — here E3 precedes E5 in the code list, so E3 is the first applicable code). Note: on strict code order, E3 applies first and the decision should be read as E3.

quote: This conceptual article delves into the potential benefits, challenges, and future directions of how educators might adapt practices to accommodate the use of AI tools
rationale: The record is a conceptual article with no empirical study, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It fails E6 (not an empirical study). Embedded systems programming is arguably STEM, but E6 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that is clearly positively met.

quote: Adopting random sampling at University S, this study distributed questionnaires to survey generative AI use among 101 undergraduates
rationale: The abstract describes a questionnaire survey with correlation and regression analysis of AI use against critical thinking, with no experimental manipulation or control group. This is a correlational/survey design, which fails the design criterion. Under the exclusion codes, this maps to E6 (not an empirical study is a weak fit; the closest code for a non-experimental survey design). Domain is also not clearly STEM. Excluding at abstract stage because positive evidence shows the design is not a randomized or quasi-experiment with a comparison group.
rationale_note: Note: no exact code for correlational/survey design exists; E6 applied as nearest match.

quote: A qualitative case study design was employed, involving four English Education students at a college in Garut
rationale: The study is a qualitative case study with four students and semi-structured interviews, with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is also an EFL argumentative writing study, which is not STEM. Per the rule to report the first applicable code in order, E2 (non-STEM content) would come before E3 and E5. The first applicable code by the protocol order is E2, so the exclusion code should be E2 rather than E3. Corrected: the first code that applies is E2.

criteria.quote: The qualitative study involved 75 fifth-year pre-service teachers at the Free University of Bozen-Bolzano (Italy), working in 23 groups.
criteria.rationale: Abstract describes a qualitative case study (document analysis and thematic coding of Teaching Units and AI Use Reports) with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. Fails comparison, design, and outcome criteria. Not an empirical study in the protocol's quantitative sense; E6 is the most applicable code given the qualitative design. Domain (English for Young Learners) is also not clearly STEM. Per the code order, E1 does not apply since GenAI is learner-used, E2 is arguably applicable too, but the qualitative design is the clearest positive failure; E6 is chosen.

quote: This paper systematically sorts out the application scenarios of artificial intelligence in chemistry courses.
rationale: The abstract describes a narrative review/discussion paper of AI applications in undergraduate chemistry courses. It reports no controlled comparison, no experimental design, and no quantitative learning outcome. Although it mentions "reform practice data" from universities, no comparison group or effect statistics are described, so the paper is not an empirical controlled study. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Note that the code order rule would place E1 first, but the abstract gives no positive evidence of a learner-facing generative tool in a specific design, so E6 is the most applicable first failing code.

quote: survey results and qualitative written responses from 24 school leaders representing 10 universities
rationale: Participants are university school leaders (administrators), not students, so the population criterion fails (E4). The study is also a descriptive survey with no control group, no learner-facing generative AI intervention, and no learning outcome; these would also fail, but the first applicable code in order is E1 for intervention. Applying the protocol order strictly: E1 applies first because the study does not involve learner-facing generative AI (AI use is institutional management by leaders). Therefore the code reported should be E1 under the stated order.
quote_text: survey results and qualitative written responses from 24 school leaders

quote: students who utilized ChatGPT outperformed those who did not in subjective history questions
rationale: The study is in history education (Malaysian Chinese Independent School history studies). History is not among the protocol's STEM domains (science, mathematics, statistics, engineering, computer science, programming, data science), so E2 applies. This is a clear positive failure of the domain criterion visible in the abstract, so it is excluded at abstract stage. The comparison group and design (quasi-experimental with a non-ChatGPT group) also appear to be present.

quote: Adopting a qualitative approach, semi-structured interviews were conducted via Zoom with a sample of 10 male and female senior university students
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of 10 students with thematic analysis. It has no control group, no comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical experimental design and fails the design, comparison, and outcome criteria. E6 is applied as the first code that clearly applies in the order given, since the study is a qualitative empirical study rather than an experiment. Domain is also not clearly STEM (academic writing). Excluded on positive evidence at the abstract stage.
rationale_code_note: E6 is used for non-experimental qualitative design; strictly, E3 (no control group) also applies, but E6 precedes E3 in the code list only if the study is judged non-empirical. The study is empirical, so the more accurate first applicable code is E3.

quote: A combination of convenience sampling and snowball sampling was employed to collect questionnaire data from 561 K-12 teachers across multiple provinces in China.
rationale: Survey study of in-service K-12 teachers' behavioral intention to use GAI (TAM/SEM). Not an empirical learning intervention with a control group; no learner-facing GAI use and no quantitative learning outcome. Population is in-service teachers, which the protocol excludes. Under the protocol's exclusion-code order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing GAI) is the first applicable code, but the design is a cross-sectional survey, which fits E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of an eligible design). Exclusion is clear from the abstract.

quote: This paper explores the potential of generative artificial intelligence (AI) to transform higher education.
rationale: The abstract describes a conceptual/position paper that proposes a strategic framework. It reports no empirical study, no comparison group, and no learning outcome data, so it is not an empirical study (E6). Domain is also not specified as STEM.

quote: Using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods approach, the study involved 50 students enrolled in an educational technology course. A quasi-experimental design was implemented
rationale: Abstract describes a quasi-experimental design with experimental and control groups among higher-education students, which fits the design and population criteria. However, the abstract says only "AI-assisted microlearning" without specifying whether the AI is generative, so intervention is unclear. The domain is also unclear: an educational technology/multimedia course is not obviously STEM. The outcome is engagement, measured via ANCOVA; whether that is a quantitative learning outcome versus an affective measure (which the protocol excludes) is unclear. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not exclusion evidence, so this goes forward to full text for the intervention, domain, and outcome checks.

quote: AI model of user's choice is run fully locally, no data is transmitted, and it can be used to do tasks with students' data, such as summarization of evaluations, simple grading, and creation of quiz materials using RAG.
rationale: The abstract describes a RAG-based local LLM used to generate open educational materials, with uses such as summarizing evaluations, grading and quiz creation. This appears to be teacher-side material preparation rather than learner-facing generative AI, and no control group, learner sample, or quantitative learning outcome is described. Excluded under E1 at abstract stage on positive evidence that the intervention is not learner-facing. Other criteria are not evidenced either way in the abstract.

quote: The results indicate a generally positive perception of these tools in enhancing students' understanding of complex biological content (M=3.26, SD=1.95)
rationale: The study is a descriptive questionnaire survey of perceptions with no control group, no intervention comparison, and no quantitative learning outcome. Perception-only outcomes are excluded. Design is a survey, which is not an empirical experimental design eligible under the protocol. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible design) is the most applicable; E3 (no control group) and E5 (no learning outcome) also apply, but E3 is coded earlier only if the intervention check passes, and the abstract gives no learning outcome. Following the order, the first applicable code given the survey-only design is E6.

The record has only a title, venue, and year, with no abstract. Linear algebra is STEM (mathematics) and the 2026 date meets the date criterion. Nothing in the title shows a generative AI intervention, a control group, or a quantitative outcome, but the absence of information is not evidence of exclusion at the abstract stage. Kept for full-text review to check intervention, comparison, design, and outcome.

criteria.criteria_note: Descriptive survey design; no control group evident

quote: "A descriptive research design of the surv ey type was adopted for the study."
rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive survey design using a structured questionnaire and descriptive statistics only. There is no separate control group that does not use generative AI, so the study fails the comparison requirement. Outcomes are self-reported attitudes and motivation, not quantitative learning measures, and the design is not an experiment or quasi-experiment. Under the abstract-stage rule, the design and comparison failures are positive evidence, so the record is excluded. E3 is the first applicable code in the protocol's order that the abstract supports; the study also lacks a learning outcome (E5) and a clearly generative AI intervention is not specified (E1 unclear).

quote: A descriptive-quantitative, cross-sectional design was employed, involving 380 students from 11 colleges of a Philippine state university.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional descriptive survey with no control or comparison group, so it fails the comparison and design criteria (E3). It also reports only perceptions and usage, with no quantitative learning outcome, and is not STEM-focused. Exclusion is reported under E3 as the first applicable code in the protocol's order, since the design lacks any comparison group. Even if the code were E5 or E2, the record would still be excluded.

quote: A cross-sectional survey, involving 147 participating students, was conducted using a structured questionnaire.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of students' knowledge, willingness, and concerns about GenAI. It has no experimental or comparison group, and it reports only perceptions and attitudes with no quantitative learning outcome. Under the protocol's ordering, E1 (intervention not learner-facing GenAI) is not clearly the first failure, so the first clear failure is E6, as the design is not an empirical experiment of the eligible type. Note: strictly, the design is a survey, which the protocol lists as an exclusion under Design; E6 is the closest code for a non-experimental empirical study.

quote: Using a qualitative approach, this study explores how study abroad staff in the Claremont Consortium engage with and assess the implications of AI within international contexts.
rationale: The abstract describes a qualitative study of international education professionals' perceptions, with no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and participants who are staff rather than students. It is not an empirical quantitative study meeting eligibility. Coded E6 (not an empirical study of the eligible type); the primary failure is design (qualitative), with population (staff, not students) and outcome (perceptions only) also failing. Note the instruction to report the first applicable code in order: E1 would arguably apply first because the AI is used by staff, not learners, but the abstract does not give clear positive evidence of learner-facing use. Given the explicit qualitative design, E6 is the most defensible code.

quote: Twenty students completed the pre-assignment questionnaire, and 18 completed matched pre- and post-assignment questionnaires after two withdrawals.
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group pre-post case study with matched pre- and post-assignment questionnaires and no control group without generative AI, which is positive evidence of a failed comparison criterion (E3). Design is a qualitative-dominant case study, which also points against eligibility. Other criteria are not clearly failed at abstract stage. Exclusion is on E3 as the first applicable code in the protocol order that the abstract supports.

quote: One hundred (100) educators are chosen from the district (V) out of 140 teachers registered with the state public school in Lagos state using simple random techniques.
rationale: The sample is in-service science teachers (educators), which the protocol excludes from the population criterion. The study is a questionnaire survey on attitudes and perceptions, with no learner-facing AI intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of failure exists for population, design, comparison, and outcome, so the record is excluded. E4 is the first applicable code in the stated order for the population failure, though E1 and E3 and E5 and E6 also apply to the same record. Under the order of codes, E1 (intervention not learner-facing) would come first; however the abstract does not show learner-facing AI, so E4 is reported as the clearest positive failure.

quote: An analytical cross-sectional study included 423 undergraduate nursing students recruited through convenience sampling from nursing colleges in Swabi, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey, not an experiment or quasi-experiment with a comparison group. It has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome measured after an intervention; the "perceived lower grades" are self-reported perceptions. Nursing is also health professions education, which falls outside the STEM domain. The protocol's first-applicable code order puts E1 (intervention) first, but the abstract does not clearly show whether GenAI was learner-facing, so E6 (not an empirical study design meeting eligibility, i.e., a non-eligible cross-sectional survey) is applied as the decisive reason. This is a judgment call on code choice; the design failure is the clearest evidence.

quote: Using 184 programming exercises from an introductory-bioinformatics course, we evaluated the extent to which one such tool-OpenAI's ChatGPT-could successfully complete programming tasks.
rationale: The study evaluates ChatGPT's own performance on exercises; learners do not interact with the tool as part of a learning activity. No control group without generative AI is described, and the outcome is the model's solve rate rather than a learner outcome. E1 applies as the first failing code, since the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

quote: Participants' answers were evaluated by one human rater and three LLMs using three prompt engineering techniques to generate an evaluation result.
rationale: At abstract stage, the LLMs are used to grade learners' open-ended answers, not as a learner-facing tool in a learning activity; the protocol excludes AI used only for grading (E1). The domain is English language learning, which is non-STEM (E2 would also apply), but E1 is the first applicable code in order. No control group without generative AI is described, and the outcome is LLM-rater agreement rather than learner learning.

quote: Within semi-structured interviews, 35 undergraduate students having experienced GenAI use expressed their perceptions
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of student perceptions with no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical comparison design, so it fails E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of a quantitative experimental/quasi-experimental design). Its STEM content is also not specified. Coded E6 as the first applicable code given the qualitative, non-experimental design; the outcome is perceptions only (E5 also applies in substance).

quote: we propose a threshold selection method based on Tukey’s IQR fences
rationale: The paper is about a threshold selection method for code plagiarism checking (Levenshtein similarity) and generating AI codes to compare against student code. It does not describe a learner-facing generative AI intervention with a control group receiving business-as-usual or non-AI conditions; there is no learning outcome or comparison group evident. Excluded under E3 (no control group without generative AI), as the design is a similarity/plagiarism analysis rather than a comparative experiment. Abstract gives positive evidence that the comparison criterion fails.

Abstract describes an LLM-based reasoning-chain and personalized explanation system used with 2,854 students in applied mathematics, with reported comprehension gains (27.8%). Intervention, population, and domain appear to fit. However, the abstract does not state whether a control group without generative AI exists or what design was used (only "experimental evaluation"), so comparison and design cannot be confirmed. Reported metrics (accuracy, satisfaction, response times) are not clearly learning outcomes. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is advanced for full-text review rather than excluded.

quote: A case study with engineering students was conducted to evaluate its effectiveness.
rationale: Abstract describes a ChatGPT 4.0 API chatbot in a flipped Statics course (generative AI, learner-facing; STEM; university students). However, it is described as a "case study" and reports positive reception and perceptions; the abstract gives no indication of a control group, a randomized or quasi-experimental design, or a quantitative learning outcome. Those cannot be ruled out from the abstract, so the record advances to full text for checking design, comparison, and outcome.

quote: Results indicate a strong openness to AI coaching, with over 50% of participants expressing a willingness to use such tools
rationale: The study is a survey of 49 university students on receptivity to AI coaching, plus a conceptual framework. It has no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome; it reports only perceptions and willingness. Domain is not STEM (coaching/wellbeing). Excluded at E5 as the first applicable code in the protocol order that is clearly supported; the design also fails (survey, not an experiment), which would apply on full text.

quote: Eighty tenth-grade students from a public high school in Indonesia were assigned to either an experimental group receiving ChatGPT-supported discovery learning instruction or a control group receiving conventional instruction
rationale: At abstract stage, all criteria appear met: ChatGPT-supported discovery learning (generative AI, learner-facing implied), a conventional-instruction control group, quasi-experimental design with comparison group, high school (K-12) students, mathematics content, problem-solving test outcome, and 2026 publication date. Publication type (journal article) is consistent with the venue listing but not fully verified. Abstract reports sufficient means and SDs for SMD computation. No positive evidence of exclusion, so include and verify at full text.

quote: Participants included 736 students from two private institutions in Quezon City and Manila, who voluntarily responded to a validated, self-developed questionnaire administered via Google Forms.
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational, survey-based mixed-methods study with no intervention and no comparison group, so there is no separate control group without generative AI. Correlation of AI dependency with self-reported deep learning and retention is a perception/survey measure rather than a quantitative learning outcome from an experimental comparison. Design is clearly not eligible (survey/correlational), so E3 is applied as the first-applying code at abstract stage given the absence of any control group.

quote: The study applied a survey design, collecting data through Google Forms from undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral students.
rationale: The study is a survey of student perceptions of ChatGPT. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and is not an experimental design. Survey designs are excluded by the Design criterion. Under the exclusion-code order, E6 (not an empirical study) is not strictly the right fit since the survey is empirical, but the design fails and no learning outcome is measured. Per the ordering rules, the first applicable code is E3 (no control group) or E5 (no quantitative learning outcome); E5 is the clearest positive evidence, since the outcome is only perceptions. Reassessing: the record is correctly excluded under E5 as the outcome is perceptions only.

quote: To the Editor, We deeply appreciate the transparency and informed consent principles articulated by Prof. Anand and Prof. Vaderhobli
rationale: This record is a letter to the editor commenting on a prior article about chairside generative AI privacy. It is a commentary, not an empirical study, so it fails E6. It also reports no comparison group or quantitative learning outcome and is dental education, which falls outside the STEM domain. The first applicable code in order is E1, but the intervention is not clearly described as learner-facing, so E6 is the clearest ground for exclusion. Publication type is also likely not eligible (editorial/letter), but E6 is the primary code.

quote: The increase in the overall self-directed learning score from 65.3 before implementation to 91.0 after implementation
rationale: The abstract describes an R&D/ADDIE study with a pretest-posttest of a single group (65.3 before, 91.0 after implementation) and no control group that does not use generative AI. This is positive evidence of a single-group pre-post design, which fails the comparison and design criteria (E3). Biology is also outside the protocol's STEM domain list, though that is not the first applicable code. The outcome is self-directed learning, which is affective-adjacent, and is not used as the basis for exclusion.

quote: We designed and implemented a programming course focusing on collaboration between students and Gen AI.
rationale: Programming course with conversational generative AI, so the intervention and domain fit. The abstract describes an empirical case study using observations, surveys, reports, dialogues, and interviews, with no control or comparison group. This is positive evidence of no comparison group, so E3 applies. Outcomes are perceptions and self-reported skills rather than a quantitative learning measure, so E5 could also apply, but the first applicable code in order is E3 is not the first; E1 and E2 do not apply and E3 is the first code that clearly fails.

quote: This article proposes a theoretically grounded methodological framework for analysing learning processes in AI-supported physics classrooms
rationale: The record presents a methodological/theoretical framework with an "illustrative application" rather than an empirical comparative study. No control group or quantitative learning outcome is described in the abstract, and the paper does not appear to be an empirical experiment. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study). Positive evidence of non-empirical nature is the framework framing; the abstract explicitly says it foregrounds process rather than effectiveness and offers no comparison group.

quote: The analysis was conducted using relevant statistical measures, including descriptive statistics, CFA, and Pearson correlation.
rationale: Abstract describes a single-sample survey of 93 undergraduates analysed with CFA and Pearson correlation, with no separate control group that avoids generative AI. Design is correlational/survey, so no comparison group exists (E3). Outcomes are self-reported perceptions and mean ratings rather than a quantitative learning measure, which would also fail E5. Exclusion code E3 is reported as the first applicable code in order, given the absence of a control group.

This is a cross-sectional PLS-SEM survey of UTAUT2 constructs (acceptance, intention, self-reported usage) among 194 Costa Rican university students. There is no experimental or quasi-experimental control group, and the outcomes are perceptions and intention/usage rather than a quantitative learning outcome. Excluded at E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) as the first clearly applicable code in the order given; the design also fails the comparison and design criteria. Abstract-stage evidence is strong enough to exclude because the study is a survey of acceptance, with no learning measure.

quote: This perspective proposes that generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools may help address this imbalance by lowering the barriers to educational content creation
rationale: The record is a perspective article describing a proof-of-concept animation made with an LLM. It reports no comparison group, no learner interaction with generative AI, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study, so it fails E6. Other criteria (no control group, no outcome data) also fail, but E6 is the first applicable code in order that is supported by the abstract.

quote: Analysis of responses to comprehensive nursing exam questions by large language models
rationale: The study compares LLM answers (ChatGPT, DeepSeek) with nursing graduates' scores on a comprehensive nursing graduation exam. Nursing is a health profession, which the protocol excludes from the STEM domain (health professions education is out of scope). The design is also cross-sectional, comparing LLMs with students rather than a control group of learners who did not use generative AI, so it does not meet the comparison or intervention criteria (the LLMs answered exams rather than learners interacting with them as part of a learning activity). Exclusion code E2 applied as the first failing criterion in code order. Note: E1 could arguably apply first since learners do not interact with the AI, but the abstract does not clearly establish that, so E2 is the clearest positive failure.

quote: A post-task survey was provided to participants to explore students' perceptions of how structured collaboration with GenAI tools influences innovation, strategic thinking, skill development
rationale: The abstract describes a single-group classroom study of 123 students using GenAI, with outcomes based on a post-task survey of perceptions. There is no described control group without generative AI, so E3 applies. Outcomes are also perception-based, which would fail E5. Domain (entrepreneurship) is not clearly STEM. E3 is the first applicable code in order, so it is reported.

criteria.quote: A qualitative case study involved 10 students from a public vocational high school in Bandung
criteria.rationale: The study is a qualitative case study with interviews, observations, and document analysis; it has no control group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical quantitative design meeting the protocol's design criterion. Coded E6 as a non-quantitative (qualitative) empirical study; the design and outcome criteria both fail on the abstract, and the domain is not clearly STEM. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of qualitative design.

quote: A qualitative case study involved 10 students from a public vocational high school in Bandung
Evaluation was conducted on 9 students with 39 submissions for three Java assignments with different difficulty levels.
rationale: Generative AI (Claude AI) feedback is learner-facing and the domain is programming, but the study is an R&D evaluation of a single group of 9 students across three assignments with no control group that lacks generative AI. The abstract reports only pre/post-style score trends and satisfaction, so the comparison and design criteria are not met (E3). Exclusion on E3 is based on positive evidence in the abstract of a single-group design.

criteria.domain_note: Vue.js front-end programming is computer science/programming content
criteria.population_note: Students implied but level not stated in abstract

quote: Teaching practice results show that the experimental group significantly outperformed the control group in engineering modeling and full lifecycle competency development.
rationale: At the abstract stage, the study appears to involve generative AI as a student-facing coding assistant in a Vue.js programming course (STEM), with an experimental vs control group and a reported significant outcome difference. Design (randomized or quasi-experimental), whether the control group lacked generative AI, the sample level, and whether the outcome data allow SMD computation cannot be determined from the abstract. No positive evidence of exclusion, so advance to full text.

criteria.stage_note: survey-based correlational association between AI use frequency and academic performance; no control group

quote: This study explores the impact of AI chatbot usage on students' academic outcomes on the basis of survey data from Duke University.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey study of AI chatbot usage and academic performance, with associations (inverted U-shaped relationship, random forest prediction) rather than a randomized or quasi-experimental design with a non-generative-AI comparison group. There is no indication of a control group without generative AI, so the comparison criterion fails on positive evidence. Design is also not experimental (survey/correlational), which would independently fail the design criterion. Coded as E3 (no control group without generative AI), the first applicable code in the order given; the abstract does not clearly show a learning intervention, so the design-based exclusion is the most direct reason.

quote: a Large Language Model (LLM) (i.e., ChatGPT) is evaluated as a zero-shot classifier that receives only natural-language summaries of temporal behavior and predicts performance tiers
rationale: The LLM is applied by researchers as a zero-shot classifier over summaries of LMS logs, not as a tool learners interact with during a learning activity. The study is also observational (clustering and ANOVA on logs, no control group with/without generative AI), so it fails the intervention criterion (E1) and the design/comparison criteria. E1 is the first applicable code in order.

quote: As a result of the testing, it was determined that digital support is one of the key elements for students' adaptation during the initial period of study at the university
rationale: University students, published 2025. The abstract describes an AI assistant prototype for the discipline "Modern information technologies" but does not say whether the tool is generative, whether a control group without generative AI exists, or whether a quantitative learning outcome was measured (it mentions "level of educational motivation" and "quality of training" without specifics). Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record advances to full text for checking the generative model, comparison group, design, and outcome data.

quote: To the best of our knowledge, Bangladeshi tertiary-level students' perception of ChatGPT use in their education has not yet been studied.
rationale: The record describes a study of tertiary students' perceptions of ChatGPT use, with a survey and thematic analysis. The text gives no control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome; the outcome is perception-based, which the protocol excludes. Although the population (tertiary students) and intervention (ChatGPT) fit, the study lacks a learning outcome. The first applicable code in order is E3 (no control group) since the design has no comparison, but the clearest and most direct failure is E5, the perception-only outcome. Exclusion is warranted on the abstract-stage evidence. Domain is unclear since STEM content is not stated. Abstract stage: the excerpt is from the body text rather than a clean abstract, but it gives positive evidence of a perception-only design.

quote: We synthesise insights from our reflections into design considerations regarding rubrics' importance, discipline-related challenges, students' perceived epistemic legitimacy, and selective use of generative AI for imagery integration.
rationale: The abstract describes a design-and-reflection paper in which the authors synthesise insights from their own reflective diary. It reports no control group, no comparison condition, and no quantitative learning outcome. This is a reflective, non-empirical account, so E6 applies. Although the protocol's order would put E3 first, the abstract gives no evidence of a comparison group, so E6 is the first code supported by positive evidence in the record.

quote: An empirical pilot study was conducted using this platform with CS I students at a state university in the southeastern United States.
rationale: Abstract describes an LLM-driven (OpenAI API) introductory programming platform with CS I students and quiz-score effect sizes (d = 0.63, 1.02), so intervention, population, domain and outcome appear met. However, the abstract does not state whether there was a control group or a randomized/quasi-experimental comparison; the effect sizes could come from a single-group pre-post design (E3). Cannot tell at abstract stage, so advance to full text to check comparison and design.

quote: Eighteen participants, including 15 medical students and 3 practicing doctors, engaged with an AI VP simulating a primary care consultation for prostate cancer risk assessment.
rationale: Single-group feasibility study: all 18 participants used the AI virtual patient, with no control group lacking generative AI. Outcomes are survey-based perceptions (fidelity, immersion, motivation, usability) rather than learning measures. Domain is medical communication training (health professions education), which is also outside the STEM scope. Exclusion code E3 applied as the first failing criterion in code order (E1 does not apply since the AI is learner-facing; E2 would also fit the health-professions domain but E3 comes first).
rationale_note: Exclusion code order: E1 not applicable; E2 (content not STEM) arguably applies since this is medical communication/health professions education; the first applicable code in order is E2, not E3. Corrected below.

quote: Through a scoping review of existing literature, we explore how GenAI can assist educators in collecting relevant assessment materials
rationale: The abstract describes a scoping review of existing literature, not an empirical study with a control group or quantitative learning outcome. It is a review, so it fails the design and empirical-study requirements (E6). Also, the GenAI use is by educators for assessment design, not learner-facing, but E6 is the first applicable code given the review design.

quote: Pre- and post-program questionnaires were administered to assess changes in student perceptions towards generative AI
rationale: Single-group pre-post design of one cohort of 99 students. Students are split into AI and non-AI user groups by prior experience, which is not a randomized or allocated control condition. Outcomes are perceptions and satisfaction, not a quantitative learning measure. Exclude under E3 (no control group without generative AI; single-group pre-post). Domain is judo therapy clinical reasoning, which is health professions education and likely fails E2 as well, but E3 is the first applicable code in the order given by the protocol's cascade at abstract stage. Stage is abstract, so the exclusion rests on the design evidence.

quote: To compare the performance of humans, GPT-4.0 and GPT-3.5 in answering multiple-choice questions from the American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) Basic and Clinical Science Course (BCSC) self-assessment program
rationale: The study compares GPT models' answers to published human performance percentages from an ophthalmology self-assessment bank. Learners do not interact with the AI as part of a learning activity, there is no separate learner control group using non-generative AI, the design is not an experiment, and the content is medical (ophthalmology) rather than STEM. The earliest applicable code is E1 (intervention not learner-facing), but the most clearly failing criteria are population/domain/design; I report E4 as the first clear failure on population (no students, human percentages are from a clinical self-assessment audience). Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract.
quote_content: To compare the performance of humans, GPT-4.0 and GPT-3.5 in answering multiple-choice questions from the American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) Basic and Clinical Science Course (BCSC) self-assessment program

quote: This study examines cases of research ethics in the generative AI era from universities internationally and domestically, proposing practical guidelines for university writing education.
rationale: The record is a policy/guideline review proposing writing-education guidelines. It is not an empirical study: there is no experiment, no comparison group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Writing education is also not STEM content. Excluded under E6 (not an empirical study), the first code that applies after checking E1 and E2 (E1 cannot be confirmed from the abstract, but E6 is decisive).
rationale_note: Abstract-stage decision; positive evidence of non-empirical design.

rationale: The record has only a title and venue (Transportation Research Part C, 2026). No abstract is available. The title describes LLM-assisted reinforcement learning for autonomous driving, which suggests a non-learner-facing use of an LLM and no students or STEM learning population. However, the abstract stage requires positive evidence of failure to exclude, and the title alone does not establish that. Nothing in the record gives positive evidence of a failed criterion, so the record is retained as unsure for full-text review.

quote: Participants were allocated to a control group receiving conventional training and an experimental group utilizing AI technology, applying a quantitative experimental design.
rationale: At abstract stage, the study appears to be a controlled experiment of MathGPT and Flexi 2.0 (LLM-based tutors) versus conventional training among pre-service mathematics educators in Calculus I (higher education, STEM), with problem-solving outcomes and published 2024. Statistics for SMD, journal status, and full-text language are not visible in the abstract, so they cannot be excluded here. Advancing to full text to verify effect-size data and publication type.

quote: A quantitative, cross-sectional research design was employed.
rationale: Cross-sectional survey of university students measuring LLM dependency and emotion regulation questionnaire scores. No learner-facing generative AI intervention is administered and there is no control group, so comparison and design criteria fail. Outcome is a psychological trait measure, not a learning outcome, and the domain is not STEM. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study is not accurate for a survey), but the first applicable code in order is E1 because no intervention is administered; however the record reports a cross-sectional survey, so the most defensible code is E3 for lacking any comparison group. Excluding at abstract stage on positive evidence of a correlational survey design with no comparison group.

The abstract describes a quantitative descriptive survey of 150 undergraduates on adoption readiness and perceived reliability of GenAI tools. There is no control group or comparison condition, and no learning outcome is measured; the study is survey-based, not a randomized or quasi-experimental design. Survey perceptions do not meet the outcome criterion. Under the protocol's first-applicable-code order, E3 (no control group without generative AI) is the first failing criterion that applies at the abstract stage, with the design and outcome also failing. Exclusion is supported by the abstract's description of a "quantitative descriptive survey design" with no comparison group.

The record has only a title and venue, with no abstract. The title ("Assessing students' intention to adopt generative artificial intelligence") suggests a survey-style study of behavioural intention (perceptions), which would fail the outcome criterion and likely the design criterion. Venue is Journal of Accounting Education, so the domain is probably non-STEM. However, none of this is positive evidence in the abstract-stage record, and the rule is to exclude only on positive evidence. Advance to full text for verification.

quote: The sample comprised 40 students (M = 20,9, SD = 2,43; 62,5% female) from Tomsk State University, who were assigned to either an experimental group (N = 20) learning with an AI lecturer or a control group (N = 20) following a conventional online format.
rationale: Abstract describes an AI lecturer (DeepTalk) with a conventional online control group, which is consistent with the protocol, and university students. However, the abstract does not state the subject domain (STEM content is not mentioned), does not indicate whether the AI is generative, and the outcomes emphasized are perceived engagement and satisfaction, which are excluded. No quantitative learning outcome is evident in the abstract. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is passed to full text to check domain, generative nature of the tool, and whether any learning measure exists.

quote: We developed an automated program that can generate three types of questions to cover basic programming concepts
rationale: At abstract stage, ChatGPT is used to generate quiz questions for teachers' materials preparation; learners are not shown as interacting with the generative AI tool as part of a learning activity. The students only answer AI-generated questions in an open-book assessment, with no described control group without generative AI and no described comparison. Positive evidence of E1 (AI used to prepare materials, not learner-facing generative AI) is present, and the comparison criterion also appears to fail, so the record is excluded on the first applicable code E1.

quote: The article analyzes the effectiveness of using artificial intelligence (AI) in English language learning and the personalized approach to language learning based on AI technologies.
rationale: The study concerns English language learning, which is non-STEM content, so the protocol's domain criterion fails (E2). This is positive evidence in the abstract, so exclusion at abstract stage is appropriate. Other criteria (comparison group, quantitative outcome, design) are not clearly stated in the abstract but do not need to be resolved given the domain failure.

quote: among students with lower levels of self-regulated learning, GenAI use was negatively associated with critical thinking, creative thinking, and computational thinking
rationale: The abstract describes a correlational/moderation analysis of GenAI usage levels against thinking skills, not a randomized or quasi-experimental design with a separate non-GenAI control group. There is no positive evidence of a control group without generative AI, so E3 applies. Design appears correlational (survey-type), which would also fail the design criterion. Population (Chinese university students) and outcomes (thinking skills) appear acceptable, but the comparison fails.

quote: Changes in their confidence in AI utilization, perception of prompt engineering, and eight core competencies ... were measured before and after the training.
rationale: The abstract describes a single group of 71 students measured before and after prompt engineering training, with paired-samples t-tests and no control group. This is a single-group pre-post design, which the protocol excludes under E3 (comparison). Domain is also unclear (liberal arts course, generic thinking competencies), but the comparison failure is the first applicable code in order of the exclusion list.

quote: A quantitative, comparative, cross-sectional research design was employed involving 350 pre-service teachers
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey measuring technology acceptance (Acceptance of Artificial Intelligence Scale) and compares genders within a single sample. There is no control group that does not use generative AI, and no learning outcome is measured; the outcome is an attitude/acceptance measure. Exclusion code E3 is applied as the first failing criterion in order of the codes for the comparison failure, with E5 also applicable since no quantitative learning outcome is reported. Under code order, E3 is reported.

Abstract describes a quasi-experimental study of AI chatbots in higher vocational humanities courses. Humanities content is not STEM, so the record fails the domain criterion (E2). This is positive evidence of failure, so exclusion at abstract stage is justified. Other criteria (chatbot generative nature, control group, quantitative outcome such as academic performance) are unclear from the abstract but do not need resolving given the domain failure. Venue "Advanced Electromagnetics" is unusual but not a basis for exclusion under the protocol here.
