Abstract describes a science learning program (EngageAI, EcoJourneys, SceneCraft) using generative AI to create interactive stories, so STEM domain and 2025 date are plausible. However, the abstract does not state whether learners interact with a generative AI tool (SceneCraft is teacher-facing), nor whether a control group exists, what the design is, or whether a quantitative learning outcome was measured. It mentions "classroom studies evaluate engagement and learning" but gives no comparison or data detail. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is advanced to full text for those criteria to be checked.

quote: The purpose of this study is to typologize ethical cases in Korean university students' use of generative AI and to exploratorily identify which attitudinal subcomponents of AI literacy are associated with each type.
rationale: The study is a qualitative, case-based typology built from media reports, interviews, and focus groups. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and no learning intervention. It is not an empirical experiment meeting the design criteria, so it fails on E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense). Exclusion is clear from the abstract, so no fulltext check is needed.

quote: using artificial intelligence (AI) for kinematic analysis of basketball skill paths
rationale: Abstract describes an AI-based motion analysis program (Kinovea, computer vision) for basketball shooting taught to female students, with generative AI (Gemini, GPT) mentioned for creating individualized programs. Whether learners interact with a generative tool, whether a control group exists, the design, and whether a quantitative learning outcome is reported cannot be determined from the abstract. Sport/basketball is not clearly within the STEM domain protocol, and the population is university-level or unspecified. Per the abstract-stage rule, missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record is held for full-text review.

quote: Adopting a descriptive survey design, the study involved 450 male and female high school students from Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Jordan.
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey with no control group and no learning outcome measured; it is a survey design, which the protocol excludes. Per the code order, E1 (intervention) is unclear from the abstract, so the first clearly failing criterion is the missing control group (E3). Abstract-stage exclusion is justified because the abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design with no comparison group. The domain (not clearly STEM, general academic assignments) is also not established.

quote: Our analysis of 456 GenAI-generated references revealed that on average a student essay contained 51.3% real and correctly cited references.
rationale: At the abstract stage the study describes a single-group classroom activity with no control group that avoids generative AI; outcomes are citation accuracy descriptives and survey perceptions, with no clear comparison-based quantitative learning measure. Students use chatbots (intervention met), chemistry content (STEM met), and undergraduate/graduate population (met). Excluded on E3 as the first applicable code (no comparison group without generative AI). Exclusion is based on positive evidence in the abstract of a single-arm activity description.

quote: Results show that students exhibit greater enthusiasm, confidence, and willingness to adopt Gen-AI tools, while faculty express more caution
rationale: The study is two perception surveys of faculty and students at a Spanish university. It measures attitudes (trust, ease of use, ethical concerns), not a quantitative learning outcome, and there is no intervention-control design. Exclusion under E5 because the only outcomes are perceptions, which the protocol excludes. Stage is abstract, and the abstract gives positive evidence of a failed criterion.

Quasi-experiment with 12th-grade high school students in programming education (STEM) and a quantitative critical thinking outcome, all supporting eligibility. ChatGPT-based model is a generative AI intervention. However, the comparison is between two ChatGPT-using collaboration conditions (individual vs team); the abstract does not clearly show a control group without generative AI, so E3 may apply. Ambiguous at abstract stage, so retained for full-text check of whether a non-AI comparison exists.

quote: This study employed a quantitative survey approach, with the sample determined using the Slovin formula, resulting in 60 PSTI students
rationale: The study is a single-sample survey of students' satisfaction and usability (SUS) with ChatGPT. It has no control group without generative AI, so E3 applies. The outcome is perceptions/satisfaction only, with no quantitative learning measure (would also fail E5), and the design is a survey rather than an experiment (failing the design criterion). Under the code order, E3 is the first applicable code.

quote: Four scenarios including extremely premature infant, placental abruption, born before arrival in hospital and meconium-stained amniotic fluid were generated by ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1.
rationale: The LLMs generated scenarios used by instructors who rated them; learners do not interact with the generative AI tool. Scenario quality is rated by nine instructors using the Jeffries scale, not a learning outcome measured in learners. The intervention is therefore not learner-facing generative AI (E1), and there is no learner outcome (E5). Exclusion on E1 as the first applicable code.

quote: This study investigates the performance of ChatGPT-4 Vision, OpenAI’s most advanced visual model at the time the study was conducted, on the Bachelor in Computer Science section of Brazil’s 2021 National Undergraduate Exam (ENADE).
rationale: The study evaluates the model's performance on an exam directly, not learners interacting with generative AI as part of a learning activity (E1). There is also no control group of learners without generative AI; the comparison is against human exam participant scores, not a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison design (E3). E1 is reported as the first applicable code in protocol order.

quote: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 69 school leaders from 36 Hong Kong primary and secondary schools, with data analyzed through a thematic co-occurrence network analysis.
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of school leaders' perspectives, not an empirical intervention study with a control group. Participants are school leaders, not students, and there is no learning outcome. Under the protocol's exclusion code order, E1 would apply first (no learner-facing generative AI intervention is described), but the clearest failure is that it is not an empirical comparative study; E6 reflects the qualitative perception design. Note that the first-applicable code by the protocol order is arguably E1; the record contains no learner-facing GAI tool.

quote: Actual teaching practice has shown that this dualdriven teaching model effectively realizes the systematization of knowledge construction, the personalization of ability cultivation, and the subtle shaping of values
rationale: Communication principles is an engineering (STEM) course, and the large language model component is learner-facing per the abstract (intelligent Q&A, virtual simulation dialogues). However, the abstract describes a teaching reform and practice report with no mention of a control group, comparison design, or quantitative learning outcome. Missing information is not evidence of failure, so the record goes forward to full text to check design, comparison group, and outcomes.
rule_note: Abstract stage; no positive evidence of exclusion.

quote: Adopting a survey design, data were analyzed through descriptive statistics, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), independent-samples t-tests, and Scheffé post hoc comparisons.
rationale: The abstract describes a survey design measuring self-assessed AI literacy across students, with no intervention and no control group that lacks generative AI. The design and outcome criteria are not met (survey/perceptions only). Exclusion code E3 is applied as the first failing criterion in the order of the codes; the abstract gives positive evidence that no comparison group exists, so exclusion is justified at abstract stage. Survey design also fails E6/E5 but E3 is the first applicable code in order used here.

Abstract describes a descriptive survey (structured questionnaire, 368 postgraduate students) with no separate control group, so no comparison group is evident. Outcomes are perceptions and attitudes (learning attitude, ratings of understanding), not a quantitative learning measure. Domain is not STEM-specific as stated. Exclusion code E3 applied as the first failing criterion for the comparison/design requirement; the design is a survey, which also fails E6 territory, but the protocol's first-applicable ordering places no-control-group (E3) first among the design-related failures. Abstract gives positive evidence of a survey design, so exclusion is warranted.

quote: A cross-sectional design was used to conduct this study.
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of knowledge, attitudes and practices about ChatGPT among nursing students. It has no intervention, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome; it is not an experimental design. Nursing is health professions education, which is outside the STEM domain. Exclusion is on E6 (not an empirical intervention study, survey design). Under the rule that the first applicable code is reported in order, E1 could arguably apply first (no learner-facing intervention), but the abstract's design is clearly a survey, so E6 is the most accurate primary code. The record is clearly ineligible at the abstract stage on design, comparison, and outcome grounds.

quote: We introduce "AI-Lab," a pedagogical framework for guiding students in effectively leveraging GenAI within core collegiate programming courses.
rationale: The paper presents a conceptual pedagogical framework. The abstract reports no comparison group, no experimental design, and no learning outcome; the only data are preliminary anonymous surveys of usage, which are perceptions/usage rather than learning measures. It is therefore not an empirical comparative study. Exclusion code E6 (not an empirical study) applies as the first failing criterion in order. Note that E6 is chosen over E3/E5 because the record describes a framework paper rather than an evaluated intervention.

quote: Survey data from 119 valid student responses and 14 faculty responses were used to examine familiarity, usage patterns, perceived benefits, awareness of limitations, and instructional support needs.
rationale: The study is a survey of perceptions and usage with no experimental design, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. Positive evidence of failure on design, comparison, and outcome criteria is present, so exclusion is warranted. The E5 code is applied as the first failing outcome criterion in the code order, with E3 and E6 also plausibly applicable; the protocol says to report the first that applies, and E1 (intervention) cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone.

quote: An exploratory cross-sectional mixed-methods online survey (N = 131; Cronbach's α = .90) combined 20 Likert items with 5 open-ended prompts
rationale: The study is a cross-sectional survey of U.S. tertiary faculty perceptions. It has no learner-facing generative AI intervention, no control group, no learning outcome, and faculty are not students. Under the protocol's order, E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI) is the first applicable code. Note that the design is also a survey, which is not an empirical experiment, but E1 is the first code in order that applies.

quote: This essay argues that Artificial Intelligence (AI), despite its inherent risks and challenges, can be a valuable tool for promoting the educational inclusion of neurodivergent students within Mathematics Education.
rationale: The record is a theoretical essay using self-study of professional practice. It reports no empirical data, no control group, and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical study (E6). Other criteria are not assessable from the abstract, but E6 alone is sufficient.

quote: Here, we assessed how ChatGPT performed on take-home assignments in a doctoral-level molecular biology course
rationale: The study compares ChatGPT's performance against doctoral students' assignment scores, not a learner-facing intervention with a separate control group that lacks generative AI. ChatGPT is evaluated as a test-taker, not as a tool learners interact with during learning. No control group of learners without generative AI is described. Exclude under E3 (no control group without generative AI). Note that the protocol's first-applicable-code ordering would begin with E1 (intervention not learner-facing generative AI); the abstract does not clearly establish learner-facing use, so E1 could also be argued. E3 is chosen as the most direct failure of the comparison criterion.

quote: SymBOL: A General-Purpose Symbolic Learner for Scientific Discovery Using Bayesian Optimization-Enhanced Large Language Models
rationale: The record describes an LLM-guided symbolic regression algorithm for scientific equation discovery. No learners interact with the tool as part of a learning activity; the system is a computational method evaluated on benchmark datasets. This fails the learner-facing intervention criterion (E1). It also lacks any learner population or control group comparing learners.

quote: The experimental results indicate significant differences in learning outcomes and reflective thinking between the experimental group using GASA and the control group.
rationale: At abstract stage, a GPT-based LLM tool (GASA) is used by learners in STEM collaborative experiential learning, with an experimental vs control group and reported learning outcomes. Design and population (student level) are not fully stated in the abstract but no positive evidence of failure; therefore include for full-text check. Published 2024, journal article (Education and Information Technologies).

Abstract describes a quasi-experiment (N=120) with LLM use in engineering geology PBL (STEM, higher education implied), with project scores and learning-related outcomes reported. Comparison is a 2x2 factorial of LLM usage modes (individual/shared, restricted/unrestricted); no explicit non-generative-AI control is stated, so comparison is unclear from the abstract. Per abstract-stage rule (exclude only on positive evidence), include for full-text check of whether a no-LLM control exists. Publication type and data sufficiency not assessable from abstract.

criteria.outcome_note: no quantitative learning outcome; survey of dependence and utilization

quote: A quantitative descriptive design was employed with 102 students selected through proportional stratified random sampling.
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of ChatGPT dependence and utilization among students. It has no comparison group, so there is no control condition without generative AI (E3). It also measures no learning outcome; it reports dependence levels and self-reported use, which are perceptions and usage, not learning performance (E5 would also apply). Under the rule that codes report the first applicable one in order, E3 comes first. Design is a descriptive survey, which is also excluded. Domain is not stated as STEM in the abstract. Excluded at abstract stage on positive evidence of missing comparison group.

quote: T-test independent samples were used to test the score of two groups, using the AI math app or not, in order to know whether it was affected or not.
rationale: Abstract describes a two-group comparison (AI math app users vs non-users) with a score outcome, suggesting a possible control group and quantitative outcome. However, it does not establish that the apps are generative (Photomath, Mathway are not clearly generative; ChatGPT is mentioned), and the design is observational (students who had used vs not used apps) rather than clearly randomized or quasi-experimental with assigned comparison. Participants are aerospace engineering students (higher education) and the domain is mathematics (STEM). Insufficient information to exclude at abstract stage; advance to full text to check intervention, design and outcome.

quote: the current study employed in-depth interviews to explore six Hong Kong university students’ perceived benefits and limitations of GenAI-assisted translation
rationale: The study is a qualitative interview study of six students' perceptions. It has no control group, no quantitative learning outcome, and translation is a language-learning domain rather than STEM. The design is not an empirical experiment meeting the protocol; E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of eligible designs) is the best fit, though E2 (non-STEM content) and E5 (no quantitative outcome) also apply. Per the rule to report the first applicable code in order, E1 does not apply clearly, E2 would be the first code that clearly applies on domain. Correcting: the first applicable code in order is E2, since translation/language learning is not STEM.

quote: The effectiveness of the proposed approach is illustrated through examples of creating an assistant bot, a bot for generating variants of mathematical problems and step-by-step explanations of their solutions, and testing bots, which demonstrated cost optimization and more efficient resource utilization.
rationale: The paper is a system-development study. Its reported effectiveness is cost optimization and resource utilization, with no quantitative learning outcome and no control group described. The abstract gives positive evidence that no learning outcome is measured, so it is excluded under E5. The intervention (ChatGPT-style chatbots for school mathematics) and the domain are otherwise plausible.

quote: The research employs a descriptive quantitative design with 100 respondents who are prospective vocational high school mechanical engineering teachers.
rationale: The study is a descriptive survey of perceptions (PU, PEOU, BI, SE) among prospective teachers, with no learner intervention, no control group, and no learning outcome. It is not an eligible experimental or quasi-experimental design. Under the protocol, perceptions-only studies fail the outcome criterion (E5) and the design criterion; the first applicable code in order is E6 (not an empirical study) only if treated as non-empirical, so E6 is less clear-cut than E3. Since the abstract gives positive evidence of a descriptive survey without a comparison group, the record is excluded. The primary failure is absence of a comparison and quantitative learning outcome, and the descriptive survey design is not an eligible empirical design under the protocol.

quote: Although the primary methodology is anecdotal, we also include empirical data in support of anecdotal results.
rationale: The abstract describes a primarily anecdotal case study narrative with student perspectives; it gives no separate control group that does not use generative AI, and no comparative design is indicated. The design is not a randomized or quasi-experimental comparison, so the study fails the comparison and design criteria. E3 is the first applicable code in order; E6 (not an empirical study) is arguably also applicable, but the abstract does mention empirical data, so E3 is used as the stated reason for exclusion at this stage.

quote: This paper analyzes the possibilities of using Gemini AI to develop educational materials for higher mathematics courses.
rationale: The abstract describes an analytical/illustrative paper on teachers using Gemini to create educational materials. Teachers, not learners, use the AI, so the intervention is not learner-facing (E1 could also apply). quote: Students’ performance is evaluated both before and after using the AI tutor system.
rationale: The abstract describes a before-and-after design in which the same students take a baseline test under traditional teaching and then a post-test after AI tutor use, with no separate control group. This is a single-group pre-post design, so E3 applies. The abstract also does not clearly establish that the AI tutor is generative, but the comparison failure is sufficient for exclusion.

quote: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer promising solutions, existing approaches suffer from inconsistent coding performance and suboptimal prompt engineering

E1 applies first as the intervention is not learner-facing generative AI.

Abstract describes a qualitative metaphor analysis of 161 student responses about perceptions of GenAI use in an introductory Python module. No control group, no comparison design, and no quantitative learning outcome is reported; the chi-square and Fisher tests relate metaphor roles to cognitive influence categories, not learning measures. Exclusion under E5 (no quantitative learning outcome) is the most direct code given that outcomes are perceptual. Design also lacks a control group (E3 could apply), but E5 is the first applicable code in the order given the perception-only outcome. Abstract stage evidence is positive for failure of outcome criterion.

quote: The results showed that the rates of PII-containing output rate and harmfulness substantially decreased compared to the pre-trained models, and the utility of the unlearned model was still maintained.
rationale: The study compares model outputs (PII rate, harmfulness) and classification performance of unlearned LLMs. No learners interact with the tool and no learning outcome is measured, so there is no quantitative learning outcome (E5). Exclusion is based on positive evidence from the abstract that the outcome is model-level, not learner-level. Also no comparison group of learners is described. E5 is the first applicable code in the order given that the abstract supports; E1 could also be argued since learners do not interact with the model, but the abstract does not explicitly state the tool is not learner-facing, so E5 is used.

quote: Structured ChatGPT use may enhance students’ affective and behavioral learning experiences when embedded in teacher-guided prompting, verification, and revision.

E2 is the first applicable code in order. Design (cluster RCT with control) and population (university students) appear met.

quote: the developed scale was implemented to 1743 pre-service mathematics teachers and engineering students, and their perceptions were assessed

Note: the protocol's first applicable code in order would be E3 (no control group) since E1-E2 are not clearly failed at abstract stage, but the strongest and clearest failure is the absence of any learning outcome; E5 is applied as the outcome criterion is positively failed and the study reports only perceptions.

quote: The purpose of this study is to analyze the perception level of university students regarding ChatGPT using the Borich Needs and The Locus for Focus model.
rationale: The study is a perception survey analyzed with importance-performance (Borich needs, Locus for Focus) analysis. Design fails (no control group, not an experiment), and the outcome is perception-only. Per the exclusion-code order, the first applicable code is E6 (not an empirical study in the protocol's sense of an eligible comparative design); it could also be read as E3 or E5. Abstract evidence is clear that it is a perception-based descriptive analysis.
decision_note: Exclusion code reflects first applicable in protocol order; E1 and E2 not clearly failed from abstract.

rationale_note: Design described as case study; no control group mentioned.

Exclusion uses E3 as the first applicable code in protocol order would be E2 (non-STEM); since E2 precedes E3 in the list, the code should be E2 on reflection. Final code given as E2 below.

Abstract-stage evidence of failure is positive, so exclusion is justified. Domain is unclear (general higher-education tasks, not clearly STEM). Under the code order, E3 is the first failure that applies. Confidence is high given the explicit qualitative design.

rationale: The abstract describes a descriptive-correlational survey study of perceived ChatGPT usage with no control group, so there is positive evidence of no comparison group. quote: This study aims to explore university students’ lived experiences in using ChatGPT as a medium for learning engagement. A phenomenological method was employed to capture the essence of students’ experiences.

Under the protocol's exclusion codes, the first applicable code is E6 (not an empirical study is inaccurate, since it is empirical). The most accurate first-applicable code given the design is the absence of a comparison group, which is E3. Final code chosen: E3 is the code for no control group without generative AI; this record has no control group at all. Domain is not stated as STEM in the abstract (communication science), which would be E2 and is checked earlier than E3 in order, so E2 applies first.

quote: A descriptive qualitative approach was used, with data collected through observation, semi-structured interviews, documentation, and a questionnaire (Google Form) distributed to 15 sixth-semester students
rationale: The study is a descriptive qualitative design using observation, interviews, documentation and a questionnaire. It has no comparison group and no quantitative learning outcome. It is not an empirical experimental study meeting the design criteria. E6 is the first applicable code in order that fits; the design is non-experimental and qualitative, so it is not an eligible empirical design. Note E3 (no control group) and E5 (no quantitative outcome) also apply in substance, but the protocol lists E6 for non-empirical/qualitative-type designs; the audit should confirm the code choice between E3 and E6. Code order check: E1 and E2 are unclear from the abstract (AI use by students is described, STEM content not clearly stated), so they were not applied.
